# Roadmap: perfectoid rings and spaces

**Summary.** Perfectoid spaces are the adic spaces on which Frobenius can be inverted: locally they
are adic spectra of perfectoid Tate rings, complete uniform Tate rings with a pseudouniformiser `ϖ`
such that `ϖ^p` divides `p` and Frobenius is an isomorphism `R°/ϖ → R°/ϖ^p`. This roadmap builds
their theory in that generality, with no perfectoid base field and with products of mixed- and
equal-characteristic rings allowed: almost mathematics over an arbitrary basic setup; perfectoid
Tate rings, tilts, Fontaine's `θ` and the classification of untilts by primitive ideals; the tilting
homeomorphism, perfectoid rational localisation, the sheaf theorem with almost acyclicity of `O⁺`,
and perfectoid spaces with fibre products; almost purity and the étale site; injections,
immersions, Zariski closed immersions and separatedness; cofiltered limits and finite-stage descent
of étale objects; `κ`-small perfectoid spaces and the pro-étale calculus; and tilde-limits and
Frobenius-controlled towers, sousperfectoid frames and spaces, analytic approximation,
perfectoid torsor presentations and the affinoid perfectoid basis of the rigid pro-étale site. The end results are the tilting equivalence
`Perfd/X ≃ Perf/X♭` with `X_ét ≃ X♭_ét`, the almost purity theorem (for a perfectoid Tate ring
`R`, `FÉt(R) ≃ FÉt(R♭)`, every finite étale `R`-algebra is perfectoid, and `S°` is almost finite
étale over `R°`), and the pro-étale calculus on which DiamondsAndVStacks builds its topologies.

Everything rests on Tau Ceti's Huber rings and adic spaces (the Foundations of adic spaces roadmap,
`TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces/README.md`, called AdicSpaces below, and its implementation under
`TauCeti.RingTheory.Huber` and `TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AdicSpace`) and on Mathlib's Witt vectors,
perfection, `PreTilt` and `WittVector.fontaineTheta`. The outputs are the geometric inputs of
pro-étale descent and diamonds (DiamondsAndVStacks) and of perfectoid Shimura varieties
and period spaces downstream. The analytic étale interfaces come from AdicEtaleGeometry;
this roadmap proves their perfectoid specializations.

| Layer | Construction |
| --- | --- |
| P0 | Almost mathematics over a basic setup |
| P1 | Perfectoid Tate rings, tilts, untilts and perfectoidness of split Tate rings |
| P2 | Rational localisation, the sheaf theorem and perfectoid spaces |
| P3 | Almost purity, sousperfectoid rings and spaces, polydiscs and the étale site |
| P4 | Injections, immersions and separatedness |
| P5 | Cofiltered limits, tubular approximation and finite-stage affinoid étale descent |
| P6 | `κ`-small perfectoid spaces, pro-étale morphisms and perfectoid torsor presentations |
| P7 | Tilde-limits, Frobenius-controlled towers and the rigid pro-étale basis |

Layers P0 and P1 can be developed in parallel up to the almost setup of a perfectoid ring, where
they meet.

## Scope and ownership

The tower-quotient and torsor-descent layers P8–P9 form the roadmap [PerfectoidTowers](../PerfectoidTowers/README.md).
Each layer's Dependencies paragraph names its mathematical suppliers by section.

**Dependencies.** DerivedModuleAlgebra §§0.1–0.11, 0.13–0.14, 0.25, 1.T.1, 1.1–1.9; AdicSpaces §§0–5, 6.1;
AdicSpacesPartII R0.0–R0.20.2, R1; AdicSpacesPartIII R2.4, R3.1, R3.5, R3.8, R3.9;
AdicEtaleGeometry A0, A1.0–A1.16, A1.2a, A1.6a, A2, A3.1–A3.2, A4.2–A4.5,
A4.2a, A4.7; PivotalSpherical Layers 2 and 7.

PerfectoidTowers imports both PerfectoidSpaces and DiamondsAndVStacks; diamond objects,
spatial presentations, and coefficient descent using diamonds belong to those two roadmaps. The
v-topology on perfectoid spaces belongs to DiamondsAndVStacks: P7 uses only the raw compact-open
covering condition
(Mathlib `IsCompactOpenCovered`), while the v-site built on that condition belongs to
DiamondsAndVStacks, its precoverage and topology to D2.2 and its subcanonicity and v-descent to
D2.7. The ordinary cotangent complex of a ring map and its square-zero deformation theory belong to
DerivedModuleAlgebra §§0.4–0.11, 0.13 and 0.25, consistently with SchemeAndStackFoundations §4.6,
and are consumed in P0.19; this roadmap owns only
its almost counterpart (P0.20). DerivedModuleAlgebra §§0.1–0.4, 0.14 and 1.1–1.9 own
the generic derived operations, ideal completion and bounded-torsion p-complete module descent.
Its §1.T.1 owns ordinary module towers, their product difference map, limits, six-term sequence
and module Milnor sequence; P0.27–P0.28 use these directly for almost annihilation and completion.
P4.15.1 consumes their carriers and maps; its finite-ideal simplicial descent extension and
transfinite compatibility feed only the prismatic construction of P4.15.2–P4.15.5.

The roadmap owns, layer by layer:

- P0: basic setups `(V, m)` (an idempotent ideal with `m ⊗_V m` flat) and their examples (the root
  setup of an element with compatible `p`-power roots, the setup `(K°, K°°)` of a valuation ring
  with non-principal maximal ideal), firm modules, the Serre quotient `V^a`-Mod of almost modules
  with almost elements and the left adjoint `M_!`, almost algebras and change of setup, almost
  finitely generated, presented, flat and projective modules with the `ε`-criteria, almost finite
  étale algebras with the trace-form criterion, the almost cotangent complex, nilpotent deformations
  of almost algebras and finite étale lifting, and almost sheaves with their almost cohomology.
- P1: perfectoid Tate rings and pairs, Frobenius on `R°/ϖ`, the tilt `R♭` with the sharp map and
  its functoriality, perfectoid fields and their tilts (compared with Mathlib's `Tilt`), Fontaine's
  map `θ` compared with `WittVector.fontaineTheta`, untilts and primitive ideals with the
  primitive-kernel theorem, the tilting equivalence for perfectoid Tate rings, completed filtered
  colimits and perfected Tate algebras, and the comparison with AdicSpaces' perfect field `F`.
- P2: the tilting homeomorphism `Spa(R, R⁺) ≅ Spa(R♭, R♭⁺)`, perfectoid rational localisation, the
  sheaf theorem with almost acyclicity of `O⁺`, affinoid perfectoid and perfectoid spaces, the tilting
  equivalence of perfectoid spaces, completed tensor products of perfectoid pairs and fibre
  products of perfectoid spaces.
- P3: the perfectoid-field application of henselian completion, almost purity in characteristic `p`, the Fontaine–Wintenberger
  theorem, the almost purity theorem, étale morphisms of perfectoid spaces with the comparison to
  AdicEtaleGeometry's étale morphisms, and the étale site of a perfectoid space with its tilting
  equivalence.
- P4: injections and immersions of perfectoid spaces, Zariski closed immersions and universal
  perfectoid Zariski closed subspaces, separated maps and the valuative criterion for separatedness.
- P5: the completed direct limit of perfectoid Tate pairs, cofiltered limits of affinoid perfectoid
  spaces with their cardinal bounds, `ω₁`-cofiltered limits, and finite-stage descent of étale objects.
- P6: `κ`-small and uniformly `κ`-small perfectoid spaces, affinoid pro-étale morphisms, pro-étale
  morphisms, products with profinite sets, the pro-category equivalence and the stability of
  pro-étale morphisms.
- P7: perfectoid tilde-limits, Frobenius-controlled integral towers, uniqueness and gluing of
  tilde-limits, the perfectoid Frobenius criterion for towers, and limits of perfectoid towers.


P1.1 owns the perfectoid Tate-ring theory and its equivalent Frobenius-modulo-`p`
criterion; P2.11 owns glued tilting. P3.17a's
sousperfectoid frames use P1.1's predicate `Perfectoid.IsPerfectoidTateRing` directly, so no
second perfectoid interface is compared with it; the modulo-`p` reformulation of P1.1 holds on
every complete Hausdorff uniform Tate ring.
The glued-tilting construction is `PerfectoidSpace.tiltFunctor` on this roadmap's
`Perfd` carrier, with the comparisons and slice equivalence specified in P2.11.

The boundaries with the neighbouring roadmaps: AdicEtaleGeometry A1.2–A1.3 and A1.6 supply the
finite étale and étale morphisms of analytic adic spaces and their sites on `TauCeti.AdicSpace`, and
A1.9 their forms `YonedaAdicSpace.IsFiniteEtale`, `IsEtaleLocalDescription` and `smallEtale` on the
analytic Yoneda carrier;
P3 restricts these notions to perfectoid spaces and compares them with its own. P6 constructs pro-étale morphisms
and the `κ`-small calculus. P7 uses Mathlib's compact-open covering condition
`IsCompactOpenCovered` directly and builds no site from it.
DiamondsAndVStacks builds the v-site on that condition (precoverage and topology in D2.2,
subcanonicity and v-descent in D2.7), uses it for its pro-étale and v-sheaf theory
and defines diamonds; PerfectoidTowers P8 proves
the quotient statements that identify the represented v-sheaf of a finite quotient. AdicSpacesPartII
owns the completed tensor product of Tate rings (R0.3–R0.4), fibre products of adic spaces (R0.7),

P2 proves that completed tensor products of
perfectoid rings are perfectoid, P1 adds only the unit criterion on the Gel'fand spectrum, and PerfectoidTowers P9

P7 compares its analytic Yoneda carrier with that theory and adds the perfectoid

## Conventions

Fix a prime `p`. A perfectoid Tate ring is complete and Hausdorff, uniform, and has a
pseudouniformiser `ϖ` with `ϖ^p | p` in `R°` such that Frobenius `R°/ϖ → R°/ϖ^p` is an isomorphism;
injectivity of Frobenius is automatic and the condition does not depend on `ϖ`. No perfectoid base
field is fixed; statements that hold only over a perfectoid field say so. A perfectoid Tate pair
`(R, R⁺)` is a Tau Ceti Huber pair with `R` perfectoid; `R°` is its maximal ring of integral elements
and `R°°` the topologically nilpotent elements. `Perfd` denotes perfectoid spaces of all
characteristics, a full subcategory of Tau Ceti's `PreAdicSpace` (sheafy pre-adic spaces covered by
affinoid perfectoid opens, P2.10), and `Perf` its characteristic-`p` subcategory, with `p = 0` in all
sections; `X♭` is the tilt, `♯` the sharp map,
which is multiplicative and continuous but not additive. Almost mathematics is always with respect
to a stated basic setup `(V, m)`: `m` idempotent with `m ⊗_V m` flat; for a perfectoid Tate ring the
setup is `(R°, R°°)`, equivalently the root ideal `(ϖ^{1/p^∞})` of a pseudouniformiser with compatible
`p`-power roots, and the two setups on `R⁺ ⊆ R°` are compared explicitly. "Almost zero", "almost
isomorphism", "almost finite étale" and "almost acyclic" are relative to that setup; an almost
statement is never silently upgraded to an actual one.

Rings of integral elements are open, integrally closed and contained in `R°`; completed colimits of
Tate pairs complete the colimit of the plus rings `ϖ`-adically and invert `ϖ`. "qcqs" means
quasicompact and quasiseparated; morphisms of perfectoid spaces are morphisms of adic spaces.
Tilde-limits carry both the topological condition and the affinoid density condition. Cardinals:
`κ`-smallness is tested on affinoid covers, and uniformly `κ`-small means `κ'`-small for a single
`κ' < κ` (P6.2); the cutoff cardinals are strong limits and may be singular.

Each target below is written with its hypotheses in the sentence, its source locator in parentheses
(short keys are resolved in the References), its API as named lemmas and its unit tests as `Checks`;
`Suggested.lean` gives typed forms for a subset of these targets and Checks. Existing definitions keep their library namespaces.
The names of definitions, lemmas and Checks in the target paragraphs are the names proposed for the
formalisation. A subsection whose targets are carried by declarations of `Suggested.lean` ends with
a `Lean:` line listing them, and the layer's Examples paragraph lists its Lean `example`s; a
target, definition or Check not named on a `Lean:` line is specified in this README only and has no
Lean declaration yet. Names of other roadmaps' declarations are theirs.

### From TauCetiRoadmap.AdicSpaces

Layers 0–1: Tate rings, pseudouniformisers, bounded sets, pairs of definition, completion,
valuation spectra and continuous valuations. Layers 2–3: Huber pairs, `Spa`, rational subsets,
completed rational localisation, structure presheaf, stalks, residue fields, pre-adic spaces. Layers
4–5: stable uniformity and the Buzzard–Verberkmoes theorem (layer 4.2, stably uniform implies
sheafy), adic spaces, open and closed subspaces, gluing. Layer 6: the perfect field `F` with its
`A_inf`, compared with the tilt of a perfectoid field in P1.

analytic Yoneda carrier `YonedaAdicSpace`, `CAff`, `ofAdicSpace`, global functions); A1.1–A1.3, A1.5,
A1.6 and A1.8: strongly sheafy rings, the finite étale pair (*finite-etale-affinoid-algebra*), étale
and finite étale morphisms of adic spaces with their stability properties (*etale-composition*,
*etale-base-change*, *etale-diagonal*), the étale site with its structure sheaf and rational descent,
and the Galois category; A1.9: the finite étale and étale predicates and sites on the analytic
Yoneda carrier (*etale-site-generalized*); A1.12: the corrected pro-étale site (*pro-etale-site-corrected*) with its
profinite-set objects, for the comparisons of P6; A1.0.1–A1.0.2: henselian pairs under
filtered colimits and along a pseudouniformiser; A1.0.3–A1.0.5: algebraic finite étale
colimits, henselian approximation, section topologies and completion comparisons;
A1.2a: uniformity of finite étale algebras; A1.6a: vector bundles on a stable étale basis;
A4.4: finite étale algebras under uniformization. The generic finite étale Galois torsor towers of AdicEtaleGeometry A4.2–A4.5 and
A4.7 supply the completed pairs, self-products and orbit homeomorphisms used by P1.32 and P6.15–P6.17. AdicSpacesPartII, by
subsection: R0.1 (adic ring homomorphisms), R0.3 and R0.4 (completed tensor products with their
universal property (*completed-tensor-product-universal-property*) and uniform completed tensor
products, Tate norm data and the spectral seminorm (*tate-ring-norm*, *spectral-seminorm*)), R0.5
(Banach tensors), R0.6–R0.10 (adic morphisms, fibre products, closed immersions, separatedness and
the valuative criterion), R0.13 (finite morphisms), and the analytification of R1. AdicSpacesPartIII,
by subsection: R3.1 (Čech acyclicity of the structure sheaf on sheafy Tate affinoids,
*sheafy-cech-acyclicity*), R3.5 (vector bundles on sheafy Tate affinoids), R3.8 (finite projective
modules and trace forms over sheafy Tate rings) and R3.9 (the Gel'fand spectrum of a Banach ring,

## How to read the build

P0 and P1 are independent until the almost setup of a perfectoid ring: P0 builds almost mathematics
over an arbitrary basic setup up to almost finite étale algebras, the almost cotangent complex and
finite étale lifting; P1 builds perfectoid Tate rings, tilts, perfectoid fields, `θ`, untilts and
the tilting equivalence of rings. P2 turns the ring theory into geometry (the tilting homeomorphism,
rational localisation, the sheaf theorem, perfectoid spaces and their fibre products), P3 proves
almost purity and builds the étale site, P4 the injections, immersions and separatedness, P5 the
cofiltered limits and finite-stage descent, P6 the `κ`-small calculus and pro-étale morphisms, P7 the
tilde-limits and Frobenius-controlled towers. Build order is by declarations: construct the
almost-algebra and module categories and the algebra adjunction in P0.8 before P0.16's
change-of-setup equivalence, then prove P0.8's `moduleEquiv`, its comparisons and the closed
monoidal structure. Construct P0.9's unitization before P0.25; its faithful-flatness comparison
uses P0.11 and is proved in P0.25. Construct `uniformTilt` in P1.7 before P1.4's perfectoid
specialization, and its comparisons with that specialization afterwards. Construct P1.24's
integral predicate and Frobenius criterion before P1.20's integral-to-Tate criterion.
A target's `*Needs:*` clause names the prerequisite declarations, the subsections of other
roadmaps and the library declarations it rests on, and each layer's Dependencies paragraph collects
the subsections of other roadmaps that the layer uses. P4.4 and the targets built on it use the
completed direct limit of P5.1–P5.3, which depends only on P1 and P2. Each subsection ends with the
Lean declarations that carry it, when there are any; targets without Lean are stated here only,
their carriers being formalisation tasks in their own right.

Each definition requires three discriminating Checks on its own carrier, including a
computed value and a degenerate case or non-example. Arithmetic identities, facts solely
about imported objects, repetitions of a target, and laws true of every morphism of the
same kind are supplementary calculations; they do not count toward these three Checks.
In particular, the following named calculations are supplementary wherever they occur:

- `cech_test_two_terms`, `naiveModel_test_two_exponents`, `lim1_test_sign`,
  `completion_test_torsion`;
- `trace_test_product`, `trace_test_dual_numbers`, `trace_test_unramified`,
  `differentials_test_char_two`, `cotangent_test_quotient`, `deformation_test_not_flat`,
  `differentials_test_sign`, `cotangent_test_unit_ideal`, `finiteEtale_test_swap`,
  `traceForm_test_product_diagonal`, `traceForm_test_dual_numbers_quotient`,
  `trace_test_quadratic_order`, `flat_squareZero_regular`, `not_isPerfectoidField_trivial`,
  `almostExact_test_nonseparated`, `cartan_zero_scalar`, `cartan_unit_scalar`,
  `cartan_two_term_additivity`;
- `filteredPrincipal_test_roots`, the root case of the powers-generate Checks of P0.1, `test_hom_formula`,
  `tight_test_principal`, `IsFiniteEtale_test_quadratic`, `kaehler_test_mathlib`,
  `map_id_test`, `test_constant_residue`, `restriction_disc_two_radii`,
  `rationalLoc_test_supplier`, `tiltHomeomorph_rationalSubset`, `pullback_tilt`,
  `perfectedTateAlgebra_fin_test`;
- `adjunction_test_two_terms`, `firmAdj_test_two_terms`, `sharp₀_zero`, `sharp₀_one`,
  `sharp₀_multiplication`, `global_sharp_zero_one`, `tiltEquiv_test_zero_one`,
  `residue_tilt_zero_one`, `rational_tilt_zero_one`, `tensor_tilt_two_constants`,
  `spaTiltHomeomorph_test_empty`, `spaTiltHomeomorph_test_whole`, `spa_space_empty`,
  `spa_space_whole`, `slice_identity`, `slice_affinoid_arrow`, `absolute_product_symmetry`,
  `pullback_identity_projection`, `homogeneous_zero`, `homLinearEquiv_zero`.

For example, `completion_test_torsion` only computes reduction from `ℤ/4` to `ℤ/2`;
it does not instantiate the completion complex. A complex comparison needs a Check
using that complex and its specified comparison map.

## Layer P0: almost mathematics over a basic setup

Almost mathematics is developed over an abstract basic setup `(V, m)`, so that it can be
instantiated later for `(R°, R°°)` and for the root ideal of a pseudouniformiser without
circularity. The layer builds the almost category as the Serre quotient of `V`-modules by almost
zero modules, with the functor of almost elements and the left adjoint `M_!`; the closed symmetric
monoidal structure; almost algebras with the left adjoint `B_!!`; almost finite generation and
presentation, flatness, projectivity, duals and traces, and the rank decomposition; flat, unramified,
étale and finite étale morphisms with the trace-form criterion and the comparison with Mathlib's
finite étale algebras; inversion of an element of `m`; almost Kähler differentials, the cotangent
complex of a ring map and the almost cotangent complex with its deformation theory; faithfully flat
descent; tight ideals, henselian pairs and modules over complete almost algebras; finite étale
lifting modulo a tight ideal; and almost sheaves with almost sheaf cohomology and almost Čech
complexes on a site.

### P0.1 basic setup `(V, m)`

The layer opens with the basic setup itself, its two standing examples and the firm-module model of
the almost category.

**Basic setup `(V, m)`: an idempotent ideal with flat `m ⊗ m`.** (*almost-basic-setup*) Let `V` be a
commutative ring (`[CommRing V]` in universe `u`) and `m` an ideal of `V`. A basic setup is a pair
`S = (V, m)` such that (i) `m` is idempotent, `m·m = m` (Mathlib `IsIdempotentElem m` in the
semiring `Ideal V`), and (ii) the `V`-module `m̃ := m ⊗_V m` is flat. Condition (i) is Gabber–Ramero's
basic setup, the only hypothesis they use before (2.5.14); it makes almost zero modules closed under
extensions ([GR] §2.1, (2.1.1), p. 7). Condition (ii) is the flatness they assume from (2.5.14) on
and use earlier for the exactness of `M ↦ M_!` in Corollary 2.2.22; it is imposed here once for all
almost mathematics of this roadmap, and every setup used here satisfies it: root ideals and maximal
ideals of valuation rings with non-finitely-generated maximal ideal satisfy condition (A) below, and
`m = V` is flat ([GR] §2.1, (2.1.1), p. 7, and (2.5.14), p. 32). Conventions: a `V`-module
`M` is almost zero if `m·M = 0`; a `V`-linear map is an almost isomorphism if its kernel and
cokernel are almost zero; `m̃` always denotes the tensor product `m ⊗_V m` (it maps onto
`m·m = m`, isomorphically when `m` is flat); the classical limit is `m = V`, which recovers ordinary
commutative algebra ([GR] §2.1, Example 2.1.2(i)-(ii), p. 7). Condition (A): `m` is a filtered union
of principal ideals; condition (B): for every `k ≥ 1` the `k`-th powers of elements of `m` generate
`m`. For an idempotent `m`, (A) implies (B): `x ∈ m = m^k` is a sum of products of `k` elements of
`m`, which lie in a common principal ideal `(z)`, so each product lies in `(z^k)`; without
idempotence (A) does not imply (B), as `(t) ⊆ 𝔽_p[t]` shows. (A) together with `m·m = m` implies
(ii) by *filtered-principal-union-tilde-flat* (P0.2). A basic setup is data, not a type class, because one
ring carries several setups: for a perfectoid Tate ring `R`, `(R°, R°°)` and `(R⁺, the root ideal of a pseudouniformiser)`, compared in layer P1. Bhatt's variant of the setup, with `m` itself flat, is a
special case ([Bhatt] §4.1, Assumption 4.1.2, p. 17). In `Almost`, define `BasicSetup` as the
structure with fields `ideal : Ideal V`, `isIdempotentElem : IsIdempotentElem ideal` and
`flat_tilde : Module.Flat V (ideal ⊗[V] ideal)`; `BasicSetup.tilde` as the `V`-module
`m̃ = S.ideal ⊗[V] S.ideal` with its multiplication map onto `m`; `BasicSetup.IsAlmostZero` (for a
`V`-module `M`: `∀ ε ∈ S.ideal, ∀ x : M, ε • x = 0`); `BasicSetup.IsAlmostIso` (kernel and cokernel
of `f : M →ₗ[V] N` almost zero); `BasicSetup.almostZero` (the object property of `ModuleCat V`
given by `IsAlmostZero`); `BasicSetup.classical` (the setup `(V, ⊤)`); `BasicSetup.zero` (the
setup `(V, ⊥)`: `⊥` is idempotent and `m̃ = 0` is flat); `BasicSetup.baseChange` (for
an algebra `W` over `V`, the setup `(W, S.ideal.map (algebraMap V W))`, *basic-setup-base-change*);
`BasicSetup.IsFilteredPrincipal` (condition (A)) and `BasicSetup.PowersGenerate` (condition (B)).
Use `IsIdempotentElem.eq S.isIdempotentElem` for `S.ideal * S.ideal = S.ideal`. Prove
`BasicSetup.isAlmostZero_classical_iff` (`(classical V).IsAlmostZero M ↔ Subsingleton M`),
`BasicSetup.IsFilteredPrincipal.powersGenerate` ((A) implies (B)),
`BasicSetup.powersGenerate` (flat `m̃` already implies (B), [GR] Proposition 2.1.7(ii), p. 9) and
`BasicSetup.isAlmostZero_iff_tensor_eq_zero` (`IsAlmostZero M ↔ Subsingleton (S.tilde ⊗[V] M)`,
the first clause of *almost-zero-iff-tilde-tensor-zero* (P0.2)). *Needs:* Mathlib `IsIdempotentElem`, `Module.Flat`,
`Ideal.span`.

**Checks.**

- Degenerate: for every commutative ring `V`, `BasicSetup.classical V`
  (ideal `⊤`) is a basic setup and `(classical V).IsAlmostZero M ↔ Subsingleton M`.
- Degenerate: for every `V`, `(V, ⊥)` is a basic setup
  (`⊥·⊥ = ⊥`, `⊥ ⊗ ⊥ = 0` is flat) and every `V`-module is almost zero for it.
- Non-example: for `V = ℤ_p` and `m` its maximal ideal, `m * m ≠ m`, so
  there is no `BasicSetup` with this ideal; accordingly `ℤ/p²`, an extension of `ℤ/p` by `ℤ/p` (both
  killed by `m`), is not killed by `m`, so a definition accepting non-idempotent ideals would lose
  closure of almost zero modules under extensions.
- Computation: for `V` the valuation ring of `ℂ_p` (or of the
  completion of `ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞})`) and `m` its maximal ideal, the residue field `V/m` is almost zero,
  while `V/pV` is not, because `p^{1/p} • 1 ≠ 0` in `V/pV` (`p^{1/2}` would not do for the second
  field when `p` is odd: `1/2 ∉ ℤ[1/p]`, so `p^{1/2} ∉ V`).
- Non-example: the principal ideal `(t) ⊆ 𝔽_p[t]`
  satisfies (A) but not (B): the squares of its elements generate `(t²) ≠ (t)`; so "(A) implies
  (B)" needs `m·m = m`.

- Over `(ℤ, ℤ)`, `tildeMul(2 ⊗ 3 + 5 ⊗ 7) = 41`.
- The same tensor ideal is linearly equivalent to `ℤ`.
- `tildeMul(1 ⊗ 1) = 1` over `(ℤ, ℤ)`;
  for `m = 0`, the entire linear map `tildeMul` is zero.
- `test_tilde_zero` — for `m = 0`, `m̃ = 0`; on the zero ring the classical and zero ideals coincide.
- Both `IsAlmostZero` and its object property kill `V/m` and the zero module; over `(ℤ, ℤ)` they reject `ℤ`.
- Scalar extension preserves the classical setup, makes the ideal zero over `V/m`, and makes it the unit ideal over `V[1/ε]` for `ε ∈ m` (including `ε = 0`).

- `filteredPrincipal_test_classical`, `filteredPrincipal_test_zero`, `filteredPrincipal_test_roots` —
  the unit ideal (common divisor `1`), zero ideal (common divisor `0`), and any compatible-root ideal satisfy (A).
- Positive powers generate the unit ideal, zero ideal, and root ideal respectively; for roots, pass far enough down the chain.
- `almostIso_test_classical` — classically, an almost isomorphism is exactly a bijective linear map.
- `almostIso_test_ideal_inclusion` — `m ↪ V` is an almost isomorphism, although it need not be surjective.
- `almostIso_test_zero_setup` — every linear map is an almost isomorphism when `m = 0`.
- `almostIso_test_classical_double` — multiplication by `2` on `ℤ` is not an almost isomorphism in the classical setup.
- `tildeToIdeal_test_classical`, `tildeToIdeal_test_zero`, `tildeToIdeal_test_two_terms` —
  multiplication onto the ideal is bijective classically and for the zero ideal, and sends `2 ⊗ 3 + 5 ⊗ 7` to `41` over `ℤ`.

### P0.2 the root setup of compatible p-power roots

**The basic setup of an element with compatible p-power roots.** (*root-ideal-basic-setup*) Let `V`
be a commutative ring, `p ≥ 2` an integer and `(ϖ_n)_{n≥0}` a sequence in `V` with
`ϖ_{n+1}^p = ϖ_n` for all `n`; put `ϖ := ϖ_0` and `m := ⋃_n ϖ_n V = Ideal.span {ϖ_n}`. No topology
and no perfectoid hypothesis enter: the construction is purely algebraic. Then `(V, m)` is a basic
setup, the root setup of `(ϖ_n)`: `m` is the increasing union of the principal ideals `ϖ_n V`,
`m·m = m`, and `m̃` is flat by condition (A). A `V`-module `M` is almost zero for it iff `ϖ_n M = 0`
for all `n` ([Bhatt] §4.1, Example 4.1.3, p. 18; cf. [ECD] §3, Definition 3.21, p. 19).
If `ϖ` is a nonzerodivisor of `V` then every
`ϖ_n` is a nonzerodivisor, each `ϖ_n V` is free of rank one, `m` is flat and countably generated,
and the multiplication `m̃ → m` is an isomorphism ([Bhatt] §4.1, Example 4.1.3, p. 18); the
nonzerodivisor hypothesis is used only for this clause. Replacing `(ϖ_n)` by the shifted sequence
`(ϖ_{n+k})_n`, or by any sequence `(ϖ'_n)` with `ϖ'_n V = ϖ_{n+c} V` for all large `n`, gives the
same setup. This is the input layer P1 instantiates with a pseudouniformiser admitting compatible
`p`-power roots. Define `BasicSetup.ofCompatibleRoots` (given `p ≥ 2` and `ϖ : ℕ → V` with
`ϖ (n+1) ^ p = ϖ n`, the setup with ideal `Ideal.span (Set.range ϖ)`); the ideal is `Ideal.span (Set.range ϖ)` by
definition. Prove `BasicSetup.mem_ofCompatibleRoots_ideal` (`x ∈ ideal ↔ ∃ n, ϖ n ∣ x`),
`BasicSetup.ofCompatibleRoots_isAlmostZero_iff` (`IsAlmostZero M ↔ ∀ n (x : M), ϖ n • x = 0`),
`BasicSetup.isIdempotentElem_span_roots` and `BasicSetup.flat_tilde_span_roots` (idempotence and
flatness of `m̃` for `Ideal.span (Set.range ϖ)`, the two fields of the structure), and, as
statements of this README with no Lean declaration yet: the simp rule `ϖ n ∈ ideal`; condition (A)
for the root setup; if `IsSMulRegular V (ϖ 0)`, flatness `Module.Flat V ideal` with `tilde → ideal` a
linear equivalence; invariance under shifting the sequence, or changing it by a cofinal equivalence
of principal ideals; and base change,
`(ofCompatibleRoots p ϖ h).baseChange W = ofCompatibleRoots p (algebraMap V W ∘ ϖ) _`. *Needs:* P0.1; Mathlib `Ideal.span`, `Module.Flat.of_free`,
`IsSMulRegular`.

Two supporting results. Almost zero modules and almost isomorphisms are detected by `m̃ ⊗ −`
(*almost-zero-iff-tilde-tensor-zero*): for a basic setup `S` and a `V`-module `M`, the conditions
`m·M = 0`, `m ⊗_V M = 0` and `m̃ ⊗_V M = 0` are equivalent; a `V`-linear `f : M → N` is an almost
isomorphism iff `1 ⊗ f : m̃ ⊗_V M → m̃ ⊗_V N` is an isomorphism; and if `m` is flat the multiplication
`BasicSetup.tildeToIdeal : m̃ → m` is bijective ([GR] §2.1, Remark 2.1.4(i), p. 8; [GR] §2.1,
(2.1.3), p. 7) — for
`V = 𝒪_{ℂ_p}` and `M = V/m`, `m ⊗ M = m/m² = 0`, while for `m = (p)` in `ℤ_p` one has
`m ⊗ ℤ_p/p = (p)/(p²) ≠ 0` (this uses Mathlib `Module.Flat.lTensor_exact`). Condition (A) implies that
`m ⊗ m` is flat (*filtered-principal-union-tilde-flat*): for an ideal `m` with `m·m = m` which is
the directed union `⋃_α V·x_α` of principal ideals, `m̃ = m ⊗_V m` is a flat `V`-module, so `(V, m)`
is a basic setup; the proof is the factorisation through `λ_{αβ}` of Mathlib
`Module.Flat.iff_forall_exists_factorization` ([GR] §2.1, (2.1.6), p. 8, and
Proposition 2.1.7(i) with proof, pp. 8–9). It applies to a root setup without assuming
`ϖ` to be a nonzerodivisor, and to a valuation ring with non-principal maximal ideal.

**Checks.**

- Computation: for
  `V = 𝔽_p[t^{1/p^∞}]` (the perfection of `𝔽_p[t]`, or the monoid algebra over `ℤ[1/p]_{≥0}`) and
  `ϖ_n = t^{1/p^n}`: `V/(t)` is not almost zero (`t^{1/p} ≠ 0` in it) while `V/m ≅ 𝔽_p` is almost
  zero.
- Degenerate: if `ϖ_0 = 1` (e.g. all `ϖ_n = 1`) then
  `m = V` and the root setup is `BasicSetup.classical V`.
- Non-example: the principal ideal `(t) ⊆ 𝔽_p[t]` (a
  single element without roots) is not idempotent, `(t)·(t) = (t²)`; so the root setup cannot be
  replaced by the ideal generated by `ϖ` alone.
- Compatibility: for `V` a valuation ring of rank
  one, `ϖ ∈ m` nonzero, equipped with compatible roots `ϖ_n` of `ϖ` for all `n` (e.g. `𝒪_{ℂ_p}`,
  `ϖ_n = p^{1/p^n}`), `ofCompatibleRoots` and `ofValuationRing` (P0.3) have the same ideal, the
  maximal ideal: `|x| < 1` forces `|x| ≤ |ϖ|^{1/p^n}` for some `n` because `|ϖ|^{1/p^n} → 1`; for
  `ϖ` a unit the root ideal is `V`, and for rank `> 1` (value group `ℤ[1/p] × ℤ[1/p]`
  lexicographic, `ϖ` of value `(1, 0)`, roots of value `(1/p^n, 0)`) the root ideal misses the
  elements of value `(0, 1)`, which lie in the maximal ideal.
- Degenerate: if every `ϖ_n = 0` the root setup is the
  zero setup `(V, ⊥)`; `ϖ_0 = 0` alone does not force this: for `V = 𝔽_p[t^{1/p^∞}]/(t)` and
  `ϖ_n = t^{1/p^n}`, `ϖ_0 = 0` but `m = (t^{1/p^n} : n ≥ 1) ≠ 0` is an idempotent ideal of
  nilpotent elements, and `V` itself is not almost zero (`t^{1/p} • 1 ≠ 0`).

- `roots_test_quotients` — for a compatible root chain with `t₁ ∉ (t₀)`, `V/(t₀)` is not almost zero while `V/m` is.
- `roots_test_unit`, `roots_test_unit_initial`, `roots_test_zero`, `roots_test_nilpotent` —
  the all-one chain is classical, a unit initial term forces the unit ideal, the all-zero chain gives zero,
  and `t₀ = 0` with `t₁ ≠ 0` forces a nonzero root ideal.
- `roots_test_no_roots` — `(X)` in `𝔽_p[X]` is not idempotent.

`ofCompatibleRoots_isAlmostZero_iff`, `isIdempotentElem_span_roots`, `flat_tilde_span_roots`,
`flat_tilde_of_isFilteredPrincipal` (*filtered-principal-union-tilde-flat*),
`isAlmostZero_iff_tensor_eq_zero` (first clause of *almost-zero-iff-tilde-tensor-zero*).

### P0.3 the setup `(K°, K°°)` of a valuation ring

**The basic setup `(K°, K°°)` of a valuation ring with non-principal maximal ideal.**
(*valuation-ring-basic-setup*) Let `V` be a valuation ring (a domain in which the ideals are
totally ordered; Mathlib `ValuationRing V` with `IsDomain V`) whose maximal ideal `m` is not
finitely generated (equivalently not principal; for a rank-one valuation: the valuation is
nondiscrete, e.g. `V = K°` for a perfectoid field `K`). No completeness and no rank-one hypothesis is
needed. Then `(V, m)` is a basic setup: `m·m = m`, `m` is torsion-free hence flat, and `m̃ ≅ m`
([GR] §2.1, Example 2.1.2(i), p. 7; [Sch12] §4, Lemma 4.2 and its proof, p. 18). A `V`-module is
almost zero iff it is killed by `m`, iff it is a vector space over the residue field `k = V/m`; in
particular `k` is almost zero ([ECD] §3, Example 3.22(i), p. 19). This is the setup of [Sch12] §4.
Define `BasicSetup.ofValuationRing` (for `[ValuationRing V] [IsDomain V]` with
`¬ (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal V).FG`, the setup with ideal the maximal ideal); the ideal is `IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal V` by definition. Prove
`BasicSetup.isIdempotentElem_maximalIdeal_iff` (for a valuation domain which is not a field,
`maximalIdeal V ≠ ⊥ → (IsIdempotentElem (maximalIdeal V) ↔ ¬ (maximalIdeal V).FG)`; for a field
the maximal ideal `⊥` is idempotent and finitely generated, so the hypothesis is needed),
`BasicSetup.isIdempotentElem_maximalIdeal_of_not_fg` (the idempotence of a maximal ideal that is not
finitely generated, fields included), `BasicSetup.flat_tilde_maximalIdeal` (`m ⊗ m` is flat, `m`
being torsion-free), the statements of this README with no Lean declaration yet that
`IsAlmostZero M ↔ maximalIdeal V • ⊤ = ⊥`, that the residue field is almost zero, that
`Module.Flat V (maximalIdeal V)` with `tilde ≃ₗ maximalIdeal`, and that condition (A) holds, and
`BasicSetup.ofValuationRing_eq_ofCompatibleRoots` (equality with the root setup when `ϖ_0` is a nonzero element of the maximal ideal and every
element of that ideal is divisible by some `ϖ_n`; this is automatic in rank one since
`|ϖ_n| = |ϖ_0|^{1/p^n} → 1`;
for `ϖ` a unit the root ideal is `V` and for `ϖ = 0` it is `0`, neither the maximal ideal). *Needs:* P0.1; Mathlib `ValuationRing`,
`Module.Flat.flat_iff_torsion_eq_bot_of_isBezout`, `IsBezout`.

**Checks.**

- Computation: for `V = 𝒪_{ℂ_p}`: the residue field `𝔽̄_p`
  is almost zero, `V/pV` is not almost zero, and the ideal is the maximal ideal.
- Non-example: for `V = ℤ_p` the maximal ideal `pℤ_p` is
  finitely generated and `(pℤ_p)² ≠ pℤ_p`, so `ofValuationRing` does not apply; its hypothesis is
  necessary.
- For `V = ℤ_p`, multiplication `m ⊗_V m → m` has image `(p²)` and misses `p`.
  Both `m` and its tensor square are flat; multiplication identifies the tensor square with

- Degenerate: for `V` a field the maximal ideal is `0`,
  which is finitely generated; the construction does not apply, while the zero setup `(V, 0)` of

### P0.4 firm modules

**Firm modules: a small-hom model of the almost category.** (*firm-module-model*) Let `S = (V, m)`
be a basic setup (`m̃ = m ⊗_V m` flat; flatness is used for the exactness of `m̃ ⊗ −` and the closure
of firm modules under kernels), with `V : Type u` and `ModuleCat.{u} V`, so that `S.Firm : Type (u+1)`
with `Category.{u}`. A `V`-module `M` is firm if the multiplication map `m̃ ⊗_V M → M` is an
isomorphism; firm modules form a full subcategory `S.Firm` of `ModuleCat V`, closed under kernels,
cokernels and finite biproducts (hence abelian, with exact inclusion `j_!`). The functor
`j^* : ModuleCat V → S.Firm`, `M ↦ m̃ ⊗_V M`, is well defined (`m̃ ⊗ m̃ ≅ m̃`), exact, right adjoint to
`j_!`, and has a fully faithful right adjoint `j_* : N ↦ Hom_V(m̃, N)`; its kernel `{M : m̃ ⊗ M = 0}`
is exactly `S.almostZero` ([Bhatt] §4.1, Construction 4.1.5, pp. 18–19). By Mathlib's
`Abelian.isLocalization_isoModSerre_kernel_of_leftAdjoint`, `j^*` is a localization functor for the
almost isomorphisms `S.almostZero.isoModSerre`, which yields the instance
`MorphismProperty.HasLocalization.{u} S.almostZero.isoModSerre` whose localized category has
Hom-types in the universe `u` of the `V`-modules; the almost category of P0.5 is defined through it
([Bhatt] §4.1, Proposition 4.1.7(2) and proof, p. 21; [GR] §2.2, Proposition 2.2.21 and Corollary
2.2.22, p. 15). The categories `S.Firm` and `Almost.Module S` are equivalent; firm modules are the
modules of the form `M_!` (P0.6). Define `BasicSetup.IsFirm` (`Function.Bijective` of
`TensorProduct.lift (multiplication) : S.tilde ⊗[V] M → M`), `BasicSetup.Firm` (the full
subcategory on firm modules), `BasicSetup.firm` (the functor `ModuleCat V ⥤ S.Firm`,
`M ↦ S.tilde ⊗[V] M`), `BasicSetup.Firm.ι` (the inclusion, `j_!`) and `BasicSetup.closure`
(`N ↦ Hom_V(S.tilde, N)`, `j_*`); prove `BasicSetup.firmInclusionAdj` (`Firm.ι ⊣ S.firm`),
`BasicSetup.firmAdj` (`S.firm ⊣ S.closure`, with `S.closure` fully faithful), the kernel identity
`S.firm.kernel = S.almostZero`, `BasicSetup.hasLocalization` (the `HasLocalization.{u}` instance
with localized category `S.Firm`), firmness of `S.tilde` and
`BasicSetup.Firm.abelian` (`Abelian S.Firm`, kernels and cokernels computed in `ModuleCat V`).
*Needs:* P0.1; Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Abelian.isLocalization_isoModSerre_kernel_of_leftAdjoint`,
`CategoryTheory.MorphismProperty.HasLocalization`, `CategoryTheory.Functor.kernel`,
`ModuleCat.monoidalClosedHomEquiv`.

Two supporting results. `m̃ ⊗ m ≅ m̃` and `m̃ ⊗ m̃ ≅ m̃` (*tilde-ideal-idempotent*): for a basic setup
`S`, the map `m̃ ⊗_V m → m̃`, `x ⊗ y ⊗ z ↦ x ⊗ yz`, is an isomorphism, so the multiplication
`m̃ ⊗_V m̃ → m̃` is an isomorphism (`m̃` is an idempotent `V`-module); for every `k ≥ 2` the symmetric
group `S_k` acts trivially on `⊗^k_V m`, in particular `x ⊗ y = y ⊗ x` in `m̃` ([GR] §2.1, Claim
2.1.10 and its proof, p. 9); for the classical setup this is the multiplication `V ⊗ V ⊗ V ≅ V ⊗ V`,
and for a root setup with `ϖ` a nonzerodivisor it is `m ⊗ m ≅ m` (Mathlib `TensorProduct.comm`).
Almost zero modules form a Serre class (*almost-zero-serre-class*): the property `S.almostZero` of
`V`-modules is a Serre class in the abelian category `ModuleCat V` (Mathlib
`ObjectProperty.IsSerreClass`), containing `0` and closed under submodules, quotients and
extensions, and it is a tensor ideal: `M` almost zero implies `M ⊗_V N`, `Hom_V(M, N)` and
`Hom_V(N, M)` almost zero for all `N`; only `m·m = m` is used ([Sch12] §4, Lemma 4.2 with proof,
p. 18; [GR] §2.2, (2.2.2), p. 11; [Berkeley] Lecture 7, §7.4, after Example 7.4.2, p. 52; [AWS] §2.9,
Definition 2.9.4, p. 73). For `V = 𝒪_{ℂ_p}`, `V/m² = V/m = k`, consistent with idempotence, whereas
for `ℤ_p` the module `ℤ/p²` is an extension of almost zero modules not killed by `(p)`; Mathlib's
`SerreClassLocalization` API applies to `S.almostZero` (Mathlib
`CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.IsSerreClass`, `CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.IsClosedUnderExtensions`).

**Checks.**

- `firm_test_tilde` (computation) — `S.tilde` is firm and
  `S.firm.obj (ModuleCat.of V V) ≅ S.tilde`.
- Non-example: if `S.ideal ≠ ⊤` then `ModuleCat.of V V` is
  not firm (the image of `m̃ ⊗ V → V` is `m`); and the tempting condition `m·M = M` does not
  characterise firm modules: for `R = 𝔽_p[t^{1/p^∞}]`, `I = (t^{1/p^∞})` and `M` the maximal ideal of
  `R/t`, `IM = M` but `I ⊗ M → M` is not injective ([Bhatt] Warning 4.1.6).
- `firm_test_classical` (degenerate) — for `S = classical V` every `V`-module is firm and
  `S.firm ⋙ BasicSetup.Firm.ι S ≅ 𝟭 (ModuleCat V)`; the composite
  `S.firm ⋙ S.closure` is also naturally isomorphic to the identity.
- Compatibility: `S.firm` satisfies the hypotheses of
  Mathlib's `Abelian.isLocalization_isoModSerre_kernel_of_leftAdjoint`; hence `S.Firm` is equivalent
  to Mathlib's constructed localization `S.almostZero.isoModSerre.Localization` (via
  `Localization.uniq`).

- `firm_test_tilde`, `firm_test_classical`, `firm_test_proper_ideal`, `firm_test_zero_setup` —
  the tensor ideal is firm, every classical module is firm, the ring fails to be firm for a proper
  setup ideal, and in the zero setup firmness means the module is zero. These check `IsFirm` and
  the full-subcategory object property together.
- `firmFunctor_test_classical`, `firmFunctor_test_zero_setup`, `firmFunctor_test_residue` —
  after inclusion, `firm` recovers a classical module, sends every module to zero in the zero
  setup, and kills `V/m`. The composite with `closure` has the same three values.
- `tildeAct_test_two_terms` — on `(ℤ, ℤ)`, `(2 ⊗ 3) ⊗ 5 + (7 ⊗ 11) ⊗ 13` acts as `1031`;
  `tildeAct_test_zero` gives the zero map for `m = 0`, and `tildeAct_test_unit` computes
  `(1 ⊗ 1) ⊗ 1 ↦ 1` over `(ℤ, ℤ)`. These fix the scalar-action convention.
- `firmAdj_test_zero`, `firmAdj_test_classical_identity`, `firmAdj_test_two_terms` — the
  tensor–Hom adjunction sends zero to zero, sends the identity of the classical firmification
  of `ℤ` to a nonzero map, and sends `2f + 3f` to five times the image of `f`.

- `tildeEquiv_test_zero`, `tildeEquiv_test_unit`, `tildeEquiv_test_two_terms` —
  the map `m̃ ⊗ m → m̃`, `(x ⊗ y) ⊗ z ↦ x ⊗ yz`, is zero on the zero setup,
  sends `(1 ⊗ 1) ⊗ 1` to `1 ⊗ 1` classically, and after multiplication sends
  `(2 ⊗ 3) ⊗ 5 + (7 ⊗ 11) ⊗ 13` to `1031`.

Lean: `BasicSetup.almostZero_isSerreClass` (*almost-zero-serre-class*) and
`BasicSetup.isAlmostIso_iff_isoModSerre` (the almost isomorphisms are the morphisms
`S.almostZero.isoModSerre` that the Serre quotient inverts). The firm-module model is specified in
this README only.

### P0.5 almost modules

The almost modules themselves come next: the Serre quotient, almost elements and `M_!`, the
monoidal structure, almost algebras and `B_!!`, the finiteness, flatness and projectivity notions,
duals and traces, and the rank decomposition.

**Almost modules over a basic setup: the Serre quotient `V^a-Mod`.**
(*almost-modules-over-perfectoid-base*) For a basic setup `S = (V, m)` (`m·m = m` and `m̃` flat; no
valuation and no perfectoid field), the category of almost `V`-modules `V^a-Mod := Almost.Module S`
is the localization of `ModuleCat V` at the almost isomorphisms `S.almostZero.isoModSerre` (maps with
almost zero kernel and cokernel), i.e. the Serre quotient of `V`-modules by the almost zero modules,
realised with Mathlib's Serre-class localization: the carrier is `MorphismProperty.Localization'`
for the `HasLocalization.{u}` instance of P0.4, so Hom-types are `V`-modules in the universe of
`V`-modules ([Sch12] §4, Definition 4.3, p. 18; [GR] §2.2, (2.2.2), p. 11). The localization functor
`M ↦ M^a` (`Almost.toAlmost S`) is exact and essentially surjective; `M^a ≅ 0` iff `M` is almost
zero; `f^a` is an isomorphism iff `f` is an almost isomorphism; `V^a-Mod` is abelian (Mathlib
`SerreClassLocalization.abelian`); a functor `G` out of `V^a-Mod` to an abelian category is exact
iff `G ∘ (−)^a` is, and an exact functor out of `ModuleCat V` factors (uniquely up to unique
isomorphism) through `(−)^a` iff it kills almost zero modules. For a perfectoid field `K` and
`S = (K°, K°°)` this is Scholze's `K°a-mod`; for a perfectoid Tate ring `R`, layer P1 instantiates
`S` with `(R°, R°°)` and `(R⁺, root ideal)` ([ECD] §3, Definition 3.21, p. 19; [KL15] §5.5,
Definition 5.5.8, p. 132, for uniform Banach algebras with enough topologically nilpotent units). All
almost-vanishing statements in consumers ("`H^i(X, O⁺)` is almost zero", "`R⁺/ϖ` is almost the
equalizer") are statements in this category. Define `Almost.Module` (`S.almostZero.isoModSerre.Localization'`
for the firm-model instance, a category with Hom-types in `Type u`), `Almost.toAlmost` (the
localization functor `ModuleCat V ⥤ Almost.Module S`) and `Almost.Module.homModule` (the `V`-module
structure on Hom-types, via *almost-hom-formula*, with no nonzero almost zero elements); prove that
`(toAlmost S).IsLocalization S.almostZero.isoModSerre`, `Almost.Module.instAbelian`, that
`toAlmost S` preserves finite limits and finite colimits, that
`IsZero ((toAlmost S).obj M) ↔ S.IsAlmostZero M`, that
`IsIso ((toAlmost S).map f) ↔ S.IsAlmostIso f.hom` (whose module-level half is the Lean
`BasicSetup.isAlmostIso_iff_isoModSerre`), that `toAlmost S` is essentially surjective (every almost
module is some `M^a`, with `M = N_*`), that `G` is exact iff `toAlmost S ⋙ G` is exact, and
`Almost.Module.classicalEquiv` (for `S = classical V`, `ModuleCat V ≌ Almost.Module S`).
For an exact `F : ModuleCat V ⥤ D` with `D` abelian, use Mathlib's
`ObjectProperty.isoModSerre_isInvertedBy_iff` to express killing almost zero modules as
inverting `S.almostZero.isoModSerre`. Then
`SerreClassLocalization.essImage_whiskeringLeft`, applied to `Almost.toAlmost S`, supplies
an exact `G : Almost.Module S ⥤ D` with `F ≅ toAlmost S ⋙ G`;
`SerreClassLocalization.fullyFaithfulWhiskeringLeft` gives the unique comparison
isomorphism compatible with these factorizations. *Needs:* *almost-zero-serre-class* (P0.4); P0.4; Mathlib
`CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.isoModSerre`, `CategoryTheory.MorphismProperty.Localization'`,
`SerreClassLocalization.abelian`, `SerreClassLocalization.isZero_obj_iff`,
`SerreClassLocalization.isIso_map_iff`, `SerreClassLocalization.preservesFiniteLimits`,
`SerreClassLocalization.preservesFiniteColimits`, `SerreClassLocalization.exactFunctor_comp_iff`,
`SerreClassLocalization.essImage_whiskeringLeft`.

**Checks.**

- `Almost.Module.test_residue_field` (computation) — for `S = ofValuationRing 𝒪_{ℂ_p}`:
  `(toAlmost S).obj (ModuleCat.of V (IsLocalRing.ResidueField V))` is a zero object, while
  `(toAlmost S).obj (ModuleCat.of V (V ⧸ Ideal.span {p}))` is not.
- `Almost.Module.almostModule_test_classical` (compatibility) — for `S = classical V`, `toAlmost S` is an
  equivalence of categories `ModuleCat V ≌ Almost.Module S` (every almost isomorphism is an
  isomorphism).
- `Almost.Module.almostModule_test_zero_setup` (degenerate) — for the setup `(V, ⊥)` every object of
  `Almost.Module S` is a zero object.
- `Almost.Module.test_not_projective` (non-example) — for `S = (K°, K°°)`, `K` the completion of
  `ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞})`: `V^a` is not a projective object of `Almost.Module S` (`Hom(V^a, −)` does not
  preserve the epimorphism `K°a → (K°/ϖ)^a` on Hom-sets, [Sch12] Remark 4.8); so "projective" in the
  categorical sense is not the notion used for almost modules.
- `Almost.Module.test_hom_formula` (characterisation) — for `V`-modules `M, N`:
  `(toAlmost S).obj M ⟶ (toAlmost S).obj N` is `V`-linearly isomorphic to `S.tilde ⊗[V] M →ₗ[V] N`;
  with `M = V` and `N = K°/ϖ` over `(K°, K°°)` this is `Hom(K°°, K°/ϖ)`.
  The canonical map from `K°/ϖ` need not be surjective ([Sch12] Remark 4.8).

- `almostModule_test_classical` — almostifying and then taking almost elements recovers every classical module.
- `almostModule_test_zero_setup` — every object of the quotient is zero for `m = 0`.
- `almostModule_test_residue` — the almostification of `V/m` is zero for every setup.
- `almostModule_test_classical_nonzero` — the almostification of `ℤ` in the classical setup is nonzero.

The category `Almost.Module S` is specified in this README only; the Lean file carries its input,
the Serre class `BasicSetup.almostZero_isSerreClass` of P0.4, together with
`BasicSetup.isAlmostIso_iff_isoModSerre`.

### P0.6 almost elements and the left adjoint

**Almost elements `M_*` and the left adjoint `M_!` of almostification.** (*almost-hom-and-adjoints*)
For a basic setup `S = (V, m)` (`m̃` flat is used for the exactness of `(−)_!`): (i) the functor of
almost elements `(−)_* : Almost.Module S → ModuleCat V`, `M_* := Hom_{V^a}(V^a, M)` with its
`V`-module structure, is right adjoint to `M ↦ M^a`, with counit `(M_*)^a → M` an isomorphism (so
`(−)_*` is fully faithful) and `(N^a)_* ≅ Hom_V(m̃, N)` naturally ([GR] §2.2, Proposition
2.2.13(ii)-(iii), p. 14); (ii) `(−)_! : Almost.Module S → ModuleCat V`, `M_! := m̃ ⊗_V M_*`, is left
adjoint to `M ↦ M^a` with unit `M → (M_!)^a` an isomorphism (so `(−)_!` is fully faithful), and it
is exact because `m̃` is flat ([GR] §2.2, Proposition 2.2.21, p. 15); (iii) for every `V`-module `N`
the unit `N → (N^a)_*` and the natural map `(N^a)_! → N` are almost isomorphisms, and `M_! → M_*` is
an almost isomorphism ([GR] §2.2, (2.2.9), p. 13); (iv) `(−)^a` preserves all limits and colimits,
`(−)_*` preserves limits and injective objects (not infinite direct sums), `(−)_!` preserves
colimits and tensor products; `Almost.Module S` is complete, cocomplete, satisfies AB5, has the
generator `V^a` and enough injectives ([GR] §2.2, Corollary 2.2.15, p. 14); (v) preimages of almost
elements exist only up to `m`: for an epimorphism `φ : M_1 → M_2`, `x ∈ (M_2)_*` and `ε ∈ m` there
is `y ∈ (M_1)_*` with `φ_*(y) = ε·x` ([GR] §2.2, Remark 2.2.14(ii), p. 14; [Sch12] §4, Proposition
4.6, p. 19, for `(K°, K°°)`). Define `Almost.Module.elements` (`M ↦ M_* = (V^a ⟶ M)`),
`Almost.Module.shriek` (`M ↦ M_! = S.tilde ⊗[V] M.elements`) and `Almost.Module.shriekToElements`
(the natural transformation `shriek ⟶ elements`, an almost isomorphism objectwise); prove
`Almost.Module.adjElements` (`toAlmost S ⊣ elements S`), `Almost.Module.elements_counit_isIso`
(`(M.elements)^a ≅ M`, natural; `elements` is fully faithful), `Almost.Module.elementsToAlmostIso`
(`((toAlmost S).obj N).elements ≅ ModuleCat.of V (S.tilde →ₗ[V] N)`, natural in `N`),
`Almost.Module.adjShriek` (`shriek S ⊣ toAlmost S`), `Almost.Module.shriek_unit_isIso`
(`M ≅ (M.shriek)^a`), `Almost.Module.shriek_preservesFiniteLimits` (`shriek` is exact),
the statement that the unit `N → ((toAlmost S).obj N).elements` is an almost isomorphism,
`Almost.Module.enoughInjectives` (`elements` and `toAlmost` preserve injectives),
`Almost.Module.hasLimits` (all limits and colimits, AB5, preserved by `toAlmost`) and
`Almost.Module.exists_elements_lift_smul` (for an epimorphism `φ`, `x : M₂.elements` and
`ε ∈ S.ideal`, `∃ y, φ.elements y = ε • x`). *Needs:* P0.5; Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Adjunction`,
`ModuleCat.monoidalClosedHomEquiv`.

For every basic setup `S` and `M : Almost.Module S`, the firm representative is
identified with `m̃ ⊗ M_*` by `Almost.Module.shriekIsoTensor`. Its inverse is the
tensor–Hom evaluation map: `Almost.Module.shriekIsoTensor_inv_apply` states
`t ⊗ f ↦ f(t)` for `t : S.tilde` and `f : M_*`. This fixes the comparison on
every pure tensor. `Almost.Module.shriekToElements_apply` then states
`shriekToElements (f(t)) = tildeMul(t) • f`; in particular, for `t = x ⊗ y`
with `x, y ∈ m`, the scalar is `xy`. These are the firm-model formulas for
[GR] §2.2, (2.2.9), p. 13, and (2.2.20), Proposition 2.2.21, p. 15.

Supporting result: `Hom(M^a, N^a) = Hom_V(m̃ ⊗ M, N)` (*almost-hom-formula*). For a basic setup `S`
and `V`-modules `M, N` there is a natural `V`-linear bijection
`Hom_{Almost.Module S}(M^a, N^a) ≅ Hom_V(m̃ ⊗_V M, N)`; in particular Hom-types of `Almost.Module S`
are `V`-modules, functorially in both variables, and contain no nonzero almost zero elements (if
`m·f = 0` then `f = 0`, stated as `Almost.Module.hom_eq_zero_of_ideal_smul` for
any `f : M ⟶ N` with `∀ ε ∈ S.ideal, ε • f = 0`); with `M = V`, `Hom(V^a, N^a) ≅ Hom_V(m̃, N)` ([GR] §2.2, (2.2.4) and the
text after it, p. 12; [Sch12] §4, Proposition 4.4, p. 18). For `S = (K°, K°°)`, `M = K°`,
`N = K°/ϖ` this is `Hom(K°a, (K°/ϖ)^a) = Hom_{K°}(K°°, K°/ϖ)` ([Sch12] Proposition 4.4 and Remark
4.8), proved with Mathlib `ModuleCat.monoidalClosedHomEquiv`.

`Almost.Module.homLinearEquiv_apply` fixes this bijection for every basic setup `S`
and ordinary `V`-modules `M, N`: almostifying the linear representative of `f`
gives `toAlmost.map (S.tildeAct M) ≫ f`, where `tildeAct` sends
`(x ⊗ y) ⊗ z` to `(xy) • z`. This equation characterises the representative.
`Almost.Module.homLinearEquiv_natural` states compatibility with precomposition
by `a : M′ → M` and postcomposition by `b : N → N′`: the representative becomes
`b ∘ homLinearEquiv(f) ∘ (id ⊗ a)`. Both formulas use [GR] (2.2.4), p. 12.

**Checks.**

The three discriminating Checks for `homLinearEquiv` are `homLinearEquiv_zero_setup`,
`homLinearEquiv_two_terms` and `homLinearEquiv_residue_nonexample`, using [GR] (2.2.4),
p. 12. When `S.ideal = ⊥`, every almost map has zero representative and its tensor
source is zero. Over the classical setup on `ℤ`, the displayed two-term tensor has
image `1031`. When `S.ideal ≠ ⊤`, the ordinary identity of `V/S.ideal` is nonzero,
but the representative of its almost identity is zero: this comparison does not
recover ordinary Hom without almostification.

- `homLinearEquiv_zero` (supplementary) — the zero almost map has zero linear representative.
- `homLinearEquiv_identity` — the identity of `M^a` has representative `S.tildeAct M`.
- `homLinearEquiv_two_terms` — over the classical setup on `ℤ`, the representative
  of the almostified identity sends `(2 ⊗ 3) ⊗ 5 + (7 ⊗ 11) ⊗ 13` to `1031`.

- `Almost.Module.elements_test_valuation` (computation) — for `S = ofValuationRing K°` and
  `N = K°°`: `((toAlmost S).obj N).elements ≅ K°` (every `x ∈ K` with `εx ∈ K°°` for all `ε ∈ K°°`
  lies in `K°`).
- `Almost.Module.elements_test_not_identity` (non-example) — for `S = ofValuationRing K°` (`K` the
  completion of `ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞})`) the unit `K°/ϖ → ((K°/ϖ)^a)_* = Hom(K°°, K°/ϖ)` is injective but
  not surjective ([Sch12] Remark 4.8): almost elements of `N^a` are not elements of `N`. Computed
  witness: set `ϖ = p` and choose compatible roots in `K`. Write
  `K°° = ⋃_n p^{1/p^n}K°`. The compatible residues
  `c_n = Σ_{j<n} p^{1−1/p^j} mod p^{1−1/p^n}` define an almost element.
  If it came from `c ∈ K°`, choose `b ∈ ℚ_p(p^{1/p^N})` with `v_p(c−b) > 1`.
  For `n > N`, compatibility forces `v_p(b−c_n) = 1−1/p^n`, since the next term has this
  valuation. But `b−c_n ∈ ℚ_p(p^{1/p^{n−1}})` has valuation in `p^{−(n−1)}ℤ`, a contradiction.
  This uses the indicated completion; nonconvergence of the displayed sum alone would not suffice.
- `Almost.Module.almostModule_test_classical` (degenerate) — for `S = classical V`:
  `M.elements ≅ M.shriek` and both are inverse to `toAlmost`.
- `Almost.Module.shriek_test_tilde` (compatibility) — `(V^a).shriek ≅ S.tilde` and
  `(N^a).shriek ≅ S.tilde ⊗[V] N`, compatible with Mathlib's tensor product of modules; the map
  `shriek → elements` is induced by `S.tilde → V`.

- `adjunction_test_zero` — both adjunctions send the zero map to the zero map.
- `adjunction_test_classical_identity` — the almostification/elements adjunction sends the identity of the almostified classical `ℤ` to a nonzero map.
- `adjunction_test_two_terms` — its Hom equivalence sends `2f + 3f` to five times the image of `f`, fixing its linearity convention.
- `shriekIsoTensor_zero` — inverse evaluation sends the zero tensor to zero.
- `shriekIsoTensor_two_terms` — inverse evaluation sends `t ⊗ f + u ⊗ g` to `f(t) + g(u)`.
- `shriekIsoTensor_not_negated` — if `f(t) ≠ −f(t)`, the inverse comparison cannot send `t ⊗ f` to `−f(t)`.
- `shriekToElements_zero` — the comparison sends zero to zero.
- `shriekToElements_two_terms` — it sends `f(t) + g(u)` to `tildeMul(t) • f + tildeMul(u) • g`.
- `shriekToElements_classical_unit` — for `(ℚ, ℚ)`, evaluation at `1 ⊗ 1` is sent back to `f`, fixing the scalar as `+1`.
- `shriekToElements_classical_two_terms` — for `(ℚ, ℚ)`, the image of `f(2 ⊗ 3) + f(5 ⊗ 7)` is `41 • f`.

### P0.7 the closed symmetric monoidal structure

**The closed symmetric monoidal structure on almost modules.** (*almost-tensor-and-internal-hom*)
For a basic setup `S = (V, m)`, `Almost.Module S` carries the symmetric monoidal structure localized
from `ModuleCat V` (Mathlib `LocalizedMonoidal` for the monoidal class of almost isomorphisms,
*almost-isomorphisms-are-monoidal*), with unit `V^a` (`≅ m^a`): the localization functor `M ↦ M^a`
is symmetric monoidal, `M^a ⊗ N^a ≅ (M ⊗_V N)^a`, and `M ⊗ N ≅ (M_* ⊗_V N_*)^a ≅ (M_! ⊗_V N_!)^a`
([Sch12] §4, Proposition 4.5, p. 19; [GR] §2.2, (2.2.11), p. 13). The tensor product is right exact
in each variable. The internal hom is `alHom(M, N) := (Hom_{V^a}(M, N))^a`, the almostification of
the `V`-module of *almost-hom-formula*; there is a natural isomorphism
`Hom(L ⊗ M, N) ≅ Hom(L, alHom(M, N))`, so `Almost.Module S` is closed, and
`alHom(M^a, N^a) ≅ (Hom_V(m̃ ⊗ M, N))^a` ([GR] §2.2, (2.2.10)-(2.2.11), p. 13). The functor `(−)_!`
preserves nonempty tensor products, `(M ⊗ N)_! ≅ M_! ⊗_V N_!`, but not the unit (see the next
paragraph), and `(−)_*` is lax symmetric monoidal ([GR] §2.4, Proposition 2.4.35, p. 29). Define `Almost.Module.alHom`
(`alHom M N := (toAlmost S).obj (ModuleCat.of V (M ⟶ N))`); prove that
`S.almostZero.isoModSerre.IsMonoidal`, `CategoryTheory.Localization.Monoidal.instMonoidalCategoryLocalizedMonoidal` (the localized monoidal
structure; `Almost.Module S` is defined as the `LocalizedMonoidal` type synonym),
`CategoryTheory.Localization.Monoidal.instSymmetricCategoryLocalizedMonoidal`, `Almost.toAlmostMonoidal` (`(toAlmost S).Monoidal`, with
`μ : M^a ⊗ N^a ≅ (M ⊗ N)^a` and `ε : 𝟙_ ≅ V^a`), `Almost.Module.tensorIsoElements`
(`M ⊗ N ≅ (toAlmost S).obj (M.elements ⊗ N.elements)`), `Almost.Module.monoidalClosed`
(`ihom M = alHom M −`), `Almost.Module.alHom_toAlmost`
(`alHom (M^a) (N^a) ≅ (toAlmost S).obj (ModuleCat.of V (S.tilde ⊗[V] M →ₗ[V] N))`),
`Almost.Module.shriekTensorIso` (`(M ⊗ N).shriek ≅ M.shriek ⊗ N.shriek`, the tensor comparison of
the oplax structure below),
`Almost.Module.elementsLaxMonoidal` and `Almost.Module.tensor_preservesFiniteColimits` (`tensorLeft M`
and `tensorRight M` preserve finite colimits). *Needs:* *almost-hom-formula* (P0.6); P0.6; Mathlib
`CategoryTheory.LocalizedMonoidal`, `CategoryTheory.Localization.Monoidal.toMonoidalCategory`,
`ModuleCat.monoidalCategory`, `ModuleCat.monoidalClosedHomEquiv`, `CategoryTheory.Functor.LaxMonoidal`.

**The left adjoint `(−)_!` is not unital.** Since `N → (N^a)_*` is an almost isomorphism (P0.6) and
`m̃ ⊗ −` inverts almost isomorphisms (P0.1), `(N^a)_! ≅ m̃ ⊗_V N`; in particular `(V^a)_! ≅ m̃`, not
`V` ([GR] §2.2, (2.2.20)–(2.2.24) and Proposition 2.2.21, p. 15). As the left adjoint of the strong
monoidal functor `(−)^a`, the functor `(−)_! : Almost.Module S → ModuleCat V` is oplax monoidal: its
tensor comparison `(M ⊗ N)_! → M_! ⊗_V N_!` is an isomorphism, because `m̃ ⊗ m̃ ≅ m̃`
(*tilde-ideal-idempotent*, P0.4), and its unit comparison is `(V^a)_! ≅ m̃ → V`, the multiplication
`tildeMul`, which is an isomorphism exactly when `m = V`. No strong monoidal functor
`Almost.Module S → ModuleCat V` is asserted. The strong monoidal statement has a different target:
`(−)_!` is a strong monoidal equivalence onto the category `S.Firm` of firm modules of P0.4, with
tensor product `⊗_V` and unit `m̃` ([Bhatt] §4.1, Construction 4.1.5 and Proposition 4.1.7, pp.
18–21). The missing unit is why P0.9 needs the unitisation `B_!!`: for an almost algebra `B`, `B_!`
is only a non-unital algebra.

Supporting result: almost isomorphisms are stable under tensor products
(*almost-isomorphisms-are-monoidal*). For a basic setup `S`, the class `S.almostZero.isoModSerre`
of almost isomorphisms is multiplicative, and for every `V`-module `X` and almost isomorphism `f`
the maps `X ⊗ f` and `f ⊗ X` are almost isomorphisms; that is, it is a monoidal morphism property
for Mathlib's monoidal structure on `ModuleCat V` (`MorphismProperty.IsMonoidal`); equivalently,
almost zero modules form a tensor ideal ([GR] §2.2, (2.2.5), p. 12; [Bhatt] §4.1, Proposition
4.1.7(3), p. 20). For `f : m ↪ V` and `X = V/m`, `X ⊗ f : m/m² = 0 → V/m` has almost zero cokernel
`V/m`, as predicted (Mathlib `CategoryTheory.MorphismProperty.IsMonoidal`, `ModuleCat.monoidalCategory`).

**Checks.**

- `Almost.Module.tensor_test_residue` (computation) — for `S = ofValuationRing K°`:
  `(toAlmost S).obj k ⊗ X ≅ 0` for every `X`, and
  `(toAlmost S).obj K°° ⊗ (toAlmost S).obj K°° ≅ 𝟙_ (Almost.Module S)`.
- `Almost.Module.tensor_test_unit` (degenerate) —
  `𝟙_ (Almost.Module S) ≅ (toAlmost S).obj (ModuleCat.of V V) ≅ (toAlmost S).obj (ModuleCat.of V S.ideal)`.
- `Almost.Module.tensor_test_mathlib` (compatibility) — `toAlmost S` is a symmetric monoidal functor
  out of Mathlib's `ModuleCat.monoidalCategory`; for `S = classical V` the equivalence
  `Almost.Module.classicalEquiv` is monoidal.
- `Almost.Module.tensor_test_unit_ideal` (non-example) — for a proper ideal `m ≠ V`, in `ModuleCat V` the ideal `m` is not a
  tensor unit (`m ⊗_V V/m = m/m² = 0 ≠ V/m`), whereas `m^a ≅ 𝟙_` in `Almost.Module S`; the unit
  isomorphism only exists after almostification.

- `alHom_test_classical_rank_one` — the almost elements of `alHom(V^a, V^a)` are linearly equivalent to `V` in the classical setup for every commutative ring `V`.
- `alHom_test_zero_source` — internal Hom out of a zero object is zero.
- `alHom_test_residue_target` — internal Hom into `(V/m)^a` is zero.
- `tensor_test_classical_two_terms` — classically, the tensor product of two free modules of rank two is free of rank four.
- `tensor_test_residue` — `(V/m)^a ⊗ M` is zero.
- `tensor_test_unit_ideal` — `m^a` is isomorphic to the tensor unit, including the zero setup.
- Zero setup (negative control for unitality): for `(V, 0)` on a nonzero ring such as `ℤ`, `m̃ = 0`,
  so `(V^a)_! = 0 ≇ V` and the unit comparison `m̃ → V` is not surjective; every module is almost
  zero for this setup.
- Classical setup (positive control): for `m = V`, `m̃ → V` is bijective and `(−)_!` is strong
  monoidal into `ModuleCat V`.

Lean: `BasicSetup.zero` and `BasicSetup.tildeMul`; the Lean `example`s for the zero setup check
`(zero V).ideal = ⊥`, that every module is almost zero, that `(zero V).tilde` is a subsingleton,
and that `(zero V).tildeMul` is not surjective when `V` is nontrivial. The monoidal structure on
`Almost.Module S` is specified in this README only.

### P0.8 almost algebras

**Almost algebras (commutative monoids in `V^a-Mod`) and their modules.** (*almost-algebras*) For a
basic setup `S = (V, m)`, an almost `V`-algebra is a commutative unital monoid object in the
symmetric monoidal category `Almost.Module S`: `Almost.Algebra S := CommMon (Almost.Module S)`
(Mathlib), with monoid morphisms ([GR] §2.2, (2.2.5), p. 12). For an almost algebra `A`,
`A_* = Hom(V^a, A)` is a commutative `V`-algebra (`a·b := μ ∘ (a ⊗ b) ∘ ν⁻¹`); `R ↦ R^a` from
commutative `V`-algebras to almost algebras is left adjoint to `A ↦ A_*`, with counit
`A ≅ (A_*)^a`, so `(−)_*` is fully faithful and `Hom_{Alg}(A, B) ≅ Hom_{V-alg}(A_*, B_*)`; every
almost algebra is `R^a` for `R = A_*` ([Sch12] §4, after Proposition 4.6, p. 19; [Bhatt] §4.2,
Remark 4.2.8, p. 25). An `A`-module is a module object over `A` (Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Mod`);
`A`-modules form an abelian, complete and cocomplete category `A-Mod`, closed symmetric monoidal
with `M ⊗_A N := (M_* ⊗_{A_*} N_*)^a`, and `A-Mod ≃ Almost.Module (S.baseChange A_*)`
by *change-of-basic-setup* (P0.16). An `A`-algebra is a morphism `A → B`. Convention:
module-theoretic notions for `A`-modules (flat, almost projective, almost finitely generated and
presented) are those of P0.11 and P0.10, evaluated through this equivalence on the `A_*`-module
`M_*`. Limits are computed on almost elements, `(lim D)_* ≅ lim D_*`. Colimits are almostified
last: `colim D ≅ (colim D_*)^a`, so free modules `((A_*)^{(I)})^a`, quotients and pushouts are `(−)^a`
of the corresponding constructions on almost elements ([GR] §2.2, Corollary 2.2.15 and 2.2.18, p.
14). The functor `(−)_*` preserves neither colimits nor epimorphisms: an almost element of the
target of an epimorphism lifts only after multiplication by an arbitrary `ε ∈ m` ([GR] §2.2, Remarks
2.2.14(ii) and 2.2.28(i), pp. 14–16), so no exactness or colimit-preservation statement is made for
`(−)_*`. Define `Almost.Algebra` (`CommMon (Almost.Module S)`), `Almost.Algebra.toAlmost`
(`CommAlgCat V ⥤ Almost.Algebra S`, `R ↦ R^a`), `Almost.Algebra.elements` (`A ↦ A_*`),
`Almost.Algebra.ModuleCat` (`A-Mod := CategoryTheory.Mod (Almost.Module S) A.X`),
`Almost.Algebra.free` (the free `A`-module `A^{(I)} := ((A_*)^{(I)})^a`, left adjoint to
`M ↦ (M_* as a set)`, [GR] 2.2.18), `Almost.Algebra.quotient` (for an ideal `I ↪ A`, the almost
algebra `A/I` with `A → A/I` an epimorphism), `Almost.Algebra.prod` (finite products with
`(A₁ × A₂)_* = A₁_* × A₂_*` and `A-Mod` decomposing accordingly) and `Almost.Algebra.tensor`
(pushouts `B ⊗_A C ≅ ((B_* ⊗_{A_*} C_*))^a`); prove `Almost.Algebra.adj` (`toAlmost S ⊣ elements S`),
`Almost.Algebra.counitIso` (`(A.elements)^a ≅ A`; `elements` fully faithful),
`Almost.Algebra.homEquiv` (`(A ⟶ B) ≃ (A.elements →ₐ[V] B.elements)`),
`Almost.Algebra.moduleEquiv` (`A-Mod ≌ Almost.Module (S.baseChange A.elements)`) and
`Almost.Algebra.monoidalCategory` (the closed symmetric monoidal structure on `A-Mod`). *Needs:*
P0.7 for the categories and algebra adjunction; Mathlib `CategoryTheory.CommMon`, `CategoryTheory.Mod`,
`CategoryTheory.MonObj`, `CategoryTheory.IsCommMonObj`. The declaration `moduleEquiv`, its
action and forgetful comparisons, and the closed monoidal structure use
*change-of-basic-setup* (P0.16), whose module categories and algebra adjunction are constructed here.

For every basic setup `S` and almost algebra `A`,
`Almost.Algebra.moduleEquiv_elements_action` identifies the almost elements of
`moduleEquiv.functor.obj M` naturally with `Hom(V^a, M.X)` as additive groups,
with the `A_*` action given by
`e_M(a • m) = γ_M ∘ (elementsHomEquiv(a) ⊗ e_M(m)) ∘ λ⁻¹`.
Here `γ_M : A.X ⊗ M.X → M.X` is the internal module action; naturality is the
equation `e_N(F(f)(m)) = f.hom ∘ e_M(m)` for every `A`-module morphism `f`.
These equations give an `A_*`-linear natural comparison with the almost-element
module constructed from the internal action ([GR] (2.2.8), p. 13; Remark 2.2.12
and Proposition 2.2.13, p. 14).
`Almost.Algebra.moduleEquiv_functor_forget` gives a natural isomorphism from
`moduleEquiv.functor`, followed by almost elements over `A_*`, restriction of
scalars along `V → A_*`, and almostification over `S`, to `Mod.forget A.X`.
Thus the comparison recovers the underlying almost module on objects and on
morphisms, compatibly with Mathlib's restriction of scalars ([GR] Remark 2.2.12
and Proposition 2.2.13, p. 14).

**Checks.**

For `moduleEquiv`, the following Checks use independently specified module objects,
with the comparison of [GR] Remark 2.2.12 and Proposition 2.2.13, p. 14:

- `moduleEquiv_zero_setup` — if `S.ideal = ⊥`, the image of every `A`-module is zero
  and `A_*` is the zero ring.
- `moduleEquiv_regular_dualNumbers` — for the classical setup on `ℚ` and
  `A = (ℚ[ε]/ε²)^a`, apply the equivalence to Mathlib's `Mod.regular A.X`.
  Taking almost elements and restricting scalars to `ℚ` gives dimension `2`.
- `moduleEquiv_nonunit` — for the classical setup on `ℤ` and `A = ℤ^a`, the
  transported multiplication-by-two endomorphism of `Mod.regular A.X` is not an
  isomorphism. Almostification here does not invert the nonunit `2`.
- `moduleEquiv_evaluation_one` — for the classical setup on `ℚ`, restrict the
  regular module of `ℚ^a` along the almostification of evaluation
  `ℚ[T] → ℚ`, `T ↦ 1`. On the almost elements of its image under `moduleEquiv`,
  the scalar coming from `T` through the algebra adjunction unit acts as the
  identity. There is a nonzero element on which it does not act by negation,
  distinguishing this module from evaluation at `T = −1`.

- `Almost.Algebra.test_mod_varpi` (computation) — for `S = ofValuationRing K°`, with
  `K = ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞})^` and `ϖ = p`: `A := (toAlmost S).obj (K° ⧸ ϖ)` is an almost algebra and
  `A.elements ≅ Hom_{K°}(K°°, K°/ϖ) ⊋ K°/ϖ`.
- `Almost.Algebra.algebra_test_classical` (degenerate) — for `S = classical V`, `Almost.Algebra.toAlmost` is
  an equivalence `CommAlgCat V ≌ Almost.Algebra S`.
- `Almost.Algebra.test_modules` (compatibility) — for a `V`-algebra `R`: modules over `(toAlmost R)`
  in `Almost.Module S` are equivalent to `Almost.Module (S.baseChange R)`, compatibly with Mathlib's
  restriction of scalars `ModuleCat R ⥤ ModuleCat V`.
- `Almost.Algebra.test_hom_elements` (characterisation) — for `A = (K°/p)^a` with
  `K = ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞})^` and `ϖ = p`, `A.elements ⊋ K°/ϖ`, and a morphism `A ⟶ B` of almost algebras is an algebra map
  `A.elements →ₐ[V] B.elements` of almost elements, with restriction along `K°/ϖ → A.elements`. For a target `B.elements`, the adjunction
  also identifies it with a map out of `K°/ϖ`; the larger ring of almost elements does not
  invalidate this latter description.

- `algebra_test_classical` — almostifying an ordinary algebra and taking its almost elements recovers it in the classical setup.
- `algebra_test_zero_setup` — for `m = 0`, every almost algebra and its algebra of almost elements are zero.
- `algebra_test_residue` — both `(V/m)^a` and its almost elements are zero.
- `algebra_test_nonzero` — `ℤ^a` over the classical setup is a nonzero algebra.
- Colimits are not computed on almost elements: for multiplication by `p` on `(K°)^a`, with `K` the
  completion of `ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞})`, the cokernel computed on almost elements is `K°/p`, the almost
  elements of the cokernel are `((K°/p)^a)_*`, and the comparison `K°/p → ((K°/p)^a)_*` is not
  surjective (the witness of P0.6 with `ϖ = p`).

The formulas for `free`, `prod`, and `tensor` are respectively almostification of
finitely supported functions, the product of the algebras of almost elements, and their tensor
over `V`. The map `homEquiv` is `elements.map`; the hom of `counitIso` is the adjunction counit.

**Checks for these operations.**

- `Almost.Algebra.counitIso_zero`, `Almost.Algebra.homEquiv_zero`, `Almost.Algebra.prod_zero`: for the zero setup all almost elements and the product vanish.
- `Almost.Algebra.counitIso_classical`, `Almost.Algebra.homEquiv_classical`, `Almost.Algebra.prod_classical`: the classical setup recovers ordinary algebra maps and products.
- `Almost.Algebra.counitIso_two`, `Almost.Algebra.homEquiv_two`, `Almost.Algebra.prod_two`: the product of two copies of the classical rational algebra has distinct endomorphisms and an invertible counit.
- `Almost.Algebra.free_empty`: the free module on the empty set is zero.
- `Almost.Algebra.free_one`: one generator gives the regular module.
- `Almost.Algebra.free_two`: two generators give two copies of the regular module.
- `Almost.Algebra.tensor_unit`: tensoring with the base algebra returns the algebra.
- `Almost.Algebra.tensor_zero`: tensoring with the zero algebra gives zero.
- `Almost.Algebra.tensor_two`: tensoring with two copies of the base gives the product of two copies.

### P0.9 the left adjoint `B_!!` on algebras

**The left adjoint `B ↦ B_!!` of almostification on algebras.** (*almost-algebra-lower-shriek-shriek*)
For a basic setup `S = (V, m)` and an almost `V`-algebra `B`, `B_! = m̃ ⊗_V B_*` is a non-unital
`V`-algebra: it inherits a multiplication from `B` through `m̃ ⊗ m̃ ≅ m̃`, but no unit, since
`(V^a)_! ≅ m̃` and the unit comparison `m̃ → V` of the oplax monoidal functor `(−)_!` is not an
isomorphism unless `m = V` (P0.7). Its unitisation is `B_!! := (V ⊕ B_!)/I`, where `I` is the `V`-submodule spanned by the elements
`(xy, −x ⊗ y ⊗ 1)` for `x, y ∈ m`, is a unital commutative `V`-algebra with `B ≅ (B_!!)^a`, and
`B ↦ B_!!` is left adjoint to `R ↦ R^a`. The span is already the ideal of the unitalisation
`V ⊕ B_!` that Gabber–Ramero quotient by: in `B_! = m̃ ⊗_V B_*` one has
`(x ⊗ y ⊗ 1)·(x' ⊗ y' ⊗ b) = x ⊗ yx'y' ⊗ b = (xy)·(x' ⊗ y' ⊗ b)`, so
`(xy, −x ⊗ y ⊗ 1)·(v, b) = v·(xy, −x ⊗ y ⊗ 1)`, and the two descriptions of `I` agree. The
adjunction is between `A_!!`-algebras and `A`-algebras, for any almost algebra `A` with `B` an
`A`-algebra ([GR] §2.2, Proposition 2.2.27, p. 15). `B` is exact if
`0 → m̃ → V ⊕ B_! → B_!! → 0` is exact; every almost algebra is exact when `m̃ → m` is an isomorphism
(e.g. `m` flat), and `V^a × B` is always exact ([GR] §2.2, Definition 2.2.25 and Remark 2.2.26,
p. 15). `B ↦ B_!!` commutes with all colimits, in particular with tensor products ([GR] §2.2, Remark
2.2.28(i), p. 16); the natural map `B_!! → B_*` is an almost isomorphism ([Bhatt] §4.2, Remark
4.2.8, p. 25); `B ↦ B_!!` preserves faithful flatness of morphisms but not flatness,
see *lower-shriek-shriek-faithful-flatness* (P0.25). Define `Almost.Algebra.shriekShriek`
(`Almost.Algebra S ⥤ CommAlgCat V`, `B ↦ B_!!`), `Almost.Algebra.IsExact` and
`Almost.Algebra.shriekShriekToElements` (the natural map `B_!! → B_*`); prove
`Almost.Algebra.shriekShriekAdj` (over `A`: `B ↦ B_!!` is left adjoint to `R ↦ R^a`),
`Almost.Algebra.shriekShriekUnitIso` (`B ≅ (B.shriekShriek)^a`), `Almost.Algebra.isExact_of_bijective`
(if `S.tilde → S.ideal` is bijective, every almost algebra is exact), `Almost.Algebra.isExact_prod`
(`V^a × B` is exact), `Almost.Algebra.shriekShriek_preservesColimits` (with `shriekShriekTensorIso : (B ⊗_A C)_!! ≅ B_!! ⊗_{A_!!} C_!!`). *Needs:* P0.8's categories and algebra adjunction.
The comparison `Almost.Algebra.shriekShriek_faithfullyFlat_iff` (`φ` faithfully flat
`↔ φ_!!` faithfully flat) is *lower-shriek-shriek-faithful-flatness* (P0.25), using this
unitization and P0.11's flatness theory.

**Checks.**

- `Almost.Algebra.shriekShriek_test_unit` (computation) —
  `(Almost.Algebra.toAlmost S (CommAlgCat.of V V)).shriekShriek ≅ V` as `V`-algebras: `(V^a)_! = m̃`
  and `(V ⊕ m̃)/I ≅ V` via `(v, x ⊗ y) ↦ v + xy`.
- `Almost.Algebra.shriekShriek_test_not_flat` (non-example) — for `S = ofValuationRing V` with
  residue field `k`: the projection `V × V → V` is flat but its image under `(−)^a` then `(−)_!!` is
  `V ×_k V → V`, which is not flat ([GR] Remark 3.1.3(ii)); so flatness of almost algebra maps cannot
  be defined through `(−)_!!`.
- `Almost.Algebra.shriekShriek_test_classical` (degenerate) — for `S = classical V`:
  `B.shriekShriek ≅ B.elements` for every almost algebra `B` (`I` contains `(1, −1 ⊗ 1 ⊗ 1)`, and
  `(v, b) ↦ v·1 + b` is the isomorphism).
- `Almost.Algebra.shriekShriek_test_zero_setup` (degenerate) — for the zero setup `(V, ⊥)`:
  `B_! = 0`, `I = 0` and `B_!! = V` for the unique almost algebra `B = 0`; `(B_!!)^a = V^a = 0 = B`
  and `B_!! = V → B_* = 0` is an almost isomorphism, as every `V`-module is almost zero.
- `Almost.Algebra.shriekShriek_test_elements` (compatibility) — the map
  `B.shriekShriek → B.elements` is an almost isomorphism of `V`-algebras, and `(toAlmost S).map` of
  it is the identity of `B` up to the unit isomorphisms.

- `shriekRelation_test_two_terms` — over any classical setup (in particular `(ℤ, ℤ)`), adding the relations for `(2,3)` and `(5,7)` gives
  `(41, −((2 ⊗ 3) ⊗ 1 + (5 ⊗ 7) ⊗ 1))` in the actual unitalization.
  Thus the relation identifies a positive scalar product with the corresponding positive tensor in the quotient.
  The classical, zero-setup, and unit-algebra cases also satisfy `IsExact`.
  The three direct quotient computations `shriekShriek_test_classical`, `shriekShriek_test_zero_setup`, and
  `shriekShriek_test_unit` mirror the classical, zero-setup, and unit-algebra Checks above.

### P0.10 almost finite generation and presentation

**Almost finitely generated, uniformly almost finitely generated and almost finitely presented
modules.** (*almost-finitely-generated-and-presented*) Let `S = (V, m)` be a basic setup, `R` a
`V`-algebra and `N` an `R`-module, `M = N^a` over `A = R^a`. `N^a` is almost finitely generated if
for every finitely generated ideal `m₀ ⊆ m` there are `n` and an `R`-linear `φ : Rⁿ → N` with
`m₀·coker φ = 0`; uniformly almost finitely generated with bound `n` if one `n` works for all `m₀`;
almost finitely presented if for every finitely generated `m₀ ⊆ m` there is a complex
`R^k →ψ Rⁿ →φ N` with `m₀·coker φ = 0` and `m₀·ker φ ⊆ im ψ` ([GR] §2.3, Proposition 2.3.10(i) and
(ii)(c), p. 18; [GR] §2.3, Definition 2.3.8(iii), p. 17). These conditions depend only on `N^a`
([Sch12] §4, Remark 4.8, p. 20), and agree with Gabber–Ramero's definitions through the uniform
structure on isomorphism classes; under condition (A) (e.g. root and valuation setups) they are
equivalent to Scholze's `ε`-formulation: for every `ε ∈ m` there is a finitely generated (presented)
`R`-module `N_ε` and `N_ε → N` with kernel and cokernel killed by `ε`,
see *almost-finite-generation-epsilon-criterion* (P0.11; [Sch12] §4, Definition/Proposition 4.7(iii),
p. 19). For an arbitrary almost algebra `A` they are applied to `M_*` over `A_*` (P0.8). Convention: the
uniform notion here (maps from `Rⁿ` with small cokernel) implies Gabber–Ramero's `U_n(A)` in general (the closure of the isomorphism classes of modules generated by `n` elements in the uniform space of [GR] Definition 2.3.8)
and is equivalent to it under (A) ([GR] Remark 2.3.9). The Lean forms are stated for `V`-modules
`N` over the setup `S` itself; the case of an `R`-module over a `V`-algebra `R` is the same
statement for the setup `S.baseChange R`. In the almost finite presentation, `k`, `n`, `ψ` and
`φ` may depend on `m₀`, and no kernel condition uniform in `m₀` is imposed: this is exactly the
`m₀`-quantified condition of [GR] Proposition 2.3.10(ii)(c). Define `BasicSetup.AlmostFG`
(`∀ m₀ ≤ S.ideal, m₀.FG → ∃ n (φ : (Fin n → V) →ₗ[V] N), ∀ ε ∈ m₀, ∀ x, ε • x ∈ range φ`, i.e.
`m₀ • ⊤ ≤ LinearMap.range φ`), `BasicSetup.UniformlyAlmostFG` (with the bound `n : ℕ` as an
argument: the same with `φ : (Fin n → V) →ₗ[V] N` for every `m₀`) and `BasicSetup.AlmostFP`
(`∀ m₀` f.g., `∃` complex `V^k —ψ→ Vⁿ —φ→ N` with `φ ∘ ψ = 0`, `m₀ • coker φ = 0` and
`m₀ • ker φ ≤ range ψ`); prove `BasicSetup.AlmostFP.almostFG` (almost finitely presented implies
almost finitely generated), invariance of `AlmostFG` under almost
isomorphisms, `Almost.Module.almostFG_of_finite` (`Module.Finite R N → AlmostFG`;
`Module.FinitePresentation R N → AlmostFP`), `BasicSetup.AlmostFG.extension` and
`BasicSetup.AlmostFP.extension` (in a short exact sequence of ordinary `V`-modules,
almost f.g., respectively almost f.p., endpoints imply the same property for the middle term;
for `M` almost f.p., a quotient is almost f.p. iff the kernel is almost f.g.,
[GR] Lemma 2.3.17(i)–(ii), p. 20), `BasicSetup.AlmostFG.baseChange` (base change along
`A → B` preserves `AlmostFG`, `AlmostFP` and uniform bounds), `Almost.Module.almostFP_iff_alHom_colim`
(`AlmostFP M ↔ alHom_A(M, −)` commutes with filtered colimits, [GR] Proposition 2.3.15) and
`Almost.Module.almostFG_iff_epsilon` (under (A): `AlmostFG ↔ ∀ ε ∈ m, ∃` f.g. `N_ε → N` with kernel
and cokernel killed by `ε`). *Needs:* P0.8; Mathlib `Submodule.FG`, `Module.Finite`,
`Module.FinitePresentation`.

**Checks.**

- `Almost.Module.AlmostFG_test_quadratic` (computation) — for `K` the completion of
  `ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞})`, `p ≠ 2`, and `L = K(√p)` (quadratic over `K`, since `√p` has value `1/2`,
  outside the value group `ℤ[1/p]` of `K`; at `p = 2`, `√2 = 2^{1/2}` lies in `K` and `L = K`, so this
  `L` is used for odd `p` only, here and in P0.11–P0.17, where it is called the odd-`p` `L` of
  P0.10): with `R_n = K° ⊕ p^{1/2p^n}K° ⊆ L°`, the cokernel of
  `R_n → L°` is killed by `p^{1/p^{n−1}}`, so `L°a` is `UniformlyAlmostFG` with bound `2` and
  `AlmostFP` ([Bhatt] Example 4.2.7).
- `Almost.Module.finiteness_test_almost_zero` (degenerate) — every almost zero `R`-module `N` gives
  `N^a ≅ 0`, which is `UniformlyAlmostFG` with bound `0` and `AlmostFP`.
- `Almost.Module.finiteness_test_classical` (compatibility) — for `S = classical V`:
  `AlmostFG (N^a) ↔ Module.Finite R N` and `AlmostFP (N^a) ↔ Module.FinitePresentation R N`.
- `Almost.Module.almostFG_test_infinite_sum_valuation` (non-example) — for `S = ofValuationRing K°`:
  `N = ⊕_{n∈ℕ} K°` is not almost finitely generated: for a fixed `0 ≠ ϖ ∈ K°°` and `m₀ = (ϖ)`, no map `(K°)^n → N` has
  cokernel killed by `ϖ` (the image misses all but finitely many summands).

- `finiteness_test_classical` — for every commutative `V`, the classical predicates are
  `Module.Finite V N` and `Module.FinitePresentation V N`.
- `finiteness_test_almost_zero` — an almost zero module satisfies all three predicates, with uniform bound zero.
- `finiteness_test_free` — `Vⁿ` satisfies all three, with uniform bound `n`, including `n = 0, 1, 2`.
