- `finiteness_test_infinite_sum` — the countable direct sum of copies of `ℚ` fails all three predicates in the classical setup, for every finite uniform bound.
- `uniform_test_rank_bound`, `uniform_test_zero_bound` — over a field, the bound for `k^r` is `n` exactly when `r ≤ n`; for any setup the bound zero means almost zero.

- Over any domain, a nonzero element of the setup ideal prevents the countable free module from being almost finitely generated: any finite family misses a basis coordinate on which that element still acts nontrivially.
- Over `(ℤ, ℤ)`, `ℤ` is almost finitely generated and presented, whereas `ℕ →₀ ℤ` is neither.
  The same infinite free module satisfies both predicates for the zero setup.

Lean: `BasicSetup.AlmostFG`, `BasicSetup.AlmostFP`, `BasicSetup.AlmostFP.almostFG`; a Lean
`example` states that for the classical setup `AlmostFP` is `Module.FinitePresentation`;
examples on `ℤ` and `ℕ →₀ ℤ` mirror the classical and zero-setup controls for both predicates.

### P0.11 flatness and almost projectivity

**Flat, faithfully flat, almost projective and almost finite projective almost modules.**
(*almost-flat-projective-finiteness*) Let `S = (V, m)` be a basic setup, `A` an almost `V`-algebra
and `M` an `A`-module (`A-Mod` as in P0.8). `M` is flat if `M ⊗_A − : A-Mod → A-Mod` is exact,
faithfully flat if moreover `M ⊗_A N ≅ 0` implies `N ≅ 0`, almost projective if
`alHom_A(M, −) : A-Mod → A-Mod` is exact, and almost finite projective if it is almost projective
and almost finitely generated (P0.10); "uniformly almost finite projective" adds a uniform bound
([GR] §2.4, Definition 2.4.4, p. 23). Convention: categorical projectivity (`Hom(M, −)`
exact) is never used — `Almost.Module S` has no nonzero projective objects when `V` is local and
`m ≠ V` ([GR] §2.4, Example 2.4.5, p. 23; [Sch12] §4, Remark 4.8, p. 20). For a `V`-algebra `R` and
an `R`-module `N`: `N` flat (faithfully flat, projective) implies `N^a` flat (faithfully flat,
almost projective) over `R^a` ([GR] §2.4, (2.4.8), p. 24). Characterisations: the Tor and Ext
criteria *almost-flatness-tor-criterion*, the `ε`-factorisation
*almost-projective-epsilon-factorisation* (P0.11) and finite projective = flat + almost finitely
presented, *almost-finite-projective-iff* (P0.11). Define `Almost.Module.Flat` (`M ⊗_A −` preserves
finite limits), `Almost.Module.FaithfullyFlat` (flat and `M ⊗_A N ≅ 0 → N ≅ 0`),
`Almost.Module.AlmostProjective` (`alHom_A(M, −)` preserves epimorphisms) and
`Almost.Module.AlmostFiniteProjective` (`AlmostProjective ∧ AlmostFG`; uniformly with bound `n`);
prove `Almost.Module.flat_toAlmost` (`Module.Flat R N → Flat ((toAlmost _).obj N)`; likewise
`FaithfullyFlat`, and `Projective → AlmostProjective`), `Almost.Module.AlmostProjective.flat`,
`Almost.Module.Flat.tensor` (`Flat` and `AlmostProjective` are stable under `⊗_A` and under base
change `B ⊗_A −`), `Almost.Module.Flat.trans` (if `B` is a flat (almost projective, almost f.g.,
almost f.p.) `A`-algebra and `M` such a `B`-module, `M` is such an `A`-module, [GR] Lemma 2.4.7),
and `Almost.Module.flat_iff_tor` (`Flat (N^a) ↔ ∀ X i, 0 < i → IsAlmostZero (Tor_i^R(N, X))`);
the characterisations `Almost.Module.almostProjective_iff_factor` (for `M` almost f.g.:
`AlmostProjective M ↔ ∀ ε ∈ m, ∃ n u v, v ∘ u = ε • 𝟙` through `A^n`) and
`Almost.Module.almostFiniteProjective_iff` (`AlmostFiniteProjective M ↔ Flat M ∧ AlmostFP M`) are
proved with the supporting results *almost-projective-epsilon-factorisation* (P0.11) and
*almost-finite-projective-iff* (P0.11). *Needs:* P0.8; P0.10; Mathlib `Module.Flat`,
`Module.FaithfullyFlat`, `Module.Projective`, `CategoryTheory.Functor.PreservesEpimorphisms`.

Two supporting results. Tor and Ext criteria for almost flatness and almost projectivity
(*almost-flatness-tor-criterion*): for a basic setup `S`, a `V`-algebra `R` and `R`-modules `M, N`,
(i) there are natural isomorphisms `Tor_i^{R^a}(M^a, N^a) ≅ Tor_i^R(M, N)^a` and
`alExt^i_{R^a}(M^a, N^a) ≅ Ext^i_R(M, N)^a`, where `Tor^{R^a}` and `alExt` are the derived functors
of `⊗` and `alHom` on `R^a-Mod` (computed by flat resp. injective resolutions; Mathlib
`CategoryTheory.Abelian.Ext`); (ii) `N^a` is flat over `R^a` iff `Tor_i^R(N, X)` is almost zero for
all `R`-modules `X` and all `i > 0`; (iii) `N^a` is almost projective iff `Ext^i_R(N, X)` is almost
zero for all `X` and `i > 0`; (iv) `N^a` is faithfully flat iff it is flat and `N ⊗_R X` almost zero
implies `X` almost zero; (v) an almost projective module is flat ([GR] §2.4, (2.4.10), p. 24; [GR]
§2.4, Remark 2.4.12(i), p. 24; [Sch12] §4, Definition/Proposition 4.7(i), p. 19). Over `(K°, K°°)`, `M^a` is flat iff `Tor_1(M, K°/ϖ) = M[ϖ]` is almost zero, iff
`M_*` has no `ϖ`-torsion ([Sch12] Lemma 5.3(i)). The `ε`-criterion for almost finite generation and
presentation under condition (A) (*almost-finite-generation-epsilon-criterion*): for a basic setup
satisfying (A) (root and valuation setups), a `V`-algebra `R` and an `R`-module `N`, `N^a` is almost
finitely generated (resp. presented) iff for every `ε ∈ m` there are a finitely generated (resp.
presented) `R`-module `N_ε` and `N_ε → N` with kernel and cokernel killed by `ε`, and `N^a` is
uniformly almost finitely generated with bound `n` iff for every `ε ∈ m` there is `Rⁿ → N` with
cokernel killed by `ε`; in a general basic setup the same holds with `ε` replaced by finitely
generated subideals `m₀ ⊆ m`, which is the definition of P0.10 ([GR] §2.3, Remark 2.3.9, p. 18;
[Sch12] §4, Definition/Proposition 4.7(iii), p. 19).

**Checks.**

- `Almost.Module.Flat_test_valuation` (computation) — for `S = ofValuationRing K°` and `0 ≠ ϖ ∈ K°°`:
  `(toAlmost S).obj K°` is `Flat` and `(toAlmost S).obj (K° ⧸ ϖ)` is not `Flat` (its almost elements
  have `ϖ`-torsion).
- `Almost.Module.projectivity_test_classical` (compatibility) — for `S = classical V` and a `V`-module `N`:
  `Flat (N^a) ↔ Module.Flat V N`, `FaithfullyFlat (N^a) ↔ Module.FaithfullyFlat V N`, and
  `AlmostProjective (N^a) ↔ Module.Projective V N`.
- `Almost.Module.projectivity_test_zero` (degenerate) — the zero module is `Flat` and
  `AlmostProjective` but not `FaithfullyFlat` (unless `A ≅ 0`).
- `Almost.Module.almostProjective_test_unit_epsilon` (degenerate) — if some `ε ∈ m` is a unit then
  `m = V` and the factorisation `v ∘ u = ε • 𝟙` through `Aⁿ` of `almostProjective_iff_factor` is an
  honest splitting, so `AlmostProjective` is `Module.Projective` and the `ε`-criterion
  `N_ε → N` of *almost-finite-generation-epsilon-criterion* is an isomorphism from a finitely generated module; both
  reduce to the classical statements, as `Almost.Module.projectivity_test_classical` requires.

Supporting result: Flat + almost finitely presented ⟺ almost projective + almost finitely
generated (*almost-finite-projective-iff*, `Almost.Module.almostFiniteProjective_iff`): for a basic
setup `S`, an almost `V`-algebra `A` and an `A`-module `M`, (i) if `M` is almost projective and
almost finitely generated, `M` is almost finitely presented (and flat); (ii) if `M` is flat and
almost finitely presented, `M` is almost projective;
hence Scholze's "finite projective" (flat and almost finitely presented) coincides with almost
finite projective; (iii) if `A → B` is a monomorphism of almost algebras and `M` is an almost
finitely generated flat `A`-module with `B ⊗_A M` almost finitely presented over `B`, then `M` is
almost finitely presented ([GR] §2.4, Proposition 2.4.18, p. 26; [Sch12] §4, Proposition 4.10 and
the text after it, p. 20). Classically this says finitely presented flat modules are projective and
finitely generated projective modules are finitely presented. 

Almost projectivity via
`ε`-factorisations through free modules (*almost-projective-epsilon-factorisation*,
`Almost.Module.almostProjective_iff_factor`): for an almost algebra `A` and an `A`-module `M`,
(i) `M` is almost projective iff for every `ε ∈ m` there are a set `I` and `A`-linear maps
`M →u A^{(I)} →v M` with `v ∘ u = ε·1_M`; (ii) if `M` is almost finitely
generated, `M` is almost projective iff for every `ε ∈ m` there are `n(ε) ∈ ℕ` and
`M →u Aⁿ →v M` with `v ∘ u = ε·1_M`, and, under condition (A), `M` is uniformly almost finite projective with bound `n`
iff `n` can be taken independent of `ε`, Kedlaya–Liu's definition ([GR] §2.4, Lemma 2.4.15, p. 25, and the proof of Lemma 2.4.29, p. 28;
[KL15] §5.5, Definition 5.5.8, p. 132). For `P = L°a` over `K°a` (`L = K(√p)`, the odd-`p` `L` of
P0.10) the maps
`L° → (K°)² → L°` with composite `p^{1/p^{n−1}}` ([Bhatt] Example 4.2.7) exhibit `P` as uniformly
almost finite projective with bound `2`.

- `projectivity_test_classical` — flatness, faithful flatness and almost projectivity become the three ordinary module predicates in the classical setup.
- `projectivity_test_zero` — the zero object is flat, almost projective, almost finite projective, and uniformly so with bound zero; it is faithfully flat exactly when the tensor unit is zero.
- `projectivity_test_free` — the almostification of `Vⁿ` is almost finite projective with uniform bound `n`, including `n = 0, 1, 2`.
- `projectivity_test_torsion` — classically, `ℤ/2` is neither flat nor almost projective.
- `faithful_test_unit` — the tensor unit is faithfully flat in every setup.
- `uniformProjectivity_test_rank` — over a field in the classical setup, a free module of rank `r` has uniform projective bound `n` exactly when `r ≤ n`.

`Almost.Module.ordinaryTor` and `ordinaryExt` use Mathlib's derived tensor and
internal-Hom functors on ordinary modules. `tor` and `alExt` almostify their values on
almost elements; `tor_toAlmost` and `alExt_toAlmost` identify the result for any honest
representatives ([GR] (2.4.10)).

- `derived_test_degree_zero` — degree zero recovers almost tensor and internal Hom.
- `derived_test_free` — positive Tor and almost Ext vanish from every finite free almost module, including rank zero.
- `derived_test_torsion` — `Tor₁^ℤ(ℤ/2, ℤ/2) = ℤ/2` and `Ext¹_ℤ(ℤ/2, ℤ) = ℤ/2`;
  their almost versions are nonzero in the classical setup.

Lean: `BasicSetup.IsAlmostFiniteProjective`, the `ε`-factorisation of
*almost-projective-epsilon-factorisation*(ii) for a `V`-module over `S` (for every `ε ∈ m`,
`ε • id_M` factors through a finite free module), which by that result agrees with
`AlmostFiniteProjective` above; and `BasicSetup.IsAlmostFiniteProjective.almostFG`. A Lean
`example` states that for the classical setup the `ε`-form is `Module.Projective ∧ Module.Finite`.

### P0.12 duals and traces

**Duals, traces of endomorphisms and the trace form of an almost finite projective algebra.**
(*almost-dual-and-trace*) Provides the duality trace whose internal almost-module realization is
used by the algebra-trace and trace-form consumers. Supplied by PivotalSpherical §Layer 2 / Left
and right trace and the common spherical `trace`.
Convention gap: this roadmap proves the required almost duality, instantiates the supplier's
standard symmetric pivotal/spherical structure (§Layer 7), and identifies the internal map
`End_A(P)^a → A` with its tensor-unit-valued trace on endomorphisms.

Let `S` be a basic setup and `A` an almost `V`-algebra. For an `A`-module `M`, the dual is
`M* := alHom_A(M, A)` with evaluation `ev_{M/A} : M ⊗_A M* → A`. For `P` almost finite projective,
`ω_{P/A} : P ⊗_A P* → End_A(P)^a` is an isomorphism by
*tensor-hom-comparison-almost-projective*. On the full subcategory of almost finite projective
`A`-modules, prove closure under duals and tensor products and both triangle identities for the
evaluation and the coevaluation obtained from `ω_{P/A}⁻¹` applied to the identity; these give the
rigid symmetric category needed by the supplier. Retain `Almost.Module.trace` only as the local
internal realization `tr_{P/A} := ev_{P/A} ∘ ω_{P/A}⁻¹ : End_A(P)^a → A`. Its comparison with the
supplied trace is an equality of internal morphisms, natural on maps `L → End_A(P)^a` for every
test `A`-module `L`, using the corresponding contraction `L ⊗_A P → P`; at `L = A` it recovers
PivotalSpherical §Layer 2's trace through `alHom_A(A, A) ≅ A`.
The carrier's docstring is: “Internal almost-module realization of PivotalSpherical §Layer 2's
trace for `Almost.Algebra.trace` and trace-form consumers. The tensor–Hom/evaluation and scalar
identifications are proved here.”

Provides cross-object cyclicity for the almost endomorphism trace through the duality comparison.
Supplied by PivotalSpherical §Layer 2 / Cyclicity (`leftTrace_comm` and the common spherical trace).
Convention gap: both source objects must carry
the proved almost duality, and this roadmap translates composition between `ψ∘φ` and Lean's
left-to-right `f ≫ g` before transporting scalar traces through the internal comparison.

Provides tensor multiplicativity for the almost endomorphism trace. Supplied by PivotalSpherical
§Layer 2 / The left trace is monoidal (`leftTrace_tensor` and the common spherical trace).
Convention gap: this roadmap transports the
supplier's tensor-unit endomorphisms and unitor formula to multiplication in `A`, preserving the
chosen tensor/dual identifications.

For an `A`-algebra `B` which is almost finite projective as an `A`-module,
`μ : B → End_A(B)^a` (`b ↦`
multiplication by `b`, defined on almost elements; [Sch12] §4, Remark 4.15, p. 20) gives the almost
trace `Tr_{B/A} := tr_{B/A} ∘ μ : B → A` using the internal realization of PivotalSpherical
§Layer 2 ([GR] §4.1, (4.1.7), p. 74), the trace form
`t_{B/A} := Tr_{B/A} ∘ μ_{B/A} : B ⊗_A B → A` and `τ_{B/A} : B → B*`; `t_{B/A}` is perfect, by
definition, iff `τ_{B/A}` is an isomorphism ([GR] §4.1, (4.1.12), p. 75). Properties:
additivity on short exact sequences of almost finite projective modules;
`Tr_{C⊗_A B/C} = 1_C ⊗ Tr_{B/A}`; `Tr_{C/A} = Tr_{B/A} ∘ Tr_{C/B}` ([GR]
§4.1, Proposition 4.1.8(ii)-(iii), p. 74); `τ` is `B`-linear and compatible with base change.
Mathlib's `LinearMap.trace` (defined through a finite basis, and `0` when the module is not finite
free) is not used for almost finite projective modules; it agrees with `tr` on finite free modules
after almostification via AdicSpacesPartIII §R3.8 / *projective-module-trace*,
`LinearMap.projectiveTrace_eq_trace` and the internal comparison above.
Define `Almost.Module.dual` (`M*` with its evaluation), `Almost.Algebra.trace` (`Tr_{B/A} : B ⟶ A`),
`Almost.Algebra.traceForm` (`t_{B/A}` and `τ_{B/A}`) and `Almost.Algebra.IsPerfectTraceForm`
(`τ_{B/A}` is an isomorphism); prove `Almost.Module.dualTensorHomIso` (`ω_{P/A} : P ⊗_A P* ≅ End_A(P)^a` for `P` almost finite projective), `Almost.Module.trace_additive`, `Almost.Module.isReflexive`
(`P ≅ P**`), `Almost.Algebra.trace_baseChange`, `Almost.Algebra.trace_trans`,
`Almost.Algebra.trace_of_iso` (simp: if `A → B` is an isomorphism, `Tr_{B/A}` is its inverse) and
`Almost.Algebra.traceFormDual_baseChange` (`η ∘ (1_C ⊗ τ_{B/A}) = τ_{C⊗B/C}`, where
`η : C ⊗_A B* → (C ⊗_A B)*` is the dual base-change comparison, [GR] Lemma 4.1.13).
*Needs:* P0.7; P0.8; P0.11; PivotalSpherical §Layer 2 (trace, cyclicity and monoidality) and §Layer 7
(standard symmetric pivotal/spherical structure); AdicSpacesPartIII §R3.8 /
*projective-module-trace*; Mathlib `LinearMap.trace`, `Algebra.trace`, `Algebra.traceForm`.

Supporting result: `E ⊗ alHom(F, N) → alHom(F, E ⊗ N)` is an isomorphism for almost finite
projective `E` or `F` (*tensor-hom-comparison-almost-projective*). For a basic setup `S`, an almost
algebra `A` and `A`-modules `E, F, N`, the natural map `E ⊗_A alHom_A(F, N) → alHom_A(F, E ⊗_A N)`
is (i) an isomorphism if `E` or `F` is almost finite projective, if `E` is flat and `F` almost
finitely presented, if `F` is almost projective and `E` almost finitely presented, or if `E` is
almost projective and `F` almost finitely generated; (ii) a monomorphism if `E` is flat and `F`
almost finitely generated, or if `E` is almost projective; (iii) an epimorphism if `F` is almost
projective and `E` almost finitely generated ([GR] §2.4, Lemma 2.4.29, p. 27). Consequently, for `P`
almost finite projective, `ω_{P/A}` is an isomorphism ([GR] §2.4, Lemma 2.4.29(i)(b), p. 27), `P` is
reflexive ([GR] §2.4, Lemma 2.4.31(ii), p. 28), and
`B ⊗_A alHom_A(P, N) ≅ alHom_B(B ⊗_A P, B ⊗_A N)` for every `A`-algebra `B`; for `P = (Rⁿ)^a` free,
`ω_{P/A}` is the usual `Rⁿ ⊗ (Rⁿ)^∨ ≅ End(Rⁿ)` after almostification.

**Checks.**

- `Almost.Module.trace_test_free_endomorphism` (compatibility) — for `P = (toAlmost _).obj (Fin n → R)`:
  `Almost.Module.trace P ((toAlmost _).map f) = (toAlmost _).map (LinearMap.trace R _ f)`, and for a
  free finite `R`-algebra `R'`, `Almost.Algebra.trace = (Algebra.trace R R')^a`.
- `Almost.Algebra.trace_test_quadratic` (computation) — for `K` the completion of
  `ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞})`, `p ≠ 2`, `L = K(√p)` (the odd-`p` `L` of P0.10, for which `Tr(1) = 2` is a
  unit): `Tr_{L°a/K°a}(1) = 2` and `IsPerfectTraceForm (L°a/K°a)`,
  while the honest trace form on `R_n = K° ⊕ p^{1/2p^n}K°` has discriminant `4p^{1/p^n}` ([Bhatt]
  Examples 4.2.7 and 4.3.2, pp. 24 and 26).
- `Almost.Algebra.trace_test_quadratic_order` — for the monic quadratic order
  `R[X]/(X²-a)`, the trace matrix on `1, X` has determinant `4a`; taking `a = p^{1/pⁿ}`
  gives the discriminant of the orders in the preceding Check.
- `Almost.Module.trace_test_almost_zero` (degenerate) — for `P = 0`, `tr_{P/A} = 0`; for `B = 0`,
  `Tr_{B/A} = 0` and `t_{B/A}` is perfect (`τ : 0 → alHom(0, A) = 0`).
- `Almost.Algebra.trace_test_self_product_dual_numbers` (computation) — for `B = A`:
  `Tr_{A/A} = 𝟙_A` and `t(b ⊗ b') = bb'` is perfect (`τ = 𝟙`); for `B = A × A`:
  `Tr((b₁, b₂)) = b₁ + b₂`, `t((b₁, b₂) ⊗ (c₁, c₂)) = b₁c₁ + b₂c₂`, perfect; for `B = A[ε]/(ε²)`:
  `Tr(1) = 2`, `Tr(ε) = 0`, `t` has matrix `[[2, 0], [0, 0]]` on the basis `1, ε` and `τ(ε) = 0`,
  so for `A ≠ 0`, `t` is not perfect even when `2` is a unit, and `B` is not unramified (P0.15).
  For `A = 0` both `B` and its trace pairing are zero, and the pairing is perfect.
- `Almost.Module.trace_test_not_linearMap_trace` (non-example) — for `P = L°a` over `K°a`, with `L`
  the odd-`p` `L` of P0.10 (`L°` is
  not a free `K°`-module), `(LinearMap.trace K° L°)^a = 0 ≠ tr_{P/A}(1) = 2`: the almost trace cannot
  be defined through Mathlib's `LinearMap.trace` of a representative.

- `dual_test_zero`, `dual_test_unit`, `dual_test_rank_two` — the duals of zero, the unit, and a free module of rank two are respectively zero, the unit, and a free module of rank two.
- `trace_test_almost_zero`, `trace_test_almost_unit`, `trace_test_almost_two` — the actual almost trace gives `0`, `1`, and `2` on the identities of those three objects.
- `trace_test_free_endomorphism` — for every endomorphism of `Vⁿ`, including ranks zero, one, and two, the trace after almostification is the scalar endomorphism of the tensor unit given by Mathlib's ordinary finite-free trace.
- `trace_test_char_two` — the identity of a classical rank-two vector space in characteristic two has trace zero.
- `tensorHom_test_zero`, `tensorHom_test_unit`, `tensorHom_test_two` — the specified tensor–Hom comparison is invertible for zero source, unit tensor factor, and free rank-two source respectively.

- `trace_test_product`, `trace_test_dual_numbers`, `trace_test_unramified` — the ordinary library computations
  give product trace matrix `diag(1,1)`, dual-number trace matrix `diag(2,0)`, and failure of formal
  unramifiedness for dual numbers over a nonzero ring. These are comparisons for the almost trace, not its definition.

- `algebraTrace_test_zero` — the relative algebra trace and its bilinear form are zero for a zero target, and the resulting map from zero to its dual is invertible.
- `algebraTrace_test_product` — the trace form of the almostification of `V × V` is perfect; its trace is nonzero unless the tensor unit is zero.
- `algebraTrace_test_dual_numbers` — over the classical setup on `ℚ`, the dual-number trace form is nonzero but not perfect. This distinguishes a nondegenerate pairing from a merely nonzero map.

`Almost.Algebra.traceElements` is the trace on almost-element rings. Its characterizing
identity `traceElements_spec` identifies its almostification with `trace` using the
monoidal unit comparison. The base-change and dual-trace identities are evaluated on
pure tensors; the transitivity and isomorphism identities are evaluated on almost elements.

**Checks.**

- `traceElements_identity` — the trace for the identity algebra is the identity function.
- `traceElements_zero` — the trace from a zero almost algebra is zero.
- `traceElements_product` — the product algebra sends `(a,b)` to `a+b`, including characteristic two.

`Almost.kummerField p r` is the closure in `ℂ_p` of the subfield generated by the
range of `r`, where `r₀ = p` and `rₙ₊₁^p = rₙ`. Its equation is `kummerField_eq`.
This choice specifies one compatible root sequence. The quadratic examples use
`L = K(√p)` inside `ℂ_p`; `kummerIntegersMap` is the inclusion on valuation rings,
characterized by its unchanged image in `ℂ_p`.

**Checks.**

- `kummerField_zero` — the zero sequence generates the closed copy of `ℚ_p`.
- `kummerField_roots` — every chosen root belongs to `K` and has norm whose `pⁿ`-th power is `p⁻¹`.
- `kummerField_quadratic` — for odd `p`, a square root of `p` is outside `K`.
- `kummerIntegersMap_identity` — equal subfields give the identity map.
- `kummerIntegersMap_composition` — two inclusions compose to the direct inclusion.
- `kummerIntegersMap_prime` — the inclusion sends the integral scalar `p` to `p`.
- `kummerIntegersMap_quadratic_not_surjective` — for odd `p`, the inclusion into
  the quadratic extension misses the integral square root of `p`.

### P0.13 rank decomposition

**Rank decomposition of uniformly almost finite projective modules.**
(*rank-decomposition-of-finite-projective*) Let `S` be a basic setup satisfying condition (B)
(`k`-th powers generate `m`; automatic from flatness of `m̃` by [GR] Proposition 2.1.7(ii), p. 9; (B) is used for
the uniform continuity of `Λ^r`, [GR] Lemma 2.3.7(vi), and for Proposition 4.3.4), `A` an almost
`V`-algebra and `P` a uniformly almost finite projective `A`-module. Then `P` has finite rank:
`Λ^r_A P = 0` for some `r` ([GR] §4.3, Remark 4.3.10(i), p. 85). For `P` almost finite projective with
`Λ^r_A P = 0` there is a unique decomposition `A ≅ A_0 × A_1 × ⋯ × A_{r−1}` such that
`P_i := P ⊗_A A_i` has constant rank `i` over `A_i`: `Λ^{i+1}_{A_i} P_i = 0` and `Λ^i_{A_i} P_i` is
an invertible `A_i`-module (`Λ^i P_i ⊗ (Λ^i P_i)* ≅ A_i`); the decomposition is compatible with base change
`A → A'` ([GR] §4.3, Proposition 4.3.27, p. 88, with the standing finiteness hypothesis on p. 83;
[GR] §4.3, Definition 4.3.9(iv), p. 85; [Sch12] §4,
Theorem 4.11, p. 20, over `(K°, K°°)`, citing the book numbering). For `L°a` over `K°a`
(`L = K(√p)`, the odd-`p` `L` of P0.10): `r = 3` and `A = A_2` (constant rank `2`); for `A = K°a × K°a` and `P = K°a × 0`,
`A_1` is the first factor and `A_0` the second. *Needs:* P0.12; Mathlib `Module.Invertible`,
`ExteriorAlgebra.exteriorPower`.

`Almost.Module.rankDecomposition_baseChange` states compatibility for every almost-algebra
map `f : A → A'`, every almost finite projective module `P` over `S.baseChange A_*`, and every
`D : RankDecomposition P r`. It produces a rank decomposition of
`(Almost.Module.baseChange S f).obj P` and a comparison between the new tensor unit and the
scalar extension of the old one. Each new projector is the corresponding transported projector
conjugated by that comparison. No flatness or faithfulness of `f` is required; a factor may become
zero. This is the naturality of [GR] Proposition 4.3.27, p. 88.

**Checks.**

- `Almost.Module.rankFactors_test_zero` (degenerate) — `P = 0` has `Λ^1 P = 0`, so `r = 1` and the
  decomposition is `A = A_0`; a module of constant rank `0` is zero, since `Λ^1 P = P`; for a
  uniformly almost finite projective `P` with bound `n` the argument gives `Λ^{n+1} P = 0` (the
  composite `P → Aⁿ → P` is `ε`, so `Λ^{n+1} P` is killed by every `ε^{n+1}`, which generate `m`
  under (B)).

- `exterior_test_degree_zero` — `Λ⁰ M` is the tensor unit, including `M = 0`.
- `exterior_test_degree_one` — `Λ¹ M ≅ M`; constant rank zero therefore forces `M = 0`.
- `exterior_test_rank_two` — for `(V²)^a`, `Λ³ = 0` and `Λ² ≅ V^a`.
- `Almost.Module.rankFactors_test_one` — a rank-one free module has `r = 2`, with `A₁ = A` and `A₀ = 0`.
- `Almost.Module.rankFactors_test_two` — a rank-two free module has `r = 3`, with `A₂ = A` and `A₀ = A₁ = 0`.
  `RankDecomposition` expresses the factors by orthogonal idempotent endomorphisms of the tensor unit,
  whose sum is the identity. The factor modules are their images. On factor `i`, `Λ^{i+1} P` vanishes
  and the evaluation of `Λ^i P` against its dual is invertible. Thus the carrier records constant rank,
  not merely a list of ring factors. `rankDecomposition` constructs it and `rankDecomposition_unique`
  fixes its projectors uniquely; `RankDecomposition.unitIso` is the base decomposition.
- `rankFactors_test_zero`, `rankFactors_test_one`, `rankFactors_test_two` — for free ranks `0, 1, 2`,
  only the matching projector is the identity and the other projectors are zero.
- `rankFactors_test_empty` — an empty rank decomposition forces the base unit to be zero.
- `Almost.Module.rankDecomposition_infinite_support` (negative control) — let `k` be a field,
  `V = ∏_{i∈ℕ} k` with the classical setup, and `I = ⊕_{i∈ℕ} V δ_i ⊂ V`, where `δ_i` is the
  coordinate idempotent. For `P = I^a`, projectivity follows from the direct sum of the projective
  summands `V δ_i`, and `Λ²_V P = 0`: distinct summands have zero tensor product, and each summand
  is cyclic. Yet `P` is not almost finitely generated, since any finite set of generators has
  support in a common finite subset of `ℕ`. Its annihilator is zero, so a rank decomposition with
  `r = 2` would force the rank-zero projector to be zero and the rank-one projector to be the
  identity. But the image of evaluation `P ⊗ P* → V^a` is `I^a`, which misses `1`; evaluation is
  not invertible and `RankDecomposition S P 2` is empty. Thus vanishing of an exterior power does
  not replace the almost finite generation hypothesis in `rankDecomposition`.

### P0.14 flat, unramified, étale and finite étale morphisms

Almost finite étale algebras are built next: the morphism classes, the trace-form criterion,
inversion of an element of `m`, the comparison with Mathlib's finite étale algebras, almost Kähler
differentials and the cotangent complex of a ring map.

**Flat, unramified, étale and finite étale morphisms of almost algebras.**
(*almost-finite-projective-and-finite-etale-algebras*) Let `S` be a basic setup and `φ : A → B` a
morphism of almost `V`-algebras; view `B` as a `B ⊗_A B`-algebra through the multiplication
`μ_{B/A} : B ⊗_A B → B`, with kernel `I_{B/A}`; the module notions are those of P0.11 and P0.10,
applied to `B` as an `A`-module and as a `B ⊗_A B`-module. `φ` is flat (faithfully flat, almost
projective) if `B` is a flat (faithfully flat, almost projective) `A`-module; (uniformly) almost
finite if `B` is a (uniformly) almost finitely generated `A`-module; weakly unramified (unramified)
if `B` is a flat (almost projective) `B ⊗_A B`-module; weakly étale (étale) if flat and weakly
unramified (unramified) ([GR] §3.1, Definition 3.1.1(iii)-(iv), p. 39). `φ` is finite étale if it is
étale and `B` is an almost finitely presented `A`-module ([Sch12] §4, Definition 4.13, p. 20;
Gabber–Ramero's `A-Ét_afp`, [GR] §3.2, (3.2.27), p. 46; Kedlaya–Liu's and Bhatt's "almost finite
étale", [Bhatt] §4.3, Definition 4.3.1, p. 25); then `B` is almost finite projective over `A`
by *almost-finite-projective-iff* (P0.11). `A_fet` denotes the full subcategory of `A`-algebras that
are finite étale over `A`. Equivalent descriptions: unramified iff there is a diagonal idempotent
`e ∈ (B ⊗_A B)_*` with `μ(e) = 1` and `I_{B/A,*}·e = 0` (*unramified-idempotent-characterisation* in P0.15,
Scholze's definition); for `B` almost finite projective over `A`, étale iff the trace form
`t_{B/A}` is perfect (P0.15). Convention: "finite étale" always means étale and almost finitely
presented; in the classical setup it is Mathlib's finite étale (P0.17), while Gabber–Ramero's
"étale" without finiteness is more general than EGA étale ([GR] §3.1, Remark 3.1.3(i), p. 39).
Define `Almost.Algebra.IsFlat` (flat, faithfully flat, almost projective `φ`),
`Almost.Algebra.IsUnramified` (with `IsWeaklyUnramified`), `Almost.Algebra.IsEtale`
(`IsFlat ∧ IsUnramified`, with `IsWeaklyEtale`), `Almost.Algebra.IsFiniteEtale`
(`IsEtale ∧ AlmostFP B` over `A`) and `Almost.Algebra.FiniteEtale` (`A_fet`, the full subcategory
of `Under A`); prove `Almost.Algebra.IsEtale.baseChange` and `Almost.Algebra.IsEtale.comp`
(stability of flat, unramified, étale, weakly étale and finite étale morphisms under base change
and composition, *etale-morphisms-stability*),
`Almost.Algebra.IsFiniteEtale.almostFiniteProjective` (by *almost-finite-projective-iff*, P0.11) and
`Almost.Algebra.isFiniteEtale_toAlmost` (Mathlib finite étale `R → R'` gives finite étale
`R^a → R'^a`); the characterisations `Almost.Algebra.isUnramified_iff_exists_idempotent` and
`Almost.Algebra.isEtale_iff_isPerfectTraceForm` are P0.15's. *Needs:* P0.11; P0.10; P0.8;
*almost-finite-projective-iff* (P0.11);
Mathlib `Algebra.Etale`, `Algebra.FormallyUnramified`, `Module.Finite`.

**Checks.**

- `Almost.Algebra.IsFiniteEtale_test_quadratic` (computation) — for `K` the completion of
  `ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞})`, `p ≠ 2`, `L = K(√p)` (the odd-`p` `L` of P0.10):
  `IsFiniteEtale ((toAlmost _).map (algebraMap K° L°))` over
  `S = ofValuationRing K°` ([Bhatt] Example 4.3.2).
- `Almost.Algebra.IsFiniteEtale_test_idempotent_not_honest` (non-example) — in the same example the
  diagonal idempotent `e = (1/(2√p ⊗ 1))(1 ⊗ √p + √p ⊗ 1)` is an almost element of `L°a ⊗ L°a` but
  does not lie in `L° ⊗_{K°} L°` (only `p^{1/p^n}e` does, for every `n`): a definition requiring an
  honest idempotent of `B_* ⊗_{A_*} B_*` would reject `L°a/K°a`.
- `Almost.Algebra.finiteEtale_test_classical` (compatibility) — for `S = classical V` and a
  `V`-algebra map `R → R'`: `IsFiniteEtale ((toAlmost S).map f) ↔ Algebra.Etale R R' ∧ Module.Finite R R'` (Mathlib).
- `Almost.Algebra.IsFiniteEtale_test_trivial` (degenerate) — `𝟙 A`, `A → 0` and the diagonal
  `A → A × A` are finite étale.

- `algebraPredicates_test_identity` — every identity map is faithfully flat, almost projective, almost finite, weakly étale, and finite étale.
- `algebraPredicates_test_zero` — a map to the zero algebra has all these properties except faithful flatness, which holds exactly when the source is zero.
- `algebraPredicates_test_product` — the diagonal `V^a → (V × V)^a` has all these properties.
- `algebraPredicates_test_dual_numbers` — the classical map `ℚ → ℚ[ε]/ε²` is faithfully flat, finite free, and almost projective, but neither weakly unramified nor unramified nor finite étale.

- `finiteEtale_test_classical` — for an arbitrary tower `V → R → T` of commutative rings, the almostified map in the classical setup is finite étale exactly when Mathlib's `Algebra.Etale R T` and `Module.Finite R T` hold.

### P0.15 the trace-form criterion

**Almost finite projective algebras are étale iff the trace form is perfect.**
(*trace-form-criterion*) Let `S` be a basic setup and `φ : A → B` a morphism of almost algebras with
`B` almost finite projective as an `A`-module. Then `φ` is étale iff the trace form
`t_{B/A} : B ⊗_A B → A` is a perfect pairing, i.e. `τ_{B/A} : B → B* = alHom_A(B, A)` is an
isomorphism (`Almost.Algebra.isEtale_iff_isPerfectTraceForm`; [GR] §4.1, Theorem 4.1.14, p. 75;
[Sch12] §4, Theorem 4.16, p. 21; [KL15] §5.5, Definition 5.5.8, p. 132, where the criterion is the
definition). In that case
`(1_B ⊗ τ_{B/A})(e_{B/A}) = ζ_B`, where `e_{B/A}` is the diagonal idempotent and
`ζ_B = ω_{B/A}⁻¹(1_B)` ([GR] §4.1, Remark 4.1.17, p. 76). In particular, for `B` almost finitely
presented, `φ` is finite étale iff `B` is flat over `A` and `t_{B/A}` is perfect. For `L°a/K°a`
(`K = ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞})^`, `p ≠ 2`, `L = K(√p)`) the trace form is perfect on the almost level (the discriminants `4p^{1/p^n}` of the
approximations `R_n` tend to a unit up to `m`); in the classical setup with `B` finite free this is
the criterion "finite free étale iff the discriminant is a unit". The trace uses P0.12's internal
realization of PivotalSpherical §Layer 2. *Needs:* P0.12; P0.14.

`Almost.Algebra.diagonalIdempotent_trace` states the identity on the relative module
`P = Almost.Algebra.relativeModule S φ`. The element `e : A → P ⊗_A P` is specified by
`μ(e) = 1` and `(b ⊗ 1)e = (1 ⊗ b)e`, expressed as equality of morphisms
`P → P ⊗_A P`; these conditions characterize the diagonal idempotent.
For `P` almost finite projective, the conclusion is
`e ≫ (1 ⊗ traceFormDual) = ζ_B`, with `ζ_B` explicitly the internal-Hom representative of
`1_P` followed by `dualTensorHomIso.inv` ([GR] Remark 4.1.17, p. 76).
`Almost.Algebra.isFiniteEtale_iff_flat_perfectTraceForm` assumes almost finite presentation of
`P` and states finite étaleness iff there is a flatness proof for which the trace pairing is
perfect. Flatness and presentation supply the almost finite projectivity needed to define that
trace ([GR] Proposition 2.4.18, p. 26, and Theorem 4.1.14, p. 75).

**Checks.**

- `Almost.Algebra.traceForm_test_product` (computation) — `B = A × A` over `A`: the diagonal
  idempotent is `e = (1,0) ⊗ (1,0) + (0,1) ⊗ (0,1)`, `μ(e) = 1`, and `t_{B/A}` has matrix `[[1, 0], [0, 1]]`, so both sides of the criterion hold.
- `Almost.Algebra.traceForm_test_dual_numbers` (non-example) — for a nonzero almost algebra `A`,
  `B = A[ε]/(ε²)` is finite free,
  `t_{B/A}` has matrix `[[2, 0], [0, 0]]` and is not perfect; correspondingly `I_{B/A}/I_{B/A}² = Ω_{B/A} = (B/(2ε))·dε ≠ 0`, so no idempotent `e` with `μ(e) = 1` and `I_{B/A}·e = 0` exists: both
  sides of the criterion fail. Over `ℚ`, `Ω` has dimension `1`; over `𝔽₂` it has dimension `2`.
- `Almost.Algebra.traceForm_test_product_diagonal` — in the split product algebra, the displayed
  tensor is idempotent, its multiplication is one, and it annihilates the diagonal ideal.
- `Almost.Algebra.traceForm_test_dual_numbers_quotient` — the differential module is
  `B/(2ε)`, with `dε` sent to one; the formula includes characteristic two.
- `Almost.Algebra.traceForm_test_dual_numbers_differentials` — after almostification,
  the module of differentials of `R[ε]/(ε²)` remains nonzero whenever `R^a` is nonzero.
- `Almost.Algebra.algebraTrace_test_zero` (degenerate) — `B = 0`: `t_{B/A}` is perfect on `0 ⊗ 0` and
  `A → 0` is étale, as `0 = A/(1)` is an idempotent quotient.

Unramified morphisms are characterised by a diagonal idempotent
(*unramified-idempotent-characterisation*, `Almost.Algebra.isUnramified_iff_exists_idempotent`):
for a basic setup `S` and `φ : A → B`, `φ` is unramified (`B` almost projective over
`B ⊗_A B`) iff there is an almost element
`e_{B/A} ∈ (B ⊗_A B)_*` with `e² = e`, `μ_{B/A}(e) = 1` and `x·e = 0` for every `x ∈ (I_{B/A})_*`;
`e` is unique, and `B ⊗_A B ≅ I_{B/A} × B` as `B ⊗_A B`-algebras (`I_{B/A}` with unit `1 − e`). More
generally, for an ideal `I` of an almost algebra `A`, `A/I` is almost projective over `A` iff `I` is
generated by an idempotent of `A_*`, which is then unique ([GR] §3.1, Proposition 3.1.4, p. 40; [GR]
§3.1, Remark 3.1.8, p. 40; [Sch12] §4, Definition 4.12(i), p. 20; [Bhatt] §4.3, Definition 4.3.1(2),
p. 26). In the classical setup with `B` finite étale over `A`, `ker μ` is a finitely generated
idempotent ideal generated by `1 − e` (Mathlib `Ideal.isIdempotentElem_iff_of_fg`, `IsIdempotentElem`).

`Almost.Algebra.diagonalIdempotent_unique` equates any two almost elements satisfying the
three displayed conditions. `Almost.Algebra.diagonalIdempotent_split` gives the product
isomorphism on almost elements: with `D = B ⊗_A B`, it is the additive and multiplicative
bijection `D_* → (diagonalIdeal S φ) × B_*`, sending `x` to `((1 − e)x, μ(x))`.
Its first factor has inherited multiplication and unit `1 − e`; its `D_*`-action is multiplication,
and the action on `B_*` is through `μ`. Thus almostification gives the asserted isomorphism of
`D`-algebras ([GR] Proposition 3.1.4, Remark 3.1.8 and Corollary 3.1.9, p. 40).

### P0.16 inverting an element of `m`

**Inverting an element of `m`: almost modules become honest modules over `V[1/ϖ]`.**
(*almost-inversion-and-completion*) Let `S = (V, m)` be a basic setup and `ϖ ∈ m` (so `ϖ` kills
almost zero modules; `ϖ` need not be a nonzerodivisor). The localisation `M ↦ M[1/ϖ] = V[1/ϖ] ⊗_V M`
is exact and kills almost zero modules (`ϖM = 0`), so it factors, uniquely up to unique
isomorphism, through an exact functor `Almost.invert ϖ : Almost.Module S → ModuleCat V[1/ϖ]` with
`invert(M^a) ≅ M[1/ϖ]` and `invert(M) ≅ M_*[1/ϖ] ≅ M_![1/ϖ]` ([GR] §5.2, proof of Corollary 5.2.15,
p. 110; [Bhatt] §4.1, Exercise 4.1.9, p. 22). Consequences: almost isomorphisms become isomorphisms
and almost exact complexes become exact after inverting `ϖ`; the setup `S.baseChange V[1/ϖ]` is
classical (`m·V[1/ϖ] = V[1/ϖ]`), so `Almost.Module` over it is `ModuleCat V[1/ϖ]`; `invert` is
symmetric monoidal and sends almost algebras to `V[1/ϖ]`-algebras ([Berkeley] Lecture 8, proof of
Proposition 8.2.8, p. 60: almost vanishing of `H^i(X, O⁺)` gives vanishing of
`H^i(X, O) = H^i(X, O⁺)[1/ϖ]`). The `ϖ`-adic completion side of this passage — completeness of `M`
versus `M_*`, and exactness of complete torsion-free complexes that are almost exact modulo `ϖ`,
with the `lim¹` term kept — is *almost-completeness-via-almost-elements* and
*almost-exactness-passes-to-completion* (P0.28). Define `Almost.invert` (the exact functor
`Almost.Module S ⥤ ModuleCat (Localization.Away ϖ)` for `ϖ ∈ S.ideal`); prove
`Almost.toAlmostCompInvertIso` (`toAlmost S ⋙ invert ϖ ≅` localisation at the powers of `ϖ`),
that `invert ϖ` preserves finite limits, `Almost.invertElementsIso`
(`(invert ϖ).obj M ≅ LocalizedModule (powers ϖ) M.elements`), that localising at the powers of `ϖ`
turns almost isomorphisms into isomorphisms and almost zero modules into zero modules,
`Almost.BasicSetup.baseChange_away_eq_classical`
(`S.baseChange (Localization.Away ϖ) = classical (Localization.Away ϖ)`), `Almost.invertMonoidal`
(with `Almost.Algebra.invert` on almost algebras) and that a complex of `V`-modules with almost
zero cohomology becomes exact after inverting `ϖ`. *Needs:* P0.5 for inversion;
P0.8's `Almost.Algebra`, `Almost.Algebra.ModuleCat` and algebra adjunction for
*change-of-basic-setup* (i); Mathlib
`SerreClassLocalization.essImage_whiskeringLeft`, `LocalizedModule`, `Localization.Away`.

On algebras, `Almost.Algebra.invert` sends `A` to `A_*[1/ε]`; on canonical numerators its map is induced by `elements.map`.

**Checks.**

- `Almost.Algebra.invert_zero`: inverting zero gives the zero algebra.
- `Almost.Algebra.invert_unit`: inverting a unit preserves the algebra of almost elements.
- `Almost.Algebra.invert_torsion`: an algebra killed by a power of the inverted scalar becomes zero.

Two supporting results. Base change of a basic setup along a ring map `V → W`
(*basic-setup-base-change*): for a basic setup `S = (V, m)` and any ring homomorphism `V → W`,
`S_W := (W, mW)` is a basic setup: `(mW)·(mW) = mW`, and the natural map `W ⊗_V m̃ → (mW) ⊗_W (mW)`
is an isomorphism, so `(mW)~` is `W`-flat; flatness of `m` alone does not pass to `mW`, which is why
the setup requires `m̃`, not `m`, to be flat ([GR] §2.1, Remark 2.1.4(ii), p. 8). For `V → V[1/ϖ]`
with `ϖ ∈ m`, `S_W` is the classical setup of `V[1/ϖ]`; for `V → V/I`, `S_{V/I} = (V/I, (m + I)/I)`,
and the base change of a root setup is the root setup of the images of the roots (Mathlib
`Module.Flat.baseChange`, `Ideal.map`). Change of basic setup (*change-of-basic-setup*): with
`S_W = (W, mW)` as above, (i) restriction of scalars gives a functor from `Almost.Module S_W` to
modules over the almost `V`-algebra `W^a` in `Almost.Module S`, and it is an equivalence with
quasi-inverse `M ↦ (M_*)^a`; it commutes with `(−)_*` and `(−)_!`, and the analogous statement holds
for almost algebras; (ii) if `V → W` is an almost isomorphism of `V`-modules (kernel and cokernel
killed by `m`), then `W^a ≅ V^a` as almost `V`-algebras and restriction of scalars
`Almost.Module S_W → Almost.Module S` is an equivalence ([GR] §2.2, Remark 2.2.12, p. 14; [Berkeley]
Lecture 7, §7.4, after Definition 7.4.3, p. 53). The case `R⁺ ⊆ R°` (`R°/R⁺` almost zero, [ECD]
Example 3.22(ii)) is the comparison `R°a-mod ≃ R⁺a-mod` stated in [ECD] after Definition 3.23,
proved in layer P1 from this lemma; for `W = V/I`, (i) identifies almost `V/I`-modules with almost
`V`-modules killed by `I` (Mathlib `ModuleCat.restrictScalars`).

**Checks.**

- Computation: for `S = ofValuationRing K°` and `ϖ ∈ K°°` nonzero:
  `(invert ϖ).obj ((toAlmost S).obj (K° ⧸ ϖ)) ≅ 0` and `(invert ϖ).obj ((toAlmost S).obj K°) ≅ K`.
- Degenerate: `0 ∈ S.ideal` always, and `invert 0` lands in
  modules over the zero ring `V[1/0] = 0`: every object goes to `0`, every statement "after
  inverting `0`" is vacuous; the localisation still detects the part of a module on which `ϖ` is invertible,
  even when the module also has `ϖ`-torsion.
- Degenerate: if `ϖ` is a unit of `V` (then `S.ideal = ⊤` as
  `ϖ ∈ S.ideal`), `invert ϖ ≅ Almost.Module.elements` composed with the identification
  `V[1/ϖ] = V`.
- Non-example: `invert ϖ` is not faithful: for
  `S = ofValuationRing K°` and `0 ≠ ϖ ∈ K°°`, the nonzero almost module `(K°/ϖ)^a` is sent to `0` ([Bhatt] Exercise
  4.1.9); almost statements are strictly finer than statements after inverting `ϖ`.
- Compatibility: `toAlmost S ⋙ invert ϖ ≅` the Mathlib localisation
  functor `M ↦ LocalizedModule (Submonoid.powers ϖ) M`, as functors
  `ModuleCat V ⥤ ModuleCat (Localization.Away ϖ)`.

- `invert_functor_test_zero` — the actual inversion functor at zero sends every almost module to zero.
- `invert_functor_test_quotient` — inversion at `ε ∈ m` kills `(V/(ε))^a`.
- `invert_functor_test_ring` — it sends `V^a` to the free rank-one module over `V[1/ε]`.

Lean: `BasicSetup.baseChange` with `isIdempotentElem_map` and `flat_tilde_map`
(*basic-setup-base-change*), and `BasicSetup.baseChange_away_eq_classical`. The functor
`Almost.invert` and *change-of-basic-setup* are specified in this README only.

### P0.17 comparison with Mathlib's finite étale algebras

**Comparison of finite étale almost algebras with Mathlib's finite étale algebras.**
(*finite-etale-localizes*) Let `S = (V, m)` be a basic setup and `R → R'` a map of commutative
`V`-algebras. (i) If `R'` is finite étale over `R` in Mathlib's sense (`Algebra.Etale R R'` and
`Module.Finite R R'`), then `R^a → R'^a` is finite étale in the almost sense ([Bhatt] §4.3,
Construction 4.3.3, p. 26: a finite étale algebra is a direct summand of a free module via the
diagonal idempotent and the trace). (ii) In the classical setup (`m = V`) the converse holds, so
`A_fet` for `A = R^a` is equivalent to Mathlib's category of finite étale `R`-algebras. (iii) For
`ϖ ∈ m`, if `R'^a` is finite étale over `R^a` then `R'[1/ϖ]` is finite étale over `R[1/ϖ]` in
Mathlib's sense (inverting `ϖ` turns almost statements into honest ones, P0.16). (iv) Gabber–Ramero's
étale morphisms in the classical setup are exactly the absolutely flat (weakly étale) maps whose
diagonal is almost projective; they need not be of finite presentation, and a classical étale map in
EGA's sense is étale in their sense ([GR] §3.4, (3.4.44), p. 64, which states the comparison in the
classical limit `m = V`; [GR] §3.1, Remark 3.1.3(i), p. 39; for a general basic setup, (i) follows because a finite étale `R'` is finite projective
over `R` and carries the diagonal idempotent, so `R'^a` is almost finite projective over `R^a` by
[GR] (2.4.8) and unramified by *unramified-idempotent-characterisation*; (iii) because finite étale
morphisms are stable under the base change `R^a → R[1/ϖ]^a` (*etale-morphisms-stability*) and
`S.baseChange V[1/ϖ]` is classical, so by *change-of-basic-setup* the base-changed morphism is the
honest `R[1/ϖ] → R'[1/ϖ]` in the classical setup, where (ii) applies). For `K` a perfectoid field
and `L/K` finite separable,
`L°a` is finite étale over `K°a` while `L°` need not be finite étale over `K°` in Mathlib's sense (it
is not finitely presented in general; for instance the odd-`p` `L°` of P0.10 need not be finitely
presented over `K°`), so (i) is strictly weaker than the almost statement; for
`R → R' = R × R` the diagonal idempotent is `(1,0) ⊗ (1,0) + (0,1) ⊗ (0,1)`. *Needs:* P0.14; P0.11;
P0.16; Mathlib `Algebra.Etale`, `Module.Finite`, `Ideal.isIdempotentElem_iff_of_fg`,
`KaehlerDifferential`.

### P0.18 almost Kähler differentials

**Almost Kähler differentials `Ω_{B/A}` and almost derivations.** (*almost-differentials*) Let `S` be
a basic setup and `A → B` a morphism of almost algebras, `I_{B/A} = ker(μ_{B/A} : B ⊗_A B → B)`.
The module of almost differentials is the `B`-module `Ω_{B/A} := I_{B/A}/I_{B/A}²`, with the
`A`-derivation `δ : B → Ω_{B/A}`, `b ↦ 1 ⊗ b − b ⊗ 1` on almost elements ([GR] §2.5, Definition
2.5.22(ii), p. 33). For a `B`-module `M`, an `A`-derivation `B → M` is an `A`-linear `∂` with
`∂(b₁b₂) = b₁∂(b₂) + b₂∂(b₁)` on almost elements; they form a `V`-module `Der_A(B, M)`, and
`f ↦ f ∘ δ` is an isomorphism `Hom_B(Ω_{B/A}, M) ≅ Der_A(B, M)` ([GR] §2.5, (2.5.23), p. 33).
Properties: `Ω_{C⊗_A B/C} ≅ C ⊗_A Ω_{B/A}`; for `A → B → C` an exact sequence
`C ⊗_B Ω_{B/A} → Ω_{C/A} → Ω_{C/B} → 0`; for `C = B/I` an exact sequence
`I/I² → C ⊗_B Ω_{B/A} → Ω_{C/A} → 0` ([GR] §2.5, Proposition 2.5.25(i)-(ii), p. 33); `Ω` commutes
with colimits; `(Ω_{B/A})_! ≅ Ω_{B!!/A!!}` ([GR] §2.5, Lemma 2.5.28, p. 34); for `V`-algebras
`R → R'`, `Ω_{R'^a/R^a} ≅ (Ω_{R'/R})^a` (Mathlib `KaehlerDifferential`). Define
`Almost.Algebra.kaehlerDifferential` (`Ω_{B/A}` as a `B`-module),
`Almost.Algebra.kaehlerDifferentialD` (the universal derivation `δ`) and `Almost.Algebra.Derivation`
(`A`-derivations `B ⟶ M`, a `V`-module); prove `Almost.Algebra.kaehlerDifferential.liftEquiv`
(`(Ω_{B/A} ⟶ M) ≃ₗ[V] Derivation A B M`), `Almost.Algebra.kaehlerDifferential.baseChangeIso`,
`Almost.Algebra.kaehlerDifferential.exact_seq` (the two exact sequences),
`Almost.Algebra.kaehlerDifferential.shriekIso` (`(Ω_{B/A})_! ≅ Ω_{B!!/A!!}`),
`Almost.Algebra.kaehlerDifferential_toAlmost` (`Ω_{R'^a/R^a} ≅ (KaehlerDifferential R R')^a`) and
`Almost.Algebra.kaehlerDifferential_eq_zero_of_isUnramified` (`φ` unramified `⇒ Ω_{B/A} = 0`, since
the diagonal idempotent `e` satisfies `1 − e ∈ I_{B/A}` and `x = x(1 − e)` for every almost
element `x ∈ I_{B/A}`, giving `I_{B/A} = I_{B/A}²`; [GR] Proposition 3.1.4, p. 40, and
Definition 2.5.22(ii), p. 33). *Needs:* P0.8; Mathlib `KaehlerDifferential`, `Derivation`.

**Checks.**

- `Almost.Algebra.kaehler_test_polynomial` (computation) — for `A` an almost algebra and
  `B = (A_*[X])^a`: `Ω_{B/A} ≅ B`, generated by `δX`.
- `Almost.Algebra.kaehler_almost_test_identity`, `Almost.Algebra.kaehler_almost_test_quotient` (degenerate) — `Ω_{A/A} = 0` and, for an ideal `I`,
  `Ω_{(A/I)/A} = 0`.
- `Almost.Algebra.kaehler_test_mathlib` (compatibility) — for `V`-algebras `R → R'`:
  `Ω_{R'^a/R^a} ≅ (toAlmost _).obj (KaehlerDifferential R R')` as `R'^a`-modules, compatible with the
  derivations.
- `Almost.Algebra.kaehler_test_not_elements` (comparison of representatives) — the
  unital differential construction uses `B_*` or `B_!!`; `B_!` is a non-unital algebra.
  The comparison `kaehlerDifferential.shriekIso` identifies `Ω_{B!!/A!!}` with
  `(Ω_{B/A})_!` ([GR] Lemma 2.5.28, p. 34), retaining the scalar extension from `V`.

- `differentials_test_sign` — over `ℤ[X]`, the convention `δb = 1 ⊗ b − b ⊗ 1`
  agrees with Mathlib: under its polynomial differential equivalence, `δ(X² + X) = 2X + 1`.
  Reversing the convention would give `−2X − 1`.

`Almost.Algebra.kaehlerDifferential` is an almost module over `B_*`, for the base-changed setup.
`kaehlerDifferentialD` is the ordinary universal derivation followed by the unit map to almost elements.

- `kaehler_almost_test_identity` — both the differential module and derivation of the identity are zero.
- `kaehler_almost_test_quotient` — both vanish for `A → A/I`, including the zero and unit ideals.
- `kaehler_almost_test_polynomial` — for classical `ℚ → ℚ[X]`, the module and derivation are nonzero.
- `kaehler_almost_test_leibniz` — on almost elements, `d(xy) = x·dy + y·dx`.

- `differentials_test_char_two` — ordinary differentials of dual numbers have dimension one over `ℚ`
  and dimension two in characteristic two.

**Checks for `Almost.Algebra.Derivation`.** `Derivation_identity` gives only the zero derivation for an identity map; `Derivation_zero` does so for zero coefficients; `Derivation_polynomial` gives a nonzero derivation for the classical rational polynomial algebra, detected by its value on `X`. These use [GR] Proposition 2.5.25.

The ordinary module `Almost.Module.homModule` has scalar multiplication
`(a • f)(x) = a • f(x)`. Its Checks are `homModule_zero` (zero source),
`homModule_classical_one` (endomorphisms of the rank-one classical module), and
`homModule_classical_two` (the two-by-two matrix module).

### P0.19 the cotangent complex of a ring map, consumed

**The cotangent complex of a ring map and its deformation theory, consumed.**
(*cotangent-complex-of-ring-map*) Ownership: the ordinary cotangent complex (simplicial
resolutions, [Stacks] Tag 08PL) and its square-zero obstruction class belong to
DerivedModuleAlgebra §§0.4 and 0.25, consistently with SchemeAndStackFoundations §4.6; Mathlib's
`Algebra.Extension.cotangentComplex` and `Algebra.H1Cotangent` cover only the two lowest degrees.
This roadmap consumes that carrier and owns only the almost construction of P0.20. What follows is
the contract that P0.20–P0.24 need of the consumed carrier, with its Checks; the names
`CotangentComplex` and its API below stand for the corresponding declarations of that roadmap. For a map of commutative rings `R → S`, the cotangent complex
`L_{S/R} ∈ D(S)` is the complex of Kähler differentials of a simplicial resolution of `S` by
polynomial `R`-algebras, tensored termwise with `S` along the augmentation
([Stacks] Tag [08PL](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08PL), Definitions 92.3.1–92.3.2), together
with: (a) `H_0(L_{S/R}) ≅ Ω_{S/R}`, compatibly with Mathlib's `KaehlerDifferential`, and `H_1`
compatible with the truncation `Algebra.Extension.Cotangent` and with `Algebra.H1Cotangent`
(Mathlib has the degree `≤ 1` truncation only, no simplicial `L_{S/R}`); (b) the transitivity
triangle `S ⊗_T^L L_{T/R} → L_{S/R} → L_{S/T}` for `R → T → S` ([Stacks] Tag 08QX), whose
`H_1`/`H_0` part is Mathlib's Jacobi–Zariski sequence `Algebra.Generators.Cotangent.exact`; (c) base change
`L_{S'/R'} ≃ S' ⊗_S^L L_{S/R}` for a Tor-independent square ([Stacks] Tag 08QQ); (d) commutation
with filtered colimits of rings ([Stacks] Tag 08S9); (e) `Ext^0_S(L_{S/R}, M) ≅ Der_R(S, M)` and
`Ext^1_S(L_{S/R}, M) ≅ Exal_R(S, M)`, the group of square-zero `R`-extensions of `S` by `M`
([Stacks] Tag [08S3](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08S3), Lemma 91.2.3,
and Tag [08RB](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08RB) for the truncation comparison); (f) for a flat `R`-algebra `S` and a square-zero extension
`R' → R` with kernel `J`, the obstruction to a flat deformation of `S` over `R'` lies in
`Ext^2_S(L_{S/R}, S ⊗_R J)`, deformations form a torsor under `Ext^1` and automorphisms are `Ext^0`
([Stacks] Tag 08SP), and for a square-zero extension `T′ → T` of `R`-algebras with kernel `J`,
the obstruction to lifting an `R`-map `S → T` to `T′` lies in `Ext^1_S(L_{S/R}, J)`,
where `J` is an `S`-module through `S → T`, with lifts a torsor under `Ext^0`
([Stacks] Tag [08S3](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08S3), Lemma 91.2.1); (g) for a map of simplicial rings `R_• → S_•`, the diagonal complex `L^Δ` with the
spectral sequence `H_j(L_{S_i/R_i}) ⇒ H_{i+j}(L^Δ)`, and `L_{S/R} ≃ L^Δ` for simplicial resolutions
([Illusie] Chapter II, 1.2.6.2). For the free simplicial resolution `S_• → S`
and `R_• = S_• ×_S R` used to compare cotangent complexes of almost-isomorphic algebras,
[GR] Proposition 8.1.7, proof, printed pp. 220–221, gives precisely
`E¹_{i,j} = H_j(L_{S_i/R_i}) ⇒ H_{i+j}(L^Δ)` in homological degrees.
The consumed carrier provides `CotangentComplex` with `CotangentComplex.homologyZeroIso`
(`H_0(L_{S/R}) ≅ Ω_{S/R}`), `CotangentComplex.transitivityTriangle`,
`CotangentComplex.baseChange` under the Tor-independence in (c), `CotangentComplex.filteredColimit`
for (d), `CotangentComplex.extZero` and `CotangentComplex.extOne` for (e),
`CotangentComplex.flatDeformation` and `CotangentComplex.liftMorphism` with the hypotheses in (f),
and `CotangentComplex.diagonalComparison` for (g). Grading is homological: `H_i(L)` is `H^{−i}(L)` in
the cohomological indexing of [Stacks]; `M[n]` places `M` in homological degree `n`, so `M[1]` places
`M` in homological degree one. The obstruction groups of P0.21–P0.23 are `Ext` groups of the full
complex, never of a two-term truncation. Tensor products of complexes in the derived category
mean derived tensor products. *Needs:* DerivedModuleAlgebra §§0.1–0.2, 0.4–0.11, 0.13 and 0.25;
Mathlib
`KaehlerDifferential`, `Algebra.Extension.Cotangent`, `Algebra.H1Cotangent`,
`Algebra.Generators.Cotangent.exact`, `CategoryTheory.SimplicialObject`.

**Checks.**

- `cotangentComplex_polynomial` (computation) — for `S = R[X_i]` the complex is `Ω_{S/R}` in degree
  `0` (free on the `dX_i`).
- `cotangentComplex_perfect_charP` (computation) — for a perfect `𝔽_p`-algebra `S`,
  `L_{S/𝔽_p} ≃ 0` (Frobenius is an isomorphism, so the relative Frobenius criterion applies).
- `cotangentComplex_not_concentrated_in_degree_zero` (non-example) — for `S = R/(f)` with `f` a
  nonzerodivisor and `(f) ≠ R`, `L_{S/R} ≃ (f)/(f²)[1] ≠ 0` ([Stacks] Tag 08SJ); for instance
  `ℤ → ℤ/2` has `L ≃ ℤ/2[1]`: a definition returning only `Ω_{S/R} = 0` is wrong.
- `cotangentComplex_identity_and_quotient` (degenerate) — `L_{R/R} ≃ 0` (the resolution is
  constant); for a surjection `R → R/I`, `H_0 = Ω_{(R/I)/R} = 0` and `H_1 = I/I²` (Mathlib
  `Algebra.H1Cotangent`), so `H_1(L_{(R/I)/R}) = 0` iff `I = I²`; `L_{(R/I)/R} ≃ 0` needs in
  addition `H_i = 0` for `i ≥ 2` (automatic when `I` is generated by an idempotent); for `I = R`
  the target is the zero ring and `L_{0/R} = 0`. For an arbitrary ideal `I`, only `H_0 = 0` and
  `H_1 = I/I²` hold in general; the formula `(f)/(f²)[1]` needs `f` to be a nonzerodivisor.
- `cotangentComplex_dual_numbers` (negative control for the nonzerodivisor hypothesis) — for
  `R = k[ε]/(ε²)` and the zero-divisor `f = ε`, the hypersurface presentation `R = k[x]/(x²)` gives
  `k ⊗ᴸ_R L_{R/k} ≃ [k —0→ k] ≃ k[0] ⊕ k[1]`, and the transitivity triangle of `k → R → k` gives
  `L_{k/R} ≃ k[1] ⊕ k[2]`, whose `H_2 = k` is missing from `(ε)/(ε²)[1] = k[1]`.

- `cotangent_test_unit_ideal` — for `I = V`, both `H₁(L_{(V/I)/V})` and `Ω_{(V/I)/V}` are zero,
  which is the negative control for the proper-ideal hypothesis above.

- `cotangent_model_test_identity` — the full derived object for `R → R` and every homology module of its model are zero.
- `cotangent_model_test_polynomial` — for `R → R[X]`, positive homology vanishes and `H₀ ≅ R[X]`.
- `cotangent_model_test_regular_quotient` — for `ℤ → ℤ/2`, `H₀ = 0` but `H₁ ≅ ℤ/2 ≠ 0`, excluding the differential-only construction.
- `cotangent_model_test_zero_target` — the full derived object for `R → R/(1)` is zero.
- `cotangent_model_test_two_faces` — the degree-one differential on `x + y` is
  `d₀x − d₁x + d₀y − d₁y`; the degreewise faces have no built-in sign.
- `cotangent_model_test_shift` — homological degrees `0, 1, 2` are placed in cohomological degrees `0, −1, −2`.
- For the standard resolution of `ℤ → ℤ/2`, `P₀ = ℤ[ℤ/2]` is additively torsion-free.
  Every additive map `ℤ/2 → P₀` is zero, so no inverse in simplicial abelian groups can
  induce the identity on `H₀ = ℤ/2`. The set-level contraction supplies no additive contraction.

`CotangentComplex.PolynomialResolution` is the carrier
`Algebra.CotangentComplex.PolynomialResolution` of DerivedModuleAlgebra §0.1: an
augmented simplicial commutative `R`-algebra with polynomial presentations in each degree
and augmentation to `T` a trivial Kan fibration of underlying simplicial sets. The supplied
standard resolution has an extra degeneracy after forgetting to sets. Its augmentation is
therefore a homotopy equivalence of simplicial sets, induces a quasi-isomorphism on the
associated complexes of abelian groups, and is degreewise surjective; the last two properties
imply that it is a trivial Kan fibration of underlying simplicial sets
([Stacks, Lemma 92.4.2, first proof](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08PT),
[Lemma 14.31.9](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08P2) and
[Lemma 14.31.8](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08P1)). The supplier's
`Algebra.CotangentComplex.PolynomialResolution.toQuasiIso` supplies the quasi-isomorphism,
and `Algebra.CotangentComplex.PolynomialResolution.comparison` uses the trivial-Kan-fibration
criterion of [Stacks, Lemma 92.4.1](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08PS).
Its `differentials` have terms
`T ⊗_{P_n} Ω_{P_n/R}`; `termIso` and `face_tmul` pin this identification and its face maps.
`complex` is Mathlib's alternating face complex. `model` uses a chosen free resolution,
and `object` extends it to nonpositive cohomological degrees before applying `DerivedCategory.Q`.
`resolutionIso` states independence of the resolution; `homologyZeroIso` and `homologyOneIso`
compare with Mathlib's differentials and first cotangent homology.

- `cotangent_test_quotient` — for `R → R/I`, Mathlib's `H1Cotangent` is zero exactly when `I² = I`;
  this is a test of first homology, not vanishing of the full complex.

DerivedModuleAlgebra §0.5 supplies `CotangentComplex.SquareZeroExtension`, using Mathlib's algebra extension,
with an injective additive kernel map whose image is the kernel, whose scalar action
is induced by the quotient, and whose products vanish. `extensionSetoid` identifies
extensions by algebra isomorphisms preserving the quotient and the kernel map;
`Exal` is its quotient. `CotangentComplex.extensionClass` assigns the specified
extension its class, and `CotangentComplex.extOne` asserts that this particular
map is bijective and sends precisely the split extensions to zero (DerivedModuleAlgebra §0.6).
`CotangentComplex.extensionClass_mk` identifies it with
`CotangentComplex.morphismObstruction` for the identity map. For an arbitrary
`R`-algebra map `f : T → B`, `morphismObstruction` is the class of the pullback
of the specified extension of `B`; `CotangentComplex.liftMorphism` tests the
vanishing of this class. Its normalization is given by
`CotangentComplex.morphismObstruction_cocycle`: lift the degree-zero polynomial
resolution to the extension, subtract its two lifted faces in the order
`d₀ − d₁`, and use the given kernel identification. The resulting degree-one
cocycle represents the class for every such lift. This is the simplicial form
of [Stacks, Remark 91.2.4](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08S3), with the
full-complex comparison of [Stacks, Lemma 92.11.3](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08RB).

**Checks.** For each of `morphismObstruction` and `extensionClass`, `_zero`
uses the zero coefficient module, `_split` uses an actual algebra lift or
section, and `_nonsplit` uses `ℤ/9 → ℤ/3` and gives a nonzero class.

**Checks.** For each of `SquareZeroExtension`, `extensionSetoid` and `Exal`, the
`_zero` Check has zero kernel and a bijective quotient; `_dual` uses the nonzero
square-zero element of rational dual numbers, whose extension class is zero;
`_nonsplit` uses `ℤ/4 → ℤ/2`, which has no ring section and a nonzero class.
These are the split and nonsplit cases of [Stacks] Tag 08S3.

DerivedModuleAlgebra §§0.4, 0.9 and 0.11 supply the following functorial models.
The functor `CotangentComplex.arrowFunctor` retains every homological degree and the
maps induced by commutative squares of rings. `arrowResolution` is the standard
polynomial resolution, `resolutionRings` forgets its base-algebra structure, and
`resolutionRingMap` commutes with the augmentation and base scalars.
`arrowModelMap_tmul` fixes its map on generators: `t ⊗ dx` goes to
`b(t) ⊗ d(a(x))`. Thus `filteredColimit` compares the canonical diagram of
complexes, with both source and target rings varying, as in [Stacks] Tag 08S9.
`diagonalModel` is the total complex of the alternating chains of this simplicial
complex. `diagonalComparison` has differential bidegree `(-r,r-1)` and an
exhaustive finite filtration on each homology group; its resolution comparison
uses extra degeneracies on underlying sets ([Illusie] II 1.2.6.2).

**Checks.** `resolutionRingMap_identity`, `resolutionRingMap_composition`, and
`resolutionRingMap_zero_target` fix functoriality and the zero-target augmentation.
For `arrowResolution`, `resolutionRings`, `arrowModel`, `arrowModelMap`, and
`arrowFunctor`, the `_identity`, `_polynomial`, and `_regular_quotient` Checks
respectively give zero homology, zero positive homology, and nonzero first
homology for `ℤ → ℤ/2`. `diagonalModel_constant`, `diagonalModel_identity`, and
`diagonalModel_regular_quotient` distinguish totalization from taking only
ordinary differentials.

The chain maps `CotangentComplex.transitivityFirst` and
`CotangentComplex.transitivitySecond` of DerivedModuleAlgebra §0.8 are induced by the squares
`(A → B) → (A → C)` and `(A → C) → (B → C)`, respectively.
`CotangentComplex.transitivityFirst_tmul` sends `c ⊗ x` to `c` times the
image of `x` under `arrowModelMap`; `CotangentComplex.transitivitySecond_apply`
is the same functorial map with the target ring fixed. Their images under
`DerivedCategory.Q` are the first two arrows in `transitivityTriangle`;
only the connecting arrow is existentially quantified. This fixes the maps
in the transitivity sequence ([Stacks] Tag 08QX; [GR] Theorem 2.5.32, p. 35).

**Checks.** `transitivityFirst_identity` is invertible when the second ring map
is the identity; `transitivityFirst_zero_source` vanishes in the derived
category when the first ring map is the identity;
`transitivityFirst_polynomial` is nonzero for `ℚ → ℚ[X] → ℚ[X]`.
`transitivitySecond_identity` is the identity when `A = B`;
`transitivitySecond_zero_target` vanishes when `B = C`;
`transitivitySecond_regular_quotient` is nonzero on the degree-one cotangent
homology of `ℤ → ℤ → ℤ/3`.

### P0.20 the almost cotangent complex

**The almost cotangent complex `L_{B/A}`.** (*almost-cotangent-complex*) Let `S` be a basic setup
(`m̃` flat is used in [GR] Proposition 2.5.34 and Theorem 2.5.35) and `A → B` a morphism of almost
algebras. Put `Ã := V^a × A` and `B̃ := V^a × B` (exact almost algebras). The almost cotangent
complex is `L_{B/A} := B_!! ⊗_{B̃_!!} L_{B̃_!!/Ã_!!}`, an object of the derived category of
`B_!!`-modules, where `L_{−/−}` is the cotangent complex of the ring map `Ã_!! → B̃_!!` (simplicial
polynomial resolution, the consumed carrier of P0.19, whose `Ext` groups are those of the full
complex); this almost construction is the one this roadmap owns. Its almostification `L^a_{B/A} ∈ D(B-Mod)` is the object used in
deformation theory ([GR] §2.5, Definition 2.5.20, p. 32; [Sch12] §5, before Remark 5.15, p. 25).
Properties: `H_0(L^a_{B/A}) ≅ Ω_{B/A}`; `Ext^i_{B!!}(L_{B/A}, M_!) ≅ Ext^i_B(L^a_{B/A}, M)` ([GR]
(3.2.8)); `Ext⁰ ≅ Der_A(B, M)` ([GR] 2.5.29) and `Ext¹ ≅ Exal_A(B, M)` (P0.21); the transitivity
triangle *cotangent-transitivity* (P0.22); Tor-independent base change
*cotangent-flat-base-change*; `L_{colim B_λ/colim A_λ} ≅ colim L_{B_λ/A_λ}` for filtered systems
([GR] §2.5, Proposition 2.5.33, p. 35); vanishing for weakly étale maps
*cotangent-vanishing-weakly-etale* (P0.24); and for `V`-algebras `R → S`,
`L^a_{S^a/R^a} ≅ (L_{S/R})^a` by *almost-cotangent-comparison-classical*, so the almost cotangent
complex depends only on `R^a → S^a` ([Sch12] §5). Define `Almost.cotangentComplex` (`L_{B/A}` in
`DerivedCategory (ModuleCat B_!!)`) and `Almost.almostCotangentComplex` (`L^a_{B/A}` in
`DerivedCategory (B-Mod)`); prove the identification `H_0(L^a_{B/A}) ≅ Ω_{B/A}`, the comparison
`Ext^i_{B!!}(L_{B/A}, M_!) ≅ Ext^i_B(L^a_{B/A}, M)`, the identifications `Ext⁰ ≅ Der_A(B, M)` and
`Ext¹ ≅ Exal_A(B, M)`, the transitivity statement (the distinguished triangle
`C ⊗ L_{B/A} → L_{C/A} → L_{C/B} →`), Tor-independent base change, the colimit statement, the
comparison `L^a_{S^a/R^a} ≅ (L_{S/R})^a` with the almostified classical complex, and vanishing for
weakly étale maps (weakly étale, more generally Tor-trivial diagonal, `⇒ L_{B/A} ≃ 0`). *Needs:* P0.9; P0.18; P0.8; P0.19; Mathlib
`Algebra.Extension.cotangentComplex`, `Algebra.H1Cotangent`, `DerivedCategory`.

The named additive map `Almost.cotangentDerivationComparison` sends a degree-zero
class to its derivation. The identification `Ext⁰ ≅ Der_A(B, M)` above asserts bijectivity
of this map. For every basic setup, algebra map and coefficient module, its evaluation
formula applies `H⁰` to the class, transports along the identification
`H_0(L^a_{B/A}) ≅ Ω_{B/A}`, and evaluates on `Algebra.kaehlerDifferentialD`. It
commutes with every coefficient-module map, and a comparison statement
identifies its value with the underlying V-linear
`cotangentDerivation` of P0.22. These are the universal-derivation comparison of
[GR] (2.5.24), p. 33, and Proposition 2.5.29, p. 34.

`Almost.cotangentExtComparison` is the named additive map from ordinary Ext
with lower-shriek coefficients to almost Ext, in each integer degree.
The comparison `Ext^i_{B!!}(L_{B/A}, M_!) ≅ Ext^i_B(L^a_{B/A}, M)` above asserts its bijectivity.
Its formula is fixed as follows: apply Mathlib's
`mapDerivedCategory` to scalar extension from `B_!!` to `B_*` followed by
almostification, use the comparison with extension by zero in every
nonpositive degree, and use the scalar-extension counit and the inverse
lower-shriek unit at the coefficient module. The canonical shift and
single-object comparisons determine the degree convention.
It is compatible with coefficient maps. Sources: [GR] Proposition 2.5.42, p. 36, and (3.2.8), p. 41.

**Checks.** `cotangentDerivationComparison_zero` sends zero to zero;
`cotangentDerivationComparison_identity` vanishes for the identity algebra map;
`cotangentDerivationComparison_polynomial` realizes `d/dX` over `ℚ[X]` and
sends every polynomial `p` to `p′` on almost elements. Thus its values at
`1`, `X`, and `X²` are `0`, `1`, and `2X`, respectively.
`cotangentExtComparison_zero` sends zero to zero;
`cotangentExtComparison_identity` is zero in every degree for an identity
algebra map; `cotangentExtComparison_nonzero` preserves every nonzero class.

Two supporting results. The almost cotangent complex of `R^a → S^a` is the almostified classical one
(*almost-cotangent-comparison-classical*): for a basic setup `S` and a map `f : R → S` of
`V`-algebras, (i) if `f^a : R^a → S^a` is an isomorphism then `(L_{S/R})^a ≃ 0` in `D(S^a-Mod)`;
(ii) the natural map `L^a_{S^a/R^a} → (L_{S/R})^a` is an isomorphism in `D(S^a-Mod)`; hence the
almost cotangent complex of a morphism coming from `V`-algebras is computed by the cotangent complex
of P0.19 and depends only on `R^a → S^a` ([GR] §8.1, Proposition 8.1.7(i)-(ii), pp. 219–220; [Sch12]
§5, before Remark 5.15, p. 25). For `R = V` and `S = V × k` (`k = V/m`), `f^a` is an isomorphism and
`L_{S/V} ≅ 0 × L_{k/V}` has homology consisting of `k`-modules, hence almost zero, as (i) predicts.
Tor-independent base change (*cotangent-flat-base-change*): for `A → B` and `A → A'` morphisms of
almost algebras, `B' := B ⊗_A A'`, with `B ⊗^L_A A' → B'` an isomorphism (`Tor^A_i(B, A') = 0` for
`i > 0`; e.g. `B` or `A'` flat over `A`), the maps `B'_!! ⊗_{B!!} L_{B/A} → L_{B'/A'}` and
`(B'_!! ⊗_{B!!} L_{B/A}) ⊕ (B'_!! ⊗_{A'!!} L_{A'/A}) → L_{B'/A}` are quasi-isomorphisms ([GR] §2.5,
Theorem 2.5.35, p. 35, and Proposition 2.5.34, p. 35; cited by [Sch12] §5, proof of Theorem 5.10,
p. 26, as Theorem 2.5.36 in the book numbering). In that proof, for `A_n` flat over `(K°/ϖ^n)^a`
the square `(K°/ϖ^n)^a → (K°/ϖ^{n−1})^a`, `A_n → A_{n−1}` is Tor-independent, so
`L_{A_{n−1}/(K°/ϖ^{n−1})^a} ≅ A_{n−1} ⊗ L_{A_n/(K°/ϖ^n)^a}`.

**Checks.**

- Computation: for `B = (A_*[X])^a`:
  `H_0(L^a_{B/A}) ≅ B·δX` and `H_i(L^a_{B/A}) = 0` for `i > 0`.
- Degenerate: `L_{A/A} ≃ 0` for every almost algebra `A`
  (the identity of `Ã_!!`).
- Compatibility: for `S = classical V` and `V`-algebras
  `R → R'`: `L^a_{R'^a/R^a} ≅ L_{R'/R}` (the cotangent complex of P0.19), and `H_1` agrees with
  Mathlib's `Algebra.H1Cotangent R R'`.
- Non-example: defining `L_{B/A}` as the cotangent
  complex of `A_* → B_*` would be wrong: for `A_* → B_*` not of the form `Ã_!! → B̃_!!` the result is
  only almost quasi-isomorphic after almostification ([GR] Proposition 8.1.7), and for `B_*` the unit
  and the non-exactness of `B_!` intervene; the definition must pass through the exact algebras
  `V^a × A`, `V^a × B`.

The concrete `cotangentComplex_test_not_naive` uses `m = 0` over a nonzero
ring `V`: the unalmostified coefficient ring `B_!!` is nonzero (indeed `V`),
whereas `B_*` is zero. There is no ring isomorphism between them. This tests
the coefficient-ring distinction; both cotangent complexes of an identity map
still vanish.

The chain model `Almost.cotangentModel` applies ordinary scalar extension to the polynomial-resolution model for `Ã_!! → B̃_!!`, along `B̃_!! → B_!!`. `almostCotangentModel` then extends to `B_*` and almostifies in the setup `S.baseChange B_*`. Both derived objects use cohomological degrees `0, −1, −2, …`. The comparison `L^a_{S^a/R^a} ≅ (L_{S/R})^a` concerns the almostified complex; it does not identify the unalmostified complexes over `B_!!` and `B_*`.

- `exactification_test_classical` — in the classical setup the almost elements of the exactification of `R^a` are `V × R`.
- `exactification_test_zero` — exactifying a zero almost algebra gives the unit algebra, whose lower shriek-shriek is `V`.
- `exactification_test_unit` — exactifying the unit algebra gives `(V × V)^a`.
- `almostCotangent_test_identity` — both derived complexes vanish for an identity map.
- `almostCotangent_test_zero_setup` — both vanish for `m = 0`: the lower shriek-shriek algebras are all `V`, and their maps are identities.
- `almostCotangent_test_polynomial` — for every honest `V`-algebra `R`, the almostified polynomial map `R → R[X]` has degree-zero homology equal to the tensor unit over its target and no positive homology.
- `almostCotangent_test_classical_quotient` — for `ℤ → ℤ/2` in the classical setup, almost cotangent homology in degree zero is zero and degree one is nonzero.

The functor `cotangentBaseFunctor` retains the `V`-module structure of
`cotangentBaseModel`. Its `cotangentBaseMap` is specified on scalar-extended
polynomial differential generators. The colimit statement says that the
canonical map from the filtered colimit of these complexes is a
quasi-isomorphism ([GR] Proposition 2.5.33).

**Checks.** For `cotangentBaseModel` and `cotangentBaseFunctor`, `_identity`
has zero homology, `_classical` agrees with the ordinary cotangent complex, and
`_regular_quotient` detects nonzero first homology of `ℤ → ℤ/2`.
`cotangentBaseMap_identity`, `cotangentBaseMap_composition`, and
`cotangentBaseMap_zero` check identities, compositions, and that the identity of
the nonzero regular-quotient model is not the zero map.

The chain maps `Almost.cotangentTransitivityFirst` and
`Almost.cotangentTransitivitySecond` use these same two squares after
exactification and lower shriek-shriek. Their formulas on pure tensors are
those of `CotangentComplex.transitivityFirst_tmul` and
`CotangentComplex.transitivitySecond_apply` in P0.19, expressed through
`cotangentBaseMap`. The almost transitivity triangle fixes these first
two arrows and asserts existence only of the third ([GR] Theorem 2.5.32, p. 35).

**Checks.** `cotangentTransitivityFirst_identity` is invertible,
`cotangentTransitivityFirst_zero_source` is zero after passing to the derived
category, and `cotangentTransitivityFirst_polynomial` is nonzero for the
classical rational polynomial algebra. `cotangentTransitivitySecond_identity`
is invertible, `cotangentTransitivitySecond_zero_target` is zero in the derived
category, and `cotangentTransitivitySecond_regular_quotient` detects the
nonzero cotangent homology of the classical map `ℤ → ℤ/3`.

### P0.21 square-zero extensions and `Ext¹`

**Square-zero extensions of almost algebras are classified by `Ext¹` of the almost cotangent
complex.** (*almost-exal-ext-comparison*) Let `S` be a basic setup, `A → B` a morphism of almost
algebras and `M` a `B`-module; `A`-extensions of `B` by `M` are short exact sequences
`0 → M → E → B → 0` in `A-Mod` with `E` an `A`-algebra and `M` a square-zero ideal with its given
`B`-module structure ([GR] 2.5.2–2.5.7). (i) Almostification from ordinary `A_!!`-extensions
of `B_!!` by `M_*` to almost `A`-extensions of `B` by `M` is an equivalence of categories,
inducing the group isomorphism `Exal_{A!!}(B_!!, M_*) ≅ Exal_A(B, M)` on
isomorphism classes, functorial in all arguments ([GR] §2.5, Lemma 2.5.17(i)–(ii), p. 32). (ii) There are
natural isomorphisms `Ext⁰_{B!!}(L_{B/A}, M_!) ≅ Der_A(B, M)` ([GR] §2.5, Proposition 2.5.29, p. 34)
and `Exal_A(B, M) ≅ Ext¹_{B!!}(L_{B/A}, M_!) ≅ Ext¹_B(L^a_{B/A}, M)` ([GR] §2.5, Theorem 2.5.30,
p. 34; [GR] §3.2, (3.2.8), p. 41). (iii) For an epimorphism `A → B` with kernel `I`,
`Hom_B(I/I², M) ≅ Exal_A(B, M)` via pushout along `u : I/I² → M` of `0 → I/I² → A/I² → B → 0`. For
the trivial extension `B ⊕ M` the class is `0`; for `A → B = A/I` with `I² = 0` the extension `A`
itself corresponds to `1_I`; in [Sch12] Theorem 5.11 these groups classify deformations of
perfectoid `K°a/ϖ`-algebras.
*Needs:* P0.20; P0.18; P0.9.

`Almost.SquareZeroExtension` records the short exact sequence of underlying
almost modules, the algebra map from the base, and the quotient-compatible kernel
action. `Almost.extensionSetoid` fixes these maps under algebra isomorphisms,
and `Almost.Exal` is its quotient.

`CotangentComplex.extensionCategory` and `Almost.extensionCategory` give these
existing extension carriers their categories: an arrow is an algebra homomorphism
that fixes the base, quotient and specified kernel. In each namespace,
`extensionSetoid_iff_iso` identifies the existing relation with categorical
isomorphism ([GR] 2.5.4–2.5.7, p. 30). For every basic setup `S`, almost algebra
map `f : A → B` and `B`-module `M`, `Almost.ordinaryExtensions S f M` is the ordinary
extension category over `A_!!`, with quotient `B_!!` and kernel `M_*`, whose
`B_!!`-action is restricted along `B_!! → B_*`.
`Almost.extensionToAlmost` applies algebra and module almostification to each
term and each arrow, using `shriekShriekUnitIso` at the base and quotient and
`moduleEquiv_functor_forget` at the kernel. That `Almost.extensionToAlmost` is an
equivalence is the category-level assertion of [GR] 2.5.17(i), p. 32, for this specific functor;
in particular it preserves and recovers automorphisms.

In both namespaces `exalAddCommGroup` equips the existing quotient with Baer
addition. The theorem `CotangentComplex.exal_add_representative` characterizes
its sum by the fibre product modulo `(i_E(m), −i_F(m))`, with
`(i_E(m), i_F(n))` mapping to `i_G(m+n)`.
The almost representative statement gives the same construction on almost modules:
the two kernel inclusions `l,r` into the algebra fibre product have equal images
in the sum, and `0 → M →[l−r] E ×_B F → G → 0` is exact.
Both constructions fix the base and quotient maps ([GR] 2.5.5–2.5.7, p. 30).
An additive equivalence is derived from this equivalence of categories, with the image of every
representative equal to the class of its termwise almostification ([GR] 2.5.17(ii), p. 32); its
underlying class bijection is the isomorphism `Exal_{A!!}(B_!!, M_*) ≅ Exal_A(B, M)` of (i).

**Checks.** `CotangentComplex.extensionCategory_zero` and
`CotangentComplex.exalAddCommGroup_zero` give a unique arrow and zero sum when the
kernel is zero. Their `_classical` checks give only the identity automorphism
and the zero class for extensions of `ℚ` over itself.
`CotangentComplex.extensionCategory_polynomial` uses
`E = ℚ[X] ⊕ εℚ[X]`: the nonidentity automorphism sends `a+εb` to
`a+ε(b+a′)`, hence `X` to `X+ε`, while fixing the kernel and quotient.
`CotangentComplex.exalAddCommGroup_nonsplit` exhibits the nonzero order-two
class for `ℤ/4 → ℤ/2`.
For each of `Almost.ordinaryExtensions`, `Almost.extensionCategory`,
`Almost.extensionToAlmost`, and `Almost.exalAddCommGroup`, `_zero` checks the
zero kernel and `_classical` checks the rational base over itself. The first
three also have `_polynomial`: a nonidentity automorphism remains nonidentity
after almostification, although all extension classes of `ℚ[X]` by itself agree.
The `_nonsplit` Check of `Almost.exalAddCommGroup` gives the nonzero order-two class over `ℤ/2`.

**Checks.** Each carrier has `_zero` (zero kernel forces an invertible projection),
`_classical` (extensions of the rational base over itself split), and `_nonsplit`
(the classical `ℤ/4 → ℤ/2` class) examples. The zero-class characterization in
the identification `Ext¹ ≅ Exal_A(B, M)` of P0.20 uses an algebra section over the specified base,
as in [GR] Theorem 2.5.30.

The identification `Ext¹ ≅ Exal_A(B, M)` of P0.20 uses the named additive equivalence
`Almost.cotangentExtensionClass`, including its specified kernel identification.
It identifies addition with the Baer sum and kernel pushout with
postcomposition, and its almostification compatibility identifies the
class of each termwise almostified ordinary extension with the image of
`CotangentComplex.extensionClass` (the consumed ordinary classifier of P0.19). Its source map is induced by the projection
from exactified rings, with `t ⊗ x ↦ t·image(x)` in every degree; its target
map is the scalar-extension counit followed by the almost-elements counit.
This fixes the class itself, including its sign ([GR] Theorem 2.5.30,
p. 34, Lemma 2.5.17, p. 32, and (3.2.8), p. 41).

For a surjection of ordinary commutative rings `R → T`,
`CotangentComplex.conormalComparison` identifies `Ext¹(L_{T/R}, M)` with
`Hom_T(I/I², M)`, using Mathlib's conormal module.
`CotangentComplex.conormalComparison_extensionClass` specifies its value:
the image of `r mod I²` under the class of `E` is the unique `m` whose
kernel inclusion equals the base image of `r` in `E`.
For every commutative algebra map, `CotangentComplex.extensionClass_add`
asserts compatibility with Baer addition ([GR] Theorem 2.5.30, p. 34).
Together with this almostification compatibility, this is the conormal
normalization of the almost classifier ([GR] Lemma 3.2.1 and (3.2.2), p. 41).

**Checks.** `conormalComparison_zero` is the zero map;
`conormalComparison_identity` vanishes for `R → R`;
`conormalComparison_zmodNine` uses `ℤ/9 → ℤ/3`, with kernel generator sent
to `3 mod 9`. The class takes `3 mod 9` in `(3)/(9)` to `1 mod 3`, while
its negative takes it to `2 mod 3`; it has order three.
`cotangentExtensionClass_zmodNine` carries this extension to the classical
almost setup, where the class differs from its negative, doubling is Baer
addition, and three copies sum to zero.

### P0.22 flat square-zero deformations

Nilpotent deformations of almost algebras come next: flat deformations, lifting of morphisms,
lifting of étale algebras, faithfully flat descent, tight ideals and henselian pairs, and modules
over complete almost algebras.

**Flat square-zero deformations of almost algebras: obstruction, torsor, automorphisms.**
