(*almost-deformation-theory*) Let `S` be a basic setup (`m̃` flat), `A` an almost algebra,
`B̃ = (0 → I → B → B₀ → 0)` an `A`-extension (`I² = 0`) and `f₀ : B₀ → C₀` a flat morphism of almost
algebras. Let `ω(B̃, f₀) := ∂(I → C₀ ⊗_{B₀} I) ∈ Ext²_{C₀}(L^a_{C₀/B₀}, C₀ ⊗_{B₀} I)`, `∂` the
boundary of the transitivity sequence for `B → B₀ → C₀`. Then (i) `ω(B̃, f₀) = 0` iff there is a
flat deformation of `C₀` over `B`, i.e. a `B`-extension `C̃ = (0 → C₀ ⊗ I → C → C₀ → 0)` with `C`
flat over `B` and `C ⊗_B B₀ ≅ C₀`; (ii) if `ω = 0`, the isomorphism classes of flat deformations
form a torsor under `Exal_{B₀}(C₀, C₀ ⊗_{B₀} I) ≅ Ext¹_{C₀}(L^a_{C₀/B₀}, C₀ ⊗_{B₀} I)`; (iii) the
automorphism group of a flat deformation (acting trivially on `C₀` and on `C₀ ⊗ I`) is
`Der_{B₀}(C₀, C₀ ⊗_{B₀} I) ≅ Ext⁰_{C₀}(L^a_{C₀/B₀}, C₀ ⊗_{B₀} I)` ([GR] §3.2, Corollary
3.2.11(i)-(iii), p. 42). More generally, for a `C₀`-module `J` and `B₀`-linear `u : I → J`, let
`u_C : C₀ ⊗_{B₀} I → J` be `c ⊗ i ↦ c·u(i)`. The obstruction
`ω(B̃, f₀, u) = (u_C)_* ω(B̃, f₀)` governs extensions `C̃` with kernel `J` ([GR] §3.2, Proposition
3.2.9, p. 41; [Sch12] §5, Theorem 5.11, p. 24, cites this proposition under the same number). If
`L^a_{C₀/B₀} ≃ 0` (e.g. `C₀` étale over `B₀`, or a perfectoid `(K°/ϖ)^a`-algebra) a flat deformation
exists and is unique up to unique isomorphism, which [Sch12] Theorem 5.10 applies over
`(K°/ϖ^n)^a → (K°/ϖ^{n−1})^a`; in the classical setup, for `A = B = B₀ ⊕ I` trivial and `C₀ = B₀[X]`, the trivial
deformation `C₀ ⊕ C₀ ⊗ I` exists and deformations form a torsor under `Ext¹(L^a, −) = 0`. *Needs:*
P0.21; P0.20; P0.18; P0.19; DerivedModuleAlgebra §0.25.

**Checks.**

- Degenerate: for `I = 0` (`B = B₀`): `ω = 0`, the only
  flat deformation is `C₀` itself, the torsor `Ext¹(L^a_{C₀/B₀}, C₀ ⊗ 0) = 0` is a point and the
  automorphism group `Der_{B₀}(C₀, 0) = 0` is trivial, as it must be.
- Computation: in the classical setup, `C₀ = B₀[X]`: `L^a_{C₀/B₀} ≃ C₀·dX` in
  degree `0`, so `Ext² = Ext¹ = 0`: every square-zero `B` admits a flat deformation, unique up to
  isomorphism, with automorphisms `Der_{B₀}(B₀[X], B₀[X] ⊗ I) ≅ B₀[X] ⊗ I` (the value on `X`).
  In a general basic setup, `B₀[X]` is only almost projective as a module over itself:
  this does not imply vanishing of ordinary `Ext¹` or `Ext²`.
- Non-example: flatness of the deformation `C` over `B` is not
  decorative: for `B₀ = k`, `B = k[t]/(t²)`, `C₀ = k`, the `B`-algebra `C = k` (`t ↦ 0`) has
  `C ⊗_B k = k` but is not flat over `B` (`(t) ⊗_B k = k → (t)·k = 0` is the zero map, see
  *almost-local-flatness-criterion*) and its kernel `0` is not `C₀ ⊗_{B₀} I = k`; the flat
  deformation of `C₀ = k` over `B` is `B` itself.

**Check `CotangentComplex.transitivityTriangle_cone_sign`.** Use Mathlib's
`CochainComplex.mappingCone.triangle`: for the zero map `ℚ[0] → ℚ[0]`,
the cone has one copy of `ℚ` in degree `−1` and one in degree `0`.
Its connecting map sends the degree `−1` generator to `−1` in `ℚ[1]`.
Thus the cone triangle uses minus projection onto the shifted source;
this is the convention for interpreting the transitivity boundary in the
obstruction formula above. The supplier is
`CochainComplex.mappingCone.inl_v_triangle_mor₃_f` in
`Mathlib/Algebra/Homology/HomotopyCategory/Pretriangulated.lean`.

Two supporting results. The transitivity triangle for almost cotangent complexes
(*cotangent-transitivity*): for `A → B → C` morphisms of almost algebras there is a natural
distinguished triangle `C_!! ⊗_{B_!!} L_{B/A} → L_{C/A} → L_{C/B} → C_!! ⊗_{B_!!} L_{B/A}[1]` in
`D(C_!!-Mod)`, hence `C ⊗_B L^a_{B/A} → L^a_{C/A} → L^a_{C/B} →` in `D(C-Mod)`; on `H_0` it extends
the exact sequence `C ⊗_B Ω_{B/A} → Ω_{C/A} → Ω_{C/B} → 0` ([GR] §2.5, Theorem 2.5.32, p. 35). For
`A → A[X] → A` (`X ↦ 0`) it gives `L^a_{A/A[X]} ≃ (X)/(X²)[1] ≅ A[1]`, the conormal module in
homological degree `1`. [Sch12]'s proof of Theorem 5.10 instead tensors `0 → A → A_n → A_{n−1} → 0`
with `L^a_{A_n/(K°/ϖ^n)^a}` and uses base change ([GR] §2.5, Theorem 2.5.35, pp. 35–36, which [Sch12]
cites as Theorem 2.5.36) to get
`L^a_{A/(K°/ϖ)^a} → L^a_{A_n/(K°/ϖ^n)^a} → L^a_{A_{n−1}/(K°/ϖ^{n−1})^a} →`. The local flatness criterion for square-zero thickenings
(*almost-local-flatness-criterion*): (i) for a ring `R`, an ideal `J ⊆ R` with `J² = 0`, `R' = R/J`
and an `R`-module `M` with `M' = M/JM`, `M` is `R`-flat iff `M'` is `R'`-flat and
`u(M) : J ⊗_{R'} M' → JM`, `x ⊗ m' ↦ xm`, is an isomorphism ([GR] §3.2, (3.2.19), p. 44); (ii) for
a basic setup `S` and a morphism `f̃ : B̃ → C̃` of `A`-extensions `0 → I → B → B₀ → 0` and
`0 → J → C → C₀ → 0` (`I² = J² = 0`) whose square is cofibred (`C₀ ≅ C ⊗_B B₀`), `B → C` is flat iff
`B₀ → C₀` is flat and `C₀ ⊗_{B₀} I → J` is an isomorphism ([GR] §3.2, Lemma 3.2.6 with proof,
p. 41); the general nilpotent case follows by induction. For `R = k[ε]/(ε²)` and `M = R`, `M' = k`
is flat and `u(M) : (ε) ⊗ k → εR` is bijective, while for `M = k`, `u(M) : (ε) ⊗ k → 0` is not
injective and `k` is not flat over `R` (Mathlib `Module.Flat`, `TensorProduct`).

The square-zero flatness criterion uses the canonical `R/J` actions on `J`,
`N = JM`, and `M/N`: a residue class `[r]` acts by the original `r` action.
The first two actions use `Module.IsTorsionBySet.module`, with annihilation
following from `J² = 0`; the third is Mathlib's quotient-module instance.
Thus the multiplication map is linear for these specified actions in both
the ordinary and almost flatness criteria ([GR] (3.2.19), p. 44, and
Lemma 3.2.6, p. 41).

**Checks.** `flat_squareZero_ideal_action` computes `[r] • a = ra`,
`flat_squareZero_image_action` computes `[r] • n = r • n`, and
`flat_squareZero_quotient_action` computes `[r] • [m] = [r • m]`.
`flat_squareZero_regular` and `flat_squareZero_residue` distinguish the
regular module over rational dual numbers from its nonflat residue module.

`Almost.FlatDeformation` is the upper algebra of the specified pushout square,
with a flat map from the thickened base. `flatDeformationSetoid` identifies exactly
isomorphisms commuting with the base and reduction maps. The obstruction and torsor
are stated by `Almost.flatDeformation`; `flatDeformation_unique` includes unique
lifting of isomorphisms when the cotangent complex vanishes ([GR] Corollary 3.2.11).

**Checks.** For both carriers, `_zero` forces an invertible reduction, `_polynomial`
gives one isomorphism class with the expected polynomial kernel automorphisms in
the classical setup, and `_nonflat` excludes the residue algebra of dual numbers.

The normalization in `Almost.flatDeformation` uses a specified universal
`B₀`-linear map `u : I → J`: for each `C₀`-module `M`, composition with `u`
identifies `Hom_{C₀}(J,M)` with `Hom_{B₀}(I,M)`. Thus `J` is the tensor
kernel `C₀ ⊗_{B₀} I`, with its generator map retained.
Its kernel statement supplies this universal map and identifies its
coefficient module with `Module.baseChange f I` ([GR] (3.2.5), p. 41). For every deformation,
the theorem supplies an extension by this kernel and an isomorphism to the
given upper algebra, commuting with the base, reduction, and kernel maps.
These hypotheses include flatness of `B₀ → C₀`; no flatness of `I` is required.

`Almost.cotangentConnecting` is the connecting arrow for the functorial
polynomial-resolution transitivity triangle, after extension to `C₀_*` and
almostification. Its triangle statement specifies its first
two arrows as the images of `cotangentTransitivityFirst` and
`cotangentTransitivitySecond`. The cone convention is the minus projection
described above ([GR] Theorem 2.5.32, p. 35). Regard the given extension
`E = (I → B → B₀)` as an extension over `B`, with base map `id_B`.
`Almost.kernelExtensionClass E f J u` is the scalar-adjoint class of its
pushout by `u`. Its degree-one conormal map is `u`, using the given
inclusion of `I`, as in [GR] (3.2.2), (3.2.7), p. 41. Define
`Almost.deformationBoundary E f J u` by composing the connecting arrow
with this class shifted by one, followed by the canonical identification
`J[1][1] ≅ J[2]`. `Almost.flatDeformation` tests this specific element for
vanishing ([GR] (3.2.10), Corollary 3.2.11, p. 42).

`Almost.cotangentExtensionClass` is the additive extension classifier:
its polynomial-resolution cocycle uses the given kernel inclusion and the
order `d₀ − d₁`, with the exactification and almostification comparisons
([GR] (2.5.31), p. 34, and (3.2.8), p. 41). `Almost.exalRestriction`
forgets part of the base without changing the upper algebra, reduction,
or kernel. Its injectivity requires the square-zero
extension of the base and identifies the injection in [GR] (3.2.15), p. 43.
The torsor in `Almost.flatDeformation` is specified by
`restriction(class([D] −ᵥ [F])) = [D] − [F]` in `Exal_B(C₀,J)`.
Consequently translation by an `Ext¹` class is Baer addition with that class;
reversing the difference changes its sign.

The automorphisms fixing the base and reduction form a subgroup of
`CategoryTheory.Aut`. Their comparison is a multiplicative equivalence to
`Multiplicative Ext⁰`, so composition corresponds to addition. Its value
is determined by
`h − id = reduction ≫ derivation ≫ kernel inclusion`, using the specified
identification of the deformation with its extension. The additive map
`Almost.cotangentDerivation` evaluates a degree-zero derived morphism on
`H⁰(L) = Ω`. Its value on the universal differential is specified, and its range
statement gives injectivity and the exact Leibniz and base-vanishing conditions on its image
([GR] Proposition 2.5.25, p. 33, (2.5.29), p. 34, and Corollary
3.2.11(iii), p. 42). In particular identity maps to zero and inverses map
to negative derivations.

DerivedModuleAlgebra §0.25 supplies the following normalized ordinary deformation laws,
on the consumed carrier of P0.19. The target `CotangentComplex.flatDeformation` retains the same
flatness and square-zero hypotheses. Its
`CotangentComplex.deformationObstruction` is the composite of
`CotangentComplex.transitivityConnecting` with the shifted
`CotangentComplex.kernelExtensionClass`. The latter sends the conormal
class of `i` to `1 ⊗ i`; it does not discard the given kernel inclusion.
`CotangentComplex.transitivityConnecting_triangle` identifies the first
two arrows with `transitivityFirst` and `transitivitySecond`. The theorem
specifies ordinary extension representatives of each classical almost
flat lift. Restriction of the torsor difference is the difference of their
`CotangentComplex.extensionClass` values. Its automorphism comparison is
again a group isomorphism with value `h − id` under
`CotangentComplex.derivationEvaluation`;
`CotangentComplex.derivationEvaluation_differential` evaluates the map on
`H⁰` at `d x` ([GR] (3.2.7)–(3.2.11), pp. 41–42, in the classical setup).

**Checks.** Each label below names a Check, specified in this README only.

- For `Almost.cotangentExtensionClass`: `_zero`, `_split`, and `_nonsplit` send zero
  and split extensions to zero and distinguish an extension without a section.
- For `Almost.cotangentDerivation`: `_zero`, `_base`, and `_nonzero` compute zero,
  vanishing on the base, and detection of a nonzero degree-zero class.
- For `Almost.exalRestriction`: `_identity`, `_zero`, and `_surjection` retain the
  extension for identity restriction, preserve zero, and preserve nonzero
  classes when the base map is the specified square-zero surjection.
- For `Almost.cotangentConnecting`: `_identity_source`, `_identity_target`, and
  `_polynomial_quotient` give zero for an identity leg and a nonzero arrow
  for `ℚ → ℚ[X] → ℚ`, with `X ↦ 0`.
- For `Almost.kernelExtensionClass`: `_zero`, `_negation`, and `_identity_nonzero`
  compute the zero kernel map, change sign when the map changes sign, and
  detect an invertible map from a nonzero kernel with `f = id`.
- For `Almost.deformationBoundary`: `_zero`, `_split`, and `_negation` give zero
  for the zero kernel map, zero for a split base extension, and the negative
  boundary for the negative kernel map. A split base extension may still
  have a nonzero kernel-extension class over its upper algebra.
- `CotangentComplex.transitivityConnecting_identity_source`,
  `_identity_target`, and `_polynomial_quotient` make the same three
  transitivity computations on the ordinary model.
- `CotangentComplex.kernelExtensionClass_zero`, `_nonzero`, and
  `_faithfully_flat` distinguish the zero kernel, a nonzero kernel with
  `T = R`, and its nonzero image under faithfully flat scalar extension.
- `CotangentComplex.deformationObstruction_zero`, `_split`, and
  `_polynomial` give zero for a zero kernel, a split base extension, and
  the polynomial algebra `ℚ[X]`, respectively.
- `CotangentComplex.derivationEvaluation_zero`, `_base`, and `_nonzero`
  test zero, vanishing on scalars, and injectivity of the comparison.

`CotangentComplex.polynomialLift_sign` computes the automorphism convention
on the flat lift `ℚ[ε]/(ε²)[X]` of `ℚ[X]`. For each `a : ℚ`, translation
`hₐ(X) = X + aε` has a unique `Ext⁰` class satisfying the difference formula;
its derivation takes `X` to `a` and `X²` to `2aX`. For a polynomial `P`
over the dual numbers, the kernel inclusion of that derivation at `P mod ε`
is exactly `hₐ(P) − P`. **Checks** `CotangentComplex.polynomialLift_positive`,
`_inverse`, and `_composition` compute the values `ε`, `−ε`, and the law
`hₐ ∘ h_b = h_{a+b}`. Since `1 ≠ −1` in `ℚ[X]`, the positive translation
cannot be assigned the negative derivation under this comparison. This is
the polynomial computation of [GR] Corollary 3.2.11(iii), p. 42.

### P0.23 lifting morphisms along square-zero extensions

**Lifting morphisms along square-zero extensions of almost algebras.** (*almost-morphism-lifting*)
Let `S` be a basic setup, `A` an almost algebra, `B̃` an `A`-extension `0 → I → B → B₀ → 0`
(`I² = 0`), and `C̃ⁱ = (0 → Jⁱ → Cⁱ → C₀ⁱ → 0)`, `i = 1, 2`, `A`-extensions with morphisms
`f̃ⁱ : B̃ → C̃ⁱ` (kernel maps `uⁱ : I → Jⁱ` and reductions `f₀ⁱ : B₀ → C₀ⁱ`), together with a `B₀`-algebra map `g₀ : C₀¹ → C₀²` and a
`C₀¹`-linear map `v : J¹ → J²` (the target action is through `g₀`) such that `u² = v ∘ u¹` and
`f₀² = g₀ ∘ f₀¹`. Regard `C̃¹` and `C̃²` as extensions over `B`, via `f̃¹` and `f̃²`.
Their class difference `v_* e(C̃¹) − e(C̃²) ∗ g₀` belongs to
`Ext¹_{C₀¹}(L^a_{C₀¹/B}, J²)`. Compatibility on `I` makes its restriction to
`Hom_{B₀}(I, J²)` zero. Its unique preimage under the transitivity injection
`Ext¹_{C₀¹}(L^a_{C₀¹/B₀}, J²) → Ext¹_{C₀¹}(L^a_{C₀¹/B}, J²)` is the
obstruction to a morphism of `A`-extensions `g̃ : C̃¹ → C̃²` over `v` and `g₀` with
`f̃² = g̃ ∘ f̃¹`; when it vanishes, such `g̃` form a torsor under
`Der_{B₀}(C₀¹, J²) ≅ Ext⁰_{C₀²}(C₀² ⊗ L^a_{C₀¹/B₀}, J²)` ([GR] §3.2, Proposition 3.2.16, p. 43). In
particular, if `C` and `C'` are flat over `B` with reductions `C₀`, `C₀'` and `f₀ : C₀ → C₀'`, the
obstruction to lifting `f₀` lies in `Ext¹(L^a_{C₀/B₀}, C₀' ⊗ I)` and lifts form a torsor under
`Hom(L^a_{C₀/B₀}, C₀' ⊗ I)` ([Sch12] §5, Theorem 5.12, p. 25, the almost version); with `L^a ≃ 0`
this gives unique lifting of morphisms, the full faithfulness in [Sch12] Theorem 5.10, and for `C₀`
étale over `B₀` morphisms lift uniquely (P0.24(i)). *Needs:* P0.21; P0.20.

`Almost.exalPush` pushes an extension along a linear map of its identified
kernel, and `Almost.exalPull` pulls it back along a map of quotient algebras.
Their representative statements specify
the resulting classes through maps of extensions that commute with the base,
quotient, and kernel inclusions ([GR] (2.5.5)–(2.5.7), p. 30, and (3.2.12)–(3.2.15),
pp. 42–43). `Almost.morphismObstruction` is the `Ext¹` class of the unique
preimage of `v_*[D₁] − g₀^*[D₂]` under `exalRestriction`.
Its existence statement supplies the unique preimage,
and its difference statement states its equality, with the
source-first order of subtraction. Its signature retains the two specified
kernel maps, their compatibility with the base extension, and `u₂ = v ∘ u₁`.

`Almost.liftMorphism` tests that particular obstruction for zero. Its torsor
is specified by the equality
`h − k = projection₁ ≫ cotangentDerivation(h −ᵥ k) ≫ inclusion₂`.
Thus a derivation acts by adding its composite through the quotient and
kernel; the negative action does not satisfy the contract. This also fixes
the identity-based automorphism comparison used in P0.22. If the relative
cotangent complex vanishes, a lift exists and is unique ([GR] Proposition
3.2.16, p. 43).

**Checks.** For `Almost.exalPush`, `_identity`, `_zero`, and `_negation` test identity,
zero, and negative identity on the kernel. For `Almost.exalPull`, `_identity`,
`_zero`, and `_section` test identity pullback, the zero extension class,
and a pullback with a specified section. For `Almost.morphismObstruction`, `_lift`,
`_zero_coefficient`, and `_unequal_classes` give zero for a supplied compatible
lift, zero for a zero target kernel, and a nonzero obstruction when the two
specified extension classes differ. These Checks are specified in this README only.

### P0.24 étale algebras lift along nilpotent ideals

**Étale almost algebras lift uniquely along nilpotent ideals.**
(*nilpotent-lifting-of-etale-almost-algebras*) Let `S` be a basic setup, `A` an almost algebra and
`I ⊆ A` a nilpotent ideal (induction reduces to `I² = 0`), `A' := A/I`. (i) For `B` weakly étale
over `A`, `C` any `A`-algebra and `J ⊆ C` nilpotent, `Hom_{A-Alg}(B, C) → Hom_{A-Alg}(B, C/J)` is
bijective ([GR] §3.2, Theorem 3.2.18(i), p. 43). (ii) `B ↦ A' ⊗_A B` is an equivalence from weakly
étale `A`-algebras to weakly étale `A'`-algebras; (iii) it restricts to an equivalence of étale
algebras `A-Ét ≃ A'-Ét` ([GR] §3.2, Theorem 3.2.18(iii), p. 43) and (iv) to an equivalence of finite
étale algebras `A_fet ≃ A'_fet` (étale and almost finitely presented; [GR] §3.2, Theorem
3.2.28(ii), p. 46; almost finite presentation lifts by [GR] §3.2, Lemma 3.2.25(iii), p. 45). For
`A = (K°/ϖ^n)^a`, `n ≥ 2`, and `I = ϖ^{n−1}A`, finite étale `(K°/ϖ^{n−1})^a`-algebras lift uniquely to
`(K°/ϖ^n)^a`, the finite-level step of [GR] Theorem 5.3.27; in the classical setup the restriction of (iii) to finitely presented étale algebras
is [SGA1] Exposé I, Corollaries 5.5 and 8.3, printed pp. 6 and 12
([public edition](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0206203)); [GR] Theorem 3.2.18 supplies the larger category used here.
*Needs:* P0.22; P0.23; P0.14; P0.10.

Supporting result: vanishing of the almost cotangent complex when the diagonal is Tor-trivial
(*cotangent-vanishing-weakly-etale*). For a basic setup `S` and a morphism `R → S'` of almost
algebras with `Tor^R_i(S', S') = 0` and `Tor^{S'⊗_R S'}_i(S', S') = 0` for all `i > 0` (the
`S' ⊗_R S'`-module structure via `μ`), `L_{S'/R} ≃ 0` in `D(S'_!!-Mod)`; in particular
`L_{S'/R} ≃ 0` for every weakly étale (hence every étale, every finite étale) morphism `R → S'`
([GR] §2.5, Theorem 2.5.36, p. 36; used for weakly étale lifting in [GR] §3.2, proof of Theorem
3.2.18, p. 43). Every idempotent quotient `A → A/eA` is weakly étale, so `L_{(A/eA)/A} ≃ 0`; for a
perfect `𝔽_p`-algebra the vanishing `L_{R/𝔽_p} = 0` is of a different nature (Frobenius; [Sch12]
Proposition 5.13, layer P1).

### P0.25 faithfully flat descent

**Faithfully flat descent for almost modules and almost algebras.**
(*almost-faithfully-flat-descent*) Let `S` be a basic setup and `φ : A → B` a faithfully flat
morphism of almost algebras (P0.11). (i) `φ` is of effective descent for modules:
`M ↦ (B ⊗_A M, can)` is an equivalence from `A-Mod` to the category `Desc(B/A)` of `B`-modules `N`
with a `B ⊗_A B`-linear isomorphism `β : p₂*N ≅ p₁*N` satisfying the cocycle condition
`p₁₂*(β) ∘ p₂₃*(β) = p₁₃*(β)`; (ii) the same holds for `A`-algebras; (iii) both statements are
stable under base change `A → A'` (universal effective descent) ([GR] §3.4, introduction and
(3.4.1), p. 55); (iv) under (i) the full subcategories of flat, almost finitely generated, almost
finitely presented and almost finite projective modules correspond, and under (ii) those of weakly
étale, étale and finite étale algebras correspond (finite étale: combine étale with almost finitely
generated projective) ([GR] §3.4, (3.4.1), pp. 55–56); (v) almost
projectivity descends when `B` is almost finitely presented over `A` (then `B` is almost finite
projective over `A`, so `B ⊗_A alHom_A(M, N) ≅ alHom_A(M, B ⊗_A N)` by
*tensor-hom-comparison-almost-projective*, `B ⊗_A I` is `alHom_A(M, −)`-acyclic for `I`
injective, and `B ⊗_A alExt^i_A(M, N) ≅ alExt^i_B(B ⊗_A M, B ⊗_A N) = 0` for `i > 0`, whence
`alExt^i_A(M, N) = 0` by faithful flatness); for a general faithfully flat `φ` it is not asserted
([GR] §3.2, Remark 3.2.26(iii)–(iv), p. 45). For `M` almost finitely generated no hypothesis on `B` is
needed, since almost finite projective = flat + almost finitely presented descends by (iv). The
honest case is part of this target: for `V`-algebras `R → R'` with `R'` faithfully flat, (i) and
(ii) for the classical setup `S = classical V` are Grothendieck's effective descent of modules and
algebras ([GR] §3.4, (3.4.1)). Mathlib supplies the comonadicity of `R' ⊗_R −` (`comonadicExtendScalars`)
and the degree `≤ 1` Amitsur statement for the ring itself (`CommRingCat.isLimitForkPushoutSelfOfFaithfullyFlat`),
and descends injectivity, surjectivity and bijectivity of linear maps
(`Module.FaithfullyFlat.bijective_of_tensorProduct`); the identification of comodules with descent
data, hence the equivalence `R-Mod ≃ Desc(R'/R)`, is proved here, and for a general setup the
almostification of that descent is (i) for `R^a → R'^a`.
DiamondsAndVStacks layer D3 applies (ii) with `(S⁺/ϖ)^a` faithfully flat over `(R⁺/ϖ)^a` to descend
the datum on `(S̃⁺/ϖ)^a` to an almost `(R⁺/ϖ)^a`-algebra. *Needs:* P0.7; P0.10; Mathlib
`comonadicExtendScalars`, `ModuleCat.extendScalars`, `CategoryTheory.Pseudofunctor.DescentData`,
`CommRingCat.isLimitForkPushoutSelfOfFaithfullyFlat`.

Three supporting results. Stability of flat, unramified and
étale morphisms (*etale-morphisms-stability*): for `φ : A → B`, `ψ : B → C`, (i) flatness, almost
projectivity, faithful flatness, almost finiteness, weak unramifiedness, unramifiedness, weak
étaleness and étaleness are stable under base change and (ii) under composition; (iii) if `φ` is
flat and `ψ ∘ φ` faithfully flat then `φ` is faithfully flat; (iv) if `φ` is weakly unramified and
`ψ ∘ φ` flat (weakly étale) then `ψ` is flat (weakly étale); (v) if `φ` is unramified and `ψ ∘ φ`
étale then `ψ` is étale; (vi) `φ` is faithfully flat iff it is a monomorphism and `B/A` is a flat
`A`-module; (vii) if `φ` is almost finite and weakly unramified then `φ` is unramified; (viii) if `ψ`
is faithfully flat and `ψ ∘ φ` flat (weakly unramified) then `φ` is flat (weakly unramified); finite
étale morphisms are stable under base change and composition ([GR] §3.1, Lemma 3.1.2(i) and
(v)-(vii), p. 39). Classically (vi) is "faithfully flat iff injective with flat cokernel"; base change
of `L°a/K°a` along `K°a → (K°/ϖ)^a` gives a finite étale `(L°/ϖ)^a` over `(K°/ϖ)^a`. `B ↦ B_!!`
preserves and reflects faithful flatness, but not flatness (*lower-shriek-shriek-faithful-flatness*):
(i) `φ` is faithfully flat iff `φ` is a monomorphism and `B/A` is a flat `A`-module ([GR] §3.1,
Lemma 3.1.2(vi), p. 39); (ii) `φ` is a monomorphism iff `φ_!! : A_!! → B_!!` is injective, and
`B_!!/A_!! ≅ B_!/A_!` is flat over `A_!!` iff `B/A` is flat over `A` (`m̃` flat is used here through
[GR] Proposition 2.4.35); (iii) hence `φ` is faithfully flat iff `φ_!!` is a faithfully flat ring map
([GR] §3.1, Remark 3.1.3(ii), p. 40); (iv) flatness is not preserved: for `S = ofValuationRing V`
with residue field `k`, the flat projection `V^a × V^a → V^a` becomes `V ×_k V → V` under `(−)_!!`,
which is not flat ([GR] §3.1, Remark 3.1.3(ii), p. 39; [Bhatt] §4.2, Remark 4.2.8, p. 25; Mathlib
`Module.FaithfullyFlat`). The Amitsur complex of an almost faithfully flat map is exact
(*almost-amitsur-complex-exact*): for `φ : A → B` faithfully flat and `M` an `A`-module, the
augmented Amitsur complex `0 → M → M ⊗_A B → M ⊗_A B ⊗_A B → ⋯` (differentials the alternating sums
of the coface maps) is exact in `A-Mod`; in honest terms, for `V`-algebras `R → R'` such that `R'^a`
is faithfully flat over `R^a` (e.g. `Tor_i^R(X, R')` almost zero for `i > 0` and `X ⊗_R R'` almost
zero only if `X` is) and any `R`-module `N`, the cohomology of
`0 → N → N ⊗_R R' → N ⊗_R R' ⊗_R R' → ⋯` is almost zero, so `N^a` is the equalizer of
`(N ⊗ R')^a ⇉ (N ⊗ R' ⊗ R')^a` ([GR] §3.4, (3.4.1), p. 55; [ECD] §8, proof of Proposition 8.8,
p. 43; Mathlib `CommRingCat.isLimitForkPushoutSelfOfFaithfullyFlat`). For `A → A × A` the Amitsur
complex is split exact; DiamondsAndVStacks layer D2 uses the almost exactness of
`R⁺/ϖ → S⁺/ϖ ⇉ S⁺/ϖ ⊗ S⁺/ϖ`.

`Module.baseChange` takes almost elements, extends scalars along the map of
almost-element rings, and almostifies. `Module.descentPseudofunctor` uses these
functors; `Algebra.descentPseudofunctor` uses pushouts of almost algebras. Their
descent data are Mathlib's `Pseudofunctor.DescentData`, including the cocycle equation.
The canonical comparison is an equivalence, also after any base change, by [GR] (3.4.1).

The coherence isomorphisms are fixed as follows. `Module.baseChangeUnit`
sends an almost element through the ordinary scalar-extension unit and the
almost-elements adjunction unit. `Module.baseChangeIdIso_exists` and
`Module.baseChangeCompIso_exists` give unique natural isomorphisms with the
prescribed generator equations; `Module.baseChangeIdIso` and
`Module.baseChangeCompIso` select them. `Module.baseChangeIdIso_unit` sends
the identity-extension generator back to the original element.
`Module.baseChangeCompIso_unit` sends an iterated generator back to its
direct-extension generator. These are the almost versions of Mathlib's
`ModuleCat.extendScalarsId` and `ModuleCat.extendScalarsComp`, and supply
`mapId` and `mapComp` of `Module.descentPseudofunctor`. For
`Algebra.descentPseudofunctor` those fields are exactly `Under.pushoutId`
and `Under.pushoutComp`. Both use `pseudofunctorOfIsLocallyDiscrete` for
2-morphisms; associativity and the two unit equations concern these fixed
isomorphisms. Faithfully flat descent (*almost-faithfully-flat-descent*) therefore applies to the
specified scalar-extension descent data, universally after base change
([GR] (3.4.1), p. 55).

**Checks.** `baseChangeUnit_zero`, `baseChangeUnit_add`, and
`baseChangeUnit_identity_injective` test zero, addition, and injectivity
along an identity base map. For each of `baseChangeIdIso` and
`baseChangeCompIso`, `_generator` fixes the comparison on generators,
`_zero` gives zero, and `_not_negated` excludes the negative comparison
whenever the generator differs from its negative.

**Checks.** The identity, zero and rank-two Checks of almost-module base change give
the identity functor, the zero module, and the free rank-two module. The module
pseudofunctor has the corresponding `_identity`, `_zero`, and `_two` Checks.
The algebra pseudofunctor's `_identity`, `_unit`, and `_two` Checks give the
identity functor, the base algebra, and the two-factor product after scalar extension.

`Algebra.relativeForget` uses the underlying module over the source's almost
elements. Its `_unit`, `_zero`, and `_two` Checks give the tensor unit, the zero
module, and two copies of the unit. `amitsurCosimplicial` is the Čech conerve in
almost algebras over the base, followed by this forgetful functor and tensoring
with the coefficient module. `amitsurComplex` takes its alternating cofaces.

**Checks.** Both Amitsur constructions have `_identity` (cohomology is the
coefficient module in degree zero only), `_zero` (zero coefficients), and `_two`
(the split cover `A → A × A`). In the last case the first differential is
`δ₀ − δ₁` and is nonzero for a nonzero base; on two scalar values this is
`(a,b) ↦ 1 ⊗ (a,b) − (a,b) ⊗ 1`, fixing the sign in [GR] (3.4.1).

### P0.26 tight ideals and henselian pairs

**Tight ideals, the Jacobson radical and henselian pairs of almost algebras.** (*tight-ideal*) Let
`S = (V, m)` be a basic setup and `A` an almost `V`-algebra; ideals of `A` are subobjects `I ↪ A`
stable under multiplication, with powers `Iⁿ` the images of `I^{⊗n}`. An ideal `I ⊆ A` is tight if
there are a finitely generated ideal `m₀ ⊆ m` and `n ∈ ℕ` with `Iⁿ ⊆ m₀·A` ([GR] §5.1, Definition
5.1.5, p. 103); for `ϖ ∈ m` the ideal `ϖA` is tight. The Jacobson radical of `A` is
`rad(A) := rad(A_*)^a` ([GR] §5.1, Definition 5.1.1, p. 103); for a `V`-algebra `R` and an ideal
`J ⊆ R`, `J^a ⊆ rad(R^a)` iff `mJ ⊆ rad(R)` ([GR] §5.1, Lemma 5.1.2, p. 103). A pair `(A, I)` with
`I ⊆ rad(A)` is henselian if `(A_*, m·I_*)` is a henselian pair (Mathlib
`HenselianRing A_* (m·I_*)`), and tight henselian if moreover `I` is tight ([GR] §5.1, Definition
5.1.8, p. 104); `(R^a, J^a)` is henselian iff `(R, mJ)` is ([GR] Lemma 5.1.10). If `A` is
`I`-adically complete (`A → lim A/Iⁿ` an isomorphism), `(A, I)` is henselian ([GR] §5.3, Remark
5.3.7, p. 112). Define `Almost.Algebra.IsTight` (`∃ m₀ ≤ S.ideal, m₀.FG ∧ ∃ n, Iⁿ ≤ m₀ • A`),
`Almost.Algebra.jacobson` (`rad(A) := (Ideal.jacobson ⊥ of A_*)^a`) and
`Almost.Algebra.IsHenselianPair` (`I ≤ rad A ∧ HenselianRing A_* (S.ideal • I_*)`); prove
`Almost.Algebra.isTight_span` (`ϖ • A` is tight for `ϖ ∈ S.ideal`), `Almost.Algebra.Ideal.IsTight.mono`
(subideals and powers of tight ideals are tight), `Almost.Algebra.Ideal.IsTight.map` (tightness is
preserved by base change), `Almost.Algebra.le_jacobson_toAlmost_iff`
(`J^a ≤ rad(R^a) ↔ S.ideal • J ≤ Ideal.jacobson ⊥`),
`Almost.Algebra.isHenselianPair_toAlmost_iff` (`IsHenselianPair (R^a) (J^a) ↔ HenselianRing R (S.ideal • J)`), `Almost.Algebra.isHenselianPair_of_isAdicComplete` and
`Almost.Algebra.Ideal.IsTight.elements_le_jacobson` (for `I` tight in `rad(A)`: `I_* ≤ rad(A_*)`, and
`(A_*, I_*)` is henselian if `(A, I)` is, [GR] Corollary 5.1.16). *Needs:* P0.8; P0.10; P0.11;
Mathlib `HenselianRing`, `Ideal.jacobson`, `IsAdicComplete`, `Submodule.FG`.

Two supporting results. The almost Nakayama lemma for tight ideals (*almost-nakayama*): for an
almost algebra `A` and `I ⊆ rad(A)` a tight ideal, (i) if `M` is an almost finitely generated
`A`-module with `IM = M`, then `M = 0` ([GR] §5.1, Lemma 5.1.6, p. 103); (ii) if `φ : N → M` is a
morphism of almost finite projective `A`-modules such that `φ ⊗_A A/I` is an isomorphism, then `φ`
is an isomorphism ([GR] §5.1, Corollary 5.1.7, p. 104); (iii) if `M` is almost finitely generated
and `M ⊗_A A/I = 0` then `M = 0` (Mathlib `Submodule.eq_bot_of_le_smul_of_le_jacobson_bot`). For
`A = K°a` and `I = ϖA`, an almost finitely generated `M` with `M = ϖM` is zero; the finiteness
hypothesis is needed, since `K = K°[1/ϖ]` satisfies `K = ϖK`. Idempotents lift uniquely along tight
henselian pairs (*tight-henselian-idempotent-lifting*): for `(A, I)` a tight henselian pair (e.g.
`A` `I`-adically complete with `I` tight), `A → A/I` induces a bijection from the idempotents of
`A_*` to the idempotents of `(A/I)_*` ([GR] §5.1, Proposition 5.1.17, p. 105; [GR] §2.5, Proposition
2.5.13(i), p. 31, for square-zero extensions; Mathlib `HenselianRing`, `IsIdempotentElem`). The
honest case (`S = classical V`, a henselian pair `(A, J)` or an `J`-adically complete `A`) is Tau
Ceti's `TauCeti.HenselianRing.exists_isIdempotentElem_sub_mem` and
`TauCeti.IsAdicComplete.exists_isIdempotentElem_eq`; the tight almost version is what is new. In the classical setup, for
`A = (V⟦X⟧)^a` and `I = XA` the idempotents of `A_*` and of `(A/I)_* = (V^a)_*` agree; with the rank
decomposition it lifts the decomposition `A/ϖ = ∏ Ā_i` to `A`
in *uniform-finite-projectivity-mod-varpi* (P0.28).

**Checks.**

- `Almost.Algebra.tight_test_principal` (computation) — for `ϖ ∈ S.ideal`, the ideal `ϖA` is tight
  (`m₀ = ϖV`, `n = 1`).
- `Almost.Algebra.IsTight_test_unit` (non-example) — for `S = ofValuationRing K°` and `A = K°a`, the
  unit ideal `A` is not tight: `A ⊆ m₀A` would force `m ⊆ m₀` for a finitely generated (hence
  principal) `m₀ = εK° ⊊ m`.
- `Almost.Algebra.adic_test_zero_ideal` (degenerate) — the zero ideal of any almost algebra is tight.
- `Almost.Algebra.IsHenselianPair_classical` (compatibility) — for `S = classical V`: every
  ideal is tight and `IsHenselianPair (R^a) (J^a) ↔ HenselianRing R J` (Mathlib), since then
  `m·J = J` and `(R^a)_* = R`.

The representative ideal `idealElements S A I` consists of those `x ∈ A_*` for which
`εx ∈ I` for every `ε ∈ m`. Thus `jacobson S A` is the saturation of the honest
Jacobson radical; the defining equation for `IsHenselianPair` uses `m·idealElements S A I`.
These are the representatives in [GR] Definition 5.1.1 and Lemma 5.1.10.

**Checks.**

- `idealElements_classical` — saturation fixes every ideal in the classical setup.
- `idealElements_zero` — the zero ideal of an almost-element ring is saturated.
- `idealElements_scalarIdeal` — saturating `mA_*` gives the unit ideal, including the zero setup.
- `jacobson_classical` — the classical radical is the ordinary Jacobson radical.
- `jacobson_field` — the radical of a classical field is zero.
- `jacobson_dual_numbers` — the nonzero nilpotent `ε` lies in the radical of classical rational dual numbers.
- `IsHenselianPair_zero` — every zero pair is henselian.
- `IsHenselianPair_unit` — if the unit ideal is tight, the unit pair is henselian exactly
  when its almost algebra is zero.
- `IsHenselianPair_valuation_unit` — for a henselian valuation domain with non-finitely-generated
  maximal ideal, the unit almost pair is henselian and nonzero; its unit ideal is not tight.
  Tightness is essential in the preceding Check ([GR] Corollary 5.1.16).
- `IsHenselianPair_classical` — henselianity agrees with Mathlib on ordinary pairs.

### P0.27 almost finite projective modules over complete algebras

**Almost finite projective modules over I-adically complete almost algebras.**
(*adic-almost-projective-modules*) Let `S` be a basic setup, `A` an almost algebra and `I ⊆ A` a
tight ideal with `A → lim_n A/I^{n+1}` an isomorphism, `A_n := A/I^{n+1}` (Gabber–Ramero's
conditions (a), (b) of [GR] Lemma 5.3.5 for the system `(A_n)`; [GR] §5.3, Lemma 5.3.5(ii), p. 112).
Then `M ↦ (M ⊗_A A_n)_n` is an equivalence from almost finite projective `A`-modules to compatible
systems `(M_n)` of almost finite projective `A_n`-modules (`M_{n+1} ⊗ A_n ≅ M_n`), with
quasi-inverse `(M_n) ↦ lim_n M_n` ([GR] §5.3, Theorem 5.3.24, p. 115; [GR] §5.3, (5.3.21), p. 115);
in particular `P ≅ lim_n P ⊗_A A_n` for every almost finite projective `P` ([GR] §5.3, Claim
5.3.25, p. 115). Moreover, if `M = lim_n M_n` for a compatible system of `A_n`-modules with
`M_{n+1} ⊗_{A_{n+1}} A_n ≅ M_n` (an `I`-c-adic module), and `M_0` is almost finitely generated,
then `M` is almost finitely generated and `M ⊗_A A_n ≅ M_n` for every `n`. For `A = K°a` and `I = ϖA`, almost finite
projective `K°a`-modules are the limits of compatible almost finite projective `(K°/ϖ^n)^a`-modules;
P0.28 uses this for the underlying modules of finite étale algebras. *Needs:* P0.26; P0.10; P0.11;
P0.6.

`Module.AdicModule` consists of the modules over `A/I^(n+1)` and adjacent
scalar-extension isomorphisms. Morphisms are compatible families of module maps.
`adicReduction` is quotient scalar extension on objects and morphisms;
`adicReduction_evaluation` fixes each evaluation functor. The equivalence on
almost finite projectives is `adic_almost_projective_equivalence`.
`adic_almost_finitely_generated` gives effectivity from almost finite generation
at level zero, under the same tightness and completeness hypotheses.

**Checks.** For `AdicModule`, `adicReduction`, and `evaluation`, `_zero_ideal`
gives the category of modules over `A`, `_zero` gives the zero module at every
stage, and `_two` gives the free rank-two module over each quotient. The
additional `AdicModule_unit_ideal` Check gives zero modules at every stage.

Supporting result: products, limits, `lim¹`, colimits, Tor and Ext of almost zero modules are
almost zero (*almost-zero-limits-and-colimits*): for a basic setup `S` and any family `(M_i)_{i∈I}`
of almost zero `V`-modules, `∏_i M_i` and `⊕_i M_i` are almost zero; the colimit of any diagram of
almost zero modules is almost zero; for an inverse system `(N_n)_{n∈ℕ}` of almost zero modules,
`lim_n N_n` and `lim¹_n N_n = coker(∏ N_n → ∏ N_n, (x_n) ↦ (x_n − φ_n(x_{n+1})))` are almost zero;
and for `M` almost zero, `Tor_i^V(M, N)`, `Ext^i_V(M, N)` and `Ext^i_V(N, M)` are almost zero for
all `i` and `N`; no finiteness or Mittag-Leffler hypothesis enters, the product being killed
elementwise. Consequently a map of inverse systems whose kernels and cokernels are termwise almost
zero induces almost isomorphisms on `lim` and on `lim¹` ([GR] §2.4, Lemma 2.4.2(i)-(ii), p. 22, the
case of the constant sequence `ε_n = m`). For `S = (𝒪_{ℂ_p}, 𝔪)` and `N_n = k[t]` (`k = V/m`) with
transition maps multiplication by `t`, `lim N_n = 0` and `lim¹ N_n = k⟦t⟧/k[t]`, which is nonzero
and almost zero (a `k`-vector space); with zero transition maps `lim¹` would vanish, the map
`(x_n) ↦ (x_n − φ_n(x_{n+1}))` being the identity, and with identity transition maps too (it is
`(x_n) ↦ (x_n − x_{n+1})`, surjective via `x_n = −Σ_{j<n} y_j`).
*Needs:* P0.5; DerivedModuleAlgebra §1.T.1 / *lim and lim¹ of a tower* and
*The six-term sequence of lim and lim¹*; Mathlib module products, colimits, Tor and Ext.

The ordinary tower is the supplied functor `N : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ ModuleCat V`, with natural
transformations as morphisms. Use `ModuleTower.Product N`, `ModuleTower.shift N`,
`ModuleTower.lim N` and `ModuleTower.limOne N` directly; the displayed difference is
`ModuleTower.shift`, with the supplier's sign. The almost-isomorphism assertion applies to
the supplied `ModuleTower.limMap` and `ModuleTower.limOneMap`, using its six-term boundary
on the kernel, image and cokernel towers. These are ordinary modules before almostification:
the polynomial example has nonzero ordinary `lim¹` although its almostification is zero.

**Checks.**

- `lim1_test_zero_maps`, `lim1_test_identity_maps` — for zero transitions the difference map is
  the identity; for identity transitions it is surjective, solved by `x_n = −Σ_{j<n} y_j`.
- `lim1_test_sign` — for transitions `·2` on `ℤ` and `(x₀,x₁) = (1,2)`, the first difference is
  `1 − 2·2 = −3`; this fixes the sign in the displayed `lim¹` presentation.
- `lim1_test_polynomial` — transitions `·X` on `k[X]` give a nonsurjective difference map,
  so the `lim¹` term cannot be dropped.

The following Checks use the same supplied tower carrier and maps.

- `tower_test_zero_maps` — the difference map is the identity and both limits are zero.
- `tower_test_identity_maps` — the limit is the constant module and `lim¹` vanishes.
- `tower_test_polynomial` — transitions given by multiplication by `X` on `k[X]` have zero limit and nonzero `lim¹`.
- `tower_test_sign` — with transition multiplication by `2` on `ℤ` and `x_n = n + 1`, the first difference is `−3`.

### P0.28 finite étale lifting modulo a tight ideal

**Finite étale almost algebras lift uniquely modulo a tight ideal of a complete almost algebra.**
(*finite-etale-lifting-along-complete-flat-almost-algebras*) Let `S = (V, m)` be a basic setup
(`m̃` flat, needed for the cotangent complex behind the nilpotent lifting), `A` an almost
`V`-algebra and `I ⊆ A` a tight ideal (e.g. `I = ϖA` with `ϖ ∈ m`) such that `A` is `I`-adically
complete (`A → lim_n A/I^{n+1}` an isomorphism); flatness of `A` over `V^a` is not needed for the
equivalence itself. Then `B ↦ B ⊗_A A/I` is an equivalence of categories `A_fet ≃ (A/I)_fet`, with
quasi-inverse `B₀ ↦ lim_n B_n`, where `B_n` is the unique finite étale `A/I^{n+1}`-algebra lifting
`B₀` ([GR] §5.3, Theorem 5.3.27 with proof, p. 116). In particular, for `ϖ ∈ m` and `A`
`ϖ`-adically complete, `A_fet ≃ (A/ϖ)_fet`; this is [Sch12] Theorem 4.17 over an arbitrary basic
setup ([Sch12] §4, Theorem 4.17 with proof, p. 21, states it for `S = (K°, K°°)` and `A` flat over
`K°a`, citing [GR] Theorem 5.3.27 under the same number). Complements: in the case `I = ϖA`, if `A` is flat over `V^a`
then every `B ∈ A_fet` is flat over `V^a` and `ϖ`-adically complete,
by *finite-etale-lift-flat-and-complete*; for root setups `B` is uniformly finite projective over
`A` iff `B/ϖB` is over `A/ϖ` by *uniform-finite-projectivity-mod-varpi*. For `A = K°a` and
`ϖ ∈ K°°`, `K°a_fet ≃ (K°a/ϖ)_fet` is the middle link in
`K_fet ≃ K°a_fet ≃ (K°a/ϖ)_fet = (K♭°a/ϖ♭)_fet ≃ K♭°a_fet ≃ K♭_fet` ([Sch12] §4); for a finite étale
`(A/ϖ)`-algebra `B₀`, pairs `(B, ι : B/ϖB ≅ B₀)` with `B` finite étale over `A` exist and
are unique up to the unique isomorphism compatible with `ι`. The classical
case `m = V` with `A` `I`-adically complete (so `(A, I)` henselian) is included in
`Almost.Algebra.finiteEtaleBaseChange_isEquivalence`: take `BasicSetup.classical V`
and use `Almost.Algebra.classicalEquiv` to identify ordinary algebras. The theorem
over a general basic setup and tight ideal is owned by P0.28 ([GR] Theorem 5.3.27,
p. 116). *Needs:* P0.14; P0.26; P0.24; P0.27; Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Equivalence`.

Five supporting results. Unramifiedness lifts from the reduction modulo a tight ideal
(*unramified-lifts-from-complete-reduction*): for `A` an almost algebra and `I ⊆ A` tight with `A`
`I`-adically complete, (i) for arbitrary ideals `I₁, I₂` and `φ : A → B`, if `φ ⊗ A/I₁` and `φ ⊗ A/I₂` are
unramified then so is `φ ⊗ A/(I₁I₂)` (no completeness is used in this clause) ([GR] §5.2, Theorem 5.2.12(ii), p. 109); (ii) if `B` is an almost
finite projective `A`-algebra such that `B/IB` is unramified over `A/I`, then `B` is unramified over
`A` ([GR] §5.3, Claim 5.3.29, p. 116); (iii) more generally, for `I ⊆ rad(A)` tight and `B` almost
finite over `A` with `B/IB` unramified over `A/I`, `B` is unramified over `A` ([GR] §5.2, Corollary
5.2.15, p. 110); for `A = K°a` and `B = L°a` (`L/K` finite étale), unramifiedness of `L°a/K°a`
follows from that of `(L°/ϖ)^a` over `(K°/ϖ)^a`. Finite étale algebras over complete flat almost
algebras are flat and complete (*finite-etale-lift-flat-and-complete*): for `ϖ ∈ m`, `A` an almost
algebra which is `ϖ`-adically complete and `B ∈ A_fet`, `B` is `ϖ`-adically complete
(`B ≅ lim_n B/ϖⁿB`), and if `A` is flat over `V^a` then so is `B` ([Sch12] §4, Theorem 4.17, p. 21,
the flatness and completeness assertion); for `A = K°a` and `B = L°a` (`L/K` finite,
`K` perfectoid), `L°a` is flat and `ϖ`-adically complete, as `L°` is. Uniform finite projectivity
of a finite étale algebra can be checked modulo `ϖ` (*uniform-finite-projectivity-mod-varpi*): for
`S` the root setup of `(ϖ_n)` (P0.2; the root setup supplies, for each `k`, elements `ϖ_{k+1}` and
`t = ϖ_{k+1}^{p^{k+1}−2}` with `ϖ = ϖ_{k+1}²·t`), `ϖ = ϖ_0`, `A` an almost algebra which is
`ϖ`-adically complete and `B ∈ A_fet`, `B` is uniformly almost finitely generated over `A` with
bound `r` iff `B/ϖB` is uniformly almost finitely generated over `A/ϖ` with bound `r`; hence `B` is
uniformly finite projective over `A` iff `B ⊗_A A/ϖ` is uniformly finite projective over `A/ϖ`
([Sch12] §4, Theorem 4.17, last sentence, p. 21, over `(K°, K°°)`; the Nakayama step is [GR] §5.1,
Lemma 5.1.6, p. 103); layer P3 uses it for "`S°a` is uniformly finite projective over `R°a`".
`ϖ`-adic completeness of an almost module and of its almost elements
(*almost-completeness-via-almost-elements*): for `ϖ ∈ m` and `M` an almost `V`-module whose almost
elements `M_*` have no `ϖ`-torsion (for `S = (K°, K°°)` this is flatness of `M`, [Sch12] Lemma
5.3(i)), (i) `(ϖⁿM)_* = ϖⁿM_*` for all `n`; (ii) `M_*/ϖⁿM_* → (M/ϖⁿM)_*` is injective with almost
zero cokernel ([Bhatt] §4.4, Lemma 4.4.1(3) with proof, pp. 30–31); (iii) `M` is `ϖ`-adically
complete (`M → lim_n M/ϖⁿM` an isomorphism in `Almost.Module S`) iff `M_*` is `ϖ`-adically complete
(Mathlib `IsAdicComplete (Ideal.span {ϖ}) M_*`); the comparison
`lim M_*/ϖⁿ → lim (M/ϖⁿ)_* = (lim M/ϖⁿ)_*` is injective with almost zero cokernel, the `lim¹` of
the almost zero cokernels being almost zero by *almost-zero-limits-and-colimits* ([Sch12] §5, Lemma
5.3(iv), p. 22; [Bhatt] §4.4, Lemma 4.4.2, p. 31; [Bhatt] §4.4, Proposition 4.4.3, p. 32, the general
setup version via derived completeness, without torsion-freeness; Mathlib `IsAdicComplete`,
`AdicCompletion`). The torsion-freeness hypothesis is not decorative for (i): for
`K = ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞})^`, `ϖ = p`, and
`M = (K°/ϖ²)^a` (`ϖ`-adically complete, with `M_* = Hom(K°°, K°/ϖ²)` having `ϖ`-torsion),
`(ϖM)_* = Hom(K°°, ϖK°/ϖ²K°) ≅ Hom(K°°, K°/ϖ)` strictly contains `ϖ·M_*`, which is the image of
`Hom(K°°, K°/ϖ²) → Hom(K°°, K°/ϖ)`: the non-honest almost element `(c_n)`, `c_n = Σ_{j<n} ϖ^{1−1/p^j}`, of `elements_test_not_identity` (P0.6) is not in that image, because any
`(d_n) ∈ Hom(K°°, K°/ϖ²) = lim K°/ϖ^{2−1/p^n}` has `d_n ≡ d_0 mod ϖ` for all `n`. For
`M = (K°/ϖ)^a` the two sides of (i) are both `0` and the failure is invisible. Complete torsion-free
complexes that are almost exact modulo `ϖ` are almost exact, with the `lim¹` term controlled
(*almost-exactness-passes-to-completion*): for `ϖ ∈ m` and `C^•` a cochain complex of `V`-modules
(`C^i = 0` for `i < 0`) such that every `C^i` is `ϖ`-torsion-free (for the exactness of
`0 → C/ϖ^{n−1} → C/ϖⁿ → C/ϖ → 0`) and `ϖ`-adically complete (`C^i = lim C^i/ϖⁿ`), if the cohomology
of `C^•/ϖC^•` is almost zero in every degree, then (i) `H^i(C^•/ϖⁿC^•)` is almost zero for all
`n ≥ 1` and all `i`; (ii) for every `i` there is an exact sequence
`0 → lim¹_n H^{i−1}(C^•/ϖⁿ) → H^i(C^•) → lim_n H^i(C^•/ϖⁿ) → 0` (the Milnor sequence of the tower
`C^• = lim_n C^•/ϖⁿ`, whose transition maps are termwise surjective), and both outer terms are
almost zero, so `H^i(C^•)` is almost zero; (iii) `C^•[1/ϖ]` is exact ([ECD] §8, proof of Proposition
8.8, p. 43; [Berkeley] Lecture 8, proof of Proposition 8.2.8, p. 60; [GR] §2.4, Lemma 2.4.2(i)-(ii),
p. 22; Mathlib `CategoryTheory.ShortComplex.ShortExact.homology_exact₂`, `IsAdicComplete`,
`HomologicalComplex.homology`). Neither the torsion-freeness nor the completeness can be dropped,
and the `lim¹` term is not discarded: it is almost zero because every `H^{i−1}(C^•/ϖⁿ)` is. For
`C^0 = V[1/ϖ]` (torsion-free, not `ϖ`-adically separated) and `C^i = 0` otherwise, `C/ϖ = 0` is
exact but `H^0(C) = V[1/ϖ]` is not almost zero; [ECD] Proposition 8.8 applies the lemma to
`0 → R⁺ → S⁺ → O⁺(Y ×_X Y) → ⋯` for a v-cover of a totally disconnected `X`.
Use the native `V`-module Milnor sequence of DerivedModuleAlgebra §1.T.1 on the tower
`(C^•/ϖ^{n+1})_n`, with its supplied injection from `ModuleTower.limOne` of the
degree-`i−1` cohomology tower and projection to `ModuleTower.lim` of the degree-`i`
cohomology tower. The identification `C^• ≅ lim_n C^•/ϖ^{n+1}` respects the canonical
projections, so these are the same Milnor maps, natural in maps of complete complexes.
P0.27 supplies their outer terms' almost annihilation.
*Needs:* P0.27 / *almost-zero-limits-and-colimits*;
DerivedModuleAlgebra §1.T.1 / *The Milnor sequence for towers of complexes*.

**Checks.**

- `completion_test_torsion` — the two-term complex `ℤ/4 → ℤ/2` in degrees `0,1`, with quotient
  differential, is `2`-adically complete and becomes the identity `ℤ/2 → ℤ/2` modulo `2`.
  Its original kernel contains the nonzero class `2`; the torsion-free hypothesis is necessary
  (take the classical setup over `ℤ`).
- `finiteEtale_test_swap` — for a field `k`, the finite étale algebra `k × k` has a nonidentity
  swap, taking `(1,0)` to `(0,1)`. Uniqueness of a lift means uniqueness respecting its specified
  reduction, even for the tight ideal `I = 0`.

The proposed Lean quotient interfaces take an ordinary ideal `I ⊆ A_*` representing the almost
ideal `I^a`; every almost ideal is represented this way by its almost elements.
`Algebra.IsTight A I` means that some finitely generated `m₀ ⊆ m` and some power `I^n`
satisfy `m I^n ⊆ m₀ A_*`, exactly the inclusion after almostification.
`IsNilpotentIdeal` similarly requires `m I^n = 0` for some positive `n`.
`adicSystem` has objects `(A_*/I^{n+1})^a`, with its transition maps pinned by
`adicSystem_map`; `adicMap` is the canonical cone map and `IsAdicComplete` says it is
invertible. `finiteEtaleBaseChange` is the pushout functor, and
`finiteEtaleBaseChange_isEquivalence` states the tight complete reduction theorem.
`nilpotentEtaleEquiv` states the general étale reduction equivalence of P0.24.

- `adic_test_zero_ideal` — zero is tight and nilpotent, every almost algebra is complete for it, and its quotient map is invertible.
- `adic_test_unit_ideal` — the quotient by the unit ideal is zero; nilpotence and completeness at that ideal each force the almost algebra to be zero.
- `tight_test_principal` — the ideal represented by `(ε)`, for `ε ∈ m`, is tight.
- `tight_test_classical` — every ideal is tight in the classical setup.
- `adic_test_dual_numbers` — the ideal generated by `ε` in the classical dual-number algebra is nilpotent, and that algebra is complete for it.
- `adic_test_nilpotent` — an almost nilpotent ideal is tight, the algebra is complete for it, and finite étale base change is an equivalence.

The module-valued reduction functor `modPowerComplex` is extension to `V/(ϖⁿ)` followed
by restriction of scalars. `almostExact_of_complete_mod` applies to nonnegative complexes
whose terms are complete and have injective multiplication by `ϖ`; it gives almost zero
homology at every positive power and before reduction, and exactness after inversion.

**Checks.** `modPowerComplex_zero_exponent` gives the zero complex at exponent zero;
`modPowerComplex_zero_parameter` gives the original complex for the zero parameter and a
positive exponent; `modPowerComplex_unit` gives zero for a unit parameter at every exponent.

### P0.29 almost sheaves and almost cohomology

**Almost sheaves, almost sheaf cohomology and almost Čech complexes on a site.**
(*almost-cech-and-sheaf-cohomology*) Let `(C, J)` be a site whose category of sheaves of
`V`-modules is abelian with enough injectives (Mathlib `sheafIsAbelian`, `HasSheafify`) and
`S = (V, m)` a basic setup. For a sheaf `F` of `V`-modules on `(C, J)` (Mathlib
`Sheaf J (ModuleCat V)`): `F` is almost zero if `m·F(U) = 0` for all `U`; almost zero sheaves form
a Serre class of the abelian category of sheaves, and the Serre localization `Almost.Sheaf J S` is
the category of sheaves of almost `V`-modules (a basic setup relative to the topos of `(C, J)`,
[GR] §3.3, (3.3.1)-(3.3.2) and the introduction, p. 47), with exact localization `F ↦ F^a`. For
`X ∈ C` and `n ≥ 0` the cohomology `H^n(X, F)` of the underlying abelian sheaf (Mathlib
`Sheaf.H'`) is a `V`-module through the action of `V` on `F`, and its almostification
`H^n(X, F)^a ∈ Almost.Module S` depends only on `F^a` (almost zero sheaves have almost zero
cohomology); `F` is almost acyclic on `X` if `H^n(X, F)^a = 0` for `n > 0`. For a family
`𝔘 = (U_i → X)` the Čech complex `Č(𝔘, F)` (Mathlib `cechComplexFunctor` on the underlying presheaf)
is a complex of `V`-modules with almostification `Č(𝔘, F)^a`, and the augmented complex
`F(X) → Č(𝔘, F)` is almost exact if its cohomology is almost zero ([Berkeley] Lecture 7, proof of
Theorem 7.4.4, p. 53). The Čech-to-derived comparison for almost acyclic bases is
*almost-cech-acyclicity-criterion*. Define `Almost.Sheaf.IsAlmostZero` (`∀ U, S.IsAlmostZero (F.val.obj U)`), `Almost.Sheaf` (the Serre localization of `Sheaf J (ModuleCat V)` at almost
isomorphisms of sheaves), `Almost.Sheaf.toAlmost` (the exact localization `F ↦ F^a`),
`Almost.Sheaf.cohomologyModule` (the `V`-module structure on `H^n(X, F)`), `Almost.Sheaf.almostH`
(`H^n(X, F)^a := (toAlmost S).obj (H^n(X, F))`), `Almost.Sheaf.IsAlmostAcyclic` (`∀ n > 0, IsZero (almostH F n X)`) and `Almost.Sheaf.almostCech` (`(toAlmost S).mapHomologicalComplex` of the Čech
complex); prove that almost zero sheaves form a Serre class, `Almost.Sheaf.almostH_eq_zero_of_isAlmostZero`
(almost zero sheaves have almost zero cohomology in all degrees; `almostH` factors through
`toAlmost`) and `Almost.Sheaf.almostH_localization` (for `ϖ ∈ S.ideal`: `almostH F n X ≅ 0 ⇒ H^n(X, F) ⊗ V[1/ϖ] = 0`, P0.16). *Needs:* P0.5; P0.16; Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Sheaf.H'`,
`CategoryTheory.Sheaf.H.map`, `CategoryTheory.cechComplexFunctor`, `CategoryTheory.sheafIsAbelian`,
`SerreClassLocalization.abelian`.

Supporting result: almost Čech acyclicity on a basis implies almost acyclicity
(*almost-cech-acyclicity-criterion*). Let `F` be a sheaf of `V`-modules and `𝔅` a full subcategory
of `C` stable under fibre products such that every covering of an object of `𝔅` is refined by a
covering by objects of `𝔅` (e.g. rational subsets of an affinoid adic space with finite rational
covers, or affinoid perfectoid objects of a pro-étale or v-site). If for every `U ∈ 𝔅` and every
covering `𝔘` of `U` by objects of `𝔅` the augmented Čech complex `F(U) → Č(𝔘, F)` is almost exact,
then `H^n(U, F)` is almost zero for all `U ∈ 𝔅` and `n > 0` (and `H^0(U, F) = F(U)`) ([ECD] §8,
proof of Proposition 8.8, printed p. 43 in
[v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1709.07343v4), for the affinoid perfectoid v-site; [Berkeley]
Lecture 7, proof of Theorem 7.4.4, p. 53). [Berkeley] Theorem 7.4.4 and [Sch12] Proposition 6.14
obtain `H^i(X, O⁺)^a = 0` for `i > 0` on a perfectoid affinoid this way.
`Almost.Sheaf.almostCech_acyclicity_criterion` states the general basis criterion.
Induct on the cohomological degree: a class vanishes on a covering, the basis hypothesis
refines that covering, and the Čech-to-cohomology spectral sequence reduces to lower
positive degrees and positive Čech cohomology. Products and finite extensions preserve
almost-zero modules because `m² = m`. For the unit ideal this gives Cartan's criterion;
DiamondsAndVStacks D0 uses this specialization.

**Checks.**

- `Almost.Sheaf.test_point` (degenerate) — for the site on the terminal category (one object, only its identity arrow) with the trivial
  covering, `Almost.Sheaf J S ≌ Almost.Module S` and `almostH F n X = 0` for `n > 0`.
- `Almost.Sheaf.test_constant_residue` (computation) — for `S = ofValuationRing K°` and the constant
  sheaf `k = K°/K°°` on any site, `F` is almost zero, so `almostH F n X ≅ 0` for all `n`, even when
  `H^n(X, k) ≠ 0`.
- `Almost.Sheaf.test_not_acyclic` (non-example) — on the site of open subsets of the circle `S¹`,
  the constant sheaf `k` has `H¹(S¹, k) = k ≠ 0` but is almost acyclic: `IsAlmostAcyclic` must not
  be defined as vanishing of `H^n`.
- `Almost.Sheaf.test_classical` (compatibility) — for `S = classical V`, `almostH F n X` is
  Mathlib's `Sheaf.H'` of the underlying abelian sheaf with its `V`-module structure, via
  `Almost.Module.classicalEquiv`.

- Sectionwise annihilation is the defining equation, the classical setup detects the zero
  sheaf, and the zero setup kills every sheaf. These also test `almostZeroSheaf`.
- `toAlmost_zero_iff`, `toAlmost_classical`, `toAlmost_residue` — the quotient functor kills
  exactly the almost zero sheaves, is an equivalence classically, and kills sheaves whose
  sections are annihilated by the setup ideal. These characterize the Serre quotient `Sheaf`.
- `cohomologyModule_injective`, `cohomologyModule_zero_sheaf`, `cohomologyModule_sections` —
  positive derived sections vanish for injectives, all degrees vanish for the zero sheaf,
  and degree zero is nonzero when the sections are nonzero. The functor `sections` is
  evaluation of the underlying presheaf; `cohomologyModule` is its right derived functor.
- `almostH_zero_setup`, `almostH_classical`, `almostH_residue` — almost cohomology vanishes
  in the zero setup, detects ordinary cohomology classically, and vanishes in every degree
  for sectionwise almost zero coefficients.
- `IsAlmostAcyclic_injective`, `IsAlmostAcyclic_zero_setup`, `IsAlmostAcyclic_classical` —
  injectives are almost acyclic, every sheaf is almost acyclic in the zero setup, and the
  classical setup requires ordinary vanishing in positive degrees.
- `almostCech_empty`, `almostCech_zero_setup`, `almostCech_classical` — an empty family
  gives the zero complex, the zero setup kills every term, and classical almostification
  detects the cohomology of Mathlib's Čech complex. On a family over `X`, use the same
  construction on the slice category over `X`, so products are fibre products over `X`.


### Examples

The worked examples of this layer are the checks above, which run through three setups: the
classical setup `(V, V)`, where almostification is an equivalence and every almost notion is the
Mathlib notion; the zero setup `(V, ⊥)`, where every module is almost zero; and the valuation
setups `(𝒪_{ℂ_p}, 𝔪)` and `(K°, K°°)` for `K` the completion of `ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞})`, together with the
root setup `𝔽_p[t^{1/p^∞}]`. On the valuation setups the residue field is almost zero while `V/pV`
is not; `((K°°)^a)_* = K°` while `((K°/ϖ)^a)_* = Hom(K°°, K°/ϖ)` strictly contains `K°/ϖ`; `V^a` is
almost projective but not a projective object; and the quadratic extension `L = K(√p)`, `p ≠ 2`,
gives `L°a` uniformly almost finitely generated with bound `2`, almost finitely presented, finite
étale over `K°a` with `Tr(1) = 2` and perfect trace form, with a diagonal idempotent that is an
almost element but not an element of `L° ⊗_{K°} L°`, and with rank decomposition `r = 3`, `A = A_2`.
The non-examples are the discrete valuation ring `ℤ_p` (`m·m ≠ m`, `ℤ/p²` breaks closure under
extensions), the ideal `(t) ⊆ 𝔽_p[t]` without roots (which also satisfies (A) but not (B)), the
field, whose zero maximal ideal is idempotent and finitely generated, the root setup with
`ϖ_0 = 0` but `ϖ_1 ≠ 0`, the dual numbers `A[ε]/(ε²)` whose trace form `[[2, 0], [0, 0]]` is not
perfect, the module `V` which is not firm when `m ≠ V`, the proper ideal
`m` which is not a tensor unit before almostification, the infinite sum `⊕_ℕ K°` which is not almost
finitely generated, `V ×_k V → V` which shows `(−)_!!` does not preserve flatness, the non-faithful
functor `invert ϖ`, the naive cotangent complex of `A_* → B_*`, the unit ideal of `K°a` which is not tight,
the complex `V[1/ϖ]` which is almost exact modulo `ϖ` but not almost exact, and the constant sheaf
`k` on `S¹` which is almost acyclic with `H¹ ≠ 0`.

The Lean `example`s of `Suggested.lean` for this layer use the classical, zero, valuation and root
setups, with `ℤ_p`, `(t) ⊆ 𝔽_p[t]` and fields as non-examples: the zero setup pins `m̃ = 0` and the
failure of the unit comparison `m̃ → V` (P0.7); the classical setup pins almost isomorphisms as
bijections (with `2 : ℤ → ℤ` excluded), almost finite presentation as finite presentation, and the
`ε`-form of almost finite projectivity as finite projectivity; `m ↪ V` is an almost isomorphism; the
all-one and all-zero root chains give the classical and zero setups, while `ϖ_0 = 0` with `ϖ_1 ≠ 0`
gives a nonzero root ideal; over `𝒪_{ℂ_p}` the residue field is almost zero and `V/p` is not.
