## Layer P1: perfectoid Tate rings, tilts and untilts

Here `ℚ_p^cycl` is the completion of `⋃_n ℚ_p(ζ_{p^n})`, and `ℤ_p^cycl` is its valuation ring
(P1.31). A trailing `^` on a valued field denotes its completion.

The layer defines perfectoid Tate rings and perfectoid fields with their characterisations, the
tilt with its integral subrings and the sharp map, the almost setup `(R°, R°°)` of a perfectoid
Tate ring, Fontaine's `θ` with its primitive kernel, untilts and their classification by primitive
ideals of degree one, integral perfectoid rings and the integral/Tate dictionary, the tilting
equivalence over an arbitrary perfectoid base through primitive ideals, and the mod-`ϖ` equivalence over a perfectoid field, completed filtered
colimits, perfected Tate algebras and the standard examples. No perfectoid base field is fixed
for the ring-level theory; the field results explicitly assume a complete nontrivially normed
ultrametric field. The zero Tate ring is allowed. Here “of characteristic `p`” means `pR = 0`
when zero rings are allowed; Lean’s `CharP R p` asserts characteristic exactly `p` and therefore
requires `R ≠ 0`. In particular `tilt.charP` has a `Nontrivial R` hypothesis, while the tilt of
the zero ring is zero (characteristic one). Statements using Mathlib’s `PreTilt` or
`fontaineTheta` assume the integral ring is nonzero; their zero-ring cases use the unique map.

<a id="p1-1"></a>

### P1.1 perfectoid Tate rings, perfectoid algebras and perfectoid Tate pairs

The layer opens with the perfectoid Tate ring itself, its characteristic-`p` form and the
pseudo-uniformizers with compatible `p`-power roots that every perfectoid Tate ring has.

**Perfectoid Tate rings, perfectoid algebras and perfectoid Tate pairs.**
(*perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras*) Fix a prime `p`. Let `R` be a commutative topological ring
which is a Tate ring (Tau Ceti `TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing`), complete and Hausdorff (`CompleteSpace R`
and `T2Space R` for the uniform structure of the additive group), with power-bounded subring `R°`
(`TauCeti.Huber.powerBoundedSubring`). For a commutative ring `A` and ideals `I, J ⊆ A` with `p ∈ J`
and `x^p ∈ J` for every `x ∈ I`, write `Φ : A/I → A/J` for the ring homomorphism
`x mod I ↦ x^p mod J`. `R` is a perfectoid Tate ring if (a) `R` is uniform, i.e. `R°` is bounded in
`R` (`TauCeti.Huber.IsBounded`; the uniformity of AdicSpaces layer 4.2, [HK] Definition 2.3), and
(b) there is a pseudo-uniformizer `ϖ` of `R` (a topologically nilpotent unit,
`TauCeti.Huber.IsPseudoUniformizer`; necessarily `ϖ ∈ R°`) such that `ϖ^p` divides `p` in `R°`, not
merely in `R`, and `Φ : R°/ϖR° → R°/ϖ^pR°` is bijective. No perfectoid base field is fixed;
characteristic `0` and characteristic `p` are both allowed (for `pR = 0` the condition `ϖ^p | p` is
vacuous), and `p` may be a nonzero nonunit (as in a product `K × K♭`). Uniformity is not implied by
(b), and (b) with the divisibility cannot be replaced by surjectivity of Frobenius on `R°/p` alone
(`ℚ_p`). A perfectoid `R`-algebra is a perfectoid Tate ring `S` with a continuous ring homomorphism
`R → S`; morphisms are continuous `R`-algebra homomorphisms. A perfectoid Tate pair is a Huber pair
`(R, R⁺)` (`TauCeti.Huber.Pair`) with `R` perfectoid; the condition depends only on `R`
(*frobenius-surjective-on-plus-ring*, P1.17) ([ECD] §3, Definition 3.1, p. 14; [Berkeley] Lecture 6,
Definition 6.1.1, p. 41; [KL16] §3.3, Definition 3.3.1, p. 58; [AWS] §2.1, Definition 2.1.1, p. 49;
[BMS] §3.2, before Lemma 3.20, p. 26). In `Perfectoid`, define `IsPerfectoidTateRing` (the Prop-valued class on a complete
Hausdorff nonarchimedean Tate ring with fields `isBounded_powerBoundedSubring` and
`exists_pseudoUniformizer`); the second field states (b) elementwise: some `ϖ ∈ R°` is a
pseudo-uniformizer with `ϖ^p ∣ p` in `R°`, every `x ∈ R°` is a `p`-th power modulo `ϖ^p` (`Φ` is
surjective), and `ϖ^p ∣ y^p` forces `ϖ ∣ y` (`Φ` is injective). The ring homomorphisms packaging
`Φ` are `frobeniusQuot` (the ring homomorphism
`A ⧸ I →+* A ⧸ J`, `[x] ↦ [x^p]`, for a commutative ring `A`, prime `p`,
`p ∈ J`, and `x^p ∈ J` for every `x ∈ I`) and `frobeniusModPow`
(the case `I = (ϖ)`, `J = (ϖ^p)`, requiring `ϖ^p ∣ p` in `A`), with the simp rule `frobeniusQuot_mk`
(`frobeniusQuot I J _ _ (mk I x) = mk J (x ^ p)`); for a Huber pair use `IsPerfectoidTateRing p R`
directly. Prove `IsPerfectoidTateRing.of_surjective` (surjectivity of `Φ : R°/ϖ → R°/ϖ^p` suffices,
injectivity being automatic), that `Φ` is bijective for every
pseudo-uniformizer with `ϖ^p | p` in `R°`, `IsPerfectoidTateRing.iff_frobenius_surjective_modP`
(for `R` uniform: perfectoid iff some `ϖ` has `ϖ^p | p` in `R°` and Frobenius on `R°/p` is
surjective; uniformity cannot be dropped, since `ℂ_p[ε]/(ε²)` satisfies the right-hand side with
`ϖ = p^{1/p}` and is not perfectoid),
`IsPerfectoidTateRing.isReduced` (the perfectoid case of `TauCeti.Huber.IsUniform.isReduced`, the
supplied theorem for uniform Hausdorff Tate rings), `IsPerfectoidTateRing.iff_perfectRing` (for `CharP R p`:
perfectoid iff `PerfectRing R p`, P1.2), transport of the predicate along a
ring isomorphism that is a homeomorphism, via `TauCeti.Huber.map_powerBoundedSubring`,
`IsPerfectoidTateRing.prod` (`R × S` is perfectoid when `R`, `S` are: `(R × S)° = R° × S°` and
`(ϖ_R, ϖ_S)` is a pseudo-uniformizer; it rests on the instance `IsTateRing.instProd` making
`R × S` a Tate ring), `map_mem_powerBoundedSubring` (a continuous ring homomorphism
`f : A → S` from a Tate ring to a uniform Tate ring has `f(A°) ⊆ S°`, since `{x^N} ⊆ ϖ^{-k}A_0` for
some `k` and a ring of definition `A_0`, so `{f(x)^N}` lies in the bounded set `f(ϖ)^{-k}S°`),
and surjectivity of Frobenius on `R⁺/p` for every ring of integral elements. Check `IsPerfectoidTateRing.isUniform`
applies the field `IsPerfectoidTateRing.isBounded_powerBoundedSubring` to construct
`TauCeti.Huber.IsUniform`: condition (a) is the supplied uniformity predicate
([ECD] Definition 3.1, p. 14). Uniform Hausdorff Tate rings are reduced
(*perfectoid-tate-ring-is-reduced*): a nonzero nilpotent `x` gives `Rx ⊆ R°` (every `rx` is
nilpotent), and `Rx ∋ ϖ^{-n}x` for all `n` is unbounded (`ϖ^n·ϖ^{-n}x = x ↛ 0`), contradicting
boundedness, so every perfectoid Tate ring is reduced, while `ℂ_p[ε]/(ε²)` is not reduced, hence
not uniform ([Sch12] §5, Proposition 5.8, proof, pp. 23–24; [Berkeley] Proposition 6.1.6, proof,
p. 43). *Needs:* Tau Ceti `TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing`, `TauCeti.Huber.IsHuberRing`,
`TauCeti.Huber.IsPseudoUniformizer`, `TauCeti.Huber.powerBoundedSubring`, `TauCeti.Huber.IsBounded`,
`TauCeti.Huber.Pair`, `TauCeti.Huber.IsRingOfIntegralElements.mem_of_isTopologicallyNilpotent`,
`TauCeti.Huber.map_powerBoundedSubring`; Mathlib `CompleteSpace`, `T2Space`, `Ideal.Quotient.mk`,
`IsReduced`.

**Checks.**

- `perfectoid_padic_negative` (non-example) — `¬ IsPerfectoidTateRing ℚ_[p]`: a
  pseudo-uniformizer of `ℚ_p` has `|ϖ| = p^{-k}` with `k ≥ 1`, so `|ϖ^p| < |p|` and `ϖ^p ∤ p` in
  `ℤ_p`, although Frobenius on `ℤ_p/p = 𝔽_p` is bijective ([ECD] Remark 3.3).
- Non-example: `R = ℂ_p[ε]/(ε²)` (product topology on
  `ℂ_p ⊕ ℂ_pε`) is a complete Tate ring with `ϖ = p^{1/p}`, `ϖ^p = p`, and Frobenius surjective on
  `R°/p = 𝒪_{ℂ_p}/p` (as `ℂ_pε ⊆ R°` and `ℂ_pε = p·ℂ_pε`), but `R° ⊇ ℂ_pε` is unbounded, so `R` is
  not perfectoid; a definition omitting uniformity would accept it.
- `perfectoid_zero` (degenerate) — the zero ring is a perfectoid Tate ring (`0` is a
  topologically nilpotent unit and all quotients vanish).
- Computation: for `ℂ_p` (Mathlib `PadicComplex p`) with
  `ϖ = p^{1/p}`: `ϖ^p = p` and `Φ : 𝒪/ϖ → 𝒪/p` is bijective because every element of `𝒪_{ℂ_p}` has
  a `p`-th root.
- Characterisation: for the `t`-adic completion `R`
  of the perfection of `𝔽_p((t))`: `IsPerfectoidTateRing R ↔ PerfectRing R p`, and both hold; for
  `𝔽_p((t))` itself (`TauCeti.Huber.LaurentSeries.isTateRing`) both fail.

For prime `p` and a complete Hausdorff Tate ring `R` with `UniformSpace R`,
`IsUniformAddGroup R` and `IsTopologicalRing R`, the predicate `IsPerfectoidTateRing p R` is
equivalent to the Frobenius-modulo-`p` formulation that P3.17a's
sousperfectoid frames use; both use P1.1's predicate itself, so the equivalence is the criterion
`IsPerfectoidTateRing.iff_frobenius_surjective_modP` together with the boundedness field.
Both sides require bounded `R°`, a pseudouniformizer with `ϖ^p ∣ p` in `R°`,
and the Frobenius condition of [ECD] Remark 3.2, p. 14.
`IsUniformAddGroup.rightUniformSpace_eq` identifies the completeness structures.
No nonzero-ring or base-field hypothesis is imposed.

**Checks.** Forward: a P1.1 instance gives bounded `R°` and the modulo-`p` criterion; reverse:
bounded `R°` with the modulo-`p` criterion recovers the P1.1 predicate; nonuniform: an unbounded
power-bounded subring is rejected, even if Frobenius modulo `p` is surjective. The equivalence
includes the zero ring tested by `perfectoid_zero` above.

The ring of [ECD] Example 3.4(iv), p. 15 is explicit. Starting with
`CyclotomicToricPolynomial`, the monoid algebra over the power-bounded ring of
`padicCyclotomic` on the two systems of nonnegative `p`-power exponents, form
`CyclotomicToricQuotient` by `TU = p`. Complete at `T` to obtain
`CyclotomicToricIntegral`, then invert `T` to obtain `CyclotomicToricRing`.
The monomials `cyclotomicToricMonomial`, their parameter `cyclotomicToricParameter`,
its completion `cyclotomicToricCompletedParameter`, and `cyclotomicToricRoot`
are given by the quotient, completion, and localization maps.

**Checks.** For each of these eight definitions, `_roots` checks both coherent
root systems, `_relation` checks `TU = p` and invertibility of `T`, and
`_nonfield` checks that `p` is not invertible while `T^(1/p)` is a
pseudo-uniformizer. The affinoid space is `IsAffinoidPerfectoid.spa_ecd34iv`.

Lean: `Perfectoid.IsPerfectoidTateRing`, `IsPerfectoidTateRing.of_surjective`,
`IsPerfectoidTateRing.iff_frobenius_surjective_modP`, `IsPerfectoidTateRing.isUniform`,
`IsPerfectoidTateRing.isReduced`, `IsPerfectoidTateRing.prod`, `IsTateRing.instProd`, and
`isTateRing_of_nontriviallyNormedField` (a nontrivially normed ultrametric field is a Tate ring,
with ring of definition the closed unit ball). The Lean `example`s check that `ℚ_p` is not
perfectoid and that the zero ring is.

### P1.2 characteristic p: perfectoid equals perfect complete Tate

**In characteristic p, perfectoid Tate rings are exactly the perfect complete Tate rings.**
(*characteristic-p-perfectoid-iff-perfect*) Let `R` be a topological ring with `pR = 0`. Then `R`
is a perfectoid Tate ring iff `R` is a perfect complete Hausdorff Tate ring; for such `R`, `R°` and
every ring of integral elements `R⁺` are perfect, `Φ : R° → R°` is an automorphism, and every
pseudo-uniformizer satisfies the condition of P1.1, `ϖ^p | p = 0` being vacuous ([ECD] §3,
Proposition 3.5 and its proof, p. 15; [KL16] Remark 3.3.4, p. 59; [AWS] Example 2.1.2, p. 49;
[Sch12] Proposition 5.9, p. 24; [Bhatt] Example 3.1.2(3), p. 10). Hence the completed perfection of
`𝔽_p((t))` is a perfectoid field, `𝔽_p((t))` (a complete Tate ring,
`TauCeti.Huber.LaurentSeries.isTateRing`) is not perfectoid, and a nonarchimedean field of
characteristic `p` is a perfectoid field iff it is perfect. The Lean form
`IsPerfectoidTateRing.iff_perfectRing` is stated on a complete Hausdorff Tate ring `R` with
`CharP R p`, where it reads `IsPerfectoidTateRing p R ↔ PerfectRing R p`; the general topological
ring `R` of the prose is the special case once `R` is known to be complete Hausdorff Tate. *Needs:* P1.1;
*integral-elements-adically-complete*; *perfectoid-condition-independent-of-pseudouniformizer*;
*perfect-complete-tate-ring-is-uniform*; Mathlib `PerfectRing`, `frobeniusEquiv`, `CharP`; Tau Ceti
`TauCeti.Huber.LaurentSeries.isTateRing`.

Three supporting results. Rings of integral elements are adically complete
(*integral-elements-adically-complete*): let `R` be a complete Hausdorff uniform Tate ring,
`R⁺ ⊆ R°` a ring of integral elements (`TauCeti.Huber.IsRingOfIntegralElements`; `R⁺ = R°` allowed)
and `ϖ ∈ R⁺` a pseudo-uniformizer. Clause (a) states that the subspace topology of `R⁺` is the
`ϖ`-adic topology and `R⁺` is `ϖ`-adically complete and separated
(`IsAdicComplete (span {ϖ}) R⁺`). Uniformity makes `R°` bounded; since `R⁺ ⊆ R°` is open,
it is an open bounded subring, hence a ring of definition by
`TauCeti.Huber.exists_pairOfDefinition_ringOfDefinition_eq_iff`.
Apply AdicEtaleGeometry A1.0.2(i)'s `PairOfDefinition.isAdicComplete_of_completeSpace`
(*power-bounded-henselian-along-pseudouniformizer*) to this ring of definition and `ϖ`.
The general topology and completeness theorem is supplied there; this corollary uses the
boundedness/ring-of-definition bridge here.
The complements proved here: (b) `ϖ` is a nonzerodivisor of `R⁺` and `R = R⁺[1/ϖ]`; (c) if `ϖ | p`
in `R⁺`, then `R⁺` is `p`-adically complete and separated; (d) if `R ≠ 0` and `p` is topologically
nilpotent in `R`, then `p` is not a unit of `R⁺`. So for `R ≠ 0` perfectoid, `R⁺` satisfies the
hypotheses `Fact ¬IsUnit (p : R⁺)` and `IsAdicComplete (span {p}) R⁺` of Mathlib's `PreTilt.untilt`
and `WittVector.fontaineTheta` ([Stacks] Tag 090T (Lemma 10.96.8); [BMS] §3.1, before Definition
3.1, p. 19; [Wedhorn] Proposition 6.14, p. 49).
*Needs:* AdicEtaleGeometry A1.0.2(i); Tau Ceti
`IsUniform.isBounded_powerBoundedSubring`,
`exists_pairOfDefinition_ringOfDefinition_eq_iff`; Mathlib `IsAdicComplete`.

**Checks.**

- For `R = ℚ_p`, `R⁺ = ℤ_p` and `ϖ = p`, clause (a) gives `p`-adic completeness,
  (b) gives regularity and `ℚ_p = ℤ_p[1/p]`, and (d) excludes `p` as a unit of `ℤ_p`.
- For the zero ring all completeness and localization assertions hold, while `p` is a unit;
  clause (d) requires `R ≠ 0`.
- For the complete nonuniform Tate ring `ℂ_p⟨T⟩/(T²)`, its ring `R°` of integral elements
  contains every scalar multiple of `T`. Thus `T ∈ ⋂_n ϖⁿR°` for a scalar
  pseudo-uniformizer `ϖ`, and `R°` is not `ϖ`-adically separated; the boundedness bridge
  requires uniformity (AdicEtaleGeometry A1.0.2).

Injectivity of Frobenius is automatic and the perfectoid
condition is independent of the pseudo-uniformizer
(*perfectoid-condition-independent-of-pseudouniformizer*): for a complete Hausdorff Tate ring `R`,
(a) for every pseudo-uniformizer `ϖ` with `ϖ^p | p` in `R°`, `Φ : R°/ϖ → R°/ϖ^p` is injective;
(b) if `R` is uniform and `ϖ, ϖ'` are pseudo-uniformizers with `ϖ^p | p` and `ϖ'^p | p` in `R°`,
`Φ` is bijective for `ϖ` iff it is for `ϖ'`; equivalently `R` is perfectoid iff some `ϖ` has
`ϖ^p | p` in `R°` and Frobenius on `R°/p` is surjective (the surjectivity forms are
*frobenius-surjectivity-criterion*, P1.5), and then `Φ` is bijective for every such
`ϖ`; (c) the same for a ring of integral elements `R⁺`: if `ϖ ∈ R⁺`, `ϖ^p | p` in `R⁺` and
`x ∈ R⁺` with `x^p ∈ ϖ^pR⁺`, then `x ∈ ϖR⁺`. Parts (a) and (c) use only that `R°` (resp. `R⁺`) is
integrally closed in `R` and that `ϖ` is a unit of `R` (`TauCeti.Huber.isPowerBounded_of_isIntegral`,
`TauCeti.Huber.isIntegrallyClosedIn_powerBoundedSubring`); (b) uses uniformity and completeness
through *frobenius-surjectivity-criterion* ([ECD] §3, Remark 3.2, p. 14; [Berkeley] Remark 6.1.3,
p. 42; [BMS] Lemma 3.20, proof, p. 26; [Sch12] Proposition 5.5, proof, p. 23). In `ℚ_p^cycl`,
`ϖ = ζ_{p²} − 1` and `ϖ' = ζ_{p³} − 1` both satisfy `ϖ^p | p` and `Φ` is bijective for both; in
`ℂ_p` the conditions for `p^{1/p}` and `p^{1/p²}` coincide. A perfect complete Tate ring of
characteristic `p` is uniform (*perfect-complete-tate-ring-is-uniform*): for `R` complete,
Hausdorff and Tate with `pR = 0` and `PerfectRing R p`, `R°` is bounded, by the open mapping theorem
(`TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing.isOpenMap`, `TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing.exists_hasBasis_nhds_zero`) ([ECD]
Proposition 3.5, proof, p. 15; [Berkeley] Proposition 6.1.6, proof, p. 43; [KL16] Remark 3.0.3,
p. 54; [AWS] Example 2.1.2, p. 49). The `t`-adic completion of the perfection of `𝔽_p((t))` is
uniform with `R°` the completion of `𝔽_p[[t]]^{perf}`, while the non-uniform `𝔽_p((t))[ε]/(ε²)`
is not perfect (`ε` is nilpotent), consistently with the lemma.

Lean: `IsPerfectoidTateRing.iff_perfectRing`.

### P1.3 pseudo-uniformizers with compatible p-power roots and the spectral gauge

**Pseudo-uniformizers with compatible p-power roots and the spectral gauge.**
(*pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots*) Let `R` be a Tate ring. A pseudo-uniformizer
with compatible `p`-power roots is an element `ϖ♭ = (ϖ^{1/p^n})_{n≥0}` of the multiplicative monoid
`lim_{x↦x^p} R` (Mathlib `Perfection R p`) such that `ϖ := ϖ^{1/p^0}` is a pseudo-uniformizer of
`R` lying in `R°` with `ϖ^p | p` in `R°`. Then every `ϖ^{1/p^n}` is a pseudo-uniformizer in `R°`,
`ϖ^q := (ϖ^{1/p^n})^m` is well defined for `q = m/p^n ∈ ℤ[1/p]_{≥0}` (and for `q ∈ ℤ[1/p]` as a
unit of `R`), and, when `R` is perfectoid, `ϖ♭` is a pseudo-uniformizer of the tilt `R♭` with `(ϖ♭)♯ = ϖ`
(*tilt-integral-subrings*, P1.5). The gauge formula is defined for any such Tate ring; its norm properties require
`R` to be complete, Hausdorff and uniform. Attached to `ϖ♭` is the spectral gauge
`|x|_ϖ := inf{2^{-q} : q ∈ ℤ[1/p], ϖ^{-q}x ∈ R°}`, a power-multiplicative, submultiplicative,
ultrametric norm defining the topology of a nonzero `R`, with `|ϖ^qx|_ϖ = 2^{-q}|x|_ϖ`,
`R° = {x : |x|_ϖ ≤ 1}` and `R°° = {x : |x|_ϖ < 1}`; the normalisation `|ϖ|_ϖ = 1/2` is a
convention for nonzero `R`. On the zero ring the same infimum is zero; power-multiplicativity holds
there for positive exponents, and its exponent-zero form requires `R ≠ 0`. Changing `ϖ` gives an equivalent norm; it need not give a single real power of the old norm on a ring with several factors. The gauge is the spectral seminorm of
AdicSpacesPartII R0.4 (`Huber.spectralSeminorm`, Mathlib's `smoothingSeminorm`) applied to
its Tate norm datum `(R°, ϖ, 1/2)` (`Huber.TateNormDatum`). The compatible roots give the
`ℤ[1/p]`-exponent formula above; this formula and its `R°`-level identities are the added assertions. Existence is
*exists-pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots* (P1.4) ([ECD] §3, Lemma 3.10, p. 16; [Sch12]
Remark 3.5, p. 16; [Berkeley] Lemma 6.2.2, proof, p. 44). Define `PseudoUniformizerRoots` (structure
on `R`: `roots : Perfection R p` with `coeff 0 roots ∈ R°`, `IsPseudoUniformizer (coeff 0 roots)`
and `(coeff 0 roots)^p ∣ p` in `R°`), `PseudoUniformizerRoots.root`
(`root n := Perfection.coeffMonoidHom R p n ϖ♭ = ϖ^{1/p^n}`), `PseudoUniformizerRoots.rootPB` (`root n` in `R°`) and `PseudoUniformizerRoots.zpow`
(`zpow m n = (root n)^m` as a unit of `R`, with equal values whenever `m/p^n` agrees;
additivity in the exponent, `zpow_mul_p`, and membership in `R°` for `m ≥ 0`),
`PseudoUniformizerRoots.toTilt` (the underlying compatible sequence as an element of
`tilt R`; when `R` is perfectoid it is a pseudo-uniformizer with `sharp ϖ♭ = ϖ`) and `PseudoUniformizerRoots.gauge` (`|x|_ϖ ∈ ℝ≥0`); prove
the root recurrence using Mathlib’s `Perfection.coeffMonoidHom_pow_p'`,
that each `root n` is a pseudo-uniformizer in `R°`, and
`PseudoUniformizerRoots.nonempty` (every perfectoid Tate ring admits one). For a prescribed
pseudo-uniformizer `ϖ_1 ∈ R°` with `ϖ_1^p | p`, there is a compatible-root
parameter congruent to `ϖ_1` modulo `ϖ_1^p` ([ECD] Lemma 3.10, proof, p. 16). Prove that the gauge
is a norm (`|xy| ≤ |x||y|`, `|x + y| ≤ max(|x|, |y|)`, `|x| = 0 ↔ x = 0`), that it is
power-multiplicative (`|x^n| = |x|^n` for `n > 0`, or for all `n` when `R ≠ 0`), the simp rule
`|ϖ^qx| = 2^{-q}|x|`, the characterisations `x ∈ R° ↔ |x| ≤ 1` and
`IsTopologicallyNilpotent x ↔ |x| < 1`, and that the
`ϖ^qR°`, `q ∈ ℤ[1/p]`, form a neighbourhood basis of `0`. *Needs:* P1.1; Mathlib `Perfection`,
`Perfection.coeffMonoidHom`; Tau Ceti `TauCeti.Huber.IsPseudoUniformizer`,
`TauCeti.Huber.isPowerBounded_of_isIntegral`, `TauCeti.Huber.powerBoundedSubring`.

**Checks.**

- `gauge_padic_formula` (computation) — for `ℂ_p` and a compatible
  choice `ϖ♭ = (p^{1/p^{n+1}})_n`, `gauge x = 2^{-p v_p(x)}` for `x ≠ 0`, with `v_p(p) = 1`.
  Thus `gauge ϖ = 1/2`, `gauge (ϖ²) = 1/4`, `gauge p = 2^{-p}`, and `gauge 0 = 0`.
- `gauge_wrong_root` (non-example) — the condition `ϖ^p ∣ p` in `O_C`
  excludes `ϖ = p`: the purported quotient has norm `p^{p−1} > 1`, including at `p = 2`.
- `gauge_product` (non-example) — on `ℂ_p × ℂ_p`, take compatible
  zeroth roots `(a,a)` and `(a,a²)` with `a^{2p} = p`. Their gauges both give `1/2` at `(a,0)`;
  at `(0,a²)` they give `1/4` and `1/2`, respectively. No single real power relates the gauges.
- `roots_padic_empty` (non-example) — `IsEmpty (PseudoUniformizerRoots ℚ_[p])`:
  a pseudo-uniformizer of `ℚ_p` has valuation `k ≥ 1`, not divisible by every `p^n`, so it has no
  compatible system of `p`-power roots; and none satisfies `ϖ^p | p` in `ℤ_p`.
- `roots_charP_unique` (degenerate) — if `R` is a perfectoid Tate ring of characteristic `p`
  (equivalently perfect, P1.2), the compatible roots of a fixed `ϖ` are unique, so
  `PseudoUniformizerRoots` over `ϖ` is a subsingleton.
- Characterisation: `⋃_{q>0} ϖ^qR° = R°°`, the
  topologically nilpotent elements (*topologically-nilpotent-elements-as-root-ideal*, P1.9).

Lean examples check that `ℚ_p` has no pseudo-uniformizer with compatible roots, that `ℂ_p`
admits one with `root 0 ^ p = p` but none with `root 0 = p`, and that the zeroth root determines
the structure in a perfect characteristic-`p` Tate ring. The gauge is
specified in this README only.

### P1.4 the tilt of a perfectoid Tate ring

The tilt comes next: the ring `R♭ = lim_{x↦x^p} R`, its integral subrings, the sharp map, the
functoriality of tilting, the tilt of a uniform Tate ring that is not assumed perfectoid, the
comparison with Mathlib's `PreTilt`, and the almost setup `(R°, R°°)`.

**The tilt `R♭ = lim_{x↦x^p} R` of a perfectoid Tate ring.** (*tilt-of-perfectoid-tate-ring*) Let `R`
be a perfectoid Tate ring. Its tilt is `R♭ := lim_{x↦x^p} R`, the multiplicative monoid
`Perfection R p` of compatible sequences `(x^{(n)})_{n≥0}` with `(x^{(n+1)})^p = x^{(n)}`, with the
inverse-limit topology (induced from `∏_ℕ R`) and the uniformity of its additive topological group, pointwise multiplication and addition
`(x + y)^{(i)} = lim_{n→∞}(x^{(i+n)} + y^{(i+n)})^{p^n}`. The limit exists and `R♭` is a topological
ring of characteristic `p` which is perfect ([ECD] §3, Definition 3.9 and Lemma 3.10, p. 16; [AWS]
Lemma 2.7.1(b), p. 66; [Berkeley] Lemma 6.2.2, p. 44); the limit addition, the topology and the
ring axioms are those of the tilt `uniformTilt R` of the complete uniform Tate ring `R` with `p`
topologically nilpotent (*tilt-of-uniform-tate-ring*, P1.7, which needs no perfectoid hypothesis),
and what perfectoidness adds is the rest of this target. Concretely, for `ϖ♭` a pseudo-uniformizer
with compatible roots and `ϖ_0` any pseudo-uniformizer dividing `p` in `R°`
(for example `ϖ_0 = ϖ♭^{(0)}`), the submonoid `lim_{x↦x^p} R°` is identified with the ring
`lim_Φ R°/ϖ_0` by *inverse-limit-of-integral-elements-along-frobenius*, `R♭ = (lim R°)[1/ϖ♭]` as
monoids, and the ring structure of `R♭` is that of this localisation; it is given by the limit
formula and does not depend on `ϖ_0` or `ϖ♭` ([ECD] Lemma 3.10, proof, p. 16). The construction
uses `ϖ_0 | p` and the completeness of `R°`; additivity of the zeroth projection is not asserted
(P1.5). For a Huber pair `(R, R⁺)` with `R` perfectoid, the tilt pair is `(R♭, R♭⁺)` with
`R♭⁺ := lim_{x↦x^p} R⁺` (*rings-of-integral-elements-under-tilting*, P1.18). If `pR = 0` then
`x ↦ x^{(0)}` is an isomorphism `R♭ ≅ R`. Define `tilt` (`tilt R := Perfection R p`, a type synonym
carrying the ring structure above; notation `R♭`), `tilt.instCommRing` (`CommRing (tilt R)` with the
monoid structure of `Perfection R p`, together with `instTopologicalSpace` induced from `ℕ → R` and
`instIsTopologicalRing`), `tilt.charP` (`CharP (tilt R) p` for `R ≠ 0`; `PerfectRing (tilt R) p` also for `R = 0`),
`tilt.coeff` (`coeff n : tilt R →* R`, the `n`-th coordinate `Perfection.coeffMonoidHom R p n`, with
`coeff_pow : coeff (n + 1) x ^ p = coeff n x`), `tilt.sharp` (P1.5), `tilt.map` (P1.6) and
`Pair.tilt` (the Huber pair `(tilt R, lim_{x↦x^p} R⁺)`); prove extensionality using Mathlib’s `Perfection.extMonoid`, `tilt.coeff_add` (`Tendsto (fun m ↦ (coeff (i + m) x + coeff (i + m) y) ^ p ^ m) atTop (𝓝 (coeff i (x + y)))`), `tilt.coeff_zero`
(`coeff n 0 = 0`), `tilt.coeff_frobeniusEquiv_symm` (simp:
`coeff n ((frobeniusEquiv (tilt R) p).symm x) = coeff (n + 1) x`), `tilt.isPerfectoidTateRing`
(`tilt R` is a perfectoid Tate ring of characteristic `p`, *tilt-is-perfectoid-tate-ring*, P1.14),
`tilt.mem_powerBoundedSubring_iff` (`x ∈ (tilt R)° ↔ ∀ n, coeff n x ∈ R° ↔ coeff 0 x ∈ R°`),
`tilt.equivOfCharP` (for `CharP R p`: `tilt R ≃+* R`, `x ↦ coeff 0 x`, a homeomorphism) and
`tilt.integralEquivPreTilt` (`(tilt R)° ≃+* PreTilt R° p`, P1.8). *Needs:* P1.1; P1.3; P1.2;
P1.7's construction of `uniformTilt` and its ring and topology laws for the carrier;
*inverse-limit-of-integral-elements-along-frobenius*; *exists-pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots*;
Mathlib `Perfection`, `Perfection.coeffMonoidHom`, `Perfection.teichmuller_spec`,
`Localization.Away`, `PerfectRing`.

Check `tilt.coeff_mul` is `map_mul` applied to the monoid homomorphism `tilt.coeff`;
`map_one` likewise gives `coeff n 1 = 1`. These are the coordinatewise multiplicative
laws in [ECD] Definition 3.9, p. 16.

**Checks.**

- `tilt_cyclotomic_twice` (compatibility) — for `R = tilt (ℚ_p^cycl)`, `tilt R ≃+* R` via `coeff 0`, a homeomorphism
  (`tilt_cyclotomic_twice`). The field identification is P1.31.
- `tilt_cyclotomic_epsilon` (computation) — in `tilt ℚ_p^cycl`, `ε := (ζ_{p^n})_n` with

- `tilt_coordinate_nonadditive` (non-example) — in `tilt ℚ_p^cycl`,
  `coeff 0 (ε − 1) ≠ coeff 0 ε − coeff 0 1 = 0`: coordinatewise subtraction is not the ring

- `tilt.nontrivial_iff` (degenerate) — `Nontrivial (tilt R) ↔ Nontrivial R`; the tilt of the zero
  ring is zero.
- `tilt.isPerfectoidTateRing_charP` (computation) — for `R = ℚ_p^cycl`, `tilt R` is the
  perfectoid Tate ring `𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^` of characteristic `p`, with pseudo-uniformizer

The carrier in the cyclotomic Check is `completedPerfectLaurentFp`: start with
`PerfectLaurentPolynomial := 𝔽_p[t^{1/p^∞}]`, whose `perfectLaurentMonomial n` is
`t^{1/p^n}`, form its t-adic completion `PerfectLaurentIntegral`, and invert the image
`perfectLaurentParameter` of t. `perfectLaurentRoot n` is the image of that monomial in
the localization. `perfectLaurentTopology_basis` specifies the topology by powers of t
multiplying the integral completion ([ECD] Example 3.4(ii), p. 15, and Lemma 3.10, p. 16).
**Checks.** Each of these six constructions has the same three checks, with names
`<definition>_roots`, `<definition>_parameter`, and `<definition>_characteristic`:
successive roots have p-th power the preceding root; t is a nonunit in the integral
completion and a pseudo-uniformizer unit after localization; p is zero while t is

Two supporting results. The inverse limit of integral elements along Frobenius
(*inverse-limit-of-integral-elements-along-frobenius*): let `R` be a nonzero complete Hausdorff
uniform Tate ring, `R⁺` a ring of integral elements and `ϖ_0 ∈ R⁺` a pseudo-uniformizer dividing
`p` in `R⁺`. Projection `(x^{(n)})_n ↦ (x^{(n)} mod ϖ_0)_n` is a multiplicative bijection
`lim_{x↦x^p} R⁺ → lim_Φ R⁺/ϖ_0R⁺` and a homeomorphism for the inverse-limit topologies (`R⁺/ϖ_0`
discrete); the inverse sends `(x̄_0, x̄_1, …)` to `(x^{(i)})_i` with
`x^{(i)} = lim_{n→∞} x_{n+i}^{p^n}` for arbitrary lifts `x_j ∈ R⁺`. The multiplicative bijection
also holds algebraically for `p` in place of `ϖ_0`, and the ring homomorphism
`lim_Φ R⁺/p → lim_Φ R⁺/ϖ_0` induced by the quotient map is an isomorphism;
`R ≠ 0` makes `R⁺/ϖ_0` of characteristic `p`. Both bijections are Mathlib's
`Perfection.quotientMulEquiv p I : Perfection R⁺ p ≃* Perfection (R⁺ ⧸ I) p` for `I = span {ϖ_0}`
and `I = span {p}` (`R⁺` is `I`-adically complete for both by *integral-elements-adically-complete*
(a), (c), and `R⁺/I` has characteristic `p`), and `Perfection (ModP R⁺ p) p` is `PreTilt R⁺ p`;
Mathlib gives multiplicative isomorphisms and the ring structure only on the `Perfection (R⁺/I) p`
side. Give `lim_Φ R⁺/p = PreTilt R⁺ p` the topology transported from `lim_Φ R⁺/ϖ_0`
with discrete `R⁺/ϖ_0` factors. This topology is independent of the choice of `ϖ_0`, makes the
modulo-`p` comparison a homeomorphism, and preserves the displayed reduction formula on every
coordinate. It is not defined by making `R⁺/p` discrete: `p` need not be a pseudo-uniformizer
or a unit of `R`, and may be zero. The transported ring structure and these topological
comparisons with the subspace topology on `lim_{x↦x^p} R⁺` are proved here ([ECD] Lemma 3.10, proof, p. 16; [BMS] Lemma
3.2(i), p. 19; [KL15] Remark 3.4.10, p. 82; [Sch12] Lemma 3.4(i), proof, p. 16). For a perfectoid
field `K` and `R⁺ = K°` this is [Sch12] Lemma 3.4(i). If `R` is also perfect of characteristic `p`,
the zeroth projection identifies `lim_{x↦x^p} R⁺` with `R⁺` as topological rings. Here `R⁺` is
perfect because a `p`-th root in `R` of an element of `R⁺` is integral over the integrally closed
subring `R⁺`. The Lean statement `bijective_coeffZero_integralElements_of_perfectRing` carries
`CharP R p` and `PerfectRing R p` and states the algebraic bijectivity of this projection.

**Checks for the inverse-limit comparison.**

- For `R = ℚ_p`, `R⁺ = ℤ_p` and `ϖ_0 = p`, both inverse limits are the Teichmüller
  representatives, with their ring structure identified with `𝔽_p`; perfectoidness is unnecessary.
- For `K` the completed perfection of `𝔽_p((t))`, the zeroth projection identifies
  `lim_Frob K°` with `K°` in its valuation topology, as in `uniformTilt_charP`.
- For `R = 𝔽_p((t))`, `R⁺ = 𝔽_p[[t]]` and `ϖ_0 = t`, the hypotheses hold and
  `t ∣ p = 0`, but `lim_Frob R⁺ ≅ 𝔽_p`: the support of a series with `p^n`-th roots for every
  `n` is divisible by every `p^n`, hence contains only exponent zero. The zeroth projection
  includes the constants and misses `t`, which has valuation one and no `p`-th root.

Every perfectoid Tate ring has a
pseudo-uniformizer with compatible `p`-power roots (*exists-pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots*):
for `R` perfectoid (the zero ring allowed) and `ϖ_1` a pseudo-uniformizer with `ϖ_1^p | p` in `R°`,
there is `ϖ♭ ∈ lim_{x↦x^p} R°` with `ϖ := ϖ♭^{(0)} ≡ ϖ_1 mod ϖ_1^pR°`; then `ϖ = ϖ_1·u` with
`u ∈ (R°)^×`, `ϖR° = ϖ_1R°`, `ϖ^p | p` in `R°`, and `ϖ♭` is a pseudo-uniformizer with compatible
`p`-power roots; if `pR = 0` every pseudo-uniformizer has unique compatible roots ([ECD] Lemma 3.10
and its proof, p. 16; [Berkeley] Lemma 6.2.2, proof, p. 44; [BMS] Lemma 3.9, p. 22; Mathlib
`Perfection.coeff_surjective`). For `R = ℂ_p` and `ϖ_1 = p^{1/p}` the construction returns a unit
multiple of `p^{1/p}` with compatible roots; in characteristic `p`, `ϖ = ϖ_1` and
`ϖ^{1/p^n} = Φ^{-n}(ϖ_1)`.

### P1.5 the sharp map

**The sharp map `♯: R♭ → R` (continuous, multiplicative, not additive).** (*sharp-map*) For a
perfectoid Tate ring `R`, the sharp map `♯ : R♭ → R`, `x ↦ x♯ := x^{(0)}` (Mathlib
`Perfection.coeffMonoidHom R p 0` on the underlying monoid `Perfection R p`) is continuous and
multiplicative with `0♯ = 0`, and is not additive in general. It satisfies `(x^{1/p^n})♯ = x^{(n)}`;
`x ∈ R♭°` iff `x♯ ∈ R°`; `x♯ = 0` iff `x = 0`; for `x, y ∈ R♭°`, `(x + y)♯ ≡ x♯ + y♯ mod pR°`;
every element of `R°` is congruent modulo `pR°` to some `y♯` with `y ∈ R♭°`; reduction of `♯`
modulo `ϖ` is the ring isomorphism `R♭°/ϖ♭ ≅ R°/ϖ` of *tilt-integral-subrings*; and `(ϖ♭)♯ = ϖ`.
If `pR = 0`, `♯` is the ring isomorphism `R♭ ≅ R` ([ECD] §3, after Lemma 3.10, p. 16; [Berkeley]
§6.2, p. 45; [AWS] Definition 2.3.14, p. 56 (`♯ = θ ∘ [·]`); [Sch12] Lemma 3.4(i), proof, p. 16).
Define `tilt.sharp` (`sharp : tilt R →* R := Perfection.coeffMonoidHom R p 0`; notation `x♯`) and
`tilt.sharp₀` (the same map as a `MonoidWithZeroHom`); prove `tilt.continuous_sharp`,
`tilt.sharp_iterate_frobeniusEquiv_symm_pow` (simp:
`sharp (((frobeniusEquiv (tilt R) p).symm)^[n] x) ^ p ^ n = sharp x`, mirroring Mathlib
`PreTilt.untilt_iterate_frobeniusEquiv_symm_pow`), `tilt.mem_powerBoundedSubring_iff_sharp`
(`x ∈ (tilt R)° ↔ sharp x ∈ R°`), `tilt.sharp_eq_zero_iff` (`sharp x = 0 ↔ x = 0`),
`tilt.sharp_add_sub_mem` (for `x, y ∈ (tilt R)°`: `sharp (x + y) − sharp x − sharp y ∈ p • R°`),
`tilt.exists_sharp_sub_mem` (`∀ x ∈ R°, ∃ y ∈ (tilt R)°, x − sharp y ∈ p • R°`),
`tilt.sharpQuotEquiv` (the ring isomorphism `(tilt R)° ⧸ (ϖ♭) ≃+* R° ⧸ (ϖ)` induced by `sharp`),
`tilt.sharp_toTilt` (simp: `sharp ϖ♭.toTilt = ϖ`), the gauge identity `|sharp x|_ϖ = |x|_{ϖ♭}`
(*spectral-norm-under-sharp*, P1.7) and `tilt.sharp_eq_untilt` (under `(tilt R)° ≃+* PreTilt R° p`,
`sharp` is Mathlib's `PreTilt.untilt`, P1.8). *Needs:* P1.4; *tilt-integral-subrings*;
*frobenius-surjectivity-criterion*; Mathlib `Perfection.coeffMonoidHom`,
`Perfection.coeff_surjective`.

**Checks.**

- `sharp_cyclotomic_two_terms` (non-example) — in `tilt ℚ_p^cycl`: `sharp (ε − 1) ≠ sharp ε − sharp 1 = 0`
  (a ring homomorphism `sharp` would fail this).
- `sharp_epsilon` (computation) — `sharp ε = 1` in `tilt ℚ_p^cycl`, and `sharp p♭ = p` in
  `tilt ℂ_p` for `p♭ = (p^{1/p^n})_n`.
- `sharp₀_zero`, `sharp₀_one`, `sharp₀_multiplication` — the zero-preserving form of sharp
  sends zero to zero and one to one and preserves products; `sharp₀_apply` identifies it
  with the zeroth coordinate. The cyclotomic subtraction Check also applies to this map.
- `tilt.sharp_ringEquiv_of_charP` (degenerate) — if `CharP R p`, `sharp` is additive and is the
  ring isomorphism `tilt.equivOfCharP`.
- `sharp_eq_zero_iff_test` (characterisation) — for `R = ℂ_p × ℂ_p♭`, a perfectoid Tate ring,
  `sharp x = 0` only for `x = 0`.

Two supporting results. The Frobenius-surjectivity criterion with the pseudo-uniformizer condition
kept (*frobenius-surjectivity-criterion*): let `R` be a complete Hausdorff uniform Tate ring and
`ϖ ∈ R°` a pseudo-uniformizer with `ϖ^p | p` in `R°` (a hypothesis, not a conclusion; `R°` is
`ϖ`-adically complete by *integral-elements-adically-complete*). The following are equivalent:
(i) `Φ : R°/ϖ → R°/ϖ^p` is surjective; (ii) Frobenius on `R°/p` is surjective; (iii) every element
of `R°/ϖpR°` is a `p`-th power. The same equivalences hold for any ring of integral elements `R⁺`
with `ϖ ∈ R⁺` and `ϖ^p | p` in `R⁺`. The divisibility is essential: surjectivity of Frobenius on
`R°/p` without any `ϖ` with `ϖ^p | p` does not give perfectoidness (`ℚ_p`). The criterion is a
statement about any ring `A` that is `π`-adically complete with `π^p | p`: surjectivity of the
relative Frobenius `A/π → A/π^p`, `[x] ↦ [x^p]`, of Frobenius on `A/p` and of Frobenius on `A/πp`
are equivalent, and for `A = R°` one takes `π = ϖ`. Negative control, separating the relative
Frobenius from the Frobenius endomorphism of `A/π`: for `A = ℤ_p[π]` with `π^p = p` (so `π = p^{1/p}`),
and `u` the class of `π` in `A/p`, the endomorphism `x ↦ x^p` of `A/π ≅ 𝔽_p` is bijective; the
relative Frobenius `A/π ≅ 𝔽_p → A/π^p = A/p ≅ 𝔽_p[u]/(u^p)` has image the constants `𝔽_p`; and
Frobenius on `A/p ≅ 𝔽_p[u]/(u^p)` also has image `𝔽_p`. So (i) and (ii) miss `u`, and Frobenius on
`A/πp` is not surjective either, `A/p` being a quotient of `A/πp`: all three conditions of the
criterion fail together, and bijectivity of the Frobenius endomorphism of `A/π` says nothing about
perfectoidness. A Lean `example` states that `u` is not a `p`-th power in `(ZMod p)[X]/(X^p)`
([ECD] Remark 3.2, p. 14; [BMS] Lemma 3.9 (i)–(iii), p. 22; [Berkeley] Remark 6.1.3, p. 42; [KL15]
Remark 3.4.9, p. 81; [AWS] Remark 2.1.5, p. 50; Mathlib `IsAdicComplete`). The integral subrings of
the tilt (*tilt-integral-subrings*): for `R` perfectoid with tilt `R♭`, `ϖ♭` with compatible roots
and `ϖ = (ϖ♭)♯` (so `ϖ^q | p` for `q ≤ p`), (a) `R♭° = lim_{x↦x^p} R° = {x ∈ R♭ : x^{(n)} ∈ R°` for
all `n} = {x : x^{(0)} ∈ R°}`, and for every pseudo-uniformizer `ϖ_0` of `R` dividing `p` in `R°`
the projection isomorphisms `R♭° ≅ lim_Φ R°/ϖ_0 ≅ lim_Φ R°/p` are
*inverse-limit-of-integral-elements-along-frobenius* (P1.4) for `R⁺ = R°`;
(b) `ϖ♭` is a pseudo-uniformizer of `R♭`, `R♭°` is an open and bounded subring whose subspace
topology is the `ϖ♭`-adic one, and `R♭ = R♭°[1/ϖ♭]`; (c) for `q ∈ ℤ[1/p]` with `0 < q ≤ p`,
`x ↦ x^{(0)} mod ϖ^qR°` induces a ring isomorphism `R♭°/ϖ♭^qR♭° ≅ R°/ϖ^qR°`, in particular
`R♭°/ϖ♭ ≅ R°/ϖ`; (d) the kernel of `R♭° → R°/ϖ^q` is `ϖ♭^qR♭°` ([ECD] Lemma 3.10 and the text
after it, p. 16; [Berkeley] Lemma 6.2.2, p. 44; [BMS] Lemma 3.10, proof, p. 23; [Sch12] Lemma
3.4(iii), p. 16; Tau Ceti `TauCeti.Huber.IsPowerBounded`, `TauCeti.Huber.isPowerBounded_of_isIntegral`;
Mathlib `Perfection.coeff_surjective`). For a perfectoid field `K`: `K♭° = lim K° ≅ lim_Φ K°/ϖ` and
`K♭°/ϖ♭ ≅ K°/ϖ`; for `R = K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩`: `R♭°/ϖ♭ = (K°/ϖ)[T^{1/p^∞}]` ([Sch12] Proposition 5.20,
proof).

### P1.6 functoriality of tilting

**Functoriality of tilting: `f ↦ f♭`.** (*tilt-functoriality*) A continuous ring homomorphism
`f : R → S` between perfectoid Tate rings induces `f♭ : R♭ → S♭`, `(x^{(n)})_n ↦ (f(x^{(n)}))_n`
(Mathlib `Perfection.mapMonoidHom p f` on the underlying monoids), a continuous ring homomorphism
with `(f♭x)♯ = f(x♯)`, `f♭(R♭°) ⊆ S♭°`, `id♭ = id` and `(g ∘ f)♭ = g♭ ∘ f♭`; on `R♭°/ϖ♭ ≅ R°/ϖ` it
induces the reduction of `f`. No condition on plus rings enters the ring-level statement. A
morphism of Huber pairs `(R, R⁺) → (S, S⁺)` (`TauCeti.Huber.Pair.Hom`) with `R, S` perfectoid
induces a morphism of the tilt pairs. Hence tilting is a functor from perfectoid Tate rings (resp.
pairs) to perfectoid Tate rings (resp. pairs) of characteristic `p`, and a perfectoid `R`-algebra
`S` gives a perfectoid `R♭`-algebra `S♭` ([Berkeley] Theorem 6.2.7, p. 45; [AWS] Definition 2.3.2,
p. 54; [ECD] Theorem 3.13, p. 17). Define `tilt.map` (`map f : tilt R →+* tilt S` for `f` continuous,
with underlying monoid hom `Perfection.mapMonoidHom p f`), `Pair.tiltHom` (`Pair.Hom P Q ↦ Pair.Hom P.tilt Q.tilt`, compatible with `id` and `comp`), `tilt.mapEquiv` (a ring isomorphism `R ≃+* S` that
is a homeomorphism induces `tilt R ≃+* tilt S`) and `tiltFunctor` (the functor from perfectoid Tate
rings with continuous ring homomorphisms to perfectoid Tate rings of characteristic `p`, and its
slice version from perfectoid `R`-algebras to perfectoid `R♭`-algebras); prove `tilt.coeff_map`
(simp: `coeff n (map f x) = f (coeff n x)`), `tilt.sharp_map` (simp: `sharp (map f x) = f (sharp x)`), `tilt.map_id`, `tilt.map_comp` (`map (g.comp f) = (map g).comp (map f)`),
`tilt.continuous_map`, `tilt.map_mem_powerBoundedSubring` (`x ∈ (tilt R)° → map f x ∈ (tilt S)°`)
and `tilt.mapQuot_comm` (the square `(tilt R)°/(ϖ♭) ≅ R°/(ϖ) → S°/(f ϖ) ≅ (tilt S)°/(map f ϖ♭)`
commutes). For `g ∈ Gal(ℚ_p^cycl/ℚ_p)` with cyclotomic character `χ(g)`, `g♭(ε) = ε^{χ(g)}`
([Berkeley] Example 6.2.4). *Needs:* P1.4; P1.5; P1.1; Mathlib `Perfection.mapMonoidHom`; Tau Ceti
`TauCeti.Huber.Pair.Hom`.

**Checks.**

- `map_id_test` (degenerate) — `tilt.map (RingHom.id ℂ_p) = RingHom.id`.
- `tilt.map_inclusion_epsilon` (computation) — for the continuous inclusion `ι : ℚ_p^cycl → ℂ_p`,
  `tilt.map ι ε = ε`.
- `tilt.map_equivOfCharP` (characterisation) — for `f : R → S` continuous between perfectoid rings
  of characteristic `p`, `tilt.equivOfCharP ∘ tilt.map f = f ∘ tilt.equivOfCharP`.
- `Pair.tiltHom_plus` (compatibility) — for a `Pair.Hom f : (R, R⁺) → (S, S⁺)`, `Pair.tiltHom f`
  carries `lim R⁺` into `lim S⁺`.

The equivalence `tilt.mapEquiv` is pinned by
`tilt.mapEquiv_coeff`: its n-th coordinate is the image under the original ring isomorphism.
**Checks.** `tilt.mapEquiv_identity` fixes every coordinate; `tilt.mapEquiv_swap` interchanges
the two factors of a product; `tilt.mapEquiv_charP` agrees with the original isomorphism under
the characteristic-p identification by the zeroth coordinate.

### P1.7 the tilt of a complete uniform Tate ring

**The tilt `B♭ = lim_{x↦x^p} B` of a complete uniform Tate ring in which `p` is topologically
nilpotent.** (*tilt-of-uniform-tate-ring*) Let `B` be a complete Hausdorff uniform Tate ring in
which `p` is topologically nilpotent (`B` is not assumed perfectoid) and `B⁺ ⊆ B°` a ring of
integral elements. Its tilt is `B♭ := lim_{x↦x^p} B` (Mathlib `Perfection B p`) with the
inverse-limit topology, pointwise multiplication, `x♯ := x^{(0)}`, and addition
`(x + y)^{(i)} := lim_{n→∞}(x^{(i+n)} + y^{(i+n)})^{p^n}`. Then: (a) the limit exists and makes `B♭`
a perfect topological ring of characteristic `p`; `♯` is continuous and multiplicative;
`B♭⁺ := lim_{x↦x^p} B⁺ = {x : x♯ ∈ B⁺}` is an open subring and `B♭° := lim_{x↦x^p} B° = {x : x♯ ∈ B°}`; `B♭` is complete and Hausdorff; (b) for every ideal of definition `I ⊆ B⁺` with `p ∈ I` (for
instance `I = (p, ϖ)` for a pseudo-uniformizer `ϖ ∈ B⁺`; Kedlaya asks `p ∈ I^p`), reduction
`x ↦ (x^{(n)} mod I)_n` is an isomorphism of topological rings `B♭⁺ ≅ lim_Φ B⁺/I` (discrete
factors), and, for `B ≠ 0` (so that `p` is not a unit of `B⁺`, as Mathlib's `PreTilt` requires),
`B♭⁺ ≅ PreTilt B⁺ p` algebraically, with topology on `PreTilt` transported from
`lim_Φ B⁺/I`, independently of `I`, rather than from discrete `B⁺/p` factors;
(c) if `B` has a pseudo-uniformizer `ϖ` with `ϖ^p | p` in `B°`
and compatible `p`-power roots, i.e. `ϖ = ϖ♭♯` for some `ϖ♭ ∈ B♭`, then `ϖ♭` is a pseudo-uniformizer
of `B♭`, `B♭°` is open and bounded with the `ϖ♭`-adic topology, `B♭ = B♭°[1/ϖ♭]`, the spectral
gauges satisfy `|x|_{ϖ♭} = |x♯|_ϖ`, and `B♭` is a complete uniform perfect Tate ring of
characteristic `p`, hence a perfectoid Tate ring; this applies whenever there is a continuous ring
homomorphism `f : A → B` from a perfectoid Tate ring `A`, with `ϖ♭ := f♭(ϖ_A♭)`; the closure in `B♭`
of a perfect subring containing `ϖ♭` and `ϖ♭⁻¹` is then a perfectoid Tate ring of characteristic
`p`; without compatible roots `B♭` need not be Tate; (d) a continuous ring homomorphism `g : B → C`
of such rings induces `g♭ : B♭ → C♭`, `(x^{(n)}) ↦ (g(x^{(n)}))`, a continuous ring homomorphism with
`(g♭x)♯ = g(x♯)`, functorially; (e) there is a unique ring homomorphism `θ_B : W(B♭⁺) → B⁺` with
`θ_B([x]) = x♯` (for `B ≠ 0` it is Mathlib `WittVector.fontaineTheta` for the `p`-adically
complete ring `B⁺`, in which `p` is not a unit; for `B = 0` it is the zero map),
natural in `B`: `θ_C ∘ W(g♭) = g ∘ θ_B`; it is not surjective in general; (f) if `B` is perfectoid,
`B♭` with `♯`, `g♭` and `θ_B` is the tilt of P1.4 with the sharp map, functoriality and `θ` of
P1.5, P1.6 and P1.18 ([AWS] Lemma 2.7.1 with (b), (c) and its proof, pp. 66–67; [AWS] Hypothesis
2.7.2, p. 67; [AWS] Lemma 2.8.4, proof, p. 70). Define `uniformTilt` (`uniformTilt B : Type := Perfection B p` with `CommRing` (limiting addition), `TopologicalSpace`, `IsTopologicalRing`,
`PerfectRing`, `CompleteSpace` and `T2Space` instances, and `CharP p` when `B ≠ 0`, for `B` complete Hausdorff
uniform Tate with `IsTopologicallyNilpotent (p : B)`), `uniformTilt.sharp` (`sharp : uniformTilt B →* B := Perfection.coeffMonoidHom B p 0`, continuous, with `sharp (x^{1/p^n})^{p^n} = sharp x`),
`uniformTilt.map` (`map g : uniformTilt B →+* uniformTilt C` for `g` continuous; continuous;
`sharp (map g x) = g (sharp x)`; `map_id`, `map_comp`) and `uniformTilt.theta` (`theta B : 𝕎 (lim B⁺) →+* B⁺` with `theta [x] = sharp x`, equal to `WittVector.fontaineTheta B⁺ p` under `plusEquiv`;
`theta C ∘ WittVector.map (map g) = g ∘ theta B`); prove `uniformTilt.coeff_add` (`coeff i (x + y) = lim_{n→∞} (coeff (i + n) x + coeff (i + n) y)^{p^n}`, in `Filter.Tendsto` form),
`uniformTilt.plusEquiv` (for an ideal of definition `I` of `B⁺` with `p ∈ I`: `lim B⁺ ≃+* Perfection (B⁺ ⧸ I) p`, a homeomorphism for discrete factors, from `Perfection.quotientMulEquiv`; and `lim B⁺ ≃+* PreTilt B⁺ p`), `uniformTilt.mem_powerBoundedSubring_iff` (`x ∈ (uniformTilt B)° ↔ sharp x ∈ B°`; likewise `x ∈ lim B⁺ ↔ sharp x ∈ B⁺`), `uniformTilt.isTateRing_of_sharp` (if `ϖ♭ : uniformTilt B` has `sharp ϖ♭` a pseudo-uniformizer of `B` with `(sharp ϖ♭)^p ∣ p` in `B°`, then `IsTateRing (uniformTilt B)`, `IsBounded (uniformTilt B)°`, `IsPerfectoidTateRing (uniformTilt B)`, and `gauge ϖ♭ x = gauge (sharp ϖ♭) (sharp x)`), `uniformTilt.isPerfectoidTateRing_closure` (under
`isTateRing_of_sharp`, the closure of the range of a ring homomorphism from a perfect ring whose
range contains `ϖ♭` and `ϖ♭⁻¹` is a closed subring that is a perfectoid Tate ring of characteristic
`p`) and `uniformTilt.equivTilt` (for `B` perfectoid, `uniformTilt B ≃+* tilt B`, the identity of
`Perfection B p`, a homeomorphism commuting with `sharp` and `map`). The limiting-addition construction and
its functoriality use complete uniform Tate rings alone; P1.4–P1.6 are its perfectoid
specialisations. *Needs:* the Huber-ring foundations; Mathlib `Perfection`, `Perfection.coeffMonoidHom`,
`Perfection.mapMonoidHom`, `Perfection.quotientMulEquiv`, `Perfection.teichmuller_spec`, `PreTilt`,
`WittVector.fontaineTheta`, `PerfectRing`; Tau Ceti `TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing`,
`TauCeti.Huber.IsBounded`, `TauCeti.Huber.powerBoundedSubring`,
`TauCeti.Huber.isPowerBounded_of_isIntegral`, `TauCeti.Huber.IsRingOfIntegralElements`.

**Checks.**

- `uniformTilt_cyclotomic` (computation) — for `B = ℚ_p^cycl`, `uniformTilt B` and `tilt B` are
  the same topological ring `𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^`, `t = ε − 1`, and `sharp` computed in either sends
  `t` to `lim_n (ζ_{p^n} − 1)^{p^n}`.
- `uniformTilt_padic` (non-example) — `uniformTilt ℚ_p ≃+* 𝔽_p` (Teichmüller representatives
  `{0} ∪ μ_{p−1}`, the elements of `ℚ_p` with compatible `p`-power roots; for `p = 2` the set is
  `{0, 1}`, as `−1` has no square root in `ℚ_2` and `1 + 4ℤ_2 ≅ ℤ_2` has no nonzero `2`-divisible
  element) with the discrete topology: it is not a Tate ring, and `ℚ_p` has no
  pseudo-uniformizer `ϖ` with `ϖ^p | p`, so (c) does not apply; a construction asserting that the
  tilt of every uniform Tate ring is Tate fails here.
- `uniformTilt_charP` (degenerate) — if `B` is a perfect uniform Tate ring of characteristic `p`,
  `sharp : uniformTilt B ≃+* B` is a topological ring isomorphism; `uniformTilt` of the zero ring
  is zero.
- `uniformTilt.isPerfectoidTateRing_of_hom` (characterisation) — for `f : A → B` continuous with
  `A` perfectoid and `B` uniform: `IsPerfectoidTateRing (uniformTilt B)`, and, for `B ≠ 0`,
  `CharP (uniformTilt B) p`; `map f ϖ♭` is a pseudo-uniformizer with `sharp (map f ϖ♭) = f ϖ`.

Supporting result: the spectral gauge is preserved by the sharp map (*spectral-norm-under-sharp*).
Let `R` be a perfectoid Tate ring, `ϖ♭` a pseudo-uniformizer with compatible roots, `ϖ = (ϖ♭)♯`,
and `|·|_ϖ`, `|·|_{ϖ♭}` the spectral gauges of `R` and `R♭` (P1.3; the second for `R♭` with its
pseudo-uniformizer `ϖ♭` and roots `ϖ♭^{1/p^n}`), normalised by `|ϖ| = |ϖ♭| = 1/2` when `R ≠ 0` (both gauges are zero when `R = 0`). Then
`|x♯|_ϖ = |x|_{ϖ♭}` for all `x ∈ R♭`; it is the norm Kedlaya–Liu put on the tilt by pullback along
`♯` ([Sch12] Lemma 5.21, proof, p. 27; [KL16] Theorem 3.3.8, proof, p. 60). For `K = ℚ_p^cycl` and
`ε = (ζ_{p^n})_n`: `|(ε − 1)♯| = lim |ζ_{p^n} − 1|^{p^n} = |p|^{p/(p−1)}`, which is `|ε − 1|` in
`K♭`.

The proposed Lean construction is `uniformTilt p B := Perfection B p`, with the inherited
inverse-limit topology and the uniformity of the new additive group. Boundedness of `B°` and
topological nilpotence of `p` are explicit `Fact` arguments. `uniformTilt.coeff_add` pins the
addition; `plusEquiv_coeff` pins reduction on every coordinate. The algebraic `plusEquiv`
requires `IsAdicComplete I B⁺` and `CharP (B⁺/I) p`; the latter restricts this signature to a
nonzero quotient. `theta_unique`, `theta_eq_fontaineTheta`, `theta_natural`, `map_id`, `map_comp`
and `equivTilt_coeff` specify the maps, rather than just their source and target types.

`uniformTilt.gauge_sharp` compares the two gauges for root systems related in every
coordinate by `coeff m (ψ.root n) = ϖ.root (n+m)`. `equivTilt_plus`, `equivTilt_theta` and
`equivTilt_map` identify the perfectoid specialization on integral subrings, Fontaine maps and
continuous homomorphisms ([AWS] Lemma 2.7.1 and §2.7).

### P1.8 the integral tilt is Mathlib's PreTilt

**The integral tilt `R♭⁺` is Mathlib's `PreTilt R⁺ p`, and `♯` is `PreTilt.untilt`.**
(*tilt-comparison-with-mathlib-pretilt*) Let `R` be a nonzero perfectoid Tate ring and `R⁺` a ring
of integral elements (e.g. `R°`); `R ≠ 0` is needed, as otherwise `p` is a unit of `R⁺ = 0`. Then
`R⁺` satisfies Mathlib's standing hypotheses `Fact ¬IsUnit (p : R⁺)` and `IsAdicComplete (span {p}) R⁺` (*integral-elements-adically-complete*, P1.2), and: (a) the subring `R♭⁺ = lim_{x↦x^p} R⁺` of
`R♭` is isomorphic as a topological ring to Mathlib's `PreTilt R⁺ p = Perfection (ModP R⁺ p) p` via
`x ↦ (x^{(n)} mod p)_n`: its algebraic multiplicative equivalence is
`Perfection.quotientMulEquiv` for `I = (p)`, with inverse built from
`Perfection.teichmuller`. Choose an actual pseudo-uniformizer `ϖ_0 ∈ R⁺` dividing `p` and give
`PreTilt R⁺ p` the topology transported along the algebraic comparison
`PreTilt R⁺ p ≃+* lim_Φ R⁺/ϖ_0`, with discrete `R⁺/ϖ_0` factors, from
*inverse-limit-of-integral-elements-along-frobenius* (P1.4). This topology is independent of
`ϖ_0` and makes the displayed map a homeomorphism; no discreteness of `R⁺/p` is assumed.
(b) Under this isomorphism `x ↦ x♯` on `R♭⁺` is
Mathlib's `PreTilt.untilt : PreTilt R⁺ p →* R⁺` (which is `Perfection.teichmuller` for `I = (p)`),
`PreTilt.coeff 0` is `♯ mod p` (`PreTilt.mk_untilt_eq_coeff_zero`), and the root compatibility
`(x^{1/p^n})♯^{p^n} = x♯` is `PreTilt.untilt_iterate_frobeniusEquiv_symm_pow`; (c) `R♭ ≅ (PreTilt R⁺ p)[1/ϖ♭]` (`Localization.Away`), the topology on `lim_{x↦x^p} R⁺` and on this localisation being
the part Mathlib does not supply.
Mathlib's `PreTilt` is thus the integral tilt of this layer; Mathlib has no ring structure on
`lim_{x↦x^p} R` and no tilt of a non-field Tate ring, which this layer supplies (the field case,
Mathlib's `Tilt` and `PreTilt.val`, is compared in P1.15) ([BMS] Lemma 3.2(i), p. 19; [KL15] Remark
3.4.10, p. 82; [Bhatt] Theorem 6.2.7(2), p. 47). For `R = ℂ_p`, `PreTilt 𝒪_{ℂ_p} p ≅ (ℂ_p)♭°` and
`PreTilt.untilt p♭ = p`; `WittVector p (PreTilt R⁺ p)` is Mathlib's `A_inf(R⁺)`, the source of
`WittVector.fontaineTheta` (P1.17). *Needs:* *inverse-limit-of-integral-elements-along-frobenius*
(P1.4); P1.5; Mathlib `PreTilt`, `PreTilt.untilt`, `PreTilt.mk_untilt_eq_coeff_zero`,
`PreTilt.coeff`, `Perfection.quotientMulEquiv`, `Perfection.coeff_zero_symm_quotientMulEquiv`,
`ModP`, `Localization.Away`.

**Checks.**

- For `R = ℂ_p`, reduction of every coordinate modulo `p` gives the algebraic comparison
  `PreTilt 𝒪_{ℂ_p} p ≅ (ℂ_p)♭°`; `PreTilt.untilt p♭ = p` and `PreTilt.coeff 0 p♭ = 0`.
- For `K` the completed perfection of `𝔽_p((t))`, the transported topology identifies
  `PreTilt K° p` with the nondiscrete valuation ring `K°`: the nonzero sequence `t^n` tends to
  zero. If instead each factor `K°/p = K°` is discrete, the Frobenius inverse limit is discrete,
  since its bijective zeroth projection has open singleton fibres. These topologies differ.
- For a pseudo-uniformizer `ϖ ∈ R⁺` with `ϖ^p ∣ p`, using `ϖ` or `ϖ^p` gives the same
  transported topology: both inverse-limit comparisons are homeomorphisms with
  `lim_{x↦x^p} R⁺` in its subspace topology, and the transition induced by
  `R⁺/ϖ^p → R⁺/ϖ` preserves reduction of every coordinate.

### P1.9 the almost setup of a perfectoid Tate ring

**The almost setup `(R°, R°°)` of a perfectoid Tate ring.** (*perfectoid-almost-setup*) Let `R` be a
perfectoid Tate ring. The pair `(R°, R°°)` is a basic setup for almost mathematics (P0.1: `R°°`
idempotent and `R°° ⊗_{R°} R°° ≅ R°°` flat), and so is `(R⁺, R°°)` for every ring of integral
elements `R⁺`. For an `R⁺`-module `M` the following are equivalent: (i) `M` is almost zero,
`R°°M = 0`; (ii) `ϖ'M = 0` for every pseudo-uniformizer `ϖ'` of `R`; (iii) `ϖ^{1/p^n}M = 0` for all
`n`, for one (equivalently any) pseudo-uniformizer `ϖ` with compatible `p`-power roots ([ECD] §3,
Definition 3.21, p. 19; [AWS] Definition 2.9.4, p. 73). The almost-zero modules form the Serre class
of P0.4, the almost categories `R°a-Mod` and `R⁺a-Mod` are the Serre quotients of P0.5 ([ECD]
Definition 3.23, p. 19), and restriction of scalars along `R⁺ → R°`, which is injective with almost
zero cokernel ([ECD] Example 3.22(ii), p. 19), induces an equivalence `R°a-Mod ≃ R⁺a-Mod` ([ECD]
after Definition 3.23, p. 19). The construction depends only on `R`. For a perfectoid field `K` it
is the classical setup `(K°, m_K)`, with `K°/m_K` almost zero and every almost zero `K°`-module a
`k`-vector space ([ECD] Example 3.22(i), p. 19). Define `almostSetup` (`almostSetup R : Almost.BasicSetup` with ring `R°` and ideal `topologicallyNilpotentIdeal R`) and `almostSetupPlus`
(`almostSetupPlus R⁺` with ring `R⁺` and ideal `R°° ∩ R⁺ = R°°`); the ideal of `almostSetup R` is
`topologicallyNilpotentIdeal R` by definition, its two fields being
`isIdempotentElem_topologicallyNilpotentIdeal` and `flat_tilde_topologicallyNilpotentIdeal`. Prove
`almostSetup_isAlmostZero_iff`
(`M` almost zero `↔ ∀ ϖ', IsPseudoUniformizer ϖ' → ϖ' • M = 0`), the root form
(`↔ ∀ n, ϖ^{1/p^n} • M = 0`, for any `ϖ♭` with compatible roots), that
`R° ⧸ R⁺` is almost zero as an `R⁺`-module,
`almostModuleEquivPlus` (restriction of scalars is an equivalence of the almost categories of `R°`
and `R⁺`), that a topological isomorphism of perfectoid Tate rings induces an
isomorphism of basic setups (the setup does not depend on `ϖ`), the field case (for a
perfectoid field `K`, `almostSetup K` is `(K°, m_K)`, the field case of P0.5) and the comparison
modulo `ϖ` (`R°/ϖ ≅ R♭°/ϖ♭` carries `R°°/ϖ` onto `R♭°°/ϖ♭`, identifying the almost
categories of `R°/ϖ` and `R♭°/ϖ♭`, used in P1.28). Theorem-level consumers: `H^i(Spa(R, R⁺), O⁺)`
is almost zero for `i > 0` ([ECD] Theorem 3.24; layer P2). *Needs:*
*exists-pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots* (P1.4); P1.3;
*topologically-nilpotent-elements-as-root-ideal*; P0.1; P0.2; P0.5; P0.6; Tau Ceti
`TauCeti.Huber.topologicallyNilpotentIdeal`, `TauCeti.Huber.IsRingOfIntegralElements`; Mathlib
`CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.IsSerreClass`.

**Checks.**

- `almost_residue` (computation) — for `K` a perfectoid field, `K° ⧸ m_K` is almost
  zero and `ϖ^{1/p^n}` acts by `0` on it for all `n`; in particular this holds for `K = ℂ_p`
  ([ECD] Definition 3.21 and Example 3.22(i), p. 19).
- `not_idempotent_padic` (non-example) — for `ℚ_p`, `(pℤ_p)² ≠ pℤ_p`, so `(ℤ_p, ℤ_p°°)` is not a
  basic setup; `ℤ_p/p` is killed by `p` but not by an idempotent ideal containing `p`.
- `almost_zero_base` (degenerate) — for `R = 0` every module is almost zero.
- `almost_principal_quotient` (characterisation) — for `K = ℂ_p`, the `𝒪`-module `𝒪/m` is almost
  zero while `𝒪/p𝒪` is not (`p^{1/p}` does not kill the class of `1`).
- `almostModuleEquivPlus_test` (compatibility) — for `K` the completed perfection of
  `𝔽_p(x)((t))` and `K⁺ ⊊ K°` the preimage of the valuation ring `𝔽_p[x]^{perf}_{(x)}` of the
  residue field `𝔽_p(x)^{perf}` (an open valuation subring of rank `2`, with `K°° ⊊ K⁺`),
  `K°a-Mod ≃ K⁺a-Mod`, and `K°/K⁺` is almost zero.
- `pair_eq_powerBounded_padicComplex` (non-example) — `ℂ_p` has no second ring of integral
  elements: an open integrally closed `K⁺ ⊆ 𝒪_{ℂ_p}` contains `m_{ℂ_p}` and corresponds to an
  integrally closed subring of the residue field `𝔽̄_p`, which is `𝔽̄_p` itself (every element is
  integral over `𝔽_p`), so `K⁺ = 𝒪_{ℂ_p}`; in particular `ℂ_p` has no open valuation subring of
  rank `2`, and a test of `almostModuleEquivPlus` on `ℂ_p` compares `K°` with itself.

Membership in the ideal of `almostSetupPlus` is topological nilpotence in `R`.
`almostModuleEquivPlus_restrict` identifies its equivalence functor, after almostification,
with ordinary restriction of scalars from `R°` to `R⁺` followed by almostification.

**Checks.**

- `almostSetupPlus_zero`, `almostModuleEquivPlus_zero`: over the zero ring the ideal and every almost module vanish.
- `almostSetupPlus_full`, `almostModuleEquivPlus_full`: for `R⁺ = R°`, the ideal is `R°°` and the equivalence functor is the identity.
- `almostSetupPlus_proper`, `almostModuleEquivPlus_proper`: a proper plus subring omits some power-bounded element, but every element of `R°°` carries it into the plus ring, and restriction is still an equivalence.

Supporting result: `R°° = ⋃ ϖ^{1/p^n}R°` is an idempotent flat ideal
(*topologically-nilpotent-elements-as-root-ideal*). Let `R` be a Tate
ring and `ϖ♭ = (ϖ^{1/p^n})_n` a pseudo-uniformizer of `R` with compatible `p`-power roots (for `R`
perfectoid, P1.3). Then the ideal `R°°` of topologically nilpotent elements of `R°`
(`TauCeti.Huber.topologicallyNilpotentIdeal`) equals `⋃_n ϖ^{1/p^n}R° = ⋃_{q∈ℤ[1/p]_{>0}} ϖ^qR°`;
it satisfies `(R°°)² = R°°` and is flat as an `R°`-module (a filtered union of the free rank-one
modules `ϖ^{1/p^n}R°`). For every ring of integral elements `R⁺`, `R°° ⊆ R⁺` and
`R°° = ⋃_n ϖ^{1/p^n}R⁺`. Hence `(R°, R°°)` and `(R⁺, R°°)` satisfy the hypotheses of
*root-ideal-basic-setup* (P0.2); the argument uses only that `R°` is open and integrally closed in
`R`, and no uniformity ([ECD] §3, Definition 3.21, p. 19, and §3 preamble, p. 14;
[Bhatt] Lemma 3.1.3(2), p. 10; Mathlib `Module.Flat`; Tau Ceti
`TauCeti.Huber.IsPowerBounded.isTopologicallyNilpotent_mul`,
`TauCeti.Huber.IsRingOfIntegralElements.mem_of_isTopologicallyNilpotent`). For a perfectoid field
`K`, `K°° = m_K` with `m_K² = m_K`; for `ℚ_p`, `ℤ_p°° = pℤ_p` and `(pℤ_p)² ≠ pℤ_p`: without
`p`-power roots the ideal of topologically nilpotent elements is not idempotent.

Lean: `isIdempotentElem_topologicallyNilpotentIdeal`, `flat_tilde_topologicallyNilpotentIdeal`
(*topologically-nilpotent-elements-as-root-ideal*), `almostSetup`, `almostSetup_isAlmostZero_iff`.

### P1.10 perfectoid fields

Perfectoid fields follow: the definition, its characterisation, the Gelfand-spectrum and uniform
Banach-field inputs behind Kedlaya's theorem that a perfectoid Tate ring which is a field is a
perfectoid field, the tilt of a perfectoid field against Mathlib's `Tilt`, primitive elements of
`W(R⁺)`, and the identification of Fontaine's `θ` with Mathlib's.

**Perfectoid fields.** (*perfectoid-field-definition*) A perfectoid field is a perfectoid Tate ring
`K` (P1.1) whose underlying topological ring is a nonarchimedean field: `K` is a field, complete
with respect to a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value `|·|` defining its topology (in Lean,
`NontriviallyNormedField K` with `IsUltrametricDist K` and `CompleteSpace K`; the Tate structure has
ring of definition `K°`, the closed unit ball, and any `0 < |ϖ| < 1` as pseudo-uniformizer; `K` is
nonzero, so `p` is not a unit of `K°`; residue characteristic `p` is forced by `|p| < 1`) ([ECD] §3,
Definition 3.6, p. 15). Equivalently (P1.11; [Sch12] Definition 3.1, p. 15; [Bhatt] Definition 3.1.1,
p. 9): `K` is a nonarchimedean field which is not discretely valued, `|p| < 1`, and Frobenius is
surjective on `K°/p`. Its value group is `p`-divisible (*perfectoid-field-value-group-p-divisible*,
P1.15). In characteristic `p` a perfectoid field is the same as a complete perfect nonarchimedean
field ([Sch12] §3, after Lemma 3.2, p. 15). A perfectoid Tate ring whose underlying ring is a field
is automatically a perfectoid field (P1.14); `ℚ_p` and all discretely valued fields are not
perfectoid. Define `IsPerfectoidField` (`class IsPerfectoidField (K) [NontriviallyNormedField K] [IsUltrametricDist K] [CompleteSpace K] : Prop`, extending `IsPerfectoidTateRing p K`) and
`Perfectoid.isTateRing_of_nontriviallyNormedField` (every nontrivially normed
ultrametric field, without a completeness hypothesis, is a Tate ring with ring of
definition the closed unit ball, power-bounded subring the closed unit ball and topologically
nilpotent ideal the open unit ball; Tau Ceti has the uniformity and the power-bounded description,
`TauCeti.Huber.IsUniform.of_normedDivisionRing`, `isPowerBounded_iff_norm_le_one`,
`isBounded_closedBall_zero`, and the Tate instance only for `ℚ_p`, `TauCeti.Huber.Padic.isTateRing`);
prove
`IsPerfectoidField.toIsPerfectoidTateRing`, `IsPerfectoidField.iff` (`IsPerfectoidField K ↔`
(valuation not discrete, in Lean: norms accumulate at `1`) `∧ ‖p‖ < 1 ∧ Surjective (frobenius (K°/p) p)`, P1.11),
the bound `‖p‖ < 1`, the existence of `ϖ` with `0 < ‖ϖ‖ < 1 ∧ ‖p‖ ≤ ‖ϖ‖ ^ p`, `IsPerfectoidField.valueGroup_pDivisible` (every element of `|K^×|` has a `p`-th root
in it), `IsPerfectoidField.iff_perfectRing` (for `CharP K p`: `IsPerfectoidField K ↔ PerfectRing K p`, P1.2), the statement that a perfectoid Tate ring which is a field is a perfectoid field (P1.14,
from `exists_absoluteValue_of_isField`), `tiltField.instIsPerfectoidField`
(the tilt of a perfectoid field is a perfectoid field of characteristic `p`, P1.15) and
`isPerfectoidField_padicComplex` (`ℂ_p`, Mathlib `PadicComplex p`, is a perfectoid field). *Needs:*
P1.1; Mathlib `NontriviallyNormedField`, `IsUltrametricDist`, `CompleteSpace`; Tau Ceti
`TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing`, `TauCeti.Huber.Padic.isTateRing`.

**Checks.**

- `field_padic_negative` (non-example) — `¬ IsPerfectoidField ℚ_[p]`: `ℚ_p` is discretely
  valued ([ECD] Remark 3.3), although Frobenius on `ℤ_p/p = 𝔽_p` is surjective.
- `field_padicComplex` (computation) — `IsPerfectoidField (PadicComplex p)`: the
  value group is `|p|^ℚ` and every element of `𝒪_{ℂ_p}` has a `p`-th root.
- Characterisation: for the completed perfection `K` of
  `𝔽_p((t))`, `IsPerfectoidField K` holds; `𝔽_p((t))` is not perfect and not a perfectoid field.
- `not_isPerfectoidField_trivial` (degenerate) — the perfect field `𝔽̄_p` with the trivial absolute
  value is not a nonarchimedean field in this sense (the absolute value must be nontrivial), so it
  is not a perfectoid field.
- Compatibility: for `K` a field with
  `IsPerfectoidTateRing K`, `IsPerfectoidField K` (Kedlaya, P1.14).

Mathlib’s proposed [perfectoid-field interface](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/pull/26389)
uses a rank-one valuation. The normed-field predicate here fixes a real-valued norm;
a comparison theorem, specified in this README only, matches it with the valuation formulation after choosing
a compatible absolute value. The comparison preserves topology, not a prescribed normalisation.

Lean: `IsPerfectoidField`, `isPerfectoidField_padicComplex`, `IsPerfectoidField.valueGroup_pDivisible`,
and `isTateRing_of_nontriviallyNormedField` (the Tate structure, also listed under P1.1); a Lean
`example` checks that `ℚ_p` is not a perfectoid field.

### P1.11 characterisation of perfectoid fields

**Characterisation of perfectoid fields.** (*perfectoid-field-characterisation*) Let `K` be a
nonarchimedean field (complete with a nontrivial rank-one nonarchimedean absolute value). Then `K`
is a perfectoid field iff (i) `K` is not discretely valued, (ii) `|p| < 1`, and (iii) Frobenius
`Φ : K°/p → K°/p` is surjective ([ECD] §3, Proposition 3.8 with (i)–(iii), p. 15; [Berkeley]
Proposition 6.1.9, proof, p. 43). Condition (i) cannot be dropped: `ℚ_p` and its unramified
extensions satisfy (ii) and (iii) ([ECD] Remark 3.3, p. 14; [Sch12] §3, after Definition 3.1,
p. 15). Hence [Sch12] Definition 3.1 agrees with [ECD] Definition 3.6, and a nonarchimedean field is
a perfectoid ring in Kedlaya's sense iff it is a perfectoid field ([AWS] Corollary 2.3.11, p. 55).
`ℂ_p`, `ℚ_p^cycl` and the completion of `ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞})` satisfy (i)–(iii) (P1.32a). *Needs:* P1.10;
Mathlib `NontriviallyNormedField`, `IsUltrametricDist`.

Lean: `IsPerfectoidField.iff`, with (i) stated as the accumulation of the norms at `1`.

### P1.12 Gelfand spectrum of a Banach ring

**The unit criterion on the Gelfand spectrum of a Banach ring.**
(*gelfand-spectrum-units-and-maximum-formula*) The Gelfand spectrum `M(A)` of a commutative
nonarchimedean Banach ring `A` (complete for a submultiplicative norm `|·|` with
`|a + b| ≤ max(|a|, |b|)`; not assumed to be over a field) — the bounded multiplicative seminorms
`α : A → ℝ_{≥0}` with the topology of pointwise convergence — together with its compactness, its
nonemptiness for `A ≠ 0` and Berkovich's maximum formula `|f|_sp = max_{α ∈ M(A)} α(f)` for the
spectral seminorm, is AdicSpacesPartIII R3.9 (*gelfand-spectrum-banach-ring*, API
`GelfandSpectrum`, `GelfandSpectrum.compactSpace_nonempty`, `GelfandSpectrum.smoothingFun_eq_sSup`);
it is used
here for arbitrary nonarchimedean Banach rings, with the hypotheses stated there. The one clause
absent there is this target's content: `f ∈ A` is a unit iff `α(f) ≠ 0` for every `α ∈ M(A)`
([KBF] Lemma 2.4, proof, p. 4). For a complete Tate ring the carrier `M(A)` is the Berkovich
spectrum that DiamondsAndVStacks D5 uses downstream. The unit criterion and the maximum formula are the form
used by Kedlaya's Banach-field theorem (P1.13) and by the pointwise sharp-approximation lemma
(*sharp-approximation-lemma*, P1.23). *Needs:* AdicSpacesPartIII R3.9
(*gelfand-spectrum-banach-ring*); Mathlib `MulRingSeminorm`, `RingSeminorm`,
`NonarchimedeanAddGroup`.

The proposed Lean form of the unit criterion, with no declaration in `Suggested.lean` yet, is
`gelfandSpectrum_isUnit_iff`, for a complete ultrametric
normed commutative ring. Its spectrum argument is written as the subtype of multiplicative
seminorms bounded by `C‖·‖` for some `C > 0`, the defining subtype of the spectrum owned by
AdicSpacesPartIII R3. No second spectrum definition is introduced.

### P1.13 uniform Banach fields over a nondiscretely valued field

**A uniform Banach field over a nondiscretely valued field is a nonarchimedean field.**
(*uniform-banach-field-over-nondiscrete-field*) Let `F` be a nonarchimedean field whose value group
`|F^×|` is dense in `ℝ_{>0}` (the discretely valued case is not covered by the proof, [KBF] Remark
3.9), and let `A` be a uniform Banach `F`-algebra (complete, with topology defined by a
power-multiplicative norm; equivalently the spectral seminorm `|·|_sp` is a norm defining the
topology) whose underlying ring is a field. Then `|·|_sp` is multiplicative, so `A` is a
nonarchimedean field ([KBF] Theorem 3.7 and its proof, pp. 10–11). The criterion used: a uniform
Banach field `A` is a nonarchimedean field iff `|t|_sp|t^{-1}|_sp = 1` for all `t ∈ A^×` ([KBF]
Remark 3.3, p. 8), because then `|x|_sp = |xy·y^{-1}|_sp ≤ |xy|_sp/|y|_sp`; the proof uses the
Berkovich spectrum (AdicSpacesPartIII R3.9 through P1.12: `M(A) ≠ ∅`, the unit criterion and
`|x|_sp = max_α α(x)`; [KBF] Lemma 2.4, proof, p. 4). Uniformity is essential: [KBF] Example 2.15, pp. 6–7, completes
`F(T_1,T_2,…)` for the norm
`β(x) = inf_{x=Σ_i x_i} max_i 2^{f(x_i)} α(x_i)`, where `α` is the multiplicative Gauss norm
and `f(x)` is the least number of initial variables needed to express `x`. This completion is
a nonuniform Banach field. The completion for `α` itself is a nonarchimedean field. The new
unit-criterion target of P1.12 is `GelfandSpectrum.isUnit_iff`; the norm target here is
`UniformBanachField.spectralNorm_mul` under the hypotheses of this paragraph. *Needs:* P1.12; Mathlib `NontriviallyNormedField`, `IsUltrametricDist`,
`CompleteSpace`.

### P1.14 a perfectoid Tate ring that is a field is a perfectoid field

**A perfectoid Tate ring whose underlying ring is a field is a perfectoid field.**
(*perfectoid-ring-field-is-perfectoid-field*) Let `A` be a perfectoid Tate ring (in the sense of
P1.1, with no perfectoid base field: such `A` need not be an algebra over any perfectoid field,
[KBF] Remark 4.3, p. 13) whose underlying ring is a field. Then the topology of `A` is defined by a
multiplicative absolute value, so `A` is a perfectoid field ([KBF] Theorem 4.2 and its proof (the
characteristic-`p` case via the base field `𝔽_p((z))^{perf}`, then the tilt), p. 13; answers [ECD]
§3, Remark 3.7, p. 15; [Berkeley] Remark 6.1.8, p. 43; [AWS] Theorem 2.9.1, p. 73). The theorem is
needed when the topology is given only by a ring of definition, e.g. for the field quotients
`ℚ_p^cycl` and `ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞})^` of Kedlaya's perfectoid ring over `ℚ_p` that lies over no
perfectoid field. *Needs:* P1.13; *tilt-is-perfectoid-tate-ring*; *perfectoid-field-iff-tilt-field*;
P1.5.

Two supporting results. The tilt of a perfectoid Tate ring is a perfectoid Tate ring of
characteristic `p` (*tilt-is-perfectoid-tate-ring*): for `R` perfectoid, `R♭` is a complete
Hausdorff uniform perfect Tate ring of characteristic `p`, hence a perfectoid Tate ring; `ϖ♭` is a
pseudo-uniformizer, `(R♭°, ϖ♭R♭°)` is a pair of definition (`TauCeti.Huber.PairOfDefinition`), and
`R♭ ≠ 0` iff `R ≠ 0` ([ECD] Lemma 3.10, p. 16; [Berkeley] Lemma 6.2.2, p. 44; [AWS] Lemma 2.7.1(b),
p. 66). A perfectoid Tate ring is a perfectoid field iff its tilt is (*perfectoid-field-iff-tilt-field*): for
`R` perfectoid with `ϖ♭` with compatible roots, `R` is a perfectoid field (a nonarchimedean field)
iff `R♭` is, and then the absolute values satisfy `|x|_{R♭} = |x♯|_R` when normalised by
`|ϖ♭|_{R♭} = |ϖ|_R`, the spectral gauges being those of P1.3 ([Sch12] Lemma 5.21 and its proof,
pp. 27–28; [KL15] Lemma 3.5.2(a), p. 82, and Example 3.3.8, p. 78; [AWS] Corollary 2.3.11). For a
perfectoid field `K`, `K × K♭` is perfectoid but not a field, and its tilt `K♭ × K♭` is not a field.

`UniformBanachField.spectralNorm_mul` states the spectral multiplicativity assertion
on a complete ultrametric normed `F`-algebra whose ring is a field. It assumes boundedness of the power-bounded elements for the given
norm and a nondiscrete value group on the complete nontrivially normed field `F`, as in [KBF]
Theorem 3.7, pp. 10–11. `exists_absoluteValue_of_isField` starts with the complete
Hausdorff perfectoid Tate topology and an algebraic field structure; its conclusion supplies an
ultrametric absolute value, a value strictly between zero and one, and the original neighbourhood
basis. It does not assume a multiplicative norm on that field ([KBF] Theorem 4.2, p. 13).

Lean: `exists_absoluteValue_of_isField`.

### P1.15 the tilt of a perfectoid field

**Tilt of a perfectoid field; comparison with Mathlib's Tilt and PreTilt.val.**
(*tilt-of-perfectoid-field*) Let `K` be a perfectoid field. Its tilt `K♭` (P1.4) is a perfectoid
field of characteristic `p` with absolute value `|x|_♭ := |x♯|`; `K♭° = lim_{x↦x^p} K° ≅ lim_Φ K°/ϖ`
is its valuation ring for any `ϖ ∈ K` with `|p| ≤ |ϖ| < 1` (so `ϖ | p` in `K°`); `|K♭^×| = |K^×|`;
`K♭°/ϖ♭ ≅ K°/ϖ` and `K♭°/m♭ ≅ K°/m`; `K♭ = K` if `char K = p`. Replacing `ϖ` by `(ϖ♭)♯` one may
assume `ϖ` has compatible `p`-power roots ([Sch12] Lemma 3.4(iii)–(iv) and Remark 3.5, p. 16;
[Berkeley] Remark 6.2.3, p. 44; [KL15] Lemma 3.5.2(a), p. 82). For `v : Valuation K ℝ≥0` the
absolute value, `O = K°` and `hv : v.Integers O`, the tilt is isomorphic to Mathlib's
`Tilt K v O hv p = FractionRing (PreTilt O p)`, and Mathlib's valuation `PreTilt.val K v O hv p`
satisfies `PreTilt.val x = v(x♯)` for `x ∈ PreTilt O p ≅ K♭°`. Prove
`tiltField.instIsPerfectoidField` (`tilt K` is a perfectoid field with this absolute
value), `tiltField.norm_def` (`‖x‖_{K♭} = ‖x♯‖_K`), `tiltField.valueGroup_eq` (`|K♭^×| = |K^×|` as
subgroups of `ℝ_{>0}`), `tiltField.integerEquiv` (`K♭° ≃+* lim_Φ K°/ϖ` for `ϖ | p`),
`tiltField.quotEquiv` (`K♭° ⧸ (ϖ♭) ≃+* K° ⧸ (ϖ)`), `tiltField.residueFieldEquiv`,
`tiltField.equivMathlibTilt` (`tilt K ≃+* Tilt K v O hv p`, restricting to `(tilt K)° ≃+* PreTilt O p`), `tiltField.preTiltVal_eq` (`PreTilt.val K v O hv p x = v (PreTilt.untilt x)`),
`tiltField.equivSelfOfCharP` (for `CharP K p`, `tilt K ≃+* K` isometrically) and `tiltField.map`
(a continuous embedding induces a continuous embedding of tilts; it is isometric if the
original embedding preserves the chosen absolute values, P1.6). For
`K = ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞})^`, `K♭ = 𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^` with `t = (p, p^{1/p}, …)` and `t♯ = p`. *Needs:*
P1.4; P1.5; P1.8; *tilt-is-perfectoid-tate-ring*; *perfectoid-field-iff-tilt-field*; Mathlib
`Tilt`, `PreTilt.val`, `PreTilt.isDomain`, `Perfection.teichmuller_spec`, `Valuation.Integers`.

**Checks.**

- `tiltField_padicComplex_pflat` (computation) — in `tilt ℂ_p`, `p♭ = (p^{1/p^n})_n` has
  `‖p♭‖ = ‖p‖` and `‖ε − 1‖ = ‖p‖^{p/(p−1)}`.
- `tiltField.equivMathlibTilt` (compatibility) — for `K = ℂ_p`: `tilt ℂ_p ≃+* Tilt ℂ_p v 𝒪_{ℂ_p} hv p` and `PreTilt.val` corresponds to the absolute value of the tilt.
- `tiltField.equivSelfOfCharP` (degenerate) — for `K` the completed perfection of `𝔽_p((t))`,
  `tilt K ≃+* K`.
- `uniformTilt_padic` (non-example) — for `ℚ_p` (not perfectoid), `PreTilt ℤ_p p ≃+* Perfection 𝔽_p p ≃+* 𝔽_p` and Mathlib's `Tilt ℚ_p v ℤ_p hv p ≃+* 𝔽_p` carries the trivial
  valuation. Here `v : Valuation ℚ_p ℝ≥0`, `hv : v.Integers ℤ_p`, and `v(p) ≠ 1` are Mathlib's
  inputs. The Check specifies the extension of `PreTilt.val` to the fraction field and its
  value `1` at every nonzero element. Thus the tilt lacks a nontrivial absolute value without
  the perfectoid hypothesis ([Sch12] Definition 3.1 and Lemma 3.4, pp. 15–16;
  Mathlib `PreTilt`, `PreTilt.val`, `Tilt` in `Mathlib/RingTheory/Perfection.lean`).

Two supporting results. The value group of a perfectoid field is `p`-divisible
(*perfectoid-field-value-group-p-divisible*): for `K` perfectoid with `Γ = |K^×| ⊆ ℝ_{>0}`, `Γ` is
`p`-divisible, and in characteristic `0` it is generated by the `|x|` with `|p| < |x| ≤ 1`; in
characteristic `p` this follows from perfectness ([Sch12] Lemma 3.2 and its proof, p. 15; [Bhatt]
Lemma 3.1.3(1), p. 10). `|ℂ_p^×| = |p|^ℚ` is `p`-divisible; `|ℚ_p^×| = |p|^ℤ` is not. Continuous
valuations of `K` and `K♭` correspond (*continuous-valuations-under-tilting*): for a perfectoid
field `K` with tilt `K♭`, `|·| ↦ |·|♭`, `|x|♭ := |x♯|`, is a bijection between continuous
valuations of `K` up to equivalence and continuous valuations of `K♭` up to equivalence, higher
rank included; continuity is Huber's (`TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.cont`), and continuous valuations
correspond to open valuation subrings `K⁺ ⊆ K°`, which contain `m`, i.e. to valuation subrings of
the common residue field `K°/m = K♭°/m♭` ([Sch12] Proposition 3.6 and its proof, p. 17; Mathlib
`Valuation.IsEquiv`). For a prime `p` and a complete nontrivially normed ultrametric field
`K` satisfying `IsPerfectoidField p K`, the comparison of continuous valuations states that
there is a homeomorphism from `spa (fieldMinimalPlus K)` to
`spa (Pair.tilt p (fieldBasePair p K).pair).plus` whose forward map is `spaTilt`.
The minimal plus ring is contained in every open valuation subring, so these carriers
include all continuous valuation classes, with no rank restriction. The target
*continuous-valuations-under-tilting* follows `fieldBasePair` in P2 and uses
`spaTiltHomeomorph` for that pair ([Sch12] Corollary 6.7(iii), pp. 34–35;
[Wedhorn] Remark 7.15(2), p. 60).

The normed presentation `tiltField p K` uses the compatible-sequence carrier of
`tilt p K`. `tiltField.toTilt_apply` identifies its ring operations, `norm_def` specifies its
norm, and `continuous_toTilt` identifies the topology. The global signatures `valueGroup_eq`,
`integerEquiv`, `residueFieldEquiv`, `equivMathlibTilt_integral` and `preTiltVal_eq` retain the
specified valuation and integral ring; Mathlib comparisons explicitly assume the library's
nonunit and adic-completeness hypotheses. The residue quotients use the ideals `‖x‖ < 1` in
the two power-bounded subrings. `equivSelfOfCharP` is an isometry for the specified norm.

`isField_iff_tilt_isField` states the field criterion without choosing a norm, including the
zero-ring boundary on both sides. The bound `‖p‖ < 1` and
`IsPerfectoidField.valueGroup_pDivisible` state the strict p bound and divisibility as an existence of a unit
whose norm has the prescribed p-th power ([Sch12] Lemmas 3.4 and 5.21).

### P1.16 primitive elements and ideals of degree one

**Primitive (distinguished) elements and ideals of degree 1 in `W(R⁺)`.**
(*primitive-degree-one-ideals*) Let `(R, R⁺)` be a perfectoid Tate pair of characteristic `p`. An
element `ξ = Σ_{n≥0} p^n[ξ_n] ∈ W(R⁺)` is primitive of degree `1` (distinguished) if `ξ_0` is
topologically nilpotent and `ξ_1` is a unit of `R⁺`; equivalently `ξ = [ξ_0] + p·u` with
`u ∈ W(R⁺)^×` ([AWS] Definition 2.3.4, p. 54; [KL16] Definition 3.2.3, p. 57). An ideal `J ⊆ W(R⁺)`
is primitive of degree `1` if it is principal with a primitive generator. Equivalently ([ECD] §3,
Definition 3.15, p. 17), `J` is generated by an element `p + [ϖ♭]α` with `ϖ♭ ∈ R⁺` a
pseudo-uniformizer and `α ∈ W(R⁺)`: every such element is primitive, and every primitive element is
a unit multiple of one of this form, because a topologically nilpotent element of `R⁺` is divisible
by a pseudo-uniformizer ([KL16] Lemma 3.2.2, p. 56; [AWS] Exercise 2.3.6, p. 54). `ξ_0 = 0` is
allowed ([KL16] Remark 3.2.5, p. 57): `ξ = p` is primitive and corresponds to the untilt `R`
itself; `p²` and `[ϖ♭]` are not primitive when `R ≠ 0`; over the zero ring every Witt vector is primitive. In the notation of an untilt `S`, `R = S♭` and
`R⁺ = S♭⁺`. The coordinate predicates themselves are defined for any commutative topological ring `S`;
the equivalences and regularity results below concern nonzero characteristic-`p` perfectoid
pairs (`CharP R p` in Lean) with perfect plus rings as above. The zero coordinate predicates
are tested separately.
Define `IsPrimitive` (for `ξ : WittVector p R⁺`: `IsTopologicallyNilpotent (ξ.coeff 0 : R) ∧ IsUnit (ξ.coeff 1)`) and `IsPrimitiveIdeal` (`J : Ideal (WittVector p R⁺)` with `∃ ξ, IsPrimitive ξ ∧ J = Ideal.span {ξ}`), together with `IsDistinguished` (a Witt vector whose first
Witt coordinate is a unit, the notion of [BMS] Remark 3.11, p. 23, used for `ker θ` in P1.18);
prove the Teichmüller form (`IsPrimitive ξ ↔ ∃ u : (W R⁺)ˣ, ξ = teichmuller p (ξ.coeff 0) + p * u ∧ IsTopologicallyNilpotent (ξ.coeff 0)`), that
`IsPseudoUniformizer ϖ → IsPrimitive (p + teichmuller p ϖ * α)` for every `α`, that every primitive
`ξ` is associated to such an element (`IsPrimitive ξ → ∃` unit `u`, pseudo-uniformizer `ϖ`, `α`,
`ξ = u * (p + [ϖ♭] α)`), that associates of primitive elements are primitive, the unit criterion
(`IsPrimitive ξ → IsPrimitive ξ' → ξ' = y * ξ → IsUnit y`,
*distinguished-element-criterion*, P1.18), that primitive elements are
nonzerodivisors ([Berkeley] Lemma 6.2.10, p. 46; [ECD] Lemma 3.16, p. 17),
`IsPrimitive.map` (for a morphism of perfectoid pairs of characteristic `p`,
`WittVector.map f` carries primitive elements to primitive elements, hence `J` to generators of
`J·W(R'⁺)`), that `p : W R⁺` is primitive (coefficients `(0, 1, 0, …)`),
`IsPrimitive.frobenius` (`φ(ξ)` and `φ^{-1}(ξ)` are primitive) and that a generator of `ker θ` is
primitive iff it is distinguished in the sense of [BMS] Remark 3.11, p. 23 (`IsDistinguished`). *Needs:* P1.2;
*witt-vectors-of-perfect-plus-ring*; Tau Ceti `TauCeti.Huber.IsPseudoUniformizer`; Mathlib
`WittVector`, `WittVector.teichmuller`.

**Checks.**

- `primitive_mixed_generators`, `primitive_two_coordinates` (computation) — in `W(𝒪_{ℂ_p♭})`, `p − [p♭] = p + [p♭]·(−1)` is
  primitive: its Witt coordinates are `(−p♭, 1, …)` for `p` odd and, since `−[x] = (x, x², x⁴, …)`
  for `p = 2`, `(p♭, 1 + (p♭)², …)` for `p = 2`; in both cases `ξ_0` is topologically nilpotent
  and `ξ_1` a unit. So is `Σ_{i=0}^{p−1}[ε]^{i/p}` (its image in `W(𝔽̄_p)` is `p`); in the proposed
  Lean form the element `ε` of `PrimitiveTests` is normalised by `coeff n ε = ζ_{p^{n+1}}`, i.e. it is
  the `ε^{1/p}` of P1.4, so the sum reads `Σ_{i<p} [ε]^i` there.
- `primitive_p_squared_and_teichmuller` (non-example) — for `R ≠ 0`, `p²` is not primitive (its Witt coordinate `ξ_1` is `0`),
  and neither is `[ϖ♭]`; a definition requiring only `ξ ∈ (p, [ϖ♭])` would accept them.
