- `primitive_p` (degenerate) — `p` is primitive, and the untilt along `(p)` is `(R, R⁺)`
  itself.
- On any topological commutative ring of characteristic `p`, `(p)` is a primitive ideal.
  Over a nonzero such ring, `(p²)` and the zero ideal are not: every element of either ideal
  has first Witt coordinate zero, so neither ideal has a primitive generator.
- Characterisation: in `W(𝒪_{ℂ_p♭})`, `Σ_{i<p}[ε]^{i/p}` is a
  unit multiple of an element `p + [ϖ♭]α`.

Supporting result: `A_inf = W(R⁺)` for a perfectoid pair of characteristic `p`
(*witt-vectors-of-perfect-plus-ring*). Let `(R, R⁺)` be a nonzero perfectoid Tate pair of characteristic
`p` (so `R` and `R⁺` are perfect, P1.2) and `ϖ♭ ∈ R⁺` a pseudo-uniformizer. Then `R⁺` is perfect,
`ϖ♭`-adically complete and `ϖ♭`-torsion free, and `A_inf(R, R⁺) := W(R⁺)` satisfies: (a) `W(R⁺)` is
`p`-torsion free and `p`-adically complete with `W(R⁺)/p = R⁺` (a strict `p`-ring; Mathlib
`WittVector.eq_zero_of_p_mul_eq_zero` and `WittVector.isAdicCompleteIdealSpanP`, using
the perfectness of `R⁺` from P1.2);
(b) every element is uniquely `Σ_{n≥0} p^n[x_n]` with
`x_n ∈ R⁺`; (c) `[ϖ♭]` is a nonzerodivisor, `W(R⁺)` is `[ϖ♭]`-adically complete and separated, and
`W(R⁺)/(p,[ϖ♭]) = R⁺/ϖ♭` — the `(p,[ϖ♭])`-adic completeness and separatedness of `W(R⁺)`, and the
Huber-ring structure of the `(p,[ϖ♭])`-adic topology, are Tau Ceti's
`WittVector.isAdicComplete_span_p_teichmuller`, `isHausdorff_span_p_teichmuller`,
`completeSpace_and_t2Space_adicTopology_span_p_teichmuller` and
`TauCeti.Huber.WittVector.isHuberRing_adicTopology_span_p_teichmuller` (for `R⁺` perfect and
`ϖ♭`-adically complete), and `isTateRing_adicTopology_span_p_teichmuller_iff` says that `W(R⁺)` with
this topology is not Tate; (d) `Σ p^n[x_n]` is a unit iff `x_0` is a unit
of `R⁺`; (e) the `(p,[ϖ♭])`-adic topology does not depend on `ϖ♭`; (f) `W(R⁺)[1/[ϖ♭]]` is the ring
`W^b(R)` of Witt vectors with bounded Teichmüller coordinates, independent of `ϖ♭` and of `R⁺` up to
the evident inclusions; (g) for every `p`-adically complete ring `S` and ring homomorphism
`R⁺ → S/p` there is a unique ring homomorphism `W(R⁺) → S` lifting it; Frobenius `W(Φ)` is an
automorphism ([Bhatt] Example 6.1.6, p. 43; [BMS] Lemma 3.2(ii), p. 19; [AWS] Definition 2.2.1,
Lemma 2.2.7 and Theorem 2.2.10, pp. 51–52; [Sch12] Remark 5.14, p. 25; Mathlib
`WittVector.teichmuller`, `Localization.Away`; Tau Ceti `WittVector.isAdicComplete_span_p_teichmuller`,
`TauCeti.Huber.WittVector.isHuberRing_adicTopology_span_p_teichmuller`). For `R = F` the perfect
field of AdicSpaces layer 6 and `R⁺ = 𝒪_F` the completeness clause is the library statement for
`A_inf = W(𝒪_F)` (P1.33).
One statement, specified in this README only, records `ϖ♭`-adic completeness and torsion freeness
of `R⁺`, the quotient `W(R⁺)/p ≃ R⁺`, and the three assertions in (c).

Lean: `IsDistinguished`, `IsPrimitive`, `IsPrimitiveIdeal`; the Lean `example`s check that `p` is
distinguished and primitive in characteristic `p` and that, over a nonzero ring of characteristic
`p`, `p²` and Teichmüller lifts are neither. The ideal examples accept `(p)` and reject `(p²)`
and the zero ideal over nonzero rings.

### P1.17 ECD's `θ` is Mathlib's `fontaineTheta`

**ECD's `θ` is Mathlib's `WittVector.fontaineTheta`; surjectivity from `surjective_fontaineTheta`.**
(*fontaine-theta-comparison-with-mathlib*) Let `R` be a nonzero perfectoid Tate ring and `R⁺` a
ring of integral elements. Mathlib's `WittVector.fontaineTheta R⁺ p : 𝕎(PreTilt R⁺ p) →+* R⁺`
(defined under `[Fact ¬IsUnit (p : R⁺)]` and `[IsAdicComplete (span {p}) R⁺]`, both supplied by
*integral-elements-adically-complete*, P1.2) corresponds, under `R♭⁺ ≅ PreTilt R⁺ p` (P1.8), to
ECD's `θ : W(R♭⁺) → R⁺`, `Σ_n p^n[r_n] ↦ Σ_n p^n r_n♯`. In particular `θ([x]) = x♯`
(`WittVector.fontaineTheta_teichmuller`) and `θ mod p` is `x ↦ x♯ mod p`
(`WittVector.mk_fontaineTheta`). Mathlib's `surjective_fontaineTheta` applies because Frobenius on
`R⁺/p` is surjective by *frobenius-surjective-on-plus-ring*, so `θ` is surjective. `θ` is the
unique ring homomorphism `W(R♭⁺) → R⁺` lifting `x ↦ x♯ mod p` ([AWS] Lemma 2.2.7 and Definition
2.7.3, p. 67; [ECD] §3, Lemma 3.14(i) and its proof (the ring-map check through the ghost map modulo
`ϖ^m`), p. 17; [KL16] Definition 3.3.6, p. 59; [BMS] Definition 3.5, p. 21). Mathlib's
`fontaineThetaInvertP` and `BDeRhamPlus R⁺ p` are built on this `θ`. For `R = ℂ_p`,
`fontaineTheta` sends `[p♭]` to `p` and `[ε]` to `1`; for `R` of characteristic `p`, `θ` is
reduction modulo `p`, `W(R⁺) → R⁺` ([Bhatt] Proposition 6.1.8, proof). *Needs:* P1.8;
*frobenius-surjective-on-plus-ring*; Mathlib `WittVector.fontaineTheta`, `surjective_fontaineTheta`,
`WittVector.fontaineTheta_teichmuller`, `WittVector.mk_fontaineTheta`, `fontaineThetaInvertP`,
`BDeRhamPlus`, `PreTilt.untilt`, `WittVector.ghostComponent`.

Supporting result: every ring of integral elements of a perfectoid Tate ring satisfies the
Frobenius condition (*frobenius-surjective-on-plus-ring*). Let `R` be a perfectoid Tate ring and
`R⁺ ⊆ R°` any ring of integral elements (open and integrally closed, so `R°° ⊆ R⁺`,
`TauCeti.Huber.IsRingOfIntegralElements.mem_of_isTopologicallyNilpotent`). Then (a) Frobenius on
`R⁺/p` is surjective, and every element of `R⁺/ϖpR⁺` is a `p`-th power for every pseudo-uniformizer
`ϖ ∈ R⁺` with `ϖ^p | p` in `R⁺`; (b) there is a pseudo-uniformizer `ϖ ∈ R⁺` with `ϖ^p | p` in `R⁺`
and `p/ϖ^p ∈ R°°`, and for every pseudo-uniformizer `ϖ ∈ R⁺` with `ϖ^p | p` in `R⁺`,
`Φ : R⁺/ϖ → R⁺/ϖ^p` is bijective; (c) consequently `(R, R⁺)` satisfies [ECD] Definition 3.1 with
`R⁺` in place of `R°`, which is the formulation of [AWS] Definition 2.1.1 and [KL16] Definition
3.3.1, and these definitions agree with ECD's: the perfectoid condition on a Huber pair depends on
`R` alone ([BMS] Lemma 3.20, proof, p. 27; [AWS] Remark 2.3.12 and Corollary 2.3.10, p. 55; [KL16]
Proposition 3.3.3, p. 58). For `K` a perfectoid field and `K⁺ ⊆ K°` an open valuation subring of
rank `2` (one exists iff the residue field of `K` is not algebraic over `𝔽_p`, e.g. for the
completed perfection of `𝔽_p(x)((t))`; `𝒪_{ℂ_p}` is the only ring of integral elements of `ℂ_p`),
Frobenius on `K⁺/p` is surjective.

### P1.18 Fontaine's `θ`: the primitive kernel

Fontaine's map `θ` is treated next: its primitive kernel for any perfectoid Tate
pair, the untilt along a primitive ideal, and the proof that the untilt is a perfectoid Tate pair
whose tilt is the pair one started from.

**Fontaine's `θ: W(S♭⁺) → S⁺` has kernel generated by a primitive nonzerodivisor.**
(*fontaine-theta-and-primitive-kernel*) Let `(S, S⁺)` be a perfectoid Tate pair (any
characteristic, no perfectoid base field) with tilt `(S♭, S♭⁺)`, and `θ : W(S♭⁺) → S⁺`,
`Σ[r_n]p^n ↦ Σ r_n♯p^n`, Fontaine's ring homomorphism. (a) `θ` is surjective, by Mathlib's
`surjective_fontaineTheta` through the identification of P1.17. (b) `ker θ` is generated by a
primitive element of degree `1`, which can be taken of the form `ξ = p + [ϖ♭]α` with `ϖ♭ ∈ S♭⁺` a
pseudo-uniformizer such that `(ϖ♭♯)^p | p` in `S⁺`, and `α ∈ W(S♭⁺)`; `ξ` is a nonzerodivisor.
(c) An element of `ker θ` generates `ker θ` iff it is primitive ([BMS] Remark 3.11, p. 23). (d) `θ`
extends to a surjection `W(S♭⁺)[1/[ϖ♭]] → S` with kernel `ξW(S♭⁺)[1/[ϖ♭]]`, and
`W(S♭⁺)/(ξ, [ϖ♭]) = S♭⁺/ϖ♭ ≅ S⁺/ϖ♭♯`. If `pS = 0` then `ker θ = (p)` ([ECD] §3, Lemma 3.14(ii) and
its proof (the auxiliary `f` with `f♯ ≡ p mod pϖR⁺`, reduction to an isomorphism modulo `[ϖ♭]`),
pp. 17–18; [Berkeley] Lemma 6.2.8, proof, p. 46; [AWS]
Lemma 2.7.5, p. 67; [KL15] Lemma 3.6.3, p. 88, for `ℚ_p`-algebras; [Bhatt] Proposition 6.1.8,
p. 43, the field case). For `S = ℂ_p`: `ker θ = (p − [p♭])`, and `Σ_{i<p}[ε]^{i/p}` is another
generator. *Needs:* P1.17; P1.16; *tilt-integral-subrings* (P1.5); P1.5;
*rings-of-integral-elements-under-tilting*; *distinguished-element-criterion*;
*quotient-by-primitive-element*.

Three supporting results. Rings of integral elements correspond under tilting
(*rings-of-integral-elements-under-tilting*): let `R` be perfectoid with tilt `R♭`, `ϖ♭` with
compatible roots satisfying `ϖ^p | p` in `R°`, where `ϖ = (ϖ♭)♯`; rings of integral elements are open, integrally closed and contained
in `R°`. (a) `R⁺ ↦ R♭⁺ := lim_{x↦x^p} R⁺ = {x ∈ R♭ : x♯ ∈ R⁺}` is an inclusion-preserving bijection
from rings of integral elements of `R` to those of `R♭`; the inverse sends `R♭⁺` to the preimage in
`R°` of the image of `R♭⁺` in `R♭°/ϖ♭ ≅ R°/ϖ`. (b) The isomorphism `R♭⁺/ϖ♭ ≅ R⁺/ϖ` of
*inverse-limit-of-integral-elements-along-frobenius* (P1.4) is compatible with `R♭°/ϖ♭ ≅ R°/ϖ`.
(c) On both sides, rings of integral elements correspond to integrally closed subrings of the
common quotient `R°/ϖ ≅ R♭°/ϖ♭` (equivalently of `R°/R°° ≅ R♭°/R♭°°`). Hence a perfectoid Tate pair
`(R, R⁺)` has tilt pair `(R♭, R♭⁺)`, and `R° ↦ R♭°` ([ECD] §3, Lemma 3.11, p. 17; [Berkeley] Lemma
6.2.5, p. 45; [Sch12] Lemma 6.2, proof, p. 30; [AWS] Lemma 2.7.10, p. 69; Tau Ceti
`TauCeti.Huber.IsRingOfIntegralElements`,
`TauCeti.Huber.mem_of_isTopologicallyNilpotent_of_isIntegrallyClosedIn`; Mathlib `integralClosure`,
`IsIntegrallyClosedIn`). For an open valuation subring `K⁺ ⊆ K°` of a perfectoid field, `K♭⁺` is
the open valuation subring of `K♭` with the same image in `K°/m = K♭°/m♭`; for `R = K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩`
and `R⁺ = R°`, `R♭⁺ = K♭°⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩`. Primitive elements are nonzerodivisors and divide each
other only up to units (*distinguished-element-criterion*): for `(R, R⁺)` a perfectoid Tate pair
of characteristic `p` (`R⁺` perfect, `ϖ`-adically separated and `ϖ`-torsion free,
*witt-vectors-of-perfect-plus-ring*), (a) every primitive `ξ ∈ W(R⁺)`, in particular every
`p + [ϖ♭]α` with `ϖ♭` a pseudo-uniformizer of `R⁺` and `α ∈ W(R⁺)`, is a nonzerodivisor ([ECD] §3,
Lemma 3.16 and its proof (division by `ϖ♭` and induction), p. 17, where the printed `α ∈ W(R⁺)` is
a misprint for `α ∈ W(R♭⁺)` in ECD's notation; [Berkeley] Lemma 6.2.10, p. 46, in characteristic-`p`
notation; [BMS] Lemma 3.10(i), p. 22); (b) if `ξ, ξ'` are primitive and `ξ' = yξ` with `y ∈ W(R⁺)`,
then `y` is a unit ([AWS] Remark 2.3.5, p. 54), so two primitive elements generating comparable
ideals are associate. In `W(𝒪_{ℂ_p♭})`, `p − [p♭]` and `ξ_cyc = Σ_{i<p}[ε]^{i/p}` both generate
`ker θ`, hence are associates ([Sch13] Lemma 6.3); `μ = [ε] − 1 = ([ε]^{1/p} − 1)·ξ_cyc` lies in
`ker θ` but does not generate it, the factor `[ε]^{1/p} − 1` having zeroth Witt coefficient
`ε^{1/p} − 1` in the maximal ideal, so membership in `ker θ` alone does not imply primitivity.
`W(R⁺)/ξ` is `[ϖ]`-torsion free and `[ϖ]`-adically complete (*quotient-by-primitive-element*): for
`(R, R⁺)` a perfectoid Tate pair of characteristic `p`, choose a primitive generator
`ξ = p + [ϖ]α` with `ϖ ∈ R⁺` a pseudo-uniformizer and `α ∈ W(R⁺)` (P1.16), `A⁺ := W(R⁺)/ξ` satisfies: (a) the image of
`[ϖ]` is a nonzerodivisor; (b) `A⁺` is `[ϖ]`-adically complete and separated, and its `[ϖ]`-adic
and `(p,[ϖ])`-adic topologies coincide; (c) `A⁺/[ϖ] ≅ W(R⁺)/(p,[ϖ]) = R⁺/ϖ`; (d) `A⁺` is
`p`-adically complete; (e) `ξW(R⁺)[1/[ϖ]] ∩ W(R⁺) = ξW(R⁺)`. These are the two properties [ECD]
Lemma 3.14 uses without proof ([ECD] Lemma 3.14, proof, p. 18; [BMS] Lemma 3.2(ii), p. 19; [Stacks]
Tag 090T). For `ξ = p − [p♭]` in `W(𝒪_{ℂ_p♭})`, `W/ξ ≅ 𝒪_{ℂ_p}`; for `ξ = p`, `W(R⁺)/p = R⁺`.

`tilt.sharpQuotEquiv` uses a small integral tilted element `t`, its sharp in `R⁺`, and the
hypothesis `t♯ ∣ p` in `R⁺`; `sharpQuotEquiv_apply` identifies the quotient map on every element.
`Pair.tilt_bijective` and `Pair.tilt_plus_le_iff` give the bijection and its order compatibility.
`tilt.primitive_iff_generates_kernel` requires membership in the Fontaine kernel before testing
primitivity. The Teichmüller form, the associate form, the stability under unit multiples, the unit
criterion and `IsPrimitive.frobenius` of P1.16 are over a perfect characteristic-p Tate pair.
`primitive_quotient_complete` specifies the same Teichmüller parameter in regularity,
adic completeness, p-adic completeness and the small quotient ([Berkeley] Lemmas 6.2.5,
6.2.8 and 6.2.10; [AWS] Remark 2.3.5; [BMS] Lemma 3.2(ii)).

Lean: `ker_fontaineTheta` (the kernel of Mathlib's `WittVector.fontaineTheta` is generated by an
`IsDistinguished` element).

### P1.19 the untilt along a primitive ideal

**The untilt of `(R, R⁺)` along a primitive ideal `J`: `(W(R⁺)[1/[ϖ]]/J, W(R⁺)/J)`.**
(*untilt-construction*) Let `(R, R⁺)` be a perfectoid Tate pair of characteristic `p`, `J ⊆ W(R⁺)`
a primitive ideal of degree `1` and `ϖ ∈ R⁺` a pseudo-uniformizer. The untilt of `(R, R⁺)` along
`J` is the pair `(A, A⁺)` with `A⁺ := W(R⁺)/J` and `A := A⁺[1/π]`, `π` the image of `[ϖ]`,
topologised so that `A⁺` is open with its `π`-adic (equivalently `(p,[ϖ])`-adic) topology;
equivalently `A = W^b(R)/J·W^b(R)` with `W^b(R) = W(R⁺)[1/[ϖ]]`. `A` is a complete Hausdorff Tate
ring with pseudo-uniformizer `π` and ring of definition `A⁺`, independent of the choice of `ϖ`; the
construction is functorial for morphisms of pairs `f` with `W(f)(J) ⊆ J'` (then
`J' = W(f)(J)·W(R'⁺)`), and comes with the multiplicative map `♯_J : R → A`, given on
`x ∈ R⁺` by `θ_J([x])` (`θ_J` the quotient map followed by localization), and extended by
inverting a pseudo-uniformizer, with `♯_J(ϖ) = π`. That `(A, A⁺)` is a perfectoid Tate pair with tilt `(R, R⁺)`
is P1.20 ([ECD] §3, Theorem 3.17, p. 18; [Berkeley] Theorem 6.2.11, p. 47; [AWS] Theorem 2.3.9,
p. 55, and Remark 2.3.3, p. 54; [Sch12] Remark 5.19, p. 27). Define `untilt` (`untilt (P : Pair R) J : Type`, the ring `W(R⁺)[1/[ϖ]] ⧸ J·W(R⁺)[1/[ϖ]]`, with the choice-free description
`W^b(R)/JW^b(R)`), `untiltPlus` (the subring `A⁺`, the image of `W(R⁺) ⧸ J` in `A`),
`untilt.instIsTateRing` (`IsTateRing`, `CompleteSpace`, `T2Space` and `NonarchimedeanRing`
instances, with pair of definition `(A⁺, πA⁺)`), the canonical `θ_J : W(R⁺)[1/[ϖ]] →+* untilt P J` from Mathlib’s
`IsLocalization.map` applied to `Ideal.Quotient.mk J`; its surjectivity and kernel are
`IsLocalization.map_surjective_of_surjective` and `IsLocalization.ker_map`, `untilt.sharp` (`sharp_J : R →* untilt P J`,
`x ↦ θ_J([x])`, continuous and multiplicative; `sharp_J ϖ` is a pseudo-uniformizer) and
`untilt.map` (for arbitrary ideals `J,J'`, a pair morphism with `W(f)(J) ⊆ J'`
induces a ring homomorphism; when both ideals are primitive this map is continuous;
`untilt.map_id`, `untilt.map_comp`, `untilt.continuous_map`); prove `untilt.quotEquiv` (`untiltPlus ⧸ (sharp_J ϖ) ≃+* R⁺ ⧸ (ϖ)`, for a
choice of `ϖ` for which `J` has a generator `p + [ϖ]α` as in *quotient-by-primitive-element*),
`untilt.congr_pseudoUniformizer` (canonical isomorphism between the constructions for two choices
of `ϖ`), `untilt.isPerfectoidTateRing` (the untilt is perfectoid with ring of integral elements
`untiltPlus`, P1.20), `untilt.tiltEquiv` (`tilt (untilt P J) ≃+* R`, identifying the plus rings and
`ker θ` with `J`, P1.20) and `untilt_p_recovery` (`untilt P (span {p}) ≃+* R`). *Needs:* P1.16;
*witt-vectors-of-perfect-plus-ring*; *quotient-by-primitive-element*; Mathlib `Localization.Away`,
`WittVector`; Tau Ceti `TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing`, `TauCeti.Huber.PairOfDefinition`,
`TauCeti.Huber.IsPseudoUniformizer`.

For every characteristic-`p` perfectoid Tate pair `P` and primitive ideal `J`,
`untilt.sharp_apply` specifies `sharp_J x = algebraMap (mk J [x])` for every `x : P.plus`.
For every pseudo-uniformizer `t : P.plus`, `untilt.nhds_zero_hasBasis` specifies the
neighborhoods of zero on the raw carrier `untilt p P J`: they have basis `π^n · untiltPlus`,
`n ∈ ℕ`, where `π = algebraMap (mk J [t])`. Thus the term at `n = 0` is the plus ring and
the term at `n = 1` is its principal ideal generated by `π`. For a morphism `f : P → P'`
of characteristic-`p` perfectoid Tate pairs and arbitrary ideals with `W(f)(J) ⊆ J'`,
`untilt.map_algebraMap` requires the induced map to send `algebraMap (mk J w)` to
`algebraMap (mk J' (W(f) w))` for every Witt vector `w`; no primitivity is needed for this
equation. For primitive `J`, `untilt.sharp_tiltEquiv` gives
`sharp_J (untilt.tiltEquiv x) = tilt.sharp x` for every `x : tilt p (untilt p P J)`.
`untilt.tiltEquiv_plus_kernel` specifies the restriction of this same equivalence to the
plus rings and requires its induced Witt-vector isomorphism to carry the Fontaine kernel
to `J` ([ECD] §3, Theorem 3.17, p. 18, with Lemma 3.14, pp. 17–18).

**Checks.**

- `untilt_large_quotient_negative` (non-example) — for `C = ℂ_p`, the class of `p` in
  `O_C/(p²)` is nonzero since `|p| > |p²|`. This quotient does not have characteristic `p`,
  whereas every quotient of `O_{C♭}` does. Thus reduction modulo the sharp of an arbitrary
  pseudo-uniformizer, such as `(p♭)²`, cannot give the comparison; the choice in the theorem
  is essential, also at `p = 2`.


- `untilt_p_recovery` (degenerate) — `untilt (R, R⁺) (span {p}) ≅ R` as topological rings, with
  `untiltPlus = R⁺`.
- `untilt_pflat` (computation) — for `R` the completed perfection of `𝔽_p((t))` and
  `J = span {p − [t]}`: the untilt is the completion of `ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞})` with `sharp_J t = p`
  ([AWS] Example 2.3.7).
- `untilt_cyclotomic_recovery` (computation) — for `J = span {Σ_{i<p}[1 + t]^{i/p}}` the untilt is
  `ℚ_p^cycl` ([AWS] Example 2.3.8).
- `untilt_not_primitive` (non-example) — for `R ≠ 0` and `J = span {p²}` (not primitive) the
  analogous quotient `W(R⁺)[1/[ϖ]]/(p²)` is not reduced: `p² = 0` there while `p ≠ 0`, because
  `W(R⁺)[1/[ϖ]]/(p) = R⁺[1/ϖ] = R ≠ 0`; hence it is not perfectoid (for `R = 0` every quotient is
  the zero ring, which is perfectoid).
- `untilt_quotEquiv_test` (characterisation) — for `J = span {p − [p♭]} ⊆ W(𝒪_{ℂ_p♭})` and
  `ϖ = p♭`: `sharp_J(p♭) = θ_J([p♭]) = p` (as `p − [p♭] ∈ J`) and `untiltPlus = 𝒪_{ℂ_p}`, so
  `untilt.quotEquiv` reads `𝒪_{ℂ_p}/(p) ≃+* 𝒪_{ℂ_p♭}/(p♭)`.

### P1.20 the untilt is a perfectoid Tate pair with tilt `(R, R⁺)`

**The untilt along a primitive ideal is a perfectoid Tate pair with tilt `(R, R⁺)`.**
(*untilt-is-perfectoid-pair*) For `(R, R⁺)` a perfectoid Tate pair of characteristic `p` and
`J ⊆ W(R⁺)` primitive of degree `1`, the untilt `(A, A⁺)` of P1.19 is a perfectoid Tate pair: `A`
is a perfectoid Tate ring, `A⁺ = W(R⁺)/J` is a ring of integral elements of `A` (open, integrally
closed, contained in `A°`), `A°/A⁺` is almost zero, and the identification `R⁺ ≅ lim_{x↦x^p} A⁺`
of *untilt-tilt-identification* extends to an isomorphism of perfectoid Tate pairs
`(R, R⁺) ≅ (A♭, A♭⁺)` under which `ker θ_A = J` ([AWS] Lemmas 2.6.14 and 2.7.9 and Theorem 2.3.9,
p. 55; [KL16] Theorem 3.3.8, p. 60; the converse functor of [ECD] Theorem 3.17 (stated before it as
straightforward to check, p. 18) and of [Berkeley] Theorem 6.2.11,
`(R, R⁺, J) ↦ (W(R⁺)[[ϖ]⁻¹]/J, W(R⁺)/J)`; [BMS] Lemma 3.21, p. 27). For `R` the completed perfection of `𝔽_p((t))` and
`J = (p − [t])` this gives `(ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞})^, ℤ_p[p^{1/p^∞}]^)`; `J = (p)` returns `(R, R⁺)`.
*Needs:* P1.19; *untilt-tilt-identification*; *perfectoid-tate-ring-from-integral-perfectoid*;
*quotient-by-primitive-element*; *frobenius-surjectivity-criterion*; P1.1. The supporting
*perfectoid-tate-ring-from-integral-perfectoid* uses P1.24's `IsIntegralPerfectoid` and
integral Frobenius criterion, constructed before this supporting result.

Two supporting results. The tilt of `W(R⁺)/J` is `R⁺`, and `θ` for `W(R⁺)/J` is the quotient map
(*untilt-tilt-identification*): in the situation of P1.19, with `J = ξW(R⁺)` primitive and
`A⁺ = W(R⁺)/J` `p`-adically complete (*quotient-by-primitive-element* (d)), let `θ_J : W(R⁺) → A⁺`
be the quotient map. Then (a) `A⁺/p ≅ R⁺/ξ_0R⁺` (`ξ_0` the zeroth Witt coordinate), Frobenius on
`A⁺/p` is surjective, and `x ↦ (θ_J([x^{1/p^n}]))_n` is a multiplicative bijection
`R⁺ → lim_{x↦x^p} A⁺` whose composite with reduction is a ring isomorphism
`R⁺ ≅ lim_Φ A⁺/p = PreTilt A⁺ p`; (b) under this identification Mathlib's `WittVector.fontaineTheta A⁺ p` is `θ_J`, so `ker θ_{A⁺} = J`; (c) `R = R⁺[1/ϖ] ≅ lim_{x↦x^p} A` as monoids ([KL16] Lemma
3.3.7 and Remark 3.3.9, p. 60; [AWS] Definition 2.3.14 and Remark 2.3.16, p. 56; [KL15] Lemma
3.4.2, p. 79; Mathlib `Perfection.quotientMulEquiv`, `WittVector.fontaineTheta`, `PreTilt`). For
`J = (p)` the identification is the identity; for `J = (p − [p♭]) ⊆ W(𝒪_{ℂ_p♭})`, `A⁺ = 𝒪_{ℂ_p}`
and this is `PreTilt 𝒪_{ℂ_p} p ≅ 𝒪_{ℂ_p♭}`. An integral perfectoid ring with a nonzerodivisor `π`
gives a perfectoid Tate ring (*perfectoid-tate-ring-from-integral-perfectoid*): let `R_0` be
`π`-adically complete and `π`-torsion free for some `π` with `π^p | p` in `R_0`, with Frobenius
surjective on `R_0/p` and `Φ : R_0/π → R_0/π^p` bijective (equivalently `R_0` integral perfectoid in
the sense of P1.24 with `π` a nonzerodivisor, [BMS] Lemma 3.10). Then `R := R_0[1/π]`, with `R_0`
open and `π`-adic, is a complete Hausdorff perfectoid Tate ring; after replacing `π` by a unit
multiple with compatible `p`-power roots `π^{1/p^n} ∈ R_0` ([BMS] Lemma 3.9, p. 22),
`R° = {x ∈ R : π^{1/p^n}x ∈ R_0` for all `n}` (the almost elements of `R_0`), `R_0 ⊆ R°`,
`πR° ⊆ R_0`, and `R°/R_0` is killed by every `π^{1/p^n}` ([BMS] Lemma 3.21 and its proof, p. 27;
[Sch12] Lemmas 5.6–5.7, p. 23; Tau Ceti `TauCeti.Huber.PairOfDefinition`, `TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing`,
`TauCeti.Huber.powerBoundedSubring`). For `R_0 = ℤ_p^cycl`, `π = ζ_{p²} − 1`: `R = ℚ_p^cycl` and
`R° = R_0`; for `R_0` the `p`-adic completion of `ℤ_p^cycl[T^{1/p^∞}]`: `R = ℚ_p^cycl⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩`
with `R° = R_0` ([ECD] Example 3.4(iii)).

**Checks.** The following use the actual localized Witt quotient and the comparison
of [ECD] Theorem 3.17, p. 18; [Berkeley] Theorem 6.2.11, p. 47.

- `untilt.sharp_zero_base` — over a zero characteristic-`p` base, every primitive
  untilt is zero and sharp takes every element to zero.
- `untilt.sharp_radical` — for an integral pseudo-uniformizer `t` and primitive
  `J = (p−[t])`, sharp sends `t²` to `p²` in the localized quotient.
- `untilt.sharp_nonadditive` — over `ℂ₂♭`, choose integral `t` with original
  sharp image `2` and primitive `J = (2−[t])`. Then `untilt.sharp` sends `t+t`
  to `0`, whereas the sum of its two images is `4 ≠ 0`. This excludes additivity.
- `untilt.map_zero_target` — over a nonzero characteristic-`p` base, enlarging
  `(p)` to the unit ideal kills the nonzero sharp image of any unit.
- `untilt.map_projection_values` — for `K = ℂ_p♭`, untilt the first projection
  `K×K → K` along `(p)`. It sends the sharp images of `(1,0)` and `(0,1)` to
  `1` and `0`, respectively, distinguishing the two projections.
- `untilt.map_noninjective` — over a nonzero characteristic-`p` base, the map
  from the quotient along `(p²)` to that along `(p)` kills the nonzero class
  of `p`, so the algebraic untilt map need not be injective. Its domain uses
  the algebraic quotient; `(p²)` is not primitive.
- `untilt.tiltEquiv_zero_base` — the tilt of an untilt over a zero base is
  zero, and every element has zero image under the specified comparison.
- `untilt.tiltEquiv_two_roots` — for compatible pseudo-uniformizer roots
  `ϖ_n` in the characteristic-`p` base, form the two tilt elements with
  coordinates `sharp(ϖ_n)` and `sharp(ϖ_{n+1})`. The comparison sends their
  sum to `ϖ_0+ϖ_1`.
- `untilt.tiltEquiv_not_frobenius` — for the same first root sequence over a
  nonzero base, its image is not `ϖ_0^p`. A nonzero topologically nilpotent
  unit cannot equal its `p`th power, so this excludes a Frobenius twist.

### P1.21 untilts are classified by primitive ideals

The classification of untilts follows, with marked untilts, the behaviour of strict inclusions
under tilting, integral perfectoid rings and the integral/Tate dictionary, and the flat deformation
of perfectoid algebras modulo `ϖ`.

**Untilts are classified by primitive ideals of degree 1.**
(*untilts-classified-by-primitive-ideals*) The functors `(S, S⁺) ↦ (S♭, S♭⁺, ker θ_S)` and
`(R, R⁺, J) ↦ (W(R⁺)[1/[ϖ]]/J, W(R⁺)/J)` are mutually quasi-inverse equivalences between
(i) perfectoid Tate pairs `(S, S⁺)` with morphisms of Huber pairs and (ii) triples `(R, R⁺, J)`
with `(R, R⁺)` a perfectoid Tate pair of characteristic `p` and `J ⊆ W(R⁺)` primitive of degree
`1`, a morphism being a morphism `f` of pairs with `W(f)(J) ⊆ J'` (then `J' = W(f)(J)W(R'⁺)`). No
perfectoid base field is fixed and both characteristics are allowed. The unit is induced by
`θ_S : W(S♭⁺)[1/[ϖ♭]]/ker θ ≅ S`, the counit is the identification of P1.20, and both are natural.
Characteristic-`p` pairs correspond to `J = (p)` ([ECD] §3, Theorem 3.17 with (ii), p. 18; [KL16]
Theorem 3.3.8, p. 60; [AWS] Theorem 2.3.9, p. 55, and Remark 2.3.18, p. 57; [KL15] Theorem 3.6.5,
p. 89, the characteristic-`0` case; [Berkeley] Definition 6.2.9, Lemma 6.2.10 and Theorem 6.2.11,
pp. 46–47). For `(K♭, K♭°)` with `K` a perfectoid field and `J = ker θ`, the construction returns
`(K, K°)`; over `𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^`, `J = (p)` gives the field itself, `J = (p − [t])` the
completion of `ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞})`, `J = (Σ_{i<p}[1+t]^{i/p})` the field `ℚ_p^cycl`, and `φ(J)` gives
Frobenius-twisted markings. *Needs:* P1.20; *untilt-tilt-identification*; P1.18; P1.19; P1.6;
*theta-kernel-base-change*; Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Equivalence`.

Supporting result: `ker θ` is compatible with base change (*theta-kernel-base-change*). Let
`f : (R, R⁺) → (S, S⁺)` be a morphism of perfectoid Tate pairs (`f` continuous with `f(R⁺) ⊆ S⁺`)
with tilt `f♭`. Then `θ_S ∘ W(f♭) = f ∘ θ_R` and `ker θ_S = W(f♭)(ker θ_R)·W(S♭⁺)`; every generator
`ξ` of `ker θ_R` maps to a generator of `ker θ_S`. For `R = K` a perfectoid field this says that
one `ξ ∈ A_inf(K, K⁺)` generates `ker θ` for every perfectoid `(K, K⁺)`-algebra ([AWS] Remark
2.3.17, p. 56; [BMS] Remark 3.11, p. 23). For `R = ℂ_p` and `S = ℂ_p⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩`,
`ker θ_S = (p − [p♭])`; for `S = R/I` a perfectoid quotient, `ker θ_S` is generated by the image of
`ξ`.

The categorical carriers are `PairCat p` and `PrimitiveTriple p`. `PairCat` stores
an actual `TauCeti.Huber.Pair` with the complete Hausdorff perfectoid Tate structure; its morphisms
are exactly `Pair.Hom`. A triple stores `p = 0` on its base and a primitive Witt ideal; a morphism
carries that ideal into the target ideal. `classificationFunctor` uses the actual Fontaine
kernel, and `primitiveUntiltingFunctor` uses the localized Witt quotient. The equations
`PrimitiveTriple.untilt_plus`, `untilt_nhds`, `tiltIso_sharp`,
`primitiveUntiltingFunctor_map`, `classificationEquivalence_unit` and
`classificationEquivalence_counit` specify the plus ring, topology, maps and natural comparisons
of `classificationEquivalence` ([Berkeley] Theorem 6.2.11, p. 47).

### P1.22 marked untilts

**Marked untilts of a perfectoid pair of characteristic p.** (*marked-untilt*) Let `(R, R⁺)` be a
perfectoid Tate pair of characteristic `p`. A marked untilt of `(R, R⁺)` is a triple `(S, S⁺, ι)`
with `(S, S⁺)` a perfectoid Tate pair and `ι : (S♭, S♭⁺) ≅ (R, R⁺)` an isomorphism of Huber pairs
(the marking is part of the data); a morphism `(S, S⁺, ι) → (S', S'⁺, ι')` is a morphism `f` of
Huber pairs with `ι' ∘ f♭ = ι`. By P1.21, `(S, S⁺, ι) ↦ W(ι)(ker θ_S)` is an equivalence from
marked untilts to the discrete category of primitive ideals `J ⊆ W(R⁺)`: a marked untilt has no
nontrivial automorphisms and isomorphic marked untilts are uniquely isomorphic. Marked untilts pull
back along morphisms of pairs `(R, R⁺) → (R', R'⁺)` (`J ↦ J·W(R'⁺)`); marked untilts of `(R, R⁺)`
and of `(R, R°)` correspond (plus rings correspond, *rings-of-integral-elements-under-tilting*);
`pS = 0` iff `J = (p)`, the marked untilt `(R, R⁺, id)` ([Berkeley] Lemma 6.2.8 and the text after
it, pp. 45–46; [AWS] Definition 2.3.13, p. 55; [ECD] §3, after Theorem 3.13, p. 17). Define
`MarkedUntilt` (`MarkedUntilt (P : Pair R)`: a perfectoid Tate ring `S` with instances, a ring of
integral elements `S⁺`, and `ι : Pair.tilt (S, S⁺) ≅ P` as Huber pairs), `MarkedUntilt.Hom`
(`Pair.Hom f` with `ι' ∘ Pair.tiltHom f = ι`; `Category` instance), `MarkedUntilt.primitiveIdeal`
(`W(ι)(ker θ_S)`, a primitive ideal of `W(R⁺)`, P1.18), `MarkedUntilt.ofPrimitive`
(`J ↦ (untilt P J, untiltPlus, tiltEquiv)`, P1.20), `MarkedUntilt.pullback` (for a morphism of
pairs `P → P'` of characteristic `p`: `MarkedUntilt P → MarkedUntilt P'`, `J ↦ J W(R'⁺)`,
compatible with `id` and `comp` up to unique isomorphism) and `MarkedUntilt.self` (the
characteristic-`p` untilt `(R, R⁺, id)` with `primitiveIdeal = span {p}`); prove
`MarkedUntilt.primitiveIdeal_ofPrimitive` (simp: `primitiveIdeal (ofPrimitive J) = J`),
`MarkedUntilt.iso_iff_primitiveIdeal_eq` (two marked untilts are isomorphic exactly when their primitive ideals agree, yielding the bijection on isomorphism classes),
`MarkedUntilt.subsingleton_hom` (`Subsingleton (X ⟶ Y)`; in particular `Unique (Aut X)`),
`MarkedUntilt.plusEquiv` (an equivalence of the categories of marked untilts of
`(R,R⁺)` and `(R,R°)`, or of their sets of isomorphism classes) and
`MarkedUntilt.charP_iff` (`pS = 0 ↔ primitiveIdeal = span {p}`; exact `CharP S p` additionally requires `S ≠ 0`). *Needs:* P1.21; P1.6; P1.19;
*rings-of-integral-elements-under-tilting*; Tau Ceti `TauCeti.Huber.Pair`,
`TauCeti.Huber.Pair.Hom`.

**Checks.**

- `marked_self_kernel` (degenerate) — for `P = (ℚ_p^cycl)♭ = 𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^`,
  `primitiveIdeal (MarkedUntilt.self P) = span {p}` in `W(P⁺)`, with `W(P⁺)/(p) = P⁺` recovering
  `P` itself, whereas the untilt `ℚ_p^cycl` has primitive ideal generated by
  `([ε] − 1)/([ε^{1/p}] − 1)`.
- `marked_padicComplex_kernel` (computation) — for `P = (ℂ_p♭, 𝒪_{ℂ_p♭})` and the
  canonical marking of `ℂ_p`: `primitiveIdeal = span {p − [p♭]}`.
- `marked_automorphism` (characterisation) — every automorphism of a marked untilt is the
  identity.
- `marked_frobenius_twist` (non-example) — for the marked untilt `(ℂ_p, ι)`, the marking
  `φ_R ∘ ι` gives primitive ideal `φ(J) ≠ J`, so `(ℂ_p, ι)` and `(ℂ_p, φ ∘ ι)` are non-isomorphic
  marked untilts with isomorphic underlying rings: the marking cannot be dropped. An explicit
  instance: for `R = 𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^` and the mixed-characteristic `J = (p − [t])`, whose untilt
  is `ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞})^` with `t♯ = p` (P1.19), `φ(J) = (p − [t]^p) ≠ J`, since the untilt map sends
  `p − [t]^p` to `p − p^p ≠ 0`; so the Frobenius-twisted marking is a different marked untilt of the
  same field. Control: the characteristic-`p` ideal `J = (p)` is Frobenius-stable, and its twisted
  marking is isomorphic to the original one through the Frobenius of `R`.

In the proposed Lean form, specified in this README only, the base of `MarkedUntilt p P` is a
bundled `PairCat p`; its marking is
an isomorphism of pairs. `MarkedUntilt.classification hp` maps to the discrete category of
primitive ideals, where `hp : (p : P) = 0`. Its `IsEquivalence` theorem includes full faithfulness
and essential surjectivity. `ofPrimitive`, `self`, `primitiveIdeal_ofPrimitive`, `self_marking`
and `pullback` specify the object constructions. The zero base is allowed: the characteristic
criterion uses `p = 0`, not exact prime characteristic.

### P1.23 strict inclusions under tilting

**Strict inclusions correspond under tilting.** (*strict-inclusions-under-tilting*) A continuous
ring homomorphism `f : A → B` of complete Hausdorff Tate rings is a strict inclusion if it is
injective and a homeomorphism onto its image with the subspace topology (equivalently, as `A` is
complete, a topological ring isomorphism onto a closed subring); strictness is a topological
condition and injectivity alone does not suffice. Let `A` be a perfectoid Tate ring, `ϖ♭ ∈ A♭` with
compatible roots, `ϖ = ϖ♭♯`, and `f : A → B` continuous. (a) If `B` is a perfectoid Tate ring, `f`
is a strict inclusion if and only if `f♭ : A♭ → B♭` (P1.6) is ([AWS] Theorem 2.4.3 and its proof
(completed by Lemma 2.8.1), p. 57). (b) More generally, let `B` be a complete Hausdorff uniform Tate ring (`p` is topologically
nilpotent in `B` because it is in `A`) and `B♭` its tilt (P1.7; `f(ϖ) = (f♭ϖ♭)♯` has compatible
roots and `f(ϖ)^p | p` in `B°`). For the spectral gauges `|·|_ϖ`, `|·|_{f(ϖ)}`, `|·|_{ϖ♭}`,
`|·|_{f♭ϖ♭}`: `f` is a strict inclusion iff `|f(a)| = |a|` for all `a ∈ A`; `f♭` is a strict
inclusion iff it is isometric; and `f` is a strict inclusion iff `f♭` is ([AWS] Lemma 2.8.1, p. 69,
whose second right-hand side should read `zW^b(A♭)`; [AWS] Lemma 2.8.4, proof, p. 70; [KL16] Lemma
3.3.23, p. 66). The analogous statement for injections that are not strict is [AWS] Corollary
2.9.13 and is not stated here. A finite extension `K ⊆ L` of perfectoid fields is a strict
inclusion, and so is `K♭ ⊆ L♭`; the continuous injection `K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ → K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩`,
`T^{1/p^n} ↦ (ϖT)^{1/p^n}`, is not strict (`|T^N| = 1` while `|(ϖT)^N| = 2^{-N}`), and neither is
its tilt `T ↦ ϖ♭T`. *Needs:* P1.6; P1.7; P1.1; P1.3; *metric-perfectoid-criterion*;
*sharp-approximation-lemma*; Tau Ceti `TauCeti.Huber.IsBounded`,
`TauCeti.Huber.powerBoundedSubring`.

Two supporting results. The metric criterion (*metric-perfectoid-criterion*): let `B` be a complete
Hausdorff uniform Tate ring and `ϖ ∈ B°` a pseudo-uniformizer with `ϖ^p | p` in `B°` admitting a
compatible system of `p`-power roots `ϖ^{1/p^n} ∈ B°`, and let
`|x| := inf{2^{-q} : q ∈ ℤ[1/p], ϖ^{-q}x ∈ B°}` be the spectral gauge of `ϖ` (the formula of P1.3
on a ring not assumed perfectoid, i.e. the spectral seminorm of AdicSpacesPartII R0.4 for the
norm datum `(B°, ϖ, 1/2)`; `B` may have characteristic `0`, `p` or neither). Then (a) `|·|`
is an ultrametric, submultiplicative, power-multiplicative norm defining the topology of `B`, with
`|ϖ^qx| = 2^{-q}|x|` and `B° = {x : |x| ≤ 1}`; (b) `B` is a perfectoid Tate ring if and only if
there is `c ∈ (0, 1)` such that for every `x ∈ B` there is `y ∈ B` with `|x − y^p| ≤ c|x|`; (c) if
`B` is perfectoid, every `c ∈ (2^{-p}, 1) = (|ϖ|^p, 1)` has this property, and `y` can be taken in
`B°` when `x ∈ B°`. Kedlaya states the criterion for a uniform analytic Huber pair with an ideal of
definition `I`, `p ∈ I^p`, and the norm attached to `I`; this is its Tate-ring form with the gauge
of a pseudo-uniformizer with compatible roots, which every perfectoid Tate ring has and which every
Tate ring receiving a continuous map from a perfectoid Tate ring has ([AWS] §2.8, Lemma 2.8.3 with
its proof and the text before it, p. 70; [KL15] Proposition 3.6.2(c), p. 87; Tau Ceti
`TauCeti.Huber.IsBounded`, `TauCeti.Huber.isPowerBounded_of_isIntegral`,
`TauCeti.Huber.IsPseudoUniformizer.hasBasis_nhds_zero`). For `B = ℂ_p` with `ϖ = p^{1/p}` every
`c ∈ (2^{-p}, 1)` works; for a perfectoid field `K`, `B = K⟨T⟩` fails the criterion at `x = T`
(the reduction of `y^p` in `(K°/K°°)[T]` is a `p`-th power, so `|T − y^p| ≥ 1 = |T|`), and `B` is
not perfectoid; the criterion passes along isometric continuous maps with dense image (layer P2).
Euclidean division by a primitive element and approximation by sharp elements
(*sharp-approximation-lemma*): let `A` be a perfectoid Tate ring, `ϖ♭ ∈ A♭` with compatible roots,
`ϖ = ϖ♭♯`, and `|·|` the spectral gauges of `A` and `A♭` (P1.3), so that `|y♯| = |y|` by
*spectral-norm-under-sharp*. Let `z = [z̄_0] + p·z_1` (`z_1 ∈ W(A♭°)^×`) be a primitive generator
of `ker(θ : W(A♭°) → A°)` (P1.18; all such differ by units), extend `θ` to
`W^b(A♭) := W(A♭°)[1/[ϖ♭]] → A`, and give `W^b(A♭)` the Gauss norm `|Σ_n p^n[x_n]| := sup_n |x_n|`;
an element `x = Σ_n p^n[x_n]` is prepared if `|x_0| ≥ |x_n|` for all `n ≥ 1`. Then: (a) (Euclidean
division) for `x ∈ W^b(A♭)` put `x′ := p^{-1}(x − [x_0])` and
`r(x) := x − z_1^{-1}x′z = [x_0] − [z̄_0]z_1^{-1}x′`; if `x ∉ zW^b(A♭)`, the terms of the sequence
`x, r(x), r(r(x)), …` are congruent to `x` modulo `z` and are prepared from some term on; no nonzero
element of `zW^b(A♭)` is prepared; (b) (norms) `|θ(x)| ≤ |x|` for every `x`, with equality when `x`
is prepared; hence the quotient norm of the Gauss norm on `W^b(A♭)/(z) ≅ A` is the spectral gauge,
and `|z̄_0| = |p|` (`|p| < 1`, and `|p| = 0` iff `pA = 0`); (c) (sharp approximation) for every
`a ∈ A` there is `y ∈ A♭` with `|a − y♯| ≤ |p|·|a|`, so `|y| = |a|`; for `a ∈ A°` one can take
`y ∈ A♭°`; (d) (pointwise form) `α ↦ α ∘ ♯` maps the Gelfand spectrum `M(A)` of bounded
multiplicative seminorms on `(A, |·|)` into `M(A♭)`, and for every `a ∈ A` and `ε > 0` there is
`y ∈ A♭` with `α(a − y♯) ≤ α(p)·max{α(a), ε}` for all `α ∈ M(A)` simultaneously; with
`|·| = max_{α ∈ M(A)} α` (P1.12; [AWS] Lemma 1.5.21, p. 25) this refines (c) up to `ε`; (e)
(quasi-additivity of `♯`) `|(x + y)♯ − x♯ − y♯| ≤ |p|·max{|x|, |y|}` for `x, y ∈ A♭`. Part (d) uses
the Gelfand spectrum and the maximum formula of P1.12; parts (a)–(c) and (e) do not ([AWS]
Definition 2.6.5, Lemma 2.6.7 and Lemma 2.6.9, p. 64; [AWS] Lemma 2.8.3, proof, and Lemma 2.8.5,
proof, p. 70; [KL16] Lemma 3.2.7(a) with proof, p. 57, and Theorem 3.3.18, proof of case (ii),
p. 65; Mathlib `WittVector`, `WittVector.teichmuller`, `WittVector.fontaineTheta_teichmuller`). For
`A = ℂ_p`, `z = p − [p♭]`: every `a ∈ ℂ_p` is `y♯` up to `|p||a|`, and `a − y♯` need not vanish; in
characteristic `p`, `z = p`, `z̄_0 = 0`, `|p| = 0`, `r(x) = [x_0]` is prepared after one step and
`a = y♯` exactly. Parts (c)–(e) are used by layer P4.

The supporting statements are the gauge laws of P1.3 (submultiplicativity, the ultrametric
inequality, separation, power-multiplicativity, the scaling rule `|ϖ^qx| = 2^{-q}|x|`, the
descriptions `x ∈ R° ↔ |x| ≤ 1` and `IsTopologicallyNilpotent x ↔ |x| < 1`, and the neighbourhood
basis) and the gauge identity under sharp of P1.5; uniformity is explicit for the gauge laws.
Power-multiplicativity requires a positive exponent or a nonzero ring, retaining the zero-ring
failure at exponent zero.
`metric_perfectoid_criterion`, `sharp_approximation`, `sharp_quasi_additive` and
`tilt.strict_inclusion_iff` use the complete Hausdorff topology; strictness means a topological
embedding, not preservation of an arbitrarily normalized norm ([AWS] §§2.6–2.8).

### P1.24 integral perfectoid rings

**Integral perfectoid rings.** (*integral-perfectoid-rings*) A commutative ring `R` is integral
perfectoid if there is `π ∈ R` with `π^p | p` such that `R` is `π`-adically complete and separated,
the Frobenius `R/p → R/p` is surjective, and the kernel of Fontaine's map `θ : W(R♭) → R` is
principal, where `R♭ = lim_{x ↦ x^p} R/p` is the tilt (Mathlib's `PreTilt`) ([BMS] §3.2, Definition
3.5, p. 21). Equivalent forms: for a nonzerodivisor `π` with `π^p | p` and `R` `π`-adically
complete, `R` is integral perfectoid iff Frobenius `R/π → R/π^p` is an isomorphism; every integral
perfectoid `R` admits a unit multiple of `π` with a compatible system of `p`-power roots ([BMS]
Lemma 3.9 and Lemma 3.10, p. 22). Integral perfectoid rings may have `p`-torsion and need not be
domains. Define `IsIntegralPerfectoid` with an admissible adic element, surjective Frobenius,
and principal kernel of the supplied Fontaine map. In Lean the last condition quantifies over
proofs that `p` is a nonunit and that the ring is `p`-adically complete. The latter follows from
the adic presentation by [Stacks] Tag 090T; if `p` is a unit, that presentation forces the zero
ring, and the unique map has principal kernel. Thus the condition includes the zero ring without
an impossible `Fact ¬IsUnit p` instance. Prove that
for every `π` with `π^p | p` and `R` `π`-adically complete, Frobenius `R/π → R/π^p`
is bijective, with no nonzerodivisor hypothesis ([BMS] Lemma 3.10(i), p. 22), and that
for `π^p ∣ p` with `R` `π`-adically
complete, a unit multiple of `π` has compatible `p`-power roots. The zero ring satisfies the
definition using the unique Fontaine map; for nonzero rings use Mathlib’s `PreTilt` and `θ`. *Needs:* Mathlib `IsAdicComplete`, `PreTilt`, `WittVector.fontaineTheta`.

**Checks.**

- Non-example: `ℤ_p` is not integral perfectoid: Frobenius
  on `ℤ_p/p = 𝔽_p` is bijective and `ker θ = 0` is principal, but no admissible `π` exists: `π^p | p`
  forces `p·v_p(π) ≤ 1`, so `π` is a unit (`π = p` fails, `p^p ∤ p`), and `ℤ_p` is not `π`-adically
  complete for a unit `π` (`lim ℤ_p/π^n = 0 ≠ ℤ_p`).
- Computation: the `p`-adic completion of
  `ℤ_p[p^{1/p^∞}]` is integral perfectoid with `π = p^{1/p}`.
- `integral_perfect_charP` (degenerate) — a perfect `𝔽_p`-algebra that is `π`-adically
  complete for some `π` is integral perfectoid (`π^p | p = 0` trivially).

The proposed Mathlib [integral-perfectoid interface](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/pull/26385)
uses a specified topological ring and pseudo-uniformizer. The definition here is the
choice-independent algebraic predicate of [BMS] Definition 3.5. A comparison target, specified
in this README only, compares these formulations when the given topology
is the complete separated `π`-adic topology and the chosen element satisfies `π^p ∣ p`; the
comparison must include the principal Fontaine-kernel condition.

`IntegralAdicPresentation p A π` records the divisibility, completeness, Frobenius and
Fontaine-kernel conditions with `π` specified. The comparison
relates it to the algebraic predicate under `π^p ∣ p` and completeness for that same `π`.
It uses the pinned Fontaine map, including its nonunit hypothesis. This specifies the algebraic
content of the proposed topological interface; a topology identified as `π`-adic supplies the
chosen presentation.

Lean: `IsIntegralPerfectoid`, with fields `exists_adic_element`, `frobenius_surjective` and
`theta_kernel_principal`; the Lean `example`s check that perfect rings of characteristic `p` and
`𝒪_{ℂ_p}` are integral perfectoid and that `ℤ_p` is not.

### P1.25 perfectoid Tate rings and integral perfectoid rings

**`R perfectoid Tate ⇔ R⁺ integral perfectoid and bounded`.** (*integral-perfectoid-comparison*) Let
`R` be a complete Hausdorff Tate ring and `R⁺` a ring of integral elements. If `R` is a perfectoid
Tate ring, then `R⁺` (and `R°`) is an integral perfectoid ring in the sense of P1.24: `π`-adically
complete for some `π ∈ R⁺` with `π^p | p` in `R⁺` (exact divisibility, as in P1.24; such a `π`
exists by *frobenius-surjective-on-plus-ring* (b), and may be taken a pseudo-uniformizer of `R`),
Frobenius surjective on `R⁺/p`, and the kernel of `θ : A_inf(R⁺) → R⁺` principal. Conversely, if
`R⁺` is integral perfectoid and bounded in `R`, then `R` is a perfectoid Tate ring; boundedness of
`R⁺` is necessary for the converse (a non-bounded `R⁺` cannot occur inside a uniform `R`; conversely
`ϖR° ⊆ R⁺` for a bounded open integrally closed `R⁺`, so `R` is uniform), and the point of the
converse is to produce a pseudo-uniformizer `ϖ'` of `R` with `ϖ'^p | p`: the given `π` is one when
`p` is a unit of `R`, but need not be a unit of `R` in general (`K × K♭` with `R⁺ = K° × K♭°` is
integral perfectoid for `π = (π_K, 0)`, and a perfect `𝔽_p`-algebra for `π = 0`) ([BMS] §3.2, Lemma 3.20 with its proof and the text before it, pp. 26–27; [BMS]
Definition 3.5, p. 21; [BMS] Lemma 3.10(ii), p. 22). The forward
direction is *frobenius-surjective-on-plus-ring* (P1.17) together with the primitive-kernel theorem
(P1.18); what is proved here is the converse. Together with
*perfectoid-tate-ring-from-integral-perfectoid* ([BMS] Lemma 3.21, P1.20) this compares the integral
notion with the Tate-ring notion of this layer.
`ℤ_p^cycl`, `𝒪_{ℂ_p}` and the `p`-adic completion of `ℤ_p^cycl[T^{1/p^∞}]` are integral perfectoid
([BMS] Example 3.6) and `ℚ_p^cycl`, `ℂ_p`, `ℚ_p^cycl⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩` are perfectoid Tate rings; perfect
`𝔽_p`-algebras are integral perfectoid with `π = 0`, but with the discrete topology they are not
Tate, so the comparison needs `R` Tate. *Needs:* P1.1; P1.24; *perfectoid-tate-ring-from-integral-perfectoid*;
*frobenius-surjective-on-plus-ring*; *integral-elements-adically-complete*.

The reverse criterion of P1.24 holds
with a nonzerodivisor `π`, `π^p ∣ p`, and completeness for that same `π` ([BMS] Lemma 3.10(ii)):
bijectivity of Frobenius `R/π → R/π^p` then gives integral perfectoidness.
`isPerfectoidTateRing_iff_integral P` states the comparison for a complete Hausdorff Tate ring
and its actual ring of integral elements, with boundedness retained on the integral side.

Lean: `isPerfectoidTateRing_iff_integral`.

### P1.26 flat deformation of perfectoid algebras modulo `ϖ`

**Unique flat deformation of perfectoid algebras modulo `ϖ` over a perfectoid field.**
(*deformation-lifting-of-perfectoid-mod-varpi-algebras*) Let `K` be a complete nontrivially
normed ultrametric perfectoid field, and choose a pseudo-uniformizer `ϖ = (ϖ♭)♯` with compatible
roots and `ϖ^p ∣ p` in `K°`. The element `ϖ` is a nonzerodivisor on `K°`, and
`ϖ^{n−1}K°/ϖ^nK° ≅ K°/ϖ` is square-zero in `K°/ϖ^n` for `n ≥ 2`. Reduction modulo `ϖ`,
`A ↦ A/ϖ`, is an equivalence between (i) `ϖ`-adically complete `K°a`-algebras `A` that are
(almost) flat over `K°a` with `Φ : A/ϖ^{1/p} ≅ A/ϖ`, and (ii) (almost) flat
`(K°/ϖ)^a`-algebras `B` with `Φ : B/ϖ^{1/p} ≅ B`. Concretely `B` lifts uniquely, through the
square-zero extensions `(K°/ϖ^n)^a → (K°/ϖ^{n−1})^a`, to a compatible system of flat
`(K°/ϖ^n)^a`-algebras `B_n` with `B_n/ϖ^{n−1} ≅ B_{n−1}`, and `A = lim B_n`; two flat
deformations with the same reduction are uniquely isomorphic compatibly with the reduction.
The limit has no `ϖ`-torsion on almost elements, which implies flatness over the valuation
ring `K°` and almost flatness over `K°a` ([Sch12] Lemma 5.3(i), p. 22).
The almost deformation theory used (obstructions in `Ext²`, torsors under `Ext¹`, automorphisms
`Hom`, lifting of morphisms) is P0.22. This is [Sch12] Theorem 5.10, p. 24, with proof on p. 26,
the step `K°a-Perf ≃ (K°a/ϖ)-Perf` of Theorem 5.2, p. 22. Base flatness is retained in the
categories; the equivalence has field scope, as in P1.28. P1.27 supplies the arbitrary-base
tilting equivalence via primitive ideals.
This is Scholze's deformation-theoretic route: the tilting equivalence (P1.27) and the mod-`ϖ`
equivalence (P1.28) are derived from P1.21 and do not depend on it. `K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩` and
`K♭⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩` have the same reduction `(K°/ϖ)[T^{1/p^∞}]` and are therefore tilts of each other
([Sch12] Proposition 5.20). *Needs:* P0.22; P0.20; P0.16; P0.19; *cotangent-complex-vanishing-mod-varpi*; Mathlib
`IsAdicComplete`, `Module.Flat`.

Supporting result: the Frobenius criterion for vanishing of the (almost) cotangent complex
(*cotangent-complex-vanishing-mod-varpi*). (a) Let `A_0 → B` be a map of `𝔽_p`-algebras such that
the relative Frobenius `A_0(Φ) ⊗^L_{A_0} B → B(Φ)` is an isomorphism in `D(A_0)` (a hypothesis on
the derived relative Frobenius, not on `Ω¹` alone). Then `L_{B/A_0} ≃ 0`; in particular
`L_{B/𝔽_p} ≃ 0` for `B` perfect, and `L_{B/A_0} ≃ 0` whenever `A_0 → B` is flat and relatively
perfect. (b) The almost version holds over any basic setup `(V, m)` with `V` an `𝔽_p`-algebra: if
the relative Frobenius of a map of almost algebras is an isomorphism in the almost derived
category, then the almost cotangent complex `L^a` (P0.20) vanishes. (c) For `R` a perfectoid Tate
ring, `ϖ = (ϖ♭)♯` with compatible roots, and `A` a `(R°/ϖ)^a`-algebra which is (almost) flat over
`(R°/ϖ)^a` with `Φ : A/ϖ^{1/p} ≅ A`, `L^a_{A/(R°/ϖ)^a} ≃ 0`; for `R = K` a perfectoid field this is
[Sch12] Corollary 5.16 ([GR] arXiv v3, Lemma 6.5.9(i) with proof, pp. 176–177 (LNM 1800 Lemma
6.5.13(i)); [Sch12] §5, Proposition 5.13(i)–(ii) with proof, p. 25, and Corollary 5.16, proof,
p. 26; [Bhatt] Proposition 6.1.4, p. 42). `Ω¹_{R/𝔽_p} = 0` for perfect `R`, since
`dx = d(y^p) = py^{p−1}dy = 0` ([Sch12] Remark 5.14); the degree `0` and `1` parts are Mathlib's
`KaehlerDifferential` and `Algebra.H1Cotangent`. The classical cotangent complex with its
simplicial description, transitivity and Tor-independent base change is P0.19.

The categories `IntegralAlmostPerfectoid p R ϖ` and `ModAlmostPerfectoid p R ϖ` are full
subcategories of the almost algebras of P0.8. Their predicates specify base flatness,
completeness on almost elements on the integral side, and the relative Frobenius condition.
`IsAlmostBijective` tests annihilation of the kernel and cokernel of the underlying semilinear
ring map by the almost ideal. The quotient-side setup is the base change to `R°/ϖ`, so its
flatness is over that quotient. `almostReductionFunctor_obj` fixes reduction on almost-elements
representatives, and `almostReductionEquivalence` states the flat deformation equivalence.
`almostReductionFunctor_map` supplies a single family of these object isomorphisms
such that every map `f : A → A′` becomes the almostification of the quotient map
`A_*/ϖ → A′_*/ϖ` induced by `elements.map f`. Its equation is
`F.map f ≫ e(A′).hom = e(A).hom ≫ toAlmost.map (quotientMap f_*)`;
the isomorphisms are chosen simultaneously for all objects and maps
([Sch12] Theorem 5.10, p. 24).
The reduction functor, `almostReductionFunctor_obj` and `almostReductionEquivalence` assume
`IsPerfectoidField p K`, with `K` complete, nontrivially normed and ultrametric. The predicates
and their full subcategories remain defined for arbitrary perfectoid Tate rings `R`.
`almost_mod_cotangent_vanishes` uses the full almost cotangent complex of P0.20 over such a
base, by the almost Frobenius criterion above; [Sch12] Corollary 5.16, p. 25, with proof on
p. 26, is its field specialization.

### P1.27 the tilting equivalence

The layer closes with the tilting equivalence over an arbitrary perfectoid base, the mod-`ϖ`
equivalence over a perfectoid field, completed filtered colimits, perfected Tate algebras, the
cyclotomic field, the standard examples and the compatibility with AdicSpaces' perfect field `F`.

**Tilting equivalence `Perf_R ≃ Perf_{R♭}` over an arbitrary perfectoid Tate ring, with the explicit
tilt.** (*tilting-equivalence-and-explicit-tilt*) Let `R` be a perfectoid Tate ring with tilt `R♭`
and `J_R := ker(θ_R : W(R♭°) → R°)`, a primitive ideal (P1.18). No perfectoid base field is fixed;
continuous homomorphisms between Tate rings preserve power-bounded elements into uniform targets
(`map_mem_powerBoundedSubring`, P1.1), so `R`-algebras are pairs over `(R, R°)`. The tilting
functor `S ↦ S♭` (`R♭ → S♭` the tilt of `R → S`, P1.6) is an equivalence from perfectoid
`R`-algebras to perfectoid `R♭`-algebras, with quasi-inverse
`T ↦ T♯ := W(T°)[1/[ϖ♭]]/J_R·W(T°)[1/[ϖ♭]]`, the untilt along `J_R·W(T°)` (P1.19); the unit
`S ≅ (S♭)♯` is induced by `θ_S` and the counit `(T♯)♭ ≅ T` by P1.20, both natural. Explicitly
`S♭ = lim_{x↦x^p} S`, `S♭° = lim_{x↦x^p} S° ≅ lim_Φ S°/ϖ` and `S♭°/ϖ♭ ≅ S°/ϖ`; the functor is
independent of choices, extends to pairs `(S, S⁺) ↦ (S♭, S♭⁺)`, and `S` is a perfectoid field iff
`S♭` is, by *perfectoid-field-iff-tilt-field*. For `R = K` a perfectoid field,
`T♯ = W(T°) ⊗_{W(K♭°)} K°[1/ϖ]` ([Sch12] Remark 5.19, p. 27; [Bhatt] Remark 6.2.8), and the functor
agrees with Scholze's chain `K-Perf ≃ K°a-Perf ≃ (K°a/ϖ)-Perf = (K♭°a/ϖ♭)-Perf ≃ K♭°a-Perf ≃ K♭-Perf` ([ECD] §3, Theorem 3.13 with its proof ("the proof works in general", here supplied by the
untilt classification) and the text after it, p. 17; [Berkeley] Theorem 6.2.7, p. 45; [AWS] Remark
2.3.17, p. 56; [Sch12] Theorem 5.2, p. 22, and Proposition 5.17, p. 26, over a perfectoid field).
The tilt of `R⟨T_1^{1/p^∞}, …, T_n^{1/p^∞}⟩` is `R♭⟨T_1^{1/p^∞}, …, T_n^{1/p^∞}⟩` with `T_i♯ = T_i`
(P1.30; [Sch12] Proposition 5.20; [AWS] Example 2.3.15). *Needs:* P1.21; *theta-kernel-base-change*;
P1.6; P1.19; P1.20; P1.1; Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Equivalence`.

`PairCat.sliceTiltFunctor p R` acts on `CategoryTheory.Under R`, sending the
structural pair map to its tilt. `sliceTriple` extends the base Fontaine kernel along the Witt
map of the structural morphism, and `sliceUntiltFunctor` uses its localized quotient.
`sliceTiltingEquivalence` has these fixed functor and inverse fields, with natural unit and
counit. Thus its signature applies to all perfectoid pairs, including zero pairs, without
requiring a pre-existing equivalence as an argument.

### P1.28 the equivalence through the mod-`ϖ` category

**`Perf_K ≃ K°a-Perf ≃ (K°a/ϖ)-Perf` over a perfectoid field.**
(*perfectoid-mod-varpi-equivalence*) Let `K` be a complete nontrivially normed ultrametric
perfectoid field, and choose compatible roots of a pseudo-uniformizer `ϖ` with `ϖ^p ∣ p` in
`K°`. Use the almost setup `(K°, K°°)`. A perfectoid `K°a`-algebra is a flat, `ϖ`-adically
complete almost algebra `A` with Frobenius `A/ϖ^{1/p} → A/ϖ` an isomorphism. A perfectoid
`(K°a/ϖ)`-algebra is a flat algebra over that almost base with Frobenius
`B/ϖ^{1/p} → B` an isomorphism. The functors `S ↦ S°a` and `A ↦ A/ϖ` are equivalences between
these categories and perfectoid `K`-algebras ([Sch12] Definition 5.1(ii)–(iii), Theorem 5.2,
pp. 21–22, and Theorem 5.10, p. 24, with proof on p. 26). Identifying the base reductions gives the chain of
equivalences with the corresponding categories over `K♭`.

The source scope here is a field. An unrestricted version over a perfectoid Tate ring `R`,
with almost flatness over `Λ = 𝔽_p[x^{1/p^∞}]/(x)` replacing base flatness, requires a reference
proving that exact category equivalence, including the inverse-limit lifting and almost-elements
claims. [ECD] Proposition 9.3, p. 44, supplies the totally disconnected application, with the
base-flatness input of Proposition 7.23; it does not supply the unrestricted statement. P1.27
retains the arbitrary-base tilting equivalence via primitive ideals.

Two supporting results have the same field scope. The *almost-integral-dictionary* sends
`S` to `S°a` and sends `A` to `A_*[1/ϖ]`, with `A_*` open and `ϖ`-adic. For a torsion-free
`K°`-module `N`, its almost elements are the elements `x ∈ N[1/ϖ]` such that
`ϖ^{1/pⁿ}x ∈ N` for every `n`. Reduction of almost elements gives an inclusion
`A_*/ϖ^qA_* ⊆ (A/ϖ^qA)_*`, not an equality in general; its cokernel is almost zero
([Sch12] Lemma 5.3, Remark 5.4, and Lemmas 5.6–5.7, pp. 22–23).

For *frobenius-inverse-limit-lifting-in-characteristic-p*, assume `K` has characteristic `p`.
A perfectoid reduction `B` lifts to `lim_Φ B`; its `K°a`-action is
`a·(b_n)_n = (a^{1/pⁿ}b_n)_n`. The lift is perfect, `ϖ`-adically complete and torsion-free,
and reduction recovers `B` ([Sch12] Remark 5.18, p. 26; [KL15] Lemma 3.4.2, p. 79;
[KL16] Lemma 3.3.7, p. 60). The first two scalar coordinates are `ab₀` and `a^{1/p}b₁`;
using `a` in both coordinates does not commute with Frobenius. The examples `B=K°/ϖ`
and `B=(K°/ϖ)[X^{1/p^∞}]` lift respectively to `K°` and `K°⟨X^{1/p^∞}⟩`.
*Needs:* P0.6, P0.8, P0.16, P0.22; P1.9; P1.26; Mathlib `Perfection` and
`Perfection.quotientMulEquiv`.

`FieldAlgebras p K` uses the maximal integral subring and continuous structural maps from
`K`. `fieldIntegralFunctor_obj` identifies its integral almost algebra with `S°a`, and
`fieldIntegralEquivalence_inverse` identifies the inverse ring with `A_*[1/ϖ]`.
For the same complete nontrivially normed ultrametric perfectoid field `K` and
chosen roots `ϖ`, `fieldIntegralFunctor_map` gives a simultaneous family of
object isomorphisms under which every continuous `K`-algebra map is sent to the
almostification of its restriction `S° → T°`. Explicitly,
`F.map f ≫ e(T).hom = e(S).hom ≫ toAlmost.map (f|S°)`
([Sch12] Definition 5.1, pp. 21–22, and Proposition 5.5, p. 23).
`fieldIntegralEquivalence` and `almostReductionEquivalence` state
the two equivalences of [Sch12] Theorem 5.2. The definitions of both almost-perfectoid predicates
have base, zero and dual-number Checks: dual numbers fail the Frobenius condition even though
their underlying module is flat.

In characteristic p, `almostInverseLimitRing` is the actual `Perfection` of the almost-elements
ring. Its coefficient ring maps use the sequence coordinates; `coeff_algebraMap` fixes the
inverse-Frobenius scalar action. `complete`, `integral` and `inverseComparison` identify its
completion and almost algebra with the lifting inverse. The zero algebra has zero inverse
limit. These statements use [Sch12] Remark 5.18 and the lifting references above.

<a id="p1-29"></a>

### P1.29 completed filtered colimits

**Completed filtered colimits of perfectoid Tate rings are perfectoid, and tilting commutes with
them.** (*completed-colimit-of-perfectoid-tate-rings*) Let `J` be a small filtered category (hence
nonempty) and `j ↦ R_j` a functor from `J` to perfectoid Tate rings (each in the sense of P1.1)
with continuous ring homomorphisms `φ_a : R_i → R_j` (no injectivity, flatness or density assumed;
characteristic `0`, `p` or neither; no perfectoid base field). Fix `j₀ ∈ J` and a
pseudo-uniformizer `ϖ♭ ∈ R_{j₀}♭` with compatible roots, `ϖ = ϖ♭♯`, which exists by
*exists-pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots*; on the tail `J_{j₀} = Under j₀` (final in `J`,
Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Under.final_forget`) the images of `ϖ` and of its roots are
pseudo-uniformizers with compatible roots and `ϖ^p | p` in every `R_j°` (a compatible
pseudo-uniformizer). The ring `R` with its maps `ι_j : R_j → R` is formed here by
`A := colim_j R_j°`, `R_0 := AdicCompletion (ϖ) A`, and `R := R_0[1/ϖ]`, with the image of
`R_0` open and `ϖ`-adic. P5.1 equips this ring with the completion of the chosen plus rings.
Its properties are: (a) `R` is a
complete Hausdorff Tate ring with pseudo-uniformizer `ϖ` and ring of definition `R_0`, `ϖ` a
nonzerodivisor on `R_0` with `R_0/ϖ^nR_0 = colim_j R_j°/ϖ^n`, the `ι_j` continuous and compatible
with dense image of `colim R_j`, the universal property for complete Hausdorff Tate rings `S` with
bounded `S⁺` (for `S` uniform: every compatible family `ψ_j : R_j → S` factors uniquely through
`R`), independence of `j₀`, of `ϖ` and of the choice of rings of integral elements `R_j⁺` in place
of `R_j°`; (b) `R` is a perfectoid Tate ring, `R_0` is `ϖ`-adically complete and integral
perfectoid with `R_0 ⊆ R°` and `ϖ^{1/p^n}R° ⊆ R_0` for all `n`, so `R`, with the `ι_j`, is the
colimit of the `R_j` in perfectoid Tate rings and in complete Hausdorff uniform Tate rings.
In addition, (c) tilting commutes with completed filtered colimits: the `R_j♭` (P1.6) form a filtered system of
perfectoid Tate rings of characteristic `p` with compatible pseudo-uniformizer `ϖ♭`, and the
continuous homomorphism from their completed colimit `T` (as in (a), with ring of definition the
`ϖ♭`-adic completion of `colim R_j♭°`) to `R♭` induced by the `ι_j♭` is an isomorphism of
perfectoid Tate rings, compatible with `♯`; dually, for a perfectoid Tate ring `R′` and a filtered
system of perfectoid `R′♭`-algebras `T_j`, the untilt over `R′` (P1.27) of their completed colimit
is the completed colimit of the untilts `T_j♯`. The `R_j` must be perfectoid: a completed colimit
of non-perfectoid rings can be perfectoid (`ℚ_p(p^{1/p^n})`) without its tilt being the colimit of
the tilts; such limits are tilde-limits (layer P7) ([Bhatt] Remark
6.2.9, p. 48, and §6.2, proof of almost purity over a field, p. 49; [Sch12] §5, Theorem 5.2 and the
text after it, p. 22, and proof of Theorem 3.7, p. 29 ("the union of the `L♯` is dense", asserted
without proof); [KL16] Corollary 3.3.22, p. 66; [Sch13] §4, end of the proof of Lemma 4.6, p. 25).
The proposed Lean carrier `completedFilteredColimit p F j₀ ϖ` is this localization of
`filteredIntegralCompletion`, with `integralDiagram` supplying the actual restricted transition
maps. `completedFilteredColimit.isTateRing` and
`completedFilteredColimit.isPerfectoidTateRing` state the Tate and perfectoid obligations
on this localization before it is bundled in `PairCat`; the instances use these theorems
([ECD] Proposition 6.5, p. 29). `ι_integral` fixes its structural maps on `R_j°`, `hasBasis_nhds_zero` fixes the topology,
and `lift_spec` with `hom_ext` fixes the continuous universal property. Prove
`completedFilteredColimit.ringOfDefinition_almostEq`
(`R_0 ≤ R°` and `ϖ^{1/p^n} • R° ≤ R_0` for all `n`), `completedFilteredColimit.tiltEquiv`
(`tilt (completedFilteredColimit F ϖ♭) ≃+* completedFilteredColimit (F ⋙ tiltFunctor) ϖ♭.toTilt`, a
homeomorphism commuting with `sharp` and sending `tilt.map (ι j)` to `ι j`),
`completedFilteredColimit.untiltEquiv` (for `G : J ⥤` perfectoid `R′♭`-algebras: the untilt over
`R′` of `completedFilteredColimit G` is isomorphic to `completedFilteredColimit (G ⋙ untiltFunctor R′)`, naturally in `G`), `completedFilteredColimit.equivOfChoice` (changing `(j₀, ϖ♭)` or
restricting along a final functor `J′ ⥤ J` gives canonically isomorphic rings, compatibly with `ι`
and `lift`; compatible rings of integral elements give the same ring) and
`completedFilteredColimit.isColimit` (the cocone `(completedFilteredColimit F ϖ♭, ι)` is a colimit
in perfectoid Tate rings with continuous ring homomorphisms). *Needs:* P1.1; P1.3;
*exists-pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots*; P1.6; P1.27;
*perfectoid-tate-ring-from-integral-perfectoid*; Mathlib
`CommRingCat.FilteredColimits.colimitCoconeIsColimit`, `CategoryTheory.IsFiltered`,
`CategoryTheory.Under.final_forget`, `AdicCompletion`, `IsAdicComplete`, `Localization.Away`; Tau
Ceti `TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing`, `TauCeti.Huber.IsPseudoUniformizer.hasBasis_nhds_zero`,
`TauCeti.Huber.IsRingOfIntegralElements.mem_of_isTopologicallyNilpotent`,
`TauCeti.Huber.powerBoundedSubring`.

**Checks.**

- `completedFilteredColimit.terminalEquiv` (degenerate) — for `J` with a terminal object `j` (in particular
  a one-object `J`), `completedFilteredColimit F ≃+* F.obj j` as topological rings, compatibly with
  `ι_j`.
- `completedColimit_test_profinite` (computation) — for a perfectoid field `K` and a
  profinite set `S = lim S_i` (finite `S_i`), the completed colimit of the perfectoid rings
  `K^{S_i} = C(S_i, K)` is `C^0(S, K)` with the sup norm, and its ring of definition is `C^0(S, K°)`.
- `completedFilteredColimit_tilt_algebraicClosure` (compatibility) — for a perfectoid field `K`,
  `tiltEquiv` identifies the completion of an algebraic closure of `K♭` with the tilt of the
  completed colimit of the untilts `L♯` of the finite extensions `L` of `K♭` inside it; the union
  of the `L♯` is dense in the untilt (layer P3; [Sch12], proof of Theorem 3.7, p. 29).
  More precisely, choose a normed algebraic closure `Ω` of `tiltField p K` with its extended
  ultrametric norm, and a small filtered diagram `G` of perfectoid pairs under the tilted
  maximal-plus pair of `K`. Continuous embeddings `c_j` must identify the stage topologies
  and base maps with finite intermediate fields `L_j ⊆ Ω`, commute with transition maps,
  and have union `Ω`. Put `F = G ⋙ sliceUntiltFunctor ⋙ Under.forget`. For any stage and
  compatible pseudouniformizer roots `η` there, the theorem gives a topological ring
  isomorphism from `completedFilteredColimit (F ⋙ tiltFunctor)` to `Completion Ω`.
  Its composite with `completedFilteredColimit.tiltEquiv` takes the tilt of each structural
  map, after the slice-tilting counit identification, to `c_j` followed by completion.
  It also asserts density of the union of the structural images of the untilted stages.
- `completedFilteredColimit_nonPerfectoid_tower` (non-example) — for `p` odd, the fields
  `ℚ_p(p^{1/p^n})` are not perfectoid and their tilts in the sense of P1.7 are `𝔽_p`, while the
  completion `ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞})^` is perfectoid with tilt `𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^`: tilting does not
  commute with completed colimits of non-perfectoid rings, so the hypothesis that every `R_j` be
  perfectoid cannot be dropped.

The perfectoidness of the Kummer field states that `Almost.kummerField p r` is
perfectoid for every prime `p` and sequence `r : ℕ → ℂ_p` with `r₀ = p` and
`rₙ₊₁^p = rₙ`, including `p = 2`. It supplies the perfectoid instance for
`fontaine_wintenberger_test_kummer_tower` ([Sch12] §1, p. 2, the completed
radical-field example preceding Definition 1.2).

`PerfectoidRingCat` is the full subcategory of perfectoid pairs with maximal plus ring.
`PairCat.maximalFunctor` supplies the continuous-ring-map diagram from any pair diagram.
`completedFilteredColimit.cocone` uses the specified structural maps, and `isColimit` states its
categorical universal property. `underObject` carries the common base map;
`untiltEquiv` compares the untilt of its completed colimit with the completed colimit after
slice untilting, with continuity in both directions. For every small filtered diagram
`G : J ⥤ Under (R′♭)`, a chosen stage `j`, compatible pseudouniformizer roots `ψ` at
`G.obj j` and `η` at its untilt, `completedFilteredColimit.untiltEquiv_ι` requires that
composing the untilt of each structural map `G.obj i → underObject G` with `untiltEquiv`
equals `ι p (G ⋙ sliceUntiltFunctor ⋙ Under.forget R′) j η i`, for every stage `i`.
This is the colimit comparison induced by the slice equivalence ([Berkeley] Theorem 6.2.7,
p. 45) and the completed-colimit universal property above; [KL16] Corollary 3.3.22,
p. 66 supplies perfectoidness in the Banach setting. `equivOfChoice_spec` fixes the cofinal
comparison on every stage.

The three Checks for `completedFilteredColimit.untiltEquiv` use these same
structural maps and [Berkeley] Theorem 6.2.7, p. 45:

- `completedFilteredColimit.untiltEquiv_zero_diagram` — when every stage of
  `G` is zero, the completed colimit of the untilted stages is zero and every
  element maps to zero under `untiltEquiv`.
- `completedFilteredColimit.untiltEquiv_two_roots` — if `j` is terminal, map
  `η.root 0 + η.root 1` from its untilt into the untilt of the colimit, apply
  `untiltEquiv`, and identify the result with the terminal untilted stage
  using `terminalEquiv`. The result is `η.root 0 + η.root 1`.
- `completedFilteredColimit.untiltEquiv_not_frobenius` — for a terminal stage
  with nonzero untilt, the image of `η.root 0` along the same composite is
  not the structural image of `(η.root 0)^p`. The terminal hypothesis makes
  the structural map injective; it is essential for this non-example.

The locally constant/profinite Check needs the functor of finite partitions of a specified
profinite space and its completed continuous-function algebra with the integral sup topology.
The algebraic-closure Check needs the finite-extension diagram and its compatible untilt
embeddings from P3. These two Checks retain those concrete carriers; the general colimit
universal property does not replace them. The non-perfectoid radical-tower Check needs the
finite radical extensions, their uniform tilts and the completion of their union, so it is a
separate comparison from the perfectoid-stage colimit.
