### P1.30 perfected Tate algebras

**Perfected Tate algebras `R⟨T_s^{1/p^∞} : s ∈ Σ⟩` in any set of variables over any perfectoid Tate
ring.** (*perfected-tate-algebra*) Let `R` be a perfectoid Tate ring (no base field) with
pseudo-uniformizer `ϖ` (`ϖ^p | p` in `R°`) and `Σ` an arbitrary set, possibly infinite (`Σ = ∅`
gives `R`; infinite `Σ` is used by layer P2 with `Σ = C♭°`, [KL16] Corollary 3.3.21, and by [AWS]
Lemma 2.8.7 with `Σ = C♭⁺`). The perfected Tate algebra `R⟨T_s^{1/p^∞} : s ∈ Σ⟩` is `A_0[1/ϖ]`,
where `A_0` is the `ϖ`-adic completion of the monoid algebra `R°[T^a : a ∈ ℤ[1/p]_{≥0}^{(Σ)}]`
(`AddMonoidAlgebra` over the finitely supported exponent vectors `Σ →₀ ℤ[1/p]_{≥0}`,
`T^a = Π_s T_s^{a(s)}`), topologised with `A_0` open and `ϖ`-adic; equivalently the completion of
the perfect polynomial ring `R[T_s^{1/p^∞} : s ∈ Σ]` for the topology in which
`R°[T_s^{1/p^∞} : s ∈ Σ]` is open with its `ϖ`-adic topology (the Gauss norm). It is a perfectoid
Tate ring with `R⟨T_s^{1/p^∞}⟩° = A_0 = {Σ_a c_aT^a : c_a ∈ R°, c_a → 0` along the cofinite filter
on exponents`}`; `R⁺⟨T_s^{1/p^∞}⟩` is a ring of integral elements for every `R⁺`. Universal
property: for every complete Hausdorff uniform Tate `R`-algebra `S` and every family, indexed by
`s ∈ Σ`, of compatible systems `(t_s^{(m)})_{m≥0}` in `S°` with `(t_s^{(m+1)})^p = t_s^{(m)}`, there
is a unique continuous `R`-algebra map `R⟨T_s^{1/p^∞}⟩ → S` with `T_s^{1/p^m} ↦ t_s^{(m)}`; for `S`
perfectoid such families are families `(x_s)` in `S♭°`, via `t_s^{(m)} = (x_s^{1/p^m})♯`. Its tilt
is `R♭⟨T_s^{1/p^∞} : s ∈ Σ⟩` with `T_s^{1/p^m} ↦ (T_s^{1/p^{m+k}})_k`, so `T_s♯ = T_s`. The
construction is functorial in `Σ`, and `R⟨T_s^{1/p^∞} : s ∈ Σ⟩` is the completed filtered colimit
(P1.29) of the algebras in finitely many of the variables. For `Σ = {1, …, n}` it is
`R⟨T_1^{1/p^∞}, …, T_n^{1/p^∞}⟩`, which contains Tau Ceti's `R⟨T_1, …, T_n⟩` as the closed subring
of series with exponents in `ℕ^n`, with a continuous `R`-linear retraction
`σ(Σ x_aT^a) = Σ_{a ∈ ℕ^n} x_aT^a`; the Laurent variant `R⟨T_s^{±1/p^∞}⟩` is perfectoid as well
([AWS] §2.1, Example 2.1.4, p. 50, Example 2.3.15, p. 56, and Lemma 2.8.7, proof, p. 71; [KL16]
Example 3.3.12, p. 61, for arbitrary index sets with plus rings, and Corollary 3.3.21, proof, p. 66,
where the source writes `A{C°}` and the images of the variables need compatible `p`-power roots,
which the elements of `C♭°` provide through `♯`; [Sch12] Proposition 5.20, proof, p. 27; [ECD]
Example 3.4(iii), p. 15). Define `perfectedTateAlgebra` (`perfectedTateAlgebra R Σ : Type` for
`Σ : Type*`, with `CommRing`, `TopologicalSpace`, `IsTopologicalRing`, `IsTateRing`, `CompleteSpace`,
`T2Space` instances and an `R`-algebra structure), `perfectedTateAlgebra.X` (`X s a = T_s^a` for
`s : Σ` and `a ∈ ℤ[1/p]_{≥0}`; `X s (a + b) = X s a * X s b`, `(X s (a/p))^p = X s a`, `X s a ∈ A°`), `perfectedTateAlgebra.lift` (for a complete Hausdorff uniform Tate `R`-algebra `S` and
`t : Σ → Perfection S° p`, the unique continuous `R`-algebra map with `X s (1/p^m) ↦ coeff m (t s)`;
`perfectedTateAlgebra.lift_spec` and `hom_ext`), `perfectedTateAlgebra.liftTilt` (for `S` perfectoid: continuous
`R`-algebra maps `perfectedTateAlgebra R Σ → S` correspond to maps `Σ → (tilt S)°`, with `sharp (tilt.map (liftTilt x) (X s 1)) = sharp (x s)`), `perfectedTateAlgebra.mapIndex` (for `g : Σ → Σ′`,
the continuous `R`-algebra map with `X s a ↦ X (g s) a`; `mapIndex id = id`, `mapIndex (g′ ∘ g) = mapIndex g′ ∘ mapIndex g`), `perfectedTateAlgebra.restrictedIncl` (for `Σ = Fin n`: the continuous
injective `R`-algebra map from `TauCeti.Huber.restrictedMvPowerSeriesCompletion n R` (`R⟨T⟩`) with
closed image, `T_i ↦ X i 1`), `perfectedTateAlgebra.retraction` (for `Σ = Fin n`: the continuous
`R`-linear `σ` onto integral exponents with `σ ∘ restrictedIncl = id`, the frame that
AdicSpacesPartIV R5 uses downstream), `perfectedTateAlgebra.plus` (for a ring of integral elements `R⁺`,
`R⁺⟨T_s^{1/p^∞}⟩` is a ring of integral elements; the resulting perfectoid pair) and
`perfectedTateAlgebra.laurent` (the Laurent variant is perfectoid); prove
`perfectedTateAlgebra.isPerfectoidTateRing`, `perfectedTateAlgebra.powerBoundedSubring_eq`
(`(perfectedTateAlgebra R Σ)° = {Σ c_a T^a | c_a ∈ R°, c_a → 0}`), `perfectedTateAlgebra.tiltEquiv`
(`tilt (perfectedTateAlgebra R Σ) ≃+* perfectedTateAlgebra (tilt R) Σ`, a homeomorphism with
`sharp (X s a) = X s a`), `perfectedTateAlgebra.equivCompletedColimit` (`perfectedTateAlgebra R Σ ≃+* completedFilteredColimit (Σ₀ ↦ perfectedTateAlgebra R Σ₀)` over finite subsets `Σ₀ ⊆ Σ`) and
`perfectedTateAlgebra.emptyEquiv` (`perfectedTateAlgebra R PEmpty ≃+* R`). *Needs:* P1.1; P1.5;
P1.6; P1.29; *rings-of-integral-elements-under-tilting*; Tau Ceti
`TauCeti.Huber.restrictedMvPowerSeriesCompletion`; Mathlib `AddMonoidAlgebra`, `AdicCompletion`,
`Localization.Away`, `Finsupp`.

**Checks.**

- `perfectedTateAlgebra.rootX_pow` (computation) — `(X s (1/p^{m+1}))^p = X s (1/p^m)`, and Frobenius
  on `A_0/ϖ` sends the class of `X s (1/p)` to that of `X s 1`; for `Σ = ℕ` the series
  `Σ_k ϖ^k X k 1` converges while, for `R ≠ 0`, `Σ_k X k 1` does not (its terms have norm one).
- `perfectedTateAlgebra.tilt_cyclotomic` (compatibility) — `tilt (ℚ_p^cycl⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩) ≃+* (tilt ℚ_p^cycl)⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ = 𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩` ([ECD] Example 3.4(iii); [AWS] Example
  2.3.15).
- `perfectedTateAlgebra_fin_test` (compatibility) — for `Σ = Fin n`, `perfectedTateAlgebra R (Fin n)` is `R⟨T_1^{1/p^∞}, …, T_n^{1/p^∞}⟩` as AdicSpacesPartII uses it, `restrictedIncl` embeds
  `TauCeti.Huber.restrictedMvPowerSeriesCompletion n R` with retraction `σ`, and for `Fin n ⊆ ℕ`
  the map `perfectedTateAlgebra R (Fin n) → perfectedTateAlgebra R ℕ` is a strict inclusion
  when `R ≠ 0`. For the zero ring both algebras are zero.
- `not_isPerfectoidTateRing_restricted` (non-example) — for `n ≥ 1` and `R ≠ 0`, `R⟨T_1, …, T_n⟩`
  is not perfectoid: `T_1` is not a `p`-th power modulo `ϖ^p` (a non-example that AdicSpacesPartIV
  R5 also uses downstream).
- `perfectedTateAlgebra.lift_one` (characterisation) — `lift` with `t_s^{(m)} = 1` for all `s, m`
  is evaluation at `T = 1`, a continuous `R`-algebra map to `R`; two continuous `R`-algebra maps
  agreeing on all `X s (1/p^m)` are equal.

The proposed Lean algebra is `perfectedTateAlgebra p ϖ σ`, constructed as an actual
`AdicCompletion` of `AddMonoidAlgebra R° (σ →₀ pPowerExponents p)` followed by
`Localization.Away` at the image of `ϖ`. Here `pPowerExponents p` is the additive submonoid
of `ℚ` generated by `p⁻ⁿ`, including zero. `hasBasis_nhds_zero` specifies the completion
 topology; `X` is the image of a monomial and `rootX` specializes to exponent `p⁻ⁿ`.
`lift_spec` and `hom_ext` state the continuous universal property, including its action on
coefficients. `plus` is the closure of the subring generated by coefficients in the chosen
`R⁺` and all monomials; `pair` supplies its ring-of-integral-elements assertion.
`tiltEquiv_rootX` specifies both root indices: coordinate `m` of the inverse image of
`T_s^{1/pⁿ}` is `T_s^{1/p⁽ⁿ⁺ᵐ⁾}`. `tiltEquiv_scalar` specifies the coefficient action.

`perfectedTateAlgebra.laurent` is the analogous localization of the completed group
algebra, with exponent group `pPowerIntegers p ⊆ ℚ`. The group contains negative p-power
exponents. Its `hasBasis_nhds_zero` and `algebraMap_integral` fix the topology and coefficient
map. `restrictedIncl` uses Tau Ceti's actual `restrictedMvPowerSeriesCompletion`; `retraction`
is continuous and R-linear, is a left inverse, and kills monomials with a nonintegral exponent.
`liftTilt_spec` specifies evaluation at integral tilted elements on both base coefficients and
every root coordinate ([AWS] Example 2.3.15; [Sch12] Proposition 5.20).

`finiteDiagram` is the functor on finite subsets of the index set, using the actual
variable-inclusion maps. `equivCompletedColimit` identifies its completed filtered colimit with
the full algebra; `equivCompletedColimit_spec` fixes all structural maps and both continuities.
For a variable collision the difference of the two variables maps to zero. This tests
functoriality for noninjective index maps as well as inclusions.

### P1.31 the completed cyclotomic field

**The completed cyclotomic field `ℚ_p^cycl` is a perfectoid field; its tilt and primitive ideal.**
(*cyclotomic-perfectoid-field*) For any prime `p` and `ζ_{p^n}` a compatible system of primitive
`p^n`-th roots of unity, the completion `ℚ_p^cycl` of `ℚ_p(μ_{p^∞})` is a perfectoid field: its
valuation ring is the `p`-adic completion `ℤ_p^cycl` of `ℤ_p[μ_{p^∞}]`, its value group
`|p|^{ℤ[1/p]/(p−1)}` is nondiscrete and Frobenius on `ℤ_p^cycl/p` is surjective; the
pseudo-uniformizer `ϖ = ζ_{p²} − 1` has `ϖ^p | p` (`v_p(ϖ^p) = 1/(p−1) ≤ 1`), whereas `ζ_p − 1`
does not (`v_p((ζ_p − 1)^p) = p/(p−1) > 1`); for `p = 2`, `ϖ = ζ_4 − 1` has `ϖ² = −2ζ_4`, so
`ϖ² | 2`, while `(ζ_2 − 1)² = 4 ∤ 2` ([ECD] §3, Example
3.4(i), p. 14; [KL15] Example 3.3.8, p. 78, and Remark 3.5.12, p. 86; [BMS] Example 3.6, p. 21).
Its tilt is the completed perfection of `𝔽_p((t))` with `t = ε − 1`, `ε = (1, ζ_p, ζ_{p²}, …)`, with
`|t♯| = |p|^{p/(p−1)}` ([Berkeley] Example 6.2.4, p. 44), and it is the untilt of
`(𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^, 𝔽_p[[t^{1/p^∞}]]^)` along the primitive ideal generated by
`Σ_{i=0}^{p−1}[1 + t]^{i/p}` ([AWS] Example 2.3.8, p. 54; [KL15] Example 3.3.8, p. 78). `ℤ_p^×`
acts compatibly, by `γ(t) = (1 + t)^γ − 1` on the tilt. For a finite extension `K` of `ℚ_p`, the
completion of `K(μ_{p^∞})` is the finite extension `K·ℚ_p^cycl` of `ℚ_p^cycl`, perfectoid by the
stability of perfectoid fields under finite extension of layer P3 ([Sch12] Theorem 3.7(i); [KL15]
Theorem 3.5.6). *Needs:* P1.11; P1.15; P1.19; Mathlib `Padic`, `PadicInt`.

Lean: `padicCyclotomic` (`ℚ_p^cycl` as the closure in `ℂ_p` of the subfield generated by the
`p`-power roots of unity), `padicCyclotomic.instCompleteSpace`, `padicCyclotomic.exists_one_lt_norm`
(`‖p‖ = p⁻¹`, so the restricted norm is nontrivial), `padicCyclotomic.instNontriviallyNormedField`,
`isPerfectoidField_padicCyclotomic`.

<a id="p1-32-split-tate-rings"></a>

### P1.32 perfectoidness

[ECD] §15, Lem. 15.3, p. 90 (stated for every Tate `ℤ_p`-algebra) and [Berkeley] Lecture 10,
Lem. 10.1.6, p. 75 (stated for every Tate ring in which `p` is topologically nilpotent) give the
perfectoidness of the completed tower; here its base ring is complete, because the henselian
comparison that transfers finite étale splittings to the completion needs that hypothesis, and
the polynomial example over `ℚ_p[T]` of [*uniform-completion-etale-comparison*](../AdicEtaleGeometry/README.md) (AdicEtaleGeometry A4.4) prevents its
removal. Throughout, `p` is a prime (`[Fact p.Prime]`, or the field `p.Prime` of the presentation
record), the case `p = 2` included; the prime enters the arithmetic only through the exponent
bound `p^{n−1} > n` of [*pseudouniformizer-dividing-p*](#p1-32-split-tate-rings) (P1.32). In the Frobenius argument
the choice of exponent also makes `p/ϖ^p` topologically nilpotent: divisibility `ϖ^p | p` alone
does not make the root algebra étale, since at `ϖ = p^{1/p}` and `f = 1 − p` the polynomial
`X^p − pX + p − 1` has a double root at `1`.

**Roots of monic polynomials with invertible derivative.** (*root-of-monic-in-split-tate-ring*)
Let `R` be a complete Hausdorff Tate ring with no nonsplit finite étale covers
(*finite-etale-split-ring*), `P ∈ R°[X]` monic of degree `d ≥ 1`, and `B := R[X]/(P)` with its
natural topology as a free `R`-module with basis `1, x, …, x^{d−1}`, `x` the class of `X`. Then
`x` is power-bounded in `B`. If moreover `P′(x) = u·(1 − τ)` in `B` with `u ∈ R^×` and `τ ∈ B`
topologically nilpotent, then `B` is complete and free, `1 − τ` is a unit (Tau Ceti
`IsTopologicallyNilpotent.isUnit_one_sub`), so `(P, 1)` is a standard étale pair (Mathlib
`StandardEtalePair`) and `B` is a faithfully flat finite étale `R`-algebra of rank `≥ 1`, which
has a section: `P` has a root in `R`, and every root of `P` in `R` lies in `R°` (a root is
integral over `R°`, which is integrally closed in `R`; `x` is power-bounded because the
subring of `R°` generated by the finitely many coefficients of `P` is bounded, also when `R` is
not uniform). Prove this ([ECD] §15, proof of Lem. 15.3, p. 90;
[Berkeley] Lecture 10, proof of Lem. 10.1.6, p. 75: the pattern "finite étale, hence a
solution"). The topological nilpotence of `τ` is what makes `P′(x)` a unit, and without it `B` need
not be étale (*frobenius-surjective-for-split-tate-ring*).
*Needs:* [*finite-etale-split-ring*](../AdicEtaleGeometry/README.md) (AdicEtaleGeometry A1.0.0); Mathlib
`AdjoinRoot.powerBasis'`, `StandardEtalePair`, `Algebra.IsStandardEtale`,
`StandardEtalePair.homEquiv`, `Polynomial.Monic`, `Polynomial.derivative`; Tau Ceti
`IsTopologicallyNilpotent.isUnit_one_sub`, `Huber.IsPowerBounded`, `Huber.powerBoundedSubring`,
`Huber.IsTateRing`. README only (no Lean declaration).


**Checks.**

- For `P = X − a` with `a` power-bounded, the root is `a` and the derivative is one.
- For `P = X² − X` the roots 0 and 1 are power-bounded and the derivative is a unit in the quotient.
- For `P = X²` over a nonzero ring, the derivative-error unit condition fails at the zero root.

**A pseudouniformizer whose `p`-th power divides `p`.** (*pseudouniformizer-dividing-p*) Let `R`
be a complete Hausdorff Tate ring in which `p` is topologically nilpotent and which has no nonsplit
finite étale covers, and `ϖ_0 ∈ R` a pseudouniformizer (Tau Ceti `IsPseudoUniformizer`). Choose
`n ≥ 1` with `p^n ∈ ϖ_0R°` and `p^{n−1} > n` (possible, since `p^n → 0` and `ϖ_0R°` is open). Then
`X^{p^n} − ϖ_0X − ϖ_0` has a root in `R`, and every root `ϖ` is a pseudouniformizer lying in `R°`
with `ϖ^{p^n} = ϖ_0(1 + ϖ)`, `1 + ϖ ∈ (R°)^×` (so `ϖ^{p^n}` and `ϖ_0` divide each other in `R°`),
`ϖ^p | p` in `R°` and `p/ϖ^p` topologically nilpotent. Here `τ = (p^n/ϖ_0)x^{p^n−1}` is
topologically nilpotent because `x^{p^n} ∈ ϖ_0·B°`, and from `p^n = ϖ^{p^n}w` one gets
`(p/ϖ^p)^n = ϖ^{p^n−pn}w`. Prove this as `Huber.exists_isPseudoUniformizer_pow_dvd_p` ([ECD] §15,
proof of Lem. 15.3, p. 90 (the root of `x^{p^n} − ϖ_0x − ϖ_0`); [Berkeley] Lecture 10, proof of
Lem. 10.1.6, p. 75 (the strengthening `p/ϖ^p` topologically nilpotent, by taking the exponent
larger)). The strict inequality `p^{n−1} > n`, rather than [ECD]'s `p^{n−1} ≥ n`, is what makes
`p/ϖ^p` topologically nilpotent, which the Frobenius step needs. *Needs:*
[*root-of-monic-in-split-tate-ring*](#p1-32-split-tate-rings) (P1.32);
[*finite-etale-split-ring*](../AdicEtaleGeometry/README.md) (AdicEtaleGeometry A1.0.0); Tau Ceti `Huber.IsPseudoUniformizer`,
`Huber.IsPowerBounded.isTopologicallyNilpotent_mul`, `IsTopologicallyNilpotent.isUnit_one_add`,
`Huber.powerBoundedSubring`; Mathlib `IsTopologicallyNilpotent`.

Lean: `Huber.exists_isPseudoUniformizer_pow_dvd_p` (a pseudouniformiser `ϖ ∈ R°` with `p = ϖ^p y`,
`y ∈ R°` topologically nilpotent); the rest is README only.

**Checks.**

- *test_exponent_table* (computation) — `p^{n−1} > n` excludes `n = 1` for every `p` (`p⁰ = 1`),
  and for `p = 2` also `n = 2` (`2 > 2` fails): the admissible exponents are `n ≥ 2` for `p ≥ 3`
  and `n ≥ 3` for `p = 2`; with `ϖ_0 = p` one may take `n = 2` (`p ≥ 3`) or `n = 3` (`p = 2`).
  When formalised, the computation uses a root of `X⁸ − 8X − 8` in `C₂`: it is a pseudouniformiser `v`
  with `2/v²` integral and topologically nilpotent. It also checks that the pseudouniformiser
  chosen by `Huber.exists_isPseudoUniformizer_pow_dvd_p` at `p = 2` is neither 2 nor 1.
- *test_tau_nilpotent* (computation) — in a complete split Tate ring, if `x² = ϖ(1+x)`, `ϖ` is topologically nilpotent,
  and `x,c` are power-bounded, then `cx` is topologically nilpotent: its square is a
  topologically nilpotent element times a power-bounded element. This is the quadratic
  instance of the derivative-error argument.
- *test_equality_not_nilpotent* (non-example for [ECD]'s `p^{n−1} ≥ n`) — `R = ℂ_2`, `p = 2`,
  `n = 2` (`2^{n−1} = n`), `ϖ_0 = 4` (so `p^n = 4 ∈ ϖ_0R°`): a root `ϖ` of `X⁴ − 4X − 4` has
  `|ϖ|⁴ = |4|`, so `|ϖ²| = |2|` and `p/ϖ^p = 2/ϖ²` is a unit of `R°`, not topologically
  nilpotent; `ϖ^p | p` holds.

**Surjectivity of Frobenius modulo `ϖ^p`.** (*frobenius-surjective-for-split-tate-ring*) Let `R`
be a complete Hausdorff Tate ring with no nonsplit finite étale covers and `ϖ ∈ R` a
pseudouniformizer with `ϖ^p | p` in `R°` and `p/ϖ^p` topologically nilpotent. Then for every
`f ∈ R°` there is `x ∈ R°` with `x^p − ϖ^px = f`; consequently `Φ : R°/ϖ → R°/ϖ^p`, `x ↦ x^p`
(a ring homomorphism since `p ∈ ϖ^pR°`, [ECD] §3, Def. 3.1, p. 14), is surjective. The second
hypothesis is what makes `P′ = −ϖ^p(1 − (p/ϖ^p)x^{p−1})` invertible; without it the algebra need
not be étale. Prove this ([ECD] §15, proof
of Lem. 15.3, p. 90). Over the perfectoid field `K`, the completion of `ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞})`, with
`ϖ = p^{1/p}` (so `p/ϖ^p = 1`) and `f = 1 − p`, the polynomial `X^p − ϖ^pX − f = X^p − pX + p − 1`
has the double root `1` (`P(1) = 0 = P′(1)`), so `K[X]/(P)` is not étale; [ECD]'s printed proof
asserts étaleness without this hypothesis. *Needs:* [*root-of-monic-in-split-tate-ring*](#p1-32-split-tate-rings) (P1.32);
[*pseudouniformizer-dividing-p*](#p1-32-split-tate-rings) (P1.32); [*finite-etale-split-ring*](../AdicEtaleGeometry/README.md) (AdicEtaleGeometry A1.0.0); Tau Ceti
`Huber.IsPowerBounded.isTopologicallyNilpotent_mul`, `Huber.powerBoundedSubring`; Mathlib
`frobenius`. README only (no Lean declaration).

**Checks.**

- *test_double_root* (non-example) — `P = X^p − pX + p − 1` over `K = ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞})^∧`,
  `ϖ = p^{1/p}`, `f = 1 − p`: `P(1) = 1 − p + p − 1 = 0` and `P′(1) = p − p = 0`, and
  `τ = (p/ϖ^p)x^{p−1} = x^{p−1}` is not topologically nilpotent; the root algebra is not étale.
- *test_frobenius_mod* (computation) — a root `x ∈ R°` of `X^p − ϖ^pX − f` has
  `x^p − f = ϖ^p·x ∈ ϖ^pR°`, so `Φ(x mod ϖ) = f mod ϖ^p`.
- *test_frobenius_injective* (characterisation) — an element whose `p`-th power is power-bounded
  is power-bounded; applied to `x/ϖ` when `x^p ∈ ϖ^pR°`, this makes `Φ` injective
  ([ECD] §3, Rem. 3.2, p. 14).

**A complete uniform Tate ring without nonsplit covers is perfectoid.**
(*split-tate-ring-is-perfectoid*) Let `R` be a complete Hausdorff uniform Tate ring (`R°`
bounded) in which `p` is topologically nilpotent. If `R` has no nonsplit finite étale covers, then
`R` is a perfectoid Tate ring in the sense of layer P1 ([ECD] §3, Def. 3.1,
p. 14): there is a pseudouniformizer `ϖ` with `ϖ^p | p` in `R°` (and `p/ϖ^p` topologically
nilpotent) such that `Φ : R°/ϖ → R°/ϖ^p` is an isomorphism; injectivity of `Φ` is automatic
([ECD] §3, Rem. 3.2, p. 14; layer P1,
*perfectoid-condition-independent-of-pseudouniformizer* (a), with the surjectivity bookkeeping of
its *frobenius-surjectivity-criterion*; the split-ring argument is the content here). Prove this
as `Huber.isPerfectoid_of_isFiniteEtaleSplit`, whose conclusion is the perfectoid Tate-ring
predicate that PerfectoidSpaces owns and every roadmap shares, `Perfectoid.IsPerfectoidTateRing p R`
(Frobenius surjective on `R°/p`), equivalent to the form above by [ECD] §3, Rem. 3.2, p. 14
([Berkeley] Lecture 10, proof of Lem. 10.1.6, p. 75: the perfectoidness argument uses only
completeness, uniformity and splitness of the completed ring). Completeness and the splitting hypothesis matter: `ℚ̄_p` has no
nonsplit finite étale
covers but is not complete, and `ℂ_p⟨T⟩` is complete and uniform but not perfectoid, hence by this
lemma has a nonsplit finite étale cover. *Needs:* [*pseudouniformizer-dividing-p*](#p1-32-split-tate-rings) (P1.32);
[*frobenius-surjective-for-split-tate-ring*](#p1-32-split-tate-rings) (P1.32); [*finite-etale-split-ring*](../AdicEtaleGeometry/README.md) (AdicEtaleGeometry A1.0.0); layer P1.

Lean: `Huber.isPerfectoid_of_isFiniteEtaleSplit` (`R°` bounded as the uniformity hypothesis; its
conclusion is PerfectoidSpaces' `Perfectoid.IsPerfectoidTateRing`); the rest is README only.


**Checks.**

- The complete algebraically closed field `ℂ_p` satisfies the splitness hypothesis and is perfectoid.
- The complete uniform ring `ℂ_p⟨T⟩` fails perfectoidness and therefore cannot satisfy finite-étale splitness.
- The uncompleted algebraic closure of `ℚ_p` fails the completeness hypothesis.

**Perfectoid uniform completion.** (*perfectoid-uniform-completion*) Let `(A, A⁺)` be a Huber pair
with `A` a complete Hausdorff Tate ring in which `p` is topologically nilpotent (a complete Tate
`ℤ_p`-algebra), `A⁺` any ring of integral elements, `T` any finite étale torsor tower over `A`
(*finite-etale-torsor-tower*) and `(Â_∞, Â_∞⁺)` its completed tower pair (*completed-tower-pair*).
Then `Â_∞` is a perfectoid Tate ring (layer P1: `Perfectoid.IsPerfectoidTateRing p Â_∞`,
the predicate PerfectoidSpaces owns); explicitly, `Â_∞` contains a
pseudouniformizer `ϖ`, a root of `X^{p^n} − ϖ_0X − ϖ_0` for any pseudouniformizer `ϖ_0` of `A` and
`n` with `p^n ∈ ϖ_0Â_∞°` and `p^{n−1} > n`, such that `ϖ^p | p` in `Â_∞°`, `p/ϖ^p` is
topologically nilpotent and `Φ : Â_∞°/ϖ → Â_∞°/ϖ^p` is bijective. So `(Â_∞, Â_∞⁺)` is a perfectoid
Huber pair with a continuous action of the profinite group `G`. Prove this ([ECD] §15, Lem. 15.3,
p. 90, the statement,
with completeness of `A` added; [ECD] §15, proof of Lem. 15.3, p. 90, pseudouniformizer then
Frobenius; [Berkeley] Lecture 10, Lem. 10.1.6, p. 75, the completion of the colimit with
`colim R_i°` open and bounded; [ECD] §3, Def. 3.1, p. 14, the definition verified). Completeness
of `A` cannot be omitted: for the non-complete Tate `ℤ_p`-algebra `ℚ_p[T]` (ring of definition
`ℤ_p[T]`, `p`-adic topology) every tower has colimit `B[T]` with `B` a colimit of finite étale
`ℚ_p`-algebras, ind-finite-étale over `ℚ_p`, and the uniform completion `B̂⟨T⟩` is not perfectoid
(its power-bounded subring is `B̂°⟨T⟩`, and modulo `p` the class of `T` is not a `p`-th power in
`(B̂°/p)[T]`), although [ECD] Lem. 15.3 is stated for all Tate `ℤ_p`-algebras. *Needs:*
[*completed-tower-pair*](../AdicEtaleGeometry/README.md) (AdicEtaleGeometry A4.5); [*finite-etale-invariance-along-tower*](../AdicEtaleGeometry/README.md) (AdicEtaleGeometry A4.5); [*split-tate-ring-is-perfectoid*](#p1-32-split-tate-rings) (P1.32);
[*finite-etale-torsor-tower*](../AdicEtaleGeometry/README.md) (AdicEtaleGeometry A4.3); layer P1; Tau Ceti `Huber.IsPseudoUniformizer`. README only (no Lean declaration).

**Checks.**

- *completion_test_Qp* (computation) — for the field tower over `ℚ_p` the perfectoid ring
  produced is `ℂ_p`, for `p = 2` as for odd `p`.


**Checks.**

- The trivial-group tower over a perfectoid split base has that original perfectoid ring as its completion.

- For the zero Tate base, all stage and completed rings are zero and the perfectoid conditions are vacuous.

### P1.32a examples and non-examples

**Examples and non-examples of perfectoid Tate rings.** (*perfectoid-examples*) The following are
perfectoid Tate rings, each a declaration of the library, checked against P1.1 through the criteria
of this layer: (1) `ℂ_p` (Mathlib `PadicComplex p`), a perfectoid field whose tilt contains
`p♭ = (p, p^{1/p}, …)` with `(p♭)♯ = p` ([Bhatt] Example 3.1.2(2), p. 9); (2) the completion `K_1`
of `ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞})`, a perfectoid field with valuation ring the `p`-adic completion of
`ℤ_p[p^{1/p^∞}]` and tilt `𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^` with `t♯ = p`, the untilt along `(p − [t])` ([AWS]
Example 2.3.7, p. 54; [Bhatt] Example 3.1.2(1), p. 9); (3) the completed perfection
`𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^`, a perfectoid field of characteristic `p` equal to its own tilt; (4) `ℚ_p^cycl`
(P1.31); (5) `ℚ_p^cycl⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩` (P1.30); (6) the ring
`R = ℤ_p^cycl[[T^{1/p^∞}]]⟨(p/T)^{1/p^∞}⟩[1/T]` with `ϖ = T^{1/p}` (`ϖ^p = T` divides `p` in `R°`),
which does not contain a nonarchimedean field ([ECD] §3, Example 3.4(iv), p. 15; [Berkeley] Example
6.1.5(4), p. 42); (7) products such as `K × K♭` for a characteristic-zero perfectoid field `K`, where `p` is a nonzero
nonunit (the product of two Tate rings is Tate, with pair of definition the product,
`Perfectoid.IsTateRing.instProd`, this roadmap's declaration in the `Perfectoid` namespace:
the library does not have a product instance). Non-examples: `ℚ_p` and every discretely valued nonarchimedean field ([ECD] Remark 3.3,
p. 14; [Berkeley] Remark 6.1.4, p. 42), `𝔽_p((t))` (not perfect), `ℂ_p[ε]/(ε²)` (not uniform),
`R⟨T_1, …, T_n⟩` for `n ≥ 1` and `R ≠ 0` (`T_1` not a `p`-th power modulo `ϖ^p`). *Needs:* P1.1;
P1.15; P1.30; P1.31; P1.2; Mathlib `PadicComplex`, `Padic`; Tau Ceti `TauCeti.Huber.Padic.isTateRing`,
`TauCeti.Huber.PadicInt.not_isTateRing`, `TauCeti.Huber.LaurentSeries.isTateRing`.

### P1.33 compatibility with AdicSpaces' perfect field `F` and `A_inf`

**Compatibility with AdicSpaces' perfect field `F` and `A_inf = W(𝒪_F)`.**
(*adicspaces-layer-6-compatibility*) Let `F` be a complete rank-one nonarchimedean perfect field of
characteristic `p` with a pseudo-uniformizer `ϖ`, as in the Foundations of adic spaces roadmap
(AdicSpaces), layer 6.1 (no algebraic closedness). Tau Ceti's Fargues–Fontaine input is more
general than a field: a perfect ring `R` (`[CharP R p] [PerfectRing R p]`) with an element `ϖ`
and the `(p, [ϖ])`-adic topology on `W(R)` (`TauCeti.FarguesFontaine.spaY`, `frobeniusHomeomorph`,
`windowU`, `windowV`, `spaX`); the statements below are for `R = 𝒪_F`. Then (a) `F` is a perfectoid
field of characteristic `p` (P1.2, P1.11), its tilt is `F` itself with `♯` the identity (P1.4), and
`(F, 𝒪_F)` is a perfectoid Tate pair of characteristic `p` ([ECD] §3, Proposition 3.5, p. 15;
[Sch12] Lemma 3.4(iv), p. 16, and §3, p. 15); (b) AdicSpaces' `A_inf = W(𝒪_F)`, with pair of
definition `(A_inf, (p, [ϖ]))`, is the ring `W(F♭⁺) = W(𝒪_F)` of this layer, its `(p, [ϖ])`-adic
completeness, separatedness and Huber-ring structure being the library's
`WittVector.isAdicComplete_span_p_teichmuller`, `isHausdorff_span_p_teichmuller` and
`TauCeti.Huber.WittVector.isHuberRing_adicTopology_span_p_teichmuller` (for the integers of a
normed field, `Complete.lean` has the instance directly), cited in
*witt-vectors-of-perfect-plus-ring* ([Bhatt] Example 6.1.6, p. 43); (c) the untilts of `F` are the
pairs `(W(𝒪_F)[1/[ϖ]]/(ξ), W(𝒪_F)/(ξ))` for primitive `ξ ∈ A_inf` (P1.21). AdicSpaces' curve
`𝒴 ⊆ Spa(A_inf, A_inf)` and its Frobenius windows stay with AdicSpaces and the library; this layer
only identifies the input objects. For `F` the completed perfection of `𝔽_p((t))`, the untilts include
`ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞})^` (`ξ = p − [t]`) and `ℚ_p^cycl` (`ξ = Σ_{i<p}[1 + t]^{i/p}`). *Needs:* P1.2; P1.11;
P1.4; *witt-vectors-of-perfect-plus-ring*; P1.21; the Foundations of adic spaces roadmap
(AdicSpaces), layer 6.1; Tau Ceti `TauCeti.FarguesFontaine.spaY`,
`WittVector.isAdicComplete_span_p_teichmuller`,
`TauCeti.Huber.WittVector.isHuberRing_adicTopology_span_p_teichmuller`.

For a complete nontrivially normed ultrametric field `F` with `CharP F p` and
`IsPerfectoidField p F`, `tilt.ainfEquiv` identifies
`WittVector p (Pair.tilt p (Pair.powerBounded F)).plus` with
`WittVector p (NormedField.valuation (K := F)).integer`. Here the latter integer
subring is `𝒪_F = {x : F | ‖x‖ ≤ 1}`. The perfect-field hypothesis above supplies
`IsPerfectoidField p F` by `IsPerfectoidField.iff_perfectRing`.
`tilt.ainfEquiv_coeff` specifies the map on every Witt coordinate as
`tilt.equivOfCharP`, so it is the Witt functor applied to the integral tilt
identification ([ECD] Lemmas 3.10–3.11, pp. 16–17).
For integral parameters `t ∈ F♭⁺` and `ϖ ∈ 𝒪_F` with
`tilt.equivOfCharP t = ϖ`, `tilt.ainfEquiv_map_ideal` identifies
`(p,[t])^n` with `(p,[ϖ])^n` for every `n : ℕ`, and
`tilt.ainfEquiv_continuous` states continuity in both directions for these
adic topologies. These are consequences of Witt functoriality and the
power-ideal neighbourhood bases; for a pseudouniformizer `ϖ` they identify
precisely the inputs to `TauCeti.FarguesFontaine.spaY` and `windowU`.
The two statements also apply to zero and unit parameters; they do not
assert that those parameters are pseudouniformizers.

**Checks.**

- `ainfEquiv_teichmuller` — for corresponding integral parameters, the comparison
  sends `[t]` to `[ϖ]`, fixing the second generator of the adic ideal.
- `ainfEquiv_prime_nonzero` — the comparison fixes `p`; this Witt vector is
  nonzero although its zeroth coordinate is zero, distinguishing it from
  the characteristic-`p` coefficient ring (also when `p = 2`).
- `ainfEquiv_zero_parameter` — setting the second parameter to zero gives
  continuity in both directions for the `p`-adic topologies.

### Examples

The worked examples of this layer are the checks above together with P1.31 and P1.32a: `ℚ_p` as the
complete uniform Tate ring with bijective Frobenius on `𝔽_p` that is not perfectoid, and
`ℂ_p[ε]/(ε²)` as the non-uniform ring a definition without uniformity would accept; `ℂ_p` with
`ϖ = p^{1/p}` and its gauge `2^{-p v_p(x)}`; the completed perfection of `𝔽_p((t))` equal to its own
tilt; `ε = (ζ_{p^n})_n` in `(ℚ_p^cycl)♭` with `ε♯ = 1`, `(ε − 1)♯ ≠ 0` and
`|(ε − 1)♯| = |p|^{p/(p−1)}`; `uniformTilt ℚ_p ≅ 𝔽_p` with the discrete topology; `𝒪/m` almost zero
and `𝒪/p^{1/p}𝒪` not, over `𝒪_{ℂ_p}`; the primitive elements `p − [p♭]` and `Σ_{i<p}[ε]^{i/p}` of
`W(𝒪_{ℂ_p♭})` against the non-primitive `p²`, `[ϖ]` and `[ε] − 1`; the untilts of
`𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^` along `(p)`, `(p − [t])` and `(Σ_{i<p}[1 + t]^{i/p})`, namely the field itself,
`ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞})^` and `ℚ_p^cycl`, with the Frobenius-twisted marking of `ℂ_p` as the non-isomorphic
marked untilt; `K⟨T⟩` failing the metric criterion at `T`; `ℤ_p` against the integral perfectoid
`ℤ_p[p^{1/p^∞}]^`; `C^0(S, K)` as a completed colimit and the tower `ℚ_p(p^{1/p^n})` for which
tilting does not commute with the completed colimit; `ℚ_p^cycl⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩` with its tilt
`𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩` against the non-perfectoid `R⟨T_1, …, T_n⟩`; and the non-field
perfectoid ring `ℤ_p^cycl[[T^{1/p^∞}]]⟨(p/T)^{1/p^∞}⟩[1/T]`.

| `field_padic_negative` | The discretely valued field `ℚ_p` is not perfectoid, although its mod-`p` Frobenius is surjective. |
| `field_padicComplex` | `ℂ_p` is perfectoid, its nonzero norms are rational powers of `p`, and integral elements have integral `p`-th roots. |
| `field_discrete_charP` | A complete characteristic-`p` field with a nontrivial discrete value group is neither perfect nor perfectoid. |
| `primitive_mixed_generators` | The radical generator `p−[p♭]` and the shifted cyclotomic sum are primitive over `𝒪_{ℂ_p♭}`; for odd `p`, the radical generator has first two Witt coordinates `−p♭` and `1`. |
| `primitive_p_squared_and_teichmuller` | In a nonzero characteristic-`p` perfectoid plus ring, `p²` and a single Teichmüller lift have zero first Witt coordinate and are not primitive. |
| `primitive_p` | The Witt vector `p` and its principal ideal are primitive. |
| `primitive_two_coordinates` | At `p=2`, the first two Witt coordinates of `2−[x]` are `x` and `1+x²`, fixing the sign and coordinate convention. |

The Lean `example`s of `Suggested.lean` for this layer cover `ℚ_p` (not perfectoid, not a perfectoid
field, no pseudo-uniformizer with compatible roots), the zero ring (perfectoid), `p` versus `p²` and
Teichmüller lifts as distinguished elements, `ℤ_p` versus `𝒪_{ℂ_p}` and perfect rings of
characteristic `p` as integral perfectoid rings, and the ramified control of P1.5 (`u` is not a
`p`-th power in `𝔽_p[u]/(u^p)`).

### Dependencies

Layer P0 of this roadmap (P0.1, P0.2, P0.4, P0.5, P0.6, P0.8, P0.16, P0.20, P0.22); Tau Ceti's
Huber-ring layer (`TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing`, `IsHuberRing`, `IsPseudoUniformizer`,
`powerBoundedSubring`, `IsBounded`, `Pair`, `Pair.Hom`, `PairOfDefinition`,
`IsRingOfIntegralElements`, `topologicallyNilpotentIdeal`, `restrictedMvPowerSeriesCompletion`,
`Padic.isTateRing`, `LaurentSeries.isTateRing`, `ValuationSpectrum.cont`); Mathlib's `Perfection`,
`PreTilt`, `Tilt`, `WittVector` and `WittVector.fontaineTheta`, `IsAdicComplete`, `AdicCompletion`,
`Localization.Away`, `PadicComplex`, `AddMonoidAlgebra`, the Serre-class and `CategoryTheory`
material listed in the subsections; Tau Ceti's Witt-vector completeness
(`WittVector.isAdicComplete_span_p_teichmuller`, `isHausdorff_span_p_teichmuller`,
`TauCeti.Huber.WittVector.isHuberRing_adicTopology_span_p_teichmuller`) and Fargues–Fontaine input
(`TauCeti.FarguesFontaine.spaY`). Other roadmaps, by subsection: P1.3 uses AdicSpacesPartII R0.4
(Tate norm data and the spectral seminorm); P1.12, and through it P1.13, uses AdicSpacesPartIII R3.9
(the Gel'fand spectrum); P1.33 uses AdicSpaces 6.1 (the perfect field `F` and `A_inf`). The
uniformity of P1.1 is Tau Ceti's `IsBounded` condition, the notion AdicSpaces 4.2 names. None of
these subsections cites this roadmap. P1.2 proves the `ϖ`-adic completeness of rings of
definition directly; P1.32 uses AdicEtaleGeometry A1.0.0, A1.0.3a and A4.2–A4.5's
split-ring, torsor-tower and completion theory. Layers P2, P3, P4, P5 and P7 of this roadmap
consume the tilting, approximation and colimit statements; the consumers in other roadmaps are
listed under Downstream consumers.

## Layer P2: rational localisation, the sheaf theorem and perfectoid spaces

The layer passes from perfectoid Tate pairs to perfectoid spaces. It constructs the tilting map
`x ↦ x♭` on adic spectra and proves that it is a homeomorphism `Spa(R, R⁺) ≅ Spa(R♭, R♭⁺)`
identifying rational subsets; shows that rational localisations of a perfectoid Tate pair are
perfectoid with tilt the rational localisation of the tilt, that completed residue fields are
perfectoid, and that perfectoid Tate pairs are stably uniform and sheafy, with `O_X` acyclic and
`O_X⁺` almost acyclic on rational subsets (the sheaf theorem); defines affinoid perfectoid spaces
and the full subcategory `Perfd` of perfectoid spaces inside the adic spaces of AdicSpaces, with
`Perf` in characteristic `p`; glues the tilt `X ↦ X♭` and proves the tilting equivalence
`Perfd/X ≃ Perf/X♭`; and builds completed tensor products of perfectoid pairs, fibre products of
perfectoid spaces (over perfectoid and over analytic bases), absolute products in `Perf`, and the
comparison with Scholze's perfectoid spaces over a perfectoid field. Throughout, `(R, R⁺)` is a
perfectoid Tate pair in the sense of ECD Definition 3.1, of characteristic `0`, `p` or mixed, with no
perfectoid base field; `ϖ = (ϖ♭)♯` is a pseudouniformiser with `ϖ^p | p` in `R°` and compatible
`p`-power roots, as in the standing conventions of this roadmap; "almost zero" refers to the
ideal of topologically nilpotent elements of `R⁺` (layer P1); and `𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞}))` abbreviates
the completed perfection `𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^∧` of `𝔽_p((t))` (the tilt of `ℚ_p^cycl` and of
`ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞})^`, layer P1), the uncompleted union `⋃_n 𝔽_p((t^{1/p^n}))` not being complete.

Global objects are Tau Ceti's pre-adic spaces (`TauCeti.PreAdicSpace`): the perfectoid
subcategory `Perfd` (P2.10) is cut out by sheafiness together with open covers by affinoid
perfectoid opens, the adic spectra `presentationLimitPreAdicSpace` of perfectoid Tate pairs (the
spectra of `Perfectoid.PairCat p` objects). Its charts are sheafy, so this is the usual category of
perfectoid adic spaces. AdicEtaleGeometry's analytic Yoneda carrier `YonedaAdicSpace` (rational
sheaves locally represented by complete Huber pairs, with its supplied underlying valuation-space
functor) receives perfectoid spaces, as adic spaces, through its fully faithful
`YonedaAdicSpace.ofAdicSpace`; the statements below that are phrased on that carrier, notably the
comparisons with AdicEtaleGeometry's predicates and sites, apply to a perfectoid space through this
embedding, and the comparison of the two presentations belongs to AdicEtaleGeometry. Rings and pairs
remain the pinned Tau Ceti rings and pairs. Characteristic `p` means `p = 0` on every affinoid
chart, including the zero chart; in Lean, `InCharP` asks for `p = 0` in every ring of sections. The bundled global category here uses small affinoid rings
and spaces covered by a set of such charts.

### P2.1 the tilting map on adic spectra

**The tilting map `x ↦ x♭` from `Spa(R, R⁺)` to `Spa(R♭, R♭⁺)`.** (*tilting-map-of-spectra*) Let
`(R, R⁺)` be a perfectoid Tate pair with tilt `(R♭, R♭⁺)` and sharp map `♯ : R♭ → R` (continuous
and multiplicative, not additive), `X = Spa(R, R⁺)`, `X♭ = Spa(R♭, R♭⁺)`; no base field. For
`x ∈ X` with valuation `v_x : R → Γ_x ∪ {0}`, the composite `v_x ∘ ♯ : R♭ → Γ_x ∪ {0}` is a
continuous valuation of `R♭` with `v_x(f♯) ≤ 1` for all `f ∈ R♭⁺`; its class is a point `x♭ ∈ X♭`,
characterised by `|f(x♭)| ≤ |g(x♭)| ⟺ |f♯(x)| ≤ |g♯(x)|` for all `f, g ∈ R♭` (written
`|f(x♭)| = |f♯(x)|`). The tilting map `τ_R : X → X♭`, `x ↦ x♭`, satisfies: (a)
`supp(x♭) = {f ∈ R♭ : f♯ ∈ supp(x)}`; (b) `τ_R` is continuous: if `f₁, …, f_n, g ∈ R♭` and some
`f_i` is a unit of `R♭` (for instance `f_n = (ϖ♭)^N`; the unit makes `f_i♯` a unit of `R` because
`♯` is multiplicative with `1♯ = 1`, and without such a normalisation the unit-ideal condition on
the `f♯` is not automatic before the homeomorphism is known), then `f₁♯, …, f_n♯` generate the unit
ideal of `R` and `τ_R⁻¹(U(f₁, …, f_n / g)) = U(f₁♯, …, f_n♯ / g♯)`; every rational subset of `X♭`
has a presentation with `f_i, g ∈ R♭⁺` and `f_n = (ϖ♭)^N` for some `N`; (c) naturality: for a
morphism of perfectoid Tate pairs `φ : (R, R⁺) → (S, S⁺)` (continuous, `φ(R⁺) ⊆ S⁺`) with tilt
`φ♭` (layer P1, P1.6), so that `φ ∘ ♯_R = ♯_S ∘ φ♭`, one has `τ_R ∘ Spa(φ) = Spa(φ♭) ∘ τ_S`; (d)
if `pR = 0` then `(R♭, R♭⁺) = (R, R⁺)` with `♯ = id` and `τ_R = id`. That `τ_R` is a homeomorphism
identifying rational subsets is P2.2; here only the map and its first properties are built
([ECD] §3, Thm 3.12, p. 17; [AWS] Lecture 2, §2.6, Lem. 2.6.12 with proof, pp. 64–65, for the
well-definedness of `v ↦ v ∘ ♯` without a base field; [Sch12] §6, proof of Thm 6.3, p. 31, for the
valuation check and for continuity through the preimage formula (b)). In `PerfectoidSpace`, define
`spaTilt` as the map `spa R⁺ → spa R♭⁺`, `x ↦ x♭`, sending `v_x` to `v_x ∘ ♯`; prove
`spaTilt_vle_iff` (`(spaTilt x).vle f g ↔ x.vle f♯ g♯` for `f g : R♭`), `supp_spaTilt` (the support
of `spaTilt x` is the preimage under `♯` of the support of `x`), `continuous_spaTilt`,
`spaTilt_preimage_rationalSubset` (if some `f_i ∈ T` is a unit of `R♭`, then
`spaTilt ⁻¹' rationalSubset R♭⁺ T s = rationalSubset R⁺ (T.image ♯) s♯`),
`exists_rationalSubset_eq_insert_pseudoUniformizer_pow` (every rational subset of `Spa(R♭, R♭⁺)`
equals `rationalSubset R♭⁺ (insert ((ϖ♭)^N) T) s` with `T ⊆ R♭⁺`, `s ∈ R♭⁺`, for some `N`),
`spaTilt_comp_spaComap` (`spaTilt ∘ φ.spaComap = φ♭.spaComap ∘ spaTilt`) and
`spaTilt_eq_id_of_charP` (simp: `spaTilt = id` under the identification of `R` with its tilt when
`pR = 0`). *Needs:* layer P1 (P1.4, P1.5, P1.6); Tau Ceti `TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.spa`,
`TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.rationalSubset`,
`TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.rationalSubset_insert_of_forall_vle`,
`TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.rationalSubset_image_mul_right`,
`TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.isTopologicalBasis_spaRationalFamily`,
`TauCeti.Huber.Pair.Hom.spaComap`; Mathlib `Valuation`.

**Checks.**

- `spaTilt_test_perfectoidDisc_point` (computation) — for `R = ℚ_p^cycl⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩` and `x` the
  point `T ↦ ϖ` (evaluation `T^{1/p^n} ↦ ϖ^{1/p^n}`), `spaTilt x` is the point `T ↦ ϖ♭` of
  `ℚ_p^cycl♭⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩`: `|T(x♭)| = |T♯(x)| = |ϖ(x)|`.
- `spaTilt_test_charP_eq_id` (degenerate) — for `R = 𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^∧⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩`
  (characteristic `p`), `spaTilt` is the identity of `Spa(R, R⁺)`.
- `spaTilt_test_preimage_disc` (compatibility) — on the perfectoid disc over `ℚ_p^cycl`,
  `spaTilt ⁻¹' U({T, ϖ♭}/ϖ♭) = U({T, ϖ}/ϖ)`, the instance of `spaTilt_preimage_rationalSubset`
  with `f₂ = ϖ♭`; so `τ⁻¹{|T| ≤ |ϖ♭|} = {|T| ≤ |ϖ|}`.
- `spaTilt_test_no_ringHom` (non-example) — there is no ring homomorphism `ℚ_p^cycl♭ → ℚ_p^cycl`
  (characteristic `p` to characteristic `0`), so `spaTilt` is not `Pair.Hom.spaComap` of any
  morphism of Huber pairs; a definition of `x♭` as the pullback of `x` along a ring map cannot
  typecheck in mixed characteristic.
- `spaTilt_test_vle_characterisation` (characterisation) — `x♭` is the unique point `y` of
  `Spa(R♭, R♭⁺)` with `y.vle f g ↔ x.vle f♯ g♯` for all `f g`; two points with the same relation
  coincide.

**Approximation of homogeneous functions on a perfectoid polydisc.**
(*approximation-on-perfectoid-polydisc*) Let `K` be a complete, nontrivially normed
ultrametric field with `IsPerfectoidField p K`, with tilt `K♭`, `ϖ♭ ∈ K♭` a pseudouniformiser
with `ϖ = (ϖ♭)♯` and `ϖ^p | p` in `K°`, and let `P = K⟨T₀^{1/p^∞}, …, T_n^{1/p^∞}⟩` be the
perfected Tate algebra, with `P° = K°⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩` and monomials of total `T`-degree in `ℤ[1/p]_{≥0}`
(`K°` in degree `0`; a series is homogeneous when all its nonzero monomials have one degree;
the completed ring itself is not a direct-sum graded ring) and tilt `P♭ = K♭⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩`, `T_i♯ = T_i` (layer P1; [KL16] §3.3, Ex. 3.3.12,
p. 61). Prove that for `f ∈ P°` homogeneous of degree `d`, every `c ∈ ℤ[1/p]` with `c ≥ 0` and every
`ε ∈ ℤ[1/p]` with `0 < ε < 1` there is `g ∈ P♭°` homogeneous of degree `d` with
`|f(x) − g♯(x)| ≤ |ϖ^{1−ε}(x)| · max(|f(x)|, |ϖ^c(x)|)` for all `x ∈ Spa(P, P°)`; in particular
`max(|f(x)|, |ϖ^c(x)|) = max(|g♯(x)|, |ϖ^c(x)|)` for all `x` ([Sch12] §6, Lem. 6.5 with proof,
pp. 33–34, the induction on `c` with loss `ε(c)`; [Bhatt] Ch. 9, Lem. 9.2.6 and the paragraph
before it, p. 101). For `f = T₀` one may take `g = T₀` for every `c`; for
`f = T₀ + ϖT₁`, `g = T₀ + ϖ♭T₁` satisfies `f ≡ g♯ mod ϖP°` because `♯` is additive modulo `ϖ`,
which gives the estimate for `c = 0`, while `c > 0` needs the inductive corrections. *Needs:*
*tilting-map-of-spectra*; layer P1 (P1.5, the sharp map; P1.30, the perfected Tate algebra and its tilt); Tau Ceti
`TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.rationalSubset`.

`Perfectoid.homogeneousPart p ϖ n d` is the closed span of monomials of total degree `d`,
not a grading by a direct sum. `homogeneous_sharp_approximation` records the quantitative
estimate over `K` with `c = a/p^m` and `ε = b/p^k`, `0 < b < p^k`,
and with `P.plus = P°`. The definition `homogeneousPart` and its component Checks apply
more generally to a perfectoid Tate base `R₀`.

**Checks for homogeneous components.** `homogeneous_degree_zero_constant`: every scalar has
degree zero. `homogeneous_two_variables`: `T₀ + ϖT₁` has degree one.
`homogeneous_wrong_degree`: `T₀` is not degree zero over a nonzero base.
`homogeneous_zero`: zero belongs to every component. These use the completed algebra itself.
The degree-preserving estimate is [Sch12] Lemma 6.5 and Remark 6.6, pp. 33–34,
for the perfectoid field `K`.

### P2.2 the tilting homeomorphism

The tilting map of P2.1 is a homeomorphism matching rational subsets; its two inputs are the
characteristic-`p` rational localisations and the approximation lemma, proved here.

**The tilting homeomorphism `Spa(R, R⁺) ≅ Spa(R♭, R♭⁺)` identifies rational subsets.**
(*tilting-homeomorphism-and-rational-subsets*) Let `(R, R⁺)` be a perfectoid Tate pair (ECD
Definition 3.1; characteristic `0`, `p` or mixed, as in ECD Example 3.4(iv); no perfectoid base
field) with tilt `(R♭, R♭⁺)`. Then the tilting map `τ_R : X = Spa(R, R⁺) → X♭ = Spa(R♭, R♭⁺)`,
`|f(x♭)| = |f♯(x)|` (see *tilting-map-of-spectra*), is a homeomorphism, natural in morphisms of
perfectoid Tate pairs. A subset `U ⊆ X` is rational if and only if `τ_R(U) ⊆ X♭` is rational;
explicitly, for `f₁, …, f_n, g ∈ R♭⁺` with `f_n = (ϖ♭)^N`,
`τ_R(U(f₁♯, …, f_n♯ / g♯)) = U(f₁, …, f_n / g)`, and every rational subset of `X` can be written
as `U(f₁♯, …, f_n♯ / g♯)` for such `f_i, g`. Consequently `τ_R` preserves the specialisation
order (Mathlib `Topology.IsInducing.specializes_iff` applied to the homeomorphism),
quasi-compact opens and rank-one (maximal) points, and restricts, for every rational
`U ⊆ X`, to the homeomorphism `Homeomorph.image τ_R U`, identifying rational subsets of `U` and of `τ_R(U)`
([ECD] §3, Thm 3.12, p. 17, and proof of Thms 3.12–3.13, p. 17, the route followed; [Sch12] §6,
Cor. 6.7(ii)–(iii) with proof, p. 35, injectivity from the approximation lemma and surjectivity by
untilting the residue field over `R`; [KL15] Thm 3.6.14(b) and [KL16] §3.3, Thm 3.3.16, p. 63, the
explicit form of the rational subsets and an independent proof for Fontaine perfectoid Tate rings,
including those in which `p` is neither `0` nor invertible; [AWS] Lecture 2, §2.5, Thm 2.5.1,
pp. 59–60, the analytic-ring generalisation). Sch12 Theorem 6.3(i) (perfectoid affinoid
`K`-algebras over a perfectoid field) is a special case. For `R = ℚ_p^cycl⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩`,
`τ({|T| ≤ |ϖ|}) = {|T| ≤ |ϖ♭|}`, the Gauss point goes to the Gauss point and the classical point
`T ↦ ϖ` to `T ↦ ϖ♭`. The theorem applies to ECD Example 3.4(iv),
`R = ℤ_p^cycl[[T^{1/p^∞}]]⟨(p/T)^{1/p^∞}⟩[1/T]` with `ϖ = T^{1/p}`, which lives over no field: its
spectrum has points with `|p(x)| = 0` and points with `|p(x)| ≠ 0`, both matched with points of the
characteristic-`p` space `X♭`. Without the approximation lemma one only obtains that rational
subsets of `X` are preimages of quasi-compact opens of `X♭` ([Bhatt] Rem. 9.2.8); that images of
rational subsets are rational needs *approximation-lemma*. *Needs:* *tilting-map-of-spectra*;
*rational-localization-in-characteristic-p*; *approximation-lemma*; layer P1 (P1.6, P1.18 (*rings-of-integral-elements-under-tilting* (a)),
P1.27); Tau Ceti `TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.rationalSubset_inter`,
`TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.rationalSubset_insert_of_forall_vle`,
`TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.rationalSubset_image_mul_right`,
`TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.isTopologicalBasis_spaRationalFamily`,
`TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.spectralSpace_spa_of_pairOfDefinition`.

**Rational localisations in characteristic p are perfect, with an explicit almost integral
model.** (*rational-localization-in-characteristic-p*) Let `(R, R⁺)` be a perfectoid Tate pair with
`pR = 0` (so `R` is a perfect complete Tate ring and `R⁺` is perfect, [ECD] §3, Prop. 3.5, p. 15),
`ϖ ∈ R⁺` a pseudouniformiser, `X = Spa(R, R⁺)`, `f₁, …, f_n, g ∈ R⁺` with `f_n = ϖ^N` (every
rational subset has such a presentation, by (b) of *tilting-map-of-spectra* applied to `R = R♭`),
and `U = U(f₁, …, f_n / g)`. Prove: (i) the rational localisation `(O_X(U), O_X⁺(U))` (AdicSpaces
layer 3.1) is a perfectoid Tate pair of characteristic `p`: Frobenius is bijective on `O_X(U)` and
on `O_X⁺(U)`; (ii) for `A_U` the `ϖ`-adic completion of the subring
`R⁺[(f_i/g)^{1/p^m} : i ≤ n, m ≥ 0]` of `R[1/g]`, `A_U` is perfect and `ϖ`-torsion free,
`A_U ⊆ O_X⁺(U) ⊆ O_X(U)°` inside `O_X(U) = A_U[1/ϖ]`, and both `O_X(U)°/A_U` and `O_X⁺(U)/A_U`
are almost zero (killed by `ϖ^{1/p^k}` for all `k`, the almost setup being the ideal of
topologically nilpotent elements of `R⁺`, generated in a perfect `R⁺` by the `ϖ^{1/p^k}`); (iii)
if `(R, R⁺)` is an algebra over a characteristic-`p` perfectoid field `K`, with continuous
scalar map carrying `K°` into `R⁺` and with the parameter and its roots coming from `K`,
the surjection `ψ : R⁺[T₁^{1/p^∞}, …, T_n^{1/p^∞}] → R⁺[(f_i/g)^{1/p^∞}]`,
`T_i^{1/p^m} ↦ (f_i/g)^{1/p^m}`, has kernel containing the ideal `I` generated by the
`g^{1/p^m} T_i^{1/p^m} − f_i^{1/p^m}` (`i ≤ n`, `m ≥ 0`), and `ker ψ / I` is almost zero; (iv)
every perfectoid Tate pair of characteristic `p` is stably uniform ([KL15] §3.1,
Prop. 3.1.7 with proof, pp. 67–68, for (i) and (iv) without a base field; [AWS] Lecture 2, §2.5,
proof of Thm 2.5.3, first paragraph, p. 60, the Frobenius universal-property argument of (i);
[Sch12] §6, proof of Lem. 6.4(i) for `K` of characteristic `p`, p. 31, the presentation (iii);
[Bhatt] Ch. 9, Lem. 9.2.3 with proof, pp. 97–98, almost vanishing of the kernel of `ψ` by
perfectness). For `K = 𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^∧` and `R = K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩`, `U = {|T| ≤ |t|}`:
`O_X(U) = K⟨(T/t)^{1/p^∞}⟩` and `A_U = K°⟨(T/t)^{1/p^∞}⟩ = O_X(U)°` exactly; for the annulus
`{|t| ≤ |T| ≤ 1}`, `O_X(U) = K⟨T^{1/p^∞}, (t/T)^{1/p^∞}⟩` is perfect. Perfectness in (i) fails
for non-perfect rings: for the Tate algebra `𝔽_p((t))⟨T⟩` (not perfectoid) the localisation at
`{|T| ≤ |t|}` is `𝔽_p((t))⟨T/t⟩`, which is not perfect. *Needs:* layer P1 (P1.1); layer P0; Tau
Ceti `TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.existsUnique_continuous_ringHom_of_forall_comap_mem_rationalSubset`,
`TauCeti.Huber.PairOfDefinition.completionLocObj`,
`TauCeti.Huber.PairOfDefinition.completedPlusSubring`,
`TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.mem_iff_forall_vle_one`; Mathlib `PerfectRing`, `frobeniusEquiv`.

**Approximation lemma: every function on a perfectoid affinoid is approximated by a sharp.**
(*approximation-lemma*) Let `(R, R⁺)` be a perfectoid Tate pair with tilt `(R♭, R♭⁺)`,
`ϖ = (ϖ♭)♯`, `X = Spa(R, R⁺)`; no base field; estimates are pointwise in `Γ_x ∪ {0}` with
`|ϖ^r(x)| := |((ϖ♭)^r)♯(x)|` for `r ∈ ℤ[1/p]`. Prove: (i) for every `f ∈ R`, every `c ∈ ℤ[1/p]` with
`c ≥ 0` and every `ε ∈ ℤ[1/p]` with `0 < ε < 1` there is `g ∈ R♭` with
`|f(x) − g♯(x)| ≤ |ϖ^{1−ε}(x)| · max(|f(x)|, |ϖ^c(x)|)` for all `x ∈ X`, so that
`max(|f(x)|, |ϖ^c(x)|) = max(|g♯(x)|, |ϖ^c(x)|)`; (ii) for `f, h ∈ R` and an integer `c ≥ 0` there
are `a, b ∈ R♭` with `{x : |f(x)| ≤ |h(x)|, |ϖ^c(x)| ≤ |h(x)|} = {x : |a♯(x)| ≤ |b♯(x)|, |ϖ^c(x)| ≤ |b♯(x)|}` ([Sch12] §6, Cor. 6.7(i) with proof, pp. 34–35, the reduction to rank-one
points and to the polydisc; [KL16] §3.2, Lem. 3.2.7 (preamble), p. 57, approximation by Euclidean
division with a Fontaine primitive element, and §3.3, proof of Thm 3.3.16, p. 63, how it moves
rational subsets across tilting without a base field; [AWS] Lecture 2, §2.6, Lem. 2.6.17 with
proof, p. 66; [Bhatt] Ch. 9, Prop. 9.2.7(1)–(2) with proof, pp. 101–103, the field case with
consequence (ii)). Sch12 Corollary 6.7(i) and Bhatt Proposition 9.2.7(1) are the case of a
perfectoid affinoid algebra over a perfectoid field. For `R = ℚ_p^cycl⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩` and `f = T + ϖ`,
`g = T + ϖ♭` satisfies `f ≡ g♯ mod ϖR°`, the estimate for `c = 0`; for `c ≥ 1` the lemma gives `g`
with `{|f| ≤ |ϖ^c|} = {|g♯| ≤ |ϖ^c|}` ([Sch12] Rem. 6.6), a rational subset of `X` that is a
preimage from `X♭`; hence every rational subset of `X` is the preimage of a rational subset of
`X♭`, the step consumed by *tilting-homeomorphism-and-rational-subsets*. *Needs:*
*tilting-map-of-spectra*; *approximation-on-perfectoid-polydisc*; layer P1 (P1.6); Tau Ceti
`TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.spa`, `TauCeti.Huber.powerBoundedSubring`.

The quantitative target is the sharp approximation on the polydisc; its two conclusions are
the error estimate and equality of the truncated valuations. The powers are
`ϖ.root m ^ a` and `ϖ.root n ^ (p^n-b)`, so no extra roots in a valuation group are implicit.
**Checks.** `sharp_approximation_zero` uses `f = g = 0`; `sharp_approximation_exact` computes the
error of an exact sharp as zero. The existing rational-set Check also tests the empty denominator.
