### P2.3 rational localisation of perfectoid affinoids

Rational localisation: the rational localisations of a perfectoid Tate pair are perfectoid, their
tilts are the rational localisations of the tilt, they form a functor on rational subsets with
tilting as a natural isomorphism, completed residue fields are perfectoid, and the structure
presheaf is a sheaf with `O⁺` almost Čech-acyclic.

**Rational localisations of a perfectoid Tate pair are perfectoid, with tilt the rational
localisation of the tilt.** (*rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids*) Let `(R, R⁺)` be a
perfectoid Tate pair (ECD Definition 3.1; characteristic `0`, `p` or mixed; no perfectoid base
field, which is the form P3.17a uses for sousperfectoid rings),
`X = Spa(R, R⁺)`, `X♭ = Spa(R♭, R♭⁺)` and `τ_R : X ≅ X♭` the tilting homeomorphism. For every
rational subset `U ⊆ X`, the rational localisation `(O_X(U), O_X⁺(U))` of AdicSpaces layer 3.1
(`O_X(U) = R⟨T/s⟩` for any presentation `U = U(T/s)`, `O_X⁺(U)` the closure in the completion of the image of the integral closure
of `R⁺[T/s]` in `R[1/s]`; Tau Ceti `PairOfDefinition.completionLocObj`, `completedPlusSubring`; the presheaf
on rational subsets is presentation independent, the comparison isomorphisms between presentations
being Tau Ceti's) is a perfectoid Tate pair, and there is a unique isomorphism of perfectoid Tate
pairs `(O_X(U), O_X⁺(U))♭ ≅ (O_{X♭}(τ_R U), O_{X♭}⁺(τ_R U))` compatible with the structure maps
from `(R♭, R♭⁺)` and with `♯`; equivalently `(O_X(U), O_X⁺(U))` is the untilt over `(R, R⁺)` of
the rational localisation of the tilt at `τ_R(U)`. For a presentation
`U = U(f₁♯, …, f_n♯ / g♯)` with `f_i, g ∈ R♭⁺` and `f_n = (ϖ♭)^N` (which exists for every `U`),
`O_X⁺(U)ᵃ = (R⁺⟨(f♯/g♯)^{1/p^∞}⟩)ᵃ`. The construction `U ↦ (O_X(U), O_X⁺(U))` is the rational
localisation in the category of perfectoid Tate pairs: every morphism `(R, R⁺) → (S, S⁺)` to a
perfectoid Tate pair whose `Spa` lands in `U` factors uniquely through it (AdicSpaces' universal
property over all complete Hausdorff Huber pairs, restricted to perfectoid targets; the tilt of the
localisation is identified only after perfectoidness is known, through the explicit model, since
the universal property quantifies over all Huber pairs, [AWS] Lecture 2, §2.5, Thm 2.5.3(b) and
proof, p. 60); and tilting gives an equivalence between the rational localisations of `(R, R⁺)`
and those of `(R♭, R♭⁺)`. In characteristic `p` the tilt identification is the identity ([ECD] §3,
Thm 3.18, p. 18, perfectoidness and the tilt identification; [HK] §3, Prop. 3.8 with proof, p. 8;
[KL16] §3.3, Thm 3.3.18, proof of case (i), p. 64, an independent Witt-vector proof;
[Berkeley] Lecture 6, Thm 6.2.6, p. 45; [Sch12] §6, Cor. 6.8 with proof, p. 35, the field-case
universal property). Sch12 Corollary 6.8, Berkeley Theorem 6.2.6, Hansen–Kedlaya Proposition 3.8
and Kedlaya–Liu II Theorem 3.3.18(i) are special cases or restatements. In `Perfectoid`, define
`rationalLocalization` as the perfectoid Tate pair `(O_X(U), O_X⁺(U))` of a rational subset `U`
of `Spa(R, R⁺)`, bundled with its structure morphism of Huber pairs from `(R, R⁺)`; prove
`rationalLocalization.isPerfectoidTateRing_affinoid` (instance: `O_X(U)` is a perfectoid Tate ring),
`rationalLocalization.tiltEquiv_affinoid` (the isomorphism `(O_X(U), O_X⁺(U))♭ ≅ (O_{X♭}(τ U), O_{X♭}⁺(τ U))`),
`rationalLocalization.tiltEquiv_affinoid_spec` (`tiltEquiv` composed with the tilt of
`R → O_X(U)` is `R♭ → O_{X♭}(τ U)`). Use Tau Ceti's supplied continuous extension,
structure-map identity and uniqueness for the rational universal property.
The additional theorem `rationalLocalization.lift_mem_plus` has Tate source and complete
Hausdorff Tate target pairs `P`, `Q`, a presentation `d`, and a pair morphism `f : P → Q`.
Assume `f(d.den)` is a unit and every `f(t) / f(d.den)`, for `t ∈ d.num`, belongs to `Q.plus`.
For any continuous ring homomorphism `g : RationalLoc d →+* S` whose composite with
`PairOfDefinition.toCompletionLoc` is `f.toRingHom`, it states
`g((RationalLoc.pair d P).plus) ⊆ Q.plus`. Together with the supplier, this gives the unique
factorization as a morphism of pairs; no perfectoid hypothesis is needed for this integral
assertion ([Wedhorn] §8.1, p. 74, the universal property immediately before Lemma 8.1;
[Sch12] Proposition 2.14, p. 9, over a nonarchimedean field).
Prove `rationalLocalization.image_spaTilt`
(`τ(U(f♯/g♯)) = U(f/g)` for `f_i, g ∈ R♭⁺`, `f_n = (ϖ♭)^N`, and every rational `U` has such a
presentation), `rootIntegralModel_almost`
(`O_X⁺(U)ᵃ ≅ (R⁺⟨(f♯/g♯)^{1/p^∞}⟩)ᵃ` as `R⁺ᵃ`-algebras), `rationalOrderIso`
(tilting is an equivalence from the rational localisations of `(R, R⁺)` to those of `(R♭, R♭⁺)`,
`U ↦ τ U`), `rationalLocalization.isUniform` (instance: `O_X(U)°` is bounded) and
`rationalLocalization.tiltEquiv_of_charP_affinoid` (simp: `tiltEquiv` is the identity when `pR = 0`).
*Needs:* *tilting-homeomorphism-and-rational-subsets*; *tilting-map-of-spectra*;
*almost-integral-model-of-untilted-rational-localization*; layer P1 (P1.1); Tau Ceti
`TauCeti.Huber.PairOfDefinition.completionLocObj`,
`TauCeti.Huber.PairOfDefinition.completedPlusSubring`,
`TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.existsUnique_continuous_ringHom_of_forall_comap_mem_rationalSubset`,
`TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.presentationRingEquivOfEq_coe_comp_toCompletionLoc`,
`TauCeti.Huber.Pair`.

**Checks.**

- `rationalLocalization_test_perfectoidDisc` (computation) — for `R = ℚ_p^cycl⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩` and
  `U = {|T| ≤ |ϖ|}`, `rationalLocalization R⁺ U ≅ ℚ_p^cycl⟨(T/ϖ)^{1/p^∞}⟩` (`≅ R` via `T ↦ ϖT`) and
  `tiltEquiv` identifies its tilt with `ℚ_p^cycl♭⟨(T/ϖ♭)^{1/p^∞}⟩ = O_{X♭}({|T| ≤ |ϖ♭|})`.
- `rationalLocalization_test_noBaseField` (compatibility) — for `R` of ECD Example 3.4(iv)
  (`R⁺ = R°`) and `U = U(T, p / p) = {|T| ≤ |p|}`: on `X` one has `|p| ≤ |T|` (`p/T ∈ R°`), so
  `|p| = |T| ≠ 0` on `U`; `isPerfectoidTateRing` holds for `O_X(U)` and `p` is a unit there, a
  rational localisation of a ring in which `p` is not invertible; the statement must not require an
  algebra structure over a perfectoid field. (For the product
  `ℂ_p × ℂ_p♭` of layer P1, in which `p = (p, 0)` is a nonzero nonunit, with `U = U({ϖ, p}/p)` for
  the pseudouniformiser `ϖ = (p, t)`, `t` a pseudouniformiser of `ℂ_p♭` (so that `U` is the `ℂ_p`
  factor, on which `p` is a unit; a `ϖ` with `ϖ^p | p` would make `U` empty).
- `rationalLocalization_test_charP` (degenerate) — if `pR = 0` then `tiltEquiv` is the identity of
  `(O_X(U), O_X⁺(U))` and the almost integral model is `R⁺⟨(f/g)^{1/p^∞}⟩` itself.
- `naiveModel_smaller_root_nonmember` (non-example) — the naive model `R°⟨f♯/g♯⟩` without
  `p`-power roots is not almost equal to `O_X(U)°`: for `R = ℚ_p^cycl⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩` and
  `U = {|T| ≤ |ϖ|}`, `O_X(U)° = K°⟨(T/ϖ)^{1/p^∞}⟩` contains `(T/ϖ)^{1/p}`, while
  `R°⟨T/ϖ⟩ = {Σ_{q ∈ ℤ[1/p]_{≥0}} c_qT^q : |c_q| ≤ |ϖ|^{-⌊q⌋}, |c_q| |ϖ|^{⌊q⌋} → 0}` (the weighted coefficients tend to zero outside finite sets) contains `c·T^{1/p}` only
  for `|c| ≤ 1`; so `ϖ^{1/p²}(T/ϖ)^{1/p} = ϖ^{1/p² − 1/p}T^{1/p} ∉ R°⟨T/ϖ⟩` (whereas
  `ϖ^{1/p}(T/ϖ)^{1/p} = T^{1/p} ∈ R° ⊆ R°⟨T/ϖ⟩`, so the exponent `1/p` is not a witness), and for
  each `k ≥ 1` the element `(T/ϖ)^{1 − 1/p^n}` with `1 − 1/p^n > 1/p^k` is not carried into `R°⟨T/ϖ⟩`
  by `ϖ^{1/p^k}`.
- `rationalLoc_test_whole` (characterisation) — for `U = X = U({1}/1)`,
  `rationalLocalization` is `(R, R⁺)` itself (`O_X(X) ≅ R`) and `tiltEquiv` is the identity of
  `(R♭, R♭⁺)`.

**Untilted rational localisations: explicit almost integral model, perfectoidness and tilt.**
(*almost-integral-model-of-untilted-rational-localization*) Let `(R, R⁺)` be a perfectoid Tate pair
with tilt `(R♭, R♭⁺)` and `ϖ = (ϖ♭)♯`, `ϖ^p | p` in `R°`; parts (i), (ii), and (iv)
require no base field. Let `f₁, …, f_n, g ∈ R♭⁺`
with `f_n = (ϖ♭)^N`, `U = U(f₁, …, f_n / g) ⊆ X♭` and `U♯ := τ_R⁻¹(U) = U(f₁♯, …, f_n♯ / g♯) ⊆ X`
(the normalisation makes `f₁♯, …, f_n♯` generate the unit ideal, (b) of *tilting-map-of-spectra*).
Prove: (i) the `ϖ`-adic completion `A` of the subring
`R⁺[(f_i^{1/p^m})♯/(g^{1/p^m})♯ : i ≤ n, m ≥ 0]` of `R[1/g♯]` is `ϖ`-torsion free and Frobenius
induces an almost isomorphism `A/ϖ^{1/p} → A/ϖ`, i.e. `A^a` is a perfectoid `R⁺ᵃ`-algebra; (ii)
`O_X(U♯) = A[1/ϖ]` is a perfectoid Tate ring and `A ⊆ O_X⁺(U♯) ⊆ O_X(U♯)°` with almost zero
quotients; (iii) if `(R, R⁺)` is an algebra over a perfectoid field `K`, with continuous
scalar map carrying `K°` into `R⁺` and with `ϖ` and all its roots coming from `K`, the map
`R⁺[T₁^{1/p^∞}, …, T_n^{1/p^∞}] → A`,
`T_i^{1/p^m} ↦ (f_i^{1/p^m})♯/(g^{1/p^m})♯`, is surjective modulo `ϖ` with kernel modulo `ϖ`
almost equal to the image of the ideal generated by `(g^{1/p^m})♯ T_i^{1/p^m} − (f_i^{1/p^m})♯`;
(iv) `(O_X(U♯), O_X⁺(U♯))` is the untilt over `(R, R⁺)` of `(O_{X♭}(U), O_{X♭}⁺(U))`, which
exists by the tilting equivalence over the perfectoid base `R` (ECD Theorem 3.13; layer P1,
P1.27): there is a unique isomorphism of perfectoid Tate pairs
`(O_X(U♯), O_X⁺(U♯))♭ ≅ (O_{X♭}(U), O_{X♭}⁺(U))` compatible with the structure maps from
`(R♭, R♭⁺)` and with `♯` ([Sch12] §6, Lem. 6.4 (statement), p. 31, and proof of Lem. 6.4(i),
(iii) for general `K`, pp. 32–33, the comparison through the untilt `S`; [Bhatt] Ch. 9, Lem. 9.2.5
with proof, pp. 99–101, written with `R⁺` in place of `R°` and with the universal-property proof
of (iv); [AWS] Lecture 2, §2.8, Lem. 2.8.8, p. 72, the tilt statement (iv) without a base field;
[ECD] §3, proof of Thms 3.12–3.13, p. 17). For a perfectoid Tate ring `R₀` and
`R = R₀⟨T₀^{1/p^∞}, …, T_n^{1/p^∞}⟩`, `g ∈ R♭⁺` homogeneous and `U_c = {|g| ≤ |ϖ♭|^c}`
(`c ∈ ℤ[1/p]_{≥0}`), the lemma gives `O_X(U_c♯)°ᵃ = R°⟨(g♯/ϖ^c)^{1/p^∞}⟩ᵃ`. Over a perfectoid
field `K` this is Sch12 Lemma 6.4(i)–(iii) and Bhatt Lemma 9.2.5; for `R = ℚ_p^cycl⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩`
and `U = {|T| ≤ |ϖ♭|}`, `O_X(U♯) = ℚ_p^cycl⟨(T/ϖ)^{1/p^∞}⟩` with tilt
`ℚ_p^cycl♭⟨(T/ϖ♭)^{1/p^∞}⟩`. The model is almost, not exactly, integral: for `R⁺ ≠ R°` (e.g.
`R⁺ = K° + K°°⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩`) and `U = X`, `A = R⁺` while `O_X(X)° = R°`. *Needs:*
*tilting-map-of-spectra*; layer P1 (P1.6, P1.27); Tau Ceti
`TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.existsUnique_continuous_ringHom_of_forall_comap_mem_rationalSubset`,
`TauCeti.Huber.PairOfDefinition.completionLocObj`,
`TauCeti.Huber.PairOfDefinition.completedPlusSubring`.

On the field disc put `S = T/ϖ`. `Perfectoid.discScale` sends `T^(1/p^n)` to
`ϖ^(1/p^n) S^(1/p^n)` and fixes the base field. `naiveDiscModel` is the closed subring generated
by the image of the original unit ball and `S`; `rootedDiscModel` also adjoins every
`S^(1/p^n)`. Closure is in the normalized disc's Tate topology. `rootedDiscModel_eq` identifies
the root-adjoined model with the unit ball, and `naiveDiscModel_not_almost` quantifies over
all `k ≥ 1`, with the monomials `ϖ^(1/p^k) S^(1-p^(-n))` witnessing failure of containment.

**Checks for the actual integral models.**
- `discScale_constants` fixes each scalar; `discScale_two_roots` computes the images of `T`
  and `T^(1/p)`; `discScale_not_surjective_unit_ball` detects the smaller radius.
- `naiveModel_fractional_member` puts `ϖ^(1/p)S^(1/p)` in the naive model;
  `naiveModel_smaller_root_nonmember` excludes `ϖ^(1/p²)S^(1/p)`;
  `naiveModel_integral_generator` includes `S` but excludes `S^(1/p)`.
- `rootedModel_fractional_generator` includes `S^(1/p)`;
  `rootedModel_unbounded_constant` excludes a scalar of norm greater than one;
  `rootedModel_two_term_sum` includes `S + S^(1/p)`.
These statements concern membership in the constructed subrings, rather than inequalities
between exponents alone.

The general model `rawRootModel` is the subring of the actual rational localization
generated by the base plus ring and all `fᵢ,m/gₘ`. Here `fᵢ,m+1^p = fᵢ,m`,
`gₘ₊₁^p = gₘ`, the zero-level numerators generate the unit ideal, and their rational subset
is the specified `U`. `rootIntegralModel` is its closure. `rootIntegralModel_completion`
identifies this closure with the separated adic completion, fixing the algebraic model;
`rootIntegralModel_invert` recovers the rational ring after inversion and states parameter
torsion-freeness. `rootIntegralModel_almost` gives root-scaled containment, and
`rootIntegralModel_frobenius` states the almost kernel and cokernel conditions modulo the
two parameters. `rootModelEval` evaluates a polynomial in variables `(i,m)` at these ratios;
`rootModelRelations` includes both `Xᵢ,m+1^p-Xᵢ,m` and `gₘXᵢ,m-fᵢ,m`.
`rootIntegralModel_presentation` specifies its almost kernel modulo the parameter for an
algebra over a complete nontrivially normed ultrametric field `K` with
`IsPerfectoidField p K`. Its scalar map is continuous and carries `K°` into `R⁺`; a
`PseudoUniformizerRoots p K` named `ϖK` satisfies
`algebraMap K R (ϖK.root k) = ϖ.root k` for every `k`.
`rawRootModel_kernel_charP` states the algebraic kernel assertion before completion under
the same scalar hypotheses and `CharP K p`, with `pR = 0`.
`rootIntegralModel_charP` includes perfectness of the chosen plus ring, including the zero
ring. The presentation is [Sch12] Lemma 6.4(i), proof on pp. 31–33: the algebraic
characteristic-`p` kernel is treated on p. 31, and the kernel modulo the parameter in
general characteristic on pp. 32–33. Its `R°` formulation gives the `R⁺` formulation
by the almost equality of `R⁺` and `R°` over `K°`. [ECD] Theorem 3.18, p. 18,
supplies the rational-localization and tilt assertions without a base field.

**Checks for the general root model.** The empty presentation gives the zero localization;
numerator and denominator one recover the base plus ring; the inverse parameter is excluded in a
nonzero localization. Evaluation fixes base coefficients, computes the sum of two consecutive root
ratios, and gives zero on the empty localization. For the relation ideal: the unit presentation
contains `X₀,₀-1`, the denominator `0` (the presentation `1/0`) gives the unit ideal, and `1` is
excluded in the nonzero unit presentation.

Lean: the theorem `isPerfectoidTateRing_rationalLocalization` (the completed rational localisation
`R⟨T/s⟩` of Tau Ceti, for an admissible presentation, is a perfectoid Tate ring: the first clause).
The bundled instance form `rationalLocalization.isPerfectoidTateRing_affinoid`, the tilt
identification and the remaining clauses are specified in this README only.

### P2.4 the presheaf of perfectoid pairs on rational subsets

**The presheaf of perfectoid pairs on rational subsets: restriction maps, plus rings, and tilting
as a natural isomorphism.** (*perfectoid-pair-rational-restriction*) Let `(R, R⁺)` be a perfectoid
Tate pair, `ϖ = (ϖ♭)♯`, `X = Spa(R, R⁺)`, `τ = τ_R`. On the poset `Rat(X)` of rational subsets of
`X`, the assignment `U ↦ (O_X(U), O_X⁺(U))` with AdicSpaces' restriction maps `ρ_{U,V}` (`V ⊆ U`;
identity and composition laws from AdicSpaces layer 3.1, Tau Ceti
`PairOfDefinition.restrictionRingHomOfSubset` for a numerator enlargement and presentation changes
for general inclusions) is a functor `Rat(X)^op → {perfectoid Tate pairs}`
(see *rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids*), with: (a) transitivity: for `V ⊆ U` rational,
`V` is rational in `U ≅ Spa(O_X(U), O_X⁺(U))` and `ρ_{U,V}` is the rational localisation of
`(O_X(U), O_X⁺(U))` at `V` — the functor on `Rat(X)^op` with its transitivity and restriction
maps is library for any Huber pair (Tau Ceti `pairHomOfRationalSubsetSubset`,
`spaCompletedLocalizationHomeomorph_spaComap_pairHomOfRationalSubsetSubset`,
`presentationLimitRationalIso`, `isIso_restrictionHom_of_rationalSubset_eq`,
`completedPlusSubring_eq_completionPlus`, `mem_completedPlusSubring_iff_forall_mem_rationalSubset_vle_one`),
and what is proved here is the perfectoidness of its values and the naturality of tilting; (b) plus rings: `O_X⁺(U) = {f ∈ O_X(U) : |f(x)| ≤ 1 for all x ∈ U}`,
`O_X(U)°° ⊆ O_X⁺(U) ⊆ O_X(U)°`, and `O_X(U)°/O_X⁺(U)` is almost zero (for the ideal of
topologically nilpotent elements of `R⁺`; its extension to `O_X⁺(U)` is the ideal of
topologically nilpotent elements there), so
`O_X⁺(U)ᵃ = O_X(U)°ᵃ`; (c) tilting is a natural isomorphism: the isomorphisms `rationalTiltIso` satisfy
`tiltEquiv_V ∘ (ρ_{U,V})♭ = ρ_{τU,τV} ∘ tiltEquiv_U`, i.e. `U ↦ (O_X(U), O_X⁺(U))♭` is isomorphic
to `U ↦ (O_{X♭}(τU), O_{X♭}⁺(τU))`; (d) consequently the ring isomorphisms
`O_{X♭}⁺(τU)/ϖ♭ ≅ O_X⁺(U)/ϖ` induced by `♯` are natural in `U` and `R♭⁺/ϖ♭ ≅ R⁺/ϖ`-semilinear;
(e) the homeomorphisms `Spa(O_X(U), O_X⁺(U)) ≅ U` and `Spa(O_{X♭}(τU), O_{X♭}⁺(τU)) ≅ τU`
(AdicSpaces layer 3.1) intertwine `τ_{O_X(U)}` and `τ|_U` ([ECD] §3, Ex. 3.22(ii), p. 19, clause
(b) for each `O_X(U)`; [ECD] §3, Lem. 3.11, p. 17, clause (d) for `U = X`; [Sch12] §6, remark after
Def. 6.1, p. 30, the sandwich `O°° ⊆ O⁺ ⊆ O°`; [Bhatt] Ch. 9, proof of Lem. 9.2.5(4), p. 100,
uniqueness of maps out of rational localisations, used for naturality in (c)). In
`PerfectoidSpace`, define `rationalPairFunctor` as the functor from rational subsets of
`Spa(R, R⁺)` ordered by `⊇` to perfectoid Tate pairs; prove `CategoryTheory.Functor.map_comp`
(`ρ_{V,W} ∘ ρ_{U,V} = ρ_{U,W}`, `ρ_{U,U} = id`), `rationalPairFunctor.isRationalLocalization_map`
(transitivity (a)), `rationalPairFunctor.mem_plus_iff` (`f ∈ O_X⁺(U) ↔ ∀ x ∈ U, |f(x)| ≤ 1`),
`rationalPairFunctor.isAlmostZero_powerBounded_quot_plus` (`O_X(U)°/O_X⁺(U)` almost zero),
`rationalTiltIso` (the natural isomorphism (c)), `tilt.sharpQuotEquiv`
(the ring isomorphisms (d), natural by `tilt.mapQuot_comm`) and `rationalPairFunctor.spaTilt_comm` (under
`Spa(O_X(U), O_X⁺(U)) ≅ U` and its tilt, `spaTilt` of `O_X(U)` is the restriction of `spaTilt` of
`R`). *Needs:* *rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids*; *tilting-map-of-spectra*;
*tilting-homeomorphism-and-rational-subsets*; layer P1; Tau Ceti
`TauCeti.Huber.PairOfDefinition.restrictionRingHomOfSubset`,
`TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.mem_iff_forall_vle_one`, `TauCeti.Huber.IsRingOfIntegralElements`,
`TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.existsUnique_continuous_ringHom_of_forall_comap_mem_rationalSubset`.

For a perfectoid pair `A` with `(p : A) = 0`,
`tilt.exists_sharpEquiv_of_prime_eq_zero` supplies a ring equivalence `A♭ ≃ A`
given by sharp, carrying `A♭⁺` onto `A⁺` and identifying the small-quotient comparison
with reduction of sharp. This includes the zero pair: its tilt, plus ring and
quotients are zero. For `A = O_X(U)`, the rational structure map carries `pR = 0`
to `pA = 0`, even when `U` is empty. Exact `CharP A p` is used only when `A` is
nonzero ([ECD] §3, Prop. 3.5, p. 15; Lem. 3.10, p. 16; Lem. 3.11, p. 17;
Thm. 3.18, p. 18).

**Checks.**

- `rationalPairFunctor_test_restriction_disc` (computation) — for `R = ℚ_p^cycl⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩`,
  `V = {|T| ≤ |ϖ|²} ⊆ U = {|T| ≤ |ϖ|}`, the restriction
  `ℚ_p^cycl⟨(T/ϖ)^{1/p^∞}⟩ → ℚ_p^cycl⟨(T/ϖ²)^{1/p^∞}⟩` sends `(T/ϖ)^{1/p^m}` to
  `ϖ^{1/p^m}(T/ϖ²)^{1/p^m}`, and `tiltIso` transports it to the same formula over `ℚ_p^cycl♭` with
  `ϖ♭`.
- `rationalPairFunctor_test_plusModEquiv_whole` (compatibility) — for `U = X`, `plusModEquiv` is
  the ring isomorphism `R♭⁺/ϖ♭ ≅ R⁺/ϖ` induced by `♯` (ECD Lemma 3.11), and naturality for `V ⊆ X`
  is the commutation with `R⁺/ϖ → O_X⁺(V)/ϖ`.
- `rationalPairFunctor_test_plus_ne_powerBounded` (non-example) — for `K = ℚ_p^cycl`,
  `R = K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩` and `R⁺ = K° + K°°⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩` (open, integrally closed), `T ∈ R° \ R⁺` while
  `ϖ^{1/p^n}T ∈ R⁺` for all `n`; a plus presheaf defined by `O_X(U)°` would violate `mem_plus_iff`
  at the points where `|T| > 1`.
- `rationalPairFunctor_test_charP` (degenerate) — if `pR = 0`, sharp identifies
  the tilted rational section pair with the original pair and `plusModEquiv`
  becomes reduction to `O_X⁺(U)/ϖ`, including for the empty rational open.
- `rationalPairFunctor_charP_empty` (non-example) — for `U = ∅`, `pA = 0`
  and the tilt equivalence sends every element to zero, while `CharP A p` is false.
  This applies in particular over the completed perfection of `𝔽_p((t))`
  ([ECD] §3, Ex. 3.4(ii), p. 15).

`Perfectoid.RationalOpen p R` is a rational subset of the supplied valuation spectrum.
`rationalPair`, `rationalMap` and `rationalPair_universal` give its completed perfectoid pair
and the factorization property for maps whose spectra land in that subset.
`rationalPair_presentation` fixes the topology, plus ring and base map by comparison with
`PairOfDefinition`'s completed presentation. `rationalRes` is the unique map commuting with
the two base maps. `tiltRationalOpen` takes the image under `spaTilt`;
`rationalTiltIso_base` and `rationalTiltIso_restriction` fix the comparison on base elements
and on nested rational subsets.

**Checks for rational pairs and restrictions.** `rational_subset_whole` makes the base map
an isomorphism; `rational_subset_empty` gives the zero ring; `rational_subset_proper` rules
out an isomorphism for a proper subset. `rational_restriction_identity`,
`rational_restriction_composition` and `rational_restriction_empty` compute identity,
composition and the zero-target map. `restriction_disc_two_radii` computes the fractional
coordinate at radii `ϖ` and `ϖ²` through the normalized disc map.
`rational_tilt_empty`, `rational_tilt_whole` and `rational_tilt_injective` test the subset
transport. `rational_tilt_zero_one`, `rational_tilt_empty_ring` and
`rational_tilt_base_coordinate` test the pair comparison on constants, the empty ring and
an arbitrary base coordinate.

`rationalOrderIso` is the order equivalence of rational subsets, with forward map
`tiltRationalOpen`; `rationalPairFunctor` uses the actual restriction morphisms,
as specified by `rationalPairFunctor_map`. The identity on base coordinates is
`rationalRes_base` evaluated at each element of `R`.
**Checks.** `rational_order_empty`, `rational_order_whole` and `rational_order_disjoint`
test the empty subset, the whole spectrum and preservation of disjointness.

### P2.5 completed residue fields

**Completed residue fields of perfectoid affinoids are perfectoid and tilt to those of the tilt.**
(*completed-residue-fields*) Let `(R, R⁺)` be a perfectoid Tate pair (no base field),
`X = Spa(R, R⁺)`, `x ∈ X`, and `(k(x)^, k(x)^⁺)` the completed residue affinoid field of `x` (the
completion of the residue field of the stalk `O_{X,x}` for the topology of `v_x`, with the
completion of the valuation ring of `v_x`; the uncompleted residue field with its valuation and
`Valued` structure and the stalk material are library, Tau Ceti
`TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.residueFieldValuation`, `valued_algebraMap_residueFieldValuation`,
`continuous_algebraMap_residueFieldValuation`,
`isLocalRing_stalk_presentationLimitPresheafInCommRingCat`, `supp_presentationLimitStalkValuation`,
`presentationLimitStalkResidueValuation`, and AdicSpaces layer 3.3 supplies the completed residue
affinoid field; the completion and the perfectoidness are what this target adds; `k(x)^` is a complete nonarchimedean field whose
topology is that of the rank-one generisation of `x`, `x` being analytic because `R` is Tate), with
its canonical morphism `(R, R⁺) → (k(x)^, k(x)^⁺)`. Then `k(x)^` is a perfectoid field and
`(k(x)^, k(x)^⁺)` is a perfectoid Tate pair. Its tilt is canonically `(k(x♭)^, k(x♭)^⁺)`,
compatibly with the canonical morphisms from `(R, R⁺)` and `(R♭, R♭⁺)` and with `♯`; in particular
the value groups `Γ_x` and `Γ_{x♭}` coincide and `x` has rank one iff `x♭` has. Explicitly,
`k(x)^⁺` is the `ϖ`-adic completion of the image in `k(x)` of `colim_{U ∋ x} O_X⁺(U)` over the
rational neighbourhoods of `x` (an element `h` of the stalk with `|h(x)| ≤ 1` lies in `O_X⁺` of the
rational neighbourhood `{|h| ≤ 1}`) ([Sch12] §6, Cor. 6.7(ii) with proof and end of proof, p. 35,
the field case, with the characteristic-`0` case deduced after the homeomorphism; [AWS] Lecture 2,
§2.5, Cor. 2.5.7 with proof, pp. 60–61, the general statement and its last step; [KL16] §3.3,
Thm 3.3.18, class (ii), p. 64, the dense-image criterion used for `k(x)^` and its tilt). For
`R = ℚ_p^cycl⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩`: at the Gauss point `k(x)^` is the completion of `ℚ_p^cycl(T^{1/p^∞})`
for the Gauss norm, whose tilt is the analogous completion of `ℚ_p^cycl♭(T^{1/p^∞})`; at the
evaluation point given by a compatible system `a_n ∈ ℤ_p^cycl`,
`a_{n+1}^p = a_n`, `T^{1/p^n} ↦ a_n`, one has `k(x)^ = ℚ_p^cycl`.
A value `a_0` alone does not specify such a point over `ℚ_p^cycl`. The uncompleted residue field is not
perfectoid in general: `ℚ_p^cycl(T^{1/p^∞})` is not complete. *Needs:*
*rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids*; *perfectoid-pair-rational-restriction*;
*tilting-homeomorphism-and-rational-subsets*; *tilting-map-of-spectra*; layer P1 (P1.15, P1.27);
AdicSpaces layer 3.3; Tau Ceti `TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.residueFieldValuation`,
`TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.presentationLimitStalkResidueValuation`.

`Perfectoid.CompletedResidue` is `Completion (WithVal (residueFieldValuation x))`.
`residueMap` composes the supplier's residue map with the completion map. `residuePlus` is
the closure of the original valuation ring's image; it retains higher-rank integral data.
`residueTiltEquiv_spec` fixes both topologies, the transported plus subring, and the map
from the base tilt.

**Checks for residue fields.** `residue_zero_one` computes the two constants;
`residue_support` identifies the kernel with the point's support;
`residue_field_recovery` recovers a complete base field. `residue_integral_image` and
`residue_integral_two_terms` include integral base elements and their sums, while
`residue_inverse_parameter_nonmember` excludes `ϖ⁻¹`.
`residue_tilt_zero_one`, `residue_tilt_injective` and `residue_tilt_inverse_parameter`
test constants, the zero fibre and the chosen tilted parameter. The last Check uses
`ϖ♭` itself in the base-map equation.

### P2.6 stable uniformity and sheafiness

**Perfectoid Tate pairs are stably uniform and sheafy, with Čech-acyclic structure sheaf.**
(*perfectoid-stably-uniform-and-sheafy*) Let `(R, R⁺)` be a perfectoid Tate pair (ECD
Definition 3.1; no base field), `X = Spa(R, R⁺)`. Then (a) `(R, R⁺)` is stably uniform: `O_X(U)` is
uniform for every rational `U ⊆ X` ([HK] Def. 3.13; the predicate is Tau Ceti
`TauCeti.Huber.IsStablyUniform`, with `TauCeti.Huber.isStablyUniform_iff_forall_isUniform_presentationLimit` and
`PairOfDefinition.isStablyUniform_completion_locTopology`; the perfectoid instance is what is
proved here); (b) `(R, R⁺)` is sheafy: the structure presheaf `O_X` (AdicSpaces layers 3.3–3.5,
presentation independent) is a sheaf of complete topological rings on `X` (Tau Ceti
`Huber.IsSheafyRing`, `IsSheafyForEveryPresentation`), and `O_X⁺` is a
sheaf; the same holds for `(O_X(U), O_X⁺(U))` for every rational `U` — the implication "stably
uniform implies sheafy" is the Buzzard–Verberkmoes theorem, AdicSpaces layer 4.2, a target of that
roadmap which this one applies (Tau Ceti has the two halves for the Laurent cover,
`injective_presentationLimitMap_inf_laurentCoverOpen_of_isStablyUniform` and
`exists_presentationLimitMap_eq_of_inf_laurentCoverOpen_of_isStablyUniform`, and sheafiness for
strongly noetherian rings, `TauCeti.Huber.isSheafyRing_of_isStronglyNoetherian`, which does not apply to
perfectoid rings); (c) for every rational `U ⊆ X` and every finite covering `𝔘` of `U` by rational
subsets the augmented Čech complex `0 → O_X(U) → ∏ O_X(U_i) → ∏ O_X(U_i ∩ U_j) → ⋯` is exact in
every degree, and `H^i(U, O_X) = 0` for `i > 0`, `H⁰(U, O_X) = O_X(U)` (sheaf cohomology of the
underlying sheaf of abelian groups, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Sheaf.H`) — this is AdicSpacesPartIII
R3.1 (*sheafy-cech-acyclicity*, for every sheafy complete Tate pair), applied to the pair
made sheafy by (b); (d) (a)–(c) depend on `R` only, not on the choice of `R⁺` ([KL15] §3.6,
Thm 3.6.15 with proof, p. 94, perfectoid `ℚ_p`-algebras; [KL16] §3.3, Cor. 3.3.19, p. 65, the
general case via Buzzard–Verberkmoes; [Berkeley] Lecture 6, Thm 6.1.10 and the following paragraph,
p. 43, and remark after Thm 6.2.6, p. 45, the characteristic-`p` case of (a); [HK] §3, Cor. 3.15 with
proof, p. 9). Kedlaya–Liu I Theorem 3.6.15, Kedlaya–Liu II Corollary 3.3.19, Berkeley
Theorems 6.1.10/7.1.1, Hansen–Kedlaya Corollary 3.15 and Kedlaya AWS Corollary 2.5.4 are this
theorem. In characteristic `p` only perfectness is used: `𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^∧⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩` is stably
uniform because each rational localisation is perfect and complete (ECD Proposition 3.5). The uniform
non-sheafy Huber rings of Buzzard–Verberkmoes and Mihara are not perfectoid, and perfectoid rings
are never noetherian unless finite products of perfectoid fields ([AWS] Cor. 2.9.3), so Huber's
strongly noetherian sheafiness theorem does not prove the general perfectoid statement;
it does apply to perfectoid fields and their finite products. *Needs:*
*rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids*; *rational-localization-in-characteristic-p*;
*perfectoid-pair-rational-restriction*; AdicSpaces 4.2 (Buzzard–Verberkmoes);
AdicSpacesPartIII R3.1 (*sheafy-cech-acyclicity*); Tau Ceti
`TauCeti.Huber.IsStablyUniform`, `TauCeti.Huber.IsSheafyRing`,
`TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.isSheaf_iff_isSheafFor_rationalCover`,
`TauCeti.Huber.powerBoundedSubring`; Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Sheaf.H`.

`Perfectoid.isStablyUniform` has conclusion
`TauCeti.Huber.IsStablyUniform R` for a complete Hausdorff perfectoid Tate ring at a prime
`p`; its characteristic-`p` case, under `CharP R p`, uses only perfectness.
`Perfectoid.PairCat.isStablyUniform` registers the instance for the ring of a bundled
perfectoid pair, whose type determines `p`.
`Perfectoid.isSheafyRing` concludes `TauCeti.Huber.IsSheafyRing R` under the same
perfectoid hypotheses, without a characteristic or plus-ring restriction
([KL16] Cor. 3.3.19, p. 65; [ECD] Thm 3.18, p. 18). Applying it to each
`rationalPair p R U` supplies sheafiness on rational localizations. The ordinary and Čech
acyclicity conclusions are applications of AdicSpacesPartIII R3.1
(*sheafy-cech-acyclicity*; [KL15] Thm 2.4.23, p. 46),
on Part II `AdicSpace.Chart`, using `c.affinoid.ring`, `c.affinoid.spa` and
the presheaf comparison below.

### P2.7 almost acyclicity of `O⁺` on rational coverings

**Almost exactness of the integral Čech complex of `O⁺` on rational coverings of a perfectoid
affinoid.** (*integral-almost-acyclicity*) Let `(R, R⁺)` be a perfectoid Tate pair (ECD
Definition 3.1; no base field), `X = Spa(R, R⁺)`. For every rational `U ⊆ X` and every finite
covering `𝔘 = (U₁, …, U_m)` of `U` by rational subsets (all finite intersections are then rational),
the augmented alternating Čech complex, with `(d⁰s)_{ij} = s_j|_{U_i∩U_j} − s_i|_{U_i∩U_j}` for `i < j`,
`C⁺(𝔘): 0 → O_X⁺(U) → ∏_i O_X⁺(U_i) → ∏_{i<j} O_X⁺(U_i ∩ U_j) → ⋯` is almost exact: each of its
cohomology modules is killed by every topologically nilpotent element of `R⁺` (equivalently by
`ϖ^{1/p^n}` for all `n`; the ideal is idempotent, layer P1). It is exact at its first two terms. The
same holds for the complex of the `O_X(V)°`, which is almost equal to `C⁺(𝔘)` termwise; in the
almost category `C⁺(𝔘)ᵃ` is exact. Consequently `H^i(U, O_X⁺)ᵃ = 0`, i.e. `H^i(U, O_X⁺)` is almost
zero, for every rational `U ⊆ X` and every `i > 0` (see *cech-to-sheaf-cohomology-on-rational-basis*)
([Berkeley] Lecture 7, proof of Thm 7.4.4, p. 53, bounded torsion plus the Frobenius step in
characteristic `p`; [Sch12] §6, proof of Prop. 6.14, p. 38, the tilting reduction of the general
case; [KL16] §3.3, Cor. 3.3.20(c), p. 65, and Rem. 3.3.11, p. 61, the same conclusion for Fontaine
perfectoid rings through almost optimal exactness). Over a perfectoid field this is Sch12
Proposition 6.14, proved there through `p`-finite algebras and Tate's acyclicity theorem
(see *p-finite-acyclicity-from-tate*), a route this layer keeps. For `R = ℚ_p^cycl⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩` and the
Laurent covering `{|T| ≤ |ϖ|}`, `{|ϖ| ≤ |T|}`, `C⁺` is exact: the Laurent decomposition of
`Σ_{k ∈ ℤ[1/p]} d_k (T/ϖ)^k` splits exactly. The conclusion is about `O⁺` up to almost zero
modules: after inverting `ϖ` it recovers the exactness of the `O`-Čech complex, but `C⁺` itself need
not be exact when `R⁺ ≠ R°`. *Needs:* *perfectoid-stably-uniform-and-sheafy*;
*integral-cech-cohomology-bounded-torsion*; *almost-exactness-from-reduction-mod-pseudouniformizer*;
*tilting-homeomorphism-and-rational-subsets*; *perfectoid-pair-rational-restriction*;
*rational-localization-in-characteristic-p*; layer P1; layer P0; Mathlib `frobeniusEquiv`,
`HomologicalComplex.ExactAt`, `CategoryTheory.Sheaf.H`.

**Almost exactness lifts from reduction modulo `ϖ` for torsion-free complete complexes.**
(*almost-exactness-from-reduction-mod-pseudouniformizer*) Let `V` be a ring, `m ⊆ V` an ideal with
`m² = m` (the basic setup of layer P0, P0.1; in the application `V = R⁺` and `m` its ideal of
topologically nilpotent elements, with `ϖ ∈ m`), `ϖ ∈ V`, and call a `V`-module almost zero if `m`
kills it (a Serre class closed under products and filtered colimits; [ECD] §3, after Ex. 3.22,
p. 19). Prove: (a) for a bounded complex `C` of `V`-modules whose terms are `ϖ`-torsion free and
`ϖ`-adically complete and separated (`C = lim_n C/ϖ^n C` with surjective transition maps), if every
cohomology module of `C/ϖC` is almost zero, so is every cohomology module of `C`; (b) conversely, if
the terms of `C` are `ϖ`-torsion free and every cohomology module of `C` is almost zero, so is every
cohomology module of `C/ϖC`; (c) for `α : M → N` `V`-linear with `M` `ϖ`-adically separated and
`N` `ϖ`-torsion free, if `α ⊗ V/ϖ` has almost zero kernel then `ker α` is almost zero; if moreover
`M` is `ϖ`-adically complete, `N` is `ϖ`-adically separated and `α ⊗ V/ϖ` has almost zero
cokernel, then `coker α` is almost zero ([Sch12] §6, proof of Prop. 6.14 (characteristic `0`), p. 38,
statement (a) in the almost category; [Bhatt] Ch. 9, footnote 1 in the proof of Lem. 9.2.5, p. 100,
the kernel statement of (c)). Completeness cannot be dropped: for `V = ℤ_p`, `m = V` (so that
"almost zero" means zero; `m = 0` would make every module almost zero and the example empty) and
`C = [ℚ_p → 0]`, `C/pC = 0` is exact while `H⁰(C) = ℚ_p ≠ 0`, `ℚ_p` being `p`-torsion free but not
`p`-adically separated. In
*integral-almost-acyclicity*, (b) is applied to the characteristic-`p` integral Čech complex and (a)
to the characteristic-`0` one after identifying both modulo `ϖ`. *Needs:* layer P0 (P0.1, P0.16);
Mathlib `CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.IsSerreClass`, `IsAdicComplete`,
`HomologicalComplex.ExactAt`.

**Integral Čech cohomology of a stably uniform sheafy Tate pair is killed by a bounded power of
`ϖ`.** (*integral-cech-cohomology-bounded-torsion*) Let `(A, A⁺)` be a complete Hausdorff Tate Huber
pair which is stably uniform (every `O_X(V)` uniform) and sheafy, with no perfectoid or noetherian
hypothesis, `ϖ ∈ A⁺` a pseudouniformiser, `X = Spa(A, A⁺)`, `U ⊆ X` rational and `𝔘 = (U₁, …, U_m)`
a finite covering of `U` by rational subsets. Let `C⁺` be the augmented alternating Čech complex
`0 → O_X⁺(U) → ∏_i O_X⁺(U_i) → ∏_{i<j} O_X⁺(U_i ∩ U_j) → ⋯ → O_X⁺(U₁ ∩ ⋯ ∩ U_m) → 0`. Prove that
`C⁺[1/ϖ]` is the augmented Čech complex of `O_X`, which is exact (AdicSpacesPartIII R3.1
(*sheafy-cech-acyclicity*),
Kedlaya–Liu I Theorem 2.4.23), that `C⁺` is exact at its first two terms, and that there is `N ≥ 0`
such that `ϖ^N` annihilates every cohomology module of `C⁺`; the same bound holds for the Čech
complex of `V ↦ O_X(V)°`, whose terms are also open and bounded ([Sch12] §6, proof of
Prop. 6.10(iii), p. 36, the open-mapping step and agreement of topologies as bounded torsion;
[Berkeley] Lecture 7, proof of Thm 7.4.4, p. 53, the same step for a perfectoid pair in
characteristic `p`). For `S = K⟨T⟩` over a complete nonarchimedean field `K` and the Laurent covering
`{|T| ≤ |ϖ|}`, `{|ϖ| ≤ |T|}` of the closed disc,
`C⁺ = [K°⟨T⟩ → K°⟨T/ϖ⟩ × K°⟨T, ϖ/T⟩ → K°⟨T/ϖ, ϖ/T⟩]` is exact (`N = 0`): every Laurent series
`Σ_{k∈ℤ} d_k(T/ϖ)^k` with `d_k → 0` in `K°` splits into its parts of non-negative and negative
degree. The lemma gives only a bounded power of `ϖ`; almost vanishing needs Frobenius
(see *integral-almost-acyclicity*). *Needs:* AdicSpacesPartIII R3.1 (*sheafy-cech-acyclicity*);
Tau Ceti
`TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing.isOpenMap`, `TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing.isStrictMap_of_isClosed_range`,
`TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.mem_iff_forall_vle_one`, `TauCeti.Huber.powerBoundedSubring`; Mathlib
`Topology.IsStrictMap`, `HomologicalComplex.ExactAt`.

The general Čech carrier is `Perfectoid.RationalTateSheaf`: an additive sheaf with the
base integral scalar action, additive coordinates in each supplied completed rational
localization, and restriction equations for the continuous localization maps. A Boolean
selects the chosen plus ring or the power-bounded ring in those coordinates.
`rationalTateSheaf` constructs both from stable uniformity.
`integral_cech_bounded_torsion` quantifies over every finite rational covering of a rational
open and supplies one exponent for both integral conventions and all positive degrees.
The positive-degree Čech complex is Mathlib’s. Exactness at the two augmentation terms
is the sheaf equalizer condition; localization at the parameter identifies its rational
terms. The bounded-torsion deduction uses strictness of the complete Tate-module
complex: each image is closed by rational acyclicity, the open-mapping theorem compares
its quotient topology with the kernel topology, and a finite alternating complex gives
a common exponent. The explicit printed calculation in Sch12 6.10(iii) is over a field;
the Tate-module strict-map input is `TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing.isStrictMap_of_isClosed_range`.

**Checks.** `general_integral_sections_empty` gives zero sections;
`general_integral_sections_whole` recovers the supplied plus ring;
`general_integral_parameter_torsionfree` rules out parameter torsion in sections on every open.
`bounded_torsion_single_open` gives zero positive cohomology, hence exponent zero,
for a one-member covering.

**From almost Čech acyclicity on the rational basis to almost vanishing of sheaf cohomology.**
(*cech-to-sheaf-cohomology-on-rational-basis*) Let `V` be a ring and `m ⊆ V` an ideal with `m² = m`
(so almost zero modules form a Serre class closed under products and filtered colimits, layer P0).
Let `X` be a topological space with a basis `ℬ` of quasi-compact open subsets closed under finite
intersections (so every open covering of `U ∈ ℬ` is refined by a finite covering by members of
`ℬ`), and `F` a sheaf of `V`-modules on `X`. Prove: if for every `U ∈ ℬ` and every finite covering
`𝔘` of `U` by members of `ℬ` the Čech cohomology `Ȟ^q(𝔘, F)` is almost zero for all `q ≥ 1`, then
the sheaf cohomology `H^q(U, F)` (derived-functor cohomology of the underlying sheaf of abelian
groups, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Sheaf.H`) is almost zero for every `U ∈ ℬ` and `q ≥ 1`;
equivalently `H^q(U, Fᵃ) = 0` for the associated sheaf of almost modules (layer P0, P0.29). For
`m = V` this is Cartan's criterion ([Stacks] Tag 01EW (Lemma 20.11.9)), also used in
DiamondsAndVStacks D0.19 and for `O_X` in AdicSpacesPartIII R3.1 (*sheafy-cech-acyclicity*), clause (2). It
applies to `X = Spa(A, A⁺)` for a Huber
pair with `ℬ` the rational subsets, a basis of quasi-compact opens closed under finite intersections
with finite rational refinements of every covering of a rational subset ([KL15] §2.4, proof of
Prop. 2.4.21, p. 46, the passage from Čech to sheaf cohomology on the rational basis; [Sch12] §6,
proof of Prop. 6.14, p. 38, for the perfectoid application; [HK] §3, Def. 3.9, p. 8, the convention for sheaf cohomology on `Spa`). With `V = R⁺`, `m`
the topologically nilpotent elements and `F = O_X⁺` on a perfectoid affinoid,
*integral-almost-acyclicity* supplies the hypothesis and the conclusion is ECD Theorem 3.24. The
hypothesis must hold for all `U ∈ ℬ` and all finite coverings: Čech acyclicity for the coverings of
`X` alone does not control `H^q(X, F)`. *Needs:* layer P0 (P0.1, P0.29); Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Sheaf.H`, `CategoryTheory.cechComplexFunctor`,
`CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.IsSerreClass`; Tau Ceti
`TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.isTopologicalBasis_spaRationalFamily`,
`TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.isCompact_of_mem_spaRationalFamily`,
`TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.rationalSubset_inter`,
`TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.exists_finite_spaRationalFamily_refinement`.

For the abstract lifting argument, apply the short exact sequences between successive
`C/ϖ^n C` to propagate almost-zero cohomology. Idempotency of `m` makes almost-zero modules
closed under extensions. The reductions form a termwise surjective tower; completeness
identifies its derived limit with `C`. The product description of `Rlim` and its cohomology
sequence then preserve almost-zero modules. The precise ordinary inverse-limit inputs are
[Stacks, Lemma 15.88.1(2), (3), (5)](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07KV) and
[§15.89](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0CQC), applied to `V`-modules. Reduction in the
reverse direction uses the multiplication-by-`ϖ` triangle.
`Perfectoid.complexMod` uses Mathlib extension and restriction of scalars along `V → V/(ϖ)`;
`almost_complex_reduction_iff`, `almost_lift_kernel` and `almost_lift_cokernel` state the
complex and linear-map forms with their completeness and torsion hypotheses.
For `almost_lift_cokernel`, idempotency strengthens the reduction hypothesis to
`mN ⊆ f(M) + ϖ·mN`. Successive corrections give a convergent series in the complete
source; the remaining error lies in every `ϖ^n N` and vanishes by separation of the target.
This applies to every idempotent ideal, including the zero and unit ideals.

**Checks for reduction.** `reduction_unit` gives the zero complex modulo one;
`reduction_zero` recovers the original complex modulo zero;
`reduction_characteristic_two` computes `2x = 0` after reduction modulo two.
`almost_lifting_zero_ideal` and `almost_lifting_identity` test the vacuous ideal and identity
map; `almostExact_test_nonseparated` remains the failure when separation is omitted.

For the Cartan step, [Stacks, Lemma 20.11.9](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01EW) verifies
the ordinary statement. Its dimension-shifting proof can be run modulo the Serre class of
`m`-annihilated modules: filtered refinements compute degree one, finite products give the
Čech terms, and `m² = m` controls extensions. The additional identification with derived
cohomology in the category of almost sheaves requires an exact almostification comparison;
that comparison is a separate target of layer P0. The ordinary-cohomology almost-vanishing
claim above does not assume that comparison. The almost Cartan criterion `almost_cartan` has the
general signature: a scalar action `V → End(F)`, an idempotent ideal, a quasi-compact basis closed
under intersections, and almost vanishing for every finite basis covering. Its conclusion
uses Mathlib’s cohomology presheaf on each basis open. The computed scalar Checks
`cartan_zero_scalar`, `cartan_unit_scalar` and `cartan_two_term_additivity` give zero,
identity and the sum of two scalar actions.

### P2.8 the sheaf theorem

The sheaf theorem collects the sheaf property, the perfectoidness of the rational localisations
and the (almost) vanishing of cohomology; the `p`-finite route of Scholze is kept alongside it.

**The sheaf theorem: `O_X` is a sheaf with vanishing higher cohomology and `H^i(X, O_X⁺)` is almost
zero.** (*sheaf-theorem-and-almost-acyclicity*) Let `(R, R⁺)` be a perfectoid Tate pair (ECD
Definition 3.1: any perfectoid Tate ring, of characteristic `0`, `p` or mixed, with no perfectoid
base field) and `X = Spa(R, R⁺)`. Then: (i) `O_X` and `O_X⁺` are sheaves on `X`; (ii) for every
rational `U ⊆ X`, `(O_X(U), O_X⁺(U))` is a perfectoid Tate pair with tilt
`(O_{X♭}(U♭), O_{X♭}⁺(U♭))`, `U♭` the image of `U` in `X♭`; (iii) `H⁰(X, O_X) = R` and
`H^i(X, O_X) = 0` for `i > 0` (AdicSpacesPartIII R3.1 (*sheafy-cech-acyclicity*), for the pair
made
sheafy by *perfectoid-stably-uniform-and-sheafy*); (iv) `H⁰(X, O_X⁺) = R⁺` and, for `i > 0`, the `R⁺`-module
`H^i(X, O_X⁺)` is almost zero, i.e. killed by every topologically nilpotent element of `R⁺`
(equivalently `H^i(X, O_X⁺ᵃ) = H^i(X, O_X°ᵃ) = 0` in the almost category, [Sch12] §6, Rem. 6.12,
p. 36); (v) (i)–(iv) hold for every rational `U` in place of `X`. Sheaf cohomology is that of
sheaves of abelian groups on the topological space `X`. This is ECD Theorems 3.18 and 3.24 in their
stated generality; ECD's citations [Sch12], [KL15] cover perfectoid algebras over a perfectoid field
and over `ℚ_p` (with characteristic `p`), and the case where `p` is neither zero nor invertible is
Kedlaya–Liu II §3.3 ([ECD] §3, Thm 3.18, p. 18, for (i)–(ii), and Thm 3.24, p. 19, for (iv);
[Sch12] §6, Thm 6.3(iii)–(iv), p. 30, and Prop. 6.14, p. 37, over a perfectoid field; [KL15] §3.6,
Thm 3.6.15, p. 94, for the vanishing of `H^i(X, O)` and the almost vanishing of `H^i(X, O⁺)`;
[Berkeley] Lecture 7, Thm 7.4.4, p. 53, (iii) for perfectoid Tate–Huber pairs; [HK] §6, Prop. 6.14,
p. 19, (iv) without a base field; [AWS] Lecture 2, §2.9, Thm 2.9.5, p. 73, (iv) for analytic
perfectoid pairs). Sch12 Theorem 6.3(iii)–(iv) and Proposition 6.14, Kedlaya–Liu II
Corollary 3.3.20, Berkeley Theorem 7.4.4, Hansen–Kedlaya Proposition 6.14 and Kedlaya AWS
Theorem 2.9.5 are instances. For `K` a perfectoid field and `X = Spa(K, K°)`, `H^i(X, O_X⁺) = 0` for
`i > 0` because `X` is a point with the trivial covering only, and `H⁰ = K°`; almost zero cannot be
improved to zero in general (Sch12 Remark 6.12 states the result as `m`-torsion). For `R` of ECD
Example 3.4(iv) the theorem applies: the Tate-ring proofs of the ingredients use no base field.
*Needs:* *perfectoid-stably-uniform-and-sheafy*; *rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids*;
*perfectoid-pair-rational-restriction*; *integral-almost-acyclicity*;
*cech-to-sheaf-cohomology-on-rational-basis*; layer P0 (P0.5, P0.29); Tau Ceti
`TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.mem_iff_forall_vle_one`; Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Sheaf.H`,
`TopCat.Presheaf.IsSheaf`.

**Almost acyclicity for p-finite perfectoid affinoids via Tate's acyclicity theorem.**
(*p-finite-acyclicity-from-tate*) Let `K` be a perfectoid field of characteristic `p` with
pseudouniformiser `ϖ`. A perfectoid affinoid `K`-algebra `(R, R⁺)` is `p`-finite if it is the
completed perfection of a reduced affinoid `K`-algebra `(S, S⁺)` of topologically finite type in
the convention of Sch12 Definition 2.6(iii), which includes `S⁺ = S°` (`S` a quotient of a Tate
algebra; an arbitrary smaller plus ring is not part of Sch12 Definition 6.9): `R⁺` is the `ϖ`-adic
completion of `colim_Φ S⁺` and `R = R⁺[ϖ⁻¹]` ([Sch12] §6, Def. 6.9, p. 35). Every perfectoid Tate
pair of characteristic `p` is a perfectoid affinoid algebra over `𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^∧` via `t ↦ ϖ`,
with `R⁺` an algebra over its ring of integers (Sch12 proof of Proposition 6.14; the same statement
is clause (a) of P5.13.2's *char-p-perfectoid-base-field*, which uses this subsection
and is not an input here), so every characteristic-`p` perfectoid Tate pair is in the scope of the base-field
convention; but only those that are completed perfections of reduced affinoid `K`-algebras are
`p`-finite, and a general characteristic-`p` perfectoid Tate pair is a completed direct limit of
`p`-finite ones (*completed-direct-limits-of-p-finite-affinoids*), not itself `p`-finite
(`K⟨T_s^{1/p^∞} : s ∈ ℕ⟩` in infinitely many variables is not). For such `(S, S⁺)` and `Y = Spa(S, S⁺)` prove: (i) `S°` is open and bounded
(`S` is uniform); (ii) for every rational `V ⊆ Y`, `O_Y(V)` is again a reduced affinoid `K`-algebra
of topologically finite type; (iii) for every finite covering of a rational `V ⊆ Y` by rational
subsets, every cohomology module of the augmented Čech complex of the `O_Y(·)°` is killed by a
power of `ϖ`; and for `X = Spa(R, R⁺)`: (iv) the projection `X → Y` is a homeomorphism identifying
rational subsets; (v) for rational `U ⊆ X` corresponding to `V ⊆ Y`, `(O_X(U), O_X⁺(U))` is the
completed perfection of `(O_Y(V), O_Y⁺(V))`; (vi) for every finite rational covering of `X` the
augmented Čech complex `0 → O_X(X)°ᵃ → ∏ O_X(U_i)°ᵃ → ∏ O_X(U_i ∩ U_j)°ᵃ → ⋯` is exact, so `O_X` is a
sheaf and `H^i(X, O_X°ᵃ) = 0` for `i > 0`, equivalently `H^i(X, O_X⁺)` is almost zero (Sch12
Proposition 6.11, Remark 6.12) ([Sch12] §6, proof of Prop. 6.10, p. 36, the rigid-analytic inputs
(i)–(iii); proof of Prop. 6.11(i) and (iii), pp. 36–37, for (iv) and (vi); [Sch12] arXiv v1,
Def. 2.6(iii), p. 8, published version p. 254 (PDF p. 10), the topologically-finite-type convention
with the maximal plus ring). The route through Tate's acyclicity is an alternative to the Frobenius
route of *integral-almost-acyclicity*; it is kept because Sch12 §7 (Lemma 7.5(ii),
Propositions 7.6, 7.7, 7.13) reduces étale statements to `p`-finite algebras and hence to
noetherian adic spaces. For `S = K⟨T⟩` and the covering by `{|T| ≤ |ϖ|}` and `{|ϖ| ≤ |T|}`,
`R = K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩` is `p`-finite, `X ≅ Y`, and the `O°`-Čech complex is exact both for `Y` and for
`X`. *Needs:* *integral-cech-cohomology-bounded-torsion*; *completed-direct-limits-of-p-finite-affinoids*;
layer P1; AdicSpacesPartII R0.9 (*reduced-affinoid-supremum-norm*); Tau Ceti
`TauCeti.Huber.IsStronglyNoetherian`,
`TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing.isOpenMap`.

**Perfectoid affinoid algebras in characteristic p are completed direct limits of p-finite ones.**
(*completed-direct-limits-of-p-finite-affinoids*) Let `K` be a perfectoid field of characteristic
`p` with pseudouniformiser `ϖ`, and `(R, R⁺)` a perfectoid affinoid `K`-algebra such that `R⁺` is a
`K°`-algebra (every perfectoid Tate pair of characteristic `p` satisfies this for
`K = 𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^∧` with `t ↦ ϖ`, Sch12 proof of Proposition 6.14; P5.13.2's
*char-p-perfectoid-base-field* (a) cites this for (i), downstream). Prove: (i) `(R, R⁺)` is the completion of a filtered direct limit of
`p`-finite perfectoid affinoid `K`-algebras `(R_I, R_I⁺)` indexed by the finite subsets `I ⊆ R⁺`:
`S_I` is the image of `K⟨T_i : i ∈ I⟩ → R` with the quotient topology, `S_I⁺` the integral closure
in `S_I` of the image of `K°⟨T_i : i ∈ I⟩` (this choice makes `S_I⁺ ⊆ R⁺` automatic, `R⁺` being
integrally closed and containing the images of the `T_i`; Sch12 instead takes `S_I⁺ = S_I°` and
uses Tate's theorem that power-bounded elements of a reduced affinoid algebra are integral over
`K°⟨T⟩`; `S_I⁺` is in general not the preimage of `R⁺` in `S_I`), and `(R_I, R_I⁺)` the completed
perfection of `(S_I, S_I⁺)`; precisely `R⁺/ϖ^n = colim_I R_I⁺/ϖ^n` for all `n`; (ii)
`Spa(R, R⁺) ≅ lim_I Spa(R_I, R_I⁺)`, and every rational `U ⊆ X` is the preimage of a rational
`U_I ⊆ X_I = Spa(R_I, R_I⁺)` for some `I`; (iii) `(O_X(U), O_X⁺(U))` is the completion of
`colim_{J ⊇ I} (O_{X_J}(U_J), O_{X_J}⁺(U_J))`, `U_J` the preimage of `U_I`; (iv) if `U_I ⊆ X_I` is a
quasi-compact open containing the image of `X`, then the image of `X_J` lies in `U_I` for some
`J ⊇ I` ([Sch12] §6, Lem. 6.13(i) with proof, p. 37, for (i), the colimit description modulo `ϖ^n`
and the hypothesis on `S_I⁺`; proof of Lem. 6.13(iv), p. 37, for (iv); proof of Prop. 6.14, p. 37,
the reduction that makes the `K°`-algebra hypothesis harmless). For `R = K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩` and
`I = {T}`, `S_I = K⟨T⟩` and `R_I = R` for this particular index; this does not assert that every transition
beyond it is an isomorphism. Part (iv) lets a
finite rational covering of `X`, and finite étale covers over it, descend to a finite `X_J` (Sch12
Propositions 6.14 and 7.6). *Needs:* layer P1; AdicSpacesPartII R0.19.5’s spectral-limit calculus; Mathlib
`UniformSpace.Completion`; Tau Ceti `TauCeti.Huber.restrictedMvPowerSeriesCompletion`,
`TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.rationalSubset`.

`Perfectoid.PFiniteModel` records a reduced strictly finite-type affinoid, its maximal plus
ring, a continuous topological embedding into the perfected algebra, density of its
`p`-power roots, and equality of the completed root-integral model with the chosen plus
ring. `IsPFinite` means that such a model exists. `PFiniteSystem` records the finite-subset
diagram, its compatible scalar maps and its map to `R`. At `I`, the reduced source is
topologically generated by the elements of `I` and embeds algebraically in `R`; it keeps
its affinoid quotient topology. The completed-perfection map need not be an embedding.
`pfiniteSystem_isColimit`, `pfiniteSystem_mod`, `pfiniteSystem_topologicalLimit`,
`pfiniteSystem_rational_descent` and `pfiniteSystem_eventual_image` state the completed
colimit, its quotient comparisons, the valuation-space limit and finite-stage descent.
`pfiniteSystem_rational_colimit` includes the rational-localization comparison, with
transition maps and the map to the limiting localization fixed over the base stages.
The modulo-parameter comparison states both surjectivity and eventual vanishing of a
representative, so it specifies the kernel as well as the image.

**Checks for p-finite models.** `pfinite_field` recovers `K`; `pfinite_disc` uses the completed
perfection of `K⟨T⟩`; `pfinite_infinite_variables_nonexample` excludes the perfected algebra
on countably infinitely many independent variables from being a single p-finite object.
`pfinite_system_empty` recovers the scalar field at the empty index when `R` is nonzero
(the zero ring instead gives a zero stage); `pfinite_system_singleton` lifts its named
integral generator; `pfinite_system_two_generators` computes the sum and product of two
generators in their common stage. `pfiniteModel_spa_homeomorph` and
`pfiniteModel_rational_correspondence` fix the p-finite source comparison on valuations.

`rationalPairFunctor` uses opposite inclusion of rational opens; its map is exactly
`rationalRes`, as `rationalPairFunctor_map` states. **Checks.**
`rationalPairFunctor_whole` identifies the whole-space value with the original pair;
`rationalPairFunctor_empty` gives the zero ring; `rationalPairFunctor_proper` shows that
a proper rational subset cannot have a surjective map on spectra.

### P2.9 affinoid perfectoid spaces

**Affinoid perfectoid spaces: adic spectra of perfectoid Huber pairs.** (*affinoid-perfectoid-space*)
A space `X` here is an object of Tau Ceti's `PreAdicSpace`; the adic spaces among them are the
sheafy ones (`PreAdicSpace.isAdic`). AdicEtaleGeometry's analytic carrier `YonedaAdicSpace`, the full
subcategory of `J_rat`-sheaves on `CAffᵒᵖ` covered by open affinoid Yoneda spectra
([Berkeley] §3.4, Def. 3.4.1, printed p. 22), receives adic spaces through
`YonedaAdicSpace.ofAdicSpace`, and the statements below phrased on it are read through that
embedding. `X` is
*affinoid perfectoid* if there are a complete Hausdorff Huber pair `(R, R⁺)` (Tau Ceti `Huber.Pair`:
`R⁺ ⊆ R°` open and integrally closed) with `R` a perfectoid Tate ring in the sense of ECD
Definition 3.1 (layer P1, P1.1: complete, uniform, with a pseudouniformiser `ϖ` such that `ϖ^p | p`
in `R°` and Frobenius `R°/ϖ → R°/ϖ^p` bijective) and an isomorphism of adic spaces
`X ≅ Spa(R, R⁺)`. Here `Spa(R, R⁺)` means Tau Ceti's `presentationLimitPreAdicSpace` of the pair
(for a pair of definition contained in `R⁺`), for `R : Perfectoid.PairCat p`; it is an adic space,
and its image under `YonedaAdicSpace.ofAdicSpace` is the Yoneda spectrum
`YonedaAdicSpace.ofSpaY (CAff.of R.pair)`, because perfectoid Tate pairs are sheafy
(see *perfectoid-stably-uniform-and-sheafy*). For such `X` the global sections recover the pair,
`(O_X(X), O_X⁺(X)) ≅ (R, R⁺)`, by the library: `TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.isIso_toPresentationLimit_top`
for `O_X(X) = R` and `TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.mem_iff_forall_vle_one` (Wedhorn Prop. 7.52(1),
`IsRingOfIntegralElements.mem_of_forall_vle_one`) for `O_X⁺(X) = {f : |f(x)| ≤ 1 for all x} = R⁺`;
so `X` is affinoid perfectoid iff it is isomorphic to the Yoneda spectrum of a complete
sheafy Huber pair and `O_X(X)` is a perfectoid Tate ring, and
then `X ≅ Spa(O_X(X), O_X⁺(X))` canonically. By [Wedhorn] §8.2, Rem. 8.24 and Prop. 8.25, p. 80,
`Spa` is an anti-equivalence from complete perfectoid Huber pairs with morphisms of Huber pairs
(Tau Ceti `Huber.Pair.Hom`: continuous ring maps carrying plus ring into plus ring) to the full
subcategory of affinoid perfectoid spaces. Conventions: (1) the predicate asks for a
presentation by a perfectoid ring ([Berkeley] Lecture 7, §7.1, Rem. 7.1.3, printed p. 49); it is
not the conjunction "affinoid and a perfectoid space"; the two agree in characteristic `p`
(see *characteristic-p-affinoid-perfectoid-criterion*), and their agreement in characteristic `0` is
not asserted; (2) no perfectoid base field is fixed ([ECD] §3, Ex. 3.4(iv), p. 15; [Sch12] §6,
after the proof of Thm 6.3, p. 38, names `Spa(R, R⁺)` of a perfectoid affinoid `K`-algebra, and the
base field is dropped here), `R⁺` is an arbitrary ring of integral elements, and the zero ring is
allowed, so the empty adic space is affinoid perfectoid; (3) morphisms are morphisms of adic
spaces. In `PerfectoidSpace`, define `isAffinoidPerfectoidModel` (the object property of
`PreAdicSpace` satisfied by the spaces `presentationLimitPreAdicSpace` of perfectoid Tate pairs) and
`isAffinoidPerfectoid` as its isomorphism closure, the predicate on a pre-adic space `X`
(there exist a complete Hausdorff Huber pair `(R, R⁺)` with `R` perfectoid and an isomorphism
`X ≅ Spa(R, R⁺)`), so that closure under isomorphisms holds by construction; and `spa` as
`Spa(R, R⁺)` of a complete Hausdorff Huber pair with `R` perfectoid. The proposed lemma names
written `IsAffinoidPerfectoid.*` below refer to this object property. Prove
`isAffinoidPerfectoid_presentationLimitPreAdicSpace` (`Spa(R, R⁺)` is affinoid perfectoid), `IsAffinoidPerfectoid.isPerfectoidTateRing_sections` (if `X` is
affinoid perfectoid then `O_X(X)` is a perfectoid Tate ring, `(O_X(X), O_X⁺(X))` is a complete
Huber pair, and `X → Spa(O_X(X), O_X⁺(X))` corresponding to the identity is an isomorphism),
the characterisation of affinoid perfectoid spectra (for a complete Hausdorff Huber pair
`A : CAff` with `[IsTateRing A.A]` and `hA : A.Sheafy`, `Spa A` is affinoid perfectoid iff
`IsPerfectoidTateRing p A.A`; sheafiness identifies the global sections with `A.A`,
by [Wedhorn] §8.2, Def. 8.21 and Prop. 8.25, p. 80, and the perfectoid presentation
uses [Berkeley] §7.1, Thm 7.1.1 and Rem. 7.1.3, printed p. 49),
`spaHomEquiv` (for a perfectoid space `Y`) and `spaHomEquiv_adic` (for any
`Y : TauCeti.AdicSpace`, embedded by `YonedaAdicSpace.ofAdicSpace`):
morphisms `Y → Spa(R, R⁺)` correspond naturally to
continuous unital ring maps `R → O_Y(Y)` carrying `R⁺` into `O_Y⁺(Y)`; for a complete sheafy
affinoid `Y = Spa(S, S⁺)` these are `Huber.Pair.Hom (R, R⁺) (S, S⁺)`. The global sections of an
arbitrary `Y` need not form a Huber ring, so the general right-hand side is the subtype of ring
maps with these two properties, `affinoidPerfectoidEquiv` (`Spa` is an equivalence from the opposite of the
complete perfectoid Huber pairs to the full subcategory of affinoid perfectoid spaces),
`IsAffinoidPerfectoid.of_iso` (closed under isomorphisms, Mathlib
`ObjectProperty.IsClosedUnderIsomorphisms`), `IsAffinoidPerfectoid.spectralSpace` (the underlying
space is spectral, in particular quasi-compact and quasi-separated),
`IsAffinoidPerfectoid.isAnalyticPoint` (every point is analytic, `R` being Tate) and
`IsAffinoidPerfectoid.rationalSubset` (rational subsets are affinoid perfectoid,
*affinoid-perfectoid-basis*). *Needs:* layer P1 (P1.1); *perfectoid-stably-uniform-and-sheafy*;
*sheaf-theorem-and-almost-acyclicity*; AdicSpaces layers 3.5 and 5; Tau Ceti `TauCeti.AdicSpace`,
`TauCeti.PreAdicSpace`, `TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.isIso_toPresentationLimit_top`,
`TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.mem_iff_forall_vle_one`, `TauCeti.Huber.Pair`,
`TauCeti.Huber.Pair.Hom`, `TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing`, `TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.spa`,
`TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.spaAnalytic_eq_spa_of_isTateRing`,
`TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.spectralSpace_spa_of_pairOfDefinition`; Mathlib
`CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.IsClosedUnderIsomorphisms`.

**Checks.**

- `IsAffinoidPerfectoid.spa_Cp` (computation) — `Spa(ℂ_p, O_{ℂ_p})` is affinoid perfectoid and its
  underlying space is a single point (the rank-one valuation).
- `affinoid_padic_nonexample` (non-example) — `Spa(ℚ_p, ℤ_p)` is an affinoid adic space
  (strongly noetherian, AdicSpaces layer 4.1) but not affinoid perfectoid: any isomorphism
  `Spa(ℚ_p, ℤ_p) ≅ Spa(R, R⁺)` gives `R ≅ O(Spa(ℚ_p, ℤ_p)) = ℚ_p`, which is not perfectoid (ECD
  Remark 3.3); a definition asking only for surjective Frobenius on the residue field would accept
  it.
- Degenerate: the empty adic space is affinoid perfectoid,
  presented by the zero ring with the zero plus ring (`0` is a pseudouniformiser of the zero ring
  and ECD Definition 3.1 holds vacuously); a definition requiring a nonzero ring or a base field
  fails this.
- `IsAffinoidPerfectoid.spa_ecd34iv` (computation) — for
  `R = ℤ_p^cycl[[T^{1/p^∞}]]⟨(p/T)^{1/p^∞}⟩[1/T]` with `ϖ = T^{1/p}` (ECD Example 3.4(iv)),
  `Spa(R, R°)` is affinoid perfectoid; no perfectoid base field is required.
- `spaHomEquiv_perfectoidField` (characterisation) — for a perfectoid field `K` and a complete
  perfectoid Tate pair `(S, S⁺)`, morphisms `Spa(S, S⁺) → Spa(K, K°)` are exactly the continuous
  ring maps `K → S` carrying `K°` into `S⁺`.
- Compatibility: `X` is affinoid perfectoid iff it
  is isomorphic to the Yoneda spectrum of a complete sheafy Huber pair (the image of the
  classical affinoid adic space under `ofAdicSpace`) and `O_X(X)` is a perfectoid Tate ring. For
  `A : CAff` with `[IsTateRing A.A]` and `hA : A.Sheafy`, the Check applies the characterisation
  of affinoid perfectoid spectra to identify this with `IsPerfectoidTateRing p A.A`.

`PerfectoidSpace.isAffinoidPerfectoid` asks for an isomorphism to the spectrum
`presentationLimitPreAdicSpace` of a `PairCat` object (`isAffinoidPerfectoidModel`). `ofPair`
constructs this spectrum in `Perfd`; `spaFunctor_map` specifies its action on morphisms, which on
the analytic carrier is AdicEtaleGeometry's sheafified Yoneda map. `affinoidPerfectoidEquiv`
and its comparison with `spaFunctor` give the anti-equivalence.

**Checks for the affinoid carrier and anti-equivalence.** `affinoid_spa_agreement` agrees with
the supplied spectrum; `affinoid_zero_pair` gives the empty spectrum;
`affinoid_padic_nonexample` excludes `Spa(ℚ_p, ℤ_p)`.
`affinoid_equivalence_empty`, `affinoid_equivalence_distinguishes_maps` and
`affinoid_equivalence_recovers_pair` test the empty object, two unequal morphisms and recovery
of the original complete pair.

For a perfectoid test space `Y`, `GlobalPairMap` is the type of continuous ring maps
`R → globalSections Y` carrying `R⁺` into `globalPlus Y`. `spaHomEquiv_apply` fixes the
correspondence as pullback followed by the inverse of the affinoid section equivalence.
**Checks.** `affine_mapping_empty` gives a unique map into the sections of the empty space;
`affine_mapping_recovers_pair` recovers the Huber-pair maps when `Y` is affinoid;
`affine_mapping_inverse_parameter` excludes the image of an inverse parameter from the
plus ring of any nonzero target chart.

For a classical `Y : TauCeti.AdicSpace`, `spaHomEquiv_adic` states the mapping equivalence
on AdicEtaleGeometry's Yoneda carrier, using the actual topological global sections and
`AdicEtaleGeometry.AdicSpace.Oplus Y ⊤`. Its value is the supplied
`YonedaAdicSpace.mapsFromAdicSpaceEquiv` applied to the underlying sheaf morphism
([Wedhorn] §8.2, Prop. 8.25, p. 80). This applies to every classical adic source,
without a perfectoid hypothesis. The supplier includes the topology and integral condition.

The comparison with the analytic carrier identifies affinoid perfectoidness of
`YonedaAdicSpace.ofAdicSpace.obj X`, for every
`X : TauCeti.AdicSpace`, with the existence of a perfectoid pair `R`, its sheafiness
proof `hR`, and a classical isomorphism `X ≅ (CAff.of R.pair).adicSpa hR`, that is, with
`isAffinoidPerfectoid` of the underlying pre-adic space.
It follows from the supplier's fully faithful embedding and `ofAdicSpace_spa`
([Berkeley] Prop. 3.2.2, printed p. 20, and §3.4, printed p. 22).
**Checks.** `adic_comparison_affinoid` tests a perfectoid pair;
`adic_comparison_empty` tests the empty classical source;
`adic_comparison_padic_nonexample` excludes the embedded spectrum of `ℚ_p`.

Lean: `PerfectoidSpace.isAffinoidPerfectoidModel`, `isAffinoidPerfectoid`,
`isAffinoidPerfectoid_presentationLimitPreAdicSpace`.

### P2.10 perfectoid spaces

Perfectoid spaces: the full subcategory `Perfd` of adic spaces, its characteristic-`p` part
`Perf`, and the glued tilt.

**Perfectoid spaces: the full subcategory Perfd of adic spaces, and Perf in characteristic p.**
(*perfectoid-space*) Fix a prime `p`. A *perfectoid space* is an adic space, that is, a sheafy
object `X` of Tau Ceti's `PreAdicSpace`, covered by open subspaces that are affinoid perfectoid
(see *affinoid-perfectoid-space*): every `x ∈ X` has an open neighbourhood `U` such that the open
subspace `X|_U` (`PreAdicSpace.restrict`) is isomorphic to `Spa(R, R⁺)` with `R` a perfectoid Tate
ring and `R⁺ ⊆ R°` a ring of integral elements ([ECD] §3, Def. 3.19, p. 18; [Berkeley] Lecture 7,
§7.1, Def. 7.1.2, printed p. 49). Sheafiness is part of the definition: without it the empty
pre-adic space with nonzero sections over `∅` would qualify, the chart condition being vacuous for
it. The category `Perfd` of perfectoid spaces is the full subcategory
of `PreAdicSpace` on these objects (Mathlib `ObjectProperty.FullSubcategory`):
morphisms are those of pre-adic spaces. Open immersions are `PreAdicSpace.IsOpenImmersion`; the
point carrier is the underlying space. Through AdicEtaleGeometry's `YonedaAdicSpace.ofAdicSpace`
these agree with the analytic carrier's open immersions `YonedaAdicSpace.IsOpenImmersion` and
points `YonedaAdicSpace.space` (`YonedaAdicSpace.ofAdicSpace_space`, and
*adic-spaces-in-yoneda-adic-spaces* for open immersions). `Perf ⊆ Perfd` is the full subcategory of perfectoid spaces of characteristic
`p`, those with `p = 0` in `O_X(X)` (in Lean, `InCharP` asks for `p = 0` in `O_X(U)` for every open
`U`, equivalent by `mem_perf_iff` below); equivalently, `X` admits a (necessarily unique) morphism to the
discrete adic space `Spa(𝔽_p, 𝔽_p)`, which is an adic space (AdicSpacesPartII R0.2
(*discrete-huber-pair-sheafy*)) but
not a perfectoid space, and which `Perf` does not contain ([ECD] §1, p. 3). With the
definition: every point of a perfectoid space is analytic, so every morphism of adic spaces into a
perfectoid space is adic (AdicSpacesPartII R0.6 (*adic-morphism*)); an adic space with `p = 0`
in its structure sheaf
is perfectoid iff it is covered by open subspaces `Spa(R, R⁺)` with `R` a perfect complete Tate
ring ([ECD] §3, Prop. 3.5, p. 15). In `PerfectoidSpace`, define `isPerfectoidSpace` (the object
property of `PreAdicSpace`: sheafy, and every point has an open neighbourhood `U` with `X|_U` affinoid
perfectoid), the category `Perfd` (its full subcategory, with hom sets those of pre-adic spaces),
`toAdicSpace` (the inclusion of `Perfd` into pre-adic spaces, landing in adic spaces, Mathlib
`ObjectProperty.ι`, fully faithful by `ObjectProperty.fullyFaithfulι`),
`ofSpa` (`Spa(R, R⁺)` as an object of `Perfd`), `InCharP` and `Perf` (the full subcategory on `p = 0` in
every ring of sections, fully faithful in `Perfd`); the proposed lemma names written
`IsPerfectoidSpace.*` below refer to the object property `isPerfectoidSpace`. Prove
`isAffinoidPerfectoid_le_isPerfectoidSpace` (affinoid perfectoid spaces are perfectoid spaces),
`isPerfectoidSpace_le_isAdic` (perfectoid spaces are adic spaces, their charts being sheafy by
`Perfectoid.isSheafyRing`), `IsPerfectoidSpace.of_iso` (closed under isomorphisms), `IsPerfectoidSpace.of_openCover` (covered
by perfectoid open subspaces implies perfectoid), `IsPerfectoidSpace.isAnalyticPoint` (every point
analytic, hence every `T → X` adic by `AdicSpace.isAdic_iff_image_analyticLocus`), `isPerfectoidSpace_restrict`
(open subspaces are perfectoid, *open-subspaces-of-perfectoid-spaces*),
`isBasis_affinoidPerfectoidOpens` (affinoid perfectoid opens form a basis,
*affinoid-perfectoid-basis*), `mem_perf_iff` (`X ∈ Perf` iff `p = 0` in `O_X(U)` for every open
`U` iff there is a unique morphism `X → Spa(𝔽_p, 𝔽_p)` iff every affinoid perfectoid open has a ring
of characteristic `p`) and the characteristic-`p` criterion (for `p = 0` in `O_X(X)`: perfectoid iff
covered by `Spa` of perfect complete Tate rings, *characteristic-p-affinoid-perfectoid-criterion*).
*Needs:* *affinoid-perfectoid-space*; layer P1 (P1.2); AdicSpacesPartII R0.2, R0.6
(*discrete-huber-pair-sheafy*, *adic-morphism*,
*adic-iff-analytic-locus*: adic morphisms, finiteness classes, locally noetherian spaces); Tau Ceti
`TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.spaAnalytic_eq_spa_of_isTateRing`,
`TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.IsAnalyticPoint`; Mathlib `CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.FullSubcategory`,
`CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.ι`, `CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.fullyFaithfulι`,
`CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.IsClosedUnderIsomorphisms`, `CharP`.

**Checks.**

- `perfectoid_empty` (degenerate) — the empty adic space is a perfectoid space (covered by
  the empty family); an empty pre-adic space is perfectoid exactly when it is sheafy, its sections
  over `∅` vanishing, the chart condition being vacuous (a Lean `example`).
- `perfectoid_padic_nonexample` (non-example) — `Spa(ℚ_p, ℤ_p)` is not a perfectoid space: its only
  nonempty open subset is the whole space, whose ring `ℚ_p` is not perfectoid (ECD Remark 3.3).
- `not_isPerfectoidSpace_closedUnitDisc_Qp` (non-example) — the closed unit disc
  `Spa(ℚ_p⟨T⟩, ℤ_p⟨T⟩)` is not a perfectoid space: the classical point `T = 0` has completed residue
  field `ℚ_p`, discretely valued and not perfectoid, whereas every completed residue field of a
  perfectoid space is a perfectoid field (*completed-residue-fields*; Kedlaya AWS
  Corollary 2.5.7).
- `not_isPerfectoidSpace_spa_Fp` (non-example) — the discrete `Spa(𝔽_p, 𝔽_p)` is an adic space of
  characteristic `p` (AdicSpacesPartII R0.2 (*discrete-huber-pair-sheafy*)) and is not
  perfectoid: its unique point has open support, so it is not
  analytic; a construction treating `Spa 𝔽_p` as a perfectoid Tate space, e.g. as a final object of
  `Perf`, is wrong.
- Computation: gluing two copies of the perfectoid
  closed disc `Spa(ℂ_p⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, O_{ℂ_p}⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩)` along the open complement of `T = 0`
  (AdicSpaces layer 5.3) gives a perfectoid space which is quasi-compact but not quasi-separated:
  the two charts meet in a non-quasi-compact open.

For every `X : TauCeti.AdicSpace`, the comparison with the analytic carrier says that
`YonedaAdicSpace.ofAdicSpace.obj X` is perfectoid in the Yoneda sense exactly when each
`x : X.obj` lies in the image of a classical open immersion from the sheafy spectrum
of a perfectoid pair. This is the classical covering definition of [ECD] §3,
Def. 3.19, p. 18, transported along the fully faithful comparison of [Berkeley] §3.4,
printed p. 22; preservation of points and open immersions identifies the covering condition.
The empty covering is allowed. Thus the Yoneda predicates also express the stated
classical notions, which are the Lean definitions, without identifying the two ambient categories by
definition.

`PerfectoidSpace.isPerfectoidSpace` asks for sheafiness and open affinoid perfectoid charts
covering every point; `Perfd` is its full subcategory of `PreAdicSpace`. `InCharP` requires `p = 0`
in every ring of sections, equivalently (by `mem_perf_iff`) in every perfectoid affinoid chart, and
`Perf` is the corresponding full subcategory.
**Checks.** `perfectoid_empty`, `perfectoid_affinoid` and `perfectoid_padic_nonexample` test
empty, perfectoid affinoid and nonperfectoid field spectra. `characteristic_p_tilt`,
`characteristic_p_empty` and `characteristic_p_mixed_nonexample` test a tilted chart, the
empty space and a characteristic-zero chart. The last condition excludes the zero ring
through `CharZero`, rather than imposing nonemptiness on all spaces.

Lean: `PerfectoidSpace.isPerfectoidSpace`, `Perfd`, `InCharP`, `Perf`,
`isAffinoidPerfectoid_le_isPerfectoidSpace`, `isPerfectoidSpace_le_isAdic`,
`isPerfectoidSpace_restrict`, `isBasis_affinoidPerfectoidOpens`.

### P2.11 the glued tilt

P2.11 owns glued tilting on `PerfectoidSpace.Perfd`, including `tiltFunctor`,
`tiltHomeomorph`, the affinoid and restriction comparisons, and
`sliceTiltFunctor_isEquivalence`. AdicSpacesPartIV R5 consumes `PerfectoidSpace.tiltFunctor`
directly, downstream; P2 uses no subsection of AdicSpacesPartIV.

**The glued tilt `X ↦ X♭` of a perfectoid space.** (*perfectoid-spaces-and-glued-tilting*) For every
perfectoid space `X` (*perfectoid-space*; any characteristic, no base field) there is a perfectoid
space `X♭` of characteristic `p`, the *tilt* of `X`, with a homeomorphism `|X| ≅ |X♭|`, `x ↦ x♭`,
constructed by gluing ([ECD] §3, the sentence after Def. 3.19, p. 18; [Berkeley] Lecture 7, §7.1,
after Rem. 7.1.3, printed p. 49, the target `Perf`; [Sch12] §6, Def. 6.16 and Prop. 6.17 with
proof, p. 38, over a perfectoid field, where property (a) is "a formal consequence" of tilting of
algebras, of rational localisations and of maps into affinoid adic spaces; [Bhatt] §9.3,
Thm 9.3.10(1), printed p. 111). Affinoid case: for `X = Spa(R, R⁺)` with `R` perfectoid,
`X♭ := Spa(R♭, R♭⁺)`, where `(R♭, R♭⁺)` is the tilt of the pair (layer P1: `R♭ = lim_{x ↦ x^p} R`,
`R♭⁺ = lim_{x ↦ x^p} R⁺`), and `x ↦ x♭` is the tilting homeomorphism `|f(x♭)| = |f♯(x)|`
(*tilting-map-of-spectra*, *tilting-homeomorphism-and-rational-subsets*), which matches rational
subsets `U ↔ U♭` and satisfies `(O_{X♭}(U♭), O⁺_{X♭}(U♭)) ≅ (O_X(U), O⁺_X(U))♭` compatibly with
restrictions (see *rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids*). General case: `X♭` is glued
(AdicSpaces layer 5.3) from the tilts `V♭` of all affinoid perfectoid open subspaces `V ⊆ X`, along
the tilts of their common rational refinements (*affinoid-perfectoid-basis* (iii)); the family being
canonical, `X♭` is defined up to unique isomorphism, and `|X♭| = |X|` as sets with the same open
subsets. A morphism `f : Y → X` of perfectoid spaces gives `f♭ : Y♭ → X♭`, affinoid-locally `Spa` of
the tilt of the corresponding morphism of perfectoid Tate pairs (layer P1, P1.6), glued because
morphisms of adic spaces form a sheaf; so `X ↦ X♭` is a functor `Perfd ⥤ Perf` with `|f♭| = |f|`
under the homeomorphisms. Properties: (a) for `U ⊆ X` open, `(X|_U)♭ = X♭|_{U♭}`, `U♭` being `U`
viewed in `|X♭|`; `U` is affinoid perfectoid iff `U♭` is, and then
`(O_{X♭}(U♭), O⁺_{X♭}(U♭)) ≅ (O_X(U), O⁺_X(U))♭`; (b) the sharp maps glue to a continuous
multiplicative map of sheaves of topological monoids `O_{X♭} → O_X` on `|X| = |X♭|`, `f ↦ f♯`, with
`|f♯(x)| = |f(x♭)|`, carrying `O⁺_{X♭}` into `O⁺_X`; it is not additive; (c) for `X` of
characteristic `p`, projection to the zeroth coordinate `R♭ → R` is a ring isomorphism, giving a
natural isomorphism `X♭ ≅ X`; (d) `X` is not determined by `X♭` (the tilt forgets the untilt); the
equivalence of slice categories, with the description of maps into `X♭` by untilts, is
*tilting-slice-equivalence*. In `PerfectoidSpace`, define `tilt` as the functor `Perfd ⥤ Perf`,
`X ↦ X♭`, `f ↦ f♭`; prove `tiltHomeomorph` (`|X| ≃ₜ |X♭|`, Mathlib `Homeomorph`, natural in `X`:
`|f♭| ∘ h_Y = h_X ∘ |f|`; on affinoids the tilting homeomorphism), `tiltSpaIso`
(`(Spa(R, R⁺))♭ ≅ Spa(R♭, R♭⁺)`, natural in morphisms of complete perfectoid Tate pairs),
`tiltSectionsIso` (for `U ⊆ X` affinoid perfectoid, `(O_{X♭}(U♭), O⁺_{X♭}(U♭)) ≅ (O_X(U), O⁺_X(U))♭`
as topological rings with plus rings, compatibly with restriction to affinoid perfectoid `U' ⊆ U`),
the statement that `U` is affinoid perfectoid iff `U♭` is, `tiltRestrictIso`
(`(X|_U)♭ ≅ X♭|_{U♭}`; the tilt maps open immersions to open immersions and open covers to open
covers), `globalSharp` (the map of sheaves of topological monoids (b)), `tiltCharPIso` (for
`X ∈ Perf` a natural isomorphism `X♭ ≅ X`, i.e. `tilt` restricted to `Perf` is isomorphic to the
identity), `tiltSpaIso_naturality` (simp: under `tiltSpaIso`, the tilt of `Spa(φ)` is `Spa(φ♭)`),
`tiltHomeomorph_image_rationalSubset` (for affinoid perfectoid `U = Spa(R, R⁺) ⊆ X` the
homeomorphism carries `U(f_1♯, …, f_n♯ / g♯)` to `U(f_1, …, f_n / g)`, `f_i, g ∈ R♭`, and every
rational subset of `U♭` arises so) and `sliceTiltFunctor_isEquivalence` (the equivalence `Perfd/X ≃ Perf/X♭`,
*tilting-slice-equivalence*). *Needs:* *perfectoid-space*; *affinoid-perfectoid-space*;
*affinoid-perfectoid-basis*; *open-subspaces-of-perfectoid-spaces*; *tilting-map-of-spectra*;
*tilting-homeomorphism-and-rational-subsets*; *rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids*;
layer P1 (P1.5, P1.6); Tau Ceti `TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.spa`; Mathlib
`CategoryTheory.GlueData`, `Homeomorph`.

**Checks.**

- `tilt_spa_cyclotomic` (computation) — `Spa(ℚ_p^cycl, ℤ_p^cycl)♭ ≅ Spa(𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞})), 𝔽_p[[t^{1/p^∞}]])`, `t = (1, ζ_p, ζ_{p²}, …) − 1` (Berkeley Example 6.2.4),
  and the homeomorphism is the identity of the one-point space.
- `tilt_spa_perfectedDisc` (computation) — for a perfectoid Tate ring `R`:
  `Spa(R⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, R⁺⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩)♭ ≅ Spa(R♭⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, R♭⁺⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩)` with
  `T ↦ (T, T^{1/p}, …)` (Kedlaya AWS Example 2.3.15).
- `tilt_empty` (degenerate) — the tilt of the empty perfectoid space is empty.
- `tilt_characteristic_p` (compatibility) — for `X ∈ Perf` the natural isomorphism `X♭ ≅ X` holds,
  e.g. `Spa(𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞})))♭ ≅ Spa(𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞})))` via the zeroth coordinate.
- `tilt_not_injective_on_iso_classes` (non-example) — `Spa(ℚ_p^cycl, ℤ_p^cycl)` and
  `Spa(𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞})), 𝔽_p[[t^{1/p^∞}]])` are not isomorphic (different characteristic) but have
  isomorphic tilts; so `tilt : Perfd ⥤ Perf` is not an equivalence, and a construction claiming to
  recover `X` from `X♭` without a chosen base is wrong.
- `tiltHomeomorph_rationalSubset` (characterisation) — for `X = Spa(R, R⁺)` perfectoid and
  `f_1, …, f_n, g ∈ R♭` generating the unit ideal, the tilting homeomorphism maps
  `U(f_1♯, …, f_n♯ / g♯)` onto `U(f_1, …, f_n / g)`.

**Rational subsets of affinoid perfectoid opens are affinoid perfectoid, and affinoid perfectoid
opens form a basis.** (*affinoid-perfectoid-basis*) Let `X` be a perfectoid space. Prove: (i) if
`V ⊆ X` is an open subspace with an isomorphism `V ≅ Spa(R, R⁺)`, `R` perfectoid, then for every
rational subset `W = R(T/s) ⊆ Spa(R, R⁺)` (Tau Ceti `ValuationSpectrum.rationalSubset`, `T·R` open;
for `R` Tate, `T` generates the unit ideal) the open subspace `W ⊆ X` is affinoid perfectoid:
`W ≅ Spa(R⟨T/s⟩, R⟨T/s⟩⁺)`, the rational localisation of AdicSpaces layer 3.1, a perfectoid Tate
pair (see *rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids*), and
`(O_X(W), O_X⁺(W)) ≅ (R⟨T/s⟩, R⟨T/s⟩⁺)` compatibly with restriction from `V`
(see *perfectoid-pair-rational-restriction*); (ii) the affinoid perfectoid open subspaces of `X` form a
basis of the topology of `|X|`, and every quasi-compact open subset of `X` is a finite union of
them; (iii) for affinoid perfectoid opens `V, V' ⊆ X` and `x ∈ V ∩ V'` there is an open `W` with
`x ∈ W ⊆ V ∩ V'` that is a rational subset of `V` and of `V'`, hence affinoid perfectoid by (i);
(iv) for every affinoid perfectoid open `V ⊆ X`, `O_X(V)` is a perfectoid Tate ring and
`V ≅ Spa(O_X(V), O_X⁺(V))` canonically. The intersection of two affinoid perfectoid opens need not
be affinoid, nor quasi-compact ([Sch12] §6, proof of Prop. 6.17, p. 38, open subspaces and their
global sections, giving (iv); [Wedhorn] §8.2, Rem. 8.23(3), p. 80, part (iii); [ECD] §3, Thm 3.18,
p. 18, part (i)). For the perfectoid closed disc `X = Spa(ℂ_p⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, O_{ℂ_p}⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩)`, the
annulus `{|p| ≤ |T| ≤ 1} = R({p, T}/T)` is affinoid perfectoid with ring
`ℂ_p⟨T^{1/p^∞}, (p/T)^{1/p^∞}⟩`; in the perfectoid disc with doubled origin
