(the doubled-origin computation of P2.10) the two charts are affinoid perfectoid and meet in a
non-quasi-compact open. *Needs:* *perfectoid-space*; *affinoid-perfectoid-space*;
*rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids*; *perfectoid-pair-rational-restriction*; Tau Ceti
`TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.rationalSubset`,
`TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.isTopologicalBasis_spaRationalFamily`,
`TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.isCompact_of_mem_spaRationalFamily`,
`TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.spaLocalizationHomeomorph`.

**Open subspaces of perfectoid spaces are perfectoid; open immersions in Perfd.**
(*open-subspaces-of-perfectoid-spaces*) Let `X` be a perfectoid space and `U ⊆ |X|` open. The
affinoid case is *rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids* together with the library fact
that a rational subset is the open affinoid subspace `Spa` of its localisation
(`TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.spaLocalizationHomeomorph`); the gluing is what is proved here. Prove
that the open adic subspace `X|_U = (U, O_X|_U, (v_x)_{x ∈ U})` of AdicSpaces layer 5.1
([Wedhorn] §8.2, Rem. 8.23(2), p. 80) is a perfectoid space, and that the inclusion
`j : X|_U → X` is an open immersion of perfectoid spaces (Tau Ceti `PreAdicSpace.IsOpenImmersion`)
with the universal property in `Perfd` and in adic spaces: a morphism `f : Y → X` from an adic space `Y` factors through `j`, uniquely, iff
`f(|Y|) ⊆ U`. Conversely: (a) the source of an open immersion of adic spaces into a perfectoid space
is perfectoid; (b) an adic space covered by open subspaces that are perfectoid spaces is
perfectoid; (c) for open `U' ⊆ U`, `(X|_U)|_{U'} = X|_{U'}`. Consequently `Perfd` is closed under
open subspaces, the open immersions in `Perfd` are AdicSpaces' open immersions between perfectoid
spaces, and `Perf` is closed under open subspaces ([Sch12] §6, proof of Prop. 6.17, p. 38). For
`X = Spa(𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞}))⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩)` the punctured disc `{T ≠ 0}` is an open perfectoid subspace
in `Perf`, not quasi-compact and so not affinoid; a morphism
`Spa(ℂ_p, O_{ℂ_p}) → Spa(ℂ_p⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, O_{ℂ_p}⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩)`, `T^{1/p^n} ↦ a^{1/p^n}` for a
compatible system of `p`-power roots of `a ∈ O_{ℂ_p}`, factors through the annulus
`{|p| ≤ |T| ≤ 1}` iff `|p| ≤ |a|`. *Needs:* *perfectoid-space*; *affinoid-perfectoid-basis*.

`PerfectoidSpace.tiltFunctor`, `tiltSpaIso` and `tiltSpaIso_naturality` identify the glued
functor with affinoid tilting. `tiltHomeomorph_spa` identifies its underlying map with the
valuation-defined `spaTilt`, using the natural affinoid coordinates `spaSpaceEquiv`.
The restriction specification fixes the open embedding and its exact image; `tiltRestrictIso_inclusion`
fixes the comparison on open subspaces by their inclusions. `isBasis_affinoidPerfectoidOpens`
asserts the basis property without a quasi-separatedness assumption.

**Checks for global tilting and opens.** `tilt_empty`, `tilt_characteristic_p` and
`tilt_affinoid_valuation` test the empty tilt, characteristic-p agreement and the strict
valuation order `0 < 1`. `restriction_empty`, `restriction_whole` and `restriction_proper`
give the empty space, an isomorphism, and a non-isomorphism. `spa_space_empty`,
`spa_space_whole` and `spa_space_map_coordinate` test the affinoid coordinates on empty and
whole subsets and on pullback of a valuation.

The global sharp map uses `PerfectoidSpace.Chart`, an open affinoid chart with its specified
inclusion. The primary carrier of global functions is the structure sheaf of the underlying
`PreAdicSpace`: `globalSections X` is a reducible abbreviation of `Γ(X, O_X)`, the global sections
of Tau Ceti's structure presheaf of `X.obj`, and `globalPlus X` of its integral subring
`Γ(X, O⁺_X)`; the description of `Γ(X, O_X)` as the subring of the product of the chart rings cut
out by all restriction equations, with the chart plus-subring conditions for `Γ(X, O⁺_X)`, is a
comparison lemma (`globalSections_eq_compatibleFamilies`), and the family type used to prove it is
auxiliary. The topology on `Γ(X, O_X)` is the one induced by the chart restriction maps; no second
ring is introduced to carry it. `globalSectionsAffinoidEquiv_spec` recovers the affinoid ring by
evaluation on its identity chart and recovers its exact plus ring; for affinoids this comparison
fixes the supplied `toPresentationLimit` sections, and for arbitrary opens it commutes with
restriction. The sharp map, pullbacks, integral conditions and the Čech and cohomology statements
below are stated on these canonical carriers. `globalPullback_chart` fixes pullback on chart maps.
`tiltChart` uses the tilted inclusion, and `globalSharp_chart` applies sharp to the
corresponding tilted chart component. `globalSharp_naturality` includes restriction to
opens, and `globalSharp_plus` gives the integral map.

**Checks for global sections and sharp.** `global_sections_empty` gives the zero ring;
`global_sections_affinoid` recovers the affinoid ring; `global_plus_inverse_parameter`
excludes the inverse parameter while `global_plus_two_integral_terms` includes a sum of
integral elements. `global_sharp_zero_one` computes zero and one,
`global_sharp_two_factors` computes a product, and `global_sharp_nonadditive` at `p = 2`
compares sharp of `1 + 1 = 0` on the tilt with `1 + 1 ≠ 0` on a characteristic-zero chart.
`global_pullback_identity`, `global_pullback_composition` and
`global_pullback_affine_two_terms` fix the contravariant convention.

### P2.12 the tilting equivalence of perfectoid spaces

The tilting equivalence of perfectoid spaces: the slice equivalence over a perfectoid base, its
affinoid form, and the completed tensor products and affinoid fibre products that it is compatible
with.

**Tilting equivalence of perfectoid spaces: `Perfd/X ≃ Perf/X♭`.** (*tilting-slice-equivalence*) Let
`X` be a perfectoid space with tilt `X♭` (*perfectoid-spaces-and-glued-tilting*; any characteristic,
no perfectoid base field). (a) The functor `Perfd/X → Perf/X♭ = Perfd/X♭` on slice categories
(Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Over`), `(f : Y → X) ↦ (f♭ : Y♭ → X♭)`, is an equivalence of categories (a
Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Equivalence`). (b) It commutes with restriction to open subspaces of `X`, and
a perfectoid space `Y` over `X` is affinoid perfectoid iff `Y♭` is; for `X = Spa(A, A⁺)` it restricts
on affinoid perfectoid spaces to the equivalence of
*affinoid-perfectoid-pairs-tilting-equivalence*. (c) Untilts over `X`: for every perfectoid space
`T` of characteristic `p` and every morphism `g : T → X♭` there are a perfectoid space `T♯` with a
morphism `T♯ → X` and an isomorphism `ι : (T♯)♭ ≅ T` over `X♭`, and the pair `(T♯ → X, ι)` is unique
up to unique isomorphism; so `Hom_Perf(T, X♭)` is in natural bijection with isomorphism classes of
such pairs, functorially in `T`. (d) Under the homeomorphisms `|Y| ≅ |Y♭|` the structure maps
correspond. Unit and counit are isomorphisms compatible with restriction to open subspaces of `X`.
The quasi-inverse depends on `X`: there is no quasi-inverse to tilting that recovers every untilt without a chosen
base (`tilt_not_injective_on_iso_classes`) ([ECD] §3, Cor. 3.20, p. 19, statement (a) over an
arbitrary perfectoid base; [Berkeley] Lecture 7, §7.1, Thm 7.1.4, printed pp. 49–50; [Sch12] §6,
Prop. 6.17, p. 38, the field case; [Bhatt] §9.3, Thm 9.3.10(2), printed p. 111). Sch12
Proposition 6.17 is the case `X = Spa(K, K⁺₀)` for a perfectoid field `K`,
where `K⁺₀` is the smallest ring of integral elements (P2.19)
(see *perfectoid-spaces-over-a-perfectoid-field-comparison*). For `X = Spa(ℚ_p^cycl, ℤ_p^cycl)`, the
perfectoid disc over `𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞}))` untilts to `Spa(ℚ_p^cycl⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, ℤ_p^cycl⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩)`,
and `Spa(𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞})))` itself (with the identity to `X♭`) untilts to `X`. *Needs:*
*perfectoid-spaces-and-glued-tilting*; *affinoid-perfectoid-basis*;
*open-subspaces-of-perfectoid-spaces*; *affinoid-perfectoid-pairs-tilting-equivalence*; Mathlib
`CategoryTheory.Over`, `CategoryTheory.Equivalence`.

**Tilting is an equivalence between perfectoid Tate pairs over `(A, A⁺)` and over `(A♭, A♭⁺)`,
compatible with rational localisation.** (*affinoid-perfectoid-pairs-tilting-equivalence*) Let
`(A, A⁺)` be a complete perfectoid Tate pair (`A` perfectoid Tate ring, `A⁺ ⊆ A°` a ring of integral
elements; no perfectoid base field) with tilt `(A♭, A♭⁺)`. Let `Perfd_{(A,A⁺)}` be the category of
complete perfectoid Tate pairs `(B, B⁺)` with a morphism of Huber pairs `(A, A⁺) → (B, B⁺)`,
morphisms being morphisms of Huber pairs under `(A, A⁺)`, and define `Perfd_{(A♭,A♭⁺)}` likewise.
The tilting equivalence of perfectoid `A`-algebras, with quasi-inverse the untilt along a
generator `ξ` of `ker(θ : W(A♭°) → A°)`, is P1.27 (*tilting-equivalence-and-explicit-tilt*); what
is proved here is its form for pairs under an arbitrary `(A, A⁺)` and its compatibility with
rational localisation: the tilt `(B, B⁺) ↦ (B♭, B♭⁺)` is an equivalence
`Perfd_{(A,A⁺)} ≃ Perfd_{(A♭,A♭⁺)}` (plus rings correspond by *rings-of-integral-elements-under-tilting*,
P1.18), with quasi-inverse sending `(S, S⁺)` to the untilt `(W(S⁺)[[ϖ♭]⁻¹]/ξ, W(S⁺)/ξ)` along a
generator `ξ` of `ker(θ : W(A♭⁺) → A⁺)`, `ϖ♭ ∈ A♭` a pseudouniformiser (ECD Lemma 3.14 and Theorem
3.17; layer P1); it carries rational localisations to rational localisations: for `f_1, …, f_n, g ∈ B♭`
generating the unit ideal, `(B⟨f♯/g♯⟩)♭ ≅ B♭⟨f/g⟩` over `B♭`, and every rational localisation of `B`
arises so; and that through `Spa` (see *affinoid-perfectoid-space*) it gives an equivalence between
affinoid perfectoid spaces over `Spa(A, A⁺)` and over `Spa(A♭, A♭⁺)`, compatible with the tilting
homeomorphisms ([ECD] §3, Thm 3.13 and its proof, p. 17, the general-base tilting equivalence of
rings, upgraded here to pairs under `(A, A⁺)`, and Thm 3.17, p. 18, the explicit quasi-inverse;
[AWS] §2.3, Rem. 2.3.17, p. 56, the relative equivalence over an arbitrary perfectoid base;
[Sch12] §6, Lem. 6.2, p. 30, the field case with plus rings). For `(A, A⁺) = (K, K°)` a perfectoid
field this is Scholze's Lemma 6.2 (for pairs whose plus ring contains `K°`); for
`(A, A⁺) = (ℚ_p^cycl, ℤ_p^cycl)`, `(𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞}))⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, 𝔽_p[[t^{1/p^∞}]]⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩)`
untilts to `(ℚ_p^cycl⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, ℤ_p^cycl⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩)`. *Needs:* *affinoid-perfectoid-space*;
*rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids*; layer P1 (P1.6, P1.19, P1.27); Tau Ceti
`TauCeti.Huber.Pair`, `TauCeti.Huber.Pair.Hom`.

`PerfectoidSpace.sliceTiltFunctor` sends an arrow and its commuting triangles to their
tilts; `sliceTiltFunctor_isEquivalence` gives the equivalence of slices in `Perfd`.
Every space mapping to the characteristic-p base has characteristic p, giving the stated
`Perf` slice. Pair-level tilting is already `Perfectoid.PairCat.sliceTiltingEquivalence`
in P1, with its specified `sliceTiltFunctor`; no second pair equivalence is defined here.
**Checks.** `slice_identity` computes the terminal arrow; `slice_affinoid_arrow` fixes the
forward arrow; `slice_fibre_product` compares a product in the slice. The P1 Checks
`slice_base`, `slice_characteristic_p_ideal` and `slice_zero_target` retain the base-marked
untilt and zero-ring tests.

### P2.13 completed tensor products of perfectoid pairs

**Completed tensor products of perfectoid Tate pairs are perfectoid, uniform, and commute with
tilting.** (*completed-tensor-of-perfectoid-is-perfectoid*) Let `(A, A⁺) → (B, B⁺)` and
`(A, A⁺) → (C, C⁺)` be morphisms of complete Hausdorff Huber pairs (Tau Ceti `Huber.Pair.Hom`) with
`A, B, C` perfectoid Tate rings (ECD Definition 3.1; any characteristic; no perfectoid base field).
Both maps are adic (AdicSpacesPartII R0.1 (*adic-ring-homomorphism*)), so the completed tensor
product
`(D, D⁺) = B ⊗̂_A C` with `inl, inr` (AdicSpacesPartII R0.3 (*completed-tensor-product*); `D⁺`
the closure of the integral closure of the image of
`B⁺ ⊗_{A⁺} C⁺`) is defined. Then: (i) `D` is a perfectoid Tate ring; in particular `D` is uniform and
the uniformisation `D → B ⊗̂ᵘ_A C` (AdicSpacesPartII R0.4 (*uniform-completed-tensor-product*))
is an isomorphism (the tensor-product norm is the
spectral norm, [KL16] §3.3, Thm 3.3.13(b), p. 62); (ii) `(D, D⁺)` with `inl, inr` is a pushout of
`(B, B⁺) ← (A, A⁺) → (C, C⁺)` in the category of complete perfectoid Tate pairs — given (i), this
is the universal property of AdicSpacesPartII R0.3
(*completed-tensor-product-universal-property*,
for complete Hausdorff targets with closed integrally closed plus ring) restricted to perfectoid
targets; (iii) tilting
commutes with it: there is a unique isomorphism of Huber pairs
`(D♭, D♭⁺) ≅ (B♭, B♭⁺) ⊗̂_{(A♭, A♭⁺)} (C♭, C♭⁺)` whose composites with `inl♭, inr♭` are the structure maps of `B♭ ⊗̂_{A♭} C♭`
([AWS] §2.4, Thm 2.4.1, p. 57; [KL16] Thm 3.3.13(a)); (iv) for a pseudouniformiser `ϖ = (ϖ♭)♯ ∈ A`
with `ϖ^p | p` in `A°` and compatible `p`-power roots (layer P1, P1.3), the `ϖ`-adic completion `F̂`
of the image `F` of `B° ⊗_{A°} C°` in `B ⊗_A C` satisfies `ϖ^{1/p^n} D° ⊆ F̂ ⊆ D°` for all `n`, and
the `ϖ`-power torsion of `B° ⊗_{A°} C°` is killed by every `ϖ^{1/p^n}`; so `F̂ → D°` is an almost
isomorphism (layer P1), which over a perfectoid field `K` (the case `A = K`) is Scholze's
statement that `B°ᵃ ⊗̂_{A°ᵃ} C°ᵃ` is a perfectoid `K°ᵃ`-algebra ([Sch12] §6, proof of Prop. 6.18,
p. 38, the affinoid formula and the plus-ring convention). The perfectoid base `A` is essential:
`ℂ_p ⊗̂_{ℚ_p} ℂ_p` is not uniform (recorded in AdicSpacesPartII R0.4
(*uniform-completed-tensor-product*)) ([KL16] §3.3, Rem. 3.3.14, p. 62: the earlier
`ℚ_p`-version [KL15] §3.6, Prop. 3.6.11, p. 92, had an incomplete proof, repaired by
Thm 3.3.13). The perfectoidness target for `B ⊗̂_A C` uses `IsAdicHom` for both structure maps,
provided by AdicSpacesPartII R0.1 (*adic-ring-homomorphism*).
`B ⊗̂_A A⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ ≅ B⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩` for every perfectoid Tate pair `(B, B⁺)` under
`(A, A⁺)`, compatibly with tilting, so `A⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ ⊗̂_A A⟨S^{1/p^∞}⟩ ≅ A⟨T^{1/p^∞}, S^{1/p^∞}⟩`;
for a finite Galois extension `L/K` of perfectoid fields with group `G`, `L ⊗̂_K L ≅ ∏_{g ∈ G} L`
(already `L ⊗_K L ≅ ∏_G L` algebraically, and the product is complete), a perfectoid Tate ring
that is not a field; that `L` is itself perfectoid is layer P3 (P3.7), cited for the example only
and not an input to this target. *Needs:* AdicSpacesPartII layer
R0 (*adic-ring-homomorphism*, *completed-tensor-product*,
*completed-tensor-product-universal-property*, *uniformization*, *uniform-completed-tensor-product*:
the completed tensor product); *perfect-uniform-completed-tensor*;
*tilting-homeomorphism-and-rational-subsets*; layer P1 (P1.3, P1.6, P1.27); layer P0 (P0.5,
P0.16); Tau Ceti `TauCeti.Huber.Pair`, `TauCeti.Huber.Pair.Hom`,
`TauCeti.Huber.Pair.isRingOfIntegralElements_integralClosure`; Mathlib `UniformSpace.Completion`,
`integralClosure`.

**Characteristic p: the completed tensor product of perfect complete Tate rings is perfect,
uniform and perfectoid.** (*perfect-uniform-completed-tensor*) Let `(A, A⁺) → (B, B⁺)` and
`(A, A⁺) → (C, C⁺)` be morphisms of complete Hausdorff Huber pairs with `A, B, C` perfectoid Tate
rings of characteristic `p`, equivalently perfect complete Tate rings (ECD Proposition 3.5). Both
maps are adic (AdicSpacesPartII R0.1 (*adic-ring-homomorphism*)), so `(D, D⁺) = B ⊗̂_A C` of
AdicSpacesPartII R0.3 (*completed-tensor-product*) is defined. Let `ϖ ∈ A` be a
pseudouniformiser, `F ⊆ B ⊗_A C` the image of `B° ⊗_{A°} C°` (a ring of definition for R0's
topology, because `ϖB° ⊆ B⁺ ⊆ B°` and likewise for `C`) and `F̂ ⊆ D` its `ϖ`-adic completion.
Prove: (i) `D` and `F̂` are perfect rings; (ii) `D` is a perfect complete Tate ring, hence uniform
and perfectoid, and the uniformisation `D → B ⊗̂ᵘ_A C` (AdicSpacesPartII R0.4
(*uniform-completed-tensor-product*)) is an isomorphism; (iii)
`ϖ^{1/p^n} D° ⊆ F̂ ⊆ D°` for all `n ≥ 0`, so `ϖD° ⊆ F̂` and `F̂ → D°` is injective with cokernel
killed by every `ϖ^{1/p^n}`, an almost isomorphism for the almost setup of `A` (layer P1); (iv) the
`ϖ`-power torsion of `B° ⊗_{A°} C°` is killed by every `ϖ^{1/p^n}` ([KL15] §3.1, Rem. 3.1.6(c),
p. 67, (i)–(ii) for perfect uniform Banach rings, perfectness being what makes the completed tensor
product uniform; [Bhatt] §9.3, proof of Cor. 9.3.13, printed p. 111; [Sch12] §6, proof of
Prop. 6.18, p. 38, statement (iv)). For a perfectoid field `K` of characteristic `p`,
`K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ ⊗̂_K K⟨S^{1/p^∞}⟩ = K⟨T^{1/p^∞}, S^{1/p^∞}⟩` with `F̂ = K°⟨T^{1/p^∞}, S^{1/p^∞}⟩`;
without perfectness the conclusion fails: `𝔽_p((t))⟨T⟩ ⊗̂_{𝔽_p((t))} 𝔽_p((t))⟨S⟩` is uniform but not
perfect. *Needs:* AdicSpacesPartII R0.1, R0.3, R0.4 (*adic-ring-homomorphism*, *completed-tensor-product*,
*uniformization*, *uniform-completed-tensor-product*); layer P1; Tau Ceti
`TauCeti.Huber.Pair.Hom`, `TauCeti.Huber.powerBoundedSubring`; Mathlib `PerfectRing`,
`Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeft`, `UniformSpace.Completion`.

`Perfectoid.PairCat.tensorPair` uses the supplied completed tensor ring and plus pair,
with scalar structures determined by the given pair morphisms. `tensorInclusions_spec`
identifies the inclusions with the actual pure tensors. `tensorPair_isPushout` supplies
the pair-level universal property; `tensorTiltIso_inclusions` identifies both tilted
inclusions under the tensor comparison.
**Checks.** `tensor_pair_zero`, `tensor_pair_identity` and `tensor_pair_two_inclusions`
test a zero factor, an identity base change and equality of the two base images.
`tensor_tilt_zero`, `tensor_tilt_two_constants` and `tensor_tilt_left_coordinate` test the
zero tensor, zero and one, and a coordinate from the left factor.

`PairCat.tensorPlusModel` is the closed image of the tensor of the *chosen* plus rings,
before integral closure. `tensorPlusModel_almost` states both containment in the supplied
completed-tensor plus ring and annihilation of its quotient by every parameter root.
`integral_tensor_torsion` states that parameter-power torsion in the algebraic integral
tensor is killed by each root; its two algebra structures are restrictions of the given
pair maps. **Checks.** `tensor_plus_model_zero` gives the zero factor,
`tensor_plus_model_identity` recovers the other plus ring under identity base change,
and `tensor_plus_model_inverse_parameter` excludes the inverse base parameter.
`tensor_affinoid_pullback` states the universal property of the specific tensor cone
against every Yoneda-adic space.

<a id="p2-14"></a>

### P2.14 the uniform completed tensor product over an arbitrary Tate ring

**The uniform completed tensor product of perfectoid rings over an arbitrary Tate ring is
perfectoid.** (*uniform-completed-tensor-of-perfectoid-over-any-base*) Let `(A, A⁺)` be a complete
Hausdorff Huber pair with `A` a Tate ring (not necessarily perfectoid, uniform or of characteristic
`p`), and let `(A, A⁺) → (B, B⁺)`, `(A, A⁺) → (C, C⁺)` be morphisms of Huber pairs with `B, C`
perfectoid Tate rings. Then the uniform completed tensor product `B ⊗̂ᵘ_A C` (AdicSpacesPartII layer
R0 (*uniform-completed-tensor-product*)) is a perfectoid Tate ring ([KL16] §3.3, Cor. 3.3.21, p. 66;
[KL15] §3.6, Cor. 3.6.18,
p. 96, over `ℚ_p`, where Kedlaya–Liu's `D` is the uniform completion of `B ⊗_A C` in the present notation). If `A` is perfectoid it equals
`B ⊗̂_A C` (*completed-tensor-of-perfectoid-is-perfectoid* (i)); otherwise `B ⊗̂_A C` need not be
uniform (`ℂ_p ⊗̂_{ℚ_p} ℂ_p` is not), and the uniformisation cannot be omitted ([KL15] §3.1,
Rem. 3.1.6(c), p. 67). For `B = C = ℚ_p^cycl` over `ℚ_p`, `ℚ_p^cycl ⊗̂ᵘ_{ℚ_p} ℚ_p^cycl` is a
perfectoid Tate ring over the non-perfectoid base `ℚ_p`; `ℂ_p ⊗̂ᵘ_{ℚ_p} ℂ_p` is perfectoid although
`ℂ_p ⊗̂_{ℚ_p} ℂ_p` is not uniform. *Needs:* AdicSpacesPartII R0.4 (*uniformization*,
*uniform-completed-tensor-product*: the spectral
seminorm, uniformisation and the uniform completed tensor product);
*completed-tensor-of-perfectoid-is-perfectoid*; *perfectoid-dense-image-criterion*; layer P1 (P1.5,
P1.30); Tau Ceti `TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing`, `TauCeti.Huber.Pair.Hom`.

**A uniform Tate ring receiving a dense-image map from a perfectoid ring is perfectoid.**
(*perfectoid-dense-image-criterion*) Let `f : A → B` be a continuous ring homomorphism with dense
image from a perfectoid Tate ring `A` to a complete Hausdorff uniform Tate ring `B` (`B°` bounded).
Prove that `B` is a perfectoid Tate ring and that `f♭ : A♭ → B♭` has dense image ([AWS] §2.8,
Lem. 2.8.4, p. 70, and §2.4, Thm 2.4.3(a), p. 58; [KL16] §3.3, Thm 3.3.18(ii), p. 64, the class of
morphisms along which the perfectoid property transfers; [KL15] §3.6, Thm 3.6.17(b), p. 95, over
`ℚ_p`). Uniformity of `B` is a hypothesis: `K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ → K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩/(T)` (closure of the
ideal) is surjective, but the target is not reduced, hence not uniform and not perfectoid
([AWS] §2.4, Ex. 2.4.9, p. 59). If `B` is the completed residue field of a point of `Spa(A, A⁺)`,
a uniform nonarchimedean field receiving a dense-image map from the completed colimit of rational
localisations, `B` is perfectoid (Kedlaya AWS Corollary 2.5.7, second proof); the uniformisation of
`B ⊗̂_A C` with `B, C` perfectoid receives a dense-image map from a perfectoid ring
(see *uniform-completed-tensor-of-perfectoid-over-any-base*). *Needs:* layer P1 (P1.1, P1.19); Tau Ceti
`TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing`, `TauCeti.Huber.powerBoundedSubring`, `TauCeti.Huber.IsBounded`.

The additional targets are the perfectoidness of the uniform completed tensor product,
`isPerfectoid_of_denseRange` and `denseRange_tiltMap`. The first allows an arbitrary Tate
base and uses the supplied `Uniformization (CompletedTensor A B C)`.
`tensorIntegralModel` is the closure of the subring generated by the two power-bounded
images under the actual completed tensor inclusions. `tensorIntegralModel_almost` bounds
it between all root-scaled copies of `D°` and `D°`; it does not replace integral closure by
an equality. `completedTensor_frobenius_bijective` uses `p = 0` in both factors and allows
the zero tensor ring.

**Checks for tensor conventions and integral models.** `tensor_inclusion_two_terms` computes
`b ⊗ c = inl(b) inr(c)`; `tensor_integral_two_inclusions` includes `b ⊗ 1 + 1 ⊗ c`;
`tensor_integral_zero` gives the whole zero ring; `tensor_integral_unbounded_scalar` excludes
`ϖ⁻¹` in a nonzero tensor. `tensor_plus_zero` computes the zero plus ring,
`uniform_tensor_zero` the zero uniform tensor, and `tensor_uniformization_perfectoid_base`
identifies ordinary and uniform completion over a perfectoid base.

### P2.15 affinoid perfectoid fibre products

**Affinoid perfectoid fibre products: `Spa(B ⊗̂_A C)` is a fibre product in adic spaces, compatible
with open subspaces.** (*perfectoid-fibre-product-universal-property*) Let `X = Spa(A, A⁺)`,
`Y = Spa(B, B⁺)`, `Z = Spa(C, C⁺)` be affinoid perfectoid spaces (any characteristic, no base field)
and `Y → X ← Z` morphisms, corresponding ([Wedhorn] Prop. 8.25) to morphisms of complete perfectoid
Tate pairs `(A, A⁺) → (B, B⁺)` and `(A, A⁺) → (C, C⁺)`. Let `(D, D⁺) = B ⊗̂_A C`, a complete
perfectoid Tate pair (see *completed-tensor-of-perfectoid-is-perfectoid*), hence sheafy
(see *perfectoid-stably-uniform-and-sheafy*). Then (a) `W = Spa(D, D⁺)` with `p = Spa(inl)` and
`q = Spa(inr)` is a fibre product `Y ×_X Z` in AdicSpaces' category of adic spaces (a Mathlib
`IsPullback` square there, against all adic spaces `T`, not only perfectoid ones), hence in `Perfd`,
and `W` is affinoid perfectoid; this is AdicSpacesPartII R0.7 (*affinoid-fibre-product*,
affinoid fibre products)
with its sheafiness hypothesis discharged; (b) for rational subsets `U' ⊆ X`, `U ⊆ Y`, `V ⊆ Z` with
`U` and `V` mapping into `U'`, the open `p⁻¹(U) ∩ q⁻¹(V) ⊆ W` is a rational subset and equals
`Spa(O_Y(U) ⊗̂_{O_X(U')} O_Z(V)) = U ×_{U'} V` (AdicSpacesPartII R0.3
(*completed-tensor-rational-localisation*)); (c) for arbitrary open subspaces `U ⊆ Y`,
`V ⊆ Z`, the open subspace `p⁻¹(U) ∩ q⁻¹(V)` with the restricted projections is a fibre product
`U ×_X V` in adic spaces; (d) the map `|W| → |Y| ×_{|X|} |Z|` is surjective (AdicSpacesPartII layer
R0 (*fibre-product-points*)) and not
injective in general ([Sch12] §6, proof of Prop. 6.18, p. 38, the universal property over a
perfectoid field; [AWS] §2.4, before Thm 2.4.1, p. 57, why the perfectoid case discharges the
sheafiness hypothesis; [ECD] §8, Prop. 8.3, p. 41, stability of affinoid perfectoid spaces under
fibre products). `Spa(K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩) ×_{Spa K} Spa(K⟨S^{1/p^∞}⟩) ≅ Spa(K⟨T^{1/p^∞}, S^{1/p^∞}⟩)` for
every perfectoid Tate ring `K`, with `{|T| ≤ |ϖ|} × {|S| ≤ |ϖ|}` corresponding to
`Spa(K⟨(T/ϖ)^{1/p^∞}, (S/ϖ)^{1/p^∞}⟩)`. *Needs:* *completed-tensor-of-perfectoid-is-perfectoid*;
*affinoid-perfectoid-space*; *perfectoid-stably-uniform-and-sheafy*;
*rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids*; AdicSpacesPartII R0.1, R0.3, R0.7
(*adic-ring-homomorphism*, *completed-tensor-rational-localisation*, *affinoid-fibre-product*,
*fibre-product-points*); Mathlib `CategoryTheory.IsPullback`; Tau Ceti
`TauCeti.Huber.Pair.Hom.spaComap`,
`TauCeti.Huber.Pair.Hom.spaComap_preimage_rationalSubset`.

### P2.16 fibre products of perfectoid spaces

Fibre products of perfectoid spaces: over a perfectoid base in all adic spaces, over an analytic
base in `Perfd`, absolute products in `Perf`, and the comparison with Scholze's category over a
perfectoid field.

**Fibre products of perfectoid spaces exist in adic spaces and are perfectoid.**
(*fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces*) Let `f : Y → X` and `g : Z → X` be morphisms of perfectoid
spaces (any characteristic; no perfectoid base field). The fibre product `W = Y ×_X Z` exists in
AdicSpaces' category of adic spaces and is a perfectoid space; with its projections `p : W → Y`,
`q : W → Z` it is therefore also a fibre product in `Perfd`, `Perfd` has all fibre products (Mathlib
`HasPullbacks`), and the inclusion `Perfd ⥤ AdicSpace` preserves them. Construction: `W` is glued
(AdicSpaces layer 5.3) from the affinoid perfectoid spaces
`W_{U,U',V} = Spa(O_Y(U) ⊗̂_{O_X(U')} O_Z(V)) = U ×_{U'} V`
(see *perfectoid-fibre-product-universal-property*), for affinoid perfectoid opens `U' ⊆ X`,
`U ⊆ f⁻¹(U')`, `V ⊆ g⁻¹(U')`, along their common open subspaces, which are fibre products of the
intersections (open compatibility (c) there). Conventions: the affinoid formula uses
AdicSpacesPartII R0.3 (*completed-tensor-product*)
with plus ring the closure of the integral closure of the image of `O_Y⁺(U) ⊗ O_Z⁺(V)`, which is
almost, but not in general exactly, the completed tensor product of the plus rings
(see *completed-tensor-plus-ring-almost-formula*); the ring is already uniform, so no uniformisation is
performed. Affinoid perfectoid spaces and `Perf` are closed under fibre products; tilting commutes
with them (see *tilting-commutes-with-fibre-products*); `|W| → |Y| ×_{|X|} |Z|` is surjective but not
injective in general. Over a perfectoid field this is Sch12 Proposition 6.18; fibre products over a
non-perfectoid analytic base are *fibre-products-over-analytic-base*, and absolute products in
`Perf` are *products-in-perf* ([Sch12] §6, Prop. 6.18, p. 38, and the paragraph before it, p. 38,
where fibre products of general adic spaces exist only under finiteness hypotheses (Huber's
Proposition 1.2.2; AdicSpacesPartII R0.7 (*fibre-products-existence*)); [Berkeley] Lecture 8,
Prop. 8.2.5(3), printed p. 59,
existence over no base field; [Bhatt] §9.3, Cor. 9.3.13, printed p. 111, the field case with the
reduction to characteristic `p`). In `PerfectoidSpace`, define `pullback` as the fibre product
`W = Y ×_X Z` in `Perfd`; prove `pullback.fst` and `pullback.snd` (the projections `p`, `q`),
`pullback.condition` (`p ≫ f = q ≫ g`), `pullback.lift` (for an adic space `T`, not necessarily
perfectoid, with `a : T → Y`, `b : T → Z`, `a ≫ f = b ≫ g`, the unique `T → Y ×_X Z`, with
the projection equations and uniqueness from `pullback.isPullback_toAdicSpace`; for perfectoid
`T`, use Mathlib's `CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.lift_fst`, `.lift_snd` and `.hom_ext`),
`hasPullbacks` (instance `HasPullbacks Perfd`),
`pullback.isPullback_toAdicSpace` (the image square in adic spaces is an `IsPullback` square; the
inclusion preserves pullbacks, and `W` agrees with any fibre product of adic spaces of
AdicSpacesPartII R0.7 (*fibre-products-existence*) that
exists for the same diagram), `pullbackSpaIso`
(`Spa(B, B⁺) ×_{Spa(A, A⁺)} Spa(C, C⁺) ≅ Spa(B ⊗̂_A C)` over the projections, with R0's plus ring),
`pullback.isAffinoidPerfectoid` (instance), `pullbackRestrictIso`
(`p⁻¹(U) ∩ q⁻¹(V) ≅ U ×_X V` for open `U ⊆ Y`, `V ⊆ Z`), `pullback_points`
(`|Y ×_X Z| → |Y| ×_{|X|} |Z|` surjective, AdicSpacesPartII R0.7 (*fibre-product-points*)),
`Perf.hasPullbacks` (`Perf` closed under fibre
products; `HasPullbacks Perf`), binary products in `Perfd/X` (given by
fibre products, Mathlib `Over.ConstructProducts.over_binaryProduct_of_pullback`) and
`pullbackTiltIso` (`(Y ×_X Z)♭ ≅ Y♭ ×_{X♭} Z♭` over the tilted projections,
*tilting-commutes-with-fibre-products*). *Needs:* *perfectoid-fibre-product-universal-property*;
*perfectoid-space*; *affinoid-perfectoid-basis*; *completed-tensor-plus-ring-almost-formula*;
AdicSpacesPartII R0.6, R0.7 (*adic-morphism*, *fibre-product-points*); Mathlib
`CategoryTheory.Limits.HasPullbacks`,
`CategoryTheory.IsPullback`, `CategoryTheory.Over.ConstructProducts.over_binaryProduct_of_pullback`.

**Checks.**

- `pullback_perfectedDiscs` (computation) — for a perfectoid Tate ring `R`:
  `Spa(R⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, R⁺⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩) ×_{Spa(R, R⁺)} Spa(R⟨S^{1/p^∞}⟩, R⁺⟨S^{1/p^∞}⟩) ≅ Spa(R⟨T^{1/p^∞}, S^{1/p^∞}⟩, R⁺⟨T^{1/p^∞}, S^{1/p^∞}⟩)` over the two projections.
- `pullback_galois_points` (computation) — for a finite Galois extension `L/K` of perfectoid fields
  with group `G`, `Spa(L, L°) ×_{Spa(K, K°)} Spa(L, L°) ≅ ⊔_{g ∈ G} Spa(L, L°)` has `|G|` points
  while `|Spa L| ×_{|Spa K|} |Spa L|` is one point: the underlying space of a fibre product is not
  the fibre product of underlying spaces.
- `pullback_id` (degenerate) — `Y ×_X X ≅ Y` via `p`, for the identity of `X`; and `Y ×_X ∅ = ∅`.
- `pullback_plus_ne_completedTensor_plus` (non-example) — for `K` the completion of
  `ℚ̆_p(μ_{p^∞})` and `L = K(p^{1/ℓ})` (`ℓ` a prime not dividing `p(p − 1)`), the plus ring of
  `Spa L ×_{Spa K} Spa L` is `(L°)^ℓ`, which strictly contains the image of `L° ⊗_{K°} L°`
  (*completed-tensor-of-perfectoid-is-perfectoid* (iv)). The example states the strict
  inclusion for every nontrivial finite Galois extension of complete normed perfectoid fields
  whose automorphisms act trivially on residue classes; `tame_cubic_perfectoid_extension`
  supplies the residue-characteristic-two instance. A construction using the completed tensor
  product of plus rings as plus ring produces a pair that is not a Huber pair.
- `pullback.isPullback_toAdicSpace` (compatibility) — the square `(W, p, q, f, g)` is a pullback
  (Mathlib `IsPullback`) in AdicSpaces' category of adic spaces, and on affinoid pieces the
  canonical map `Spa(B ⊗̂ᵘ_A C) → Spa(B ⊗̂_A C)` from AdicSpacesPartII R0.4
  (*uniform-completed-tensor-product*) is an isomorphism.
- `pullback_tilt` (characterisation) — for `Y → X ← Z` in `Perfd`, the fibre product of
  `Y♭ → X♭ ← Z♭` in `Perf` is `(Y ×_X Z)♭` with the tilted projections.

**The plus ring of a perfectoid completed tensor product: almost equal to the completed tensor
product of plus rings, but not equal.** (*completed-tensor-plus-ring-almost-formula*) In the
situation of *completed-tensor-of-perfectoid-is-perfectoid*, with `ϖ ∈ A` as there, prove: (i) the
`ϖ`-power torsion of `B⁺ ⊗_{A⁺} C⁺` is killed by every `ϖ^{1/p^n}`; (ii) the natural map from the
`ϖ`-adic completion `(B⁺ ⊗_{A⁺} C⁺)^∧` to `D⁺` has kernel and cokernel killed by every `ϖ^{1/p^n}`,
i.e. it is an almost isomorphism of `A⁺`-modules; (iii) `D⁺` is the `ϖ`-adic completion of the
integral closure in `B ⊗_A C` of the image of `B⁺ ⊗_{A⁺} C⁺`, and it contains `D°°` and
`ϖ^{1/p^n} D°` for all `n`. The map in (ii) is not an isomorphism in general (layer P3) ([Bhatt]
§9.3, Ex. 9.3.14, printed p. 112, part (ii) over a perfectoid field; [ECD] §3, Ex. 3.22(ii), p. 19,
used in (i); [AWS] §2.8, proof of Lem. 2.8.7, p. 71, whose claim holds only up to almost isomorphism
and after passing to the integral closure, as corrected here and in layer P3). Over a perfectoid
field `K` and `B = C = K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩` with plus rings `K°⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩`, the map of (ii) is an
isomorphism onto `K°⟨T^{1/p^∞}, S^{1/p^∞}⟩`. *Needs:*
*completed-tensor-of-perfectoid-is-perfectoid*; AdicSpacesPartII R0.3
(*completed-tensor-product*); layer P1; layer
P0; Mathlib `integralClosure`.

**Tilting commutes with fibre products of perfectoid spaces.**
(*tilting-commutes-with-fibre-products*) This is the space-level form of
*completed-tensor-of-perfectoid-is-perfectoid* (iii): for morphisms `Y → X ← Z` of perfectoid
spaces the tilts of the projections exhibit `(Y ×_X Z)♭` as the fibre product `Y♭ ×_{X♭} Z♭` in
`Perf` and in adic spaces, the canonical morphism `(Y ×_X Z)♭ → Y♭ ×_{X♭} Z♭` being, on affinoid
pieces, the isomorphism `(B ⊗̂_A C)♭ ≅ B♭ ⊗̂_{A♭} C♭` of P2.13 (iii), glued; more generally the tilting equivalence
`Perfd/X ≃ Perf/X♭` preserves every limit that exists in `Perfd/X` ([AWS] §2.4, Thm 2.4.1, p. 57,
the affinoid case; [ECD] §3, Cor. 3.20, p. 19, the equivalence whose limit preservation gives the
lemma). For `K` perfectoid, `(Spa K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ ×_{Spa K} Spa K⟨S^{1/p^∞}⟩)♭ ≅ Spa K♭⟨T^{1/p^∞}, S^{1/p^∞}⟩`; for `L/K` finite Galois of perfectoid fields,
`(Spa L ×_{Spa K} Spa L)♭ ≅ Spa L♭ ×_{Spa K♭} Spa L♭`, both `⊔_{g ∈ G}` of the tilt. *Needs:*
*tilting-slice-equivalence*; *fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces*;
*completed-tensor-of-perfectoid-is-perfectoid*; Mathlib
`CategoryTheory.Over.ConstructProducts.over_binaryProduct_of_pullback`,

ambient category of pre-adic spaces (and, through `YonedaAdicSpace.ofAdicSpace`, in the Yoneda-adic
category), and `tilt_preservesPullbacks` gives the tilted comparison.
`pullback_points` asserts surjectivity onto compatible pairs of valuation points.

### P2.17 fibre products over an analytic base

**Fibre products of perfectoid spaces over an analytic adic space, in Perfd, via uniform completed
tensor products.** (*fibre-products-over-analytic-base*) Let `S` be an analytic adic space
(AdicSpaces layer 5; every point analytic, e.g. `Spa(K, K⁺)` for any nonarchimedean field `K`, or
any rigid space) and `f : Y → S`, `g : Z → S` morphisms from perfectoid spaces. Then the fibre
product `Y ×_S Z` exists in `Perfd`: there is a perfectoid space `W` with morphisms `p : W → Y`,
`q : W → Z`, `f p = g q`, such that for every perfectoid space `T`,
`Hom(T, W) = Hom(T, Y) ×_{Hom(T, S)} Hom(T, Z)`. Affinoid-locally, for an open affinoid
`U' = Spa(A, A⁺) ⊆ S` with `A` a complete Tate ring (the analytic locus is covered by such,
AdicSpaces layer 2.3) and affinoid perfectoid `U ⊆ f⁻¹(U')`, `V ⊆ g⁻¹(U')`, the piece of `W` over
`U, V` is `Spa(O_Y(U) ⊗̂ᵘ_A O_Z(V))`, the uniform completed tensor product (AdicSpacesPartII layer
R0 (*uniform-completed-tensor-product*)), which is perfectoid (see
*uniform-completed-tensor-of-perfectoid-over-any-base*). If `S` is
perfectoid, `W` is the fibre product of *fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces* (in all adic spaces).
If `S` is not perfectoid, `W` is a fibre product in `Perfd` only: the test objects are uniform, the
completed tensor product itself need not be uniform (`ℂ_p ⊗̂_{ℚ_p} ℂ_p` is not) and its sheafiness
is not known. The diagonal `Y → Y ×_S Y` is defined ([KL16] §3.3, Cor. 3.3.21, p. 66, the affinoid
pieces over a non-perfectoid base are perfectoid; [KL15] §3.1, Rem. 3.1.6(c), p. 67, the
uniformisation cannot be omitted; [AWS] §2.4, before Thm 2.4.1, p. 57, why the universal property is
in `Perfd` only). For `K` a nonarchimedean field that is not perfectoid (e.g. `ℚ_p`) and perfectoid
spaces `Y, Z` over `Spa(K, K°)`, `Y ×_{Spa K} Z` is a perfectoid space, the fibre product used for
analytic separatedness in layer [P8](../PerfectoidTowers/README.md#layer-p8-finite-quotients-and-closed-perfectoid-loci-in-towers). In `PerfectoidSpace`, define `pullbackOverAnalytic` as the
perfectoid space `Y ×_S Z` in `Perfd` for `S` analytic; prove `pullbackOverAnalytic.fst` and `.snd`
(the projections), `pullbackOverAnalytic.condition` (`p ≫ f = q ≫ g` in adic spaces),
`pullbackOverAnalytic.lift` (for a perfectoid space `T` with `a : T → Y`, `b : T → Z`,
`a ≫ f = b ≫ g`, the unique `T → Y ×_S Z`, with both projection equations in
`pullbackOverAnalytic.lift_spec` and uniqueness in `pullbackOverAnalytic.isPullback`),
`pullbackOverAnalyticSpaIso` (`Spa(B) ×_{Spa A} Spa(C) ≅ Spa(B ⊗̂ᵘ_A C)` with `A` Tate),
`pullbackOverAnalyticIsoPullback` (if `S` is perfectoid, `pullbackOverAnalytic f g → pullback f g`
is an isomorphism), `pullbackOverAnalytic.isAffinoidPerfectoid` (instance: for `Y, Z` affinoid
perfectoid and `S` affinoid with Tate ring), `pullbackOverAnalyticRestrictIso` (for opens `U ⊆ Y`,
`V ⊆ Z`, `S' ⊆ S` with `f(U), g(V) ⊆ S'`: `p⁻¹(U) ∩ q⁻¹(V) ≅ U ×_{S'} V`), `diagonalOverAnalytic`
(`Δ : Y → Y ×_S Y = lift (𝟙 Y) (𝟙 Y)`, used for analytic separatedness in layer [P8](../PerfectoidTowers/README.md#layer-p8-finite-quotients-and-closed-perfectoid-loci-in-towers)) and
`pullbackOverAnalytic.surjective_points` (`|Y ×_S Z| → |Y| ×_{|S|} |Z|` is surjective: `Spa` of
the uniformisation is homeomorphic to `Spa` of the completed tensor product, AdicSpacesPartII layer
R0 (*uniformization*), property (d), and
valuations amalgamate, AdicSpacesPartII R0.7 (*valuation-amalgamation*)). *Needs:*
*uniform-completed-tensor-of-perfectoid-over-any-base*;
*fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces*; *completed-tensor-of-perfectoid-is-perfectoid*;
*perfectoid-fibre-product-universal-property*; *perfectoid-space*; AdicSpacesPartII R0.3, R0.4, R0.6, R0.7
(*completed-tensor-rational-localisation*, *uniformization*, *uniform-completed-tensor-product*,
*adic-iff-analytic-locus*, *valuation-amalgamation*).

**Checks.**

- `pullbackOverAnalytic_empty`, `pullbackOverAnalytic.fst_empty`, `pullbackOverAnalytic.snd_empty`, `pullbackOverAnalytic.lift_empty`: an empty factor gives an empty pullback.
- `pullbackOverAnalytic_perfectoid`, `pullbackOverAnalytic.fst_perfectoid`, `pullbackOverAnalytic.snd_perfectoid`, `pullbackOverAnalytic.lift_perfectoid`: over a perfectoid base the comparison with the perfectoid pullback preserves both projections.
- `pullbackOverAnalytic_identity`, `pullbackOverAnalytic.fst_identity`, `pullbackOverAnalytic.snd_identity`, `pullbackOverAnalytic.lift_identity`: the identity cospan has an invertible first projection and its diagonal lift composes to the identity.

- `diagonalOverAnalytic_identity`: the identity map has invertible diagonal.
- `diagonalOverAnalytic_empty`: an empty source has invertible diagonal.
- `diagonalOverAnalytic_two`: the fold from two copies of a nonempty affinoid has a noninvertible diagonal.

- `pullbackOverAnalytic_Cp_Qp` (non-example) — for `S = Spa(ℚ_p, ℤ_p)` and
  `Y = Z = Spa(ℂ_p, O_{ℂ_p})`, the affinoid piece is `Spa(ℂ_p ⊗̂ᵘ_{ℚ_p} ℂ_p)` and not
  `Spa(ℂ_p ⊗̂_{ℚ_p} ℂ_p)`: the completed tensor product is not uniform (Kedlaya–Liu I
  Remark 2.8.5), so a construction without uniformisation does not produce a perfectoid ring.
- `pullbackOverAnalytic_perfectoid` (compatibility) — if `S` is perfectoid,
  `pullbackOverAnalytic f g ≅ PerfectoidSpace.pullback f g` over `Y` and `Z`.
- `pullbackOverAnalytic_empty` (degenerate) — if `Y = ∅` then `Y ×_S Z = ∅`.
- `pullbackOverAnalytic_cyclotomic` (computation) — for `S = Spa(ℚ_p, ℤ_p)` and
  `Y = Z = Spa(ℚ_p^cycl, ℤ_p^cycl)`, `Y ×_S Z = Spa(ℚ_p^cycl ⊗̂ᵘ_{ℚ_p} ℚ_p^cycl)`, a perfectoid space
  mapping to `Y` by `p`; it is nonempty and its points surject onto `|Y| ×_{|S|} |Z|` (a point).

Analyticity of the base means locally the spectrum of a Tate pair ([Berkeley] Definition 4.3.2,
printed p. 33): AdicSpacesPartII R0.6's `AdicSpace.IsAnalytic` on adic spaces, which on
AdicEtaleGeometry's analytic carrier is `YonedaAdicSpace.IsAnalytic`.
`pullback_over_analytic` produces a perfectoid cone that is a limit against every
perfectoid test space, including a nonperfectoid analytic base.
**Checks.** `analytic_perfectoid` includes every perfectoid space; `analytic_empty` includes

### P2.18 absolute products in Perf

**Absolute products in Perf.** (*products-in-perf*) Let `X, Y` be perfectoid spaces of
characteristic `p`. The product `X × Y` exists in `Perf` ([Berkeley] Lecture 8, §8.3, Lem. 8.3.5
and Rem. 8.3.6, printed p. 61; [ECD] §11, proof of Prop. 11.4, p. 55, where products in `Perf` are
what the diamond theory needs). It is also the fibre product `X ×_{Spa(𝔽_p, 𝔽_p)} Y` in
AdicSpaces' category of adic spaces, over the discrete adic space `Spa(𝔽_p, 𝔽_p)`, which is not a
perfectoid (nor Tate, nor analytic) space; for nonempty `X`, the structure maps `X → Spa(𝔽_p, 𝔽_p)` are not adic, so
neither *fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces* nor AdicSpacesPartII R0.7
(*fibre-products-existence*) applies, and `Perf` has no
final object ([Berkeley] Rem. 8.3.6), so the absolute product is not a fibre product in `Perf`.
Affinoid charts: for `X = Spa(A, A⁺)`, `Y = Spa(B, B⁺)` affinoid perfectoid of characteristic `p`
with pseudouniformisers `ϖ ∈ A`, `ϖ' ∈ B`, and integers `m, n ≥ 1`, put `E = A ⊗_{𝔽_p} B`,
`u_m = (ϖ^m ⊗ 1)(1 ⊗ ϖ')⁻¹` and `v_n = (1 ⊗ ϖ'^n)(ϖ ⊗ 1)⁻¹` in `E`,
`D_{m,n} = (A° ⊗ B°)[u_m, v_n] ⊆ E`; topologise `E` so that `D_{m,n}` is open with the
`(ϖ ⊗ 1)`-adic topology (equal to the `(1 ⊗ ϖ')`-adic one, since `ϖ^m = u_m ϖ'` and `ϖ'^n = v_n ϖ`
in `D_{m,n}`); let `C_{m,n}` be the completion and `C⁺_{m,n}` the completion of the integral
closure in `E` of the image of `(A⁺ ⊗ B⁺)[u_m, v_n]`, an open integrally closed subring. Then
`(C_{m,n}, C⁺_{m,n})` is a complete perfectoid Tate pair (`C_{m,n}` is a perfect complete Tate
ring); a morphism of pairs `(C_{m,n}, C⁺_{m,n}) → (R, R⁺)` to a complete Huber pair with `R` Tate
is the same as morphisms `φ : (A, A⁺) → (R, R⁺)`, `ψ : (B, B⁺) → (R, R⁺)` with
`φ(ϖ)^m ψ(ϖ')⁻¹ ∈ R⁺` and `ψ(ϖ')^n φ(ϖ)⁻¹ ∈ R⁺`; for `m ≤ m'`, `n ≤ n'`, `Spa(C_{m,n})` is the
rational subset `{|u_m| ≤ 1, |v_n| ≤ 1}` of `Spa(C_{m',n'})`; and
`X × Y = ⋃_{m,n} Spa(C_{m,n}, C⁺_{m,n})`, glued along these rational open immersions (AdicSpaces
layer 5.3). For general `X, Y` the affinoid products glue. The plus ring must contain `u_m` and
`v_n`: the integral closure of the image of `A⁺ ⊗ B⁺` alone, as written in Berkeley's proof, is not
open ([Berkeley] Lecture 8, proof of Lem. 8.3.5, printed pp. 61–62, the chart construction, whose
plus ring is corrected here). The absolute product of two perfectoid fields need not be a point:
`Spa 𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞})) × Spa 𝔽_p((s^{1/p^∞}))` is the perfectoid punctured open unit disc
`{0 < |s| < 1}` over `𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞}))` ([ECD] proof of Prop. 11.4), the union of the perfectoid
annuli `{|t|^m ≤ |s| ≤ |t|^{1/n}}`, which is not quasi-compact and has infinitely many points. Here the open-disc notation
means this union of annuli (equivalently the strict radius condition at rank-one
generisations), not the literal inequality `|s| < 1` in every higher-rank value group. For
`X, Y ∈ Perf` over a common perfectoid `Z`, the canonical morphism `X ×_Z Y → X × Y` is not an
isomorphism in general: for `K = 𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞}))`, `Spa K ×_{Spa K} Spa K = Spa K` is a point,
while `Spa K × Spa K` is not. In `PerfectoidSpace.Perf`, `hasBinaryProducts_perf` supplies
`CategoryTheory.Limits.HasBinaryProducts (Perf p)`. Use Mathlib's `CategoryTheory.Limits.prod`
for `X × Y`, with `prod.fst`, `prod.snd` and `prod.lift` for the projections and the map
from `T ∈ Perf` determined by `a : T → X` and `b : T → Y`. The projection equations and
uniqueness are `CategoryTheory.Limits.prod.{lift_fst, lift_snd, hom_ext}`
in `Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Limits/Shapes/BinaryProducts/BinaryProducts.lean`.
Define `prodChart` as the complete perfectoid Tate pair `(C_{m,n}, C⁺_{m,n})` with its maps
from `(A, A⁺)` and `(B, B⁺)`. Its `ProductChart.universal` field identifies morphisms to
any complete Tate pair with pairs `(φ, ψ)` satisfying the two integrality conditions
([Berkeley] Lemma 8.3.5, proof, printed pp. 61–62). Prove
`prodChart_isRationalSubset` (for `m ≤ m'`, `n ≤ n'`, `Spa(C_{m,n}) → Spa(C_{m',n'})` is the
inclusion of `{|u_m| ≤ 1, |v_n| ≤ 1}`: the ring map `C_{m',n'} → C_{m,n}` fixes the maps
from `A` and `B`, is `CAff.IsRationalLocalization` for numerators `{1, u_m, v_n}` and
denominator `1`, and induces an open embedding with exactly this image; this includes
equal exponents and empty charts when an exponent is zero, [Berkeley] Lemma 8.3.5,
proof, printed pp. 61–62), `prodChartMap_cover` (for affinoid perfectoid `X, Y`,
`X × Y = ⋃_{m,n} Spa(C_{m,n}, C⁺_{m,n})`, an increasing union of affinoid perfectoid opens),
the pullback identification (`X × Y` is a pullback of `X → Spa(𝔽_p, 𝔽_p) ← Y` in adic spaces) and
`prodPerfectoidFieldsIso` (`Spa 𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞})) × Spa 𝔽_p((s^{1/p^∞})) ≅` the perfectoid punctured
open unit disc over `𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞}))`). *Needs:* *perfectoid-space*;
*characteristic-p-affinoid-perfectoid-criterion*; *fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces*;
*open-subspaces-of-perfectoid-spaces*; AdicSpacesPartII R0.2, R0.6 (*discrete-huber-pair-sheafy*,
*adic-iff-analytic-locus*); layer P1; Mathlib
`CategoryTheory.Limits.HasBinaryProducts`, `UniformSpace.Completion`,
`UniformSpace.Completion.extensionHom`, `integralClosure`; Tau Ceti `TauCeti.Huber.Pair`,
`TauCeti.Huber.IsRingOfIntegralElements`.

**Checks.**

- Computation: `Spa 𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞})) × Spa 𝔽_p((s^{1/p^∞})) ≅ {0 < |s| < 1} ⊆ Spa 𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞}))⟨s^{1/p^∞}⟩`, the union of the affinoid perfectoid annuli
  `Spa(C_{m,n}) = {|t|^m ≤ |s| ≤ |t|^{1/n}}`; the absolute product of two perfectoid fields is not
  a point and not quasi-compact.
- `absolute_product_empty` (degenerate) — `X × ∅ = ∅` for every `X ∈ Perf`.
- `not_isPerfectoidSpace_spa_Fp_final` (non-example) — `Spa(𝔽_p, 𝔽_p)` with the discrete topology
  is not an object of `Perf` (its point is not analytic), `Perf` has no final object (Berkeley

- `prodChart_plus_open` (non-example) — for `A = B = 𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞}))` with `ϖ = t`, `ϖ' = s`:

  `1 ⊗ s^j`: `A° ⊗ (B°/s^j)` is free over `A°`), so the integral closure of `A⁺ ⊗ B⁺` is not open in
  `E` and `(E, integral closure of A⁺ ⊗ B⁺)` is not a Huber pair; the plus ring must contain
  `u_m, v_n`.
- Compatibility: `X × Y` with its projections is a pullback of
  `X → Spa(𝔽_p, 𝔽_p) ← Y` in AdicSpaces' category of adic spaces, and it agrees with the absolute
  product of Berkeley Lemma 8.3.5.
- Characterisation: for morphisms `X → Spa K_t`, `Y → Spa K_s` with
  `K_t = 𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞}))`, `K_s = 𝔽_p((s^{1/p^∞}))` (which exist locally: `t^{1/p^n} ↦ ϖ^{1/p^n}`),

  `X → K`, `Y → L` in `Perf`, as in the example.

**Characteristic p: perfectoid spaces are adic spaces locally Spa of perfect Tate rings, and
affinoid perfectoid spaces are the affinoid ones.** (*characteristic-p-affinoid-perfectoid-criterion*)
Let `X` be an adic space with `p = 0` in `O_X(X)`. Prove: (i) `X` is a perfectoid space iff `X` is
covered by open subspaces isomorphic to `Spa(R, R⁺)` with `R` a perfect complete Tate ring; (ii) if
`X` is a perfectoid space, then `O_X(U)` is a perfect ring (Mathlib `PerfectRing (O_X(U)) p`) for
every open `U ⊆ X`; (iii) (Mihara) if `X ≅ Spa(A, A⁺)` for a complete Hausdorff sheafy Huber pair
`(A, A⁺)` with `A` Tate, and `X` is a perfectoid space, then `A` is perfect, hence a perfectoid Tate
ring, and `X` is affinoid perfectoid. The analogue of (iii) in characteristic `0` is not asserted:
whether an affinoid adic space that is a perfectoid space is affinoid perfectoid is recorded as
unclear in [Bhatt] §9.3, Rem. 9.3.11, printed p. 111 ([Bhatt] §9.3, Ex. 9.3.12 (Mihara), printed
p. 111, part (iii), proved by gluing `p`-th roots; [ECD] §3, Proposition 3.5, p. 15, perfect complete
Tate rings of characteristic `p` are perfectoid (uniformity is automatic); [AWS] §2.1, Ex. 2.1.2,
p. 49, for uniform pairs, used in (i) and (iii)). For
`A = 𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞}))⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩`, `Spa(A, A⁺)` is a perfectoid space and `A` is perfect; for
`A = 𝔽_p((t))⟨T⟩` (not perfect), `Spa(A, A°)` is not a perfectoid space, by (iii). *Needs:*
*perfectoid-space*; *affinoid-perfectoid-space*; *perfectoid-spaces-and-glued-tilting*; layer P1;
Mathlib `PerfectRing`.

### P2.19 perfectoid spaces over a perfectoid field

**Scholze's perfectoid spaces over a perfectoid field K are the perfectoid spaces over
`Spa(K, K⁺₀)`.** (*perfectoid-spaces-over-a-perfectoid-field-comparison*) Let `K` be a perfectoid
field (layer P1), `K°` its valuation ring and `K⁺₀ ⊆ K°` the smallest ring of integral elements of
`K`, the integral closure of `ℤ·1 + K°°` in `K` ([Wedhorn] §7.3, Rem. 7.15(2), p. 60); `K⁺₀ = K°`
iff the residue field of `K` is algebraic over `𝔽_p`. (i) Sch12's perfectoid `K`-algebras
(Definition 5.1) and perfectoid affinoid `K`-algebras (Definition 6.1) are the perfectoid Tate
rings, respectively complete perfectoid Tate pairs `(R, R⁺)`, with a continuous `K`-algebra
structure; no condition `K° ⊆ R⁺` is imposed ([Sch12] §2, Def. 2.6(ii), p. 8). (ii) Sch12's category
of perfectoid spaces over `K` ([Sch12] §6, Def. 6.15, p. 38: objects of Huber's category of triples
whose structure sheaf is a sheaf of complete topological `K`-algebras, locally affinoid perfectoid;
morphisms continuous `K`-linear; [Sch12] §2, before Def. 2.18, p. 10, adic spaces over `k` carry a
`k`-algebra structure, not a map to `Spa(k, k°)`) is equivalent to the slice category
`Perfd/Spa(K, K⁺₀)`: a morphism `X → Spa(K, K⁺₀)` is a continuous ring map `K → O_X(X)`
([Wedhorn] Prop. 8.25), and every such map sends `K⁺₀` into `O_X⁺(X)`, which contains all
topologically nilpotent elements and is integrally closed. The full subcategory `Perfd/Spa(K, K°)`
([Bhatt] §9.3, Def. 9.3.9, printed p. 111) consists of those `X` with `K° ⊆ O_X⁺(X)`; it is all of
Sch12's category when the residue field of `K` is algebraic over `𝔽_p` (e.g. `K = ℂ_p`, `ℚ_p^cycl`,
`𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞}))`), and a proper full subcategory otherwise. (iii) Sch12's tilt (Definition 6.16)
of `X` over `K` is the glued tilt `X♭` with its structure map to `Spa(K♭, K♭⁺₀)` (tilting preserves
the smallest ring of integral elements, ECD Lemma 3.11), and Sch12 Proposition 6.17 is
*tilting-slice-equivalence* for the base `Spa(K, K⁺₀)`: the functorial bijection
`Hom(Spa(R♭, R♭⁺), X♭) = Hom(Spa(R, R⁺), X)` over `K♭`, resp. `K`, holds. (iv) Sch12's fibre
products (Proposition 6.18) are those of *fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces*. For `K = ℂ_p`,
Sch12's perfectoid spaces over `ℂ_p` are the perfectoid spaces over `Spa(ℂ_p, O_{ℂ_p})`; for `K` the
completed perfection of `𝔽_p(x)((t))` and `R⁺` the preimage in `K°` of the valuation ring
`𝔽_p[x]^{perf}_{(x)}` of the residue field `𝔽_p(x)^{perf}`, `Spa(K, R⁺)` is a perfectoid space over
`K` in Sch12's sense with no morphism to `Spa(K, K°)`. *Needs:* *perfectoid-space*;
*tilting-slice-equivalence*; *fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces*; *affinoid-perfectoid-space*;
layer P1 (P1.1, P1.15); Tau Ceti
`TauCeti.Huber.IsRingOfIntegralElements.mem_of_isTopologicallyNilpotent`; Mathlib
`CategoryTheory.Over`.

`PerfectoidSpace.fieldMinimalPlus` is the integral closure of the subring generated by
the topologically nilpotent elements (which already contains the prime subring).
`fieldBasePair` bundles it. `FieldSpace` records a perfectoid space and a continuous scalar
map into its compatible global sections; continuity uses the subspace topology of the
product of chart rings. Morphisms preserve that map through `globalPullback`.
`fieldSpaceEquivalence_space` and `fieldSpaceEquivalence_scalar` fix the comparison with
the minimal-plus slice. `fieldSpace_maximalPlus_criterion` states the extra integrality
condition for the maximal-plus slice.
**Checks.** `field_minimal_topologically_nilpotent` includes topologically nilpotent scalars;
`field_minimal_inverse_parameter` excludes the inverse parameter;
`field_minimal_cyclotomic` and `field_minimal_cp` identify the minimal and maximal plus rings
in the two algebraic-residue examples. `field_category_empty`,
`field_category_scalar_two_terms` and `field_category_recovers_object` test the empty space,
the scalar addition law and recovery under the equivalence. The proper minimal-plus example uses `ResidueLaurentField`, the localization of the
`t`-adic completion of the monoid algebra over `RationalResiduePerfection`.
`residueValuationRing` is the valuation ring at `x=0`, specified by fractions with
denominator nonzero at zero and their compatible Frobenius roots.
`residueLaurentReduction_spec` fixes reduction on constants and its kernel of
topologically nilpotent elements. `mem_residueLaurentPlus` specifies the inverse
image of that residue valuation ring. `residueLaurentPlus_proper` proves this plus
ring is strictly smaller than the power-bounded ring and contains every
 topologically nilpotent element.

**Checks.** The ten definitions `RationalResiduePerfection`, `residueValuationRing`,
`ResidueLaurentPolynomial`, `residueLaurentMonomial`, `ResidueLaurentIntegral`,
`residueLaurentParameter`, `ResidueLaurentField`, `residueLaurentRoot`,
`residueLaurentReduction`, and `residueLaurentPlus` have shared examples:
`_roots` checks the root relation and the integral pseudouniformizers; `_zero`
checks reduction of zero and the nonzero nonunit integral parameter; `_proper`
puts `x` in the plus ring and `x⁻¹` in its power-bounded complement.

**Checks for the affinoid definitions.** The presentation notation `RationalLoc 𝔭`
abbreviates the carrier of `PairOfDefinition.completionLocObj`; `RationalLoc.pair` and `RationalLoc.structureMap`
bundle the supplier's plus ring and structure morphism. `IsTiltPresentation` means that
both numerator sets span the unit ideal and their rational subsets correspond under `spaTilt`.
The comparison `rationalLocalization.tiltEquiv_affinoid` satisfies
`rationalLocalization.tiltEquiv_affinoid_spec`: continuity in both directions,
equality of the transported plus rings, and commutation with the tilted structure map.
These conditions apply in every characteristic, including the zero-ring localization.

- `spaTilt_test_zero_one` — at any point, `|0| ≤ |1|` and not `|1| ≤ |0|`.
- `spaTilt_test_two_powers` — `|ϖ♭²| < |ϖ♭|`; this fixes the direction of `vle` using two powers.
- `spaTilt_test_charP_eq_id` — in characteristic `p`, transport by `tilt.equivOfCharP` gives the original point.
- `spaTilt_test_no_ringHom` — there is no unital ring map from the characteristic-`p` tilt of `ℚ_p^cycl` to `ℚ_p^cycl`.
- `spaTiltHomeomorph_test_empty`, `spaTiltHomeomorph_test_whole`,
  `spaTiltHomeomorph_test_charP` — the homeomorphism carries the empty and whole subsets
  to themselves and agrees with characteristic-`p` transport on points.
- `rationalLoc_test_empty` — denominator zero gives the zero ring, its full plus ring,
  and the zero structure map.
- `rationalLoc_test_whole` — the presentation `({1},1)` recovers `(R,R⁺)` as a topological
  pair, with the structure map inverse to the comparison.
- `rationalLoc_test_supplier` — the pair's plus ring is `completedPlusSubring` and its
  morphism is `toCompletionLoc`, exactly. Together these three Checks apply to
  `RationalLoc`, `RationalLoc.pair`, and `RationalLoc.structureMap`. The carrier equality
  with `completionLocObj` also holds by reflexivity, as does equality of
  `RationalLoc.instTopologicalSpace` with the supplied object's topology.
  `RationalLoc.instTopologicalSpace_empty`, `RationalLoc.instTopologicalSpace_whole`, and
  `RationalLoc.instTopologicalSpace_supplier` use these same three examples to check
  the zero ring, the homeomorphism for the whole space, and the supplied topology.
  The mirrored example labels for the carrier and pair bundles are
  `RationalLoc_empty`, `RationalLoc_whole`, `RationalLoc_supplier`,
  `RationalLoc.pair_empty`, `RationalLoc.pair_whole`, `RationalLoc.pair_supplier`,
  `RationalLoc.structureMap_empty`, `RationalLoc.structureMap_whole`, and
  `RationalLoc.structureMap_supplier`.
- `isTiltPresentation_test_whole`, `isTiltPresentation_test_empty`,
  `isTiltPresentation_test_mismatch` — `({1},1)` matches itself, `({1},0)` matches itself,
  and these two presentations cannot match each other on a nonempty spectrum.
- `tiltEquiv_test_zero_one`, `tiltEquiv_test_empty`, `rationalLocalization_test_charP` —
  the comparison sends `0,1` to `0,1`, sends every element to zero for two empty
  localizations, and agrees with the characteristic-`p` structure-map comparison.
- `cech_test_two_terms` — with `d⁰(a,b)=b−a`, `(2,5)` maps to `3`, `(5,2)` to `−3`,
  and the augmented section `(2,2)` to zero. This fixes the alternating Čech sign.
- `naiveModel_test_two_exponents` — at `p=2`, multiplication of `(T/ϖ)^{1/2}` by
  `ϖ^{1/2}` gives coefficient exponent `0`, whereas multiplication by `ϖ^{1/4}`
  gives exponent `−1/4`. The inequality `1−2^{-n}>1` never holds, so the family
  `1−p^{-n}>p^{-k}` in the naive-model Check requires `k≥1`.
- `almostExact_test_nonseparated` — on `ℚ_p`, `(p)=ℚ_p` and `⋂_n p^nℚ_p=ℚ_p`:
  reduction of `[ℚ_p→0]` is zero, but the complex has nonzero degree-zero cohomology.

The structure presheaf is the one supplied by Tau Ceti on the underlying `PreAdicSpace`
(`presentationLimitPresheafInCommRingCat`, with `presentationLimitPlusPresheaf`); it is also
described by compatible rational sections, and that description is a comparison, not a second
carrier: `Perfectoid.rationalSections U`, the subring of the product of all `O(V)`, rational
`V ⊆ U`, cut out by restriction compatibility, and `rationalIntegralSections U`, requiring every
component to belong to `O⁺(V)`, are auxiliary family types; `rationalPresheaf` and
`integralPresheaf`, the presheaves of such families with the literal projection along an open
inclusion, are identified with the supplied presheaves by the comparisons below and are not used
downstream in their own right. For a perfectoid pair `R` at a prime `p` and any pair
of definition `D`, `rationalSectionsEquivPresentationLimit` identifies these ordinary
sections with `presentationLimitPresheafInCommRingCat D R.pair.plus` on each open.
`rationalSectionsEquivPresentationLimit_base` sends the family induced by any `a : R`
to Tau Ceti’s canonical `toPresentationLimit` section ([Wedhorn] §8.1, pp. 74–75).
`rationalSectionsEquivPresentationLimit_natural` states compatibility with every restriction;
`rationalPresheaf_iso_presentationLimit` packages its underlying additive maps as a natural
isomorphism. If `D.ringOfDefinition ≤ R.pair.plus`,
`rationalSectionsEquivPresentationLimit_plus` identifies the integral subrings and
`integralPresheaf_iso_presentationLimit` gives the induced natural isomorphism with
Tau Ceti's `presentationLimitPlusPresheaf` ([Wedhorn] §8.1, equation (8.1.1) and its extension
to opens, p. 75; Def. 8.13 and Prop. 8.16, pp. 78–79).
`rationalPresheaf_isSheaf` and `integralPresheaf_isSheaf` give `rationalSheaf` and
`integralSheaf` through these comparisons ([ECD] Thm 3.18, p. 18, and the pointwise integral
condition). Ordinary acyclicity comes from AdicSpacesPartIII R3.1 on the supplied structure
sheaf. `integralSheaf_almost_acyclic` and `integral_cech_almost_acyclic` use Mathlib's
`Sheaf.H` and Čech homology maps; `integralScalar_apply` fixes multiplication on every
rational component ([ECD] Thm 3.24, p. 19). Applying to `rationalPair U` gives the
rational-open forms.

**Checks for the presentation-limit comparison.**
`rationalSectionsEquivPresentationLimit_empty` sends every section of the empty open to zero;
`rationalSectionsEquivPresentationLimit_two_constants` computes `(2 + 5) ↦ 7` on any open;
`rationalSectionsEquivPresentationLimit_nonintegral` excludes the image of `ϖ⁻¹` from the
supplied integral subring on an open containing a point, for a compatible `D`.

**Checks for sections, scalar actions and the Čech sign.** `sections_empty` gives zero
ordinary and integral sections; `sections_rational_recovery` evaluates a compatible family
on its largest rational member and recovers its pair; `sections_nonintegral_constant`
excludes `ϖ⁻¹` on a nonempty open. `sections_restriction_two_constants` and
`integral_restriction_two_constants` compute restriction of sums componentwise.
`integral_scalar_zero`, `integral_scalar_one` and `integral_scalar_two_terms` fix the scalar
endomorphisms. `rationalCechDifference` is `res_V(b) − res_U(a)` on an intersection:
`cech_actual_two_terms` computes `(2,5) ↦ 3`, `cech_actual_reverse` computes `(5,2) ↦ −3`,
and `cech_actual_diagonal` computes `(2,2) ↦ 0` in the actual rational-localization ring.

The global criterion detects `InCharP` on global functions;
`characteristic_p_open_functions` states perfectness of functions on every open.
The nested-restriction statement fixes nested restrictions by their inclusions.
**Checks for chart coordinates.** `chart_identity_sections` recovers a scalar on the identity
chart; `chart_empty_ring` forces every chart of the empty space to have zero ring;
`chart_parameter_nonzero` distinguishes a parameter from zero and from its square.
`characteristic_p_affine_empty` gives the empty characteristic-p affinoid,
`characteristic_p_affine_roots` gives bijective Frobenius on its functions, and
`characteristic_p_affine_agreement` recovers the supplied affinoid ring.
`localization_charp_zero` checks the empty localization without imposing exact `CharP` on
the zero ring; `sections_charp_roots` checks bijective Frobenius on sections.
`perfectoid_cp_point` computes the spectrum of `(ℂ_p, ℂ_p°)` as a singleton.
`tiltCharPIso_sharp` fixes the characteristic-p comparison by sharp on functions, and
`characteristic_p_sharp_two_terms` computes it on a sum of two sections.

### Examples

The worked examples of this layer are the checks above and the running computations in the
subsections: on the perfectoid disc `Spa(ℚ_p^cycl⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩)` the point `T ↦ ϖ` tilts to `T ↦ ϖ♭`,
`{|T| ≤ |ϖ|}` tilts to `{|T| ≤ |ϖ♭|}`, its localisation is `ℚ_p^cycl⟨(T/ϖ)^{1/p^∞}⟩` with tilt
`ℚ_p^cycl♭⟨(T/ϖ♭)^{1/p^∞}⟩`, the naive model `R°⟨T/ϖ⟩` without roots is not almost integral, the
restriction to `{|T| ≤ |ϖ|²}` sends `(T/ϖ)^{1/p^m}` to `ϖ^{1/p^m}(T/ϖ²)^{1/p^m}`, the completed
residue field at the Gauss point is the Gauss-norm completion of `ℚ_p^cycl(T^{1/p^∞})`, and the
integral Čech complex of the Laurent covering is exact; the ring
`ℤ_p^cycl[[T^{1/p^∞}]]⟨(p/T)^{1/p^∞}⟩[1/T]` of ECD Example 3.4(iv), over no field, whose
localisation at `{|T| ≤ |p|}` inverts `p`; the plus ring `K° + K°°⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩` which differs from
`R°`; `Spa(ℂ_p, O_{ℂ_p})` as a one-point affinoid perfectoid space, `Spa(ℚ_p, ℤ_p)`, the closed unit
disc over `ℚ_p` and the discrete `Spa(𝔽_p, 𝔽_p)` as adic spaces that are not perfectoid, and the
perfectoid disc with doubled origin which is quasi-compact but not quasi-separated; the tilts
`Spa(ℚ_p^cycl, ℤ_p^cycl)♭ ≅ Spa(𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞})), 𝔽_p[[t^{1/p^∞}]])` and
`Spa(R⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩)♭ ≅ Spa(R♭⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩)`, with the untilt of the perfectoid disc over
`𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞}))` to the one over `ℚ_p^cycl`; the products
`A⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ ⊗̂_A A⟨S^{1/p^∞}⟩ ≅ A⟨T^{1/p^∞}, S^{1/p^∞}⟩` and `L ⊗̂_K L ≅ ∏_G L` for a Galois
extension of perfectoid fields, whose `Spa` has `|G|` points over a one-point fibre product of
spaces, and whose plus ring `(L°)^ℓ` strictly contains the image of `L° ⊗_{K°} L°`;
`ℂ_p ⊗̂_{ℚ_p} ℂ_p`, not uniform, against the perfectoid `ℂ_p ⊗̂ᵘ_{ℚ_p} ℂ_p` and
`ℚ_p^cycl ⊗̂ᵘ_{ℚ_p} ℚ_p^cycl`; and the absolute product
`Spa 𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞})) × Spa 𝔽_p((s^{1/p^∞}))`, the perfectoid punctured open unit disc, with the
chart whose plus ring must contain `u_m, v_n`.

The Lean `example` of `Suggested.lean` for this layer checks that an empty pre-adic space is
perfectoid exactly when it is sheafy (its sections over `∅` vanish), the chart condition being
vacuous.

## Layer P3: almost purity and the étale site

Layer P3 proves the almost purity theorem for perfectoid Tate rings and builds the étale site of a
perfectoid space. It opens with the algebraic prefix — henselian pairs, Elkik's approximation theorem
and its non-noetherian form, and the invariance of finite étale algebras under henselian completion
and under completed colimits — then proves almost purity in characteristic `p`, constructs the
untilting functor on finite étale algebras, treats finite extensions of perfectoid fields and the
Fontaine–Wintenberger theorem, and assembles the almost purity theorem with its three conclusions:
finite étale algebras over a perfectoid Tate ring are perfectoid, tilting is an equivalence of finite
étale algebras, and the integral closure is almost finite étale. On the geometric side it defines
finite étale and étale morphisms of perfectoid spaces, compares them with the adic notions of
AdicEtaleGeometry A1.2–A1.3 (finite étale Huber pairs, finite étale and étale morphisms) and A1.6
(the sites), and builds the étale site with its tilting equivalence and the almost
acyclicity of `O⁺`. AdicEtaleGeometry A1.0.4–A1.0.5 supplies classical henselian approximation
and finite étale completion. The perfectoid-ring results require no perfectoid base field;
the field results explicitly assume a perfectoid field.

### P3.2 perfectoid-field specialization of henselian completion

The perfectoid-field application of henselian completion is supplied by
AdicEtaleGeometry A1.0.5 (*henselian-finite-etale-approximation*): for a perfectoid
field `K`, a pseudouniformiser `ϖ ∈ K°` and a flat `K°`-algebra `A` henselian
along `(ϖ)`, apply its part (a) with `R = A`, `t = ϖ` and `I = A` to obtain
`FÉt(A[ϖ⁻¹]) ≃ FÉt(Â[ϖ⁻¹])`, where `Â` is the `ϖ`-adic completion
([Sch12] §7, Proposition 7.4). *Needs:* P1.10; AdicEtaleGeometry A1.0.5.

### P3.3 almost purity in characteristic p

Almost purity in characteristic `p` is the case in which perfectness does the work: a finite étale
algebra over a perfect complete Tate ring is again perfectoid, and its integral closure is almost
finite étale.

**Almost purity in characteristic `p`: finite étale algebras over a perfectoid Tate ring of
characteristic `p`.** (*finite-etale-covers-in-characteristic-p*) Let `R` be a perfectoid Tate ring of
characteristic `p` (equivalently a perfect complete Tate ring of characteristic `p`, layer P1; no base
field), `ϖ ∈ R` a pseudouniformiser (it has all `p`-power roots `ϖ^{1/pⁿ}` in `R°`), `R⁺ ⊆ R°` a ring
of integral elements, and `S ∈ FÉt(R)` with its natural topology and plus ring `S⁺` = the integral
closure of `R⁺` in `S`. Then: (i) `S` is perfect, complete and uniform, hence a perfectoid Tate ring of
characteristic `p`, and `(S, S⁺)` is a perfectoid Huber pair; (ii) `S°` is the integral closure of `R°`
in `S` and `S°/S⁺`, viewed as an `R⁺`-module, is killed by `R°°`;
thus `S°a` and `S⁺a` agree after transport between the basic setups
`(R⁺, R°°)` and `(R°, R°°)`; (iii) `S°a` is an almost finite étale `R°a`-algebra
(almost finitely presented projective and unramified: the diagonal idempotent `e ∈ S ⊗_R S` lies in
`(S°a ⊗_{R°a} S°a)_*`); (iv) `S°a` is uniformly almost finite projective: there is `n ≥ 0` such that
for every `ε ∈ R°°` there are `R°`-linear maps `S° → (R°)ⁿ → S°` whose composite is multiplication by
`ε`; (v) if `S` is faithfully flat over `R`, then `Tr_{S/R}(S°°) ⊇ R°°` and `R°a → S°a` is almost
faithfully flat and almost split. Almost mathematics is that of the basic setup `(R°, R°°)`
(layer P1), equivalently of the ideal `(ϖ^{1/p^∞})`, and almost finite étale is the notion of
layer P0. Not claimed: `S°` finite, flat or étale over `R°`, or `S` free over `R`. The statement
specialises to the case of a perfectoid `K`-algebra over a perfectoid field `K` of characteristic `p`,
and to the finite separable extensions of such a field ([Sch12] §5, Prop. 5.23, pp. 28–29, over a field; [GR] §3.5,
Thm 3.5.28, pp. 69–71, applied to `R°`, gives the base-field-free argument). *Needs:*
layer P1 (perfectoid Tate rings, the characteristic-`p` criterion, the basic setup `(R°, R°°)`).

`finiteEtale_charP_perfectoid` proves perfectness and supplies the Tate structure,
completeness and Hausdorffness for the finite-module topology in (i).
Its characteristic hypothesis is `pR = 0`, allowing the zero base and zero algebra;
it requires no `CharP S p` instance for the zero algebra.
For the resulting finite étale pair, `Pair.integralClosure_powerBounded`
states (ii), including the annihilation formula `εs ∈ S⁺` for every
`ε ∈ R°°` and `s ∈ S°`. `Pair.integralClosure_almostFiniteEtale` states (iii),
`Pair.integralClosure_uniformlyAlmostFiniteProjective` states the fixed-rank
factorizations in (iv), and `Pair.integralClosure_faithfullyFlat` states (v),
including exact trace lifts of topologically nilpotent elements and linear
splittings after multiplication by each almost scalar. These pair theorems
also give the characteristic-independent conclusions of P3.12. The trace
and splitting clauses follow from the almost purity assertion and
[GR] Cor. 4.1.11 and Thm 4.1.14, pp. 74–75.

Two lemmas feed the proof. Relative Frobenius of a weakly étale map is an isomorphism, and étale
algebras over perfect rings are perfect (*etale-over-perfect-is-perfect*): for a weakly étale map
`A → B` of `𝔽_p`-algebras (flat with flat multiplication `B ⊗_A B → B`) the square of `A → B` with the
absolute Frobenii (Mathlib `frobenius`) is a pushout, so `B ⊗_{A, Frob} A → B` is an isomorphism and `B`
is perfect (Mathlib `PerfectRing`) when `A` is; the same holds for weakly étale morphisms of almost
algebras over a basic setup of characteristic `p`, so for a finite étale `(R°a/ϖ)`-algebra `B`, relative Frobenius identifies
`B/ϖ^{1/p}` with `B`, with the base rings identified by `x ↦ x^p` ([Bhatt] Ch. 4, §4.3, Lem. 4.3.8).
Uniformity and the power-bounded integral-closure comparison for finite étale algebras
are supplied by AdicEtaleGeometry A1.2a (*finite-etale-over-uniform-is-uniform*).

Lean: `perfectRing_of_etale` (*etale-over-perfect-is-perfect* for étale algebras over a perfect ring
of characteristic `p`).

### P3.4 characteristic p: inverting `ϖ` is an equivalence

**Characteristic `p`: inverting `ϖ` is an equivalence between almost finite étale `R°a`-algebras and
finite étale `R`-algebras.** (*characteristic-p-almost-purity-equivalence*) Let `R` be a perfectoid
Tate ring of characteristic `p` with pseudouniformiser `ϖ`, and `(R°a)_afet` the category of almost
finite étale `R°a`-algebras (layer P0). Then the functor `(R°a)_afet → FÉt(R)`, `A ↦ A_*[ϖ⁻¹]`
(`A_*` the ring of almost elements, layer P0), with its natural topology, is an equivalence of
categories, compatible with tensor products; a quasi-inverse is `S ↦ S°a`. Moreover every
`A ∈ (R°a)_afet` is uniformly almost finite projective, `A_*` is perfect, `ϖ`-torsion free and
`ϖ`-adically complete, and `A_*` is the integral closure of `R°` in `A_*[ϖ⁻¹]`; almost faithful
flatness of `A` corresponds to faithful flatness of `A_*[ϖ⁻¹]` ([GR] §3.5, 3.5.26 and Thm 3.5.28,
p. 69). *Needs:* P3.3.

The construction `AlmostFiniteEtale p R` uses P0's category under the almost
base algebra. `almostInversion p R ϖ` sends `A` to the localization of its
actual algebra of almost elements. `almostInversionMap_scalars` identifies
`R° → A_* → A_*[1/ϖ]` with the structural map through `R`;
`almostInversion_isLocalization` specifies its universal property and
`almostInversionMap_natural` its action on arrows. The equivalence instance is
`almostInversion_isEquivalence`; the same construction applies in all
characteristics by P3.11. Parameter comparison `almostInversionParameterIso`
fixes every almost element and satisfies the cocycle equation.

`almostInversion_charP_perfect` states bijectivity of Frobenius on the ring
of almost elements when `pR = 0`, including the zero ring ([GR] proof of Thm 3.5.28,
Claim 3.5.35, pp. 70–71). For every almost finite étale algebra,
`almostInversion_elements_complete` states injectivity of multiplication
by `ϖ` and `ϖ`-adic completeness of its almost elements;
`almostInversion_elements_integralClosure` states that the localization map
is injective and its image consists exactly of elements integral over `R°`.
`almostInversion_uniformlyAlmostFiniteProjective` gives a single finite bound,
and `almostInversion_faithfullyFlat_iff` identifies almost faithful flatness
with faithful flatness after inversion. These four assertions hold in all
characteristics by P3.11 ([Sch12] Lem. 5.3(iv), p. 22, Prop. 5.23 and
Thm 5.25, pp. 28–29, Thm 7.9, p. 42; [GR] Claims 3.5.31–35, pp. 70–71).

**Checks.** `inversion_rank_zero`, `inversion_rank_one`, `inversion_rank_two`
apply this actual functor to the almostifications of `(R°)⁰`, `R°`, `(R°)²`,
with outputs `0`, `R`, `R²`. `inversion_characteristic_p_wrong_parameter`
asserts that the image of `almostSplit p R 1` under `almostInversion p R ϖ`
is nontrivial for a nonzero characteristic-`p` perfectoid pair and admits no
ring equivalence to `Localization.Away (p : R)`. Thus replacing `ϖ` by `p=0`
changes the functor's actual output.

### P3.5 the untilting functor on finite étale algebras

**The untilting functor on finite étale algebras, `T ↦ T♯`, via almost finite étale integral
structures.** (*finite-etale-untilting-functor*) Let `R` be a perfectoid Tate ring with tilt `R♭`
(layer P1) and choose a pseudouniformiser `ϖ♭ ∈ R♭` with `ϖ := (ϖ♭)♯` satisfying `ϖ^p | p` in `R°`
(layer P1), so that `R♭°/ϖ♭ = R°/ϖ` (layer P1). In `Perfectoid.FiniteEtale`, define `untilt` as the
untilting functor `(−)♯ : FÉt(R♭) → FÉt(R)` (`CommAlgCat.FiniteEtale R♭ ⥤ CommAlgCat.FiniteEtale R`),
the composite

`FÉt(R♭) ≃ (R♭°a)_afet → (R♭°a/ϖ♭)_afet = (R°a/ϖ)_afet ≃ (R°a)_afet → FÉt(R), T ↦ T°a ↦ T°a/ϖ♭ ↦ A ↦ A_*[ϖ⁻¹] =: T♯,`

where the first equivalence is *characteristic-p-almost-purity-equivalence*, the middle equivalence
is the unique flat deformation of almost finite étale algebras along the `ϖ`-adically complete flat
`R°a` (layer P0), and the last functor inverts `ϖ` (natural module topology on `T♯`).
Prove `untilt_isPerfectoid` directly for the constructed `T♯`, from layer P1's primitive-ideal
untilting: `T♯ = W(T⁺)[1/[ϖ♭]]/ξ` is the untilt of the perfectoid ring `T` (of characteristic
`p`, `T` being finite étale over the perfectoid `R♭`, hence perfectoid as a uniform complete Tate
ring that is perfect) along the primitive element `ξ`, and untilts of perfectoid rings are
perfectoid (layer P1); no statement about arbitrary finite étale `R`-algebras is used. The
general theorem `FiniteEtale.naturalPerfectoid` — for every finite étale algebra `S` over a
complete Hausdorff perfectoid Tate ring `R`, the supplied `Huber.FiniteEtale R S` with its natural
module topology is perfectoid ([ECD] Theorem 6.1(i), p. 26) — is NOT a target of this subsection:
it is the essential-surjectivity milestone of *finite-etale-tilting-equivalence* (P3.9) and is
exposed, and registered as an instance, only there and in P3.10, after that milestone; nothing in
P3.5–P3.8 depends on it. Prove `tiltUntiltIso`
(a canonical isomorphism `(T♯)♭ ≅ T` of `R♭`-algebras, natural in `T`, so that `(−)♯` is inverse to
tilting on its image and compatible with the untilting of perfectoid algebras of layer P1). Further,
`T♯` is finite étale over `R`; `(T♯)°a = A` is almost finite étale over `R°a`; the functor is
independent of `ϖ♭` up to canonical isomorphism, preserves tensor products, finite products, ranks
(the rank of `T♯` at `x ∈ Spa R` equals the rank of `T` at `x♭`) and faithful flatness; and it
commutes with base change along every map of perfectoid Tate rings `R → R'` (for example a rational
localisation or the completed residue field at a point): `(T ⊗_{R♭} R'♭)♯ ≅ T♯ ⊗_R R'`. Equivalently
`T♯ = W(T⁺)[1/[ϖ♭]]/ξ`, with `T⁺` the integral closure of `R♭⁺` in `T`, for a generator `ξ` of `ker(θ : W(R♭⁺) → R⁺)` (layer P1), which shows finite
étaleness without almost mathematics ([KL15] Lem. 3.6.20; [AWS] Lem. 2.8.10) ([Sch12] §5, Prop. 5.22
and the diagram following it, p. 28). *Needs:* P3.4; layer P0 (flat deformation of almost finite
étale algebras along a complete flat almost algebra); layer P1 (tilts, untilts, `θ`).

**Checks.**

- Degenerate: `untilt R♭ ≅ R` (`R♭` as a finite étale
  `R♭`-algebra), `untilt 0 = 0`, and `untilt (T₁ × T₂) ≅ untilt T₁ × untilt T₂`.
- Computation: for `K = ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞})^`,
  `K♭ = 𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^` with `t♯ = p` and `p` odd: `untilt (K♭[u]/(u² − t)) ≅ K[u]/(u² − p)`.
- Computation: for `T = R♭ × R♭`, the sharps of
  the marked idempotents `(1,0)` and `(0,1)` become the respective idempotents of `R × R`.
  The general comparison `tilt (untilt T) ≅ T` is `FiniteEtale.tiltUntiltIso`;
  `FiniteEtale.untiltPairIso` identifies this untilt with P1's untilt.

The split-algebra Checks are `untilt_test_rank_zero`, `untilt_test_rank_one`
and `untilt_test_rank_two`: the finite étale algebras `R♭⁰`, `R♭` and `R♭²` untilt
respectively to the zero algebra `R⁰`, `R` and `R²`.

`FiniteEtale.tiltFunctor`, the geometric tilting functor on all of `FÉt(R)`, has carrier the
tilt of the supplied finite-algebra module topology, with `tiltFunctor_map_coeff` giving its
coordinatewise action on algebra homomorphisms; it is defined only on the full subcategory of
finite étale `R`-algebras that are perfectoid (the essential image of P3.6) until P3.9's
essential-surjectivity milestone shows that this is all of `FÉt(R)`, and it is never used to
prove that perfectoidness. `untilt_isPerfectoid`, `tiltUntiltIso`,
`untiltTiltIso`, and `tiltUntilt_triangle` specify the geometric inverse and
its triangle identity. `finiteEtaleTiltEquiv_comparison` identifies the
categorical inverse with this geometric functor. For every perfectoid Tate

using the extension `J` of `ker θ_R` to `W(T⁺)`. Its scalar action comes from
P1's slice structural map through `PrimitiveTriple.untiltCarrierEquiv`.
Write `m_T : (T♯)♭ ≅ T` for `tiltUntiltIso.app T`.
`untiltWittIso_apply` fixes the equivalence by
`(m_T⁻¹(x))♯ ↦ [x] mod J` for every `x ∈ T⁺`, followed by localization.
`untiltWittIso_scalars` sends the scalar `θ_R(w)` to the class of the image
of `w` in `W(T⁺)`, for every `w ∈ W(R♭⁺)`; this also specifies the base

pair, preserving the integral-closure plus ring, and `untiltPairIso_app`
identifies its carrier map with this very Witt equivalence. These are the
finite étale restriction of P1's marked untilting construction ([KL15]
Lemma 3.6.20, p. 97; for general perfectoid Tate rings, [ECD] Theorem 6.1(ii),
p. 26).

For every continuous map `f : R → R'` of perfectoid Tate rings,
`untiltBaseChangeIso` uses the scalar actions from `f` and `f♭`.
`untiltBaseChangeIso_app` sends
`(m_(R'♭ ⊗ T)⁻¹(a ⊗ t))♯` to `a♯ ⊗ (m_T⁻¹(t))♯` for every
`a ∈ R'♭` and `t ∈ T`. `untiltBaseChangeIso_id` identifies the identity
base map with `CommAlgCat.FiniteEtale.baseChangeSelfIso`.
For continuous `R → R' → R''`, `untiltBaseChangeIso_comp` equates the
two successive comparisons with the comparison for the composite, after
`Algebra.TensorProduct.cancelBaseChange` on both sides. No injectivity or
nonzero-ring hypothesis is required ([ECD] Theorem 6.1(ii), p. 26, and the
functorial construction of [Sch12] Proposition 5.22 and Theorem 5.25,
pp. 28–29).

For finite étale `T,U` over `R♭`, `untiltProductIso_app` characterizes
`untiltProductIso` as the ordered pair of the untilted projections.
`untiltProductIso_natural` commutes with arbitrary maps of both factors;
`untiltProductIso_id` and `untiltProductIso_comp` give its identity and
composition equations. These are the product comparison laws for the
same equivalence ([ECD] Theorem 6.1(ii), p. 26). The functor
`finiteEtalePairFunctor` uses the supplied natural module topology, and
`finiteEtalePairFunctor_map` fixes its action on ring maps.

**Checks.** `untiltWittIso_zero`, `untiltWittIso_one`,

The characteristic-`p` Check `fontaine_wintenberger_test_char_p` sends a tilt sequence
to its zeroth coefficient, the `p`th power of its first coefficient ([Berkeley]
Lemma 6.2.2, p. 44). `fontaine_wintenberger_test_algebraically_closed` computes
