Theorem 6.1(ii), p. 26).

**Checks.** `finite_pair_zero`, `finite_pair_one`, `finite_pair_two` compute

`geometric_tilt_zero`, `geometric_tilt_one`, `geometric_tilt_two`
compute the actual geometric functor on the three split algebras.
`untilt_actual_tilt` fixes both ordered idempotents of the split rank-two algebra;

`untilt_test_quadratic` states the quadratic computation over every perfectoid
field with `p ≠ 2` and every nonzero `t ∈ K♭`, hence in particular the Kummer

`untilt_quadratic_nonsplit` adds that nonsquareness of `t` forces

to `AdjoinRoot (X²−t)`. This excludes the quadratic algebra from the domain of
`FiniteEtale.untilt`, including `t=0`.

### P3.6 untilting is fully faithful and inverse to tilting on its image

**The untilting functor `FÉt(R♭) → FÉt(R)` is fully faithful, inverse to tilting on its image, with
image the `S` having almost finite étale integral structure.**
(*tilting-finite-etale-algebras-fully-faithful*) Let `R` be a perfectoid Tate ring with tilt `R♭`
(any characteristic, no perfectoid base field). The untilting functor `(−)♯ : FÉt(R♭) → FÉt(R)` of
*finite-etale-untilting-functor* is fully faithful and, on its essential image, inverse to tilting:
for `S = T♯`, `S` is perfectoid and `S♭ ≅ T`. Its essential image consists exactly of the finite
étale `R`-algebras `S` such that `S` (with its natural topology) is perfectoid and `S°a` is almost
finite étale over `R°a`; for such `S`, `S°a` is uniformly almost finite projective over `R°a`. The
functor preserves degrees (rank functions), tensor products and faithful flatness. For `R = K` a
perfectoid field this is the input of [Sch12] Thm 3.7; for `R` of characteristic `p` (`R♭ = R`) it is
the identity ([Sch12] §5, Thm 5.25, p. 29). *Needs:* P3.5.

### P3.7 finite extensions of perfectoid fields

**Finite extensions of perfectoid fields are perfectoid, and tilting is a degree-preserving
equivalence of finite extensions.** (*finite-extensions-of-perfectoid-fields*) Let `K` be a perfectoid
field (characteristic `0` or `p`) with tilt `K♭`. (i) Every finite extension `L/K`, with its natural
topology (the unique extension of the absolute value, Mathlib `spectralNorm`), is a perfectoid field.
(ii) The untilting functor `(−)♯` of P3.5 is an equivalence `FÉt(K♭) ≃ FÉt(K)` with quasi-inverse
`L ↦ L♭`; it restricts to an equivalence between finite field extensions of `K♭` and of `K`,
preserving degrees, automorphism groups and Galois extensions. (iii) `K` is algebraically closed if
and only if `K♭` is: `isAlgClosed_tilt [IsAlgClosed K]` gives
`IsAlgClosed (tiltField p K)`, since the degree-preserving equivalence in (ii) forces every
finite extension of `K♭` to have degree one ([Sch12] §3, Thm 3.7(ii), p. 17).
Here `p` is prime and `K` is complete, nontrivially normed, ultrametric and perfectoid at `p`;
`isAlgClosed_of_tilt` gives the reverse implication ([Sch12] §3, Prop. 3.8, pp. 17–18).
(iv) For every finite extension `L/K`, `L°a` is almost finite étale over `K°a`
(Tate; [GR] §6.6 for deeply ramified fields), uniformly almost finite projective ([Sch12] §3,
Thm 3.7(i), p. 17). *Needs:* P3.6.

Three lemmas accompany the theorem. If the tilt of a perfectoid field is algebraically closed, so is
the field (*untilt-of-algebraically-closed-field*): for `K` a perfectoid field with tilt `K♭`
(layer P1), `IsAlgClosed K♭` implies `IsAlgClosed K` (Mathlib `IsAlgClosed`); in characteristic `p`,
`K♭ = K` and the statement is trivial ([Sch12] §3, Prop. 3.8). The completed cyclotomic extension of
a finite extension of `ℚ_p` is perfectoid (*cyclotomic-completion-of-finite-extension*): for `K` a
finite extension of `ℚ_p` inside a fixed algebraic closure, with completion `C`, the closure `L` of
`K(μ_{p^∞})` in `C` is a perfectoid field, namely the compositum `L = K·ℚ_p^cycl` with the completed
cyclotomic field `ℚ_p^cycl` (layer P1), a finite extension of `ℚ_p^cycl` of degree at most
`[K : ℚ_p]` in which `K(μ_{p^∞})` is dense, and its tilt `L♭` is a finite extension of
`(ℚ_p^cycl)♭ = 𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^` of degree `[L : ℚ_p^cycl]`, with
`Gal(L/ℚ_p^cycl) ≅ Gal(L♭/(ℚ_p^cycl)♭)` by (ii) ([Sch12] §3, Thm 3.7(i)). The completed tensor
product of plus rings
need not be integrally closed (*completed-tensor-plus-ring-not-integrally-closed*): for `K` the
completion of `ℚ̆_p(μ_{p^∞})`, with algebraically closed residue field and
`|K×| = |p|^{ℤ[1/p]/(p−1)}`,  `ℓ` a prime with `ℓ ∤ p(p − 1)` and `L = K(p^{1/ℓ})` — a cyclic Galois extension of
degree `ℓ`, perfectoid by (i), with trivial residue extension — one has `L ⊗̂_K L ≅ L^ℓ` with plus ring
`(L°)^ℓ`, while `L° ⊗_{K°} L° → (L°)^ℓ` is injective and not surjective; so the map from the `ϖ`-adic
completion of `B⁺ ⊗_{A⁺} C⁺` to `D⁺` in layer P2 is an almost isomorphism that is not an isomorphism,
and the completed tensor product of plus rings is not integrally closed in `D`, hence not a ring of
integral elements. Indeed every tensor has the same residue in all `ℓ` factors,
and this condition persists on completion; the integral idempotent `(1,0,…,0)`
fails it. This calculation uses the Galois product decomposition and P3.12
for the almost comparison.

`completed_tensor_plus_not_integrally_closed` gives the same obstruction for any
nontrivial finite Galois extension of perfectoid fields whose automorphisms act
trivially on the residue field. It specifies the completed-tensor map on pure
tensors and exhibits the integral idempotent of the identity factor outside its
image. `tame_cubic_perfectoid_extension` supplies the residue-characteristic-two,
degree-three instance inside `ℂ₂`. The finite-field theorem and Galois product
decomposition above supply the hypotheses; equal residues exclude that idempotent.

Lean: `IsPerfectoidField.of_finiteDimensional` (finite extensions of perfectoid fields are
perfectoid) and `isPerfectoidField_of_isAlgClosed` (a complete algebraically closed nonarchimedean
field with `‖p‖ < 1` is a perfectoid field).

### P3.8 the Fontaine–Wintenberger theorem

The Fontaine–Wintenberger theorem is the field case of the tilting equivalence, passed to the
limit over all finite extensions.

**Fontaine–Wintenberger: the absolute Galois groups of a perfectoid field and of its tilt are
isomorphic.** (*fontaine-wintenberger*) Let `K` be a perfectoid field with tilt `K♭`. Fix an algebraic
closure `K̄` of `K` with completion `C`, so that `C♭` is an algebraically closed perfectoid field
containing `K♭` (P3.7(iii), `isAlgClosed_tilt`), and let `K♭^sep` be the separable
closure of `K♭` in `C♭`. Then `L ↦ L♭` (for finite Galois `L/K` inside `K̄`, with `L♭ ⊆ C♭` by
functoriality of tilting) defines an isomorphism of profinite groups
`Gal(K̄/K) ≅ Gal(K♭^sep/K♭)` (Mathlib `Field.absoluteGaloisGroup` up to the choice of closures),
compatible with the Galois correspondences (Mathlib
`InfiniteGalois.IntermediateFieldEquivClosedSubgroup`): finite subextensions of `K̄/K` correspond to
finite subextensions of `K♭^sep/K♭` with the same degrees ([Sch12] §3, Thm 3.7(ii), p. 17, the
degree-preserving equivalence of finite extensions; §1, Thm 1.1, p. 2, is the case
`K = ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞})^`). The
direction of the comparison is fixed by the functor: `L ↦ L♭` goes from finite extensions of `K`
to finite extensions of `K♭`, and its quasi-inverse is the untilt `M ↦ M♯` of P3.5; on Galois groups
the isomorphism `Gal(K̄/K) → Gal(K♭^sep/K♭)` sends `σ` to the automorphism of `K♭^sep` induced on
the inverse limit `lim_{x ↦ x^p}` of `C` by the continuous extension of `σ` to `C`. *Needs:* P3.7;
AdicEtaleGeometry A1.0.5 (henselian completion); layer P1 (the tilt of a perfectoid field).

**Checks.**

- `fontaine_wintenberger_test_kummer_tower` (computation) — `K = ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞})^`: `K♭ = 𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^` with `t = (p, p^{1/p}, p^{1/p²}, …)`, `t♯ = p`; `K♭^sep` is the separable closure
  of `𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^`, and `Gal(K♭^sep/K♭) = Gal(𝔽_p((t))^sep/𝔽_p((t)))` since
  `𝔽_p((t)) ⊂ K♭` is a purely inseparable, then completed, extension, neither of which changes
  finite étale algebras (*finite-etale-under-completed-perfection*, *henselian-finite-etale-approximation*);
  so `G_{ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞})} ≅ G_{𝔽_p((t))}` (the uncompleted `ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞})` has the same Galois group
  as its completion by AdicEtaleGeometry A1.0.5(b)). For `p` odd the quadratic extensions correspond: `K(√p) ↔ K♭(√t)`
  (P3.5, `untilt_test_quadratic`).
- `fontaine_wintenberger_test_p_two_cyclotomic` (degenerate, `p = 2`) — `K = ℚ_2(ζ_{2^∞})^`:
  `K♭ = 𝔽_2((t^{1/2^∞}))^` with `t = ε − 1`, `ε = (1, −1, ζ_4, ζ_8, …)` (for `p = 2` the first
  nontrivial root of unity is `ζ_2 = −1`, and `ε` is a compatible system of `2^n`-th roots of `1`),
  and `G_{ℚ_2(ζ_{2^∞})} ≅ G_{𝔽_2((t))}`; in characteristic `2` no polynomial `u² − a` is separable
  (`t^{1/2}` already lies in `K♭`), so the separable quadratic extensions of `𝔽_2((t))` are the
  Artin–Schreier ones `u² − u = f`, and they match the quadratic extensions of `ℚ_2(ζ_{2^∞})`: the
  unramified one `K(ζ_3) = K(√−3)` corresponds to `u² − u = 1`, i.e. `𝔽_4((t))`, and all others are
  wildly ramified (`√−1 = ζ_4` and `√2 = ζ_8 + ζ_8^{-1}` already lie in `K`). The
  Kummer-type check `untilt_test_quadratic` of P3.5 needs `p` odd for this reason.
- `fontaine_wintenberger_test_char_p` (degenerate) — `K` of characteristic `p`: `K♭ = K`, the
  isomorphism is the identity of `Gal(K^sep/K)`.
- `fontaine_wintenberger_test_algebraically_closed` (degenerate) — `K = C` algebraically closed:
  `C♭` is algebraically closed by `isAlgClosed_tilt` (P3.7(iii)) and both groups are trivial;
  conversely a nontrivial `Gal(K̄/K)` forces `K♭` not separably closed.

In characteristic `p`, finite étale algebras are insensitive to completed perfection
(*finite-etale-under-completed-perfection*): for `S` a complete Tate ring of characteristic `p` with
ring of definition `S₀ ∋ ϖ` and `R = (S^{perf})^` the completion of `S^{perf} = colim(S → S → ⋯)`
along Frobenius, for the Tate topology with ring of definition `colim S₀^{1/pⁿ}` — a perfect complete
Tate ring, hence perfectoid (layer P1, P1.2) — base change is an equivalence
`FÉt(S) ≃ FÉt(R)`; in particular, for a `p`-finite perfectoid affinoid `(R, R⁺)`, the completed
perfection of a reduced affinoid `(S, S⁺)` of topologically finite type over a characteristic-`p`
perfectoid field, `R_fét ≃ S_fét`, and the base field is not needed ([Sch12] §7, Lem. 7.5(ii)).

The continuous group isomorphism is `Perfectoid.fontaineWintenberger` on
Mathlib's absolute Galois groups. Its marking by the action on the completed
algebraic closure is the coordinatewise convention above.
`fontaine_wintenberger_test_p_two_unramified` computes the actual untilt over
`ℚ₂^cycl`: the Artin–Schreier algebra `u²−u−1` over its tilt becomes the
algebra `v²+v+1`, adjoining a primitive third root of unity. This is the
unramified quadratic check, not a characteristic-two Kummer polynomial.

`fontaineWintenbergerFiberIso` identifies the geometric fibre of the actual
untilt with the tilted geometric fibre. `fontaineWintenberger_fiber_action`
fixes the action convention by postcomposition on algebra maps into the
chosen algebraic closures. Thus the continuous group isomorphism is tied to
the finite-algebra equivalence; changing compatible fibres conjugates it.

**Check.** `fontaine_wintenberger_p_two_action` identifies the nonidentity
unramified quadratic action `u ↦ u+1` on `u²−u=1` with `ζ₃ ↦ ζ₃²` on
`ζ₃²+ζ₃+1=0`, through the untilt functor over `ℚ₂^cycl`.

### P3.9 tilting is an equivalence of finite étale algebras

**Tilting is an equivalence between finite étale algebras over a perfectoid Tate ring and over its
tilt.** (*finite-etale-tilting-equivalence*) Let `R` be a perfectoid Tate ring ([ECD] Def. 3.1;
layer P1: any characteristic, no perfectoid base field) with tilt `R♭`. Then the untilting functor
`(−)♯ : FÉt(R♭) → FÉt(R)` of *finite-etale-untilting-functor* is an equivalence of categories, with
quasi-inverse the tilting functor `S ↦ S♭` (`S` being perfectoid). It is compatible with tensor
products, with base change along maps of perfectoid Tate rings (in particular rational localisations
and completed residue fields), and preserves ranks and faithful flatness. For every ring of integral
elements `R⁺ ⊆ R°` with tilt `R♭⁺` (layer P1), it induces an equivalence between finite étale
morphisms of Huber pairs `(R, R⁺) → (S, S⁺)` and `(R♭, R♭⁺) → (S♭, S♭⁺)` (plus rings the integral
closures; the finite étale Huber pair of AdicEtaleGeometry A1.2), i.e. between finite étale
affinoid perfectoid spaces over `Spa(R, R⁺)` and over `Spa(R♭, R♭⁺)` ([ECD] §6, Thm 6.1(ii), p. 26).
The content beyond P3.6 is essential surjectivity, stated as its own milestone
(*finite-etale-untilting-essentially-surjective*): every finite étale `R`-algebra `S` (natural
module topology) is perfectoid with `S°a` almost finite étale over `R°a`, hence lies in the
essential image of P3.6. Full faithfulness and the description of the restricted essential image do
not give this; the proof is local-to-global, with the following inputs, each a named statement:
(i) the field case — for a perfectoid field `K`, `FÉt(K♭) → FÉt(K)` is essentially surjective
([Sch12] Thm 3.7 and §7, proof of Thm 7.9, pp. 42–43; P3.7); (ii) the completed-residue-field
case at a point `x ∈ Spa(R, R⁺)` — `S ⊗_R k(x)^` is in the image, by (i) applied to the perfectoid
field `k(x)^` (P3.8); (iii) rational-neighbourhood spreading — the untilt `T_x♯ ≅ S ⊗_R k(x)^`
found in (ii) spreads to a rational neighbourhood `U_x` of `x` with `T_{U_x}♯ ≅ S ⊗_R O(U_x)`, by
the finite-étale approximation of AdicEtaleGeometry A1 (*finite-etale-approximation*, Henselian
spreading of finite étale algebras along the filtered colimit `colim_{U ∋ x} O(U) → k(x)^`,
[Sch12] Lemma 7.5(i)) and the base-change compatibility of P3.5; (iv) overlap compatibility — on
`U_x ∩ U_y` the two untilts are identified by full faithfulness (P3.6) applied to the tilts of the
transition isomorphisms; (v) affinoid gluing — the `T_{U_x}` glue to a finite étale `R♭`-algebra
`T` by finite étale descent on the finite rational cover (A1's *finite-etale-rational-descent*,
with finite projectivity of the pieces), and `T♯ ≅ S` by the sheaf property. The residue-field
spreading statement below is (iii). Only after this milestone are `FiniteEtale.naturalPerfectoid`
(P3.10) and the unrestricted `FiniteEtale.tiltFunctor` (P3.5) exposed as consequences. *Needs:*
P3.6; P3.7; P3.8; P3.5 (base change); AdicEtaleGeometry A1 (*finite-etale-approximation*,
*finite-etale-rational-descent*); P2.3.

Use `Perfectoid.finiteEtaleTiltEquiv` for the inverse equivalence to `untilt`.
**Checks.** `finiteEtaleTiltEquiv_test_rank_zero`, `finiteEtaleTiltEquiv_test_rank_one`
and `finiteEtaleTiltEquiv_test_rank_two` compute its values on `R⁰`, `R` and `R²`
as `R♭⁰`, `R♭` and `R♭²`. `finiteEtaleTiltEquiv_test_direction` checks that tilting
followed by untilting is naturally isomorphic to the identity.

Finite étale algebras over the completed residue field spread out to a rational neighbourhood
(*residue-field-finite-etale-colimit*): for `(A, A⁺)` a complete Tate Huber pair (Tau Ceti
`Huber.Pair`, `Huber.IsTateRing`), `X = Spa(A, A⁺)` (Tau Ceti `ValuationSpectrum.spa`), `x ∈ X` with
completed residue field `k(x)^`, and `O(U)` the rational localisation on rational subsets `U ∋ x` (Tau
Ceti `ValuationSpectrum.rationalSubset`; the Foundations of adic spaces roadmap (AdicSpaces),
layer 3), base change induces an equivalence `2-colim_{U ∋ x} FÉt(O(U)) ≃ FÉt(k(x)^)` compatible with
tensor products: every finite étale `k(x)^`-algebra is `L ⊗ k(x)^` for some `U ∋ x` and
`L ∈ FÉt(O(U))`, every `k(x)^`-algebra map between such comes from an `O(V)`-algebra map over some
rational `x ∈ V ⊆ U`, and two maps agreeing over `k(x)^` agree over some such `V`; no sheafiness of
`(A, A⁺)` is required ([Berkeley] Lecture 7, §7.4, Lem. 7.4.6 and the argument after Thm 7.4.8).

`Perfectoid.rationalResidueMap` evaluates a rational localization of any complete
Tate pair at a point in its rational subset. `rationalResidueMap_spec` states
continuity and agreement with the original residue map; no sheafiness or
perfectoidness is assumed ([Berkeley] Lemma 7.4.6 and the argument after
Theorem 7.4.8, pp. 53–55). Its Checks are
`rationalResidueMap_base` (its kernel on base elements is the valuation support),
`rationalResidueMap_denominator` (the denominator stays nonzero),
`rationalResidueMap_fraction` (`t/s` maps to `t(x)/s(x)`, with the inverted
denominator in the actual completed rational localization), and
`rationalResidueMap_empty` (a zero rational localization cannot contain the point).
The statements `residue_field_finite_etale_essSurj`, `residue_field_finite_etale_full`
and `residue_field_finite_etale_faithful` give objects, morphisms and eventual
equality, with the refinement and scalar maps explicitly recorded.

### P3.10 finite étale algebras over a perfectoid Tate ring are perfectoid

**Finite étale algebras over a perfectoid Tate ring are perfectoid.**
(*finite-etale-over-perfectoid-is-perfectoid*) Let `R` be a perfectoid Tate ring (any characteristic,
no perfectoid base field) and `S` a finite étale `R`-algebra (Mathlib `Module.Finite R S`,
`Algebra.Etale R S`) with its natural topology as a finite `R`-module. The target `Perfectoid.isPerfectoidTateRing_of_finiteEtale` supplies a Tate structure,
completeness and Hausdorffness for that topology, and proves that `S` is perfectoid; `S ≅ (S♭)♯` with `S♭ ∈ FÉt(R♭)`; for every ring of integral elements `R⁺ ⊆ R°`, with `S⁺` the
integral closure of `R⁺` in `S` (the finite étale pair `Huber.Pair.finiteEtale R⁺ S` of
AdicEtaleGeometry A1.2, *finite-etale-affinoid-algebra*), `(S, S⁺)` is a perfectoid Huber pair whose tilt `(S♭, S♭⁺)` has `S♭⁺`
the integral closure of `R♭⁺` in `S♭`. Consequently `Spa(S, S⁺) → Spa(R, R⁺)` is a finite étale
morphism of affinoid perfectoid spaces (AdicEtaleGeometry A1.3). AdicSpacesPartIV R5 uses this as its
finite étale step downstream ([Berkeley] Thm 7.4.5(1); [HK] Prop. 2.15(a)) ([ECD] §6, Thm 6.1(i), p. 26).
This subsection re-exports P3.9's essential-surjectivity milestone
(*finite-etale-untilting-essentially-surjective*): `isPerfectoidTateRing_of_finiteEtale` and the
instance `FiniteEtale.naturalPerfectoid` are that milestone's conclusion, registered here, and are
not a second proof target; nothing in P3.5–P3.9 depends on them. *Needs:* P3.9
(*finite-etale-untilting-essentially-surjective*); AdicEtaleGeometry A1.2 and A1.3.

Lean: `isPerfectoidTateRing_of_finiteEtale` (with the finite-module topology, `S` is a complete
Hausdorff perfectoid Tate ring); the Lean `example` checks the split case `R × R`.

### P3.11 almost purity, categorical form

**Almost purity, categorical form: `(R°a)_afet ≃ FÉt(R)` by inverting `ϖ`, compatibly with
tilting.** (*almost-finite-etale-equivalence*) Let `R` be a perfectoid Tate ring with tilt `R♭`,
`ϖ = (ϖ♭)♯` a pseudouniformiser with `ϖ^p | p`, and `R⁺ ⊆ R°` any ring of integral elements. Then:
(a) the functor `(R°a)_afet → FÉt(R)`, `A ↦ A_*[ϖ⁻¹]` (natural topology), is an equivalence of
categories with quasi-inverse `S ↦ S°a`, identified with `S⁺a` after the
change of basic setup in (c), compatible with tensor products and base change along
maps of perfectoid Tate rings; (b) the six categories

`FÉt(R) ≃ (R°a)_afet ≃ (R°a/ϖ)_afet = (R♭°a/ϖ♭)_afet ≃ (R♭°a)_afet ≃ FÉt(R♭)`

of Scholze's diagram are equivalent by the functors of *finite-etale-untilting-functor*, and the
composite is the tilting equivalence of *finite-etale-tilting-equivalence*; (c)
`(R⁺a)_afet ≃ (R°a)_afet` by extension along `R⁺ → R°`: the quotient
`R°/R⁺` is almost zero as an `R⁺`-module. The two almost categories use the
basic setups `(R⁺, R°°)` and `(R°, R°°)` respectively (layer P1; [ECD] Def. 3.23). For a perfectoid algebra over a characteristic-zero perfectoid field, inverting `p` gives
`R°a_afet ≃ R_fet`; in characteristic `p`, inverting a pseudouniformiser `t` gives `S°a_afet ≃ S_fet`. Tilting gives
`R°a_afet ≃ S°a_afet` for `S = R♭` ([Sch12] §7, Thm 7.9(ii)–(iii) and its proof, p. 42;
[ECD] §6, Thm 6.1 for the general perfectoid Tate ring). *Needs:* P3.9.

For (b), `finiteEtaleTiltEquiv_sixCategories` uses compatible rooted
pseudouniformisers `ϖ♭` and `ϖ = (ϖ♭)♯` with `ϖᵖ | p` in `R°`.
It states that the two reduction functors, each P0's
`Almost.Algebra.finiteEtaleBaseChange` along the actual quotient map, are
equivalences. The middle equivalence transports the scalar action by sharp
modulo the parameters; ring equivalences on almost elements, natural on
arrows, specify that transport. The composite of inverse inversion,
reduction, inverse sharp transport, inverse reduction and inversion is
naturally isomorphic to `(finiteEtaleTiltEquiv p R).functor` ([Sch12] diagram
after Prop. 5.22, pp. 28–29, and Thm 7.9, p. 42).

For (c), `almostFiniteEtale_equivPlus` states the equivalence for every
perfectoid pair `(R,R⁺)`. It specifies the inverse as restriction from
`R°` to `R⁺` through natural ring equivalences on almost elements that
preserve the inclusion's scalar action. Thus its forward functor is
extension along `R⁺ → R°`; it uses P1's `almostSetupPlus` and
`almostModuleEquivPlus` ([ECD] Example 3.22(ii) and Def. 3.23, p. 19).

### P3.12 the integral closure is almost finite étale

**The integral closure is almost finite étale: `S°` over `R°` for `S` finite étale over a perfectoid
Tate ring `R`.** (*integral-closure-almost-finite-etale*) Let `R` be a perfectoid Tate ring (any
characteristic, no perfectoid base field), `R⁺ ⊆ R°` a ring of integral elements, `ϖ` a
pseudouniformiser, `S ∈ FÉt(R)` and `S⁺` the integral closure of `R⁺` in `S`; almost mathematics is
that of `(R°, R°°)` (layer P1). Then: (i) `S°` is the integral closure of `R°` in `S`,
`S°° ⊆ S⁺ ⊆ S°`, and `S°a` is almost finite étale over `R°a`; equivalently,
`S⁺a` is almost finite étale over `R⁺a` under the change of basic setup in P3.11(c): almost finitely
presented, almost projective, and unramified (the diagonal idempotent of `S ⊗_R S` is an almost
element of `S° ⊗_{R°} S°`); (ii) `S°a` is uniformly almost finite projective: there is `n ≥ 0` such
that for every `ε ∈ R°°` there are `R°`-linear maps `S° → (R°)ⁿ → S°` composing to multiplication by
`ε`; (iii) `Tr_{S/R}(S°) ⊆ R°` and the trace pairing induces an almost isomorphism
`S°a → alHom_{R°a}(S°a, R°a)`; (iv) if `S` is faithfully flat over `R`, `S°a` is almost faithfully
flat over `R°a`, `Tr_{S/R}(S°°) ⊇ R°°` (up to almost zero), and `R°a → S°a` is almost split. Not
claimed, and false in general: `S°` finite, flat or étale over `R°`, or `S` free over `R` ([ECD] §6,
Thm 6.1(iii), p. 26, for (i); [Sch12] Thm 5.25 and Thm 7.9(iii), pp. 29, 42, for (ii) over a
perfectoid field; [GR] §4.1, Theorem 4.1.14 and Corollary 4.1.11, pp. 74–75, for (iii)–(iv)).
*Needs:* P3.11.

The proposed Lean hypotheses are `f : R ⟶ S` between `PairCat p` objects and
`Pair.IsFiniteEtale f`, which fixes the finite-module topology and the
integral-closure plus ring. Clause (i) is
`Pair.integralClosure_powerBounded` together with
`Pair.integralClosure_almostFiniteEtale`; clause (ii) is
`Pair.integralClosure_uniformlyAlmostFiniteProjective`, with a bound `n`
chosen before `ε`. Clause (iii), `Pair.integralClosure_trace`, states both
trace containment and an almost isomorphism from `S°` to its `R°`-linear
dual whose evaluation is `Tr(st)`. Clause (iv),
`Pair.integralClosure_faithfullyFlat`, assumes faithful flatness of the
specified ring map and gives almost faithful flatness, a topologically
nilpotent trace preimage for every `ε ∈ R°°`, and `R°`-linear maps
`rε : S° → R°` with `rε(f(a)) = εa`. Sources for the additional clauses are
[Sch12] Prop. 5.23, pp. 28–29, and Thm 7.9(iii), pp. 42–43;
[GR] (4.1.7), Cor. 4.1.11 and Thm 4.1.14, pp. 74–75.

`Perfectoid.FiniteEtale.trace` is the trace of multiplication for a finite
projective étale algebra. `FiniteEtale.trace_retraction` characterizes it
using any retraction `S → Rⁿ → S`: if `aᵢ` are the coordinate functionals
and `bᵢ` the images of the standard basis, its value at `s` is `∑ᵢ aᵢ(s bᵢ)`.
This agrees with P0's trace in the classical basic setup and requires no
freeness assumption ([GR] Def. 4.1.1, p. 72, and (4.1.7), p. 74).
`FiniteEtale.trace_eq_of_free` identifies it with Mathlib’s `Algebra.trace`
whenever the algebra is finite free.

**Checks.** `FiniteEtale.trace_zero` gives zero on the zero algebra;
`FiniteEtale.trace_one` gives `Tr(s)=s` on the identity algebra;
`FiniteEtale.trace_two` gives `Tr(s₀,s₁)=s₀+s₁` on the split rank-two algebra.
`FiniteEtale.trace_nonconstant_rank` uses the projection `K × K → K` for a
field `K`: the module is not free and the trace sends `x` to `(x,0)`.
`integral_trace_zero_not_faithful` excludes the zero algebra from the faithful
clause over a nonzero base. `integral_trace_characteristic_two` gives
`Tr(1,1)=0` but `Tr(1,0)=1` in characteristic two: faithful flatness does not
require the trace of the unit to be a unit.

Lean: `exists_uniformlyAlmostFiniteProjective_powerBounded` (one `n` such that for every `ε ∈ R°°`,
`ε • id_{S°}` factors through `(R°)ⁿ`).

### P3.13 the almost purity theorem

The almost purity theorem collects the three conclusions proved above into one statement over an
arbitrary perfectoid Tate ring.

**The almost purity theorem for perfectoid Tate rings.** (*almost-purity-theorem*) For a perfectoid
Tate ring `R` ([ECD] Def. 3.1; characteristic `0`, `p`, or neither; no perfectoid base field) with
tilt `R♭`, the almost purity theorem ([ECD] §6, Thm 6.1, p. 26) is implied by the conjunction of P3.10 (every
`S ∈ FÉt(R)` is perfectoid), P3.9 (tilting `S ↦ S♭` is an equivalence `FÉt(R) ≃ FÉt(R♭)` with
quasi-inverse the untilting functor) and P3.12 (`S°` is almost finite étale and uniformly almost
finite projective over `R°`, equivalently `S⁺a` over `R⁺a`; categorically P3.11; P3.12's uniform
almost finite projectivity being [Sch12] Thm 5.25 and Thm 7.9(iii), pp. 29, 42), and is not stated
again here; for `R = K` a perfectoid field it is P3.7, and its consequence that (finite) étale
morphisms of perfectoid spaces are strongly (finite) étale is *etale-is-strongly-etale* (P3.17).
*Needs:* P3.10; P3.9; P3.12.

**Checks.**

- `almost_purity_test_identity` (degenerate) — `S = R`: (i) `R` is perfectoid; (ii) `R♭ ↦ R♭`;
  (iii) `R° = R°`, finite étale over itself, so almost finite étale, with `n = 1`: for each `ε ∈ R°°` use
  the identity followed by multiplication by `ε`. The composite sends `x` to `εx`;
  `almost_purity_test_scalar_composite` asserts uniform almost finite projectivity
  with bound one for `Almost.toAlmost (almostSetup p R) R°` and computes
  this composite in the almost category. `almost_purity_test_identity_negative`
  asserts that two identity arrows there do not compose to `0 • id` when `R ≠ 0`.
  Thus both Checks use the almost module occurring in the theorem.
  The example `almost_purity_test_identity` applies
  `Pair.integralClosure_almostFiniteEtale` to `𝟙 R` itself ([ECD] Theorem 6.1(iii), p. 26).
- `almost_purity_test_product` (degenerate) — `S = R × R` (finite étale of rank `2`, the split
  cover): `S` is perfectoid with `ϖ_S = (ϖ, ϖ)` and `S° = R° × R°`
  (`almost_purity_test_product_uniform`, `almost_purity_test_product_perfectoid`);
  the latter Check also computes `S° = R° × R°` and the pseudouniformizer `(ϖ,ϖ)`.
  Here `S♭ = R♭ × R♭`, and `S°` is
  finite étale over `R°` outright, so the almost statement holds with `n = 2`: use the identity followed by componentwise multiplication by
  any `ε ∈ R°°`. The ordinary finite projectivity also gives a splitting for `ε = 1`.
  The example `almost_purity_test_product` applies `Pair.integralClosure_almostFiniteEtale`
  to the diagonal pair map `(R,R⁺) → (R × R,R⁺ × R⁺)`;
  `almost_purity_test_product_finiteEtale` applies `FiniteEtale.isPerfectoid` to this
  split algebra with its product topology ([ECD] Theorem 6.1(i), (iii), p. 26).
- `almost_purity_test_zero` (degenerate) — `S = 0`, the finite étale algebra of rank `0`: the zero
  ring satisfies the definition of a perfectoid Tate ring (`0` is a topologically nilpotent unit,
  `0^p ∣ p`, Frobenius on `0` is bijective) and `0♭ = 0`; the statement is vacuous.
- `almost_purity_test_not_etale_integrally` (non-example of a stronger claim) — `R = K = ℚ_p^cycl`
  and `S = L = K(p^{1/ℓ})` for a prime `ℓ ∤ p(p − 1)`: `|p|^{1/ℓ} ∉ |K^×| = |p|^{ℤ[1/p]/(p−1)}`, so
  `L/K` is totally ramified of degree `ℓ` with value group index `ℓ`; `L° ≠ K°[p^{1/ℓ}]` (an
  element `a p^{1/ℓ}` with `1 < |a| < |p|^{−1/ℓ}`, which exists since `|K^×|` is dense, lies in
  `L°` but not in `K°[p^{1/ℓ}]`) and `L°` is not a finite free `K°`-module, while `L°a` is almost
  finite étale over `K°a` (Tate); (iii) does not assert étaleness or finiteness of `S°` over `R°`.
  The Check supplies a finite étale pair map with `L = K(a)`, `a^ℓ = p`,
  degree `ℓ`, and almost finite étale integral map, while its ordinary integral
  map is neither finite nor étale. Almost purity is [ECD] Theorem 6.1(iii), p. 26;
  the obstruction is the displayed value-group calculation (compare the
  shrinking-different computation in [Berkeley] Example 7.3.3, p. 51).
  The extension `K(√p)` is not an example: `√p ∈ ℚ_p(ζ_p)` for `p ≡ 1 (mod 4)` and
  `K(√p) = K(ζ_4)` is unramified for `p ≡ 3 (mod 4)`.

### P3.14 finite étale morphisms of perfectoid spaces

**Finite étale morphisms of perfectoid spaces.** (*finite-etale-morphism-of-perfectoid-spaces*) Let
`X, Y` be perfectoid spaces (layer P2: the full subcategory of the adic spaces of AdicSpaces locally
of the form `Spa(R, R⁺)`, `R` perfectoid). A morphism `f : Y → X` is finite étale if it is finite
étale as a morphism of analytic adic spaces (AdicEtaleGeometry A1.3: `X` has a cover by open
affinoids `V = Spa(A, A⁺)` with `f⁻¹(V) ≅ Spa(B, B⁺)` over `V`, `B ∈ FÉt(A)` with its natural
topology and `B⁺` the integral closure of `A⁺`). AdicEtaleGeometry states this
predicate in Lean on `TauCeti.AdicSpace` (`AdicSpace.IsFiniteEtale`, A1.3) through finite étale
maps of Huber pairs (`Huber.Pair.Hom.IsFiniteEtale`, A1.2); its form on the analytic Yoneda carrier,
`YonedaAdicSpace.IsFiniteEtale`, is an A1.9 target specified in its README only. In
`PerfectoidSpace`, define `IsFiniteEtale f` as `YonedaAdicSpace.IsFiniteEtale` applied to the image
of `f` under `YonedaAdicSpace.ofAdicSpace` (A1.16; perfectoid spaces being adic spaces);
`IsFiniteEtale.iff_adic` records this identity. Prove `IsFiniteEtale.iff_forall_affinoidPerfectoid` (the defining condition of [ECD]:
for every open affinoid perfectoid `U = Spa(R, R⁺) ⊆ X` the preimage `f⁻¹(U) = Spa(S, S⁺)` is
affinoid perfectoid with `R → S` finite étale and `S⁺` the integral closure of `R⁺` in `S`), which is
equivalent by *perfectoid-vs-analytic-finite-etale*, as are [Sch12] Def. 7.1(ii) (a cover of `X` by
such affinoids) and [Berkeley] Def. 7.5.1(1). `X_fét` denotes the category of perfectoid spaces
finite étale over `X` (all `X`-morphisms); for `X = Spa(R, R⁺)` affinoid perfectoid, global sections
give `X_fét ≃ FÉt(R)^op`. Conventions: the plus ring is the integral closure, never `S°` when
`R⁺ ≠ R°`; `f` need not be surjective; the degree `x ↦ dim_{k(x)}(O_Y ⊗ k(x))` is locally constant
([ECD] §6, Def. 6.2(i), p. 26). *Needs:* AdicEtaleGeometry A1.2 and A1.3 (finite étale Huber pairs
and finite étale morphisms of analytic adic spaces) and A1.9 (their Yoneda form).

**Checks.**

- `PerfectoidSpace.IsFiniteEtale.test_fold` (degenerate) — for every perfectoid space `X`,
  `X ⊔ X → X` and `∅ → X` are finite étale, and the identity is finite étale of degree `1`.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsFiniteEtale.test_kummer` (computation) — over
  `X = Spa(ℚ_p^cycl⟨T^{±1/p^∞}⟩, ℤ_p^cycl⟨T^{±1/p^∞}⟩)`, `Spa(R[u]/(u^ℓ − T)) → X` (`ℓ ≠ p` prime)
  is finite étale of degree `ℓ`, and its source is perfectoid.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsFiniteEtale.test_rational` (non-example) — the inclusion of the rational subset
  `{|T| ≤ |p|}` into the perfectoid closed disc is étale but not finite étale.

The global signatures use P2's `PerfectoidSpace.Perfd p`, the full subcategory
of `PreAdicSpace` defined by sheafiness and actual open perfectoid affinoid charts.
`IsFiniteEtale` quantifies over every such chart and requires a cartesian
square with `Spa(S) → Spa(R)` induced by a finite étale pair map.
The perfectoid-pair condition `Perfectoid.Pair.IsFiniteEtale` includes the finite
module, étale algebra, module topology, and integral-closure plus-ring conditions.
`finiteEtale_spa_iff` identifies the affinoid condition with the global one.
`IsFiniteEtale.iff_adic` compares this with the supplied
`YonedaAdicSpace.IsFiniteEtale`, which requires a finite étale cartesian
chart around each point of the target. There is only one analytic finite étale
predicate on the Yoneda carrier.

**Checks.** `finite_identity`, `finite_empty`, `finite_open_not_closed`
compute the identity, the empty inclusion, and the failure of finiteness for
any nonclosed open inclusion. The analogous analytic Checks are
`analytic_finite_identity`, `analytic_finite_empty`, `analytic_finite_nonclosed`.
At pair level, `pair_finite_identity`, `pair_finite_zero`, and
`pair_finite_strict_plus` test the identity, the zero algebra, and a bijective
ring map whose target plus ring is strictly larger than the image of the
source plus ring. The last map is not finite étale.

### P3.15 étale morphisms of perfectoid spaces

Étale morphisms of perfectoid spaces are the local composites of open immersions and finite étale
maps; the strong variants carry the almost finite étale condition explicitly, and the comparison with
AdicEtaleGeometry A1.3 identifies étale with strongly étale, and finite étale with strongly finite étale.

**Étale morphisms of perfectoid spaces.** (*etale-morphism-of-perfectoid-spaces*) A morphism
`f : Y → X` of perfectoid spaces is étale if it is étale in the local sense of AdicEtaleGeometry
A1.3 (`AdicSpace.IsEtaleLocalDescription`, stated in Lean on `TauCeti.AdicSpace`; its Yoneda form
`YonedaAdicSpace.IsEtaleLocalDescription` is an A1.9 target specified in AdicEtaleGeometry's README
only): every `y ∈ Y` has an open neighbourhood `V ⊆ Y` such
that `f|_V` factors as `V ↪ W → U ↪ X` with `V → W` an open immersion, `W → U` finite étale (P3.14)
and `U ⊆ X` open. `W` is then automatically perfectoid. This is [ECD] Def. 6.2(ii) (whose printed
condition `y ∈ Y` is read as `y ∈ V`), [Sch12] Def. 7.1(iii) and [Berkeley] Def. 7.5.1(2). Equivalent
local form: `U` may be taken a rational subset of an affinoid perfectoid open of `X`, `W = Spa(S, S⁺)`
with `S ∈ FÉt(O(U))`, and `V` a rational subset of `W` — here `R = O(U)` is a perfectoid Tate ring,
`S` is finite étale over it, and almost mathematics on the chart is that of `(R°, R°°)` (layer P1) —
so étale morphisms are locally composites "rational embedding, finite étale, rational embedding" of
affinoid perfectoid spaces; they need not be separated or quasi-compact. In `PerfectoidSpace`, define
`IsEtale f` as `YonedaAdicSpace.IsEtaleLocalDescription` applied to the image of `f` under
`YonedaAdicSpace.ofAdicSpace` (A1.16); `IsEtale.iff_adic` records this identity. Prove `IsEtale.of_isOpenImmersion`
(open immersions are étale) and `IsEtale.id` (the identity of any perfectoid space is étale)
([ECD] §6, Def. 6.2(ii), p. 26; [Sch12] Definition 7.1(iii), p. 39). *Needs:* AdicEtaleGeometry A1.3
(étale morphisms by the local description) and A1.9 (its Yoneda form); P3.14; layer P2.

**Checks.**

- `PerfectoidSpace.IsEtale.test_openImmersion` (degenerate) — open immersions of perfectoid spaces
  are étale; the identity is étale.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsEtale.test_rational_in_cover` (computation) — for `R` perfectoid, `S ∈ FÉt(R)`
  and a rational subset `V ⊆ Spa(S, S⁺)`, the composite `V → Spa(R, R⁺)` is étale (standard affinoid
  étale map).
- Non-example: the inclusion of the open unit disc (a
  non-quasi-compact open) into the closed perfectoid disc is étale but not finite étale; so is the
  quasi-compact open immersion `{|T| ≤ |p|} ↪ {|T| ≤ 1}` (P3.14, `test_rational`), whose image is
  not closed, while finite maps are closed.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsEtale.test_frobenius` (degenerate) — for `X` of characteristic `p` the
  absolute Frobenius `φ : X → X` is an isomorphism of perfectoid spaces (every `R` is perfect), hence
  finite étale of degree `1` and étale; nothing in this layer calls it inseparable, which it is only
  on the non-perfect `𝔽_p((t))` of P3.8.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsEtale.test_separatedness_not_required` (characterisation) — the doubled disc
  `X ⊔_U X → X` for a rational `U ⊊ X` is étale and not separated; étale morphisms need be neither
  separated nor quasi-compact, and the étale site of P3.18 contains such objects.

The proposed `IsEtale` uses open factorizations in `Perfd p` and their equality
with the given map; A1’s `YonedaAdicSpace.IsEtaleLocalDescription` uses the
corresponding factorizations on the analytic Yoneda carrier. `IsEtale.iff_adic` compares these, and
`perfectoid_of_analyticEtale` supplies perfectoidness of an analytic étale
source over a perfectoid base.

**Checks.** `etale_identity`, `etale_empty`, `etale_open_not_finite` test
identity, empty inclusion, and a nonclosed open inclusion which is étale but
not finite. `analytic_etale_identity`, `analytic_etale_empty`,
`analytic_etale_nonclosed` make the same distinctions on the analytic carrier.

### P3.16 strongly finite étale and strongly étale morphisms

**Strongly finite étale and strongly étale morphisms of perfectoid spaces; tilting invariance and
base change.** (*strongly-etale-morphisms-and-base-change*) Over an arbitrary perfectoid base
([Sch12] Def. 7.2 over a perfectoid field): a morphism `(R, R⁺) → (S, S⁺)` of perfectoid Huber pairs
is strongly finite étale if it is finite étale (`S ∈ FÉt(R)` with its natural topology, `S⁺` the
integral closure of `R⁺`) and `S°a` is almost finite étale over `R°a` (layer P0). A morphism
`f : Y → X` of perfectoid spaces is strongly finite étale if `X` has a cover by open affinoid
perfectoid `V` with `f⁻¹(V)` affinoid perfectoid and `(O_X(V), O⁺_X(V)) → (O_Y(f⁻¹V), O⁺_Y(f⁻¹V))`
strongly finite étale; strongly étale if locally on `Y` it factors as an open immersion, a strongly
finite étale map and an open immersion. Define `Perfectoid.Pair.IsStronglyFiniteEtale` (the affinoid
condition on a map of perfectoid pairs), `PerfectoidSpace.IsStronglyFiniteEtale` and
`PerfectoidSpace.IsStronglyEtale` (the two Prop-valued classes on morphisms). Properties: (a) `f` is
strongly (finite) étale iff its tilt `f♭` is (the almost finite étale condition is transported by
*almost-finite-etale-equivalence* (b)); (b) base change along arbitrary maps `Z → X` of perfectoid
spaces preserves both classes, with finite-étale affinoid formula `D = A ⊗_B C` (already complete, being finite
projective over `C`), `D⁺` the integral closure of `C⁺` in `D`, and `|Y ×_X Z| → |Y| ×_{|X|} |Z|`
surjective ([Sch12] Lem. 7.3(i)–(ii), with the printed `|X ×_Z Y|` read as the fibre product of the
base change); (c) composites of strongly (finite) étale maps are strongly (finite) étale ([Sch12]
Cor. 7.8); (d) in characteristic `p` every (finite) étale map is strongly (finite) étale, and by
almost purity this holds in general, by *etale-is-strongly-etale*, so the strong classes coincide with
*finite-etale-morphism-of-perfectoid-spaces* and *etale-morphism-of-perfectoid-spaces* ([Sch12] §7,
Def. 7.2(i), p. 39). *Needs:* P3.14; P3.15; P3.11; P3.12; layer P0
(almost finite étale algebras).

**Checks.**

- `PerfectoidSpace.IsStronglyFiniteEtale.test_charp` (computation) — for a characteristic-`p`
  perfectoid pair `R`, the diagonal `R → R × R` gives a strongly finite étale cover;
  `(a+b)^p = a^p+b^p` and componentwise Frobenius on `R × R` is bijective.
  The characteristic hypothesis is needed for these Frobenius assertions
  ([Berkeley] Proposition 6.1.6, pp. 42–43; [ECD] Theorem 6.1 and Definition 6.2, p. 26).
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsStronglyEtale.test_open` (degenerate) — open immersions are strongly étale;
  they are strongly finite étale only when also closed.
- Compatibility: `IsStronglyFiniteEtale f ↔ IsStronglyFiniteEtale f♭`.

`Pair.almostMap` is almostification of the actual restriction `R° → S°` of
the continuous pair map, over the source basic setup. `Pair.IsStronglyFiniteEtale`
requires it to be almost finite étale, in addition to the finite étale pair
condition. The global strong finite condition uses a covering by such
cartesian affinoid squares; the strong étale condition uses local open
factorizations. `Pair.finiteEtale_iff_strong`, `finiteEtale_iff_strong` and
`etale_iff_strong` are the three comparison theorems.

**Checks.**

- `pair_strong_identity`, `pair_strong_zero`, `pair_strong_tilt` test the
  identity, zero algebra, and preservation and reflection by actual pair tilting.
- `strong_finite_identity`, `strong_finite_clopen`, `strong_finite_tilt` test
  identity, a clopen inclusion, and geometric tilting.
- `strong_etale_identity`, `strong_etale_empty`, `strong_etale_open_not_finite`
  test identity, the empty open, and a nonclosed open which is strongly étale
  but not strongly finite étale.

### P3.17 comparison with AdicEtaleGeometry layer A1 and with finite étale algebras

**Comparison of perfectoid finite étale and étale morphisms with AdicEtaleGeometry layer A1 and with
finite étale algebras.** (*perfectoid-vs-analytic-finite-etale*) Let `X` be a perfectoid space.
(a) (Perfectoidness) If `g : Y → X` is a finite étale (resp. étale) morphism of analytic adic spaces
in the sense of AdicEtaleGeometry A1.3, then `Y` is a perfectoid space. (b) (Morphism classes) For
morphisms of perfectoid spaces the following are equivalent: finite étale in the sense of
AdicEtaleGeometry A1.3 (= *finite-etale-morphism-of-perfectoid-spaces*); [ECD] Def. 6.2(i) (for
every open affinoid perfectoid `U` the preimage is affinoid perfectoid, finite étale with
integral-closure plus ring); [Sch12] Def. 7.1(ii) (for one open affinoid perfectoid cover); [Berkeley]
Def. 7.5.1(1); strongly finite étale. Likewise étale in the sense of AdicEtaleGeometry A1.3 ⇔
[ECD] 6.2(ii) ⇔ [Sch12] 7.1(iii) ⇔ [Berkeley] 7.5.1(2) ⇔ strongly étale. (c) (Algebraic comparison)
For `X = Spa(R, R⁺)` affinoid perfectoid, the functors `X_fét → FÉt(R)^op` (global sections),
`FÉt(R) → {finite étale morphisms of Huber pairs (R, R⁺) → (S, S⁺)}` (`Huber.Pair.finiteEtale`, plus
ring forced to be the integral closure) and the latter `→` Mathlib `CommAlgCat.FiniteEtale R` (forget
topology and plus ring) are equivalences; every finite étale `R`-algebra is perfectoid for its
natural topology. (d) (Sites) The category of perfectoid spaces étale (resp. finite étale) over `X` is
the small étale (resp. finite étale) site of the underlying adic space in the sense of
AdicEtaleGeometry A1.6, with the same coverings; that layer's structure sheaves `O`, `O⁺` on it,
its Galois category of finite étale objects and its basis of affinoid objects apply. (e) (Base change
from adic spaces) If `Y' → X'` is a finite étale (resp. étale) morphism of locally strongly sheafy
analytic adic spaces (e.g. locally noetherian ones) and `Z → X'` is a morphism from a perfectoid
space, then `Y' ×_{X'} Z` exists and is finite étale (resp. étale) over `Z`, with ring on a finite-étale affinoid chart
`D = A ⊗_B C` and `D⁺` the integral closure of `C⁺` — this is AdicEtaleGeometry A1.5
(*etale-base-change*, pullback along finite étale and étale maps), used with its hypotheses; the
clause proved here is that `Y' ×_{X'} Z` is perfectoid ([Sch12] Lem. 7.3(iii)–(iv) and Prop. 7.10)
([ECD] §6, paragraph after Def. 6.2, p. 26). *Needs:* P3.10; AdicEtaleGeometry A1.1 (strongly
sheafy rings), A1.3 (finite étale and étale morphisms), A1.5 (*etale-base-change*) and A1.6 (the
sites).

`perfectoid_of_analyticFiniteEtale` and `perfectoid_of_analyticEtale` take
A1’s `YonedaAdicSpace.IsFiniteEtale` and `.IsEtaleLocalDescription`, respectively,
and a perfectoid target; their conclusion is `isPerfectoidSpace p Y` for the adic space underlying `Y`.
For (e), `perfectoid_finiteEtale_baseChange` and `perfectoid_etale_baseChange`
take locally strongly sheafy adic spaces `Y, X`, a finite étale or étale map
`f : Y → X`, a perfectoid `Z`, and a map
`Z.obj → YonedaAdicSpace.ofAdicSpace.obj X`. They produce a perfectoid `W`,
a projection `W → Z` in the corresponding perfectoid morphism class, and
a cartesian square in `YonedaAdicSpace` over `ofAdicSpace.map f`.
Thus the universal property includes all Yoneda-adic test spaces
([Sch12] Lemma 7.3(iii)–(iv), p. 40, Proposition 7.10, p. 43; [ECD]
Theorem 6.1 and Definition 6.2, p. 26, give the perfectoid Tate-ring form).

For (d), `globalSections_adicComparison` gives ring equivalences from
`globalSections p X = Γ(X, O_X)` (P2, the structure-sheaf sections of the underlying
`PreAdicSpace`) to the global sections of every adic representative
`A` with `ofAdicSpace.obj A ≅ X.obj`. They carry `globalPlus p X` exactly to
`AdicSpace.Oplus A ⊤` and commute with every pair of corresponding morphisms.
`etaleSheaves_adicComparison` gives an equivalence with the small étale
site of a locally strongly sheafy adic representative, preserving and reflecting
covering sieves, and natural isomorphisms identifying `etaleO` and `etaleOPlus`
with A1’s `structureSheafEtale` and `structureSheafPlusEtale` after forgetting
to additive groups and changing universes. The site comparison also transports
A1’s affinoid basis and Galois-category results.
`smallEtale.affinoidCover` gives every étale object an open covering by
affinoid perfectoid étale objects, and `smallFiniteEtale.galoisCategory`
concludes `GaloisCategory (smallFiniteEtale p X)` when
`ConnectedSpace (YonedaAdicSpace.space.obj X.obj)` holds ([Sch12]
7.11–7.13, p. 43; AdicEtaleGeometry A1.6
`AdicSpace.smallEtaleBasis_openCover` and `AdicSpace.smallFiniteEtale.galoisCategory`).

The following results support the comparison. Perfectoid Tate rings are strongly sheafy, and perfectoid
spaces are locally strongly sheafy (*perfectoid-tate-rings-are-strongly-sheafy*): for `R` perfectoid
Tate and every `n ≥ 0`, the Tate algebra `R⟨T_1, …, T_n⟩` (Tau Ceti
`Huber.restrictedMvPowerSeriesCompletion n R`) is stably uniform, hence sheafy for every ring of
integral elements, so `R` is strongly sheafy in the sense of AdicEtaleGeometry A1.1;
`PerfectoidSpace.stronglySheafy p R` concludes A1’s `Huber.IsStronglySheafy R`
for every complete Hausdorff perfectoid Tate ring `R`.
`PerfectoidSpace.locallyStronglySheafy p X` gives an adic space `A` with
`AdicSpace.IsLocallyStronglySheafy A` and an isomorphism
`YonedaAdicSpace.ofAdicSpace.obj A ≅ X.obj`. Every rational localisation and every finite étale algebra of a
perfectoid Tate ring is strongly sheafy, and the local-to-global description of finite étale maps,
fibre products of étale maps and the étale sites of AdicEtaleGeometry A1.3–A1.6 apply to perfectoid
spaces ([Berkeley] Lecture 6, §6.3, Example 6.3.2(1),
Propositions 6.3.3(3) and 6.3.4, pp. 47–48). Preimages of
affinoid perfectoid opens under finite étale maps are affinoid perfectoid, with strongly finite
étale ring map (*strongly-finite-etale-maps-are-affinoid-over-affinoids*): for `f : Y → X` finite
étale (a morphism of perfectoid spaces, or of analytic adic spaces with `X` perfectoid) and
`V = Spa(R, R⁺) ⊆ X` open affinoid perfectoid, `f⁻¹(V) = Spa(S, S⁺)` with `S = O_Y(f⁻¹V) ∈ FÉt(R)`
perfectoid and `S⁺` the integral closure of `R⁺`, `(R, R⁺) → (S, S⁺)` is strongly finite étale,
global sections give `V_fét ≃ FÉt(R)^op`, and strongly finite étale covers of `V` correspond to finite
étale `R`-algebras; in particular every finite étale morphism of perfectoid spaces satisfies [ECD]
Def. 6.2(i) ([Sch12] §7, Prop. 7.6). Every finite étale (resp. étale) morphism of perfectoid spaces is
strongly finite étale (resp. strongly étale) (*etale-is-strongly-etale*): for `f : Y → X` a morphism
of perfectoid spaces, `f` is finite étale iff strongly finite étale and étale iff strongly étale — in
characteristic `p` by *finite-etale-covers-in-characteristic-p*, in general by
*integral-closure-almost-finite-etale* — so the tilting invariance and base-change properties of the
strong classes hold for all (finite) étale morphisms ([Sch12] §7, after Thm 7.9).

### P3.17a.1 sousperfectoid rings

**Sousperfectoid Tate rings and perfectoid frames.** (*sousperfectoid-ring*) Fix a prime `p`
(the Lean declarations `PerfectoidFrame` and `IsSousperfectoid` take any `p : ℕ`). Let
`R` be a complete Hausdorff Tate ring (Tau Ceti `Huber.IsTateRing`) in which `p` is topologically
nilpotent — equivalently, a Tate ring with a continuous ring map `ℤ_p → R`, that is, a complete Tate
`ℤ_p`-algebra. A perfectoid frame for `R` is a triple `(R̃, ι, σ)` consisting of a perfectoid Tate
ring `R̃` satisfying P1.1's `Perfectoid.IsPerfectoidTateRing p R̃`,
a continuous ring homomorphism `ι : R → R̃`, and a continuous `R`-linear map
`σ : R̃ → R` (`R̃` an `R`-module through `ι`) with `σ ∘ ι = id_R`.
The ring predicate, as P1.1 defines it, is a condition on a complete Hausdorff Tate ring:
`R̃°` is bounded and some pseudouniformiser `ϖ ∈ R̃°` has `ϖ^p ∣ p` with Frobenius
`R̃°/ϖ → R̃°/ϖ^p` bijective; equivalently it includes completeness, Hausdorffness, uniformity,
an explicit prime, a pseudouniformizer with the required divisibility, and surjective
Frobenius modulo `p` (`TauCetiRoadmap.PerfectoidSpaces.Perfectoid.IsPerfectoidTateRing.iff_frobenius_surjective_modP`;
Berkeley Definition 6.1.1).
`R` is sousperfectoid if it admits a perfectoid frame; a Huber pair `(R, R⁺)` is
sousperfectoid if `R` is. Conventions: `ι` is then injective and a homeomorphism onto the closed
subring `ι(R) = ker(id − ι∘σ)`; `σ` need not be multiplicative and need not map any ring of integral
elements into `R⁺`; no perfectoid base field is fixed, and `R̃` is not required to contain one;
characteristic `p` is allowed, and then `R̃` is a perfect complete Tate ring. In `Huber`, define the
structure `PerfectoidFrame` (a perfectoid frame `(R̃, ι, σ)` for `R`) and the class
`IsSousperfectoid` (`R` is a Tate ring admitting a perfectoid frame); prove that a perfectoid
frame makes `R` sousperfectoid, `IsSousperfectoid.of_isPerfectoidTateRing` (perfectoid Tate rings
are sousperfectoid, with the identity frame `PerfectoidFrame.refl`),
`PerfectoidFrame.powerBoundedSubring_eq_comap` (`a ∈ R°` iff `ι(a) ∈ R̃°`: power-boundedness is detected in the
frame, Tau Ceti `Huber.powerBoundedSubring`), `IsSousperfectoid.isUniform` (sousperfectoid rings are
uniform, [*sousperfectoid-uniform*](#p3-17a-2) (P3.17a.2)), `IsSousperfectoid.isReduced` (sousperfectoid rings are reduced,
uniform rings being reduced), invariance under isomorphisms of
topological rings, base change of a frame along a map `R → S` of
complete Tate rings whose completed tensor product `R̃ ⊗̂_R S` is perfectoid (P3.17a.2, through
AdicSpacesPartIII R3.5's [*split-injection-completed-base-change*](../AdicSpacesPartIII/README.md) (AdicSpacesPartIII R3.5)), `isSousperfectoid_ratLoc` (rational
localisations of sousperfectoid rings are sousperfectoid, [*sousperfectoid-rational-localisation*](#p3-17a-2) (P3.17a.2)),
`IsSousperfectoid.finiteEtale` (finite étale algebras over sousperfectoid rings are sousperfectoid,
[*sousperfectoid-finite-etale*](#p3-17a-2) (P3.17a.2)), `IsSousperfectoid.restrictedMvPowerSeries` (Tate algebras over
sousperfectoid rings are sousperfectoid, [*sousperfectoid-rings*](#p3-17a-2) (P3.17a.2)), `isUniform_ratLoc`
(sousperfectoid pairs are stably uniform, [*sousperfectoid-stably-uniform*](#p3-17a-3) (P3.17a.3)) and
`IsSousperfectoid.isSheafyRing` (sousperfectoid pairs are sheafy and strongly sheafy, [*sousperfectoid-sheafy*](#p3-17a-3) (P3.17a.3)).
The closed-embedding assertion is Mathlib `Function.LeftInverse.isClosedEmbedding` applied to
`σ ∘ ι = id_R` and the continuity of `σ` and of `ι`, using the Hausdorff property of `R̃`
(Berkeley Lecture 6, §6.3, Def. 6.3.1, p. 47; HK §7, Def. 7.1, p. 25 (perfectoid frames); BHW §3.1,
Def. 3.2(1), p. 1724; Berkeley Lecture 6, §6.3, Ex. 6.3.2(1), p. 47 (perfectoid rings are
sousperfectoid with the frame `(R, id, id)`); Berkeley Lecture 6, §6.3, Ex. 6.3.2(2), p. 47
(`ℚ_p⟨T⟩` is sousperfectoid with frame `ℚ_p^cycl⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩` but not perfectoid)). *Needs:*
P1.1 (`Perfectoid.IsPerfectoidTateRing`) and P1.31 (`ℚ_p^cycl`); Tau Ceti `Huber.IsTateRing`,
`Huber.IsHuberRing`; Mathlib `ContinuousLinearMap`. Lean: `Huber.PerfectoidFrame`,
`Huber.PerfectoidFrame.refl`, `Huber.IsSousperfectoid`,
`Huber.IsSousperfectoid.of_isPerfectoidTateRing`,
`Huber.PerfectoidFrame.powerBoundedSubring_eq_comap`, `Huber.IsSousperfectoid.isUniform`,
`Huber.IsSousperfectoid.isReduced`.

**Checks.**

- Computation: `ℚ_p⟨T⟩` is sousperfectoid:
  `ι : ℚ_p⟨T⟩ → ℚ_p^cycl⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩` with `σ` = (the retraction `ℚ_p^cycl → ℚ_p`) applied to the
  coefficients followed by deleting the non-integral exponents is a perfectoid frame (Lean
  `example`, with the following non-example).
- Non-example: `ℚ_p⟨T⟩` is not a
  perfectoid Tate ring: Frobenius on `ℤ_p⟨T⟩/p = 𝔽_p[T]` is not surjective (`T` is not a `p`-th
  power), so "sousperfectoid" is strictly weaker than "perfectoid".
- Non-example: `A = ℚ_p⟨X, Q⟩/(Q²)` is strongly noetherian
  and sheafy (the AdicSpaces layer 4 example) but not sousperfectoid: a sousperfectoid ring is
  uniform, hence reduced, and `Q ≠ 0` is nilpotent. A definition by "sheafy", or by a splitting of
  abstract modules into a non-perfectoid ring, fails this test (Lean `example`).
- Degenerate: `ℚ_p` (the Tate algebra in zero variables) is
  sousperfectoid, with frame `ℚ_p → ℚ_p^cycl` split by a continuous `ℚ_p`-linear retraction
  (*sousperfectoid-p-adic-field*).
- Compatibility: every perfectoid Tate ring in the sense of
  layer P1 (for example `ℚ_p^cycl`, or `𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^∧`) is sousperfectoid via
  the identity frame.
- Characterisation: for a uniform complete Tate ring `A` of
  characteristic `p` whose Frobenius is finite, `A` is sousperfectoid iff Frobenius `A → A` splits as
  `A`-modules (HK §7, Lem. 7.10) (Lean `example`); for example `𝔽_p((t))⟨T⟩` is sousperfectoid.

- Non-example: the uncompleted field `ℚ_p(ζ_{p^∞})` with its
  `p`-adic topology is a Tate ring that admits no perfectoid frame at all: a
  frame `(R̃, ι, σ)` makes `ι` a homeomorphism onto the closed subgroup `ker(id − ι∘σ)` of the
  complete Hausdorff group `R̃`, so a sousperfectoid ring is complete and Hausdorff, which
  `ℚ_p(ζ_{p^∞})` is not (Lean `example`: a sousperfectoid ring is Hausdorff and complete). The class
  `Huber.IsSousperfectoid` therefore omits completeness and
  the Hausdorff property, and omits the topological nilpotence of `p` (which holds in `R̃` since
  `ϖ^p ∣ p` there, and descends along the embedding `ι`): all three are consequences, not
  hypotheses. The same control shows that [*split-injection-completed-base-change*](../AdicSpacesPartIII/README.md) (AdicSpacesPartIII R3.5) cannot produce a
  frame on a non-complete `S`.
- Convention: the identity `σ ∘ ι = id_R` is on `R`;
  on `R̃` the composite `ι ∘ σ` is only an idempotent: for `R = ℚ_p`, `R̃ = ℚ_p^cycl` and
  `σ` = Tate's normalised trace (a continuous `ℚ_p`-linear retraction, `σ = [K_n : ℚ_p]^{-1} Tr`
  on `K_n = ℚ_p(ζ_{p^n})`), `ι(σ(ζ_{p²})) = σ(ζ_{p²}) = 0 ≠ ζ_{p²}` (the primitive `p²`-th roots of
  unity sum to `μ(p²) = 0`), while `σ(ι(1)) = 1`; `ζ_p` is a poorer witness, since for `p = 2`,
  `ζ_2 = −1 ∈ ℚ_2` and `ι(σ(ζ_2)) = ζ_2`. The assertion that the reversed composite
  can fail assumes `R ≠ 0` (Lean `example`: `σ ∘ ι = id`, `ι ∘ σ` is idempotent, and over a nonzero
  `R` it is not the identity for every frame).
- Negative control: for `R = 0` the unital map
  `ι : R → R̃` forces `R̃ = 0`, and both composites are identities. A counterexample to
  the reversed identity cannot be demanded over the zero ring.

<a id="p3-17a-2"></a>

### P3.17a.2 stability of the class

**Base change of a frame.** The continuous splitting used here is AdicSpacesPartIII R3.5's
[*split-injection-completed-base-change*](../AdicSpacesPartIII/README.md) (AdicSpacesPartIII R3.5), which this roadmap cites and does not restate. For a
frame `(R̃, ι, σ)` of a Tate ring `R` and a continuous map `R → S` to a complete Tate ring for
which the completed tensor product `R̃ ⊗̂_R S` (AdicSpacesPartII R0, [*completed-tensor-product*](../AdicSpacesPartII/README.md) (AdicSpacesPartII R0.3))
is perfectoid, `(R̃ ⊗̂_R S, s ↦ 1 ⊗ s, σ ⊗̂ id)` is a frame of `S`, with embedding `s ↦ 1 ⊗ s`
and retraction `x ⊗ s ↦ σ(x)s` on pure tensors (HK Rem. 7.2, p. 25). Completeness and
Hausdorffness of the target are required. Its unit-coefficient, zero-scalar and two-term Checks
are `σ_S(x ⊗ 1) = σ(x)`, `σ_S(x ⊗ 0) = 0` and `σ_S(x ⊗ s + y ⊗ t) = σ(x)s + σ(y)t`.


**Checks.**

- For `S = R` the pure-tensor formula recovers the original retraction.
- A tensor with zero second factor is sent to zero.
- For `x⊗s + y⊗t` the retraction gives `σ(x)s + σ(y)t`.

*Needs:* P3.17a.1; AdicSpacesPartIII R3.5 (*split-injection-completed-base-change*);
AdicSpacesPartII R0.3 (*completed-tensor-product*).

**Sousperfectoid rings are uniform.** (*sousperfectoid-uniform*) Let `R` be a complete Tate ring
that is sousperfectoid with frame `(R̃, ι, σ)`. Prove that `R° = ι^{-1}(R̃°)` and that `R°` is
bounded, that is, `R` is uniform in the sense of HK Definition 2.3 (AdicSpaces layer 4.2); in

HK §2, Def. 2.3, p. 3 (uniformity descends along strict inclusions); HK §2, after Def. 2.3, p. 3
(uniform rings are reduced); Berkeley Lecture 7, introduction, p. 49 (perfectoid Tate rings are
uniform by definition)). As predicted, `ℚ_p⟨T⟩° = ℤ_p⟨T⟩` is bounded, while `ℚ_p⟨X, Q⟩/(Q²)` has
the unbounded power-bounded subring `ℤ_p⟨X⟩ + ℚ_p⟨X⟩Q` and so is not sousperfectoid. *Needs:*

**Rational localisations of sousperfectoid rings are sousperfectoid.** (*sousperfectoid-rational-localisation*) Let `(R, R⁺)` be a Huber pair with `R` sousperfectoid,

`(R̃, ι, σ)` and a ring of integral elements `R̃⁺ ⊆ R̃°` containing `ι(R⁺)` — which can be taken to
be the integral closure in `R̃` of the subring generated by `ι(R⁺)` and the topologically nilpotent
elements `R̃°°`, an open subring contained in `R̃°` — the preimage `Ũ` of `U` in `X̃ = Spa(R̃, R̃⁺)`

and `(𝒪_X̃(Ũ), ι ⊗̂ id, σ ⊗̂ id)` is a perfectoid frame for `𝒪_X(U)` (Berkeley Lecture 6, §6.3,

along the rational localisation); Berkeley Lecture 6, §6.2, Thm 6.2.6, p. 45 (rational
localisations of perfectoid Tate rings are perfectoid); HK §3, Prop. 3.8, p. 8 (rational
localisations of perfectoid rings, with no base field, are perfectoid)). For `R = ℚ_p⟨T⟩` and

of `A → B`)). Thus if `R → S` is a finite Galois étale cover and `S` is sousperfectoid then `R` is

**Laurent algebras and annuli over sousperfectoid rings are sousperfectoid.** (*sousperfectoid-annulus*) Let `R` be sousperfectoid with pseudo-uniformizer `ϖ` and let `a ≤ b` be
integers, so that the annulus is non-empty when `R ≠ 0`; the radii are integral powers of `|ϖ|`.
Prove that `R⟨T^{±1}⟩` and the annulus ring `R⟨T/ϖ^a, ϖ^b/T⟩ := 𝒪(W)` for the rational subset
`W = {|ϖ^b| ≤ |T| ≤ |ϖ^a|}` of `Spa(R⟨S⟩, R⁺⟨S⟩)` with `T = ϖ^a S` are sousperfectoid (HK §7,
Lem. 7.3, p. 25). In `Spa R⟨S⟩` one has `|S| ≤ 1`, so `|T| ≤ |ϖ^a|` is automatic and `W` is the
rational subset `R({ϖ^{b−a}}/S) = {|ϖ^{b−a}| ≤ |S|}` (its weight `ϖ^{b−a}` is a unit, so it
generates the unit ideal and `|S| ≠ 0` is implied). Witness of the convention: for `R = ℚ_p`,
`ϖ = p`, `a = 0`, `b = 1`, `W = {|p| ≤ |T| ≤ 1}` is the closed annulus with `𝒪(W) = ℚ_p⟨T, p/T⟩`;
for `a = 1`, `b = 0` the inequalities `|p^0| ≤ |T| ≤ |p|` have no solution and `W = ∅`, whose ring
`𝒪(∅) = 0` is sousperfectoid for a trivial reason — the hypothesis `a ≤ b` is what makes the
identification of `W` with `R({ϖ^{b−a}}/S)` correct (a formal statement reading the exponent as
`(b − a).toNat` would, for `a > b`, describe the Laurent annulus `R({1}/S)` instead of `∅`).
Over a perfectoid field `L`, the closed annulus `{|ϖ| ≤ |T| ≤ 1}` is a
sousperfectoid, non-perfectoid affinoid. *Needs:* [*sousperfectoid-rings*](#p3-17a-2) (P3.17a.2);
[*sousperfectoid-rational-localisation*](#p3-17a-2) (P3.17a.2); Tau Ceti `ValuationSpectrum.rationalSubset`.

**Checks.** The ambient disc condition
`|S| ≤ 1` is explicit for every valuation of the chosen plus ring. At `(a,b)=(0,1)` rational
membership is then exactly `|p| ≤ |S| ≤ 1`; reversing the exponents would replace `p` by `1`.


**Checks.**

- For `R = ℚ_p` and `(a,b) = (0,1)`, the section ring is `ℚ_p⟨T,p/T⟩`.
- At `a = b`, the Laurent coordinate has absolute value exactly `|ϖ|^a`.
- For `(a,b) = (1,0)` the annulus is empty; replacing `b−a` by its truncated natural value would give a nonempty Laurent annulus.

**Bounded retractions for countable extensions of discretely valued fields.**
(*countable-extension-retraction*) Let `K` be a complete nonarchimedean field with discrete
nontrivial valuation, and `L/K` a complete isometric nonarchimedean field extension whose
underlying `K`-vector space is the closure of the span of a countable family. Construct a
continuous `K`-linear map `σ : L → K` with `σ(a) = a` for `a ∈ K` and `|σ(z)| ≤ |z|`
(HK §7, Rem. 7.8, p. 26, for the countable-extension splitting; Schneider11 §1, Lem. 1.7(ii),
pp. 6–7, for spherical completeness of `K`). Prove the bounded extension step: start with
the identity on `K`, adjoin the countable generators one at a time, and extend a functional
`f` satisfying `|f(v)| ≤ |v|` by choosing its value `b` on the new vector `z` in the nested
closed balls `{b ∈ K : |b − f(v)| ≤ |z − v|}`, `v` in the previous span. The ultrametric
inequality makes these balls nested; spherical completeness gives their intersection.
The resulting compatible functionals have bound `1` on the dense union; completeness of `K`
extends them to `L`, giving the cyclotomic retraction in the field application. *Needs:* Mathlib `ContinuousLinearMap`, `Submodule.span`, `Dense`,
`CompleteSpace`; P1.31 for the cyclotomic completion used in the application.
Lean: `Huber.exists_countable_extension_retraction`.

**Checks.**

- For `L = K`, the retraction is the identity and has operator norm `1`.
- For `K/ℚ_p` finite and `L = K^cycl`, a union of finite cyclotomic levels supplies a
  countable spanning family and the retraction fixes `1`.
- An orthonormal basis for the given norm is not needed: `ℚ_p(√p)` contains a vector of
  norm `p^{-1/2}`, whereas coefficients in an orthonormal `ℚ_p`-basis would give only
  norms in `p^ℤ`. Weighted orthogonal coordinates are compatible with the construction.

**Finite extensions of `ℚ_p` are sousperfectoid.** (*sousperfectoid-p-adic-field*) Let `K` be a
finite extension of `ℚ_p` and `K^cycl` the
completion of `K(μ_{p^∞})`. Prove that `K → K^cycl` admits a continuous `K`-linear retraction, so
that `(K^cycl, inclusion, retraction)` is a perfectoid frame and `K` is sousperfectoid; more
generally `K⟨T₁, …, Tₙ⟩` and every rational localisation and finite étale algebra of it are
sousperfectoid (HK §7, Rem. 7.8, p. 26 (nonarchimedean fields with a perfectoid countable profinite
étale extension are sousperfectoid); Berkeley Lecture 6, §6.3, Ex. 6.3.2(2), p. 47). The
retraction is supplied by [*countable-extension-retraction*](#p3-17a-2) (P3.17a.2): the finite cyclotomic levels have
a countable union dense in `K^cycl`, and the valuation on `K` is discrete. The perfectoidness
of `K^cycl` follows from P1.31 and P3.10, since it is a finite extension of
`ℚ_p^cycl`. Thus
`K` is sousperfectoid but not perfectoid. Write `p = uπ^e` for a uniformizer `π` of `K`.
If `e < p`, no topologically nilpotent `ϖ` satisfies `ϖ^p ∣ p`. If `e ≥ p`, that divisibility
can hold (take `ϖ = π`), but Frobenius on `𝒪_K/p` is not surjective: the class of `π` has
valuation `1`, whereas a nonzero `p`-th power has valuation divisible by `p`, modulo `π^e`.
For `K = ℚ_p`, Frobenius on `𝔽_p` is surjective and the divisibility is the obstruction;
for the totally ramified extension with `π^p = p`, the divisibility holds and Frobenius fails.
Both examples fail the perfectoid input predicate: `ℚ_p` fails the divisibility condition,
and the extension with `π^p = p` fails Frobenius surjectivity modulo `p`. Every affinoid algebra of the form `K⟨T⟩⟨f/g⟩`, and every
smooth affinoid over `K` that is étale over a polydisc through a composite of rational localisations
and finite étale maps, is sousperfectoid. *Needs:* [*sousperfectoid-ring*](#p3-17a-1) (P3.17a.1); [*sousperfectoid-rings*](#p3-17a-2) (P3.17a.2);
[*sousperfectoid-rational-localisation*](#p3-17a-2) (P3.17a.2); [*sousperfectoid-finite-etale*](#p3-17a-2) (P3.17a.2); [*countable-extension-retraction*](#p3-17a-2) (P3.17a.2); the Frobenius criterion of P1.1
(`Perfectoid.IsPerfectoidTateRing.iff_frobenius_surjective_modP`) and `ℚ_p^cycl` (P1.31), with finite étale perfectoid extensions (P3.10).
Lean: `Huber.IsSousperfectoid.of_finite_padic`.

**Checks.**

- `ℚ_p` is sousperfectoid but fails perfectoid divisibility (Lean `example`).
- The finite extension with `π^p = p` satisfies divisibility and fails Frobenius
  surjectivity modulo `p` (Lean `example`).
- `K⟨T⟩` is sousperfectoid; Frobenius on `K°⟨T⟩/p` misses its
  coordinate `T`, so sousperfectoidness does not imply perfectoidness.

<a id="p3-17a-3"></a>

### P3.17a.3 stable uniformity and sheafiness

**Sousperfectoid pairs are stably uniform.** (*sousperfectoid-stably-uniform*) Let `(R, R⁺)` be a
Tate Huber pair with `R` complete Tate and sousperfectoid and `R⁺` any ring of integral elements.
That `(R, R⁺)` is stably uniform — for every rational subset `U ⊆ Spa(R, R⁺)`, `𝒪(U)` is uniform
(HK Definition 3.13; AdicSpaces layer 4.2) — is the splitting criterion *stably-uniform-sheafy*
(AdicSpacesPartIII layer R3; KL15 Rem. 2.8.12) applied to the frame map `ι : R → R̃`, `R̃` perfectoid and hence
stably uniform by the perfectoid rational-localization argument, with the retraction `σ` (Berkeley Lecture 6, §6.3,
Prop. 6.3.4, p. 48). BHW's Proposition 3.3 is this statement; on the closed unit disc over `ℚ_p`
it says that every rational localisation `ℚ_p⟨T⟩⟨f/g⟩` is reduced and uniform. *Needs:*
[*sousperfectoid-rational-localisation*](#p3-17a-2) (P3.17a.2); [*sousperfectoid-uniform*](#p3-17a-2) (P3.17a.2); *stably-uniform-sheafy*
(AdicSpacesPartIII layer R3); the perfectoid rational-localisation argument of P2.3.
Lean: `Huber.isUniform_ratLoc`.


**Checks.**

- The whole-space rational localization recovers the uniform coefficient ring.
- The rational annulus `ℚ_p⟨T,p/T⟩` is uniform by its localized frame.
- The empty rational subset has zero section ring and vacuous boundedness.

**Sousperfectoid pairs are sheafy, strongly sheafy and `𝒪`-acyclic.** (*sousperfectoid-sheafy*) Let
`(R, R⁺)` be a Tate Huber pair with `R` sousperfectoid, as in [*sousperfectoid-stably-uniform*](#p3-17a-3) (P3.17a.3).
Prove that `(R, R⁺)` is sheafy, so that `Spa(R, R⁺)` is an affinoid adic space in the sense of
AdicSpaces layer 5, that `H^i(Spa(R, R⁺), 𝒪) = 0` for `i > 0`, and that `R` is strongly sheafy:
every `R⟨T₁, …, Tₙ⟩` is sheafy — the predicate `Huber.IsStronglySheafy` of AdicEtaleGeometry
AdicEtaleGeometry layer A1 (*strongly-sheafy-huber-pair*) (BHW §3.1, Prop. 3.3, p. 1724 (citing Berkeley 6.3.4); HK §7,
Cor. 7.4, p. 25 (strong sheafiness of sousperfectoid rings); HK §3, Prop. 3.14, p. 9
(Buzzard–Verberkmoes–Mihara)). By this route `Spa(ℚ_p⟨T⟩, ℤ_p⟨T⟩)` is sheafy without using
noetherianity. For nonzero perfectoid `S`, `Spa(S⟨T⟩, S⁺⟨T⟩)` is sheafy although
`S⟨T⟩` is not perfectoid. It can be noetherian: take `S` to be a perfectoid field. *Needs:* [*sousperfectoid-stably-uniform*](#p3-17a-3) (P3.17a.3); [*sousperfectoid-rings*](#p3-17a-2) (P3.17a.2);
*stably-uniform-sheafy*, [*sheafy-cech-acyclicity*](../AdicSpacesPartIII/README.md) (AdicSpacesPartIII R3.1) (AdicSpacesPartIII layer R3); AdicEtaleGeometry layer A1
(*strongly-sheafy-huber-pair*).

The sheafiness statement supplies the affinoid adic space for any
chosen ring of integral elements, and the strong sheafiness is
AdicEtaleGeometry A1's predicate; both are `Huber.IsSousperfectoid.isSheafyRing` in Lean. The acyclicity statement
asserts vanishing of the ordinary additive structure-sheaf cohomology in positive
degree, using Mathlib's `Sheaf.H` and its explicit sheafification and Ext assumptions; it is
specified in this README only.

<a id="p3-17a-4"></a>

### P3.17a.4 sousperfectoid spaces


**Checks.**

- For the closed `ℚ_p` disc, sheafiness follows without a noetherianity premise.
- For nonzero perfectoid `S` the one-variable disc is sheafy although its coordinate is not a p-th power modulo `ϖ`.
- The empty affinoid has zero structure sheaf and vanishing positive-degree cohomology.

**Sousperfectoid adic spaces.** (*sousperfectoid-adic-space*) An adic space `X` (AdicSpaces layer 5:
an object of Huber's category `𝒱` covered by affinoid adic spaces) is sousperfectoid if it admits an
open cover by affinoid adic spaces `Spa(R, R⁺)` with `R` sousperfectoid (*sousperfectoid-ring*);
such `Spa(R, R⁺)` are adic spaces by [*sousperfectoid-sheafy*](#p3-17a-3) (P3.17a.3). Equivalently, the open affinoid
subspaces `Spa(R, R⁺) ⊆ X` with `R` sousperfectoid form a basis of the topology of `X`. No base is
fixed; `X` lives over `Spa ℤ_p` because `p` is topologically nilpotent on every chart. A
sousperfectoid space is analytic, its charts being Tate. A morphism of sousperfectoid spaces is a
morphism of adic spaces. In `AdicSpace`, define the predicate `IsSousperfectoid` (`X` admits an open
cover by `Spa(R, R⁺)` with `R` sousperfectoid); prove `IsSousperfectoid.spa` (`Spa(R, R⁺)` is a
sousperfectoid adic space for `R` sousperfectoid), that
perfectoid spaces are sousperfectoid, that open subspaces of
sousperfectoid spaces are sousperfectoid, that the sousperfectoid
affinoid opens form a basis of the topology of `X`, `IsSousperfectoid.isAnalytic` (every point of a
sousperfectoid space is analytic), that `𝒪_X(U)` is reduced for
every open `U`, `IsSousperfectoid.of_etale` (étale over sousperfectoid is sousperfectoid,
[*sousperfectoid-etale-stability*](#p3-17a-4) (P3.17a.4)), that relative polydiscs exist
(`𝔹^n_X = X ×_{Spa ℤ_p} Spa ℤ_p⟨T₁, …, Tₙ⟩` exists and is sousperfectoid, locally `Spa R⟨T⟩`; on a

  opens.
- Non-example: `Spa(ℚ_p⟨X, Q⟩/(Q²))` is an adic
  space (strongly noetherian) but not sousperfectoid: sections of `𝒪` over any open of a
  sousperfectoid space are reduced (products and equalizers of reduced rings), while `Q ≠ 0` is
  nilpotent in the global sections.
- Degenerate: the empty adic space and
  `Spa(ℚ_p, ℤ_p)` are sousperfectoid.


The predicate `AdicSpace.IsSousperfectoid p X` is exactly the existence, at each
point, of a Part II `AdicSpace.Chart` whose coordinate ring is sousperfectoid
and whose open immersion contains that point in its image.
The empty space satisfies this condition (Lean `example`);
a nonzero nilpotent section on any open excludes it (Lean `example`);
the closed disc over `ℚ_p` satisfies it.
Together with the closed-disc and perfectoid Checks above, these distinguish the
local condition from perfectoidness and from merely being analytic.

**Étale spaces over a sousperfectoid space are sousperfectoid adic spaces.** (*sousperfectoid-etale-stability*) Let `X` be a sousperfectoid adic space and `f : Y → X` étale in
the local-description sense of AdicEtaleGeometry layer A1 (Kedlaya–Liu Definition 8.2.16: every
`y ∈ Y` has an open neighbourhood on which `f` factors as an open immersion, a finite étale morphism
and an open immersion, where finite étale means affinoid-locally on the target
`Spa(S, S⁺) → Spa(R, R⁺)` with `R → S` finite étale and `S⁺` the integral closure of `R⁺`); for
locally noetherian targets this is Huber's étale ([*differentials-unramified-smooth-etale*](../AdicSpacesPartII/README.md) (AdicSpacesPartII R0.16), AdicSpacesPartII layer R0;
the comparison with the local description is AdicEtaleGeometry layer A1,
[*etale-morphisms-local-description-and-comparison*](../AdicEtaleGeometry/README.md) (AdicEtaleGeometry A1.4)). Prove that `Y` is an adic space (not
merely a preadic space) and is sousperfectoid. In particular every object of the étale site `X_ét`
is a sousperfectoid adic space, and for a finite étale `R`-algebra `S` over a sousperfectoid `R` and
a composite of rational localisations and finite étale maps `R → S'`, the ring `S'` itself is
sousperfectoid. For a general étale map, sousperfectoidness is a property of the space `Y`, not of a
global ring: `Y` is covered by sousperfectoid affinoids, while the sousperfectoid property of rings
is not known to be of local nature (Berkeley Appendix to Lecture 19, §19.5, p. 179 (étale objects
over a sousperfectoid space are sousperfectoid adic spaces); KL15 §8.2, Def. 8.2.16, p. 162 (étale
morphisms of (pre)adic spaces by local description); KL15 §8.2, Rem. 8.2.18, p. 162 (why a class
stable under finite étale maps is needed); HK §5, Def. 5.1, p. 14 (étale in the naive sense:
locally a composition of rational localisations and finite étale maps); BHW §3.1, proof of
Cor. 3.4, p. 1725 (the étale step, which BHW attribute to 6.3.3(ii), the finite étale case)). Thus
any `Y ∈ X_ét` is itself sousperfectoid and in particular an adic space, and BHW's step "algebras
étale over a sousperfectoid algebra are again sousperfectoid" holds for composites of rational
localisations and finite étale maps and, for general étale maps, in the space-level form above.

**Sousperfectoid spaces are stably adic.** (*sousperfectoid-stably-adic*) Let `X = Spa(R, R⁺)` with
`R` sousperfectoid, with `X_ét` in the local-description sense of AdicEtaleGeometry layer A1, and
let `B_X` be the class of objects `Y → X` of `X_ét` of the form `Y = Spa(S, S⁺)` with

an affinoid adic space). Define on AdicEtaleGeometry A1's small étale category of `X` the class generated by
the identity: start with the identity object up to isomorphism and close under rational
embeddings, finite étale maps and isomorphisms over `X`. This is `B_X`.
Prove that its members are basic objects in the sense of AdicEtaleGeometry A1's [*basis-comparison*](../AdicEtaleGeometry/README.md) (AdicEtaleGeometry A1.6) for an
affinoid base. AdicEtaleGeometry A1's class also starts from arbitrary affinoid open charts; those charts are
not additional starting objects of `B_X`. Prove,
for an explicit base `X = Spa(A₀, A₀⁺)` with `A₀` sousperfectoid (`Huber.IsSousperfectoid p A₀`) and
`U ∈ B_X`: for every sheafy complete affinoid presentation
`U ≅ Spa(A, A⁺)`, the ring `A` is sousperfectoid. Rational localisation and finite
étale stability give this assertion (HK Def. 7.1 and Lemma 7.5(a), p. 25); a cover by
sousperfectoid charts alone does not give it, since locality of the ring property is unknown
(HK Def. 7.1, p. 25).
The stable-basis statement says that `B_X` consists of affinoids, covers
every étale object by open immersions, and admits fibre products over `X` within `B_X`;
it also names the local strong-sheafiness supplied by [*sousperfectoid-sheafy*](#p3-17a-3) (P3.17a.3).
The constructors include every rational subdomain and finite étale extension of a member.
Thus `B_X` is a stable basis in the sense of Kedlaya–Liu Definition 8.2.19, p. 163,
using the identity-generated basis of HK's proof of Proposition 5.5, p. 15.
The covering-reduction criterion is supplied by AdicEtaleGeometry A1.6
(*etale-covering-reduction*). Consequently, by
[*stable-basis-etale-vector-bundles*](../AdicEtaleGeometry/README.md) (AdicEtaleGeometry A1.6a) (Kedlaya–Liu Theorem 8.2.22(c),(d)): for every finite projective
`R`-module `M`, `M̃` is an acyclic sheaf on `B_X`, in particular `H^i(X_ét, 𝒪) = 0` for `i > 0`; and
finite projective `R`-modules are equivalent to finite locally free `𝒪_{X_ét}`-modules. For a
general sousperfectoid adic space these statements hold on every sousperfectoid affinoid open, and
such opens cover `X`. The class of all affinoid objects `Spa(S, S⁺)` of `X_ét` with `S`
sousperfectoid is not used as the basis: its closure under fibre products would need

define `X_ét` and stable bases for preadic spaces over an analytic field; here, as in Berkeley
§19.5, they are used over `ℤ_p`, the proofs of Kedlaya–Liu 8.2.20–8.2.22 not using the base field
(KL15 §8.2, Def. 8.2.19, p. 163 (stable bases and stably adic spaces); KL15 §8.2, Rem. 8.2.18,
p. 162; HK §1, Introduction, p. 3 (finite étale covers of sousperfectoid spaces); KL15 §8.2, after
Def. 8.2.19, p. 163 (a stable basis must be closed under fibre products, which is why the basis is
the composites of rational localisations and finite étale maps); HK §5, proof of Prop. 5.5, p. 15

particular sousperfectoid, pairs); KL15 §8.2, Thm 8.2.22(c),(d), p. 165). For `X` affinoid

**Base change of étale maps to locally noetherian spaces along sousperfectoid spaces.** (*sousperfectoid-etale-base-change*) Let `Z` be a sousperfectoid adic space, possibly non-noetherian. Its charts are stably sheafy; the formula below uses the stably sheafy case of [*fibre-products-existence*](../AdicSpacesPartII/README.md) (AdicSpacesPartII R0.7), rather than requiring the locally noetherian case; let `W` be a locally noetherian analytic adic space (for example a rigid space),
so that étale maps to `W` have the local open-immersion/finite-étale description (Huber Lemma 2.2.8
through AdicEtaleGeometry layer A1); let `g : Z → W` be a morphism and `f : Y → W` étale (AdicSpacesPartII layer R0).
Prove that the fibre product `Z ×_W Y` exists in the category of adic spaces, that the projection
`Z ×_W Y → Z` is étale in the local-description sense of AdicEtaleGeometry layer A1, and that
`Z ×_W Y` is sousperfectoid. Affinoid formula: if `Y' ⊆ Y` is open and `f|_{Y'}` factors as an open
immersion `Y' → Y''` followed by a finite étale morphism `Y'' = Spa(B, B⁺) → W' = Spa(A, A⁺)` onto
an affinoid open `W' ⊆ W` (`A → B` finite étale, `B⁺` the integral closure of `A⁺`; such
factorisations exist locally by Huber Lemma 2.2.8), and `Z' = Spa(C, C⁺) ⊆ g^{-1}(W')` is an
affinoid open with `C` sousperfectoid, then `C ⊗_A B` is sousperfectoid,
`Z' ×_{W'} Y'' = Spa(C ⊗_A B, integral closure of C⁺ in C ⊗_A B)`, and `Z' ×_W Y'` is its open
subspace lying over `Y'` (Berkeley Lecture 7, §7.5, after Def. 7.5.1, p. 55 (Huber-étale maps of
analytic adic spaces are locally an open immersion followed by a finite étale map); KL15 §8.2,
Def. 8.2.16, p. 162; BHW §3.1, proof of Cor. 3.4, p. 1725 (the étale step)). For `W = 𝔹^n_L`,
`Z = X ×_L 𝔹^n` with `X` affinoid perfectoid and `Y → 𝔹^n` étale, `Z ×_W Y = X ×_L Y` is the BHW
product; for `Y = W'` an open subspace of `W`, `Z ×_W Y = g^{-1}(W')`. *Needs:*
