### P3.17b perfectoid spaces times polydiscs


**Checks.**

- Base change of an identity map is the original sousperfectoid space.
- For a rational open the pullback is its rational preimage with the localized frame.
- An empty source gives the empty pullback, which is sousperfectoid.

**Perfectoid space times a polydisc: sousperfectoid, not perfectoid.** (*perfectoid-times-polydisc*)
Let `L` be a perfectoid field, `X = Spa(S, S⁺)` an affinoid perfectoid space over `L` and
`𝔹^n_L = Spa(L⟨T₁, …, Tₙ⟩, 𝒪_L⟨T⟩)`. Prove that the fibre product `X ×_L 𝔹^n_L` exists in adic
spaces and equals `Spa(S⟨T₁, …, Tₙ⟩, S⁺⟨T₁, …, Tₙ⟩)`, which is a sousperfectoid affinoid adic space
(BHW §3.1, proof of Cor. 3.4, p. 1725 (the perfectoid-times-polydisc step); Berkeley Lecture 6,
§6.3, Prop. 6.3.3(3), p. 47), and that for `n ≥ 1` and `S ≠ 0`, `S⟨T₁, …, Tₙ⟩` is not perfectoid
(proved here: `T₁` is not a `p`-th power in `S°⟨T⟩/ϖ` for nonzero `S`, the argument of the
`ℚ_p⟨T⟩` non-example of [*sousperfectoid-ring*](#p3-17a-1) (P3.17a.1); Berkeley Lecture 6, §6.3, Ex. 6.3.2(2), p. 47, for
`ℚ_p⟨T⟩`).
Thus `ℚ_p^cycl⟨T⟩` is sousperfectoid and not perfectoid, its perfectoid cover
`ℚ_p^cycl⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩` being a frame; and a smooth weight disc times a nonempty perfectoid space is not
perfectoid. *Needs:* [*sousperfectoid-rings*](#p3-17a-2) (P3.17a.2); [*sousperfectoid-sheafy*](#p3-17a-3) (P3.17a.3);
[*completed-tensor-restricted-power-series*](../AdicSpacesPartII/README.md) (AdicSpacesPartII R0.3), [*affinoid-fibre-product*](../AdicSpacesPartII/README.md) (AdicSpacesPartII R0.7) (AdicSpacesPartII layer R0); P1.1, P1.10 and P2.9; Tau Ceti
`ValuationSpectrum.mem_iff_forall_vle_one`, `Huber.restrictedMvPowerSeriesCompletion`.
Lean: `Huber.not_isPerfectoidTateRing_restrictedMvPowerSeries`.


**Checks.**

- Degenerate: the zero ring is a perfectoid Tate ring in the sense of
  the P1 structure (`0` is a topologically nilpotent unit, `0^p ∣ p = 0`, Frobenius on `0` is
  surjective), hence sousperfectoid with the identity frame; this is why
  [*perfectoid-times-polydisc*](#p3-17b) (P3.17b) needs `S ≠ 0`: `0⟨T⟩ = 0` is perfectoid (Lean `example`).
- In zero variables the product is the original perfectoid affinoid.
- For a nonempty perfectoid affinoid and one variable, the coordinate is not a p-th power modulo the pseudouniformizer.

### P3.18 the étale site and the finite étale site

The étale site of a perfectoid space is the étale site of its underlying adic space; tilting
identifies it with the site of the tilt, and `O⁺` is almost acyclic on affinoids.

**The étale site `X_ét` and the finite étale site `X_fét` of a perfectoid space.**
(*etale-site-of-perfectoid-space*) Let `X` be a perfectoid space. Its étale site `X_ét` is the small
étale site of the underlying locally strongly sheafy analytic adic space (AdicEtaleGeometry A1.6;
*perfectoid-tate-rings-are-strongly-sheafy*): objects the adic spaces étale over `X` — all perfectoid
(*perfectoid-vs-analytic-finite-etale* (a)), i.e. the perfectoid spaces étale over `X` of [ECD] —
with all `X`-morphisms (étale by *etale-morphisms-composition-base-change-open* (cancellation)), and the topology
generated by jointly surjective families (on all points, including higher-rank ones). The finite
étale site `X_fét` is the full subcategory of finite étale objects with the induced jointly surjective
topology (AdicEtaleGeometry A1.6). `X_ét` has finite limits (fibre products of perfectoid spaces,
layer P2) and a basis of affinoid perfectoid objects closed under rational subsets and finite
étale maps. Fibre products admit covers by these objects; over an affinoid perfectoid
base, the fibre product of two affinoid perfectoid objects is affinoid perfectoid; a morphism `X' → X` of perfectoid spaces induces a morphism of sites
`X'_ét → X_ét` by base change, and a morphism to a locally strongly sheafy analytic adic space `Y`
induces `X_ét → Y_ét`; `U ↦ O_U(U)` and `U ↦ O⁺_U(U)` are sheaves of commutative
rings on `X_ét`, as is the sheaf quotient `O⁺/ϖ`. Relative to an explicit almost
basic setup, `O^{+a}` is a sheaf of almost algebras; on each affinoid base
`Spa(R,R⁺)` the geometric setup is `(R⁺, R°°)`; for `X = Spa(R, R⁺)` affinoid perfectoid, `X_fét ≃ FÉt(R)^op` (the contravariance
is global sections: the split cover `X ⊔ X = Spa(R × R, R⁺ × R⁺) → X` corresponds to the algebra
`R × R`, and the map `X ⊔ X → X` to the diagonal `R → R × R`).
The two-component Check `finite_etale_test_contravariance_two_components` applies
`finiteEtaleAffinoidEquiv` to the actual first inclusion
`Spa(R) → Spa(R × R)`, with the finite-algebra pair supplied by
`finiteEtalePairFunctor`. Through `finiteEtaleAffinoidSectionsIso` and the affinoid
section identifications, its image sends `(x,y)` to `x`; its composite with the
fold map is the identity on `Spa(R)` ([ECD] Def. 6.2 and the following affinoid
comparison, p. 26). For `X` connected,
`X_fét` is a Galois category with fundamental group `π₁(X)` (AdicEtaleGeometry A1.6 and A1.8), equal to
`Gal(K^sep/K)` for `X = Spa(K, K⁺)`, `K` a perfectoid field. In `PerfectoidSpace`, define
`smallEtale X` as the category of perfectoid spaces étale over `X` (equivalent to `YonedaAdicSpace.smallEtale X.obj`,
where here and below `X.obj` also denotes the image of the underlying adic space under
`YonedaAdicSpace.ofAdicSpace`) and `smallEtaleTopology` as the Grothendieck topology of jointly surjective
families; `smallEtale.isPerfectoid` takes an object of the supplied
`YonedaAdicSpace.smallEtale X.obj` and proves that its adic source is perfectoid.
Its input has no perfectoid-source hypothesis ([ECD] Theorem 6.1 and Definition 6.2,
p. 26; [Sch12] §7, Definition 7.11, p. 43). *Needs:* *perfectoid-tate-rings-are-strongly-sheafy*; P3.17;
*strongly-finite-etale-maps-are-affinoid-over-affinoids*.

**Checks.**

- Computation: for `K` a perfectoid field,
  `Spa(K, O_K)_fét ≃` finite continuous `Gal(K^sep/K)`-sets (via the Galois category of
  AdicEtaleGeometry A1.8; by *fontaine-wintenberger* these are also the finite continuous
  `Gal(K♭^sep/K♭)`-sets, which is the tilting equivalence `Spa(K, O_K)_fét ≃ Spa(K♭, O_{K♭})_fét` of
  P3.20 on this example).
- `PerfectoidSpace.smallEtale.test_empty` (degenerate) — for `X = ∅` the site has a single object
  (`∅`) covered by the empty family; for `X = Spa(C, C⁺)` with `C` algebraically closed, every finite
  étale object is a finite disjoint union of copies of `X`, so `X_fét ≃ FintypeCat`.
- Computation: for `X = Spa(C, O_C)` with `C`
  algebraically closed, `|X|` is one point and the étale objects are the (arbitrary, not only
  finite) disjoint unions of copies of `X`, with all maps between them: `X_ét ≃ Set` with the
  jointly surjective coverings, so `Sh(X_ét) ≃ Set` and every sheaf has vanishing higher
  cohomology; for `X = Spa(C, C⁺)` with `C⁺ ⊊ O_C`, `|X|` consists of the rank-one point and its
  specialisations, the valuations of the residue field of `O_C` bounded by `1` on `C⁺/C°°`.
  When that residue field is algebraic over `𝔽_p`, integral closedness forces
  `C⁺ = O_C`, so the strict inclusion case does not occur. In general these
  specialisations need not form a chain, and `X_ét` has the open
  subspaces of disjoint unions of `X` as further objects, while `X_fét ≃ FintypeCat` still.
- Compatibility: `PerfectoidSpace.smallEtale p X ≌ YonedaAdicSpace.smallEtale X.obj`,
  with covering sieves preserved and reflected for
  `YonedaAdicSpace.smallEtaleTopology X.obj (isAnalytic_adic p X)`.

Étale and finite étale morphisms of perfectoid spaces satisfy composition, base change,
cancellation, openness and tilting (*etale-morphisms-composition-base-change-open*): since P3.14
and P3.15 agree with the classes of AdicEtaleGeometry A1.3 by the comparisons `IsFiniteEtale.iff_adic` and
`IsEtale.iff_adic`, the stability properties —
composites of (finite) étale morphisms are (finite) étale; for `f : Y → X` (finite) étale and any
`g : X' → X` the fibre product `Y ×_X X'` (layer P2, agreeing with the fibre product of adic spaces)
is (finite) étale over `X'` with finite-étale affinoid formula `D = A ⊗_B C`, `D⁺` the integral closure of `C⁺`,
and `|Y ×_X X'| → |Y| ×_{|X|} |X'|` surjective; cancellation (if `g` and `g ∘ f` are (finite) étale,
so is `f`); openness of étale morphisms, quasi-compact open image when the source is quasi-compact,
and the diagonal of an étale (resp. finite étale) morphism an open (resp. open and closed) immersion
— are AdicEtaleGeometry A1.5 (*etale-composition*, *etale-base-change*, *etale-diagonal*),
used here with the hypotheses stated there (perfectoid spaces are locally strongly sheafy by
*perfectoid-tate-rings-are-strongly-sheafy*); the one clause proved here is tilting: `f` is
(finite) étale iff its tilt `f♭ : Y♭ → X♭` is, which is P3.16(a) together with *etale-is-strongly-etale*
([Berkeley] Lecture 7, §7.5, Proposition 7.5.2(4), p. 55, for tilting;
Proposition 7.5.2(1)–(3) for the stability properties).

`smallEtale` and `smallFiniteEtale` are full subcategories of the actual slice
`Over X`; their morphisms are all commuting triangles. `smallEtaleTopology`
and `smallFiniteEtaleTopology` declare a sieve covering exactly when its maps
are jointly surjective on valuation points. `finiteEtaleAffinoidEquiv` gives
the opposite finite-algebra comparison. `etaleBaseChange` is the geometric
pullback functor. `etaleTiltFunctor` restricts P2's slice tilt, and
`etaleTilt_covers` preserves and reflects covering sieves.
The geometric obligation is `etaleTiltFunctor_isEquivalence` for every perfectoid
`X` ([ECD] Theorem 6.3, p. 26). `etaleTilt_preservesFiniteLimits` applies Mathlib’s
`CategoryTheory.Adjunction.isEquivalencePreservesLimits` to that instance.

**Checks.**

- `site_identity_object`, `site_empty_object`, `site_nonfinite_object` test
  membership of identity, empty inclusion, and nonclosed open inclusion in the
  étale slice. `finite_site_identity_object`, `finite_site_empty_object`,
  `finite_site_excludes_nonclosed_open` distinguish the finite subcategory.
- `topology_empty_cover`, `topology_nonempty_no_empty_cover`,
  `topology_identity_cover`: the empty sieve covers exactly an empty object,
  and the identity sieve covers every object. The finite-site versions are
  `finite_topology_empty_cover`, `finite_topology_nonempty_no_empty_cover`,
  `finite_topology_identity_cover`.
- `site_geometric_point`: the equivalence `etaleGeometricPointEquiv` sends the
  split double cover of `Spa(C,O_C)` to a set of cardinality two. The equivalence
  covers arbitrary permitted disjoint unions and uses the full valuation ring.
- `site_point_galois`: `finiteEtaleGaloisEquiv` sends the split double cover
  of `Spa(K,O_K)` to a two-element set with trivial absolute Galois action
  ([ECD] Definition 6.2, p. 26).
- `tilt_site_identity` and `tilt_finite_identity`: the identity object over
  `Spa(R,R⁺)` tilts to `Spa(R♭,R♭⁺)` with the structure map prescribed by
  `tiltSpaIso`, in the étale and finite étale slices ([ECD] Theorem 6.3, p. 26).

`smallEtaleAdicEquiv` and `smallFiniteEtaleAdicEquiv` compare the perfectoid
sites with the supplied Yoneda-adic sites. Their object equations keep the
underlying spaces and maps, and their covering equations identify the two
joint-surjectivity topologies. `stronglySheafy` supplies the perfectoid input
to the analytic stability theorems of P3.17. `IsEtale.cancel`,
`IsFiniteEtale.cancel`, `IsEtale.isOpenMap` and `IsEtale.diagonal` state
cancellation, openness and the open diagonal. P2.16's `pullback_points`
gives surjectivity on compatible pairs of valuation points for all morphisms of
perfectoid spaces, including étale morphisms.

**Checks.** `site_empty_unique` and `finite_site_empty_unique` identify each
empty-base category with the one-object category; `finite_site_geometric_point`
identifies finite étale objects over `Spa(C,O_C)` with finite sets.

The supplied sites are `YonedaAdicSpace.smallEtale`,
`YonedaAdicSpace.smallFiniteEtale`, `YonedaAdicSpace.smallEtaleTopology`,
and `YonedaAdicSpace.smallFiniteEtaleTopology`; their topologies take the
analyticity proof `isAnalytic_adic p X`.
`smallEtaleAdicEquiv` and `smallFiniteEtaleAdicEquiv` forget the perfectoid
structure, with object, map and covering equations. `finiteEtaleAffinoidSectionsIso`
identifies the algebraic comparison with actual global sections and pullback.

**Checks.** `analytic_site_identity`, `analytic_site_empty`, and
`analytic_site_nonfinite` compute the identity and empty objects and retain
nonfinite open immersions. `analytic_finite_site_identity`,
`analytic_finite_site_empty`, and `analytic_finite_site_nonclosed` make the
corresponding finite-site distinction. `analytic_topology_empty`,
`analytic_topology_nonempty`, and `analytic_topology_identity` test the empty
cover, its failure on a nonempty object, and the identity cover;
`analytic_finite_topology_empty`, `analytic_finite_topology_nonempty`, and
`analytic_finite_topology_identity` test the finite-site topology.

**Checks.** `smallEtaleAdicEquiv_identity`, `smallEtaleAdicEquiv_empty`,
and `smallEtaleAdicEquiv_nonfinite` assert that forgetting to A1 preserves
an identity object, the empty source, and failure of finiteness of an étale object.
`smallFiniteEtaleAdicEquiv_identity`, `smallFiniteEtaleAdicEquiv_empty`, and
`smallFiniteEtaleAdicEquiv_distinct_arrows` preserve identity and empty sources
and distinguish two different arrows in the finite site.

The fold Check `PerfectoidSpace.IsFiniteEtale.test_fold` uses the actual
natural pair of `R²`. The rational-disc Check
`PerfectoidSpace.IsFiniteEtale.test_rational` uses P1's `perfectedTateAlgebra`,
its coordinate, and P2's valuation-space homeomorphism: the subdisc
`|T| ≤ |ϖ|` is étale but not finite. The affine Frobenius Check
`PerfectoidSpace.IsEtale.test_frobenius_affinoid` specifies the ring map
`x ↦ x^p`, its geometric isomorphism, and both étale classes.

The Laurent-torus Check `PerfectoidSpace.IsFiniteEtale.test_kummer` fixes
constants and sends every monomial of exponent `a ∈ ℤ[1/p]` to exponent
`ℓa`, for positive `ℓ` prime to `p`; it is finite étale on pairs and spectra.
`PerfectoidSpace.IsEtale.test_rational_in_cover` tests restriction of any
finite étale map to an open source. The doubled-open Check
`PerfectoidSpace.IsEtale.test_separatedness_not_required` constructs the
pushout of two copies of `X` along a nonclosed open `U`: the fold map is
étale and its diagonal has nonclosed image. This applies to the doubled-disc
example. The two `…BaseChange_map_fst` equations fix base change on morphisms
by the pullback projections.

### P3.19 étale descent

**Étale descent for finite étale morphisms and finite projective modules on perfectoid spaces.**
(*etale-descent-perfectoid*) Let `X` be a perfectoid space with étale site `X_ét`
of *etale-site-of-perfectoid-space*. (a) (Locality) A morphism `f : Y → X` of perfectoid spaces is
finite étale if, for some covering `{X_i → X}` in `X_ét`, every base change `Y ×_X X_i → X_i` is
finite étale; étaleness of `f` is local on `Y` and on `X` for open coverings — for rational
coverings this is AdicEtaleGeometry A1.2 (*finite-etale-rational-descent*, KL 2.6.9), and the
étale-covering case is proved here. (b) (Stack) The prestack `U ↦ U_fét` (finite étale perfectoid
spaces over `U`, with isomorphisms) on `X_ét` is a stack for the étale topology (Mathlib
`CategoryTheory.Pseudofunctor.IsStack`): finite étale spaces with descent data along an étale
covering descend uniquely (the sheaf property of `U ↦ O(U)` on `X_ét` that it rests on is
AdicEtaleGeometry A1.6, *etale-structure-sheaf*). (c) (Vector bundles) For `X = Spa(R, R⁺)`
affinoid perfectoid, the equivalence `M ↦ M ⊗_R O_{X_ét}` between finitely generated projective
`R`-modules and finite locally free `O_{X_ét}`-modules, with `M ⊗ O` a sheaf on `X_ét` and
`M ⊗ O(Y) = M ⊗_R O(Y)` on affinoid perfectoid `Y ∈ X_ét` ([KL15] Thm 8.2.22(c), (d)), is
AdicEtaleGeometry A1.6a (*stable-basis-etale-vector-bundles*, for pairs with the stable étale basis supplied by strong sheafiness;
the rational-site form is AdicSpacesPartIII R3.5 (*sheafy-tate-acyclicity-and-kiehl-gluing*)),
used here with `(R, R⁺)` perfectoid and strongly sheafy by P3.17. The ordinary
finite-étale descent is [KL15] Theorems 1.3.4–1.3.5, and the étale vector-bundle
comparison is Theorem 8.2.22(c)–(d), p. 165. Descent along
v-covers belongs to the downstream consumer DiamondsAndVStacks layer D3.
*Needs:* P3.18;
AdicEtaleGeometry A1.2, A1.6 (*finite-etale-rational-descent*, *etale-structure-sheaf*);
AdicEtaleGeometry A1.6a (*stable-basis-etale-vector-bundles*); AdicSpacesPartIII R3.5
(*sheafy-tate-acyclicity-and-kiehl-gluing*).

The target `finiteEtale_descent` states locality for any jointly surjective
family of étale objects, without a finiteness condition on that family.
For a morphism `f : Y → X` in `Perfd p`,
`etale_iff_openCover_source` and `etale_iff_openCover_target` state that
AdicEtaleGeometry's `YonedaAdicSpace.IsEtaleLocalDescription`, applied to the image of `f` under
`YonedaAdicSpace.ofAdicSpace`, is
equivalent to the same predicate on every source restriction or target
pullback, respectively. Each takes an arbitrary indexed family of opens
covering every valuation point, without quasi-compactness or finiteness
hypotheses ([KL15] Definition 8.2.16 and 8.2.17(c), p. 162).
`TauCetiRoadmap.AdicSpacesPartIII.AdicSpace.vectorBundleEquivalence`
supplies rational gluing on Part II `AdicSpace.Chart`, with a Tate coefficient
ring `c.affinoid.ring` ([KL15] Theorem 2.7.7, p. 58), and
AdicEtaleGeometry A1.6a's *stable-basis-etale-vector-bundles* supplies
(c) on the stable basis of affinoid perfectoid objects ([KL15] Definition
8.3.1, p. 166).

**Checks.** `etale_openCover_whole_source` and
`etale_openCover_whole_target` specialize locality to the singleton cover
by the whole source or target. `etale_openCover_empty_source` uses the
empty covering family of an empty source and concludes that its morphism
to any perfectoid target is étale.

`finiteEtalePrestack` has the actual finite étale slice categories as fibres
and `finiteEtaleBaseChange` as transition functor; `finiteEtale_isStack`
asserts effective descent, including descent of morphisms. Both small
categories have finite limits. `prestack_empty_base` and
`prestack_geometric_point` compute its fibres over the empty space and an
algebraically closed field point.

For any perfectoid `X` and étale object `U → X`,
`finiteEtalePrestack_mapId_hom_app` identifies the component on every finite
étale `T → U` with `Over.pullbackId`. For composable slice arrows
`W → V → U`, `finiteEtalePrestack_mapComp_hom_app` identifies the component
with `Over.pullbackComp`, directed from pullback along the composite to
successive pullbacks. These are equalities of morphisms in the actual slice,
so both projections are fixed. The action on a 2-morphism is `eqToHom` of the
equality extracted by `LocallyDiscrete.eq_of_hom`. This is the pullback
coherence used by `finiteEtale_isStack` ([KL15] Definitions 1.3.1–1.3.2,
pp. 15–16; Theorems 1.3.4–1.3.5, p. 16).

**Checks.** `finiteEtalePrestack_identity_projection` gives the first
projection for pullback along the identity. `finiteEtalePrestack_two_steps`
sends the direct pullback to the iterated pullback while preserving the
projection to `T`. `finiteEtalePrestack_nontrivial_automorphism` shows that
postcomposing the unit component with any nonidentity automorphism of `T`
changes that component.

`etaleO` and `etaleOPlus` evaluate P2's actual global sections and integral
sections on each object as additive groups; their restriction maps are pullbacks
of functions. `etaleO_isSheaf` and `etaleOPlus_isSheaf` assert descent for these
presheaves. `etaleORing` and `etaleOPlusRing` retain multiplication on those same
carriers, with the same ring-homomorphism pullbacks. `etaleORing_isSheaf` and
`etaleOPlusRing_isSheaf` assert ring-valued descent for every perfectoid `X`,
and `etaleRing_forget` identifies their additive presheaves with `etaleO` and
`etaleOPlus` ([Sch12] Proposition 7.13, p. 43; [ECD] Theorem 6.3, p. 26).
The affinoid basis supplies sheafification in the universe containing these
sections and the corresponding Ext groups.

For any integral base section `a`, `etaleOPlusQuotient_ring` equips the
additive sheaf cokernel `etaleOPlusQuotient p X a` with a commutative ring
sheaf lift. The statement identifies the ring quotient arrow with the additive
cokernel arrow on every section. Thus the multiplication descends from `O⁺`,
and the quotient is taken in sheaves, without asserting that every section is
a pointwise quotient. This applies in particular to a locally chosen
pseudouniformiser ([Sch12] Proposition 7.13, p. 43, and the sheaf quotient
construction).

`etaleOPlusAlgebra` uses pullback along `U → X` to make `O⁺(U)` an algebra
over `globalPlus p X`. `etaleOPlusAlgebra_forget` identifies its underlying
ring presheaf and asserts descent. For any basic setup `S` on this base ring,
`etaleOPlusAlmost` applies P0's `Almost.Algebra.toAlmost S` to that algebra
presheaf; `etaleOPlusAlmost_isSheaf` asserts descent in `Almost.Algebra S`.
This retains the algebra unit and multiplication in almost modules.
`etaleOPlusAlmost_affinoidSetup` supplies a setup on
`globalPlus p (ofPair p R)` whose ideal consists exactly of the sections whose
images in `R` are topologically nilpotent. It is P1's `almostSetupPlus p R R.pair`
transported across the integral global section isomorphism. This specifies
`O^{+a}` locally on affinoid bases, with no fixed base field ([GR] §3.3,
3.3.1–3.3.2, p. 47; [ECD] Theorem 6.3, p. 26).

For a perfectoid `X`, a locally strongly sheafy adic `Y`, and
`f : X.obj → ofAdicSpace.obj Y`, `etaleAdicBaseChange` is the functor
`AdicSpace.smallEtale Y → smallEtale p X`. Its object is `U ×_Y X`.
`etaleAdicBaseChange_isPullback` supplies the projection to `U`, its adic
pullback square, and naturality in every arrow of the supplied adic site.
`etaleAdicBaseChange_continuous` and
`etaleAdicBaseChange_preservesFiniteLimits` give the morphism of sites
`X_ét → Y_ét`. The locally strongly sheafy hypotheses use A1's étale base
change and `perfectoid_etale_baseChange`; [Sch12] Lemma 7.3(iii)–(iv), p. 40,
Proposition 7.10 and the paragraph following Definition 7.11, p. 43, give the
locally noetherian case, while [ECD] Theorem 6.1 and Definition 6.2, p. 26,
supply the perfectoid Tate-ring input to this generality.

**Checks.**

- `etaleORing_affinoid`, `etaleORing_empty`, and `etaleORing_first_component`:
  the identity object over `Spa(R,R⁺)` has ring `R`; the empty object's ring
  is zero; restriction from `Spa(R × R)` to the first component sends `(a,b)` to `a`.
- `etaleOPlusRing_affinoid`, `etaleOPlusRing_empty`, and
  `etaleOPlusRing_second_component`: the corresponding integral ring is `R⁺`,
  the empty object has zero ring, and restriction to the second component
  sends `(a,b)` to `b` for `a,b ∈ R⁺`.
- `etaleOPlusAlgebra_scalars`, `etaleOPlusAlgebra_empty`, and
  `etaleOPlusAlgebra_nonzero`: the scalar map is the actual integral pullback;
  the empty object's algebra is zero; on the identity object over a nonzero
  affinoid ring, `1 ≠ 0`.
- `etaleOPlusAlmost_classical`, `etaleOPlusAlmost_zero_ideal`, and
  `etaleOPlusAlmost_classical_nonzero`: the classical setup recovers the
  integral algebra through P0's equivalence, the zero almost ideal kills
  every underlying module, and the classical almostification of a nonzero
  affinoid's identity object remains nonzero.
- `etaleAdicBaseChange_identity_object`, `etaleAdicBaseChange_empty`, and
  `etaleAdicBaseChange_split_two`: pulling back an isomorphism gives an
  isomorphism over `X`; pulling back the empty object gives the empty object;
  pulling back the split two-component cover of `Spa(ℚ₂,ℤ₂)` gives `X ⊔ X`.

### P3.20 tilting identifies the étale sites

**Tilting identifies the étale sites: `X_ét ≃ X♭_ét`, compatibly with affinoids, fibre products,
coverings and `O⁺/ϖ`.** (*etale-site-tilting-equivalence*) Let `X` be a perfectoid space with tilt
`X♭` (layer P2). The tilting functor `Y ↦ Y♭` of the slice equivalence (layer P2: perfectoid spaces
over `X` `≃` perfectoid spaces over `X♭`) restricts to equivalences of categories `X_ét ≃ X♭_ét` and
`X_fét ≃ X♭_fét` of *etale-site-of-perfectoid-space*. These equivalences preserve and reflect affinoid
perfectoid objects (with `Spa(S, S⁺)♭ = Spa(S♭, S♭⁺)`), fibre products, and covering families
(`|Y| ≅ |Y♭|` compatibly with the maps to `|X| ≅ |X♭|`); hence they are equivalences of sites and
induce equivalences of topoi `Sh(X_ét) ≃ Sh(X♭_ét)` (Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Equivalence.sheafCongr`).
They are functorial in `X`: compatible with the morphisms of sites induced by maps `X' → X` and their
tilts. Locally choose a pseudouniformiser `ϖ♭` with `ϖ = (ϖ♭)♯` and
`ϖ^p | p` in the integral ring (as in P3.5); they identify the sheaves `O⁺_X/ϖ` and
`O⁺_{X♭}/ϖ♭`, and the almost sheaves `O⁺a/ϖ` and `O⁺a_{X♭}/ϖ♭`, on the identified sites. For affinoid
`X = Spa(R, R⁺)` the restriction to `X_fét` is the tilting equivalence `FÉt(R) ≃ FÉt(R♭)` of
*finite-etale-tilting-equivalence* ([ECD] §6, Thm 6.3, p. 26). *Needs:* P3.18.

**Checks.** On `X = Spa(ℂ_p, O_{ℂ_p})`,
`etale_site_tilting_test_wrong_scale` takes `a=p` in `globalPlus p X` and
rejects the chartwise hypothesis `a^p ∣ p` required by
`etaleIntegralQuotientTiltIso`. This tests its stated sufficient hypothesis;
it does not assert failure of every comparison modulo `p`.
`etale_site_tilting_Cp_wrong_scale` evaluates the actual cokernel sheaf
`etaleOPlusQuotient p X (p²)` on the identity étale object: the cokernel
projection sends `p` to a nonzero section. On the corresponding tilted object,
`p` kills every section of every `etaleOPlusQuotient`. Thus these quotient
sheaves cannot be identified at scale `p²` ([Sch12] Thm 5.2 and Lem. 5.3,
p. 22; Thm 7.12 and Prop. 7.13, p. 43).

`finiteEtaleTiltFunctor` is the restriction of P2’s geometric slice tilt to
finite objects; its equivalence instance and `finiteEtaleTilt_covers` give
the finite-site assertion. `etaleOPlusQuotient` is the cokernel of scalar
multiplication in abelian sheaves. `etaleIntegralQuotientTiltIso` compares
these quotient sheaves when `b♯=a`, with `a` a pseudouniformiser and `a^p | p`
on every affinoid chart. `etaleIntegralQuotientTiltIso_sharp` fixes the
comparison on local sections by the sharp map and the cokernel projections.
`etaleTiltSheafEquiv` is Mathlib's `CategoryTheory.Equivalence.sheafCongr`
applied to `etaleTiltFunctor`, using `etaleTilt_covers` to identify the topologies.
For every perfectoid `X` and every sheaf on its tilted étale site,
`etaleTiltSheafEquiv_inverse_obj` identifies inverse image with precomposition
by this geometric site tilt ([ECD] Theorem 6.3, p. 26). This is a sheaf quotient; taking global sections
need not give the ordinary quotient before almostification.

**Checks.** `etaleTiltSheafEquiv_sections` computes sections over an object as
sections over its tilt; `etaleTiltSheafEquiv_restriction` computes restriction
along an arbitrary arrow as restriction along its tilt; `etaleTiltSheafEquiv_empty`
states that sections over an empty object form a singleton.
`integral_quotient_zero`, `integral_quotient_unit`, and
`integral_quotient_empty` give respectively `O⁺`, the zero sheaf, and zero
sections over the empty object. `tilt_site_empty`, `tilt_site_nonfinite`,
`tilt_finite_empty`, and `tilt_finite_nonempty` distinguish empty objects and
preservation of the finite/nonfinite distinction under tilting.

### P3.21 almost acyclicity on the étale site

**Almost acyclicity of `O⁺` and acyclicity of `O` on the étale site of an affinoid perfectoid
space.** (*etale-almost-acyclicity*) Let `X = Spa(R, R⁺)` be an affinoid perfectoid space (`R`
perfectoid Tate, no base field) with étale site `X_ét`, and write `H^i(X_ét, −)` for sheaf cohomology
of abelian sheaves on `X_ét` (Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Sheaf.H`). Then: (a) `H⁰(X_ét, O⁺) = R⁺` and
`H^i(X_ét, O⁺)` is almost zero (killed by `R°°`) for `i > 0`; (b) `H⁰(X_ét, O) = R` and
`H^i(X_ét, O) = 0` for `i > 0`; (c) for every finite covering `{U_j → U}` in `X_ét` of an affinoid
perfectoid object `U` by affinoid perfectoid objects, the augmented Čech complex of `O⁺` is almost
exact and that of `O` is exact; (d) `H⁰(X_ét, O⁺/ϖ)^a = (R⁺/ϖ)^a` and `H^i(X_ét, O⁺/ϖ)` is almost zero
for `i > 0`; (e) for every finitely generated projective `R`-module `M`, `H^i(X_ét, M ⊗_R O) = 0` for
`i > 0`. The same holds on the analytic site (layer P2) and for every affinoid perfectoid object of
`X_ét` ([ECD] §6, Thm 6.3, second paragraph, p. 26 (`O⁺`); [Sch12] Prop. 7.13, p. 43 (`O^{°a}` and
hence `O` on `X_ét`, over a perfectoid field)). *Needs:* P3.18; P3.19 (finite projective coefficients).

`etaleOSheaf` and `etaleOPlusSheaf` are these concrete presheaves with their
sheaf proofs. `etaleIntegralScalar_apply` fixes multiplication by a pulled-back
integral base section. `etaleO_acyclic` and `etaleOPlus_almost_acyclic` use
Mathlib `Sheaf.H` and require `q > 0`; the latter says the induced scalar map
is zero for each topologically nilpotent base element. `etaleTiltSheafEquiv`
is the equivalence of sheaf categories for the displayed covering topologies.
`etaleOPlusQuotient_almost_acyclic` is the corresponding positive-degree
almost vanishing for an integral quotient by a pseudouniformiser.
`etaleOCoefficients` evaluates `M ⊗_R O(U)` with the scalar action pulled
back from the base; `etaleOCoefficients_map` sends `m ⊗ s` to `m ⊗ f*(s)`.
For finite projective `M`, `etaleOCoefficients_isSheaf` and
`etaleOCoefficients_acyclic` give its sheaf property and positive-degree
vanishing. The general vector-bundle equivalence remains the R5 supplier.

**Checks.** `coefficients_zero`, `coefficients_rank_one`, and
`coefficients_rank_two` compute `0`, `O`, and `O ⊕ O`.

**Checks.** `etale_sections_empty` gives zero sections over the empty object;
`etale_sections_affinoid` recovers `R` and `R⁺` on the identity affinoid object;
`etale_sections_two_constants` restricts `(a,b) ∈ R × R` to `a` on the first
component; `etale_integral_two_constants` restricts `(a,b) ∈ R⁺ × R⁺` to `b`
on the second component, through the affinoid section comparison. `etale_H0_not_zero` excludes degree zero from
acyclicity for every nonzero affinoid ring.

`etale_sections_split_two` computes both structure presheaves on the split
cover `Spa(R²)`: their values are `R²` and `(R⁺)²`. Together with the empty
and base-affinoid computations these are three distinct values for each
presheaf. `finite_basechange_split_two` computes the two copies of the new
base obtained by pulling back that split cover.

### P3.22 the tilting equivalence of étale sites with almost acyclicity

**The tilting equivalence of étale sites and the almost acyclicity of `O⁺` on `X_ét`.**
(*etale-site-tilting-and-etale-almost-acyclicity*) [ECD] §6, Thm 6.3, p. 26 — the equivalence of
sites `X_ét ≃ X♭_ét`, `Y ↦ Y♭`, for a perfectoid space `X` over an arbitrary perfectoid base, and
the almost vanishing of `H^i(X_ét, O⁺)` for `i > 0` on an affinoid perfectoid `X` (whence
`H^i(X_ét, O) = 0` by inverting `ϖ`, P3.21(b)) — is the conjunction of P3.20 and P3.21 (with the sheaf property of `O` on
`X_ét` from P3.18) and is not stated again; on `Spa(K, O_K)` for a perfectoid field `K` the
equivalence is the Fontaine–Wintenberger identification of P3.8. *Needs:* P3.20; P3.21.

**Checks.**

- `etale_site_tilting_test_char_p` (degenerate) — for `X` of characteristic `p`, `X♭ = X` and the
  equivalence is the identity of `X_ét`.
- `etale_site_tilting_test_point` (computation) — `X = Spa(K, O_K)` with `K = ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞})^`:
  `X_fét ≃ X♭_fét` is `FÉt(K) ≃ FÉt(𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^)`; the objects of `X_ét` are the disjoint
  unions of the `Spa(L, O_L)`, `L/K` finite separable, so `Sh(X_ét)` is the category of discrete
  `G_K`-sets, `O⁺` corresponds to the discrete `G_K`-module `O_{K^sep} = colim_L O_L`, and
  `H^i(X_ét, O⁺) = H^i(G_K, O_{K^sep})`, which is almost zero for `i > 0` by P3.7(iv) and is not
  claimed to vanish exactly; `H^i(X_ét, O) = H^i(G_K, K^sep) = 0` for `i > 0` by the normal basis
  theorem, exactly. The example `etale_site_tilting_test_point` checks the geometric
  comparison for every finite extension of perfectoid fields with maximal plus rings:
  `etaleTiltFunctor` sends `Spa(L,O_L) → Spa(K,O_K)` to the map of tilted pairs,
  through `tiltSpaIso` on both source and base. Its hypothesis is the supplied
  `YonedaAdicSpace.IsFiniteEtale`; the equation fixes the map over the tilted base
  ([Berkeley] Theorem 7.3.1, p. 50; [ECD] Theorem 6.3, p. 26).

### Examples

The worked examples of this layer are the checks above and the standard instances of the theorems:
`ℤ_(3)` is not henselian along `3` (`X² − 7` has a simple root modulo `3` and no root), so `ℚ` with
the `3`-adic topology is not topologically henselian and `FÉt(ℚ) → FÉt(ℚ_3)` is not full, whereas
`FÉt(L) ≃ FÉt(L̂)` for every algebraic extension `L` of a perfectoid field; the Artin–Schreier
extension `S = K[u]/(u^p − u − t^{-1})` of `K = 𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^`, a perfectoid field with `S°a`
almost finite étale and uniformly almost finite projective (`n = p`) over `K°a` though `S°` is not
finite free over `K°`; the untilt of `K♭(t^{1/2})` being `K(p^{1/2})` for `K = ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞})^` and
`p` odd; `L = ℚ_p^cycl(p^{1/ℓ})`, `ℓ ∤ p(p − 1)`, perfectoid and totally ramified of degree `ℓ`
with `L°a/K°a` almost finite étale although `L°` is not finite free over `K°` (the quadratic
`ℚ_p^cycl(√p)` is not such an example: `√p ∈ ℚ_p(ζ_p)` for `p ≡ 1 (mod 4)`, and
`ℚ_p^cycl(√p) = ℚ_p^cycl(ζ_4)` is unramified for `p ≡ 3 (mod 4)`); the Fontaine–Wintenberger
isomorphism `G_{ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞})} ≅ G_{𝔽_p((t))}`, with the `p = 2` cyclotomic case
`G_{ℚ_2(ζ_{2^∞})} ≅ G_{𝔽_2((t))}`; the Frobenius of a characteristic-`p` perfectoid space as an
isomorphism; the almost purity theorem on `S = R`, `S = R × R` and `S = 0`; the Kummer cover
`u^ℓ = T` of the perfectoid torus over `ℚ_p^cycl`, finite étale of degree `ℓ` with perfectoid source
and tilt the Kummer cover of the tilted torus; the open unit disc inside the closed perfectoid disc,
étale but not finite étale; `Spa(K, O_K)_fét ≃` finite continuous `Gal(K^sep/K)`-sets and
`Spa(C, C⁺)_fét ≃ FintypeCat` for `C` algebraically closed; and, for a finite étale Galois cover
`Y → X` of affinoid perfectoids with group `G`, `H^i(G, O⁺(Y))^a = 0` for `i > 0` and
`O⁺(Y)^G = R⁺`.

The Lean `example` of `Suggested.lean` for this layer checks that the split finite étale algebra
`R × R` of a perfectoid Tate ring is perfectoid.

## Layer P4: injections, immersions and separatedness

The layer builds the points of a perfectoid space with values in affinoid perfectoid fields,
injections together with the qcqs isomorphism criterion, immersions, Zariski closed immersions and
the universal perfectoid space over a Zariski closed subset, the theorem that Zariski closed
immersions are strongly Zariski closed, diagonals, separatedness with its valuative criterion, and
the behaviour of all of these under tilting.

### P4.1 affinoid perfectoid fields and their points

**Affinoid perfectoid fields and `(K, K⁺)`-valued points of perfectoid spaces.**
(*affinoid-perfectoid-field-points*) An affinoid perfectoid field is a pair `(K, K⁺)` of a
perfectoid field `K` (a perfectoid Tate ring that is a nonarchimedean field, [ECD] §3,
Definition 3.6; P1.10) and an open and bounded valuation subring `K⁺ ⊂ K`; equivalently `K⁺` is a
valuation subring with `K°° ⊂ K⁺ ⊂ K° = O_K`, so `(K, K⁺)` is a Huber pair and `Spa(K, K⁺)` is an
affinoid perfectoid space; it is algebraically closed if `K` is. A morphism `(K, K⁺) → (L, L⁺)` is a
morphism of Huber pairs, also called an extension of affinoid perfectoid fields. The points of
`Spa(K, K⁺)` are the valuation subrings `V` with `K⁺ ⊆ V ⊆ K°`; they form a chain, `K⁺` is the
unique closed point, `K°` the unique rank-one point, and the nonempty quasicompact open subsets
are the rational subsets `{|h| ≤ 1} = Spa(K, K'⁺)`, `h ∈ K`, where `K'⁺` is the smallest valuation
subring containing `K⁺[h]`, with `h ∈ K°` for a nonempty subset (a finite union of such sets is again one, the chain being totally
ordered); when `K⁺` has finite rank every valuation subring `K⁺ ⊆ K'⁺ ⊆ K°` is of this form, but
in general `Spa(K, K'⁺)` need not be open, and in particular the rank-one point `K°` need not be
open (see the Checks). For a perfectoid space `X` (P2.10) the set of
`(K, K⁺)`-valued points is `X(K, K⁺) := Hom(Spa(K, K⁺), X)`, covariant in `X` and in extensions of Huber pairs
`(K, K⁺) → (L, L⁺)` (precomposition with `Spa(L, L⁺) → Spa(K, K⁺)`), with the closed-point map `X(K, K⁺) → |X|`; for `X = Spa(R, R⁺)` affinoid perfectoid it
is the set of morphisms of Huber pairs `(R, R⁺) → (K, K⁺)`, and the closed-point map sends `φ` to
`spaComap φ` of the closed point. In `PerfectoidSpace`, define `AffinoidField` (a perfectoid field
with an open and bounded valuation subring), `AffinoidField.toPair` (the underlying Huber pair),
`AffinoidField.ofRankOne` (the pair `(K, K°)`), `AffinoidField.closedPoint` and `fieldPoints`
(`X(K, K⁺)`, with `fieldPoints.map`, `fieldPoints.restrict`, `fieldPoints.closedPointImage`); prove
`AffinoidField.valuationEquiv`, `AffinoidField.isOpen_iff` and `fieldPoints_affinoidEquiv`
(`X(K, K⁺) ≃ Huber.Pair.Hom (R, R⁺) (K, K⁺)` for `X` affinoid) ([ECD] §5, Proposition 5.3 (ii),
p. 21; [Berkeley] Lecture 8, Definition/Proposition 8.3.3 (2)–(3), p. 61). *Needs:* P1.10; P2.10;
Tau Ceti `TauCeti.Huber.Pair`, `TauCeti.Huber.Pair.Hom.spaComap`; Mathlib `ValuationSubring`.

**Checks.**

- `AffinoidField.subsingleton_spa_ofRankOne` (computation) — for every perfectoid field `K`,
  `|Spa(K, K°)|` has exactly one point.
- `AffinoidField.card_spa_eq_two` (computation) — if `K⁺ ⊊ K°` is the preimage of a rank-one
  valuation ring `k⁺ ⊊ k` of the residue field `k = K°/K°°`, then `|Spa(K, K⁺)|` has exactly two
  points and only `K⁺` is closed.
- `AffinoidField.fieldPoints_affinoidEquiv_closedPoint` (compatibility) — for `X = Spa(R, R⁺)`
  affinoid perfectoid and `φ ∈ X(K, K⁺) = Huber.Pair.Hom (R, R⁺) (K, K⁺)`, the closed-point image of
  `φ` is Tau Ceti `Huber.Pair.Hom.spaComap φ` applied to the closed point of `Spa(K, K⁺)`.
- `AffinoidField.not_isOpen_rankOnePoint` (non-example) — let `K⁺` be the preimage of a valuation
  ring `k⁺` of the residue field `k = K°/K°°` with value group `⋃_n ℚⁿ` ordered lexicographically
  with the last coordinate dominant, whose convex subgroups are `0 ⊂ ℚ ⊂ ℚ² ⊂ ⋯` with union the
  whole group. Then `|Spa(K, K⁺)|` is the chain `K⁺ = W_0 ⊂ W_1 ⊂ W_2 ⊂ ⋯ ⊂ K°` with
  `K° = ⋃_n W_n`; each `{V ⊇ W_n} = {|h_n| ≤ 1}` (`h_n` of value `−e_n`, for `n ≥ 1`) is open, but every open
  set containing `K°` contains some `{V ⊇ W_n}`, so `Spa(K, K°) = {K°}` is a quasicompact subset
  that is not open: not every `Spa(K, K'⁺)` is an open subset. The divisible group is essential:
  the residue field of a perfectoid field is perfect, so any valuation on it has
  `p`-divisible value group. The negative control `rank_group_not_integer` takes
  `K : AffinoidField 2` and an actual residue presentation `ρ : K° → k`,
  surjective with kernel the elements of norm less than one. It asserts that no
  valuation `k → WithZero (Multiplicative ℤ)` is surjective, excluding an integer
  residual value group for this carrier.

The structure `AffinoidField` stores a complete nontrivially normed ultrametric field,
its perfectoid-field instance, and a valuation subring satisfying `IsRingOfIntegralElements`.
`AffinoidField.valuationEquiv` gives the valuation-subring classification above;
`AffinoidField.closedPoint_spec` identifies the unique closed point. The two-point test uses
strict inclusion and the absence of intermediate valuation subrings, the equivalent
valuation-ring formulation of the rank-one residual hypothesis.

Additional Checks for the field and its projections:

| Check | Computation or distinction |
| --- | --- |
| `AffinoidField.toPair_rankOne` | The maximal-plus pair has plus ring exactly `K°`. |
| `AffinoidField.toPair_proper` | A strict smaller plus ring gives a different pair on the same field. |
| `AffinoidField.closedPoint_rankOne` | Every point of the maximal-plus spectrum equals its closed point. |
| `AffinoidField.closedPoint_two` | For strict smaller plus, a second point exists and is not closed. |
| `AffinoidField.no_padic` | No affinoid perfectoid field is topologically isomorphic to `ℚ_p`. |
| `fieldPoints_quadratic` | A separable degree-two extension has two distinct geometric field points with the same image. |
| `fieldPoints_map_identity`, `fieldPoints_map_composition` | The identity field point sends each scalar `t` to `t`; postcomposition along `R → S` sends `t` to `a(f(t))` under the affinoid comparison. |
| `fieldPoints_restrict_identity`, `fieldPoints_restrict_composition` | The identity field point extended along `e : K → L` sends `t` to `e(t)`; a further extension `d : L → M` sends it to `d(e(t))`. |
| `fieldPoints_closedPoint_natural` | Postcomposition sends the closed-point image by the underlying continuous map. |

The Check `fieldPoints_restrict_identity` evaluates the identity field point after
extension `e : K → L`: its scalar map sends `t` to `e(t)` ([ECD] §5, p. 21).

`AffinoidField.exists_infiniteRank` supplies this realization for every prime `p`:
a characteristic-`p` affinoid perfectoid field `K`, a surjective residue map
`ρ : K° → k` with kernel `{a | ‖a‖ < 1}`, and a surjective valuation of the perfect
field `k` with value group `⊕ₙ ℚ`, ordered with the largest index dominant.
It identifies `K⁺` with the inverse image of its valuation ring, and supplies
all the proper coarsenings `W_n`, strictly increasing from `K⁺` and exhausting `K°`.
One construction takes the Hahn field `k = 𝔽_p((⊕ₙ ℚ))` and
`K = k((t^{1/p^∞}))^` with its `t`-adic norm. Divisibility of the exponent group
makes `k` perfect; completing the perfect `t`-power tower leaves residue field `k`.
Thus `K` is perfectoid by [ECD] Proposition 3.5, p. 15. The convex subgroups
supported on the first `n` coordinates give the asserted coarsenings; the
valuation-ring description of points is [Berkeley] Example 2.3.8, p. 16.
The example `AffinoidField.not_isOpen_rankOnePoint_realization` applies
`AffinoidField.not_isOpen_rankOnePoint` to this existence theorem and exhibits
an actual non-open rank-one singleton.

### P4.2 quasicompact and quasiseparated morphisms

**Quasicompact and quasiseparated morphisms of perfectoid spaces.**
(*quasicompact-and-quasiseparated-maps*) A perfectoid space `X` is quasicompact (resp.
quasiseparated) if `|X|` is quasicompact (resp. a Mathlib `QuasiSeparatedSpace`). A morphism
`f : Y → X` of perfectoid spaces is quasicompact if `f⁻¹(U)` is quasicompact for every quasicompact
open `U ⊆ |X|`, equivalently for every open affinoid `U ⊆ X`; it is quasiseparated if the diagonal
`Δ_f : Y → Y ×_X Y` (Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.diagonal` in the category of perfectoid
spaces, whose fibre products are P2.16) is quasicompact; qcqs means both. Equivalently, `f` is
quasiseparated if and only if for every open affinoid `U ⊆ X` and all open affinoids
`V, W ⊆ f⁻¹(U)` the intersection `V ∩ W` is quasicompact; if `X` is affinoid (or quasiseparated),
`f` is quasiseparated if and only if `|Y|` is quasiseparated. The comparison with the topos-theoretic notions for represented sheaves is owned by
AdicSpacesPartII R0.19.10 ([ECD] §8, Proposition 8.3, p. 41). In `PerfectoidSpace`, define `QuasiCompact` and `QuasiSeparated`; prove
`quasiCompact_iff_affinoid` (the test on open affinoids), `quasiSeparated_iff_affinoid_inter`,
`quasiSeparated_iff_quasiSeparatedSpace`, `QuasiCompact.comp`, `QuasiSeparated.comp`,
`QuasiCompact.baseChange` and `QuasiSeparated.baseChange` ([ECD] §5, remark after Proposition 5.11,
p. 25). *Needs:* Mathlib `CompactSpace`, `QuasiSeparatedSpace`,
`CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.diagonal`; P2.16.

`QuasiCompact` lives on `Perfd`; `quasiCompact_iff_adicCompactOpens` identifies it with
AdicSpacesPartII R0.6's `AdicSpace.QuasiCompact` through `YonedaAdicSpace.ofAdicSpace`. Since a
perfectoid space is itself an adic space on the pre-adic carrier of P2.10, the representatives below
may be taken to be `Y.obj` and `X.obj` themselves, with `eY`, `eX` the identities.
Precisely, for `f : Y → X`, adic representatives `A, B`, isomorphisms
`eY : ofAdicSpace(A) ≅ Y.obj`, `eX : ofAdicSpace(B) ≅ X.obj`, and `g : A → B`
with `ofAdicSpace(g) ≫ eX.hom = eY.hom ≫ f.hom`, it equates `QuasiCompact p f`
with compactness of `g⁻¹(U)` for every compact open `U` of `B`. These are the
compact-open tests in R0 and [ECD] §5, p. 25; the comparison uses
`YonedaAdicSpace.ofAdicSpace_space`, which is natural in the adic space (AdicEtaleGeometry A1.16).

**Checks.**

- `QuasiCompact_affinoid` and `QuasiSeparated_affinoid` (computation) — every morphism `Spa(S, S⁺) → Spa(R, R⁺)` of affinoid
  perfectoid spaces is quasicompact and quasiseparated.
- `not_quasiCompact_openDisc` (non-example) — the open immersion of the open unit disc
  `⋃_n {|T|^n ≤ |ϖ|}` into `Spa(C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, O_C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩)` is not quasicompact: the preimage of
  the whole disc is not quasicompact.
- `QuasiCompact_identity` and `QuasiSeparated_identity` (degenerate) — the identity of any perfectoid space is qcqs.

Further Checks use the global `Perfd` carrier:
`QuasiCompact_identity` and `QuasiSeparated_identity` test arbitrary identities;
`QuasiCompact_empty` and `QuasiSeparated_empty` test the empty open subspace;
`QuasiCompact_affinoid` and `QuasiSeparated_affinoid` test all maps between affinoids.
`not_quasiCompact_openDisc` supplies the non-quasicompact counterexample on the P1 root disc.

### P4.3 injections of perfectoid spaces

Injections are the monomorphisms of the category of perfectoid spaces; this subsection and the six
after it define them, build the residue-field points on which they are tested, and characterise
them by points, by residue fields and by base change.

**Injections of perfectoid spaces.** (*injection-of-perfectoid-spaces*) Throughout, `p` is a fixed
prime; perfectoid fields are those of [ECD] Definition 3.6, of either characteristic, with no base
field; `K⁺` is a valuation subring, and open integrally closed subrings that are not valuation
subrings (they occur in [ECD] Lemma 9.9) do not give affinoid perfectoid fields. A morphism
`f : Y → X` of perfectoid spaces is an injection if for every perfectoid space `Z` the map
`f_* : Hom(Z, Y) → Hom(Z, X)` is injective ([ECD] §5, Definition 5.1, p. 21). It suffices to test
affinoid perfectoid `Z`, because two morphisms `Z → Y` that agree on an open affinoid cover of `Z`
agree ([ECD] §5, sentence after Definition 5.1, p. 21). In the category `Perfd` of perfectoid spaces
this says exactly that `f` is a monomorphism (Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Mono`), and, fibre products
existing in `Perfd` (P2.16), it is equivalent to the diagonal `Δ_f : Y → Y ×_X Y` being an
isomorphism (Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.isIso_diagonal_iff`). In `PerfectoidSpace`,
use `CategoryTheory.Mono` directly for injections. The comparison
`isInjection_iff_affinoid_tests` identifies it with injectivity on affinoid test objects.
Use Mathlib’s `pullback.isIso_diagonal_iff`, monomorphism composition and cancellation, and
split-monomorphism instances for the categorical consequences; sections and diagonals are injections.
The affinoid form `IsInjection_affinoid` is stated for a morphism `φ : (R, R⁺) → (S, S⁺)` of
arbitrary complete Hausdorff Tate Huber pairs (not assumed perfectoid or sheafy) as the
epimorphism condition towards perfectoid Huber pairs `(W, W⁺)`: `a ∘ φ = b ∘ φ` forces `a = b`;
for `R`, `S` perfectoid this is the notion above for `Spa(S, S⁺) → Spa(R, R⁺)`, since
`Hom(Spa(W, W⁺), Spa(S, S⁺)) = Hom((S, S⁺), (W, W⁺))` for affinoid perfectoid pairs (P2.9).
*Needs:* Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Mono`, `CategoryTheory.IsSplitMono`,
`CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.diagonal`; P2.10; P2.16.

**Checks.**

- `injection_id` (degenerate) — the identity pair map cancels against every perfectoid test
  pair, including when the source ring is zero.
- `injection_rational` (computation) — for `X = Spa(R, R⁺)` affinoid perfectoid and `U ⊆ X`
  rational, the open immersion `U → X` is an injection.
- `isInjection_diagonal` (computation) — for the split double cover `X ⊔ X → X`
  with `X` nonempty, the diagonal is an injection but is not surjective on points.
  In general, for every morphism `f : Y → X` of perfectoid spaces,
  `Δ_f : Y → Y ×_X Y` is an injection, being a split monomorphism.
- `injection_quadratic` and `injection_quadratic_pair` (non-example) — for a perfectoid field `K` and a separable
  quadratic extension `L/K` with continuous structure map (`L` carries the extended valuation and is perfectoid by P3.7), `Spa(L, O_L) → Spa(K, O_K)` is bijective
  on underlying spaces but not an injection: the two `K`-embeddings of `L` into a completed
  algebraic closure `C` give distinct `(C, O_C)`-points with the same image.

Integral perfectoid rings give perfectoid Tate rings
(*integral-perfectoid-criterion-for-annuli*): that `R := R₀[1/π]`, for `R₀` `π`-adically complete
and integral perfectoid with `π` a non-zero-divisor and `π^p | p`, with chosen compatible roots of `π`, is a perfectoid Tate ring with
`R₀ ⊆ R°`, `πR° ⊆ R₀` and `R°/R₀` killed by every `π^{1/pⁿ}` is
*perfectoid-tate-ring-from-integral-perfectoid* (P1.20, [BMS] §3.2, Lemma 3.21, p. 27); it is
applied here to the compatible-root annulus rings `R⟨T^{1/p^∞}, (ϖ^a/T)^{1/p^∞}⟩`, which are
therefore perfectoid. For a nonzero perfectoid field `R = K` and a nondegenerate annulus
(`a` a positive integer), the ordinary annulus `K⟨T, ϖ^a/T⟩` is not perfectoid; the zero-ring case
does not give a non-example.

The carrier `ordinaryAnnulus` is the quotient of the supplier's two-variable restricted
series ring by `TU − ϖᵃ`, with the quotient topology and its additive uniformity.
`ordinaryAnnulus_not_perfectoid` requires `a > 0` and an affinoid perfectoid field.
`rootAnnulus` instead rationally localizes the P1 root disc at `|ϖᵃ| ≤ |T|`.
`rootAnnulus_isPerfectoid` reads the resulting `PairCat.perfectoid` field. The proof
obligation is P2’s theorem `isPerfectoidTateRing_rationalLocalization` on the actual
`RationalLoc` carrier for a presentation whose numerators generate the unit ideal;
`rationalPair_presentation` identifies the bundled annulus with that localization
([ECD] Theorem 3.18, p. 18).
Checks `ordinaryAnnulus_coordinate_product`, `ordinaryAnnulus_nonzero` and
`ordinaryAnnulus_no_coordinate_root` compute the defining product, exclude the zero ring,
and show in characteristic p that `T` has no pth root. Checks `rootAnnulus_zero_radius`,
`rootAnnulus_nonzero` and `rootAnnulus_frobenius` identify the unit annulus at `a = 0`,
exclude the zero ring, and give bijective Frobenius in characteristic p.

### P4.4 filtered intersections of rational subsets

**The perfectoid space attached to a filtered intersection of rational subsets.**
(*intersection-of-rational-subsets*) Let `X = Spa(R, R⁺)` be an affinoid perfectoid space,
`ϖ ∈ R⁺` a pseudouniformizer with `ϖ^p | p` admitting compatible `p`-power roots (P1.3), and `𝒰` a
nonempty family of rational subsets of `X` that is filtered (for `U, V ∈ 𝒰` some `W ∈ 𝒰` lies in
`U ∩ V`); put `T := ⋂_{U∈𝒰} U ⊆ |X|`. Construct `(S_𝒰, S⁺_𝒰)` from the filtered system of section rings
`(O_X(U), O⁺_X(U))`, `U ∈ 𝒰` (P2.3): `S⁺_𝒰` the `ϖ`-adic completion of `colim_{U∈𝒰} O⁺_X(U)` and
`S_𝒰 := S⁺_𝒰[1/ϖ]` with the `ϖ`-adic topology on `S⁺_𝒰`; and let `ι_𝒰 : Z_𝒰 := Spa(S_𝒰, S⁺_𝒰) → X`
be induced by the compatible maps `O_X(U) → S_𝒰`. Prove for this rational-localisation system: (a) `S_𝒰` is a perfectoid
Tate ring, `S⁺_𝒰` is a ring of integral elements, `S⁺_𝒰 ⊆ S_𝒰°` with almost zero cokernel,
`S⁺_𝒰/ϖⁿ = colim_U O⁺_X(U)/ϖⁿ`, and the union of the images of the `O_X(U)` is dense in `S_𝒰`;
(b) `|ι_𝒰|` is a homeomorphism of `|Z_𝒰|` onto `T` with its subspace topology, and `T` is
pro-constructible and stable under generalization; (c) a morphism `g : W → X` from a perfectoid
space factors through `ι_𝒰` if and only if `|g|(|W|) ⊆ T`, and then uniquely, so `ι_𝒰` is an
injection and `Z_𝒰` is the limit of the `U ∈ 𝒰` in `Perfd`; (d) `Z_𝒰` depends, up to unique
isomorphism over `X`, only on `T`. The completions do not depend on the choice of `ϖ`. In
`PerfectoidSpace`, define `proRationalSubspace` (the space `Z_𝒰`) and `proRationalSubspace.ι`
(the morphism `ι_𝒰`). Prove
`proRationalSubspace.integralCompletion_isIntegralPerfectoid`: for a nonempty filtered
`RationalSystem`, an integral pseudouniformizer `π` with `π^p ∣ p` in `R⁺`, the actual
`AdicCompletion (π) (colim O⁺(U))` is integral perfectoid and its image of `π` is a
nonzerodivisor ([ECD] Proposition 6.5, p. 29, and the remark following Lemma 7.6, p. 31).
The construction `proRationalPair` must supply `PairCat.perfectoid` and
`pair.isRingOfIntegralElements` for its localized completion, identified by
`proRationalSubspace.integralCompletion` and `proRationalSubspace.localization`;
`proRationalSubspace.isPerfectoid` exposes the former field. Prove
`proRationalSubspace.plus_mod_pow` (simp:
`S⁺_𝒰/ϖⁿ ≅ colim_U O⁺_X(U)/ϖⁿ`), `proRationalSubspace.range_ι`, `proRationalSubspace.lift` (with
factorization and uniqueness in the `∃!` statement), `proRationalSubspace.isInjection`, `proRationalSubspace.isLimit` and
`proRationalSubspace.congr` ([ECD] §7, remark after Lemma 7.6, p. 31; [ECD] §5, Example 5.2, p. 21;
[Bhatt] §9.4, Proposition 9.4.1 (1)–(3), p. 112 for the Zariski special case). *Needs:* *injection-of-perfectoid-spaces*; P1.3;
P2.3; *almost-integral-perfectoid-criterion* below; Tau Ceti `TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.rationalSubset`; Mathlib
`AdicCompletion`.

**Checks.**

- `proRationalSubspace_stage_not_dense` (non-example) — take the two-member filtered
  family `{X, U}` with `X` the perfectoid closed disc and `U = {|T| = 1}`. The limit is `U`;
  the map `C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ → C⟨T^{±1/p^∞}⟩` is not dense: every element of the source
  has zero `T⁻¹` coefficient, whereas `T⁻¹` has that coefficient equal to one.
- `proRationalSubspace_singleton` (degenerate) — for `𝒰 = {U}`, `ι_𝒰` is isomorphic over `X` to
  `U → X`.
- `proRationalSubspace_rationalNhds` (compatibility) — for `𝒰` the rational neighbourhoods of
  `x ∈ X`, `Z_𝒰 ≅ Spa(K(x), K(x)⁺)` over `X`, compatibly with *residue-field-point-injection*.
- `proRationalSubspace_annulusClosure` (computation) — for
  `X = Spa(C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, O_C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩)` and `𝒰 = {{|ϖ^{1/pⁿ}| ≤ |T|} : n ≥ 0}`:
  `S_𝒰 = C⟨T^{±1/p^∞}⟩`, `S⁺_𝒰` is the `ϖ`-adic completion of
  `O_C[T^{1/p^∞}] + 𝔪_C[T^{−1/p^∞}]`, and `T` is the annulus `{|T| = 1}` together with the rank-two
  point `y` with `|T(y)| = 1⁻`.

Morphisms of perfectoid spaces are generalizing and spectral
(*maps-of-perfectoid-spaces-are-generalizing*): for a morphism `f : Y → X` of perfectoid spaces
(more generally of analytic adic spaces), `|f|` is generalizing (Mathlib `GeneralizingMap`) and is a
spectral map between open affinoids `V ⊆ Y`, `U ⊆ X` with `f(V) ⊆ U` (Mathlib `IsSpectralMap`), so
images of morphisms are stable under generalization ([ECD] §2, sentence before Lemma 2.5, p. 11).

**Almost Frobenius criterion without a base field.** (*almost-integral-perfectoid-criterion*)
Prove the P4 target `perfectoid_of_almost_frobenius` (the almost Frobenius criterion). Let `p` be prime, `A⁺` a
commutative ring and `t : ℕ → A⁺` satisfy `t(n+1)^p = t(n)`. Assume `ϖ := t(0)` is a
non-zero-divisor, `ϖ^p | p`, and `A⁺` is `ϖ`-adically complete and separated. Set
`𝔪 := (t(n) : n ∈ ℕ) = ⋃_n t(n)A⁺`. Assume the Frobenius map
`Φ : A⁺/(t(1)) → A⁺/(ϖ)`, `[a] ↦ [a^p]`, is almost bijective: `𝔪` annihilates its
kernel and, for every `ε ∈ 𝔪` and `y ∈ A⁺/(ϖ)`, `εy` lies in its image
(`Perfectoid.IsAlmostBijective`). The signature also supplies `p ∈ (ϖ)` and
`a ∈ (t(1)) → a^p ∈ (ϖ)` to form `frobeniusQuot`; these follow from the divisibility and
root hypotheses. Then `A := A⁺[1/ϖ]`, with zero-neighbourhood basis `ϖ^nA⁺`, is a complete
Hausdorff perfectoid Tate ring, `A⁺ ⊆ A°`, and `t(n)A° ⊆ A⁺` for every `n`. Thus
`A°/A⁺` is almost zero. This target extends the argument of [Sch12] §5, Lemmas 5.6–5.7,
p. 23, to the root ideal in `A⁺`; those source statements and the P1.28 dictionary have
perfectoid-field scope. Apply this P4 criterion to `S⁺_𝒰` above. *Needs:* P0.2; P1.1;
`frobeniusQuot`; `IsAlmostBijective`; Mathlib `IsAdicComplete` and `Localization.Away`.

The carrier `RationalSystem` records an actual nonempty family of P2 rational subsets,
filtered by intersection. Its `plusDiagram` uses the integral rings of `rationalPair` and
`rationalRes`; `scalar_stage` fixes the base-ring map into its ring colimit. The pair
`proRationalPair` and its map are characterized by `proRationalSubspace.integralCompletion`,
`proRationalSubspace.range_ι` and `proRationalSubspace.lift`. `proRationalStage_base` and
`proRationalStage_comp` fix the stage maps; `proRationalStage_dense` asserts density of their
union. `proRationalSubspace.cone` is a limit cone on `RationalSystem.spaceDiagram`.
`plus_mod_pow` identifies the integral quotient with the quotient of the filtered colimit
by the image of `ϖⁿ`; quotienting commutes with that ring colimit, giving the formula above.
These statements include `n = 0`, when both quotients are the zero ring.

Additional Checks:

| Carrier | Checks and values |
| --- | --- |
| `RationalSystem` | `RationalSystem_singleton`: intersection is `U`; `RationalSystem_empty_member`: one empty member forces empty intersection; `RationalSystem_whole`: the singleton whole space gives the whole space. |
| `proRationalSubspace` and its inclusion | `proRationalSubspace_singleton`: the actual P2 rational localization; `proRationalSubspace_empty_member`: empty space; `proRationalSubspace_whole`: inclusion is an isomorphism. |
| `rationalNeighborhoods` | `rationalNeighborhoods_field_closed`: all of a field spectrum; `rationalNeighborhoods_rankOne`: singleton at a rank-one point; `rationalNeighborhoods_generalizations`: every generalization belongs to the intersection. |

For the disc calculations, `discPair` is the P1 completed root-polynomial algebra with
power-bounded plus ring; `discAnnulus n` is the rational inequality
`|ϖ^{1/pⁿ}| ≤ |T|`, and `annulusSystem` is precisely this family. `unitAnnulus` is `1 ≤ |T|`.
`unitAnnulus_laurent` identifies its topological ring with P1's completed Laurent algebra.
The following Checks pin the carriers independently of their notation:

| Carrier | Checks and values |
| --- | --- |
| `discPair` | `disc_roots_two_terms`: the first two root equations; `disc_origin`: the universal quotient by `T` is the base field and kills every root; `disc_ordinary_quotient_nilpotent`: in the ordinary quotient, `T^{1/p}` is nonzero with pth power zero. |
| `discAnnulus` | `annulus_root_radius`: the next radius shrinks the annulus; `annulus_gauss`: every radius contains the Gauss point; `annulus_excludes_origin`: no radius contains a zero of `T`. |
| `unitAnnulus` | `annulus_gauss`: contains the Gauss point; `annulus_excludes_origin`: excludes the origin; `unitAnnulus_subset_all`: lies in every annulus of the system. |
| `annulusSystem` | `annulusSystem_closed_complement`: its intersection is the complement of the open unit disc; `annulusSystem_proper`: this intersection is proper; `unitAnnulus_subset_all`: the unit annulus belongs to the intersection. |
| `openUnitDisc` | `openUnitDisc_origin`: contains every zero of `T`; `openUnitDisc_excludes_gauss`: excludes the Gauss point; `not_quasiCompact_openDisc`: its inclusion fails quasicompactness. |

`proRationalSubspace.integralCompletion` identifies the plus ring with the actual adic
completion and fixes the image of every base integral scalar. `proRationalSubspace.localization`
specifies inversion of that scalar pseudouniformizer; `proconstructible`, `generalizations`
and `almost_plus` give the topological and almost-integral clauses.

For the annulus-closure computation, `annulusBoundaryPlus` is the closed subring of the
completed Laurent algebra generated by `aTʳ` with `r ≥ 0, |a| ≤ 1`, or `|a| < 1`.
`proRationalSubspace.annulusClosure_plus` identifies the integral ring of the intersection
with this subring. Checks `annulusBoundaryPlus_positive`,
`annulusBoundaryPlus_small_negative` and `annulusBoundaryPlus_negative_not_integral`
show that positive root monomials are integral, negative ones become integral after
multiplication by a topologically nilpotent coefficient, and a negative monomial with
coefficient one is not integral. This distinguishes the boundary plus ring from the
power-bounded subring of the same Laurent algebra ([ECD] §5, Example 5.2, p. 21).

### P4.5 the completed residue field point

**The completed residue field point `i_x : Spa(K(x), K(x)⁺) → X`.** (*residue-field-point-injection*)
For a perfectoid space `X` and a point `x ∈ X` (of any rank), the completed residue field `K(x)`
with its open and bounded valuation subring `K(x)⁺` is an affinoid perfectoid field (P2.5), and
there is a canonical morphism `i_x : Spa(K(x), K(x)⁺) → X` sending the closed point to `x`: on an
affinoid perfectoid neighbourhood `U = Spa(R, R⁺)` of `x` it is given by `(R, R⁺) → (K(x), K(x)⁺)`,
independently of `U`. Moreover ([ECD] §5, Example 5.2, p. 21): (a) `i_x` is isomorphic over `U` to
the pro-rational subspace `ι_𝒰` for `𝒰` the rational neighbourhoods of `x` in `U`
(P4.4), so `K(x)⁺` is the `ϖ`-adic completion of
`colim_{V∋x} O⁺_X(V)` and `K(x)⁺/ϖ = colim_{V∋x} O⁺_X(V)/ϖ`; (b) `i_x` is an injection and `|i_x|`
is a homeomorphism onto the set of generalizations of `x`; (c) every `(K, K⁺)`-valued point `φ` of
`X` whose closed point maps to `x` factors uniquely as `φ = i_x ∘ φ'` with
`φ' : Spa(K, K⁺) → Spa(K(x), K(x)⁺)` given by a morphism of affinoid perfectoid fields; (d) for
`f : Y → X` and `y ∈ Y` with `f(y) = x`, `f ∘ i_y = i_x ∘ Spa(K(x) → K(y))`. In `PerfectoidSpace`,
define `residueFieldPoint` (the morphism `i_x`); prove `residueFieldPoint_closed` (simp: `i_x`
maps the closed point to `x`), `residueFieldPoint_injection`, `residueFieldPoint_range`,
`residueFieldPoint_factor` ((c)), `residueFieldPoint_naturality` ((d)) and
`residueFieldPoint_eq_proRationalSubspace` ((a)). *Needs:* *intersection-of-rational-subsets*;
*affinoid-perfectoid-field-points*; *injection-of-perfectoid-spaces*; P2.5.

**Checks.**

- `residueFieldPoint_closedPoint` (degenerate) — for `X = Spa(K, K⁺)` and `x` the closed point,
  `i_x` is the identity of `X`.
- `residueFieldPoint_gauss` (computation) — for the Gauss point `η` of
  `Spa(C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, O_C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩)`, `K(η)` is the completion of `C(T^{1/p^∞})` for the Gauss
  norm, `K(η)⁺ = K(η)°`, and `|i_η|` has image `{η}`.
- `residueFieldPoint_not_isImmersion` (non-example) — `i_η` is an injection whose image `{η}`
  is not open (and not locally closed), so `i_η` is not an immersion.

Completed tensor products over a nonarchimedean field preserve kernels and strictness
(*completed-tensor-over-analytic-field-kernel*): for `K` complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean
absolute value, Banach `K`-modules `V, W, X` and a bounded `K`-linear `f : V → W`,
`V ⊗_K W → V ⊗̂_K W` is injective, `ker(f) ⊗̂_K X → ker(f ⊗̂ id_X)` is a bijection, and `f ⊗̂ id_X`
is strict when `f` is ([KL15] §2.2, Lemma 2.2.9, p. 31). The stalk of `O⁺/ϖ` at `x` is `K(x)⁺/ϖ`
(*stalk-of-plus-sheaf-modulo-pseudouniformizer*): for `ϖ` a pseudouniformizer near `x`, the map
`O⁺_{X,x} → K(x)⁺` has dense image with kernel `I = ϖI`, so `O⁺_{X,x}/ϖ → K(x)⁺/ϖ` is an
isomorphism ([Torsion] §II.3.1, Lemma II.3.1, p. 16).

Use the sibling declarations `BanachModule.CompletedTensor.injective_tensorProduct_of_field`,
`ker_map_of_field`, `injective_kerMap_of_field` and `isStrictMap_map_of_field` in
AdicSpacesPartII R0.5 (completed tensor products of Banach modules) for the Banach tensor assertions; no further tensor construction is needed.
The kernel assertion has no strictness hypothesis on `f`.

`integralStalk` is the ring colimit of the integral rational-neighbourhood diagram.
`integralStalkToResidue` maps it to the P2 completed residue plus ring;
`integralStalkToResidue_scalar`, `integralStalkToResidue_dense` and
`integralStalkToResidue_kernel` specify its base map, density and `I = ϖI`.
`integralStalk_mod_equiv` and its `_apply` equation give the induced quotient isomorphism.
This uses the rational basis description of the stalk, so it applies in every affinoid
neighbourhood of a point of a general perfectoid space.

Checks `integralStalk_field`, `integralStalk_mod_one` and `integralStalk_two_scalars` compute,
respectively, the stalk at a field's closed point as `K⁺`, the quotient by `1` as zero
in contrast to the nonzero quotient by a pseudouniformizer, and
the two scalar germs `(1,0)` and `(0,1)` on `Spa(K × K,K⁺ × K⁺)` as `1` and `0`
at the closed point of the first component.
`integralStalk_rankTwo_generic` computes the generic stalk of the two-point spectrum
`Spa(K,K⁺)` as `K°`, with every scalar in `K⁺` sent to itself. Here `K⁺ ⊊ K°`
and there are exactly two valuation overrings between them.
`integralStalk_origin` distinguishes a stalk from its residue field: at the origin
of the perfectoid disc the coordinate germ is nonzero. The matching map Checks
`integralStalkToResidue_field` and `integralStalkToResidue_rankTwo_generic` give
bijective evaluation for the two field stalks; `integralStalkToResidue_origin`
sends that nonzero coordinate germ to zero. The field computations use
[ECD] Example 5.2, p. 21; the kernel computation uses [Torsion] Lemma II.3.1,
p. 16, and the root-disc rational sections of P2.
`residueFieldPoint_rankOne_range` computes the singleton image at a rank-one point;
`residueFieldPoint_nonlocallyclosed` excludes an immersion when that singleton is not locally
closed. `gaussPoint_polynomial` specifies the Gauss valuation on finite root polynomials by
the maximum coefficient norm. Its Checks are `gauss_two_coefficients` (the maximum of the
two coefficient norms), `gauss_nonzero_coordinate` (`T` has nonzero value), and
`gauss_not_locallyClosed` (its singleton is not locally closed). Thus the Gauss-point
Checks above refer to the actual root disc and its P2 residue pair.

For a perfectoid pair `R`, a point `x`, and a rational neighbourhood `U` of `x`,
choose a presentation `q` whose numerators generate the unit ideal and whose rational
subset is `U`. Evaluation is `Perfectoid.rationalResidueMap (CAff.of R.pair)`
composed with the comparison supplied by `rationalPair_presentation`.
Its base identity identifies its composite from `R` with
the residue map, and its integrality statement places every integral
section in the completed residue plus ring, and `integralStalkToResidue_stage`
identifies the stalk map on each colimit stage with this same evaluation
([Berkeley] Lemma 7.4.6 and the argument after Theorem 7.4.8, pp. 53–55).
Checks `rationalResidue_zero`, `rationalResidue_scalar` and `rationalResidue_two_terms`
compute a nonzero base function in the valuation support as zero, a base scalar
as its residue value, and `(a+b)/s` as `(a(x)+b(x))/s(x)`.

`gaussRationalField` is the fraction field of the root-polynomial monoid algebra
`C[T^{1/p^∞}]`. `gaussRationalValuation_polynomial` fixes its valuation by the maximum
coefficient norm. `gaussCompletion` is its valued-field completion, and
`residueField_gauss_completion` identifies it topologically with the P2 completed residue
field at the Gauss point, compatibly with constants. Checks `gaussRational_constant`,
`gaussRational_two_terms` and `gaussRational_inverse_monomial` compute a constant, two
distinct exponents, and an inverse root monomial. Checks `gaussCompletion_nonzero`,
`gaussCompletion_constants` and `gaussCompletion_root_monomial` exclude the zero ring,
embed the constant field, and make every root monomial a unit.

### P4.6 the isomorphism criterion for qcqs maps

**Isomorphism criterion for qcqs maps: bijectivity on points and on `(C, C⁺)`-points.**
(*qcqs-isomorphism-criterion*) Let `f : Y → X` be a quasicompact and quasiseparated morphism of
perfectoid spaces (P4.2). The following are equivalent: (i) `f` is
an isomorphism; (ii) `|f| : |Y| → |X|` is bijective and for every rank-one point `y ∈ Y` with image
`x` the map `K(x) → K(y)` is an isomorphism; (iii) for every affinoid perfectoid field `(K, K⁺)` the
map `Y(K, K⁺) → X(K, K⁺)` is a bijection; (iv) for every algebraically closed affinoid perfectoid
field `(C, C⁺)` the map `Y(C, C⁺) → X(C, C⁺)` is a bijection. The qcqs hypothesis makes `|f|` a
spectral map of spectral spaces over an affinoid in (ii)+(iii) ⇒ (i) ([ECD] §5, Lemma 5.4, p. 23).
*Needs:* *quasicompact-and-quasiseparated-maps*; *affinoid-perfectoid-field-points*;
*residue-field-point-injection*; P2.16.

**Checks.**

- `isIso_of_bijective_qcqs_id` (computation) — the identity of `Spa(K,K⁺)` with
  `K⁺ ⊊ K°` and exactly two valuation overrings has two underlying points,
  satisfies the residue-field bijectivity clause (ii), and is bijective on both
  field-valued and algebraically closed field-valued points, (iii)–(iv).
  Its isomorphism assertion is obtained through `isIso_iff_residueFields`.
  `isIso_of_bijective_qcqs_empty` gives the empty-space case, whose sets of
  field-valued points are empty ([ECD] Lemma 5.4, p. 23).
- `not_isIso_openDisc_sum` (non-example, the qcqs hypothesis) — for
  `X = Spa(C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, O_C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩)`, `D ⊆ X` the open unit disc and `Z_𝒰 → X` the closed
  immersion onto its complement `T = ⋂_n {|ϖ^{1/pⁿ}| ≤ |T|}` (P4.17), the map `D ⊔ Z_𝒰 → X` is
  bijective on points with isomorphic completed residue fields at every point, so (ii) holds, but it
  is not quasicompact (the preimage of `X` is not quasicompact) and not an isomorphism: `D` is open
  and closed in `D ⊔ Z_𝒰` and not closed in `X` (the point `y` with `|T(y)| = 1⁻` lies in its
  closure).

The proof rests on five results. A qcqs perfectoid space with a unique closed point `x` is
`Spa(K(x), K(x)⁺)` (*qcqs-with-unique-closed-point-is-a-field-point*): `i_x` is an isomorphism, so
`X` is affinoid with `O_X(X) = K(x)` and `O⁺_X(X) = K(x)⁺` ([ECD] §5, Example 5.2, last paragraph,
p. 21). Points of fibre products surject onto compatible pairs (*fibre-product-points-surjective*):
for `W = Y₁ ×_X Y₂` (P2.16), `|W| → |Y₁| ×_{|X|} |Y₂|` is surjective and spectral on spectral opens,
so points `y₁, y₂` over the same `x` lift to `(K(w), K(w)⁺)`-points `pr_i ∘ i_w` with the same
image ([ECD] §5, proof of Proposition 5.3, p. 22). Every affinoid perfectoid field embeds into an
algebraically closed one, and `(K, K⁺)`-points are detected there
(*algebraically-closed-extension-of-affinoid-field*): for `C` the completion of an algebraic
closure of `K` and `C⁺ ⊆ C°` the preimage of a valuation subring of the residue field of `C°`
dominating the image of `K⁺`, `(C, C⁺)` is an algebraically closed affinoid perfectoid field with
`C⁺ ∩ K = K⁺`, and `Y(K, K⁺) → Y(C, C⁺)` is injective for every perfectoid `Y` ([ECD] §5, proof of
Lemma 5.4, p. 23). A map of perfectoid fields that is injective on geometric points is an
isomorphism (*rank-one-residue-field-rigidity*): a continuous homomorphism `K → L` of perfectoid
fields such that any two continuous homomorphisms `L → C` agreeing on `K` are equal, for every
algebraically closed perfectoid field `C`, is an isomorphism ([ECD] §5, proof of Proposition 5.3,
p. 22). A homeomorphism inducing isomorphisms of completed residue pairs is an isomorphism
(*isomorphism-from-homeomorphism-and-residue-pairs*): if `|f|` is a homeomorphism and
`(K(x), K(x)⁺) → (K(y), K(y)⁺)` is an isomorphism for every `y` over `x`, then `f` is an
isomorphism ([ECD] §5, proof of Lemma 5.4, p. 23; *stalk-of-plus-sheaf-modulo-pseudouniformizer*
for the sheaf half).

The declarations are `isIso_iff_fieldPoints`, `isIso_iff_geometricPoints` and
`isIso_iff_residueFields`, each with explicit quasicompactness and quasiseparatedness.
`isIso_residueFieldPoint_of_uniqueClosed`, `AffinoidField.exists_algebraicallyClosed`,
`AffinoidField.rigidity` and `isIso_of_homeomorphism_residuePairs` state the supporting
interfaces. Fibre-product point surjectivity is already `pullback_points`
in P2.16; the spectral assertion on affinoids follows from `QuasiCompact_affinoid`.
`not_isIso_openDisc_sum` uses the genuine coproduct of the open disc and its pro-rational
complement, and states bijectivity, residue-pair isomorphisms and failure of quasicompactness
and of being an isomorphism together.

### P4.7 characterisations of injections

**Characterisations of injections of perfectoid spaces.** (*injection-criteria*) Let `f : Y → X` be
a morphism of perfectoid spaces, with no quasicompactness hypothesis. The following are equivalent:
(i) `f` is an injection (P4.3); (ii) for every affinoid perfectoid
field `(K, K⁺)`, `Y(K, K⁺) → X(K, K⁺)` is injective; (ii') the same for every algebraically closed
affinoid perfectoid field `(C, C⁺)`; (iii) `|f|` is injective and `K(x) → K(y)` is an isomorphism
for every rank-one point `y ∈ Y` with image `x`; (iv) `|f|` is injective and, for every perfectoid
space `Z`, `Hom(Z, Y) → Hom(Z, X) ×_{C⁰(|Z|, |X|)} C⁰(|Z|, |Y|)` is a bijection, i.e. `f` is final
among morphisms `g : Z → X` for which `|g|` factors through a continuous map `|Z| → |Y|`. This is
the continuous-factorisation contract of [ECD] Proposition 5.3(iv): continuity of `|Z| → |Y|` is for
the topology of `|Y|`, which need not be the subspace topology of the image. In
particular injections `Y → X` are determined, up to unique isomorphism over `X`, by the continuous
injection `|Y| → |X|`, not by its image set; `|Y|` need not carry the subspace topology of `|X|`.
Only when `|f|` is in addition a topological embedding does the factorisation condition reduce to
`|g|(|Z|) ⊆ |f|(|Y|)`, so that the injection is determined by its image subset with the subspace
topology ([ECD] §5,
Proposition 5.3 (iii)–(iv) and the paragraph after it, p. 21; [Berkeley] Lecture 8,
Definition/Proposition 8.3.3 (3), p. 61 for (ii')). *Needs:* *injection-of-perfectoid-spaces*;
*affinoid-perfectoid-field-points*; *residue-field-point-injection*; *qcqs-isomorphism-criterion*;
P2.16.

The step (iii) ⇒ (iv) uses the `(K, K⁺)`-points of a map that is injective on points with
isomorphic rank-one residue fields (*field-points-of-residually-injective-maps*): under (iii), for
every affinoid perfectoid field `(K, K⁺)` the map `f_* : Y(K, K⁺) → X(K, K⁺)` is injective with image
the `φ` whose closed point maps into `f(|Y|)` ([ECD] §5, proof of Proposition 5.3, (iii) ⇒ (iv),
p. 22).

The four criteria are `injection_iff_fieldPoints`, `injection_iff_geometricPoints`,
`injection_iff_residueFields` and `injection_iff_continuous_lift`; the affinoid comparisons
are `isInjection_iff_affinoid_tests` and `isInjection_affinoid_iff`.
`fieldPoints_image` specifies the image as precisely the points whose closed point lands in
that of the injection.

**Checks.**

- Same image, not isomorphic: the injection of P4.6 from the open disc together with its
  pro-rational complement has the same image as the identity of the closed disc, but the two are not
  isomorphic over the disc, since its `|f|` is a continuous bijection and not a homeomorphism; so an
  injection is not determined by its image set.
- Embedding case: a rational open immersion is an injection whose `|f|` is an open embedding, so it is
  determined by its image with the subspace topology.

### P4.8 base change of injections

**Base change of injections, and the underlying space of a pulled-back injection.**
(*injections-base-change-composition*) Let `f : Y → X` be an injection of perfectoid spaces and
`X' → X` any morphism, with base change `f' : Y' = X' ×_X Y → X'`. Then `f'` is an injection, and
the natural map `|Y'| → |X'| ×_{|X|} |Y|` is a homeomorphism (the target with the fibre product
topology). Moreover composites of injections are injections, and if `g ∘ f` is an injection then so
is `f` (use the supplier monomorphism instances for these categorical assertions) ([ECD] §5,
Corollary 5.5 (i), p. 24). *Needs:* *injection-of-perfectoid-spaces*; *injection-criteria*;
*maps-of-perfectoid-spaces-are-generalizing*; P2.16.

`injectionPullbackHomeomorph` identifies the actual categorical pullback with the
subspace of pairs `(y,z)` having the same image, and `injectionPullbackHomeomorph_apply`
fixes both projections in the order `(pullback.fst, pullback.snd)`.

### P4.9 universally injective maps

**Injections are exactly the universally injective maps.** (*injection-iff-universally-injective*)
A morphism `f : Y → X` of perfectoid spaces is an injection if and only if it is universally
injective: for every morphism `X' → X` the base change `f' : X' ×_X Y → X'` is injective on
underlying spaces; nothing beyond the existence of fibre products is assumed ([ECD] §5,
Corollary 5.5 (ii), p. 24). *Needs:* *injections-base-change-composition*; *injection-criteria*.

### P4.10 immersions, open immersions and closed immersions

Immersions are injections that are topological embeddings with locally closed image; this
subsection and the next define them and match the open ones with the open immersions of AdicSpaces.

**Immersions, open immersions and closed immersions of perfectoid spaces.** (*perfectoid-immersion*)
A morphism `f : Y → X` of perfectoid spaces is an immersion if `f` is an injection
(P4.3) and `|f| : |Y| → |X|` is a locally closed immersion, i.e. a
topological embedding (Mathlib `Topology.IsEmbedding`; `|Y|` carries its own spectral topology, and
the embedding condition says it is the subspace topology) with locally closed image (Mathlib
`IsLocallyClosed`). It is an open immersion (resp. closed immersion) if moreover `|f|` is an open
(resp. closed) embedding (Mathlib `Topology.IsOpenEmbedding`, `Topology.IsClosedEmbedding`). No
quasicompactness is assumed. The definition is possible because perfectoid spaces carry no nilpotent
structure: an injection is determined by its continuous injection `|Y| → |X|`
(*injection-criteria* (iv)), and when `|f|` is an embedding by its image with the subspace topology,
so an immersion is determined up to unique isomorphism over `X` by the locally closed subset
`f(|Y|)`. Neither condition on `|f|` follows from P4.7, so the definition is not redundant: the
injection of P4.6 from the open disc and its pro-rational complement is a bijection onto the closed
set `|X|` but not an embedding, and `i_η` at the Gauss point (P4.5) is an injection that is not an
immersion.
Closed immersions are strictly more general than Zariski closed immersions (P4.17). In
`PerfectoidSpace`, define `IsImmersion`, `IsOpenImmersion` and `IsClosedImmersion`.
`IsImmersion.isInjection` projects the `Mono f` conjunct of `IsImmersion`. Prove `IsImmersion.ext` (two immersions into `X` with the same image are
uniquely isomorphic over `X`), `IsImmersion.stableUnderGeneralization_range`,
`IsClosedImmersion.quasiCompact` and `IsOpenImmersion.of_isOpen` (for `U ⊆ |X|` open, the open
perfectoid subspace `U → X` is an open immersion) ([ECD] §5, Definition 5.6 and the sentence after
it, p. 24). *Needs:* *injection-of-perfectoid-spaces*; Mathlib `Topology.IsEmbedding`,
`IsLocallyClosed`, `Topology.IsOpenEmbedding`, `Topology.IsClosedEmbedding`; P2.10.

**Checks.**

- `isOpenImmersion_rationalSubset` (computation) — for `X = Spa(R, R⁺)` affinoid perfectoid and
  `U ⊆ X` rational, `U → X` is an open immersion.
- `isClosedImmersion_origin` (computation) — the point `T^{1/pⁿ} = 0` (all `n`), i.e.
  `Spa(C, O_C) → Spa(C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, O_C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩)`, is a closed immersion.
- `IsOpenImmersion_empty`, `IsClosedImmersion_empty`, `IsOpenImmersion_identity` and `IsClosedImmersion_identity` (degenerate) — the empty perfectoid space maps to every `X` by an open and
  closed immersion; the identity is both.

Additional Checks for these predicates are
