`IsImmersion_identity`, `IsImmersion_empty`, `IsImmersion_open`;
`IsOpenImmersion_identity`, `IsOpenImmersion_empty`, `IsOpenImmersion_open`;
and `IsClosedImmersion_identity`, `IsClosedImmersion_empty`, `IsClosedImmersion_principal`.
They compute identity and empty inclusions, arbitrary open restrictions, and the universal
closed inclusion for a principal ideal. The Gauss-point and annulus-closure Checks provide
the distinctions from a general injection and from a Zariski closed immersion.

### P4.11 open immersions agree with those of AdicSpaces

**Open immersions of perfectoid spaces agree with AdicSpaces' open immersions.**
(*open-immersion-comparison*) The P4 notion lives on `Perfd`:
`openImmersion_iff_adic` identifies it with `YonedaAdicSpace.IsOpenImmersion` on the
underlying sheaf morphism. For any adic representatives `g : A → B`, `eY`, `eX`
compatible with `f : Y → X` as in P4.2, `openImmersion_iff_preAdic` identifies it with
`TauCeti.PreAdicSpace.IsOpenImmersion g.hom` (AdicSpaces §5.1), through
`YonedaAdicSpace.ofAdicSpace`. On the pre-adic carrier of P2.10 this second identification is
definitional: open immersions of `Perfd` are `TauCeti.PreAdicSpace.IsOpenImmersion` between
perfectoid spaces. AdicEtaleGeometry A1.16's *adic-spaces-in-yoneda-adic-spaces*, by which `ofAdicSpace` preserves and
reflects open immersions, relates these two adic formulations. Equivalently, `f` identifies `Y` with the open
subspace `X|_U`, where `U = f(|Y|)`. Every open subset of `X` has its perfectoid
restriction (P2), and rational subsets of affinoid perfectoid spaces are affinoid
perfectoid. Thus open immersions into `X` correspond to its open subsets
([ECD] Proposition 5.3(iv), p. 21, and Definition 5.6, p. 24).
*Needs:* *perfectoid-immersion*; *injection-criteria*; layer P2;
`TauCeti.PreAdicSpace.IsOpenImmersion`; AdicEtaleGeometry's
*adic-spaces-in-yoneda-adic-spaces*.

### P4.12 Zariski closed subsets and Zariski closed immersions

Zariski closed subsets of an affinoid perfectoid space are the zero loci of ideals; this subsection
and the next define the two notions of closed immersion attached to them, which P4.15 shows agree.

**Zariski closed subsets and Zariski closed immersions into affinoid perfectoid spaces.**
(*zariski-closed-immersion*) Let `X = Spa(R, R⁺)` be an affinoid perfectoid space. For an ideal
`I ⊆ R` put `V(I) := {x ∈ |X| : |g(x)| = 0 for all g ∈ I}`; a subset `Z ⊆ |X|` is Zariski closed if
`Z = V(I)` for some ideal `I` ([Torsion] §II.2, Definition II.2.1, p. 13). A morphism `f : Z → X` of
perfectoid spaces is a Zariski closed immersion (defined by `I`) if `f` is a closed immersion
(P4.10) and `f(|Z|) = V(I)` ([ECD] §5, Definition 5.7 (i), p. 24). Conventions:
`V(I)` depends only on the closure of `I` and on its radical; `V(I) = ⋂_{F ⊆ I finite} U_F` with
`U_F := {x : |g(x)| ≤ 1 for g ∈ F}` rational, because `I` is an ideal and `|ϖ(x)|ⁿ → 0` cofinally at
every continuous valuation; `V(I)` is closed, pro-constructible and stable under generalization;
`V(I + J) = V(I) ∩ V(J)` and `V(IJ) = V(I ∩ J) = V(I) ∪ V(J)`; for a closed ideal `J`, `V(J)` is
the range of the closed embedding `spaComap` of the quotient pair (Tau Ceti
`Huber.Pair.Hom.range_spaComap_quotientHom`, `ValuationSpectrum.isClosedEmbedding_spaComap_quotientMk`),
which gives `isClosed_zeroLocus`. Every Zariski closed subset is the
image of exactly one Zariski closed immersion up to unique isomorphism (P4.14). A Zariski closed immersion defined by `I` need not be
`Spa(R/I, ·)`: the perfectoid structure on `V(I)` kills all compatible `p`-power roots. The global
notion over non-affinoid `X` (locally Zariski closed) is layer [P8](../PerfectoidTowers/README.md#layer-p8-finite-quotients-and-closed-perfectoid-loci-in-towers). In `PerfectoidSpace`, define
`zeroLocus` (`V(I)`), `IsZariskiClosed` and `IsZariskiClosedImmersion`; prove
`zeroLocus_eq_iInter_rational` (`V(I) = ⋂_F U_F`), `isClosed_zeroLocus`,
`stableUnderGeneralization_zeroLocus`, `zeroLocus_sup`, `zeroLocus_mul`, `zeroLocus_closure`
(simp: `V(closure I) = V(I)` and `V(√I) = V(I)`).
`IsZariskiClosedImmersion.isClosedImmersion` projects the closed-immersion conjunct
of [ECD] Definition 5.7(i), p. 24. *Needs:* *perfectoid-immersion*; Tau Ceti
`TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.rationalSubset`, `TauCeti.Huber.Pair.Hom.range_spaComap_quotientHom`,
`TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.isClosedEmbedding_spaComap_quotientMk`.

**Checks.**

- `zeroLocus_T` (computation) — for `R = C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩`, `V((T)) = {origin}`, and the Zariski closed
  immersion is `Spa(C, O_C) → X`; its kernel is the closure of the ideal generated by all
  `T^{1/pⁿ}`, not `(T)`.
- `zeroLocus_T_sub_one` and `zeroLocus_T_sub_one_char_p` (computation) — for `C = ℂ_p`, with the power-bounded plus ring and a chosen
  compatible system of primitive roots `ζ_{pⁿ}`, `V((T − 1)) ⊆ Spa(C⟨T^{±1/p^∞}⟩, C⟨T^{±1/p^∞}⟩°)` is homeomorphic to `ℤ_p`
  (compatible systems of `p`-power roots of unity, `γ ↦ (ζ_{pⁿ}^γ)_n`); for a perfectoid field `C` of characteristic `p`,
  `T − 1 = (T^{1/pⁿ} − 1)^{pⁿ}` and `V((T − 1))` is the single point `T^{1/pⁿ} = 1` for all `n`.
- `zeroLocus_bot_top` (degenerate) — `V(0) = |X|` and `V(R) = ∅`.

Additional Checks: `zeroLocus_bot_top` computes the whole and empty spaces;
`zeroLocus_two_ideals` computes `V(a,b) = V(a) ∩ V(b)` and
`V(ab) = V(a) ∪ V(b)`; `zeroLocus_nilpotent_quotient` computes
`V(aⁿ) = V(a)` for `n > 0`. Checks `isZariskiClosed_whole`, `isZariskiClosed_empty` and
`isZariskiClosed_union` test the subset predicate; `zariskiImmersion_id`,
`zariskiImmersion_empty` and `zariskiImmersion_nonclosed` test identity, empty source and the
obstruction of a nonclosed image. These use valuation support ideals, as in the supplier's
quotient-spectrum range formula.

### P4.13 strongly Zariski closed immersions

**Strongly Zariski closed immersions: surjective perfectoid quotients.**
(*strongly-zariski-closed-immersion*) Let `X = Spa(R, R⁺)` be an affinoid perfectoid space. A
morphism `f : Z → X` is strongly Zariski closed if `Z = Spa(S, S⁺)` is affinoid perfectoid, `f` is
induced by a morphism `(R, R⁺) → (S, S⁺)` with `R → S` surjective, and `S⁺` is the integral closure
of the image of `R⁺` in `S` ([ECD] §5, Definition 5.7 (ii), p. 24); `S` perfectoid is part of the
data. Equivalently (by the open mapping theorem, Tau Ceti `Huber.IsTateRing.isQuotientMap`), with
`I := ker(R → S)` closed, `(S, S⁺)` is isomorphic to the library's quotient pair
`TauCeti.Huber.Pair.quotient (R, R⁺) I`, whose plus ring is the integral closure of the image of
`R⁺` (`Huber.Pair.quotient_plus`), and `R/I` is perfectoid. The plus-ring clause is part of the
definition: it is what makes a strongly Zariski closed map a closed immersion (P4.21).
The algebraic predicate `IsStronglyZariskiClosed_affinoid` is defined for arbitrary Huber pairs
by these two clauses, without completeness or perfectoidness; its geometric interpretation and
the base-change theorem here require perfectoid Tate rings. For base change along `(A,A⁺) → (C,C⁺)`,
the resulting ring map is `C → B ⊗̂_A C`, the supplier’s `completedTensor.inr` (in `Huber.Pair`). In `PerfectoidSpace`, define `IsStronglyZariskiClosed`;
prove `stronglyZariskiClosed_affinoid_iff` (the affine predicate supplies both surjectivity
and the plus-ring equality through its fields), `stronglyZariskiClosed_isClosed_ker`,
`stronglyZariskiClosed_quotient_comparison` and `stronglyZariskiClosed_iff_zariskiClosed`
(the quotient immersion is defined by `ker(R → S)`). *Needs:* Tau Ceti
`TauCeti.Huber.Pair`, `TauCeti.Huber.Pair.quotient`, `TauCeti.Huber.Pair.quotient_plus`,
`TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing.isQuotientMap`.

**Checks.**

- `completedTensor_inr_two_terms` (convention) — base change sends `c + d ∈ C` to
  the completion of `1 ⊗ c + 1 ⊗ d ∈ B ⊗_A C`; with `c = 2`, `d = 3` its value is `5`.
- `isStronglyZariskiClosed_origin` (computation) — `C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ → C`, `T^{1/pⁿ} ↦ 0`, with plus
  rings `O_C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ → O_C`, is strongly Zariski closed.
- `stronglyClosed_id` (degenerate) — the identity of `X` and the map from the empty space
  `Spa(0, 0)` are strongly Zariski closed.
- `stronglyClosed_quotient` (supplier agreement) — for any Huber pair `P` and any ideal `I`,
  `Pair.quotientHom P I` satisfies the algebraic predicate; `I = 0` and `I = ⊤` give
  the identity quotient and the zero quotient. No perfectoidness of the quotient is inferred.
- `not_isStronglyZariskiClosed_ofPowerBounded` (non-example) — for `R⁺ ⊊ R°`,
  `Spa(R, R°) → Spa(R, R⁺)` has `R → R` surjective and `R⁺ → R°` almost surjective ([ECD] Example
  3.22 (ii)), but `R°` is not the integral closure of `R⁺`, so it is not strongly Zariski closed
  (nor a closed immersion).

The geometric predicate `IsStronglyZariskiClosed` requires an affinoid presentation of the
source and the actual algebraic strong-quotient condition on its presenting map.
Checks `strongImmersion_id`, `strongImmersion_empty`, `strongImmersion_larger_plus` give
identity, empty source, and failure for a strict enlargement of the plus ring on the same
ring. `stronglyZariskiClosed_affinoid_iff` compares it to the affine predicate.

### P4.14 the universal perfectoid space over a Zariski closed subset

The universal perfectoid Zariski closed subspace is the pro-rational subspace of the rational
neighbourhoods `U_F` of `V(I)`; this subsection builds it and the next two show it is a surjective
perfectoid quotient and match it with the closed immersions of AdicSpaces.

**The universal perfectoid space over a Zariski closed subset.**
(*universal-perfectoid-zariski-closed*) Let `X = Spa(R, R⁺)` be an affinoid perfectoid space with a
pseudouniformizer `ϖ ∈ R⁺` with `ϖ^p | p` admitting compatible `p`-power roots, and `I ⊆ R` an ideal (not necessarily
closed or finitely generated). Let `𝒰_I := {U_F : F ⊆ I finite}`,
`U_F = {x : |g(x)| ≤ 1 for g ∈ F}`, and use `zariskiClosedSubspace.presentation_affinoid D F` for the presentation
`({1} ∪ F)/1`. This definition only needs a commutative topological ring and a pair of
definition `D`, without a perfectoid hypothesis. Let `ι_I : Z_I = Spa(S_I, S_I⁺) → X` be the pro-rational
subspace of `𝒰_I` (P4.4): `S_I⁺` is the `ϖ`-adic completion of
`colim_F O⁺_X(U_F)` and `S_I = S_I⁺[1/ϖ]`. Then: (a) `Z_I` is affinoid perfectoid and `R → S_I`
has dense image; (b) `|ι_I|` is a homeomorphism onto `V(I)`; (c) a morphism `g : W → X` from a
perfectoid space factors through `ι_I` if and only if `g^*(h) = 0` in `O_W(W)` for all `h ∈ I`, if
and only if `|g|` lands in `V(I)`, and then uniquely; (d) `ι_I` is a Zariski closed immersion
defined by `I` (P4.12); (e) `I^perf := ker(R → S_I)` is a closed ideal
containing `I`, equal to `{h ∈ R : |h| = 0 on V(I)}`, and `Z_{I^perf} = Z_I`; (f) `Z_I` depends
only on `V(I)`. In `PerfectoidSpace`, define `zariskiClosedSubspace` (`Z_I`) and
`zariskiClosedSubspace.ι` (`ι_I`); prove `zariskiClosedSubspace.range_ι` (homeomorphism onto
`V(I)`), `zariskiClosedSubspace.lift` (with factorization and uniqueness in the `∃!` statement),
`zariskiClosedSubspace.isZariskiClosedImmersion`, `zariskiClosedSubspace.denseRange`,
`zariskiClosedSubspace.ker_eq` ((e)), `zariskiClosedSubspace.congr` ((f)) and
`zariskiClosedSubspace_bot` (simp: `Z_0 = X`, `Z_R = ∅`) ([Torsion] §II.2, Lemma II.2.2, p. 13, and
Remark II.2.3, p. 14; [Bhatt] §9.4, Proposition 9.4.1 (1), p. 112). *Needs:*
*intersection-of-rational-subsets*; *zariski-closed-immersion*; *perfectoid-immersion*.

**Checks.**

- `presentation_empty` (degenerate) — `F = ∅` gives numerators `{1}` and denominator `1`.
- `presentation_zero` (computation) — `F = {0}` gives `{1,0}/1`; the extra inequality is
  `0 ≤ 1`, so its rational subset is the whole spectrum.
- `presentation_two_terms` (convention) — `F = {a,b}` gives `{1,a,b}/1`, imposing both
  `|a| ≤ 1` and `|b| ≤ 1`. In `presentation_two_term_bounds`, `(a,b) = (0,1)`
  gives the whole spectrum, while `(0,ϖ⁻¹)` gives the empty set for a topologically
  nilpotent unit `ϖ`: the second value is greater than one.
- `presentation_membership` (supplier agreement) — membership is exactly membership in
  `spa(R⁺)` together with `x.toValuativeRel.vle a 1` for every `a ∈ F`.
- `zariskiClosedSubspace_T` (computation) — `R = C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩`, `I = (T)`: `S_I = C`, and
  `ker(R → S_I)` is the closure of `(T^{1/pⁿ} : n ≥ 0) ⊋ (T)`; `R/(T)` is not reduced.
  The example uses `zariskiClosedMap`, a continuous ring isomorphism `S_I ≃ C`
  fixing constants, and equality with that closed ideal. Evaluation of the root
  polynomials at zero gives the calculation; the universal perfectoid quotient
  is [Torsion] Lemma II.2.2 and Remark II.2.3, pp. 13–14.
- `zariskiClosedSubspace_T_sub_one` (computation) — `C = ℂ_p`, `R = C⟨T^{±1/p^∞}⟩`, `I = (T − 1)`:
  `S_I = C⁰(ℤ_p, ℂ_p)`, with `T^{1/pⁿ} ↦ (γ ↦ ζ_{pⁿ}^γ)` ([AWS] Lecture 2, Example 2.4.10); the
  image is dense (the characters of `ℤ/pⁿ` span the functions on `ℤ/pⁿ`, `p` being invertible),
  `R → S_I` is surjective by P4.15, and `I^perf ⊋ (T − 1)` although `(T − 1)` is closed (P4.15).
- `zariskiClosedSubspace_bot` (degenerate) — `Z_0 = X` and `Z_R = ∅`.

Every Zariski closed immersion is the universal one (*zariski-closed-immersion-is-universal*): for
a Zariski closed immersion `f : Z → X = Spa(R, R⁺)` defined by `I`, there is a unique isomorphism
`Z ≅ Z_I` over `X`; consequently `Z` is affinoid perfectoid, `Z = lim_{F ⊆ I finite} U_F`, and a
Zariski closed immersion is determined by its image `V(I)` ([Torsion] §II.2, after Remark II.2.3,
p. 14).

`zariskiClosedPair_universal` characterizes the ring map by unique factorization among
perfectoid pairs annihilating `I`; `zariskiClosedSubspace.lift` gives the corresponding
factorization for every perfectoid space. `range_ι`, `ker_eq`, `congr` and `universal`
fix the underlying subset, the vanishing ideal and the isomorphisms over `X`.
Checks `zariskiClosedSubspace_bot`, `zariskiClosedSubspace_top` and
`zariskiClosedSubspace_radical` compute identity, empty source and invariance under radical;
`disc_origin` and `disc_ordinary_quotient_nilpotent` distinguish the perfectoid quotient
from the ordinary quotient by `(T)`.

`zariskiClosedSubspace_T_sub_one` specifies the continuous-function quotient over `ℂ_p`
with a chosen compatible sequence of primitive roots, sending the nth root of `T` to
`γ ↦ ζ_{pⁿ}^{γ mod pⁿ}`. It also states the strict enlargement of the kernel beyond
`(T−1)`. `zariskiClosedSubspace_T_sub_one_char_p` computes the contrasting characteristic-p
quotient: every root of `T` maps to `1`.

### P4.15 Zariski closed immersions are strongly Zariski closed

The proof route is [BS22] §7.1–§7.3. P4.15.1 consumes the generic derived-algebra inputs
and supplies the additional compatibilities specified below; P4.15.2–P4.15.5 own the
prismatic construction. They use P1 and P0.19's supplied ordinary cotangent complex, independently of the
Zariski-closed theorem in P4.15.6 and of its consumers in P6, PerfectoidTowers and
DiamondsAndVStacks. The algebraic constructions apply to integral perfectoid rings,
including rings with p-torsion and the zero ring.

#### P4.15.1 derived completion and complete flat descent

**Derived algebra for the semiperfectoid construction, consumed and specialized.**
(*semiperfectoid-derived-completion-descent*) Use DerivedModuleAlgebra's generic
carriers and maps in the following table. For a commutative ring `B` write
`D(B) = DerivedCategory (ModuleCat B)` with cohomological indexing; connective means
`H^i = 0` for `i > 0`. For finite `J ⊂ B`, `Λ_J` means that supplier's completion
reflector, with its specified unit.

| Supplier subsection | Imported API and use |
| --- | --- |
| DerivedModuleAlgebra §§0.1–0.4 and 0.14 | `Algebra.CotangentComplex.PolynomialResolution`, its `comparison` and `toQuasiIso`, `DerivedDeRham.derivedTensor`, `DerivedDeRham.leftDerivedNonadditive`, `DerivedDeRham.derivedExteriorPower` and the ordinary cotangent complex supply the resolution and power models for P4.15.2–P4.15.3. |
| DerivedModuleAlgebra §§1.1–1.6 | `DerivedDeRham.derivedLimit`, `DerivedDeRham.derivedCompleteness`, `DerivedDeRham.derivedCompletion`, `DerivedDeRham.completionUnit`, `DerivedDeRham.completionAdjunction`, `DerivedDeRham.completeNakayama`, `DerivedDeRham.koszulCompletionTower`, `DerivedDeRham.ordinaryQuotientCompletion` and `DerivedDeRham.simplicialRingCompletion` supply completion and its algebra unit. |
| DerivedModuleAlgebra §§1.7–1.9 | `DerivedDeRham.completeFlatness`, its discrete predicate `DerivedDeRham.IsCompletelyFlatModule`, `DerivedDeRham.completeFlatBaseChange`, `DerivedDeRham.boundedTorsionCriterion` and `DerivedDeRham.completeFlatDescent` supply complete flatness and descent for p-complete ordinary rings with bounded p-power torsion. |

Convention: `M` is J-completely flat precisely when `M ⊗_B^L B/J` is a flat
`B/J`-module in degree zero; complete faithful flatness additionally means that this
reduction is faithfully flat. Neither predicate includes completeness. The equivalent
J-power-torsion-module criterion is the supplier's §1.7. A completed tensor is
`Λ_J(M ⊗_B^L N)`. Realizations use direct-sum totalization of simplicial module models,
while Čech descent uses product totalization of cosimplicial complexes; completion is
applied to the resulting derived objects. Retain simplicial algebra models and their
multiplication through `simplicialRingCompletion`, rather than treating normalization as
a strictly commutative differential graded algebra. For discrete modules, ordinary
completion agrees with derived completion when the higher Koszul homology towers are
pro-zero; in particular a principal ideal and bounded power torsion on the module suffice
([BS22] §1.2, pp. 10–12, footnotes 5–7;
[Stacks, tag 0920](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0920)).

The additional targets below use these same carriers and units.

- `semiperfectoidFiniteIdealDescent`: for a commutative ring `B`, finite
  `J = (f₁, …, f_r)` and a J-completely faithfully flat map `E• → F•` of simplicial
  commutative B-algebras, prove effective descent for derived J-complete modules along
  its derived J-completed Čech nerve. Thus the complete module category over `E•` is
  equivalent to the limit of those over that nerve, and a complete module is recovered
  by product totalization of its completed base changes. Complete flatness is measured
  after reduction to `π₀(E•)/Jπ₀(E•)`. This is strictly more general than the supplier's
  §1.9: it permits arbitrary finite ideals and simplicial bases without a bounded-torsion
  hypothesis. Supply the derived module models over simplicial bases and their coherent
  descent data, using simplicial resolutions and quasi-isomorphisms on underlying module
  complexes. Build the adapter to compatible systems over the simplicial Koszul quotients
  on `(f₁^n, …, f_r^n)` with the supplier's module-limit models. Prove simplicial
  faithfully flat descent at each Koszul level, then take the inverse limit. On §1.9's domain,
  identify this equivalence and its augmentation with `DerivedDeRham.completeFlatDescent`
  ([BS22] §1.2, footnote 7, p. 12). Composition, completed base change and completed
  filtered colimits preserve complete flatness; complete faithful flatness is preserved
  for diagrams of covers over a fixed base, as detected by faithfully flat reduction.
- `semiperfectoidCompletionSurjectivity`: for a p-completely faithfully flat map of
  ordinary rings `B → C`, and a map `M → N` of discrete derived p-complete B-modules,
  surjectivity on `H⁰` after derived p-completed base change implies surjectivity of
  `M → N`. Use the supplier's derived Nakayama and complete-flat reduction on the
  cokernel. Degree-zero completion is right exact on connective complexes for every
  finite ideal: completing a triangle of connective complexes gives the right exact
  sequence on `H⁰` ([BS22] §1.2 and proof of Theorem 7.4, p. 62;
  [Stacks, tag 0G1U](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0G1U) and
  [tag 0AAJ](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0AAJ)).
- `semiperfectoidCompletionTransfinite`: for a fixed finite ideal of `B`, derived
  completion commutes with `ω₁`-filtered colimits in `D(B)` and in simplicial B-algebras,
  compatibly with `completionUnit` and `ringCompletionUnit`. The finite-generator Koszul
  tower has countably many levels; `ω₁`-filtered colimits commute with the countable
  products in its derived-limit model. Apply this to `(p,d)` in P4.15.2 and `(p)` in
  P4.15.4 ([BS22] proof of Proposition 7.2, p. 55).

*Needs:* DerivedModuleAlgebra §§0.1–0.4, 0.14 and 1.1–1.9 as listed above;
Mathlib `DerivedCategory`, `CategoryTheory.SimplicialObject` and `TensorProduct`.

The simplicial module and faithfully flat descent adapters are included in
`semiperfectoidFiniteIdealDescent` here, as in [BS22] §1.2, footnote 7.
P4.15.2–P4.15.5 consume this subsection; the transfinite constructions use P1's
integral perfectoid interfaces.

**Checks.**

- For `J = (p)` and `B = ℤ_p`, completion fixes `B` in degree zero.
- The derived p-completion of `ℚ` is zero; `ℚ` is not itself derived p-complete.
- Over `ℤ_p`, the derived tensor of `𝔽_p` with `𝔽_p` has nonzero first Tor,
  so `ℤ_p → 𝔽_p` is not p-completely flat despite its flat ordinary reduction.
- Finite-ideal descent along the identity of the simplicial algebra
  `𝔽_p ⊗^L_ℤ 𝔽_p`, with `J = (p)`, retains its nonzero `H^−1`; descent does not
  replace a simplicial base by its degree-zero ring.
- For `J = (p,d)` and `B = ℤ_p[[d]]`, descent along `B → B × B` recovers every
  complete B-module with its canonical augmentation, using both ideal generators.
- For nonzero derived p-complete `M`, derived p-completed base change to `B[1/p]`
  kills `M`, so it cannot reflect surjectivity of `0 → M`; its zero reduction is not
  faithfully flat when `B/p ≠ 0`.
- Degree-zero completion sends the surjection `ℤ → ℤ/p` to `ℤ_p → ℤ/p`.
- A constant `ω₁`-filtered diagram has the identity comparison with completion.
- In the `ω₁`-filtered union of countable subsets `S` of `ω₁`, the union of the
  p-completions of `⨁_{s∈S} ℤ` is the p-completion of `⨁_{s<ω₁} ℤ`: every completed
  element has countable support.
- Countable filtered colimits alone fail: the union of `ℤ_p^n` under zero-extension
  is not p-complete; the compatible reductions of `(1,p,p²,…)` are missing.

#### P4.15.2 universal prisms and perfection

**Prisms for semiperfectoid rings.** (*semiperfectoid-universal-prism*) Develop `δ`-rings,
free `δ`-algebras, distinguished elements, and their divided-power comparison as in
[BS22] §2, restricted to the constructions below. A prism `(B, J)` has `B` a `δ`-ring,
`J` a Cartier-divisor ideal, derived `(p, J)`-complete `B`, and `p ∈ J + φ(J)B`;
bounded means `B/J` has bounded p-power torsion, and perfect means `φ` is invertible.
Prove rigidity `JB' = J'` for maps of prisms. For a bounded prism `(B,J)` and a
`(p,J)`-completely flat `δ`-`B`-algebra `D`, construct the prismatic envelope of an ideal
`K ⊇ JD` locally generated by `J` and a `(p,J)`-completely regular sequence relative
to `B`; prove its complete flatness over `B`, completed base change in bounded prisms
and compatibility with flat localization in `D`. Prove the equivalence between
perfect prisms and P1.24's integral perfectoid rings.
For any prism construct its initial perfect prism by Frobenius colimit and
`(p, J)`-completion; this construction includes the bounded-torsion comparison that
makes the completed perfection an ordinary ring ([BS22] §3, Definition 3.2,
Lemmas 3.5, 3.8–3.9, Theorem 3.10 and Proposition 3.13, pp. 28–35).

For an integral perfectoid `R`, prove that `(A_inf(R), ker θ)` is initial among prisms
with a map from `R` to their quotient ([BS22] Lemma 4.8, pp. 38–39). For a derived
p-complete quotient `A = R/K`, construct the initial prism `(Δ_init(A), (d))` with
`A → Δ_init(A)/d`: freely `δ`-adjoin `k/d` for lifts of generators of `K`, kill the
`δ`-ideal generated by d-power torsion, and iterate degree-zero derived `(p,d)`-completion
and torsion removal transfinitely until d is regular. Prove independence of the
presentation by initiality. Perfect this prism and take its quotient to construct
`semiperfectoidPerfectoidization` and its universal map ([BS22] Proposition 7.2 and
Corollary 7.3, pp. 55–56). This construction proves initiality without surjectivity.
*Needs:* P1.16–P1.18 and P1.24; P4.15.1; P0.19's cotangent and lifting API for Lemma 4.8.

**Checks.**

- For a perfect `𝔽_p`-algebra `k`, the corresponding perfect prism is `(W(k), (p))`.
- For integral perfectoid `A`, the initial prism is `(A_inf(A), ker θ)`, and its
  perfect-prism quotient recovers `A` with the identity structural map.
- For `A = 0`, the initial prism, its perfection and its quotient are zero;
  regularity is interpreted in the zero ring as well.

#### P4.15.3 the affine Hodge–Tate input

**Affine prismatic comparison and quasisyntomic covers.**
(*semiperfectoid-affine-hodge-tate*) For a bounded oriented prism `(B, (d))` and a
p-completely smooth `B/d`-algebra `C`, construct `Δ_{C/B}` with Frobenius by the
Čech–Alexander complexes of prismatic envelopes. Prove the affine Hodge–Tate comparison
`H^i(Δ_{C/B} ⊗_B^L B/d) ≅ Ω̂^i_{C/(B/d)}`, using the orientation to trivialize the
twists, and completed base change along maps of bounded oriented prisms. Here
`Ω̂^i_{C/(B/d)} := H^0(Λ_(p)(L∧^i_C L_{C/(B/d)}))` is the module of continuous
p-completed differential forms: use the ordinary cotangent complex of P0.19 and
DerivedModuleAlgebra's `derivedExteriorPower` and `derivedCompletion`, as supplied
by P4.15.1. For p-completely smooth `C`, this completed derived exterior power is
concentrated in degree zero; for `C = (B/d)⟨T⟩`, its degree-one module is `C dT`.
This subsection
owns the characteristic-p polynomial divided-power calculation and the universal
oriented-prism reduction used to prove that comparison ([BS22] §4.3,
Construction 4.18 and Lemmas 4.19–4.21; §5, Corollary 5.5; §6, Proposition 6.2 and
Theorem 6.3, pp. 42–53). No global prismatic-cohomology output is required.

Extend this affine construction by polynomial simplicial resolutions and derived
completion, as in [BS22] Construction 7.6, pp. 56–57. Prove resolution independence,
completed base change and preservation of homotopy colimits. The Hodge–Tate reduction
has an exhaustive conjugate filtration with graded pieces the derived p-completions of
`∧^i L_{C/(B/d)}[-i]` in cohomological indexing, with twists trivialized by `d`.
A quasisyntomic `B/d`-algebra here is p-completely flat over `B/d`, derived p-complete
with bounded p-power torsion, and has p-complete relative cotangent Tor amplitude
`[-1,0]`; a cover is also p-completely faithfully flat.
Construct the covers obtained by adjoining all p-power roots of polynomial generators.
For bounded-torsion `C` with p-completely flat `L_{C/(B/d)}[-1]`, prove that the
Hodge–Tate reduction is discrete and p-completely faithfully flat over `C`, and that
the prismatic complex is discrete with the `δ`-structure and prism of Lemma 7.7.
For quasiregular semiperfectoid `A` (bounded p-power torsion and p-completely flat
`L_{A/ℤ_p}[-1]`), prove that `Δ_{A/A_inf(R)}` and its Hodge–Tate reduction are
discrete, identify the resulting prism with `Δ_init(A)`, and prove that
`A → Δ_init(A)/d` is p-completely faithfully flat. Include the regular-quotient envelope
calculation and the idempotent-retract argument needed for this identification
([BS22] Lemmas 7.7–7.8, Example 7.9 and Proposition 7.10, pp. 57–60).
*Needs:* P4.15.1–P4.15.2; P0.19's full cotangent complex with transitivity and filtered
colimits; P1's perfected polynomial algebras. These prismatic and quasisyntomic inputs
are owned here, rather than assigned to the cotangent supplier.

**Checks.**

- For `(B,d) = (ℤ_p,p)` and `C = 𝔽_p`, the prismatic complex is `ℤ_p` in degree zero.
- For `C = 𝔽_p[T]` over that prism, the Hodge–Tate reduction has `H^0 = C`,
  `H^1 = C dT`, and no higher cohomology.
- For the bounded oriented prism `B = ℤ_p[[u]]`, `d = u-p`, `φ(u) = u^p`,
  with `B/d = ℤ_p`, and `C = ℤ_p⟨T⟩`, the Hodge–Tate reduction has `H^0 = C`,
  `H^1 = Ω̂^1_{C/ℤ_p} = C dT`, and no higher cohomology. For `F = exp(p²T) ∈ C`,
  completion kills `dF − p²F dT`, a nonzero class in ordinary algebraic
  `Ω^1_{C/ℤ_p}`; thus the ordinary differential module cannot replace `Ω̂^1`.
- For `A = 𝔽_p[T^{1/p^∞}]/(T)`, the quasiregular comparison applies although `A`
  is nonreduced: the class of `T^{1/p}` is nonzero with p-th power zero.

#### P4.15.4 André's root-adjoining cover

**Completely faithfully flat perfectoid root cover.** (*semiperfectoid-andre-cover*)
For every integral perfectoid `R`, construct a p-completely faithfully flat map
`R → R'` with `R'` integral perfectoid and every monic polynomial over `R'` having
a root in `R'`. In particular every element of `R'` admits compatible p-power roots.
Supply Proposition 7.11's input: for a bounded oriented prism `(B,(d))` and a
quasisyntomic `B/d`-algebra `C`, construct a prism `(D,dD)` with a p-completely
faithfully flat map `C → D/dD`. The prism map is completely flat, and is completely
faithfully flat if `B/d → C` is p-completely faithfully flat; these properties persist
on perfection when `B` is perfect. Build it using the root-adjoining quasisyntomic cover and the discrete
Hodge–Tate comparison of P4.15.3. Apply this to adjoining solutions of all monic
equations, and iterate with completed transfinite colimits to obtain `R'`
([BS22] Proposition 7.11, p. 60; Theorem 7.14 and its proof, p. 61).
*Needs:* P4.15.1–P4.15.3; P1.24. No Zariski-closed or tower theorem is an input.

**Checks.**

- For an algebraically closed characteristic-p field, the identity is a cover with
  the asserted monic-root property.
- The zero ring admits the identity cover, and its unique element has zero roots.
- Merely adjoining a single root is insufficient: `𝔽_p[X]/(X^p−1)` has nonzero
  nilpotent `X−1`, so is not integral perfectoid. The prism and perfection steps
  supply the perfectoid target of the cover.

#### P4.15.5 rooted quotients and the surjectivity reduction

**Rooted quotient and descent of the perfectoidization map.**
(*semiperfectoid-rooted-quotient-reduction*) Let `R` be integral perfectoid and
`r : ℕ → R` satisfy `r(n+1)^p = r(n)`. Put `J = (r(n) | n ∈ ℕ)` and
`Q = (R/J)^∧_p`. Prove `isIntegralPerfectoid_completedRootQuotient`: `Q` is integral
perfectoid; also prove `surjective_completedRootQuotientMap` for the canonical
`R → R/J → Q`. Prove reducedness of integral perfectoid rings using the perfect-prism
comparison. Hence every map from `R/(r(0))` to an integral perfectoid ring kills `J`.
Completeness of the target then gives the
unique factorization through `Q`. Thus `Q` is its perfectoidization, with surjective
structural map ([BS22] proof of Theorem 7.4, p. 62).

For a p-completely faithfully flat map `R → R'` of integral perfectoid rings and
a derived p-complete quotient `A` of `R`, let `A' = (A ⊗_R^L R')^∧_p`.
Prove the flat base-change comparison
`(A_perfd ⊗_R^L R')^∧_p ≅ A'_perfd`, with the structural maps fixed. This includes
discreteness of both base changes and integral perfectoidness of the completed tensor
on the left, using the perfect-prism comparison and flat completed base change of
P4.15.2–P4.15.3. Descend surjectivity by P4.15.1. Supply the completed filtered-colimit
reduction to finitely generated defining ideals and the successive-principal-quotient
reduction, carrying derived p-completeness at each step. Use P4.15.4 to root the
principal defining element after flat base change and apply the rooted quotient
calculation. This proves `semiperfectoidPerfectoidization_surjective` from its
construction, without using the Tate-space application ([BS22] proof of Theorem 7.4,
p. 62, with the base-change machinery of Construction 7.6(4)–(5), pp. 56–57).
*Needs:* P4.15.1–P4.15.4; P1.24's integral perfectoid theory.

**Checks.**

- For `r(n) = 0`, `Q = R` and the structural map is the identity.
- For `r(n) = 1`, `Q = 0` and the structural map is the surjection to zero.
- For `R = 𝔽_p[T^{1/p^∞}]` and `r(n) = T^{1/p^n}`, `Q = 𝔽_p`. The ordinary
  quotient `R/(T)` is nonreduced and is not this perfectoid quotient.

#### P4.15.6 the Zariski-closed application

**Zariski closed immersions are strongly Zariski closed.** (*zariski-closed-is-strongly-zariski-closed*)
Let `X = Spa(R, R⁺)` be an affinoid perfectoid space and `I ⊆ R` an ideal. The universal perfectoid
space `Z` over the Zariski closed subset `V(I)` (P4.14) is affinoid
perfectoid, `Z = Spa(S, S⁺)`, with `R → S` surjective, `S⁺` the integral closure of the image of
`R⁺`, and `R⁺ → S⁺` almost surjective; in particular `|Z| → V(I)` is a homeomorphism. Hence every
Zariski closed immersion is strongly Zariski closed, and the two notions coincide.
The direction "Zariski closed implies strongly Zariski closed" is stated for
`f : Y ⟶ ofPair p R`, and `stronglyZariskiClosed_iff_zariskiClosed` retains the equivalence; the
ring-level core, the universal perfectoid quotient of `R` killing `I`, is the Lean
`Perfectoid.exists_surjective_perfectoidQuotient`. The input is
the perfectoidization of semiperfectoid rings, applied to the `ϖ`-adic completion
`A := (R⁺/(I ∩ R⁺))^∧_ϖ`, as in [BS22] Remark 7.5: the target
`semiperfectoidPerfectoidization` of P4.15.2 constructs, for a derived `p`-complete ring `A` that is a
quotient of an integral perfectoid ring, the initial integral perfectoid ring `A_perfd` under `A`.
P4.15.5 proves `semiperfectoidPerfectoidization_surjective`; its kernel consists of the elements killed
by every map from `A` to an integral perfectoid ring. Also prove
`semiperfectoidPerfectoidization_tensor`: for every integral perfectoid `A`-algebra `B`, the
multiplication map `A_perfd ⊗_A B → B` is an isomorphism. Applied to the completed quotient
above, this gives `S = A_perfd[1/ϖ]` and `S⁺` the integral closure of the image of `R⁺` in `S`
([BS22] §7, Corollary 7.3, Theorem 7.4 and Remark 7.5, p. 56; proof of Theorem 7.4, p. 62;
[ECD] §5, Theorem 5.8, p. 25). *Needs:*
*universal-perfectoid-zariski-closed*; *strongly-zariski-closed-immersion*;
*zariski-closed-immersion*; P1.24; P4.15.1–P4.15.5.

A surjection of perfectoid Tate rings is almost surjective on integral elements
(*surjective-perfectoid-map-almost-surjective-on-plus-rings*): for a surjective continuous
homomorphism `ψ : R → S` of perfectoid Tate rings and rings of integral elements `R⁺`, `S⁺` with
`ψ(R⁺) ⊆ S⁺`, the cokernels of `R° → S°` and `R⁺ → S⁺` are killed by every `ϖ^{1/pⁿ}`
([AWS] Lecture 2, Lemma 2.8.5, pp. 70–71). Zariski closed and strongly Zariski closed immersions are stable
under base change (*zariski-closed-base-change*): for `Z → X` Zariski closed defined by `I` and
`X' = Spa(R', R'⁺) → X` any morphism of affinoid perfectoid spaces, `Z ×_X X' → X'` is Zariski
closed defined by `IR'`, with `Z_I ×_X X' ≅ Z_{IR'}`, and strongly Zariski closed when `Z → X` is
([Torsion] §II.2, Lemma II.2.9 (i)–(ii), pp. 15–16).

The structure `SemiperfectoidRing` requires both a derived p-complete ring and an actual
surjective map from an integral perfectoid ring. `DerivedPComplete` uses the equivalent
sequence test: `(x_n) ↦ (x_n − p x_{n+1})` is bijective. This is the telescope criterion for
`RHom(ℤ[1/p], A) = 0` ([Stacks, §15.93, tag 091N](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/091N)).
`semiperfectoidPerfectoidization_universal`, `_surjective`, `_kernel` and `_tensor`
state universality, the quotient property, the universal vanishing kernel, and the tensor
isomorphism, with the latter fixing `1 ⊗ b ↦ b`.

Checks:

| Definition | Checks and results |
| --- | --- |
| `DerivedPComplete` | `derivedComplete_characteristic_p`: every characteristic-p ring passes; `derivedComplete_padic`: `ℤ_p` passes; `derivedComplete_rational_negative`: `ℚ` fails, since `(p^{-n})` gives a nonzero kernel sequence. |
| `SemiperfectoidRing` | `SemiperfectoidRing_characteristic_p`: a perfect characteristic-p ring; `SemiperfectoidRing_quotient`: any quotient of such a ring; `SemiperfectoidRing_no_rational`: no underlying ring is isomorphic to `ℚ`. |
| `semiperfectoidPerfectoidization` | `semiperfectoid_fixed`: an integral perfectoid input is fixed; `semiperfectoid_zero`: the zero input stays zero; `semiperfectoid_kills_roots`: in characteristic p, an element whose p-power is zero maps to zero. |

`surjective_almostSurjective_plus` quantifies every chosen root of a pseudouniformizer;
`stronglyZariskiClosed_iff_almostSurjective` retains the integral-closure condition as well.
`zariskiClosedSubspace.baseChange` identifies the actual pullback with the universal
subspace for the extended ideal, over the new base.

`completedIntegralQuotient` has the actual carrier
`AdicCompletion (ϖ) (R⁺/(I ∩ R⁺))`; its structure records the hypotheses needed by
semiperfectoid perfectoidization. `completedIntegralQuotientMap` is the canonical quotient
followed by completion. `zariskiClosedPair_from_perfectoidization` identifies
`A_perfd[1/ϖ]` with the universal Zariski quotient, fixes the map on `R⁺`, and identifies
its plus ring with the integral closure of the image. Here `ϖ ∈ R⁺` is a
pseudouniformizer as in [BS22] Remark 7.5, p. 56, chosen moreover with `ϖ^p | p` (possible since
`R` is perfectoid).
Checks `completedIntegralQuotient_zero_ideal`, `completedIntegralQuotient_unit_ideal`
and `completedIntegralQuotient_can_have_nilpotents` recover `R⁺` at the zero ideal,
give the zero ring at the unit ideal, and exhibit a nonreduced completed quotient before
perfectoidization.

Lean: `exists_surjective_perfectoidQuotient` (a surjection `R → S` onto a perfectoid Tate ring
killing `I`, initial among continuous maps to perfectoid Tate rings that kill `I`); the Lean
`example` checks that a map killing the unit ideal has zero target, fixing the vanishing convention
of the universal quotient.

### P4.16 comparison with the closed immersions of AdicSpaces

For a morphism `f : Y ⟶ ofPair p R` of perfectoid spaces, the reverse implication
(*strongly-zariski-closed-is-zariski-closed*) goes from `IsStronglyZariskiClosed p R f`
to `IsZariskiClosedImmersion p R f` ([ECD], following Definition 5.7, p. 24).

**Comparison with AdicSpaces' closed immersions.** (*adicspaces-closed-immersion-comparison*)
(a) For `X = Spa(R, R⁺)` affinoid perfectoid, a morphism `f : Z → X` of perfectoid spaces is
strongly Zariski closed if and only if it is isomorphic over `X` to the library's closed immersion
of affinoid adic spaces `Spa(Huber.Pair.quotient (R, R⁺) J) → Spa(R, R⁺)` (Tau Ceti
`Huber.Pair.quotient` with `TauCeti.Huber.Pair.quotient_plus`, the closed embedding
`Pair.Hom.isClosedEmbedding_spaComap_quotientHom` with range `V(J)`,
`range_spaComap_quotientHom`) for a closed ideal `J ⊆ R` with `R/J` perfectoid; then
`J = ker(R → S)`.
(b) For arbitrary `X`, the quotient-defined adic notion is AdicSpacesPartII R0.8's
`AdicSpace.IsClosedImmersion`. P4's `IsAdicClosedImmersion` lives on `Perfd` and agrees
with that condition through `YonedaAdicSpace.ofAdicSpace`, as expressed by
`isAdicClosedImmersion_iff_adicCharts`: on compatible adic representatives `g : A → B`,
every point of `B` has a complete sheafy affinoid chart whose entire inverse image
is affinoid, with an open quotient coordinate homomorphism and the integral closure
of the image plus ring. Equivalently, the map is locally on `X` strongly Zariski closed;
such a morphism is a closed immersion in the sense of [ECD]
Definition 5.6 whose restrictions over the affinoid perfectoid opens contained in a chart of the
cover are Zariski closed. With its quantifiers: a map `f : Z → X` of perfectoid spaces is a closed
immersion in the cover-local sense of R0.8 (some affinoid cover of `X` whose preimages are quotient
charts) if and only if there exists an open cover of `X` by affinoid perfectoid `U_i` with every
`Z ×_X U_i → U_i` strongly Zariski closed; then the same holds over every affinoid perfectoid open
contained in a chart of the given cover. The converse direction uses the open mapping theorem
(AdicSpaces 0.6): the surjection `O(U_i) → O(Z ×_X U_i)` is open, so the preimage of `U_i` is a
quotient chart; the forward direction uses P4.12 and P4.15, the image over an affinoid perfectoid
`W` inside a chart `Spa(A, A⁺)` with ideal `J` being `V(J·O(W))`. This is the only global
identification made here. It is not PerfectoidTowers P8.14's notion of Zariski-closed embedding,
which asks for strong Zariski closedness over every open affinoid perfectoid of `X`; the two global
notions are not identified in this roadmap. (c) AdicSpaces' closed
immersion defined by a closed ideal `J` of a perfectoid `R` need not have perfectoid source: for
`R = C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩` and `J = (T)`, `R/J` is not reduced, whereas the Zariski closed subspace `V(T)` is
`Spa(C, O_C)` ([AWS] Lecture 2, Example 2.4.9). (d) That every Zariski closed immersion into an
affinoid is of the form (a) is [ECD] Theorem 5.8 (P4.15). *Needs:*
*strongly-zariski-closed-immersion*; P4.15; P4.12; AdicSpacesPartII R0.8
`AdicSpace.IsClosedImmersion`; AdicSpaces 0.6 (the open mapping theorem); Tau Ceti `TauCeti.Huber.Pair.quotient`,
`TauCeti.Huber.Pair.quotient_plus`, `TauCeti.Huber.Pair.Hom.isClosedEmbedding_spaComap_quotientHom`,
`TauCeti.Huber.Pair.Hom.range_spaComap_quotientHom`.

Immersions are stable under base change and composition, and closed immersions are quasicompact
(*immersions-base-change-and-composition*): immersions, open immersions and closed immersions are
stable under composition and under base change along arbitrary morphisms, the image of the base
change of `f` being the preimage of `f(|Y|)`; closed immersions are quasicompact ([ECD] §5,
Corollary 5.5 (i), p. 24). A surjective perfectoid quotient is a Zariski closed immersion
(*strongly-zariski-closed-is-zariski-closed*): for `ψ : R → S` a surjective continuous
homomorphism onto a perfectoid Tate ring, `I := ker ψ` and `S⁺` the integral closure of `ψ(R⁺)`,
the ideal `I` is closed, `(S, S⁺) ≅ Huber.Pair.quotient (R, R⁺) I`, and `Spa(S, S⁺) → X` is a
Zariski closed immersion defined by `I`, isomorphic to `Z_I` over `X`; thus every strongly Zariski
closed map is Zariski closed, the direction that needs the plus-ring clause ([ECD] §5, after
Definition 5.7, p. 24; Tau Ceti `TauCeti.Huber.Pair.Hom.isClosedEmbedding_spaComap_quotientHom`).

`stronglyZariskiClosed_quotient_comparison` identifies a strong quotient with
`Huber.Pair.quotient` by its kernel, including the topology, plus ring and the quotient map.
The global geometric equivalence is `stronglyZariskiClosed_iff_zariskiClosed`.
The composition and base-change declarations are `IsImmersion.comp`, `.baseChange`,
`IsOpenImmersion.comp`, `.baseChange`, `IsClosedImmersion.comp`, `.baseChange`;
`IsClosedImmersion.quasiCompact` gives quasicompactness.

`IsAdicClosedImmersion` expresses the adic cover-local condition of (b) on the actual `Perfd`
morphism, with the same quantifier everywhere: there exists an affinoid cover of the target such
that over each chart of that cover the source is an affinoid quotient, with the quotient topology
and the integral closure of the image as plus ring. The equivalence
`isAdicClosedImmersion_iff_locally_strong` identifies this with the existence of an affinoid
perfectoid cover on whose charts the map is strongly Zariski closed (the statement of (b)); there
is no `isAdicClosedImmersion_iff_strong`: for an affinoid target the direct comparison is (a),
whose source is supplied as an affinoid quotient, and no upgrade from a cover-local immersion into
an affinoid target to a quotient presentation over the whole target is asserted or used (see the
note after the chart condition below).
`IsAdicClosedImmersion.isClosedImmersion` compares the cover-local quotient condition with
P4's topological closed immersion. Checks `adicClosed_identity`, `adicClosed_empty`,
`adicClosed_principal` and `adicClosed_annulus_negative` give the identity, empty source,
a principal perfectoid quotient, and the annulus boundary that fails the quotient
condition. `isAdicClosedImmersion_iff_adicCharts` uses the complete sheafy charts
`AdicSpacesPartII.AdicSpace.Chart` and `AdicSpace.Affinoid.map` to express R0's quotient-chart
condition on adic representatives, again as the existence of a cover by quotient charts; all
representative isomorphisms commute with the morphism being tested.

**No local-to-global upgrade is asserted.** No implication from the cover-local predicate to a global
quotient presentation over an arbitrary affinoid target is used in this roadmap. If a global closed
ideal `J ⊆ R` with image `V(J)` is supplied, P4.15 identifies the immersion with the universal
perfectoid quotient, whose kernel is `J^perf` (equal to `J` only when `J` is already perfectoid-saturated,
as the root-disc example `R/(T)` shows). PerfectoidTowers P8.14 retains its separate every-affinoid
condition (Hansen–Johansson, Definition 5.4 and the caution following it). Any further upgrade of a
cover-local immersion into an affinoid target to a global quotient would need an independent
descent theorem for arbitrary closed ideals — the restricted kernels must be identified with the
extended ideals after closure and perfectoid saturation, the locally given ideals must descend (the
obstruction lives in `H^1(X, J)`, not in the acyclicity of `O` or `O⁺`), and `J = J^perf` must be
shown — and such kernels need not be finitely generated (`ker(K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ → K)` is a nonzero
idempotent ideal of a domain), so AdicSpacesPartIII R3.5's finite-projective glueing does not
apply; this is not deduced here from acyclicity, is not a target, and is not used to satisfy any
downstream contract. [ECD] Definitions 5.6–5.7 and Theorem 5.8, pp. 24–25,
distinguish this condition from P4's broader `IsClosedImmersion`, as does the remark
after [Berkeley] Definition 17.4.2, p. 155. The affine construction uses the pinned
quotient-pair suppliers above.

### P4.17 closed immersions versus Zariski closed immersions

**Closed immersions and Zariski closed immersions are different notions.**
(*closed-immersion-vs-zariski-closed*) (a) Every strongly Zariski closed map is Zariski closed, and
every Zariski closed immersion is a closed immersion (*strongly-zariski-closed-is-zariski-closed*,
*zariski-closed-immersion*). (b) The image of an immersion is stable under generalization, so a
closed subset of `|X|` that is not (the closed point of `Spa(K, K⁺)` for `K⁺` of rank two) is not
the image of any immersion: the Zariski statements do not extend to arbitrary closed subsets. (c) A
closed immersion need not be Zariski closed: for `X = Spa(C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, O_C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩)` with `C` a
perfectoid field and `ϖ ∈ C` a pseudouniformizer with compatible roots, the subset
`T := ⋂_n {|ϖ^{1/pⁿ}| ≤ |T|}` (the closed annulus `{|T| = 1}` together with the rank-two point `y`
with `|T(y)| = 1⁻`) is the complement of the open unit disc, hence closed, and `ι : Z_𝒰 → X` for
`𝒰 = {{|ϖ^{1/pⁿ}| ≤ |T|}}` (P4.4) is a closed immersion with image
`T`; but `T` is not Zariski closed, since every `g ∈ C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩` vanishing on `T` vanishes at the
Gauss point, hence is `0` (the Gauss norm is the spectral norm), while `T ≠ X`. (d) Equivalently, a
closed immersion `Spa(S, S⁺) → Spa(R, R⁺)` of affinoid perfectoid spaces does not force `R → S` to
be surjective ([Berkeley] Lecture 17, remark after Definition 17.4.2, p. 155). *Needs:*
*intersection-of-rational-subsets*; *perfectoid-immersion*; *zariski-closed-immersion*.

**Checks.**

- `not_isZariskiClosed_annulusClosure` (non-example) — the closed immersion `Z_𝒰 → X` of (c):
  `T = {|T| = 1} ∪ {y}` is closed, `S_𝒰 = C⟨T^{±1/p^∞}⟩` (P4.4), `R → S_𝒰` is the
  (non-surjective) inclusion `C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ ⊆ C⟨T^{±1/p^∞}⟩`, and the only `g ∈ R` with
  `|g| = 0` on `T` is `g = 0`, so `V(I) = T` has no solution `I`.
- `not_range_isImmersion_closedPoint` (non-example) — for `K⁺ ⊊ K°` the closed point `K⁺` of
  `Spa(K, K⁺)` is a closed subset that is not stable under generalization (`K°` generalizes it),
  so no immersion has image `{K⁺}`; the closed immersions into `Spa(K, K⁺)` are `∅` and the
  identity.

The Check `zariskiImmersion_annulus_negative` also tests the morphism predicate
`IsZariskiClosedImmersion` itself on this closed boundary inclusion.

### P4.18 the diagonal is an immersion

**The diagonal of a morphism of perfectoid spaces is an immersion.** (*diagonal-of-perfectoid-map*)
Let `f : Y → X` be any morphism of perfectoid spaces. Then `Δ_f : Y → Y ×_X Y` is an immersion
(P4.10). More precisely: (a) `Δ_f` is a split monomorphism, hence an injection;
(b) for open affinoids `V ⊆ Y` and `U ⊆ X` with `f(V) ⊆ U`, the restriction `V → V ×_U V` is strongly
Zariski closed: the multiplication map from the affinoid ring of `V ×_U V` onto `O_Y(V)` is
surjective and `O⁺_Y(V)` is the integral closure of the image of the plus ring; (c) the open subsets
`V ×_U V` cover an open `W ⊆ |Y ×_X Y|` containing `Δ_f(|Y|)`, and `Δ_f(|Y|)` is closed in `W`, with
`|Δ_f|` a homeomorphism onto its image ([ECD] §5, Proposition 5.9, p. 25). *Needs:*
*injection-of-perfectoid-spaces*; *perfectoid-immersion*; *strongly-zariski-closed-immersion*;
P2.16; Mathlib `CategoryTheory.IsSplitMono`.

`diagonalMultiplication` is the map from the actual P2 tensor pair, fixed by its two
identity composites in `diagonalMultiplication_inclusions`.
`diagonalMultiplication_strong` includes both ring surjectivity and the plus-ring clause.
Checks `diagonalMultiplication_zero`, `diagonalMultiplication_identity` and
`diagonalMultiplication_two_terms` compute a zero target, the tensor over the identity,
and the sum of a left and a right scalar.

### P4.19 separated morphisms

Separatedness is the closedness of the diagonal; this subsection defines it and the next gives its
valuative criterion.

**Separated morphisms of perfectoid spaces.** (*separated-perfectoid-map*) With fibre products as
in P2, a morphism `f : Y → X` of perfectoid spaces is separated if its diagonal `Δ_f : Y → Y ×_X Y`
is a closed immersion (P4.10) ([ECD] §5, Definition 5.10, p. 25); it is
quasiseparated if `Δ_f` is quasicompact (P4.2). In Mathlib's
vocabulary, `IsSeparated = MorphismProperty.diagonal IsClosedImmersion` on `Perfd`, the pattern of
`AlgebraicGeometry.IsSeparated`. Since `Δ_f` is always an immersion (P4.18),
`f` is separated if and only if `Δ_f(|Y|)` is closed. This is the notion that DiamondsAndVStacks
layer D3 (*immersions-separatedness-and-truncatedness*) restricts to on perfectoid spaces downstream.
The adic supplier is AdicSpacesPartII R0.10's `AdicSpace.IsSeparated`, and the comparison is made
only for `f` locally of weakly finite type (AdicSpacesPartII R0.6), the fibre product being that of
P2.16. P4's notion lives on `Perfd` and agrees with R0.10 through `YonedaAdicSpace.ofAdicSpace` when the
adic representative is locally of weakly finite type and its source has stably sheafy
charts. More precisely, `isSeparated_iff_adicDiagonal` identifies `IsSeparated p f`
with closedness of the diagonal of any compatible adic representative `g : A → B`
with a self-pullback, using the representative isomorphisms and commutative square
of P4.2. R0 includes the two additional hypotheses in its predicate; P4 imposes
neither on an arbitrary perfectoid morphism ([ECD] Definition 5.10 and Proposition
5.11, pp. 25–26). In `PerfectoidSpace`, define `IsSeparated`;
prove `isSeparated_iff_isClosed_range_diagonal`, `IsSeparated.quasiSeparated`,
`IsSeparated.of_affinoid`, `IsSeparated.of_isInjection`, `IsSeparated.comp`,
`IsSeparated.baseChange`. The identity `isSeparated_eq_diagonal` unfolds the
definition into Mathlib’s diagonal operation ([ECD] Definition 5.10, p. 25). *Needs:* *perfectoid-immersion*;
*quasicompact-and-quasiseparated-maps*; Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.diagonal`,
`CategoryTheory.MorphismProperty.diagonal`, `AlgebraicGeometry.IsSeparated`; P2.16.

Analytic separatedness, a diagonal that is a Zariski-closed embedding, is a different condition,
owned by [PerfectoidTowers P8.15](../PerfectoidTowers/README.md#p815-analytically-separated-perfectoid-spaces);
it and its comparison with this subsection's notion belong to P8.15 and are not used here. That
comparison has two distinct conclusions there. `PerfectoidSpace.IsAnalyticallySeparated.isSeparated`
takes a morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` with both `X` and `Y` in `Perfd p` and concludes
this subsection's `IsSeparated p f`; in particular it applies over a perfectoid
field. `PerfectoidSpace.IsAnalyticallySeparated.closed_diagonal` takes
`f : X.obj ⟶ B`, analytic separation of `f`, and any chosen
`AnalyticSelfProduct p X B f`, and concludes that its diagonal is a closed
immersion. This is the representable closed-diagonal clause for v-sheaf
separatedness over an analytic base, including a nonperfectoid field
([ECD] Definition 10.7(ii)–(iii), p. 51). Its interpretation as separation of
`X^◇ → Spd(K, K⁺)` uses PerfectoidTowers' diamond comparison; the
perfectoid-base conclusion uses [ECD] Definition 5.10, p. 25.

**Checks.**

- `IsSeparated_affinoid` (computation) — every morphism `Spa(S, S⁺) → Spa(R, R⁺)` of affinoid
  perfectoid spaces is separated: its diagonal is strongly Zariski closed (P4.18 (b)), hence a
  Zariski closed immersion ([ECD] §7, after Lemma 7.19, p. 37).
- `IsSeparated.of_isInjection` (degenerate) — injections, in particular identities and open
  immersions, are separated: their diagonal is an isomorphism; so is the map from the empty space
  (`Δ : ∅ → ∅`).
- `isSeparated_sum_iff` (computation) — for `Y = Y₁ ⊔ Y₂` over `X`,
  `Y ×_X Y = ⊔_{i,j} Y_i ×_X Y_j` and `Δ_Y(|Y|) = Δ_{Y₁}(|Y₁|) ⊔ Δ_{Y₂}(|Y₂|)` lies in the two
  components `Y_i ×_X Y_i`, so `Y → X` is separated if and only if both `Y_i → X` are; two
  copies of `Spa(C, O_C)` over `Spa(C, O_C)` are separated although `Y → X` is not an injection.
- `not_isSeparated_gluedDisc` (non-example) — glue two copies of the perfectoid closed disc over a
  perfectoid field `C` along the rational subset `{|ϖ| ≤ |T|}`; the result `Y` is quasiseparated
  over `Spa(C, O_C)` but not separated: for the rank-two point `y` of the disc with
  `|T(y)| = |ϖ|⁻` (in the closure of the overlap, not in it), the point `Δ_D(y)` of the chart
  `D₁ ×_C D₂ = D ×_C D` lies in the closure of `Δ_Y(|Y|)` but not in `Δ_Y(|Y|)`.

Checks `IsSeparated_identity`, `IsSeparated_empty` and `IsSeparated_affinoid` test the
three basic cases. `sumSpaceEquiv` identifies the topological coproduct through its two
inclusions; `sumPullbackEquiv` orders the four pullback components as
`(1,1), (1,2), (2,1), (2,2)`. `sum_diagonal_four_components` places the diagonal in exactly
`(1,1)` and `(2,2)`, with the separate diagonals inside those components.
`sum_empty_left` computes the coproduct with the empty space;
`sum_disjoint_components` gives disjoint images of the two inclusions;
`sum_two_fields` gives a separated map which is not an injection.
The theorem `isSeparated_sum_iff` applies to arbitrary two maps over the same base.

`sumPullbackEquiv_coordinates` fixes both projections on each of the four components,
so the order is part of the comparison. `glueSelf X U` is the categorical pushout of
the two inclusions of the open subspace `U` in `X`; `glueSelf.fold` is induced by the
two identity maps. `glueSelf.openCharts` and `glueSelf.overlap` specify the two open
charts, their cover, and their intersection. Checks `glueSelf_whole`, `glueSelf_empty`
and `glueSelf_two_copies` compute gluing along the whole space, along the empty
space, and the two distinct copies of a point outside the overlap.
`discAnnulusOpen` is the rational overlap above, with Checks `discAnnulusOpen_gauss`,
`discAnnulusOpen_not_closed` and `discAnnulusOpen_compact`. The Check
`not_isSeparated_gluedDisc` applies quasiseparatedness and failure of separatedness to
the actual glued space and its structure map to the base field.

### P4.20 the valuative criterion for separatedness

Separatedness is detected on rank-one points of affinoid perfectoid fields.

**Valuative criterion for separatedness of perfectoid spaces.**
(*valuative-criterion-separatedness*) Let `f : Y → X` be a morphism of perfectoid spaces. The
following are equivalent: (i) `f` is separated; (ii) `|Δ_f| : |Y| → |Y ×_X Y|` is a closed
immersion of topological spaces; (iii) `f` is quasiseparated and for every affinoid perfectoid
field `(K, K⁺)` and every commutative square formed by `a : Spa(K, O_K) → Y` and
`b : Spa(K, K⁺) → X` with `f ∘ a = b ∘ j` (`j : Spa(K, O_K) → Spa(K, K⁺)` the inclusion of the
rank-one point) there is at most one `c : Spa(K, K⁺) → Y` with `c ∘ j = a` and `f ∘ c = b`
([ECD] §5, Proposition 5.11 (i)–(iii), p. 25). *Needs:* *separated-perfectoid-map*;
*diagonal-of-perfectoid-map*; *immersions-base-change-and-composition*.

Maps from `Spa(R, R⁺)` into a separated space are determined on `Spa(R, R°)`
(*separated-unique-extension-from-rank-one-locus*): for `f : Y → X` separated, `(R, R⁺)` any
perfectoid Tate ring with a ring of integral elements, and `a, b : Spa(R, R⁺) → Y` with
`f ∘ a = f ∘ b` and `a ∘ j = b ∘ j` for `j : Spa(R, R°) → Spa(R, R⁺)`, one has `a = b`; for
`(R, R⁺) = (K, K⁺)` this is the uniqueness in (iii) ([ECD] §10, Proposition 10.10, p. 52).

The declarations `valuativeCriterion_separated` and `separated_unique_extension` use the
actual rank-one inclusion and the identity-ring map from the smaller to the maximal plus
ring. The first retains quasiseparatedness; the second quantifies arbitrary perfectoid
Tate pairs. `valuativeCriterion_adicDiagonal` transports the first equivalence to
closedness of the actual diagonal of a compatible adic representative `g : A → B`
with a self-pullback; its right side is P4 quasiseparatedness and uniqueness for all
`AffinoidField p` tests. AdicSpacesPartII R0.10's `AdicSpace.IsSeparated.iff_valuativeCriterion`
is the corresponding uniqueness-of-centres criterion on adic spaces (Huber 1.3.7):
it assumes analytic source and target, stably sheafy source charts, local weak finite
type, and a quasicompact diagonal. On perfectoid representatives under those hypotheses,
`isSeparated_iff_adicDiagonal` and `valuativeCriterion_adicDiagonal` identify the two
criteria with the same closed diagonal (Huber 1996, Proposition 1.3.7, pp. 52–53).
The P4 field criterion itself retains the
generality of [ECD] Proposition 5.11, pp. 25–26.

### P4.21 tilting

**Tilting of injections, immersions, separatedness and strongly Zariski closed immersions.**
(*zariski-closed-tilting*) Let `X` be a perfectoid space with tilt `X♭` and `f : Y → X` a morphism
with tilt `f♭ : Y♭ → X♭` (P2.11; `|Y| = |Y♭|`, `|X| = |X♭|`). (a) `f` is an injection, an
immersion, an open or closed immersion, quasiseparated or separated if and only if `f♭` is. (b) For
`X = Spa(R, R⁺)` and `Z = Spa(S, S⁺)` affinoid: `f : Z → X` is strongly Zariski closed if and only
if `f♭` is ([Torsion] §II.2, Lemma II.2.7, p. 15). (c) Formulas for a strongly Zariski closed `f`
with `I := ker(R → S)`, choose `ϖ♭` with sharp `ϖ`, compatible roots,
and `ϖ^p | p` in `R⁺` (and use their images in `S`): `I♭ := ker(R♭ → S♭)` is a closed perfect ideal and `I` is the closure of the
ideal generated by `♯(I♭)`; `S♭⁺ = lim_{x↦x^p} S⁺` and `S♭⁺/ϖ♭ ≅ S⁺/ϖ` compatibly with
`R♭⁺/ϖ♭ ≅ R⁺/ϖ`; `S⁺ = {s ∈ S : |s(z)| ≤ 1 for z ∈ |Z|}`; and `|Z| = V(I) = V(I♭)` inside
`|X| = |X♭|`. *Needs:* *injection-of-perfectoid-spaces*; *perfectoid-immersion*;
*separated-perfectoid-map*; *strongly-zariski-closed-immersion*; P2.11.

Surjectivity and closed ideals with perfectoid quotient are detected on tilts
(*surjections-and-closed-ideals-under-tilting*): for a continuous homomorphism `f : A → B` of complete Hausdorff Tate
rings with `A` perfectoid, if `B` is uniform and `f` surjective then `B` is perfectoid; if `B` is
perfectoid then `f` is surjective iff `f♭` is; and `I ↦ I♭ := ker(A♭ → (A/I)♭)` is a bijection
between closed ideals with `A/I` perfectoid and closed perfect ideals of `A♭`, with inverse `J ↦`
the closure of the ideal generated by `♯(J)` ([AWS] Lecture 2, Theorem 2.4.4 and Corollaries 2.4.5–2.4.6, p. 58). Strong Zariski
closedness is characterised by almost surjectivity on plus rings
(*strongly-zariski-closed-criterion*): for `f : Spa(S, S⁺) → Spa(R, R⁺)` a morphism of affinoid
perfectoid spaces and `T⁺` the integral closure of the image of `R⁺` in `S`, `f` is strongly Zariski
closed iff `R⁺ → S⁺` (equivalently `R⁺/ϖ → S⁺/ϖ`) is almost surjective and `S⁺ = T⁺` (almost
surjectivity of `R⁺ → S⁺` already forces `R → S` surjective, `S = S⁺[1/ϖ]`, and the converse
is *surjective-perfectoid-map-almost-surjective-on-plus-rings*). Almost surjectivity without the
clause `S⁺ = T⁺` is strictly weaker: `Spa(R, R°) → Spa(R, R⁺)` with `R⁺ ⊊ R°` has `R → R` the
identity and `R⁺ → R°` almost surjective but `R° ≠ T⁺ = R⁺`, and it is not a closed immersion
(P4.13). If, however, `|Spa(S, S⁺)|` is in addition closed in `|X|`, the clause is automatic:
`Spa(S, S⁺) ⊆ Spa(S, T⁺) = V(I)` is closed, contains every rank-one point (`S⁺ ⊆ S°`), and the
rank-one points are dense in `Spa(S, T⁺)`, so `Spa(S, S⁺) = Spa(S, T⁺)` and
`S⁺ = {s : |s| ≤ 1 on Spa(S, S⁺)} = T⁺`. This is why [ECD] (after Definition 5.7) records, via
[KL15] Proposition 3.6.9 (c), that its definition agrees with [Torsion] Definition II.2.6, where
almost surjectivity is asked for a closed subset of `|X|` presented as `Spa(S, S⁺)`
([Torsion] §II.2, Definition II.2.6, p. 15; [ECD] §5, after Definition 5.7, p. 24).

The ideal correspondence is `tiltIdealEquiv`. `PerfectoidQuotientIdeal` consists of
closed ideals presented as kernels of continuous surjections onto perfectoid pairs;
the Tate open-mapping theorem gives the quotient topology. `ClosedPerfectTiltIdeal`
consists of closed ideals stable under taking pth roots in the perfect tilt.
`tiltIdealEquiv_kernel` fixes the forward map on a quotient presentation, and
`tiltIdealEquiv_symm` fixes the inverse as the closed ideal generated by sharp images.
`surjective_iff_tilt` and `stronglyZariskiClosed_tilt_iff` give the map predicates.
The complete uniform-target assertion is P2's `isPerfectoid_of_denseRange` (P2.14),
applied to a surjection. The integral quotient isomorphism is P1's
`Perfectoid.tilt.sharpQuotEquiv`, with its `_apply` characteristic equation;
its `sharp_quotient_two_terms` Check supplies both addition and multiplication conventions.

Checks `perfectoidIdeal_zero`, `perfectoidIdeal_unit`, `perfectoidIdeal_reduced_quotient`
test the zero and unit ideals and exclude a nonreduced quotient.
`tiltIdeal_zero`, `tiltIdeal_unit`, `tiltIdeal_characteristic_p` compute the correspondence
at the endpoints and under the characteristic-p untilt identification.
`tilt_surjection_identity`, `tilt_kernel_zero_target`, `tilt_kernel_two_roots` compute the
identity kernel, the whole kernel for a zero target, and the sharp-generated ideal's
closure under a two-term sum, together with sharp's multiplication equation.

### Examples

The worked examples of this layer are the checks above: `Spa(K, K°)` as a single point and the
two-point space `Spa(K, K⁺)` for `K⁺` of rank two; the open unit disc, quasiseparated but not
quasicompact over the perfectoid closed disc; the quadratic extension `Spa(L, O_L) → Spa(K, O_K)`,
bijective on points but not an injection; the closure of the annulus `{|T| = 1}` as a filtered
intersection of rational subsets and as the image of a closed immersion that is not Zariski
closed; the Gauss point `η` with `K(η)⁺ = K(η)°` and `i_η` an injection that is not an immersion;
the origin `Spa(C, O_C) → Spa(C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, O_C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩)` as a closed, Zariski closed and
strongly Zariski closed immersion with kernel the closure of `(T^{1/pⁿ})` and not `(T)`;
`V((T − 1)) ≅ ℤ_p` with `S_I = C⁰(ℤ_p, ℂ_p)`; `Spa(R, R°) → Spa(R, R⁺)` as almost surjective on
plus rings but not strongly Zariski closed; and the glued disc, quasiseparated but not separated.

The Lean `example` of `Suggested.lean` for this layer checks that a map killing the unit ideal has
zero target, fixing the vanishing convention of the universal perfectoid quotient (P4.15).

`AdicSpace.QuasiCompact`, `.IsClosedImmersion`, `.IsSeparated` and
`.IsSeparated.iff_valuativeCriterion`; AdicEtaleGeometry A1.16's
`YonedaAdicSpace.ofAdicSpace` and `.ofAdicSpace_space` (*adic-spaces-in-yoneda-adic-spaces*);

`CategoryTheory.Mono`, `CategoryTheory.IsSplitMono`, `CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.diagonal`,
