## Layer P5: cofiltered limits and finite-stage étale descent

The layer builds the completed direct limit `(R, R⁺)` of a cofiltered system of perfectoid Tate
pairs — the `ϖ`-adic completion of the colimit of the plus rings, with `R = R⁺[1/ϖ]` — proves that
it is again a perfectoid Tate pair, and shows that `Spa(R, R⁺)` is the limit of the affinoid
perfectoid spaces `Spa(R_i, R_i⁺)` in the category of perfectoid spaces, with underlying space the
inverse limit of the `|X_i|` and with every rational subset, quasicompact open and finite cover by quasicompact opens
coming from a finite stage. It then shows that no completion is needed when the index category is
`ω₁`-cofiltered, that every affinoid perfectoid space is an `ω₁`-cofiltered limit of topologically
countably generated ones, and that cofiltered limits respect cutoff cardinals. Finally it constructs
the filtered 2-colimit of a pseudofunctor of categories and proves finite-stage descent: finite
étale, quasicompact quasiseparated étale, and quasicompact separated étale objects over the limit
form the 2-colimit of those over the stages, with surjectivity, isomorphism and separatedness
recognised at a finite stage. No perfectoid base field is assumed anywhere.

### P5.1 the completed direct limit of a cofiltered system of perfectoid Tate pairs

The ring construction in P5.1–P5.3 depends on P1 and P2. The uses of P4 below concern
examples and the étale descent arguments in P5.10–P5.12.
Standing setting of the whole layer: `p` is a fixed prime; `I` is a small cofiltered category;
`X_i = Spa(R_i, R_i⁺)`, `i ∈ I`, is a cofiltered diagram of affinoid perfectoid spaces, given at ring
level by a functor `Iᵒᵖ → CAff` into complete Huber pairs (AdicEtaleGeometry A1.16),
`i ↦ (R_i, R_i⁺)`, with each `R_i` a perfectoid Tate ring in the sense of [ECD] Def. 3.1 (P1.1;
characteristic `0`, `p` or mixed, no perfectoid base field) and `R_i⁺ ⊆ R_i°` open and integrally
closed; for a morphism `a : j → i` of `I` the transition map `φ_a : R_i → R_j` is continuous with
`φ_a(R_i⁺) ⊆ R_j⁺` (Tau Ceti `Huber.Pair.Hom`). No injectivity, flatness or density of the
transition maps is assumed.

Prove first that every perfectoid Tate pair
has a pseudouniformiser in its plus ring with compatible roots and `ϖ^p | p` in that plus ring.
Using preservation of units, topological nilpotence and divisibility under morphisms of pairs,
the system has a compatible pseudouniformiser on a tail
(*compatible-pseudouniformizer*): for every object `i₀` of `I` there is `ϖ ∈ R_{i₀}⁺` such that
(a) `ϖ` is a pseudouniformiser of `R_{i₀}` (a topologically nilpotent unit, Tau Ceti
`Huber.IsPseudoUniformizer`), `ϖ^p` divides `p` in `R_{i₀}⁺`, and `ϖ` has a compatible system of
`p`-power roots `ϖ^{1/p^n} ∈ R_{i₀}⁺`, `(ϖ^{1/p^{n+1}})^p = ϖ^{1/p^n}`; (b) for every morphism
`a : j → i₀` of `I`, `φ_a(ϖ)` is a pseudouniformiser of `R_j`, `φ_a(ϖ)^p` divides `p` in `R_j⁺`,
and the `φ_a(ϖ^{1/p^n})` are compatible `p`-power roots of `φ_a(ϖ)` in `R_j⁺`. Such a pair
`(i₀, ϖ)` is a compatible pseudouniformiser of the system, with compatibility understood on that tail. The comma category `I/i₀` (Mathlib
`CategoryTheory.Over i₀`) is initial in `I`, so every limit over `I` may be computed on the tail
`I/i₀`; for parallel `a, b : j ⇉ i₀` the elements `φ_a(ϖ)`, `φ_b(ϖ)` need not agree in `R_j` but
have the same image in `colim_i R_i⁺`, the only place where compatibility is used ([ECD] §6,
Prop. 6.4, statement, p. 27; [ECD] §3, Lem. 3.10, p. 16; [ECD] §3, Ex. 3.22(ii), p. 19). For
`R_{i₀} = ℂ_p⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩` the element `ϖ = p^{1/p}` with roots `p^{1/p^{n+1}}` works and its image
under `T^{1/p^m} ↦ p^{1/p^{m+1}}T^{1/p^m}` is again such a pseudouniformiser; in characteristic `p`
the condition `ϖ^p | p = 0` is empty and `ϖ = t` with roots `t^{1/p^n}` works in `𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^`
([ECD] §3, Prop. 3.5). *Needs:* P1.1, P1.3; Tau Ceti
`TauCeti.Huber.IsRingOfIntegralElements.mem_of_isTopologicallyNilpotent`; Mathlib
`CategoryTheory.IsCofiltered`, `CategoryTheory.Over.initial_forget`.

**The completed direct limit `(R, R⁺)` of a filtered system of perfectoid Tate pairs.**
(*completed-colimit-of-perfectoid-pairs*) In the standing setting fix a compatible pseudouniformiser
`(i₀, ϖ)`. Put `A := colim_{i ∈ Iᵒᵖ} R_i⁺`, the filtered colimit of rings (Mathlib
`CommRingCat.FilteredColimits.colimit`), and write `ϖ` for its image in `A`. Define
`R⁺ := Â = lim_n A/ϖ^nA`, the `ϖ`-adic completion of `A`, and `R := R⁺[1/ϖ]`, topologised so that
`R⁺` is an open subring with its `ϖ`-adic topology; thus `(R⁺, ϖR⁺)` is a pair of definition and `R`
is a complete Tate ring with pseudouniformiser `ϖ`. For `i` in the tail `I/i₀` the canonical map
`ι_i : R_i = R_i⁺[1/ϖ] → R` is continuous with `ι_i(R_i⁺) ⊆ R⁺` and `ι_j ∘ φ_a = ι_i`; `(R, R⁺)` with
the `ι_i` is the completed direct limit of the system. The completion is the `ϖ`-adic completion of
the uncompleted colimit of the plus rings, never a completion of `colim R_i` for another topology;
`A` need not be `ϖ`-adically separated, so the `ι_i` need not be injective; `R⁺` is integrally
closed in `R` and `(R, R⁺)` is a perfectoid Tate pair (P5.2); the
construction is independent of `(i₀, ϖ)` and of the tail (see *limit-independence-of-tail-and-choice*).
Universal property: for every complete Tate pair `(S, S⁺)` with `S⁺` bounded in `S` (for instance
`S` uniform; the plus ring is then `ϖ`-adically complete — the property is not claimed for arbitrary
complete Huber pairs) and every compatible family of morphisms of pairs
`ψ_i : (R_i, R_i⁺) → (S, S⁺)`, `i ∈ I/i₀`, there is a unique morphism of pairs
`ψ : (R, R⁺) → (S, S⁺)` with `ψ ∘ ι_i = ψ_i`. In `Perfectoid`, define `completedColimit` (the
topological ring `R = R⁺[1/ϖ]` of a functor `D : Iᵒᵖ ⥤ CAff` with perfectoid Tate values and a
compatible pseudouniformiser), `completedColimitPlus` (`R⁺`, the Mathlib `AdicCompletion` of the
`CommRingCat` filtered colimit, as an open subring of `R`), `completedColimitPair` (`(R, R⁺)` as a
Tau Ceti `Huber.Pair`, using that `R⁺` is open, integrally closed and power-bounded) and
`completedColimit.ι` (the morphism of Huber pairs `ι_i` for `i` in the tail); prove
`completedColimit.hasBasis_nhds_zero` (powers of `ϖ` times `R⁺` form a neighbourhood
basis). `completedColimit.instIsTateRing` exposes the Tate field supplied by
`completedFilteredColimit.isTateRing`; completeness and Hausdorffness are P1 instances. Prove `completedColimit.ι_comp` (`ι_j ∘ φ_a = ι_i` for every
`a : j → i` of the tail), `completedColimit.lift` (the induced morphism `(R, R⁺) → (S, S⁺)` for
`S⁺` bounded), `completedColimit.lift_comp_ι` (`lift ψ ∘ ι_i = ψ_i`), `completedColimit.hom_ext`
(two morphisms into a complete Hausdorff pair agreeing after every `ι_i` are equal),
`completedColimit.plusQuotientEquiv` (`R⁺/ϖ^nR⁺ ≅ colim_i R_i⁺/ϖ^nR_i⁺` for `n ≥ 1`, compatibly
with the `ι_i`), `completedColimit.denseRange_ι` (`⋃ ι_i(R_i⁺)` is dense in `R⁺` and `⋃ ι_i(R_i)`
in `R`), and
`completedColimit.equivOfInitial` (restricting along an initial functor `I' → I` with `I'` small cofiltered, or changing
`(i₀, ϖ)`, gives a canonically isomorphic pair) and
`completedColimit.colimitEquiv_of_isCardinalFiltered` (if `Iᵒᵖ` is `ℵ₁`-filtered then
`colim R_i⁺ ≅ R⁺` and `colim R_i ≅ R`, P5.5) ([ECD] §6, Prop. 6.4, statement, p. 27; [Sch12] §6,
proof of Lem. 6.13(i), p. 37 (characteristic-`p` field case); [KL15] §2.6, Def. 2.6.1, p. 53; [Bhatt] §6.2, Rem. 6.2.9, printed
p. 48). *Needs:* *compatible-pseudouniformizer*; P1.1; AdicEtaleGeometry A1.16 (`CAff`); Mathlib
`CommRingCat.FilteredColimits.colimitCoconeIsColimit`, `AdicCompletion`,
`AdicCompletion.isAdicComplete`; Tau Ceti `TauCeti.Huber.Pair`, `TauCeti.Huber.Pair.Hom`,
`TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing`, `TauCeti.Huber.PairOfDefinition`,
`TauCeti.Huber.IsPseudoUniformizer.hasBasis_nhds_zero`.

**Checks.**

- `completedColimit_test_initial` (degenerate) — if `I` has an initial object `i_*` (so the diagram
  of rings has a terminal index), `ι_{i_*} : (R_{i_*}, R_{i_*}⁺) → (R, R⁺)` is an isomorphism of
  Huber pairs.
- `completedColimit_test_const` (degenerate) — for the constant system `R_i = R₀`, `R_i⁺ = R₀⁺`
  with identity transition maps (`Iᵒᵖ` filtered, hence connected), `colim R_i⁺ = R₀⁺` is already
  `ϖ`-adically complete and every `ι_i` is the identity of `(R₀, R₀⁺)`.
- `completedColimit_test_profinite` (computation) — for `S = lim_n {0,1}^n` and `R_n = K^{S_n}`,
  `R_n⁺ = O_K^{S_n}` over a perfectoid field `K`: `R⁺ = C^0(S, O_K)` and `R = C^0(S, K)`; the function
  `s ↦ Σ_k s_k ϖ^k` lies in `R⁺` but in no `ι_n(R_n⁺)`.
  The Check evaluates the first-coordinate idempotent at the all-zero and all-one
  sequences as `0` and `1`; it is neither zero nor one. `binaryFunctionEquiv`
  and `binaryFunctionEquiv_ι` give the general comparison; the non-cylinder
  continuous functions are tested by `completedColimit_test_uncompleted`
  ([ECD] Proposition 6.5, p. 29).
- `completedColimit_test_plusQuotient` (characterisation) — in the profinite example
  `R⁺/ϖ^n = C^0(S, O_K/ϖ^n)` equals the ring of locally constant functions `S → O_K/ϖ^n`, which is
  `colim_n (O_K/ϖ^n)^{S_n}`.
- `completedColimit_test_uncompleted` (non-example) — in the profinite example the uncompleted
  colimit `colim R_n = LC(S, K)`, with the `ϖ`-adic topology on `LC(S, O_K)`, is not complete, so it
  is not the ring of functions of the limit.
- `completedColimit_test_compatibility_sch12` (compatibility) — for a system of perfectoid affinoid
  `K`-algebras over a characteristic-`p` perfectoid field `K`, with each `R_i⁺` a
  `K°`-algebra, `(R, R⁺)` uses the completion construction of [Sch12] Lem. 6.13. For a system with a common choice of `ϖ`, `R_i⁺` as norm unit balls and
  submetric transition maps, the infimum seminorm induces the same `ϖ`-adic topology.
  [KL15] Def. 2.6.1 uses this seminorm construction for affinoid systems over `ℤ((z))`; it
  does not itself state the comparison for arbitrary norms on perfectoid algebras.
- `completedColimit_test_not_injective` (non-example) — for `R_n = K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩` (all `n`) with
  `R_n⁺ = R_n°` and transition maps `T^{1/p^m} ↦ ϖ^{1/p^m}T^{1/p^m}`, the nonzero element
  `T ∈ R_0⁺` is divisible by every `ϖ^n` in `colim R_n⁺`, so `ι_0(T) = 0` in `R⁺ = O_K`:
  the `ι_i` need not be injective. The completed pair is `(K, K°)`, represented by
  `(AffinoidField.ofRankOne p K).toPairCat p`, since the closure of the integral images is
  `K°`, independently of the specified `K⁺` ([ECD] Proposition 6.4, p. 27).
- `completedColimit_proper_plus` (non-example) — if `K⁺ ⊊ K°`, this completed disc pair is
  not isomorphic to `(K, K⁺)`: every topological field automorphism preserves `K°`, whereas
  a pair isomorphism must carry the plus ring onto the plus ring. This includes the
  two-point case of `AffinoidField.card_spa_eq_two`, with residue field `𝔽_p(t)^perf` and
  `K⁺` the inverse image of its `t`-adic valuation ring `𝔽_p[t]^perf_(t)`.

The completion step rests on a ring lemma (*completion-preserves-integral-closedness*): let `A` be a
commutative ring and `ϖ ∈ A` a nonzerodivisor such that `A` is integrally closed in `A[1/ϖ]` (Mathlib
`IsIntegrallyClosedIn A (Localization.Away ϖ)`), and `Â := lim_n A/ϖ^nA` its `ϖ`-adic completion
(Mathlib `AdicCompletion (Ideal.span {ϖ}) A`); no noetherian or separatedness hypothesis on `A`,
since filtered colimits of separated rings need not be separated. Use Mathlib `AdicCompletion.isAdicComplete` for completeness and separatedness and
`AdicCompletion.pow_smul_top_eq_ker_eval` with `AdicCompletion.evalₐ` for the quotient
comparison `A/ϖ^nA ≅ Â/ϖ^nÂ`, `n ≥ 1` ([Stacks] Tag 05GG, Lem. 10.96.3). Prove
(a) `ϖ` is a nonzerodivisor on `Â`; (b) the kernel of `A → Â` is `J := ⋂_n ϖ^nA`, which
satisfies `J = ϖJ`, and `A/J` is again `ϖ`-torsion free and integrally closed in `(A/J)[1/ϖ]`;
(c) `Â` is integrally closed in `Â[1/ϖ]` (unlike Tau Ceti’s topological closure theorem, this identifies the algebraic `AdicCompletion`
and its localization without a given ambient topology) ([Bhatt] §5.1, Lem. 5.1.2, printed p. 34); (d) if `A` is
`p`-root closed in `A[1/ϖ]` (`g ∈ A[1/ϖ]` and `g^p ∈ A` imply `g ∈ A`), so is `Â` in `Â[1/ϖ]`
([Bhatt] §5.1, Lem. 5.1.1 and its proof, printed p. 33); (e) for the topology on `Â[1/ϖ]` in which
`Â` is open with its `ϖ`-adic topology, the image of `A[1/ϖ]` is dense. For
`A = ℤ_p[p^{1/p^∞}]` and `ϖ = p`, `Â` is the valuation ring of the completion of `ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞})`;
the hypothesis of (c) is needed, since for `p` odd `A = ℤ_p[pζ_p] ⊆ ℚ_p(ζ_p)` is `p`-adically
complete (a finite `ℤ_p`-module) and `ζ_p ∈ A[1/p]` is integral over `A` but not in `A`
(`|ζ_p − a| ≥ p^{−1/(p−1)} > |p|` for every `a ∈ ℤ_p`); for `p = 2` one has `ζ_2 = −1 ∈ ℤ_2`, and
`A = ℤ_2[2i] ⊆ ℚ_2(i)` with `i ∉ A` (`|i − a| ≥ |2|^{1/2} > |2|`) is the example instead. *Needs:*
Mathlib `AdicCompletion`,
`AdicCompletion.isAdicComplete`, `IsAdicComplete`, `IsIntegrallyClosedIn`.

**Checks for the algebraic completion and indexing conventions.**

- `completion_unit` — for `A = ℤ`, `ϖ = 1`, the completion is the zero ring; regularity
  does not imply that the completion is nonzero.
- `completion_zero` — for `A = ℤ`, `ϖ = 0`, the canonical map to the completion is
  bijective. The regular-element hypothesis fails, so this is a Check of the completion
  construction, not an instance of the regularity theorem.
- `completion_two_terms` — in the `2`-adic completion of `ℤ`, reduction modulo `2`
  sends the images of `1` and `2` to `[1]` and `0`. This pins the exponent convention
  `n = 1`; at `n = 0` the quotient by `(2)^0 = (1)` is zero.
- `cofiltered_two_terms` — for an affinoid perfectoid diagram on `(Fin 2)ᵒᵖ`,
  `cofilteredLimit.π` at `1` is an isomorphism, and its composite with `X₁ → X₀`
  equals the projection at `0`. This computes the actual limit cone
  ([ECD] Prop. 6.5, p. 29).
- `profinite_two_terms` — send the two-digit cylinder function `s₀ + s₁ϖ`
  through `completedColimit.ι` and `binaryFunctionEquiv`. Its values on the
  zero sequence and the sequences supported at `0` and `1` are `0`, `1`, `ϖ`.
  The Check applies to every perfectoid pair and retains these values in
  characteristic `2`.

<a id="p5-2"></a>

### P5.2 the completed direct limit is a perfectoid Tate pair

**The completed direct limit of perfectoid Tate pairs is a perfectoid Tate pair.**
(*completed-colimit-is-perfectoid*) In the situation of *completed-colimit-of-perfectoid-pairs*,
with `(i₀, ϖ)` a compatible pseudouniformiser with `ϖ^p | p` in `R_{i₀}⁺`, prove: (a) `R⁺` is open
and bounded in `R` and integrally closed in `R`, so `R⁺` is a ring of integral elements and
`ϖR° ⊆ R⁺ ⊆ R°`; (b) `R` is uniform; (c) `ϖ^p` divides `p` in `R⁺`, `ϖ` is a nonzerodivisor on
`R⁺`, and Frobenius `R⁺/ϖR⁺ → R⁺/ϖ^pR⁺`, `x ↦ x^p`, is an isomorphism, so `R⁺` is an integral
perfectoid ring ([BMS] Def. 3.5; [BMS] §3, Lem. 3.20, p. 26; [BMS] §3, Lem. 3.10(ii), p. 22);
(d) `R` is a perfectoid Tate ring in the sense of [ECD] Def. 3.1, by (c) and
*perfectoid-tate-ring-from-integral-perfectoid* (P1.20: `R⁺` integral perfectoid with `ϖ` a
nonzerodivisor and `R = R⁺[1/ϖ]`), so `(R, R⁺)` is a perfectoid Tate pair and the `ι_i` are
morphisms of perfectoid Tate pairs; its tilt `R♭` is the completed direct limit of the `R_i♭`
(P1.29 (c), tilting commutes with completed colimits); (e) if all `R_i` have characteristic
`p` then `R` is a perfect complete Tate ring of characteristic `p`, and if the system lives over a
perfectoid Tate ring `B` (compatible maps `B → R_i`) then `R` is a perfectoid `B`-algebra. No
perfectoid base field is assumed. P1.29 supplies the underlying ring
`Perfectoid.completedFilteredColimit`; P5 adds the chosen plus ring through
`Perfectoid.completedColimitPlus` and `Perfectoid.completedColimitPair`.
Prove `completedColimitPlus_isRingOfIntegralElements` on the specified closure subring
of `completedFilteredColimit`: it is open, integrally closed in the ambient ring,
and contained in `powerBoundedSubring`. Prove `completedColimitPlus_isBounded` on
that same subring. Both assume a small filtered diagram of perfectoid pairs and
compatible roots of a pseudouniformizer at the chosen stage; no injectivity of the
transition maps is assumed ([ECD] Proposition 6.5, p. 29). The constructor
`completedColimitPair` uses the first theorem as its integral-elements proof.
`completedColimit.isPerfectoidTateRing` exposes P1’s
`completedFilteredColimit.isPerfectoidTateRing` on the bundled pair.
`Perfectoid.completedColimit.plusCompletionEquiv` identifies that plus ring with the completion
of `colim_i R_i⁺` ([ECD] Proposition 6.5, p. 29). P4.4 gives the pro-rational application;
P7.6 treats Frobenius-controlled towers. A completed colimit of
non-perfectoid rings can be perfectoid — the tower `ℚ_p(p^{1/p^n})` of discretely valued fields
([ECD] Rem. 3.3) has perfectoid completed colimit — but that is a tilde-limit (layer P7), not an
instance of this theorem. For every profinite `S` and perfectoid field `K`, `C^0(S, K)` is a
perfectoid Tate ring with `C^0(S, K)° = C^0(S, O_K)`; over a perfectoid field this is the end of the
proof of [Sch13] §4, Lem. 4.6, p. 25, here proved without a base field ([ECD] §6, proof of Prop. 6.5,
p. 29). *Needs:* *completed-colimit-of-perfectoid-pairs*; *completion-preserves-integral-closedness*;
P1.1; P1.20; P1.29 (for the ring and its tilt); Tau Ceti
`TauCeti.Huber.IsRingOfIntegralElements`,
`TauCeti.Huber.IsRingOfIntegralElements.mem_of_isTopologicallyNilpotent`,
`TauCeti.Huber.powerBoundedSubring`.

<a id="p5-3"></a>

### P5.3 cofiltered limits of affinoid perfectoid spaces

The second group passes to spaces: the limit in perfectoid spaces, its underlying space, and the
`ω₁`-cofiltered case in which no completion is needed.

**Cofiltered limits of affinoid perfectoid spaces.** (*cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces*)
In the standing setting let `(R, R⁺)` be the completed direct limit for a compatible
pseudouniformiser (P5.1), a perfectoid Tate pair
(P5.2), and put `X := Spa(R, R⁺)`, an affinoid perfectoid space (P2.9),
with projections `p_i : X → X_i` induced by `ι_i` (`i` in the tail; for general `i` through any
`j → i`, `i₀`). Then `(X, (p_i))` is a limit of the diagram `(X_i)` in the category of perfectoid
spaces: for every perfectoid space `Y`, `Hom(Y, X) → lim_i Hom(Y, X_i)` is bijective. In particular
`X` is the limit in the full subcategory of affinoid perfectoid spaces, `O_X(X) = R` and
`O⁺_X(X) = R⁺`, and `X` is independent of the choices up to unique isomorphism
(see *limit-independence-of-tail-and-choice*). Morphisms into affinoid perfectoid spaces are described
by the adjunction of AdicEtaleGeometry A1.16 for sheafy pairs, and perfectoid pairs are sheafy
(P2.6). The limit is claimed in perfectoid spaces only: for a non-uniform adic space `Y` a
compatible family `Y → X_i` need not induce a map continuous for the `ϖ`-adic topology of
`colim R_i⁺`; and the `X_i` are affinoid perfectoid — towers of non-perfectoid spaces are
tilde-limits (layer P7). Companion statements: `|X| → lim |X_i|` is a homeomorphism of spectral
spaces (P5.4); rational subsets and their rings are computed at finite stages
(see *limit-restriction-to-rational-subsets*); for `ω₁`-cofiltered `I` no completion is needed (P5.5);
cardinal bounds (P5.7). In `PerfectoidSpace`, define `cofilteredLimit` (for a cofiltered diagram
`X : I ⥤ PerfectoidSpace` of affinoid perfectoid spaces, the affinoid perfectoid space `Spa(R, R⁺)`
of the completed direct limit) and `cofilteredLimit.π` (the projections `p_i`, with `π_comp`:
`X(a) ∘ p_j = p_i` for `a : j → i`); prove `cofilteredLimit.isLimit` (the cone `(cofilteredLimit X, p)`
is a limit cone in perfectoid spaces, with `lift` for a compatible family `Y → X_i`),
`cofilteredLimit.lift_π` (`p_i ∘ lift f = f_i`), `cofilteredLimit.hom_ext` (two morphisms
`Y → cofilteredLimit X` agreeing after every `p_i` are equal), `cofilteredLimit.isAffinoid`
(`cofilteredLimit X` is affinoid perfectoid with `O(X) ≅ Perfectoid.completedColimit` and
`O⁺(X) ≅ Perfectoid.completedColimitPlus`), `cofilteredLimit.homeomorph` (`|cofilteredLimit X| ≃ₜ lim |X_i|`
as spectral spaces, P5.4), `cofilteredLimit.restrictRational` (for a rational `U_i ⊆ X_i` the open
subspace `p_i⁻¹(U_i)` is the cofiltered limit of the preimages `U_j`), `cofilteredLimit.baseChange`
(for a qcqs `Y_i → X_i`, `Y_i ×_{X_i} cofilteredLimit X = lim_j Y_i ×_{X_i} X_j`,
*limit-of-qcqs-base-changes*), `cofilteredLimit.isoOfInitial` (for an initial functor `u : I' ⥤ I` with `I'` small cofiltered,

**Checks.**

- `cofilteredLimit_test_residueField` (characterisation) — for `x ∈ X₀` affinoid perfectoid, the

- `cofilteredLimit_test_notPerfectoidTower` (non-example) — the system

- `cofilteredLimit_test_uncompletedPair` (non-example) — in the profinite example the Huber pair

  `O(X) = C^0(S, K) ≠ LC(S, K)`.
- `cofiltered_empty_index` (non-example) — the empty category is not cofiltered.
  The localization defining `FilteredTwoColimit` of the empty diagram with

Two lemmas support the construction. Independence of the choices
(*limit-independence-of-tail-and-choice*): in the situation of
*completed-colimit-of-perfectoid-pairs*, (a) if `(i₀, ϖ)` and `(i₀', ϖ')` are two compatible
pseudouniformisers, the `ϖ`-adic and `ϖ'`-adic topologies on `A = colim R_i⁺` coincide and the
identity of `A` induces an isomorphism of Huber pairs `(R_ϖ, R_ϖ⁺) ≅ (R_{ϖ'}, R_{ϖ'}⁺)` compatible
with all `ι_i`; (b) for an initial functor `u : I' → I` with `I'` small cofiltered (the inclusion of a tail `I/i₁`, or of a
cofinal subposet) the completed direct limit of the restricted system is canonically isomorphic to
that of the original one, compatibly with the `ι`; (c) these isomorphisms compose (for three choices
the composite of two comparison isomorphisms is the third) and commute with `lift`; (d) consequently
`Spa(R, R⁺)` with its projections to the `X_i` is well defined up to unique isomorphism. In the
profinite example `ϖ`, `ϖ^{1/p}` and `uϖ` (`u ∈ O_K^×`) give the same `C^0(S, O_K)`, and restricting
to `S_n` with `n ≥ 5` gives the same pair; if `I` has a terminal object `t` the tail `I/t` is all of
`I` and (b) is the identity ([ECD] §6, Prop. 6.5, statement, p. 29; [ECD] §3, Rem. 3.2, p. 14).
*Needs:* *completed-colimit-of-perfectoid-pairs*; *completed-colimit-is-perfectoid*; Mathlib
`CategoryTheory.Over.initial_forget`, `CategoryTheory.Functor.Final.colimitIso`.

Uniformity of perfectoid spaces (*integral-sections-are-varpi-complete*): let `Y` be a perfectoid
space (P2.10) and `ϖ ∈ O_Y(Y)` a unit whose restriction to every affinoid perfectoid open `U ⊆ Y` is
a pseudouniformiser of `O_Y(U)` (for instance the pullback of a pseudouniformiser along a morphism
`Y → Spa(R_{i₀}, R_{i₀}⁺)`). Prove that `O_Y⁺(Y)` is `ϖ`-torsion free and `ϖ`-adically complete and
separated, and that the restriction maps `O_Y⁺(Y) → O_Y⁺(U)` to affinoid perfectoid opens are
continuous for the `ϖ`-adic topologies, the `ϖ`-adic topology of `O_Y⁺(U)` being its subspace
topology in `O_Y(U)`; consequently, for every ring `A` with a specified element `t` and every ring map
`f : A → O_Y⁺(Y)` satisfying `f(t) = ϖ`, `f` extends uniquely to the `t`-adic completion `Â`, and the induced maps
`Â[1/t] → O_Y(U)` are continuous. This integral completeness gives the
universal property; for `Y = S × Spa(K, O_K)` with `S` profinite, `O⁺(Y) = C^0(S, O_K)` is
`ϖ`-adically complete although it is a limit over the finite covers of `S`; for a complete Tate
ring `S` with `S⁺` unbounded the `ϖ`-adic topology of `S⁺` is strictly coarser than its subspace
topology (the subspace neighbourhoods `ϖⁿS_0`, `S_0 ⊆ S⁺` a ring of definition, lie in the `ϖⁿS⁺`,
and no `ϖⁿS⁺` lies in `ϖS_0` when `S⁺` is unbounded; for `S = K[ε]/ε²` with `S⁺ = S° = O_K ⊕ Kε`
one has `⋂_n ϖⁿS° = Kε ≠ 0`, so the `ϖ`-adic topology is not even Hausdorff), so a compatible
family into such an `S` need not extend to the completion, which is why the limit is taken in
perfectoid spaces ([ECD] §6, proof of Prop. 6.5, p. 29). *Needs:* P2.10, P2.9, P2.8, P2.6; Mathlib
`IsAdicComplete`, `AdicCompletion`.

### P5.4 the underlying space of the limit

**The underlying space of a cofiltered limit of affinoid perfectoid spaces is the inverse limit.**
(*limit-underlying-space-homeomorphism*) Let `X = lim_i X_i` be the limit of a cofiltered diagram of
affinoid perfectoid spaces `X_i = Spa(R_i, R_i⁺)` (P5.3).
Then the map `|X| → lim_i |X_i|` induced by the projections is a homeomorphism. That `lim_i |X_i|`
(inverse limit in topological spaces) is spectral with spectral projections, for a cofiltered
system of spectral spaces along spectral maps, is AdicSpacesPartII R0.19.5’s
spectral-limit lemma ([ECD] Lemma 2.11, p. 13), applied to
the `|X_i|` and the spectral transition maps
(Tau Ceti `isSpectralMap_spaComap_of_isTateRing`); what is proved here is the homeomorphism, and
that every rational subset `U ⊆ X` equals `p_i⁻¹(U_i)` for some `i` and some rational subset
`U_i ⊆ X_i`. The proof route is completion (Huber) followed by the direct-limit computation. For profinite `S`,
`|S × Spa(K, O_K)| = S × |Spa(K, O_K)|` with `S` in its profinite topology; for `x` in an affinoid
perfectoid `X₀`, `|Spa(K(x), K(x)⁺)| = ⋂_{U ∋ x} U` with the subspace topology, `U` ranging over the
rational neighbourhoods of `x` ([ECD] §6, Prop. 6.4(o), p. 27; [ECD] §6, proof of Prop. 6.4, p. 27;
[Sch12] §6, Lem. 6.13(ii), p. 37). *Needs:* *cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces*;
AdicSpacesPartII R0.19.7 (*spa-of-filtered-colimit-of-tate-pairs*); AdicSpacesPartII R0.19.8 (*quasicompact-opens-in-limits-of-spectral-spaces*);
*completed-colimit-of-perfectoid-pairs*; P1.1, P2.9; AdicSpacesPartII R0.19.5 (the spectral-limit lemma); Tau Ceti `TauCeti.Huber.Pair.Hom.isSpectralMap_spaComap_of_isTateRing`.

The generic Tate-pair spectrum comparison and finite-stage detection of opens are supplied by

open subspaces and rational restrictions.

(*limit-of-qcqs-base-changes*): in the situation of
*cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces* let `g_i : Y_i → X_i` be a morphism of perfectoid
spaces with `Y_i` quasicompact and quasiseparated (for instance a qcqs étale `Y_i`), and put
`Y_j := Y_i ×_{X_i} X_j` (`a : j → i`) and `Y := Y_i ×_{X_i} X`, fibre products of perfectoid spaces
(P2.16; fibre products of affinoid perfectoid spaces are affinoid perfectoid). Prove that

spectral spaces, and that for every affinoid perfectoid open `V_i ⊆ Y_i` the `V_j := V_i ×_{X_i} X_j`
are affinoid perfectoid with `V := V_i ×_{X_i} X = lim V_j`, so `O(V)` is the completed direct limit
of the `O(V_j)`. This gives `|Z| = lim |Z_j|` for `Z_i = Y_i' ×_{X_i} Y_i''` with `Y_i', Y_i''` qcqs
étale, and `Y = S × Y_0`, `|Y| = S × |Y_0|` for a finite étale
`Y_0 → Spa(K, O_K)` in the profinite example ([ECD] §6, proof of Prop. 6.4(ii), pp. 27–28).
*Needs:* *cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces*; *limit-underlying-space-homeomorphism*;

### P5.5 `ω₁`-cofiltered limits need no completion

**`ω₁`-cofiltered limits of affinoid perfectoid spaces need no completion.**
(*omega1-cofiltered-uncompleted-colimit*) In the situation of
*cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces* assume that `I` is `ω₁`-cofiltered: every
functor `J → I` from a category `J` with countably many morphisms extends to a cone `J^◁ → I`
(equivalently Mathlib `CategoryTheory.IsCardinalFiltered Iᵒᵖ ℵ₁`, `ℵ₁` regular by
`Cardinal.isRegular_aleph_one`; [ECD] §6, Prop. 6.5, definition following the statement, p. 29).
The supporting ring theorem `Perfectoid.isAdicComplete_colimit_of_isCardinalFiltered` takes
a small `ℵ₁`-filtered diagram of commutative rings `A_j`, compatible elements `t_j`, and
`(t_j)`-adic completeness of every `A_j`; it asserts `(t)`-adic completeness of `colim A_j`,
where `t` is their common image. Neither injectivity nor a nonzerodivisor hypothesis is needed
for this statement. Apply it on the tail of the perfectoid diagram.
Then `A = colim_i R_i⁺` is `ϖ`-adically separated and complete, so the canonical maps
`colim_i R_i⁺ → R⁺` and `colim_i R_i → R` are ring isomorphisms (bijective). Equivalently, for an
`ℵ₁`-filtered diagram of perfectoid Tate pairs the uncompleted colimit `(colim R_i, colim R_i⁺)`,
with `colim R_i⁺` carrying its `ϖ`-adic topology, is a perfectoid Tate pair and
`O(lim X_i) = colim O(X_i)`. For countable index categories such as `I = ℕᵒᵖ` both properties fail
in general: for the profinite system `colim R_n⁺ = LC(S, O_K) ≠ C^0(S, O_K) = R⁺` (not surjective),
and for `R_n = K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩` with `T^{1/p^m} ↦ ϖ^{1/p^m}T^{1/p^m}` the element `T` lies in
`⋂ ϖ^n colim R_n⁺`, so `colim R_n⁺ → R⁺ = O_K` is not injective. That `O` and `O⁺` commute with
`ω₁`-filtered colimits of affinoid perfectoid pairs ([ECD] §8, end of the proof of Prop. 8.5, p. 42,
and Cor. 8.6) is this theorem applied to `X ↦ O(X)` ([ECD] §6, Prop. 6.5, statement, p. 29; [ECD]
§6, proof of Prop. 6.5, p. 29). *Needs:* *completed-colimit-of-perfectoid-pairs*;
*completed-colimit-is-perfectoid*; *cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces*; Mathlib
`CategoryTheory.IsCardinalFiltered`, `Cardinal.isRegular_aleph_one`, `IsAdicComplete`.

Lean: `isAdicComplete_colimit_of_isCardinalFiltered`.

### P5.6 every affinoid perfectoid space is an `ω₁`-cofiltered limit of countably generated ones

The third group makes the `ω₁`-cofiltered case the general one, bounds cardinalities, and sets up
the 2-colimits of categories used for finite-stage descent.

Every countable subset of a perfectoid Tate ring lies in a closed, topologically countably
generated perfectoid subring (*countable-perfectoid-hull*): let `(R, R⁺)` be a perfectoid Tate pair
([ECD] Def. 3.1) and `ϖ ∈ R⁺` a pseudouniformiser with `ϖ^p | p` in `R⁺` and compatible `p`-power
roots `ϖ^{1/p^n}` (*compatible-pseudouniformizer* for the constant system). Prove that for every
countable subset `C ⊆ R` there is a closed subring `R' ⊆ R` such that
`C ∪ {ϖ, ϖ⁻¹} ∪ {ϖ^{1/p^n}} ⊆ R'`; `R'` has a countable dense subset (equivalently `R'` is the
closure of a countably generated subring, i.e. topologically countably generated); `R'` with the
subspace topology is a perfectoid Tate ring with `R'° = R' ∩ R°`; `R'⁺ := R' ∩ R⁺` is a ring of
integral elements of `R'`, and the inclusion `(R', R'⁺) → (R, R⁺)` is a morphism of perfectoid Tate
pairs; moreover `|R'| ≤ 2^{ℵ₀}` ([ECD] §6, proof of Prop. 6.5, p. 29; [ECD] §4, Rem. 4.3, p. 20). For
`R = C^0(S, K)` with `S = {0,1}^{ℵ₁}`, `K = ℂ_p`, a constant pseudouniformiser with constant chosen roots, and `C` a countable set
of functions depending only on the coordinates in a countable `J ⊆ ℵ₁`, one may take `R' = C^0({0,1}^J, ℂ_p)` pulled back to
`S`; if `R` already has a countable dense subset (for example `ℂ_p⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩`), one may take
`R' = R`. *Needs:* *compatible-pseudouniformizer*; P1.1; layer P1; Tau Ceti
`TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing`, `TauCeti.Huber.IsRingOfIntegralElements`,
`TauCeti.Huber.powerBoundedSubring`; `completion_cardinality_bound` (P6.2); Mathlib `Cardinal.power_le_power_left`.

**Every affinoid perfectoid space is an `ω₁`-cofiltered limit of topologically countably generated
affinoid perfectoid spaces.** (*countably-generated-decomposition*) Let `X = Spa(R, R⁺)` be an
affinoid perfectoid space, with no countability assumption on `R`, and `ϖ` as in
*countable-perfectoid-hull*. Let `𝒮(R)` be the set of closed subrings `R' ⊆ R` containing `ϖ^{±1}`
that are perfectoid Tate rings for the subspace topology and admit a countable dense subset,
ordered by inclusion, and put `R'⁺ := R' ∩ R⁺`. Then: (a) `𝒮(R)` is `ω₁`-directed (every countable
subset of `𝒮(R)` has an upper bound in `𝒮(R)`) and `⋃_{R' ∈ 𝒮(R)} R' = R`;
(b) `colim_{R' ∈ 𝒮(R)} (R', R'⁺) → (R, R⁺)` is an isomorphism of Huber pairs, without completion
(P5.5 for the `ω₁`-directed `𝒮(R)`);
(c) `X = lim_{R' ∈ 𝒮(R)} Spa(R', R'⁺)` in perfectoid spaces and `|X| = lim |Spa(R', R'⁺)|`: `X` is
an `ω₁`-cofiltered limit of affinoid perfectoid spaces with topologically countably generated rings
of functions; (d) every `R' ∈ 𝒮(R)` has cardinality `≤ 2^{ℵ₀}`, hence for every uncountable strong
limit cardinal `κ` (in particular every cutoff cardinal of [ECD] Lem. 4.1) `X` is an `ω₁`-cofiltered
limit of affinoid perfectoid spaces whose rings have cardinality `< κ`. This `ω₁`-presentation is
the form in which the cutoff-independence argument of [ECD] §8, proof of Prop. 8.2, p. 39, is
carried out for singular cutoff cardinals. For `X = Spa(C^0(S, ℂ_p), C^0(S, O_{ℂ_p}))` with
`S = {0,1}^{ℵ₁}` and constant `ϖ` the subrings `C^0({0,1}^J, ℂ_p)`, `J ⊆ ℵ₁` countable, are cofinal in `𝒮(R)`, since
a continuous function on `S` depends on countably many coordinates; if `R` has a countable dense
subset, `R` is the largest element of `𝒮(R)` and the presentation is trivial; if `R` has no
countable dense subset, `X` is not the limit of an `ℕᵒᵖ`-indexed tower of topologically countably
generated affinoid perfectoid spaces (the union of the countable dense subsets of the images would
be a countable dense subset of `R`), so an uncountable `ω₁`-cofiltered index category is necessary
([ECD] §6, Prop. 6.5, statement, p. 29; [ECD] §6, proof of Prop. 6.5, p. 29). *Needs:*
*countable-perfectoid-hull*; *omega1-cofiltered-uncompleted-colimit*;
*cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces*; *limit-underlying-space-homeomorphism*;
Mathlib `Cardinal.IsStrongLimit`, `CategoryTheory.IsCardinalFiltered`,
`Cardinal.isRegular_aleph_one`.

### P5.7 cardinal bounds

**Cardinal bounds for cofiltered limits of affinoid perfectoid spaces.** (*limit-cardinal-bounds*)
Let `κ` be a cutoff cardinal as in [ECD] §4, Lem. 4.1(iii), p. 19, `λ < κ` a
cardinal, `I` a cofiltered category with fewer than `λ` morphisms, and `X_i = Spa(R_i, R_i⁺)`
(`i ∈ I`) a cofiltered diagram of affinoid perfectoid spaces such that `|R_i| < κ'` for all `i`, for
some strong limit cardinal `κ' < κ` (this holds when all `X_i` are `κ'`-small in the sense of [ECD]
Def. 4.2). Let `X = Spa(R, R⁺) = lim X_i`. Then `|colim R_i⁺| < κ`, `|R⁺| < κ`, `|R| < κ`, `|X| < κ`
(by `|X| ≤ 2^{|R|}`, [ECD] §4, proof of Prop. 4.4, p. 20), and `|O_X(U)| < κ` for every open affinoid
`U ⊆ X`. These are the two conditions of [ECD] Def. 4.2, so `X` is `κ`-small; layer P6 defines
`κ`-smallness by exactly these conditions. For `I = ℕᵒᵖ`, `K = ℂ_p`, `S = {0,1}^ℕ`:
`|C^0(S, ℂ_p)| = 2^{ℵ₀} < κ` for every cutoff cardinal `κ`; and `X_∞ = lim_J X_J` over fewer than `κ`
finite subsets `J` with all `X_J` bounded by one strong limit `κ' < κ` is `κ`-small, as in the proof of [ECD] Lem. 7.18
(which DiamondsAndVStacks D1 uses downstream) ([ECD] §6, Prop. 6.4, final statement, p. 27; [ECD] §6, proof of
Prop. 6.4, p. 27). *Needs:* *cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces*;
*completed-colimit-of-perfectoid-pairs*; P2.3, P2.6; `completion_cardinality_bound` (P6.2); Tau Ceti `TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum`; Mathlib `Cardinal.IsStrongLimit`,
`Cardinal.mk_set`, `Cardinal.power_le_power_left`.

### P5.8 the 2-colimit of a filtered diagram of categories

**The 2-colimit of a filtered diagram of categories.** (*filtered-two-colimit-of-categories*) Let
`J` be a small filtered category and `F` a pseudofunctor from `J` (as a locally discrete
bicategory) to categories (Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Pseudofunctor`; base change is only defined up to
canonical isomorphism, hence a pseudofunctor): categories `C_j`, functors `F_a : C_i → C_j` for
`a : i → j`, and coherent natural isomorphisms `F_{ba} ≅ F_b ∘ F_a` and `F_{id} ≅ id`. The filtered
2-colimit `2-colim_j C_j` is the category whose objects are pairs `(i, x)` with `x` an object of
`C_i`, whose morphisms are

`Hom((i, x), (j, y)) := colim_{(k, a: i → k, b: j → k)} Hom_{C_k}(F_a x, F_b y)`

(a filtered colimit of sets over the category of cospans under `i` and `j`), with composition and
identities induced from the `C_k`. It carries functors `ι_i : C_i → 2-colim C_j` and isomorphisms
`ι_j ∘ F_a ≅ ι_i`, and is the pseudo-colimit of `F`: pseudo-cocones (`G_i : C_i → D`,
`G_j ∘ F_a ≅ G_i` coherently) correspond, up to unique isomorphism, to functors
`G : 2-colim C_j → D`, together with specified comparison isomorphisms; uniqueness is
among natural isomorphisms respecting those comparisons. For a pseudo-cocone the induced `G` is faithful iff morphisms in some `C_k`
with equal images in `D` become equal in some further `C_{k'}`; full iff every morphism
`G_i x → G_j y` of `D` comes from a morphism in some `C_k`; essentially surjective iff every object
of `D` is isomorphic to some `G_i x`. In this layer `J = Iᵒᵖ`, `C_i` is a category of objects over
`X_i` and `F_a` is base change; "the base change functors induce an equivalence
`2-colim (X_i)_? → X_?`" means that the induced `G` is an equivalence. In `CategoryTheory`, define
`FilteredTwoColimit` (the category `2-colim F` with objects `Σ j, F.obj j`), `FilteredTwoColimit.ι`
(the canonical functor `ι_j : F.obj j ⥤ FilteredTwoColimit F`), `FilteredTwoColimit.ιCompIso` (for
`a : i → j`, the isomorphism `F_a ⋙ ι_j ≅ ι_i`, compatible with the coherence isomorphisms of `F`)
and `FilteredTwoColimit.desc` (the functor `FilteredTwoColimit F ⥤ D` induced by a pseudo-cocone);
prove `FilteredTwoColimit.homEquiv` (`Hom((i, x), (j, y)) ≃` the colimit over cospans `(k, a, b)` of
`Hom_{F k}(F_a x, F_b y)`), `FilteredTwoColimit.ιCompDescIso` (`ι_i ⋙ desc G ≅ G_i`),
`FilteredTwoColimit.descUniqueIso` (any `H` with isomorphisms `ι_i ⋙ H ≅ G_i` compatible with the
cocone has a unique isomorphism to `desc G` respecting those specified comparisons), `FilteredTwoColimit.isEquivalence_desc_iff` (`desc G`
is an equivalence iff (a) `colim_k Hom(F_a x, F_b y) → Hom_D(G_i x, G_j y)` is bijective for all
`(i, x)`, `(j, y)` and (b) every object of `D` is isomorphic to some `G_i x`),
`FilteredTwoColimit.equivOfFinal` (for a final functor `u : J' ⥤ J` between small filtered categories,
`FilteredTwoColimit (F ∘ u) ⥤ FilteredTwoColimit F` is an equivalence: restriction to a tail),
`FilteredTwoColimit.fullSubcategory` (if `C'_j ⊆ C_j` are full subcategories stable under the `F_a`,
then `2-colim C'_j` is equivalent to the full subcategory of `2-colim C_j` on the `(i, x)` with
`x ∈ C'_i`) and `FilteredTwoColimit.equivConst` (for the constant pseudofunctor at a category `C`,
with identity transition functors, `FilteredTwoColimit ≌ C`). Use Mathlib
`((Functor.const J).obj (Cat.of C)).toPseudofunctor'` for that constant pseudofunctor. For the filtered system of categories
of finite étale algebras over complete Tate rings `A_i`, `Hom` in the 2-colimit is the colimit of
`Hom` over common targets, and the comparison functor to finite étale algebras over the completed
colimit is an equivalence (layer P3, read through `isEquivalence_desc_iff`) ([Berkeley] Lecture 7,
Rem. 7.4.7, printed p. 54; [KL15] §1.2, Rem. 1.2.9, p. 15). *Needs:* Mathlib
`CategoryTheory.Pseudofunctor`, `CategoryTheory.IsFiltered`, `CategoryTheory.Functor.IsEquivalence`,
`CategoryTheory.Grothendieck`.

**Checks.**

- `filteredTwoColimit_test_const` (computation) — for a one-object index with discrete
  Boolean fibre, each included object has exactly one endomorphism and there is no
  morphism from `false` to `true`. For a general constant fibre `C`, `equivConst`
  supplies `FilteredTwoColimit F ≌ C`.
- `filteredTwoColimit_test_discrete` (computation) — for `J = ℕ` and `C_n` the discrete category on
  a set `E_n` with maps `E_n → E_{n+1}`, `FilteredTwoColimit F` is equivalent to the discrete
  category on `colim_n E_n`.
- `filteredTwoColimit_test_finitelyPresentedModules` (compatibility) — for a filtered diagram of
  rings `B_j` with colimit `B`, base change `2-colim_j Mod^{fp}(B_j) → Mod^{fp}(B)` on finitely
  presented modules is an equivalence ([Stacks] [Tag 05N7](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05N7),
  Lem. 10.127.6; filtered categories reduce to directed sets by §4.21, Lem. 4.21.5).
- `filteredTwoColimit_test_notNaive` (computation) — for the two-stage diagram from
  the discrete Boolean category to the one-object category, the initial cross-Hom
  is empty and the cross-Hom in the 2-colimit has exactly one element, an isomorphism.
  More generally `eventually_isomorphic` applies when `C_0` has two objects with no
  morphisms between them and `C_n` (`n ≥ 1`) has two distinct isomorphic objects:
  the category with object set `colim Ob(C_n)` but morphisms taken in `C_0` misses
  their isomorphism in the 2-colimit. These computations use the cospan description
  of morphisms in P5.8. The discrete Boolean and one-object carriers are Mathlib's
  `CategoryTheory.Discrete`.

**Checks for constant pseudofunctors and their 2-colimits.** Each uses the
roadmap's `FilteredTwoColimit` and its canonical inclusions.

- `constantPseudofunctor_empty_fibre` — the 2-colimit over a one-object index
  with empty discrete fibre has no objects.
- `constantPseudofunctor_point` — every object of the 2-colimit of the one-point
  fibre is isomorphic to the included point, and its endomorphisms are unique.
- `constantPseudofunctor_two_terms` — over `0 → 1` in `Fin 2`, the inclusions
  of `false` at the two stages are isomorphic, as are the inclusions of `true`.
  There is no arrow from the included `false` to the included `true`.

### P5.9 finite étale objects come from a finite stage

Throughout P5.9–P5.12, for a perfectoid space `Z`, `Z_ét` is the category of perfectoid spaces
étale over `Z` ([ECD] Def. 6.2; P3.18), and `Z_fét`, `Z_ét,qcqs` and `Z_ét,qc,sep` are its full
subcategories of finite étale, of quasicompact quasiseparated (P4.2), and of quasicompact
separated étale spaces; base change along `X_j → X_i` or `X → X_i` is the fibre product of
perfectoid spaces (P2.16), which preserves these classes (layer P3; P3.18).

**Finite étale objects over a cofiltered limit of affinoid perfectoid spaces come from a finite
stage.** (*finite-etale-finite-stage-approximation*) Let `X = Spa(R, R⁺) = lim_i X_i` be a
cofiltered limit of affinoid perfectoid spaces `X_i = Spa(R_i, R_i⁺)`
(P5.3), with `(i₀, ϖ)` a compatible pseudouniformiser.
Then the base change functors `(X_i)_fét → X_fét` induce an equivalence of categories
`2-colim_i (X_i)_fét → X_fét` (P5.8). Ring form: base change
`S_i ↦ S_i ⊗_{R_i} R` (no completion; the tensor product is finite projective over `R`) induces an
equivalence `2-colim_i FÉt(R_i) → FÉt(R)`, compatible with tensor products and ranks — for the
uncompleted colimit `colim_i R_i` this is AdicEtaleGeometry A1.0.3
(*finite-etale-algebras-filtered-colimit*: `2-colim FÉt(A_i) ≃ FÉt(colim A_i)` for any filtered
colimit of rings), and invariance under completion `FÉt(colim R_i) ≃ FÉt(R)` is
AdicEtaleGeometry A1.0.5, `finiteEtale_completedColimit` (*finite-etale-completed-direct-limit*). AdicEtaleGeometry A4.5's
*finite-etale-invariance-along-tower* is its specialization to finite étale torsor towers, downstream
of AdicEtaleGeometry A1.0.5; it does not supply the arbitrary-transition case here and is not an input. What is
proved here is the perfectoid cofiltered index with its compatible pseudouniformiser and the plus
rings: the plus rings of the corresponding perfectoid spaces are the integral closures of `R_i⁺`,
`R⁺`. Explicitly, the cited equivalences say: (lifting) every finite étale `R`-algebra is
`S_i ⊗_{R_i} R` for some `i` and some finite étale `R_i`-algebra `S_i`; (uniqueness) for finite
étale `R_i`-algebras `S_i`, `S_i'`, every `R`-algebra map `S_i ⊗ R → S_i' ⊗ R` is the base change
of an `R_j`-algebra map for some `j → i`, and two `R_j`-algebra maps with the same base change to
`R` agree over some `R_k`. The theorem concerns
finite étale algebras; finitely presented algebras over `R` do not in general come from a finite
stage: for `S = {0,1}^ℕ`, `0 < |ϖ| < 1` and `f(s) = Σ_k s_k ϖ^k`, the algebra
`B = C^0(S, K)/(f)` is finitely presented but not flat. Indeed `f` vanishes precisely at the
all-zero sequence; this singleton is not open, so `(f)` is not generated by an idempotent.
A flat quotient by a finitely generated ideal would have an idempotent kernel. Every algebra
over the finite product of fields `K^{S_n}` is flat as a module, and base change preserves
flatness, so `B` cannot descend. The two-term calculation `f(0) = 0`, `f(e_n) = ϖ^n ≠ 0`, where
`e_n` has just its `n`-th digit equal to one, also shows that `f` lies in no finite stage. The algebraic input — finite étale algebras over a completed direct
limit of complete Tate rings, through the henselian approximation theorem ([Berkeley] Lecture 7, Thm 7.4.8, printed p. 54)
— is supplied by AdicEtaleGeometry A1.0.5 (the invariance of finite étale algebras under completed colimits); here the
completion is identified with the limit's ring and the statement is carried to spaces. Over `C^0(S, K)`
finite étale algebras are locally on `S` constant: each is an `S_n`-indexed family of finite étale
`K`-algebras tensored with `C^0(S, K)` for some `n`; and a finite étale cover of the limit is the
pullback of one at a finite stage. A specified isomorphism between two pullbacks descends,
and two lifts of that specified isomorphism agree after enlarging the stage (used
in [ECD] proof of Prop. 7.16: a splitting over a connected component extends to a neighbourhood)
([ECD] §6, Prop. 6.4(i), p. 27; [ECD] §6, proof of Prop. 6.4(i), p. 27; [Sch12] §7, proof of
Lem. 7.5(i), p. 41). *Needs:* *completed-colimit-of-perfectoid-pairs*;
*completed-colimit-is-perfectoid*; *cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces*;
*filtered-two-colimit-of-categories*; AdicEtaleGeometry A1.0.5, P3.17, P3.14, P3.10, P2.16; layer P3;
AdicEtaleGeometry A1.0.3 (*finite-etale-algebras-filtered-colimit*); Mathlib `CommAlgCat.FiniteEtale`.

**Checks for ranks and uniqueness.**

For the constant diagram on `Spa(R,R⁺)` indexed by `ℕᵒᵖ`, these Checks pass
from finite étale algebras through `finiteEtaleAffinoidEquiv.inverse`, the
canonical `FilteredTwoColimit.ι`, and `finiteStageFiniteEtaleEquiv`.

- `finiteStage_rank_zero` — the image of `R^{Fin 0}` has empty underlying space.
- `finiteStage_rank_one` — the image of `R^{Fin 1}` has an isomorphism as its
  structural arrow to the limit.
- `finiteStage_iso_not_unique` — when `R ≠ 0`, the coordinate swap of `R × R`
  still differs from the identity after these functors, and its square is the
  identity. Thus uniqueness of finite-stage descent concerns a specified
  isomorphism over the limit ([ECD] Prop. 6.4(i), p. 27).

### P5.10 quasicompact quasiseparated étale objects form the 2-colimit

**Quasicompact quasiseparated étale objects over a cofiltered limit form the 2-colimit.**
(*qcqs-etale-finite-stage-descent*) Let `X = lim_i X_i` be a cofiltered limit of affinoid
perfectoid spaces (P5.3). Then the base change
functors `(X_i)_ét,qcqs → X_ét,qcqs` induce an equivalence of categories
`2-colim_i (X_i)_ét,qcqs → X_ét,qcqs` (the 2-colimit of *filtered-two-colimit-of-categories* for
the base-change pseudofunctor on `Iᵒᵖ`). Explicitly: for `Y_i, Y_i' ∈ (X_i)_ét,qcqs`,
`colim_{j → i} Hom_{X_j}(Y_j, Y_j') → Hom_X(Y, Y')` is bijective, and every qcqs étale `Y → X` is
isomorphic to the base change of some qcqs étale `Y_i → X_i`. Quasicompactness is necessary: the
non-quasicompact open `X ∖ ({s₀} × Spa(K, O_K))` of `S × Spa(K, O_K)` does not descend. Uses: for
`Y = lim Y_i` affinoid pro-étale over `X`, `Y_ét,qcqs = 2-colim (Y_i)_ét,qcqs` ([ECD] §7, proof of
Prop. 7.10, p. 33); a qcqs étale cover of `X` that splits over a connected component
`Spa(C, C⁺) = lim` of its clopen neighbourhoods splits over a neighbourhood ([ECD] proof of
Prop. 7.16, which DiamondsAndVStacks D1 uses downstream) ([ECD] §6, Prop. 6.4(ii), p. 27). *Needs:*
*finite-stage-faithfulness*; *finite-stage-fullness*; *qcqs-etale-essential-surjectivity*;
*filtered-two-colimit-of-categories*; *cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces*; P3.18,
P2.16; layer P3.

Three lemmas give the equivalence. Faithfulness by the graph argument
(*finite-stage-faithfulness*): in the situation of *cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces*
let `Y_i, Y_i' ∈ (X_i)_ét,qcqs` and `f_i, g_i : Y_i → Y_i'` morphisms over `X_i`. Prove that if their
base changes `f, g : Y → Y'` over `X` are equal, then `f_j = g_j` for some `a : j → i` (`f_j`, `g_j`
the base changes to `X_j`); equivalently `2-colim_i (X_i)_ét,qcqs → X_ét,qcqs` is faithful. Two
`X_0`-endomorphisms of a finite étale `Y_0 → X_0` that agree over the limit agree at a finite
stage; faithfulness fails for non-quasicompact `Y_i`, since the argument needs the images of the
graphs to be quasicompact: for `X_n = {|T| ≤ |ϖ|ⁿ} ⊆ X_0 = Spa(K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, O_K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩)`
with limit the origin `Spa(K, O_K)`, `Y_0 := ⊔_{m ≥ 1} X_0` and `Y_0' := ⊔_{m ≥ 1} (X_0 ⊔_{X_m} X_0)`
(two copies of the disc glued along `X_m`), the maps `f_0, g_0 : Y_0 → Y_0'` that are the first,
resp. second, inclusion on the `m`-th component differ on the components `m > n` over every
`X_n`, but agree over the origin, which lies in every `X_m` ([ECD] §6, proof of Prop. 6.4(ii),
pp. 27–28; [ECD] §5, Prop. 5.3, p. 21, injections are determined by their image). *Needs:*
*limit-of-qcqs-base-changes*;
*descent-of-quasicompact-opens*; P3.15, P3.17, P4.3, P4.7, P2.16; layer P3; AdicEtaleGeometry
A1.3.

Fullness by graph approximation (*finite-stage-fullness*): in the same situation let
`Y_i, Y_i' ∈ (X_i)_ét,qcqs` and `f : Y → Y'` a morphism over `X` between their base changes. Prove
that there are `a : j → i` and a morphism `f_j : Y_j → Y_j'` over `X_j` whose base change to `X` is
`f`; with *finite-stage-faithfulness*, `2-colim_i (X_i)_ét,qcqs → X_ét,qcqs` is fully faithful. For
an affinoid pro-étale `Y = lim Y_i` and an étale `Z`, `Hom_X(Y, Z) = colim_i Hom_X(Y_i, Z)` ([ECD]
proof of Prop. 7.10) is this fullness applied to `Y_i ×_X Z → Y_i`; a section over the limit of an
étale cover descends to a section over a finite stage ([ECD] §6, proof of Prop. 6.4(ii), p. 28).
*Needs:* *finite-stage-faithfulness*; *limit-of-qcqs-base-changes*; *descent-of-quasicompact-opens*;
*finite-stage-isomorphism-detection*; P3.17; layer P3; layer P2; AdicEtaleGeometry A1.3.

Every qcqs étale space over the limit descends to a finite stage
(*qcqs-etale-essential-surjectivity*): in the same situation prove that every `Y ∈ X_ét,qcqs` is
isomorphic over `X` to `Y_i ×_{X_i} X` for some `i` and some `Y_i ∈ (X_i)_ét,qcqs`, by the local
structure of étale maps ([ECD] §6, Def. 6.2(ii), p. 26) and gluing along quasicompact overlaps. A
rational subset of a finite étale cover of a rational subset of `X` descends, and a finite union of
such opens glued along quasicompact overlaps descends; for `X = S × Spa(K, O_K)` with `S` profinite
without isolated points, the open subspace `Y = X ∖ ({s₀} × Spa(K, O_K))` is étale and
quasiseparated but not quasicompact, and is not the base change of an open subspace of any finite
stage ([ECD] §6, proof of Prop. 6.4(ii), p. 28). *Needs:* *finite-etale-finite-stage-approximation*;
*finite-stage-fullness*; *finite-stage-faithfulness*; *descent-of-quasicompact-opens*;
*limit-restriction-to-rational-subsets*; *limit-of-qcqs-base-changes*; P3.15, P3.17;
AdicEtaleGeometry A1.3 (étale morphisms by the local open-immersion/finite-étale description);
layer P3; layer P2.

### P5.11 quasicompact separated étale objects form the 2-colimit

**Quasicompact separated étale objects over a cofiltered limit form the 2-colimit.**
(*quasicompact-separated-etale-finite-stage-descent*) Let `X = lim_i X_i` be a cofiltered limit of
affinoid perfectoid spaces. Then the base change functors `(X_i)_ét,qc,sep → X_ét,qc,sep` induce an
equivalence of categories `2-colim_i (X_i)_ét,qc,sep → X_ét,qc,sep`, where
`X_ét,qc,sep ⊆ X_ét,qcqs` is the full subcategory of quasicompact separated étale perfectoid spaces
over `X` (a separated étale space over an affinoid is quasiseparated). A quasicompact separated
étale space with descent data over an affinoid pro-étale limit comes from a finite stage together
with its descent datum ([ECD] §9, proof of Prop. 9.7, p. 48; used by DiamondsAndVStacks D3 downstream) ([ECD]
§6, Prop. 6.4(iii), p. 27; [ECD] §6, proof of Prop. 6.4(iii), p. 28). *Needs:*
*qcqs-etale-finite-stage-descent*; *separatedness-recognition-at-finite-stage*;
*filtered-two-colimit-of-categories*; P4.19.

Separatedness is recognised at a finite stage (*separatedness-recognition-at-finite-stage*): in
the situation of *cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces* let `f_i : Y_i → X_i` be qcqs
étale. Prove that if the base change `f : Y → X` is separated ([ECD] Def. 5.10: `Δ_f` is a closed
immersion; P4.19), then `f_j : Y_j → X_j` is separated for some `a : j → i`, by the topological
criterion for separatedness ([ECD] §5, Prop. 5.11(ii), p. 25) and the clopen descent of
AdicSpacesPartII R0.19.8 (*quasicompact-opens-in-limits-of-spectral-spaces*). The stage must be enlarged in general: for
`X_n := {|T| ≤ |ϖ|^n} ⊆ X_0 = Spa(K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, O_K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩)`, with limit `Spa(K, K⁺)` (the
origin), `Y_1 :=` two copies of `X_1` glued along `V_1 = {|T| ≤ |ϖ|^2}` is qcqs étale over `X_1` and
not separated, while its base change to `X_2` (two copies of `X_2` glued along `X_2`) is `X_2`,
which is separated ([ECD] §6, proof of Prop. 6.4(iii), p. 28). *Needs:* *limit-of-qcqs-base-changes*;
*descent-of-quasicompact-opens*; P4.19, P4.20, P4.18; layer P3.

**Finite-stage descent along cofiltered limits of affinoid perfectoid spaces.**

### P5.13.1 tubular neighbourhoods and sousperfectoid specializations

**Tubular neighbourhoods of standard étale loci: a nonarchimedean implicit function theorem.**
(*tubular-neighbourhood*) Let `(A, A⁺)` be a complete Tate Huber pair with pseudouniformiser `ϖ`
and `A` sousperfectoid (P3.17a), so that `A⟨T₁, …, T_N⟩` and its rational
localisations are sousperfectoid, hence uniform, and `O⁺(W')` is a `ϖ`-adically complete ring of
definition of `O(W')` for every rational `W'`; the Newton arguments below use only this
uniformity, but the targets are stated, and used, over sousperfectoid bases. Let
`X = Spa(A, A⁺)`, `e = (e₁, …, e_N) ∈ A⁺⟨T₁, …, T_N⟩^N`, `k ≥ 0` and `m ≥ 2k + 1`, and let
`R ⊆ B^N_X` be a finite intersection of rational subsets `R(g_j/h_j)` with
`g_{j,1}, …, g_{j,r_j}, h_j ∈ A⁺⟨T⟩` and `ϖ^{c_j} ∈ (g_{j,1}, …, g_{j,r_j}, h_j)·A⁺⟨T⟩` for some
`c_j < m − k` (the empty intersection being `B^N_X`), so that `R` is unchanged when a point is
moved by `ϖ^{m−k}·A⁺⟨T⟩` (AdicSpaces layer 3, perturbation invariance; `tubeSet` is the tube in
the whole ball, and `R` enters the proposed Lean statements through the hypothesis on the rational
subset `W`). Let `Δ := det(∂eᵢ/∂T_j) ∈ A⁺⟨T⟩` and
`W := R ∩ {|eᵢ| ≤ |ϖ^m| for all i} ∩ {|ϖᵏ| ≤ |Δ|}`, a rational subset, the [*tube*](../AdicSpacesPartIII/README.md) (AdicSpacesPartIII R2.4) of `e` of
radius `|ϖ|^m`, on which the Jacobian is bounded below by `|ϖᵏ|`. Put
`C := O(W)/closure(e·O(W))` with `C⁺` the integral closure of the image of `O⁺(W)`, and
`V(e) ∩ W := Spa(C, C⁺)`. Prove (a) `tube_product_equiv_sousperfectoid` (its section clause alone
is `exists_section_tube_sousperfectoid`, for a single `R(g/h)`), (b) `tube_product_restrict` and
(c) `tube_quotient_baseChange`: (a) there is a unique isomorphism of complete Huber pairs over
`(A, A⁺)`

`Φ : (C⟨u₁, …, u_N⟩, C⁺⟨u⟩) → (O(W), O⁺(W)),   Φ(uᵢ) = ϖ^{−m}eᵢ,`

such that `Φ` restricted to `C` is a ring section `ρ` of the quotient map `q : O(W) → C` with
`ρ(q(T)) − T ∈ ϖ^{m−k}O⁺(W)^N`; geometrically `W ≅ (V(e) ∩ W) ×_X B^N_X(|ϖ|^m)` with `e`
corresponding to `ϖ^m u` (the section `ρ` is the Newton solution `t*` of `e(t*) = 0` starting
from `t = T`, and the point `T ↦ t*` lies in `W` because `|Δ(t*) − Δ| ≤ |ϖ|^{k+1} < |ϖᵏ| ≤ |Δ|`
and because `R` is stable under the move; the inverse of `Φ` sends `T` to the Newton solution
of `e(τ) = ϖ^m u` over `C⟨u⟩`); (b) the same holds, with `C` replaced by
`C_{W'} := O(W')/closure(e·O(W'))`, for every rational subset `W' ⊆ W` which is the preimage of a
rational subset `V' ⊆ V(e) ∩ W` under the projection `W → V(e) ∩ W` of (a), and for
`W' = W ∩ R'` with `R'` subject to the same condition as `R` (this second case is (a) for the
family `R ∩ R'`, and is covered by `tube_product_equiv_sousperfectoid`); it does not hold for an
arbitrary rational `W' ⊆ W` (*test_small_ball_not_product*, *test_section_fails_off_locus*); (c) for
every rational `W' ⊆ W` the ideal `e·O(W')` is closed (`isWeaklyRegular_tube_sousperfectoid`),
`O(W')/(e) = C_{W'} = C ⊗̂_{O(W)} O(W')`, and `V(e) ∩ W'` is the rational subset of `V(e) ∩ W` cut
out by the same inequalities (for `W' ∩ V(e) = ∅` both sides are the zero ring).
Integrality of `e` as a power series in `T` is essential: the Newton step needs integral Taylor
coefficients, and for `e ∈ O⁺(R)` involving the rational coordinates of `R` the statement fails;
equations with rational coordinates are handled by adjoining those coordinates as variables
([*standard-presentation-basic-pieces*](../AdicEtaleGeometry/README.md) (AdicEtaleGeometry A3.2) (c)). This is the analytic-algebra replacement of
Fargues–Scholze's local statement that smooth spaces are balls near sections ([FS] §IV.4.1, before
Lem. IV.4.14, p. 137; proof of Lem. IV.4.16, p. 139, which establishes the local product
structure after reduction modulo `ϖ`, here obtained directly by Newton iteration); the
perturbation argument of [ECD] §6, proof of Prop. 6.4(iv), p. 28, is carried out inside such a
tube. Prove clauses (a)–(b) first from Newton's theorem, independently of
`isWeaklyRegular_tube_sousperfectoid`. Then prove [*fs-iv-4-13-regular-sequence*](#p5-13-1) (P5.13.1) using only those
two tube clauses and its listed inputs. Finally prove clause (c) from that regular-sequence
theorem. *Needs for (a)–(b):* [*restricted-power-series-newton*](../AdicEtaleGeometry/README.md) (AdicEtaleGeometry A3.2); P3.17a
(sousperfectoid rings, stably uniform); AdicSpacesPartII layer R0 (completed tensor products, rational localisation,
continuous differentials); Tau Ceti
`TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.exists_mem_nhds_forall_rationalSubset_eq_of_sub_mem`,
`TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.existsUnique_continuous_ringHom_of_forall_comap_mem_rationalSubset`,
`TauCeti.Huber.existsUnique_continuous_ringHom_completion_weightedRestrictedSubring`,
`Huber.PairOfDefinition.completionLocalization`, `TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.mem_iff_forall_vle_one`,
`ValuationSpectrum.rationalSubset`. *Needs for (c):* clauses (a)–(b);
[*fs-iv-4-13-regular-sequence*](#p5-13-1) (P5.13.1); AdicSpacesPartII layer R0 (rational base change of completed
quotients). README only (no Lean declaration).

**Checks.**

- *tube_integral_certificate* — For `F = 4T` over `Q₂`, `tubeSet` with `k = 0` is empty, while `k = 2` gives a nonempty tube; the integral Jacobian bound detects the difference.
- *test_translation* — `N = 1`, `R = B¹_X`, `e = T − a` with `a ∈ A⁺`, `k = 0`, `m = 1`:
  `W = {|T − a| ≤ |ϖ|}` (the check *tube_linear*, for every radius `|ϖ|^m`), `C = A` and `Φ` is
  the translation `u ↦ ϖ^{−1}(T − a)`.
- *test_unit_jacobian_product* — for `R = B^N_X`, `k = 0` and `e` with `Δ ≡ 1 modulo (e₁, …, e_N)·A⁺⟨T⟩` (so `|Δ| = 1` on `{|e| ≤ |ϖ|}`), the tube is `W = {|e| ≤ |ϖ|}` and
  `W ≅ V(e) ×_X B^N(|ϖ|)`.
- *test_small_ball_not_product* (non-example for (b) with arbitrary `W'`) — `A = ℚ_p`, `N = 1`,
  `e = T`, `k = 0`, `m = 1`, `W = {|T| ≤ |p|}`, `C = ℚ_p`, and `W' = {|T| ≤ |p|²} ⊆ W`:
  `C_{W'} = ℚ_p`, but `O(W') = ℚ_p⟨T/p²⟩` is not `ℚ_p⟨u⟩` with `u ↦ T/p`, since the image of
  `ℚ_p⟨u⟩` is `ℚ_p⟨p·(T/p²)⟩ ⊊ ℚ_p⟨T/p²⟩`. Writing `v = T/p²`, the series
  `∑ p^n v^n` has no restricted preimage, whereas `v` itself is the image of `p⁻¹u`; equally, with `R = {|T| ≤ |p|^{10}}` (here
  `c = 10 ≥ m − k = 1`) the claim (a) fails for `W = R`.
- *test_section_fails_off_locus* (non-example) — same data, `W' = {|T − p| ≤ |p|²} ⊆ W`: `T` is a
  unit on `W'` (`|T| = |p|` there), so `C_{W'} = 0` while `O(W') ≠ 0`, and no ring section
  `C_{W'} → O(W')` of the quotient map exists; the Newton point `t* = 0` of `e = T` does not lie
  in `W'`.
- *test_integral_coefficients_needed* (non-example) — `A = ℚ_p`, `p` odd, `ϖ = p`, `N = 1`,
  `R = {|T| ≤ |p|}`: `e = (T/p)²` lies in `O⁺(R)` but not in the image of `ℤ_p⟨T⟩`,
  `Δ = 2T/p²`, and for `k = 0`, `m = 2` the set `W = {|T| = |p|²}` is a nonempty rational subset on
  which `e` is a unit, so `C = 0` while `O(W) ≠ 0` and no isomorphism `C⟨u⟩ ≅ O(W)` exists
  (when formalised, the check presents `W` as `R({T², p²T, p⁴}/p²T)` and records that `T` is a unit of the
  nonzero ring `O(W)`).

The proposed theorem `tube_product_restrict` applies to the product isomorphism `Φ` and a rational
localisation `C → C'`. Its numerators in `O(W)` are exactly the images under the coefficient
section `C → O(W)`. It produces `C'⟨u⟩ ≅ O(W')`, commuting with coefficients and labelled
coordinates and preserving plus rings. The proposed theorem `tube_quotient_baseChange` allows any
rational inclusion `W' ⊆ W` inside the tube. It states closedness of both equation ideals,
identifies their images under `ratLocRestriction`, and identifies the completed tensor
quotient with `O(W')/(e)`, including the plus ring. Its formula on pure tensors fixes the
comparison map. Together with rational base change, these statements identify the
restricted zero locus and its quotient pair.

**Stability of standard étale presentations under perturbation.**
(*standard-presentation-perturbation*) Let `(N, F, 2k, π)` be a standard étale presentation of
`(C, C⁺)` in explicit-inverse form with exponent `k`, `F = (F', S·J_{F'} − ϖᵏ)`, over a complete
Tate pair `(A, A⁺)` with `A` sousperfectoid (as in [*tubular-neighbourhood*](#p5-13-1) (P5.13.1): the argument uses the
uniformity of the rational localisations of the Tate algebras over `A`), and put
`m₀ := 4k + 2`. For every
`G ∈ A⁺⟨T⟩^N` with `G − F ∈ ϖ^{m₀}A⁺⟨T⟩^N` coefficientwise, prove: (a) the quotient pair
`(C_G, C_G⁺) := A⟨T⟩/closure(G)` has the standard étale presentation `(N, G, 2k, π_G)`, the
Jacobian of `G` being invertible on `V(G)` with inverse bounded by `|ϖ|^{−2k}`; (b) `V(G)` and
`V(F)` both lie in the tube `W` of `F` with Jacobian exponent `2k` and radius `|ϖ|^{4k+1}`, and
there is a unique isomorphism of complete Huber pairs `α_{F,G} : (C, C⁺) → (C_G, C_G⁺)` over
`(A, A⁺)` with `α_{F,G}(π(T)) − π_G(T) ∈ ϖ^{m₀−2k}(C_G⁺)^N`, and it is already the only continuous
`A`-algebra map `C → C_G` with this congruence; (c)
if `G = (G', S·J_{G'} − ϖᵏ)` is itself in
explicit-inverse form with exponent `k` (which is the case when `G' − F' ∈ ϖ^{m₀}A⁺⟨T'⟩^{N−1}` and
the last equation is rebuilt from `G'`), then `α_{G,F}` is defined and `α_{G,F} = α_{F,G}^{−1}`, the
comparison maps being mutually inverse on the permitted tube with no further shrinking,
`α_{G,H}∘α_{F,G} = α_{F,H}` whenever all three are defined, and `α` is compatible with base change
along morphisms of complete Tate pairs, all by the uniqueness in (b); (d) plus rings correspond,
`α(C⁺) = C_G⁺`. In the proposed Lean form, for `F = P.withInverse.F` the explicit-inverse form of
a presentation `P`, `α_{F,G}` is `StandardEtalePresentation.perturb`, and (a), (b) and (d), with the
uniqueness, are its specification over a sousperfectoid base; a perturbed system that is itself in
explicit-inverse form presents its quotient pair by `nonempty_ofExplicitInverse`.
The inverse is characterised by the reverse coordinate congruence: every continuous reverse
comparison satisfying it is that inverse. The composite
with any continuous, plus-preserving nearby comparison `G → H` is the chosen comparison
`F → H`. Taking the reverse or intermediate comparison supplied by `perturb` on an
explicit-inverse system gives `α_{G,F} = α_{F,G}⁻¹` and the cocycle identity without shrinking.
The base-change square on rings commutes for
compatible presentations over sousperfectoid source and target bases, fixing the maps
on coefficients and labelled coordinates; the coordinate formula of `baseChange` supplies these
equations for completed base change. Hence
`Spa(C_G, C_G⁺) ≅ Spa(C, C⁺)` over `X`, and every property of `V(F)` over `X` (étale,
sousperfectoid, perfectoid) holds for `V(G)`. If `A` has a noetherian ring of definition this
agrees with Huber's 1.7.2 (AdicSpacesPartII layer R0, [*etale-presentation-perturbation*](../AdicSpacesPartII/README.md) (AdicSpacesPartII R0.17); the
closure-of-the-ideal form over a non-noetherian base is the content here) ([ECD] §6,
proof of Prop. 6.4(iv), p. 28: slightly perturbed equations still define an affinoid
sousperfectoid space étale over `X`, and close approximations are isomorphic to `Y`, here through
`α_{F,G}`; [Huber96] §1.7, Cor. 1.7.2(i), p. 85, gives neighbourhood-wise perturbation
stability for Huber’s affinoid rings; the explicit exponent here is additional). *Needs:* [*standard-etale-presentation*](../AdicEtaleGeometry/README.md) (AdicEtaleGeometry A3.2);
[*perturbation-of-generators*](../AdicEtaleGeometry/README.md) (AdicEtaleGeometry A3.2); [*tubular-neighbourhood*](#p5-13-1) (P5.13.1); AdicSpacesPartII layer R0; Tau Ceti
`TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.existsUnique_continuous_ringHom_of_forall_comap_mem_rationalSubset`,
`TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.exists_mem_nhds_forall_rationalSubset_eq_of_sub_mem`. README only (no Lean declaration).

**Checks.**

- *test_perturb_linear_identity* — `F = (T − a, S − 1)` with `a ∈ A⁺` (explicit-inverse form with

- *perturb_coordinate* — For the same shifted idempotent equation, the coordinate error is `−δ` and differs from `1 − 2Tᵢ + δ`, the error obtained by exchanging the two roots.
- *test_perturb_rational* — perturbing `s, t` in `(tT − s)` inside `ϖ^{m₀}` does not change

**Standard étale loci over sousperfectoid bases are sousperfectoid affinoids.**
(*standard-etale-locus-sousperfectoid*) Let `(A, A⁺)` be a complete Tate Huber pair with `A`
sousperfectoid (P3.17a; for instance perfectoid, or a rational localisation of
`A'⟨T⟩` with `A'` perfectoid) and `(N, F, k, π)` a standard étale presentation of `(C, C⁺)` over

`W` is the tube of `F` (*tubular-neighbourhood*),
`ρ : C → O(W)` the section and `q : O(W) → C` the quotient, so that `C` is a `C`-linear direct
summand of the sousperfectoid `O(W)`, and `(P̃, ι, σ)` is a perfectoid frame of `O(W)`, then
`(P̃, ι∘ρ, q∘σ)` is a perfectoid frame of `C`. Consequently `(C, C⁺)` is sheafy and stably
uniform, `Spa(C, C⁺)` is a sousperfectoid affinoid adic space (P3.17a,
sousperfectoid sheafy, stably uniform, sousperfectoid adic space), and for every rational
`U ⊆ Spa(C, C⁺)` the ring `O(U)` is sousperfectoid with a standard étale presentation over

sousperfectoid clause of [FS] §IV.4.1, Prop. IV.4.17, p. 139 (vanishing loci of functions with
independent differentials are sous-perfectoid spaces smooth over `X`), using the stability
properties of sous-perfectoid rings of [FS] §IV.4.1, p. 135. Whenever the locus is already known

sousperfectoidness is P3.17a [*sousperfectoid-etale-stability*](#p3-17a-4) (P3.17a.4) (P3.17a); the direct

spaces). README only (no Lean declaration).
