#### Pseudocoherent and finite étale specializations

Finite étale algebras over perfectoid rings admit the standard étale presentations of
AdicEtaleGeometry A3.2 and are perfectoid by P3.10 ([ECD] §6, Theorem 6.1(i), p. 26).
The sousperfectoid specializations of AdicEtaleGeometry A3.1 are
`cech_injective_of_isStablyPseudoCoherent_sousperfectoid`,
`exact_tensor_ratLoc_sousperfectoid` and `isStrictMap_mul_X_sub_sousperfectoid`:
apply its sheafy-base Čech injectivity, tensor exactness and strict Laurent multiplication
theorems with the sheafiness and uniformity of P3.17a. They retain AdicEtaleGeometry A3.1's stably
pseudocoherent hypotheses, ordered restriction maps and four strict multiplication maps.
*Needs:* P3.17a.1–P3.17a.3; AdicEtaleGeometry A3.1
([*stably-pseudocoherent-module*](../AdicEtaleGeometry/README.md) (AdicEtaleGeometry A3.1), [*rational-localisation-pseudoflat*](../AdicEtaleGeometry/README.md) (AdicEtaleGeometry A3.1),
[*simple-laurent-strict-multiplication*](../AdicEtaleGeometry/README.md) (AdicEtaleGeometry A3.1)) and AdicEtaleGeometry A3.2 (*standard-etale-presentation*).

**Checks.**

- Over a perfectoid field, the regular module has the supplied augmented Čech exactness.
- Over `ℚ_p⟨T⟩`, these specializations recover the strongly noetherian flat restriction maps.
- The zero module gives zero maps and an exact zero Čech complex.
- A nonzero constant sequence does not tend to zero in a Hausdorff coefficient ring,
  so it cannot be used as the null coefficient sequence in the strict Laurent argument.
<a id="p5-13-2"></a>

- *test_valuationRing_residue* (non-example; the degree shifts are sharp) — for a valuation ring
  `O` whose maximal ideal `𝔪` is not finitely generated, such as the valuation ring of `ℂ_p` or of
  any perfectoid field, `O/𝔪` is 0- but not 1-pseudocoherent, and in `0 → 𝔪 → O → O/𝔪 → 0` the
  middle term is pseudocoherent while `𝔪` is not even 0-pseudocoherent. So (c) at `m = 0` fails
  when `M₂` is only 0-pseudocoherent, and (b) at `m = 1` fails without the hypothesis on `M₁`. For
  `0 → ℤ →(×2) ℤ → ℤ/2 → 0` the projective dimensions are `0, 0, 1` (check *fpd_not_projective*), so
  (e) cannot conclude that `M₂` is m-fpd.
- *test_not_stably* (non-example) — [KL16] §2.4, Ex. 2.4.2, pp. 35–36: an affinoid perfectoid
  `(A, A⁺)` and a non-zero-divisor `f` with `fA` closed, so `A/fA` strictly pseudocoherent, but
  `fB` not closed for some rational localisation `B`, so `A/fA` is not stably pseudocoherent. A
  definition using only completeness of `M` itself fails this test.
- *test_disc_localisation* — for `A = ℚ_p⟨X⟩` and `f = X/p`: `B₁ = ℚ_p⟨X, T⟩/(T − X/p) = ℚ_p⟨X/p⟩`, the ring of `U₁ = {|X| ≤ |p|}`, and `B₂ = ℚ_p⟨X, T⟩/(1 − XT/p) = ℚ_p⟨X, p/X⟩`, the
  ring of `U₂ = {|X| ≥ |p|}`: on `U₂` the element `T = p/X` is the power-bounded inverse of `f`.
  For `f = 1/p ∈ ℚ_p` (not power-bounded), `T − 1/p = −p^{−1}(1 − pT)` is a unit of `ℚ_p⟨T⟩`, so
  `B₁ = 0 = O(∅)`, as `U₁ = {|1/p| ≤ 1} = ∅`. When formalised, the checks identify `B₁` with the rational
  localisation at `R({X, p}/p)` and `B₂` with that at `R({X, p}/X)`.

### P5.13.2 the Fargues–Scholze specialisations by analytic algebra

The étale specialisations of [FS] §IV.4.1, pp. 135–141, are reconstructed by analytic algebra.
The order is: tube clauses (a)–(b) give regular sequences and finite projective dimension,
which then give tube clause (c); the characteristic-`p` Jacobian criterion supplies the étale parts of IV.4.15 and IV.4.17;
pseudocoherent gluing and the integral cut-off then give the closed-image and conormal statements
used in IV.4.19. The arguments of IV.4.14, IV.4.16 and IV.4.18 involving diamonds are not inputs.
The specialisations are exactly those [ECD] 6.4(iv) uses: étale (relative dimension `0`) loci and
closed immersions of affinoid étale perfectoid spaces into rational subsets of relative balls over
affinoid perfectoid bases; the smooth cases over general sousperfectoid bases are outside this
construction.

**A perfectoid Tate ring of characteristic `p` is an algebra over a perfectoid field and a
completed colimit of `p`-finite algebras.** (*char-p-perfectoid-base-field*) Let `(R, R⁺)` be a
perfectoid Tate pair of characteristic `p` (layer P1: `R` a perfect complete
Tate ring) and `ϖ ∈ R⁺` a pseudouniformiser (Tau Ceti `Huber.IsPseudoUniformizer`); no base
field is assumed, it is constructed. The compatible roots `ϖ^{1/pⁿ}` of the given `ϖ`, each again
a pseudouniformiser, are `exists_pow_roots_pseudoUniformizer_charP`. Let `K := F_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^∧` be the `t`-adic completion of
the perfection of `F_p((t))`, a perfectoid field (layer P1). Prove: (a) there is
a unique continuous ring homomorphism `K → R` with `t^{1/pⁿ} ↦ ϖ^{1/pⁿ}`, the unique `pⁿ`-th
roots in the perfect ring `R`; it is injective when `R ≠ 0` and maps `K° = F_p[[t^{1/p^∞}]]^∧`
into `R⁺`, so `(R, R⁺)` is a perfectoid affinoid `K`-algebra with `R⁺` a `K°`-algebra; (b)
consequently `(R, R⁺)` is the completion of a filtered colimit of `p`-finite perfectoid affinoid
`K`-algebras `(R_α, R_α⁺)`, each the completed perfection of a reduced affinoid `K`-algebra
`(S_α, S_α⁺)` of topologically finite type ([Sch12] §6, Lem. 6.13(i), p. 37, under the hypothesis
supplied by (a); `p`-finite is [Sch12] §6, Def. 6.9, p. 35; layer P2, completed
direct limits of `p`-finite affinoids), and `R⁺/ϖ^M = colim_α colim_r S_α^{+,1/p^r}/ϖ^M` for
every `M`, so finitely many elements of `R⁺` are approximated modulo `ϖ^M` by elements of one
`S_α^{1/p^r} ≅ S_α`, again a reduced `K`-affinoid algebra of topologically finite type, hence
strongly noetherian. *Needs:* layers P1 and P2; Mathlib `PerfectRing`,
`frobenius`; Tau Ceti `Huber.IsPseudoUniformizer`.

**Checks.**

- *test_base_field_identity* — `R = K` itself: the map is the identity.
- *test_perfectoid_disc_pfinite* — `R = K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩` is `p`-finite, the completed perfection of
  `K⟨T⟩`. The inclusion has the Gauss topology, roots of integral elements are dense in the
  integral subring, and each positive root `T^{1/pⁿ}` lies outside the original disc algebra.


**Checks.**

- A constant system of characteristic-p perfectoid fields recovers its coefficient field and identity completed colimit.

**Jacobian criterion over characteristic-`p` perfectoid bases.** (*jacobian-criterion-char-p*)
Let `(A, A⁺)` be a perfectoid Tate pair of characteristic `p`, `X = Spa(A, A⁺)`, and
`(B, B⁺) := (O(Q), O⁺(Q))` for a rational subset `Q ⊆ B^m_X` (`m ≥ 0`; `m = 0` and `Q = X` give
`(B, B⁺) = (A, A⁺)`; `B` is sousperfectoid, P3.17a). Let `(N, F, k, π)` be a
standard étale presentation of `(C, C⁺)` over `(B, B⁺)`, put in explicit-inverse form first.
Prove: (a) `Spa(C, C⁺) → Spa(B, B⁺)` is étale in the local-description sense
([*etale-morphisms-local-description-and-comparison*](../AdicEtaleGeometry/README.md) (AdicEtaleGeometry A1.4) of AdicEtaleGeometry layer A1: every point has an open
neighbourhood on which the map factors as an open immersion, a finite étale morphism and an open
immersion); (b) if `m = 0`, then `C` is a perfectoid Tate ring (`C` is perfect), `Spa(C, C⁺)` is
an affinoid perfectoid space and `Spa(C, C⁺) → X` is étale in the sense of [ECD] Def. 6.2
(layer P3); the ring part is that `C` is perfect and a perfectoid Tate ring
(PerfectoidSpaces' `Perfectoid.IsPerfectoidTateRing`); (c) a morphism `g : U → V` over `X` between rational subsets
`U ⊆ B^n_X` and `V ⊆ B^n_X` such that `det(∂gᵢ/∂T_j)` is a unit of `O(U)` with bounded inverse is
étale in the local-description sense (the étale case of [FS] §IV.4.1, Prop. IV.4.15(ii), p. 138:
an isomorphism on differentials gives étaleness; Prop. IV.4.17, p. 139: vanishing loci with
independent differentials, étale when `r = n`). The proof approximates the finitely many
coefficients by a strongly noetherian `K`-affinoid algebra (*char-p-perfectoid-base-field*), uses
Huber's noetherian theory (AdicSpacesPartII layer R0: étale local structure, the finite étale
embedding of an étale affinoid, the local open–finite étale factorisation), base changes along
the sousperfectoid `Spa(B)` (P3.17a, sousperfectoid étale base change) and
perturbs back (*standard-presentation-perturbation*) — the strategy of [Sch12] §7, Prop. 7.7, p. 41
(in characteristic `p` étale maps of perfectoid spaces are locally base changes of étale maps of
noetherian adic spaces); [ECD] §6, proof of Prop. 6.4(iv), p. 28, uses that the perturbed locus is
étale over `X` and thus perfectoid. No diamond, no [ECD] 11.30 or 15.6 and no v-descent is used:
the printed proofs of IV.4.15 and IV.4.17 rest on [ECD] Lem. 12.17 (the deformation step, [FS]
§IV.4.1, proof of Prop. IV.4.15, p. 138), on Lem. IV.4.14 and on Lem. IV.4.16 (descent to
strictly totally disconnected bases). *Needs:* [*standard-etale-presentation*](../AdicEtaleGeometry/README.md) (AdicEtaleGeometry A3.2);
[*standard-presentation-perturbation*](#p5-13-1) (P5.13.1); [*standard-etale-locus-sousperfectoid*](#p5-13-1) (P5.13.1);
[*char-p-perfectoid-base-field*](#p5-13-2) (P5.13.2); [*etale-morphisms-local-description-and-comparison*](../AdicEtaleGeometry/README.md) (AdicEtaleGeometry A1.4) (AdicEtaleGeometry layer A1);
AdicSpacesPartII layer R0 (Huber 1.7.1, étale local structure, completed tensor products);
P3.17a (sousperfectoid étale base change, sheafiness);
layers P1–P3; Tau
Ceti `TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.exists_mem_nhds_forall_rationalSubset_eq_of_sub_mem`; Mathlib
`PerfectRing`. README only (no Lean declaration).

**Checks.**

- *test_rational_finite_etale_pieces* — rational subsets of `X` and finite étale algebras over
  rational subsets (*standard-presentation-basic-pieces*) give étale affinoid perfectoid spaces,
  as they must ([ECD] §3, Thm. 3.18 (rational subsets) and §6, Thm. 6.1(i) (finite étale
  algebras)).
- *test_frobenius_locus_not_etale* (non-example) — `F = T^p − a` has `J_F = 0` and is not a
  standard étale presentation; when the quotient is nonzero, its locus `Spa(A⟨T⟩/(T^p − a))` is not étale over `X`.


**Checks.**

- In zero variables the Jacobian is the empty determinant 1 and the locus is the original base.

**Comparison of a graph neighbourhood with the original target and its quotient modules.**
(*graph-neighbourhood-target-comparison*) Let `(A, A⁺)` be a complete sousperfectoid Tate pair
with pseudouniformiser `ϖ`, `X = Spa(A, A⁺)`, `R ⊆ B^N_X` rational, `B = O(R)`,
`B⁺ = O⁺(R)`, and `q : (B, B⁺) → (C, C⁺)` a quotient mapping to a complete Huber pair
over `(A, A⁺)`. Suppose `(C, C⁺)` has a standard
étale presentation `(n, H, k, π_c)` with **exact** lifts `w ∈ (B⁺)^n`,
`π_c(v_l) = q(w_l)`. Write `Y = Spa(C, C⁺)`, `g : Y → R`,
`E = B ⊗̂_A C`, and `p : Spa(E, E⁺) = R ×_X Y → R`; `E⁺` is the completed tensor pair's
plus ring. The scalar map is `B → E`, `b ↦ b ⊗ 1`, and the graph map on rings is
`E → C`, `b ⊗ c ↦ q(b)c`. Its equations are
`h_i = T_i ⊗ 1 − 1 ⊗ q(T_i)` for `1 ≤ i ≤ N`. Prove:

(a) There is a finite rational cover `{U_j}` of `R` such that each member is either disjoint
from `g(Y)`, or admits a rational `W_j ⊆ Spa(E, E⁺)` containing the graph over
`Y_j := g⁻¹U_j`, for which `p|_{W_j} : W_j → U_j` is an isomorphism of adic spaces,
inducing an isomorphism of complete Huber pairs. In particular the induced scalar map
`B_j := O(U_j) → D_j := O(W_j)` is an isomorphism; this is the scalar map used to transfer
the graph resolution.
The neighbourhood `W_j` lies in a graph tube over `C` for the integral equations `h_i`,
whose Jacobian in the `T` coordinates is the identity. Choose its radius small enough that
the rational inequalities defining `R ×_X Y` are preserved by translation from the graph.

Construct these comparisons by quantitative Newton iteration, not by restriction of scalars
along `B → E`. On sufficiently small rational neighbourhoods of `g(Y)`, impose
`H(w) ∈ ϖ^m O⁺(U_j)^n` and
`ϖ^k/det J_H(w) ∈ O⁺(U_j)`, with `m ≥ 2k + 1`; take `m` larger as needed for the finitely
many rational inequalities. These conditions hold on `Y` since `H(qw) = 0` and the standard
presentation bounds the inverse Jacobian. Newton supplies `r ∈ O⁺(U_j)^n` with `H(r) = 0`
and `r − w ∈ ϖ^{m−k}O⁺(U_j)^n`, hence a pair map `C → B_j`, `π_c(v) ↦ r`.
In `p⁻¹U_j`, the rational inequalities
`|v_l − w_l| ≤ |ϖ^{k+1}|` select this branch: both `v` and the image of `r` solve `H = 0`
in that congruence class, so [*restricted-power-series-newton*](../AdicEtaleGeometry/README.md) (AdicEtaleGeometry A3.2) identifies them. Thus this
branch projects isomorphically to `U_j`. Shrink it inside a graph tube, carrying the
shrinking across this isomorphism to `U_j`. The graph is retained because Newton
functoriality along the ambient pair map to `O(Y_j)` gives `q(r) = q(w)`.
The quotient-pair hypothesis identifies `g(Y)` with the closed vanishing set of `ker q`,
so rational subsets disjoint from it complete the cover. Compactness gives a finite cover.

(b) On every rational `V ⊆ U_j`, transfer the Koszul resolution of the graph equations
through `O(V) ≅ O((p|_{W_j})⁻¹V)`. Its quotient is
`C_V := O(g⁻¹V)`, with plus ring the integral closure of the image of `O⁺(V)`.
The equation ideal is closed, the quotient has its natural Hausdorff complete topology,
and the transferred resolution and its kernel give stably pseudocoherent modules over
`B_j`. These identifications commute with rational restriction: restrict `W_j` by the
inverse image under its isomorphism with `U_j`, use [*fs-iv-4-13-regular-sequence*](#p5-13-1) (P5.13.1) on that
rational subchart, and identify both quotient maps with the given map to `C_V`.
For members disjoint from `g(Y)`, the quotient module is zero and the kernel is `B_j`.

(c) Glue these quotient modules and their kernels as sheaves on `R`. Their identifications
with `g_*O_Y` and `ker(O_R → g_*O_Y)` fix the overlap maps. Apply
[*pseudocoherent-kiehl-gluing*](../AdicEtaleGeometry/README.md) (AdicEtaleGeometry A3.1) to these locally stably pseudocoherent modules, rather than
assuming that an algebraic tensor product of `C` is already complete. Global sections
are `C` and `I := ker q`, so both are stably pseudocoherent **B-modules**. For every rational
`V ⊆ R`, `B' = O(V)`, prove the algebraic comparisons

`0 → I ⊗_B B' → B' → C ⊗_B B' → 0, C ⊗_B B' ≅ C_V = B'/I B' ≅ C ⊗̂_B B'.`

The maps are multiplication and restriction, `I ⊗_B B'` identifies with the closed ideal
`ker(B' → C_V)`, and both algebraic tensor modules are Hausdorff complete for their natural
`B'`-module topologies. The quotient comparison is a homeomorphism; its plus ring is the
integral closure of the image of `O⁺(V)`. These assertions follow from gluing and rational
pseudoflatness after stable pseudocoherence has been obtained, and include the empty preimage.

This target supplies the analytic graph comparison underlying the étale-source case of
[FS] §IV.4.1, Lem. IV.4.14, p. 137, and Prop. IV.4.19, p. 140, using Newton iteration in place
of their spreading and differential arguments; the module passage is [KL16] §2.5,
Thm. 2.5.5 and Cor. 2.5.6, pp. 42–43. It does not require `E` to be finite or pseudocoherent
over `B`. *Needs:* [*restricted-power-series-newton*](../AdicEtaleGeometry/README.md) (AdicEtaleGeometry A3.2); [*standard-etale-presentation*](../AdicEtaleGeometry/README.md) (AdicEtaleGeometry A3.2);
[*standard-etale-locus-sousperfectoid*](#p5-13-1) (P5.13.1); [*tubular-neighbourhood*](#p5-13-1) (P5.13.1);
[*fs-iv-4-13-regular-sequence*](#p5-13-1) (P5.13.1); [*pseudocoherent-sheaf*](../AdicEtaleGeometry/README.md) (AdicEtaleGeometry A3.1); [*pseudocoherent-kiehl-gluing*](../AdicEtaleGeometry/README.md) (AdicEtaleGeometry A3.1);
[*rational-localisation-pseudoflat*](../AdicEtaleGeometry/README.md) (AdicEtaleGeometry A3.1); AdicSpacesPartII layer R0 (completed tensor pairs and
quotient pairs); P3.17a (rational sousperfectoid algebras and balls);
Tau Ceti `Pair.quotient`, `TauCeti.Huber.Pair.Hom.isClosedEmbedding_spaComap_quotientHom` and rational
perturbation invariance. README only (no Lean declaration).

**Checks.**

- *test_graph_comparison_nonfinite_ambient* — `K` a perfectoid field, `A = K⟨s⟩`,
  `C = K⟨s,s⁻¹⟩ = A⟨v⟩/(sv−1)`, `B = A⟨T⟩`, `q(T) = v`, `w = T`:
  `E = B⟨1/s⟩` is not finite over `B`. Indeed `B → E` is injective and `s` is a nonunit
  of `B`; integrality of `1/s` would make it a unit. The graph equation `T−v` over `E`
  has quotient `C`, whereas over `B` the resolution is
  `0 → B → B → C → 0`, with differential `sT−1`. On
  `U = {|sT−1| ≤ |ϖ|}`, both `s` and `T` have absolute value one; Newton gives the integral
  root `r = 1/s` and the branch `|v−T| ≤ |ϖ|` projects isomorphically onto `U`.
- *test_graph_comparison_section* — `C = A`, `R = B^N_X`, and `q(T_i) = a_i ∈ A⁺`:
  `E = B`, the projection comparison is the identity on a tube around the section,
  and the graph Koszul resolution is the one for `T_i−a_i`; it gives the original-base
  quotient and kernel after every rational restriction.
- *test_graph_comparison_empty* — on a rational `V` disjoint from `g(Y)`,
  `C ⊗_B O(V) = C_V = 0` and `I ⊗_B O(V) → O(V)` is an isomorphism;
  when `N = n = 0`, `C = A`, `R = X` and `q = id`, the comparison instead has zero kernel.

**Local presentations of a closed subspace from integral cut-offs and graphs; pseudocoherence of
its ideal.** (*integral-cutoff-graph-presentation*) Let `(A, A⁺)` be a complete Tate Huber pair
with `A` sousperfectoid, so that rational subsets of relative balls are sheafy, `X = Spa(A, A⁺)`,
`R ⊆ B^N_X` a rational subset with coordinates `T₁, …, T_N`, and `(C, C⁺)` a complete Huber pair
with a standard étale presentation `(n, F, k, π_v)` over `(A, A⁺)` in variables `v₁, …, vₙ`. Let
`g : Spa(C, C⁺) → R` be a morphism over `X`, i.e. a continuous `A`-algebra map `g* : O(R) → C`
with `g*(O⁺(R)) ⊆ C⁺`. Suppose given `w₁, …, wₙ ∈ O(R)`, not necessarily power-bounded, monic
polynomials `P_l(Z) ∈ O⁺(R)[Z]` and `M ≥ 1` such that (i) `c_l := g*(w_l)` satisfies
`c_l − π_v(v_l) ∈ ϖ·π_v(A₀⟨v⟩)` for a ring of definition `A₀ ⊆ A⁺`, and (ii)
`g*(P_l(w_l)) ∈ ϖ^{M+1}C⁺` for all `l`. Put `R'' := R ∩ ⋂_l {|P_l(w_l)| ≤ |ϖ^M|}` and
`Q_l := R ∩ {|P_l(w_l)| ≥ |ϖ^M|}`. Prove: (a) `{R''} ∪ {Q_l}` is a finite rational covering of
`R`, `g` factors through `R''` and `g⁻¹(Q_l) = ∅`; (b) `w_l ∈ O⁺(R'')` for all `l` — a monic
polynomial with bounded coefficients is large where its argument is; (c) `g* : O(R'') → C` is a
quotient mapping of complete Huber pairs, and for every rational `R''' ⊆ R''` the induced
`O(R''') → O(g⁻¹R''') = C ⊗̂_{O(R'')} O(R''')` is again one. Before substituting the lifts,
use [*perturbation-of-generators*](../AdicEtaleGeometry/README.md) (AdicEtaleGeometry A3.2) to replace `π_v` by `π_c = π_v ∘ θ`, `π_c(v_l) = c_l`,
and replace the equations by `H_l = θ⁻¹(F_l)`. The inverse coordinate substitution preserves
the inverse-Jacobian bound up to an integral unit, so the exponent `k` still works.
The exact lifts `w_l ∈ O⁺(R'')` of `c_l` then give the quotient mapping in (c):
`π_c` factors through `O(R'') → C`, and its plus image makes `C⁺` integral over the image
of `O⁺(R'')`. The transported equations satisfy `g*(H(w)) = 0`.
(d) Put `B = O(R'')`, `I = ker(B → C)`. Apply [*graph-neighbourhood-target-comparison*](#p5-13-2) (P5.13.2)
to this quotient and exact-lift presentation. It gives stable pseudocoherence of `C` and `I`
over `B`, and, for every rational `B → B' = O(R''')`, an exact sequence
`0 → I ⊗_B B' → B' → C ⊗_B B' → 0` of naturally Hausdorff complete modules,
with `C ⊗_B B' ≅ O(g⁻¹R''')` and `I ⊗_B B' ≅ ker(B' → O(g⁻¹R'''))`.
The intermediate quotient `B/closure(H(w))` admits a pair map from `C` by `v ↦ w` and
a retraction to `C`, but may be larger: for `n = 0`, `C = A` and `g` a section of `R → X`,
the equation list is empty. The graph comparison supplies the full ideal, including the
remaining ambient coordinates. (e) Hence the ideal sheaf
`I := ker(O_R → g_*O_{Spa C})` is a pseudocoherent sheaf on `R`, equal to `O_R` on each `Q_l`.
The integral cut-off, possible because plus rings of rational localisations are completed integral
closures ([KL15] §2.4, Lem. 2.4.13(a), p. 42), removes the boundary specialisations (points with
`|w| = 1⁺`) that otherwise prevent the image of `Y` from being closed; the graph argument replaces
Fargues–Scholze's local identification of an étale closed immersion ([FS] §IV.4.1, proof
of Prop. IV.4.19, p. 140). Quotient mappings of Huber pairs are `Pair.Hom.IsQuotientMapping`:
surjective and open, with target plus ring the integral closure of the image of the source plus
ring (Huber's quotient mappings of affinoid rings; between complete Tate rings openness follows
from surjectivity by the open mapping theorem, and the notion is the affinoid condition of [FS]
§IV.4.1, Prop. IV.4.19(i), p. 140). *Needs:* [*pseudocoherent-module*](../AdicEtaleGeometry/README.md) (AdicEtaleGeometry A3.1); [*stably-pseudocoherent-module*](../AdicEtaleGeometry/README.md) (AdicEtaleGeometry A3.1);
[*pseudocoherent-sheaf*](../AdicEtaleGeometry/README.md) (AdicEtaleGeometry A3.1); [*pseudocoherent-kiehl-gluing*](../AdicEtaleGeometry/README.md) (AdicEtaleGeometry A3.1); [*perturbation-of-generators*](../AdicEtaleGeometry/README.md) (AdicEtaleGeometry A3.2);
[*standard-etale-presentation*](../AdicEtaleGeometry/README.md) (AdicEtaleGeometry A3.2); [*standard-presentation-basic-pieces*](../AdicEtaleGeometry/README.md) (AdicEtaleGeometry A3.2);
[*graph-neighbourhood-target-comparison*](#p5-13-2) (P5.13.2); AdicSpacesPartII layer R0; P3.17a; Tau Ceti
`TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.mem_iff_forall_vle_one`, `ValuationSpectrum.rationalSubset`.

**Checks.**

- *test_identity_cutoff* (degenerate) — `N = n = 0`, `R = X`, `C = A` and `g = id`:

  A positive-dimensional ball `C = A⟨T₁,…,T_N⟩` is not étale over nonzero `A` for `N > 0`,

- *test_surjective_application* — in [*fs-iv-4-19-zariski-closed-char-p*](#p5-13-2) (P5.13.2): `g* : O(R) → C`

- *test_cutoff_transport_equations* — `A = C = K` a perfectoid field, `F(v) = v`,

  *test_graph_comparison_nonfinite_ambient*, with `P(Z) = Z−T` and any `M ≥ 1`:

- *quotient_identity*, *quotient_top*, *quotient_ideal* — the identity of a pair, the quotient by
  the unit ideal (zero ring, full plus ring) and every Tau Ceti quotient pair `Pair.quotientHom`
  are quotient mappings; the last is the agreement with Tau Ceti's `Huber.Pair.quotient`.
- *quotient_plus_too_big* (non-example) — the identity of a field `K` from `(K, K⁺₁)` to

  integral elements is integrally closed. The identity of `ℤ_p` from the discrete to the `p`-adic
  topology is continuous and bijective but not open, which the openness clause excludes.
  When formalised, the check specifies both topologies explicitly on the identity function and asserts
  continuity, bijectivity and failure of `IsOpenMap` for every prime `p`.

**Zariski closed immersions of affinoid étale perfectoid spaces into relative balls.**
(*fs-iv-4-19-zariski-closed-char-p*) Let `(A, A⁺)` be a perfectoid Tate pair, `X = Spa(A, A⁺)`,
`Y' ⊆ B^N_X` an open subspace which is a finite union of rational subsets (for instance a
rational subset or `B^N_X` itself; `Y'` is sousperfectoid and smooth over `X`), `Y` an affinoid
perfectoid space with an étale morphism `Y → X` ([ECD] Def. 6.2), and `g : Y → Y'` a morphism
over `X`. Prove that the following are equivalent: (i) `Y'` is covered by rational subsets
`V' ⊆ B^N_X` such that `V := g⁻¹(V')` is affinoid and `O(V') → O(V)` is a quotient mapping
(surjective, `O⁺(V)` the integral closure of the image of `O⁺(V')`); (ii) for every rational
subset `V' ⊆ Y'` the same holds ([FS] §IV.4.1, Prop. IV.4.19(i), p. 140; the passage (i) ⇒ (ii)
is Kedlaya–Liu's gluing, proof of Prop. IV.4.19, p. 140). If they hold, `g` is a Zariski closed
immersion ([FS] §IV.4.1, Def. IV.4.20, p. 141), and: (a) the ideal sheaf
`I_{Y⊂Y'} := ker(O_{Y'} → g_*O_Y)` is pseudocoherent ([FS] §IV.4.1, Prop. IV.4.19, p. 140); (b)
for every rational `V' ⊆ Y'`, `I(V')` is a stably pseudocoherent `O(V')`-module and
`O(V')/I(V') ≅ O(g⁻¹V')`, the *affine quotient description*, with plus ring the integral closure of
the image of `O⁺(V')`, the *plus-ring description*. The statement holds for
perfectoid `(A, A⁺)` of any characteristic; characteristic `p` is the case used in P5.13.4.
Fargues–Scholze prove IV.4.19 for smooth maps of sous-perfectoid spaces using the
diamond-dependent IV.4.15 and IV.4.17 and Kedlaya–Liu's gluing; here only the gluing is used,
together with [*integral-cutoff-graph-presentation*](#p5-13-2) (P5.13.2). *Needs:* [*pseudocoherent-sheaf*](../AdicEtaleGeometry/README.md) (AdicEtaleGeometry A3.1);
[*pseudocoherent-kiehl-gluing*](../AdicEtaleGeometry/README.md) (AdicEtaleGeometry A3.1); [*standard-etale-presentation*](../AdicEtaleGeometry/README.md) (AdicEtaleGeometry A3.2); [*integral-cutoff-graph-presentation*](#p5-13-2) (P5.13.2);
P3.17a; layer P3
(étale morphisms of perfectoid spaces); Tau Ceti `TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.mem_iff_forall_vle_one`,
`ValuationSpectrum.rationalSubset`.

The proposed Lean form states the ring-level equivalence on each
rational chart of the ball, and a companion gives every rational
restriction its quotient map, stably pseudocoherent kernel and homeomorphic quotient-ring
comparison; the quotient-map predicate includes the integral-closure condition on plus rings.
These are the affine assertions of [FS] IV.4.19, printed p. 140 (PDF page 140). README only (no Lean declaration).

  closure of `(tTᵢ − sᵢ)` and plus ring the completed integral closure ([KL15] §2.4,

**Affinoid étale perfectoid spaces have standard rational coverings by standard étale pieces.**
(*etale-standard-piece-cover*) Let `X = Spa(A, A⁺)` be an affinoid perfectoid space and

immersion into a space finite étale over an open of `X`) with `Y` affinoid perfectoid. Prove that
there are `σ₁, …, σ_m ∈ B` generating the unit ideal such that every
`V_j := Y(σ/σ_j) = {|σᵢ| ≤ |σ_j| for all i}` is `X`-isomorphic to a rational subset of an affinoid

every rational subset of `Y` contained in some `V_j` ([ECD] §6, proof of Prop. 6.4(ii), p. 28:
the reduction of qcqs étale maps to composites of rational subsets and finite étale maps; remark
after Def. 6.2, p. 26: composites and base changes of (finite) étale maps are (finite) étale).

`TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.exists_span_eq_top_forall_rationalSubset_subset_of_isTateRing`,

### P5.13.3 the closed embedding of an affinoid étale object


**Checks.**

- For a constant identity étale object the unit numerator gives one standard piece.

**Local plus-generators are approximated by elements integral over global plus elements and
ratios.** (*integral-approximation-of-generators*) Let `(B, B⁺)` be a complete Tate Huber pair
with pseudouniformiser `ϖ` (in P5.13.3 `B` is perfectoid or sousperfectoid); let
`σ₁, …, σ_m ∈ B` generate the unit ideal, `V := Y(σ/σ_j) ⊆ Y = Spa(B, B⁺)` and `ū ∈ O⁺(V)`.
Prove that for every `M ≥ 0` there are finitely many `β₁, …, β_r ∈ B⁺`; an element `z ∈ O⁺(V)`
with `z − ū ∈ ϖ^M O⁺(V)`; a monic polynomial `P(Z) = Z^d + Σ_{e<d} a_e Z^e` with `P(z) = 0` whose
coefficients `a_e` are polynomials in the ratios `σ₁/σ_j, …, σ_m/σ_j` with coefficients in
`ℤ[β₁, …, β_r]`; and `b ∈ B`, `s ≥ 0` with `b/σ_j^s − z ∈ ϖ^M O⁺(V)`
(`exists_integral_approx`). Since `O⁺(V)` is the closure of the integral closure of
`B⁺[σ/σ_j]` in `B[1/σ_j]` ([KL15] §2.4, Lem. 2.4.13(a), p. 42; Tau Ceti
`Huber.PairOfDefinition.completedPlusSubring`) and `ϖ^M O⁺(V)` is an open neighbourhood of `0`, an
element `z = b/σ_j^s` of that integral closure close to `ū` does it, with `P` its integral
equation; no uniformity of `B` is used. *Needs:* Tau Ceti
`Huber.PairOfDefinition.completedPlusSubring`, `Huber.PairOfDefinition.completionLocalization`,
`ValuationSpectrum.rationalSubset`.

**Checks.**

- *test_ratio_is_generator* — `B = K⟨X⟩` (`K` a perfectoid field of characteristic `p`),
  `σ = (X, ϖ)`, `j = 1`, `V = {|ϖ| ≤ |X|}`: `ū = ϖ/X` is itself the ratio `σ₂/σ₁`, with
  `P(Z) = Z − σ₂/σ₁` and `r = 0`.


**Checks.**

- For a global plus element, take that element itself and zero approximation error.
- For the zero element the integral polynomial and every ratio can be chosen zero.

**An affinoid étale perfectoid space is Zariski closed in a relative ball, with stably
pseudocoherent ideal.** (*affinoid-etale-zariski-closed-embedding*) Let `(A, A⁺)` be a perfectoid
Tate pair of any characteristic, `X = Spa(A, A⁺)`, and `f : Y = Spa(B, B⁺) → X` an étale
morphism of affinoid perfectoid spaces ([ECD] Def. 6.2). Prove that there are `N ≥ 0` and
`b = (b₁, …, b_N) ∈ (B⁺)^N` such that the `X`-morphism `g_b : Y → B^N_X`, `Tᵢ ↦ bᵢ`, is a Zariski
closed immersion in the sense of [*fs-iv-4-19-zariski-closed-char-p*](#p5-13-2) (P5.13.2) with `Y' = B^N_X`;
equivalently, `π_b : A⟨T₁, …, T_N⟩ → B`, `T ↦ b`, is surjective and `B⁺` is the integral closure
of `π_b(A⁺⟨T⟩)`, a quotient mapping; the ideal `I := ker π_b` is a stably pseudocoherent
`A⟨T⟩`-module; the ideal sheaf `Ĩ` on `B^N_X` is pseudocoherent; and for every rational
`V' ⊆ B^N_X`, `O(V')/I·O(V') ≅ O(g_b⁻¹V')` with plus ring the integral closure of the image. Any
enlargement `b' = (b, b'')` with `b'' ∈ (B⁺)^{N'}` has the same properties. When `(B, B⁺)` is
given with a standard étale presentation over a sousperfectoid base, the stable pseudocoherence
of its ideal `closure (F)` in `A⟨T⟩` is part of this target.
[ECD] §6, proof of
Prop. 6.4(iv), p. 28, asserts this closed immersion without constructing it, and affinoid
subdomains of non-noetherian adic spaces are not controlled in general ([KL15] §2.4, after
Def. 2.4.12, p. 41); the construction takes global coordinates — the `σᵢ` of
[*etale-standard-piece-cover*](#p5-13-2) (P5.13.2), a unit-ideal certificate `aᵢ`, the coefficients `β` of the monic
equations and the numerators `b` of the approximations of
[*integral-approximation-of-generators*](#p5-13-3) (P5.13.3) — forms the rational covering
`R₀ = {|h| ≥ |ϖ^{2c+1}|} ∪ {R''_j} ∪ {Q_{jl}}` of the whole ball from the integral cut-off, and
verifies the local-on-the-target condition of [FS] §IV.4.1, Prop. IV.4.19(i), p. 140, for it,
applying [*fs-iv-4-19-zariski-closed-char-p*](#p5-13-2) (P5.13.2) with `Y' = B^N_X` (Zariski closed immersions in the
sense of [FS] §IV.4.1, Def. IV.4.20, p. 141). *Needs:* [*stably-pseudocoherent-module*](../AdicEtaleGeometry/README.md) (AdicEtaleGeometry A3.1);

[*integral-approximation-of-generators*](#p5-13-3) (P5.13.3); P3.17a; Tau Ceti
`ValuationSpectrum.rationalSubset`, `Huber.restrictedMvPowerSeriesCompletion`.

`I/I² → C ⊗_B Ωᶜ_{B/A} → Ωᶜ_{C/A} → 0`, whose first map is `e ↦ 1 ⊗ de`.

### P5.13.4 finite-stage approximation and Scholze's Proposition 6.4(iv)

The tilting input is layers P1, P3 and P5: For a cofiltered system
`X_i = Spa(R_i, R_i⁺)` of affinoid perfectoid spaces with limit `X = Spa(R, R⁺)`, the tilts form a
cofiltered system of affinoid perfectoid spaces of characteristic `p` with limit `X^♭`, with
`R^{♭+}/ϖ^♭ = R⁺/ϖ = colim R_i⁺/ϖ` (layer P1,

(*cofiltered-limit-presentation-approximation*) In the situation of layer P5

described by approximation of `R⁺` modulo every `ϖ^M` through monotone directed images); the
same holds for the numerators and denominator of a rational subset of `B^N_X`, and for `M` large

étale presentation of `(C_i, C_i⁺)` over `(R_i, R_i⁺)` and `Y_i := Spa(C_i, C_i⁺)` is affinoid

coordinate formula, for any morphism of complete Tate pairs), and `Y_i ×_{X_i} X = Spa(R⟨T⟩/closure(φ_i(F_i)), integral closure)` as perfectoid spaces, the fibre product with `X` ([ECD] §6, Prop. 6.4

and `F'_i ∈ R_i⁺⟨T'⟩^{N−1}` with `φ_i(F'_i) ≡ F'` modulo `ϖ^{m₀}`

**The Zariski closed immersions of this layer are strongly Zariski closed.**
(*zariski-closed-immersion-ecd-comparison*) Let `(A, A⁺)` be a perfectoid Tate pair of
characteristic `p`, `X = Spa(A, A⁺)`, `Y = Spa(B, B⁺)` affinoid perfectoid étale over `X` and
`b ∈ (B⁺)^N` as in [*affinoid-etale-zariski-closed-embedding*](#p5-13-3) (P5.13.3). Let
`B^{N,perf}_X := Spa(A⟨T₁^{1/p^∞}, …, T_N^{1/p^∞}⟩, A⁺⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩)` be the perfectoid relative
ball and `g^perf : Y → B^{N,perf}_X` the map `T_i^{1/pⁿ} ↦ b_i^{1/pⁿ}`. Prove that `g^perf`, the
closed embedding of P5.13.3 composed into the perfectoid ball, is strongly Zariski closed in the
sense of [ECD] §5, Def. 5.7(ii), p. 24, directly: `A⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ → B` is surjective, its image
containing the image of `A⟨T⟩`, which is `B`; `B⁺` is the integral closure of the image of
`A⁺⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩` (it is the integral closure of the smaller image of `A⁺⟨T⟩`, and the roots
`bᵢ^{1/pⁿ}` lie in `B⁺`); and `A⁺⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ → B⁺` is almost surjective, i.e. `ϖ^{1/pⁿ}B⁺` lies
in the image for every `n`: the image is open, so it contains `ϖ^c B°` for some `c`, and it is
perfect (the source plus ring is integrally closed in the perfect source ring, hence closed
under the unique p-th roots), so with `b ∈ B⁺` and
`ϖ^c b^{pⁿ} ∈ image` also `ϖ^{c/pⁿ}b ∈ image`. These are the two forms in which strong Zariski
closedness is used ([ECD] §5, Def. 5.7(ii) and Thm. 5.8: surjectivity on the rings with the plus
ring the integral closure of the image, and almost surjectivity on the plus rings); in particular
`g^perf` is a Zariski closed immersion ([ECD] 5.7(i)). The proof
of [*affinoid-etale-finite-stage-6-4-iv*](#p5-13-4) (P5.13.4) does not use [ECD] Thm. 5.8 (Zariski closed implies
strongly Zariski closed), which is not an input of this roadmap: the closed immersions it needs
are into the sousperfectoid ball `B^N_X` and are constructed as quotient mappings
(*affinoid-etale-zariski-closed-embedding*), and the transfer between characteristics is done on
étale categories (P3’s [*etale-site-tilting-equivalence*](#p3-20) (P3.20) and P5’s [*completed-colimit-is-perfectoid*](#p5-2) (P5.2)), not on Zariski closed immersions.
*Needs:* [*affinoid-etale-zariski-closed-embedding*](#p5-13-3) (P5.13.3); P3.17a; PerfectoidSpaces
layer P1.

`Huber.Pair.Hom.quotientMapping_perfect_extension_charP` applies to the extension of the
ball quotient map to the perfectoid ball: any pair map extending that quotient is again
a quotient mapping and is almost surjective on plus rings.
`Huber.Pair.Hom.almost_surjective_of_quotient_charP` states the general ring-level implication:
for each compatible root `ϖ^(1/p^n)` and each integral target element its product lies in
the image of the source plus ring. These are the conditions of [ECD] 5.7(ii), printed p. 24. README only (no Lean declaration).

**Checks.**

- *ambient_perfect_not_plus_perfect* — in the perfection of `𝔽₂(t)`, let
  `B = 𝔽₂[t^(1/2^∞)]` and `S = 𝔽₂ + tB`. The integral closure of `S` is `B` and
  `tB ⊆ S`, but the unique square root `t^(1/2)` is absent from `S`. Thus an ambient
  perfect ring and a conductor bound do not suffice without integral closure of the source plus ring.
- *test_almost_surjective_of_perfect* — if the source plus subring is integrally closed in a
  perfect characteristic-p ring and `ϖ^c S⁺` lies in its image, taking p-power roots inside
  that subring gives the bounded lifts used in the argument. Perfectness of the ambient
  ring alone does not assert perfectness of an arbitrary subring.
- *test_rational_strongly_closed* — `Y = X(s/t)`: `g^perf` identifies `Y` with the Zariski closed
  subset `V(t^{1/pⁿ}T^{1/pⁿ} − s^{1/pⁿ} : n)` of the perfectoid ball, which is strongly Zariski
  closed.


#### Examples for analytic approximation

The worked examples of the layer run along its build. A rational subset `Y = X(s/t)` descends to
`X_i(s_i/t_i)` for approximations `s_i, t_i` of `s, t` (Tau Ceti's perturbation of rational
subsets, `exists_mem_nhds_forall_rationalSubset_eq_of_sub_mem`), and its closed embedding is
`Tᵢ ↦ sᵢ/t` with ideal the closure of `(tTᵢ − sᵢ)` ([*affinoid-etale-zariski-closed-embedding*](#p5-13-3) (P5.13.3),
[*finite-stage-approximation-char-p*](#p5-13-4) (P5.13.4)). For a finite étale `Y`, the model from an approximated
monic presentation agrees with [ECD] 6.4(i) of layer P5. The tube of
`e = T − a` on `B¹_X` is the translation `{|T − a| ≤ |ϖ|} ≅ B¹(|ϖ|)` (*tubular-neighbourhood*),
and the perturbation of `(T − a)` to `(T − a')` with `a ≡ a' mod ϖ²` gives the identity of `A`
(*standard-presentation-perturbation*). `F = T^p − a` in characteristic `p` is rejected by the
Jacobian condition, `J_F = 0`, and a nonempty such locus is not étale ([*standard-etale-presentation*](../AdicEtaleGeometry/README.md) (AdicEtaleGeometry A3.2),
[*jacobian-criterion-char-p*](#p5-13-2) (P5.13.2)). Over `ℚ_p⟨T⟩`, strongly noetherian, the pseudocoherent theory
reduces to Kiehl's coherent theory (AdicSpacesPartIII layer R3, Kiehl's theorem on Tate affinoids;
[*pseudocoherent-kiehl-gluing*](../AdicEtaleGeometry/README.md) (AdicEtaleGeometry A3.1)) and pseudoflatness to flatness
(*rational-localisation-pseudoflat*). The applications in [ECD] are those recorded under
[*affinoid-etale-finite-stage-6-4-iv*](#p5-13-4) (P5.13.4): in the proof of Lemma 7.18, affinoid étale covers descend
to a finite level of a tower; in the proof of Lemma 7.11(i), composites of affinoid pro-étale
maps are formed via Proposition 7.10 and 6.4(iv). Alongside these sit the non-examples that fix
the definitions: the finitely presented but not 2-pseudocoherent `R/xR` over
`k[x, y₁, y₂, …]/(x·yᵢ)`, the strictly but not stably pseudocoherent quotient `A/fA` of [KL16]
Ex. 2.4.2, the non-pseudoflat `ℚ_p⟨T⟩/(T)`, the pushforward `j_*O_U` that is not pseudocoherent,
the dilation `X ↦ ϖX` that is no automorphism of `A⟨X⟩`, and the non-integral equation `(T/p)²`
for which the tube theorem fails.

**Checks.**

- For the identity object use the zero-dimensional ball and zero ideal.

### Characteristic maps and computations

The ring used for P5.1 is P1's `Perfectoid.completedFilteredColimit p D j₀ ϖ`;
`completedColimit` denotes that ring here and does not introduce another completion type.
`Perfectoid.plusDiagram` remembers the **chosen** plus rings. Inside the P1 ring,
`completedColimitPlus` is the topological closure of their images and
`completedColimitPair` equips the ring with that plus ring. The ring's Tate, completeness,
Hausdorff and perfectoid instances are those of P1. The comparison
`completedColimit.plusCompletionEquiv`, characterized by `plusCompletionEquiv_ι`, identifies
this subring with the adic completion of the chosen integral colimit.
`completedColimit.integralPerfectoid` states regularity and the Frobenius quotient
isomorphism, assuming `ϖ^p ∣ p` in the chosen stage plus ring. Its topology is specified
by `completedColimit.hasBasis_nhds_zero`. The construction uses the chosen `R_i⁺`
at every stage. These identifications use [ECD] Proposition 6.5, p. 29.
`compatible_pseudouniformizer_map` carries the plus-ring root system, its divisibility
condition and its topologically nilpotent unit along each transition; on the category
over the chosen stage these images form the compatible system.

On a tail, choose actual compatible elements `t_j ∈ R_j⁺`, with
`φ_a(t_i) = t_j` and `t_j₀ = ϖ`. `completedColimit.quotientDiagram` is the functor
`j ↦ R_j⁺/(t_j^n)`. `plusQuotientEquiv` identifies its ring colimit with `R⁺/(ϖ^n)` for
`n > 0`; `plusQuotientEquiv_ι` sends the class of a stage element to the class of its canonical
image. This is the finite-quotient statement, with the distinguished element fixed before
passing to the colimit ([Bhatt] Lemmas 5.1.1–5.1.2, pp. 33–34; [Stacks] Tag 05GG).
`adicCompletion_kernel_divisible`, `adicCompletion_separatedQuotient` and
`adicCompletion_rootClosed` state the nonseparated completion arguments; the last assumes
`q > 1`, regularity of `t`, and root closure in `A[1/t]`.
`adicCompletion_localized_density` specifies the principal neighbourhood basis after
inverting `t` and proves density of the canonical map from `A[1/t]`.
`NormedAffinoidSystem` specifies complete nonarchimedean norms defining the stage
 topologies, with the chosen plus rings as unit balls and submetric transition maps.
`ringDiagram` retains the structural ring maps. `colimitSeminorm_apply` specifies the
infimum over all representatives, and `NormedColimit` is its Hausdorff completion.
`completedColimit_test_compatibility_sch12` identifies this completion with the adic
completed colimit when the common pseudouniformizer multiplies every norm by the
same number in `(0,1)` ([Sch12] Lemma 6.13, p. 37; [KL15] Definition 2.6.1 and
Remark 2.6.3, p. 53). The comparison agrees with every stage map.

**Checks.** For each of `ringDiagram`, `NormedAffinoidSystem`, `colimitSeminorm`,
and `NormedColimit`, `_zero` gives the zero ring and zero seminorm; `_terminal`
computes the seminorm at a terminal stage and recovers that complete stage;
`_killed` makes an element killed by a transition have zero class and seminorm.

The global declarations use P2's `PerfectoidSpace.Perfd`, `IsAffinoidPerfectoid`,
`globalSections` and `globalPlus`. In `PerfectoidSpace.cofilteredLimit`, `cone` and `isLimit`
specify the limit in that category; `homeomorph_apply` specifies the compatible tuple of
points, and `pairIso_π` identifies the projections with the maps induced by
`completedColimit.ι`. `baseChangeDiagram` uses the actual pullbacks over `Over i`;
`baseChangeHomeomorph_apply` fixes every coordinate of its homeomorphism.
`sectionsDiagram` and `plusSectionsDiagram` use actual pullback homomorphisms.
`globalSections_of_isCardinalFiltered` and `globalPlus_of_isCardinalFiltered`, together with
their `_ι` equations, identify the uncompleted ring colimits when `Iᵒᵖ` is `ℵ₁`-filtered
([ECD] Proposition 6.5, p. 29).
`globalPlusQuotientDiagram` uses compatible global integral sections `t_i`; on every
stage chart their values must be pseudouniformizers. `cofilteredLimit.plusQuotient_ι`
fixes the quotient comparison on every stage section. `cofilteredLimit.globalPlusCompletion`
gives the integral completion comparison, again fixed on every stage section. Applying it
to the rational base-change diagram supplies the completed plus-ring formula in P5.4.
`integral_sections_completion_extension` fixes the image of the adic element;
`integral_sections_localization_extension` gives the unique extension after inverting it;
`integral_sections_chart_continuous` and `integral_sections_localized_continuous` give
continuity on every affinoid chart, with the principal topology explicitly specified.

For a cofiltered diagram `S` of finite profinite sets, `profiniteFunctionDiagram` uses
precomposition on continuous functions. `cofilteredLimit_prodProfinite` identifies its
space limit with the affinoid of continuous functions on `limit S`, and its `_π` equation
identifies each projection with `profiniteProjectionMap`. The underlying topology is fixed
by `continuousFunctionSpaceHomeomorph`; its `_eval` equation sends the point obtained by
evaluation at `s` and a point `x` of the coefficient affinoid to `(s,x)` ([Sch13] end of the
proof of Lemma 4.6, p. 25; [ECD] Proposition 6.5, p. 29).

`tateColimit_spectrum` states the general Tate-pair result without perfectoidness,
completeness or injectivity of the stages. Its input includes compatible open rings of
definition `A_{j,0} ⊆ A_j⁺`, a compatible pseudouniformizer, and the principal-adic topology
on each `A_{j,0}`. `TateColimitModel` carries a Tate pair and a specified ring equivalence to Mathlib's algebraic ring colimit. The theorem fixes
the plus ring, the neighbourhood basis, the canonical ring maps, the homeomorphism and
finite-stage rational descent. Completion of this spectrum uses the existing Tau Ceti
completion homeomorphism ([KL15] Remark 2.6.3, p. 53; [Wedhorn] Proposition 7.48, p. 68).
`cofilteredLimit.rational_descent` states rational descent for the completed perfectoid pair.
`cofilteredLimit.finite_qcOpen_cover` descends a finite cover by compact opens as a cover
at one common stage, including the empty-cover case when the limit is empty.
The independent spectral statements are `spectralLimit_qcOpen`,
`spectralLimit_constructible`, `spectralLimit_eventual_inclusion` and
`spectralLimit_eventual_clopen`, with a specified limit cone and spectral transition maps
([Stacks] Tags 0A30 and 0A2Y).

`Perfectoid.countablePerfectoidSubrings p R ϖ` is precisely the poset `𝒮(R)` of P5.6:
closed subrings containing `ϖ` and its inverse, perfectoid for their subspace topology,
with a countable dense subset. `countableSubring_powerBounded` identifies its power-bounded
subring with the inverse image of `R°`. `countablePerfectoidHull` additionally contains the specified
countable subset and every chosen root. The directedness, covering and cardinal assertions
are `countablePerfectoidSubrings_directed`, `_cover`, `_card` and
`_isCardinalFiltered`. `countableSubringPair` takes the inverse image of the ambient plus
ring; `countableSubringDiagram`, `countableSubringCocone` and `countableSubringIsColimit`
specify the pair presentation. The projection identity of the countable-subring limit isomorphism
fixes the global comparison on all projections. `cofilteredLimit.card_colimit_lt` bounds the uncompleted integral colimit.
`cofilteredLimit.card_lt` retains one common strong-limit
stage bound `κ' < κ`; it does not infer such a bound from separate inequalities `|R_i| < κ`
([ECD] Proposition 6.5, p. 29, for the countable-subring presentation; Proposition 6.4, last clause
and first paragraph of the proof, p. 27, and Lemma 4.1, pp. 19–20, for the cardinal bounds).

`CategoryTheory.FilteredTwoColimit` uses Mathlib's localization of
`Pseudofunctor.Grothendieck F` at arrows whose fibre component is invertible.
`HomRepresentative` carries a stage, two legs and a morphism between the transported
objects. Its relation compares two representatives after a common refinement, including
the pseudofunctor's composition isomorphisms. `homEquiv_symm_mk` identifies the representative
with the composite of the two transport isomorphisms and the stage morphism.
`ι_obj`, `ι_map`, `ιCompIso_id`, `ιCompIso_comp` and `ιCompDescIso_coherence` fix the
inclusions and their coherence. A cocone is Mathlib's `Pseudofunctor.StrongTrans` to the
constant diagram. `descUniqueIso` fixes its comparison isomorphisms before asserting
uniqueness. `equivOfFinal_ι` specifies reindexing, and `fullSubcategory` restricts to a family
of full subcategories stable under transitions ([KL15] Remark 1.2.9, p. 15;
[Berkeley] Remark 7.4.7, p. 54). `fpModuleDiagram` uses
`Module.FinitePresentation` and Mathlib's extension of scalars, with comparison
`fpModuleColimitEquiv_ι` ([Stacks] Tag 05N7).

The geometric pseudofunctors are `finiteStageFiniteEtaleDiagram`, `finiteStageQcqsDiagram`
and `finiteStageSeparatedDiagram`. For every small category `I`,
diagram `X : I ⥤ Perfd p`, stage `i` and object in the indicated slice,
`finiteStageFiniteEtaleDiagram_mapId_hom_app`,
`finiteStageQcqsDiagram_mapId_hom_app` and
`finiteStageSeparatedDiagram_mapId_hom_app` identify the unit component
with `Over.pullbackId`, after transport by `X.map_id`. For arrows
`a : j → i` and `b : k → j`,
`finiteStageFiniteEtaleDiagram_mapComp_hom_app`,
`finiteStageQcqsDiagram_mapComp_hom_app` and
`finiteStageSeparatedDiagram_mapComp_hom_app` identify the composition
component with `Over.pullbackComp (X.map b) (X.map a)`, after transport by
`X.map_comp b a`. Thus the component goes from direct pullback to successive
pullbacks and preserves the projection to the original object. The
2-morphism action is equality transport. The equivalences to the limit
categories additionally require a cofiltered index and affinoid perfectoid
stages ([ECD] Proposition 6.4(i)–(iii), pp. 27–28). Their three equivalences,
ending in `Equiv`, have `_ι`
isomorphisms identifying each stage functor with geometric base change.
`finiteStage_faithfulness`, `_fullness`, `_essentialSurjectivity`, `_separatedness`,
`_surjectivity` and `_isomorphism` state recognition with qcqs hypotheses on the actual
étale slice objects. `finiteStagePullbackIso_fst` fixes the iterated pullback used in the
fullness formula ([ECD] Proposition 6.4(i)–(iii), pp. 27–28).

**Checks for the constructions and maps.** Each name below is a Check specified in this README
only, to become a Lean `example`.
The Checks above also give worked examples of these constructions.

| Construction or map | Check names and discriminating computations |
| --- | --- |
| General Tate colimit carrier | `tateColimitModel_zero`: a zero algebraic colimit forces a zero model; `tateColimitModel_nonzero`: a nonzero colimit cannot have a zero model; `tateColimitModel_terminal`: a terminal index gives a bijective canonical ring map. |
| Contracting disc diagram | `contractingDisc_one_step`: the coordinate maps to `ϖT`; `contractingDisc_two_steps`: it maps to `ϖ²T`; `contractingDisc_constants`: the scalar `ϖ` remains fixed; `completedColimit_test_not_injective`: the nonzero coordinate dies in the completion and the completed pair is `(K, K°)`; `completedColimit_proper_plus`: it is not isomorphic to `(K, K⁺)` when `K⁺ ⊊ K°`. |
| Completed pair, plus ring and inclusions | `completedColimit_test_initial`: a terminal ring index gives an isomorphism; `completedColimit_test_const`: the constant diagram recovers the original pair and each inclusion; `completedColimit_test_zero_terminal`: a zero terminal ring gives the zero plus ring and zero completed ring; `completedColimit_test_profinite`: the first binary coordinate gives a nontrivial idempotent, evaluating to `0` and `1` on the two constant sequences; `uncompleted_cylinders_dense_proper`: the cylinder subring is dense and not closed. |
| Universal map of completed pairs | `completedColimit_lift_identity`: the canonical cocone induces the identity; `completedColimit_lift_terminal`: the lift of a map from a terminal stage restricts to that map; `completedColimit_lift_zero`: every value is zero for a zero target. |
| Quotient diagram | `quotientDiagram_zero`: exponent zero gives the zero ring; `quotientDiagram_unit`: a unit gives the zero ring at every exponent; `quotientDiagram_zero_element`: for positive exponent and zero distinguished element, the quotient map is bijective. |
| Continuous-function pair | `continuousFunctions_empty`: the empty source gives the zero ring; `continuousFunctions_point`: evaluation at the unique point is bijective; `continuousFunctions_two_points`: evaluation gives the product of two copies of the coefficient ring. |
| Binary cylinder diagram | `binaryFunctions_zero_coordinates`: the zeroth stage is one copy of the coefficient ring; `binaryFunctions_one_coordinate`: the next stage is two copies; `binaryFunctions_two_terms`: the transition from one digit to two evaluates the original function on the first digit. |
| Global limit and projections | `cofilteredLimit_test_initial`: the initial stage is the limit; `cofilteredLimit_test_const`: every projection of a constant system is its canonical isomorphism; `cofilteredLimit_test_empty_stage`: a diagram with an empty stage has an empty limit; `cofilteredLimit_test_profinite`: the binary function diagram gives the continuous-function affinoid. |
| Limit lift | `cofilteredLimit_lift_identity`: the limit cone lifts by the identity; `cofilteredLimit_lift_two_terms`: for `1 → 0`, the lift is the component at `1` followed by the inverse stage comparison; `cofilteredLimit_lift_empty`: two cones with specified empty vertex have the same induced map. |
| Base change | Identity: base change of the identity gives the limit; empty: an empty source stays empty; split: a split degree-two cover gives two copies of the limit. |
| Rational restriction | `rationalLimit_empty`: an empty rational domain gives the empty limit; `rationalLimit_whole`: the whole domain gives an isomorphism; `rationalLimit_clopen`: a clopen rational domain remains clopen in the limit. |
| Countable-subring poset | `countableSubrings_separable_top`: a separable ambient ring is its largest member; `countableSubrings_nonseparable_top`: a nonseparable ring is not a member; `countableSubrings_zero`: the zero ring has exactly one member; `countableSubrings_countable_union`: a countable family has a common upper bound; `countableSubrings_nonseparable_no_countable_cofinal`: no countable family is cofinal in the nonseparable case; `countableSubrings_no_countable_tower`: no completed colimit of any countable filtered diagram of separable perfectoid pairs can be a nonseparable pair. |
| Categorical colimit | `filteredTwoColimit_test_const`: a constant discrete Boolean fibre has singleton endomorphism sets and no morphisms between its two objects; `filteredTwoColimit_empty`: empty fibres give an empty colimit; `filteredTwoColimit_bool`: the two objects of a constant discrete Boolean fibre have no cross-morphism; `filteredTwoColimit_test_discrete`: the colimit is equivalent to the discrete category on the set colimit, and a stage element maps to its canonical image; `filteredTwoColimit_test_finitelyPresentedModules`: the comparison is extension of scalars; `filteredTwoColimit_test_notNaive`: an isomorphism first acquired at stage `1` survives. |
| Finite étale diagram coherence | `finiteStageFiniteEtaleDiagram_identity_projection`: the unit is the first pullback projection; `finiteStageFiniteEtaleDiagram_two_steps`: the composition component preserves the projection through both stages in their specified order; `finiteStageFiniteEtaleDiagram_nontrivial_automorphism`: a nonidentity automorphism changes the unit component. |
| Qcqs diagram coherence | `finiteStageQcqsDiagram_identity_projection`: the unit is the first pullback projection; `finiteStageQcqsDiagram_two_steps`: successive pullbacks preserve the projection to the original object; `finiteStageQcqsDiagram_nontrivial_automorphism`: a nonidentity automorphism changes the unit component. |
| Separated diagram coherence | `finiteStageSeparatedDiagram_identity_projection`: the unit is the first pullback projection; `finiteStageSeparatedDiagram_two_steps`: successive pullbacks preserve the projection to the original object; `finiteStageSeparatedDiagram_nontrivial_automorphism`: a nonidentity automorphism changes the unit component. |
| Coherent transport | `transport_empty_unique`: empty fibres give the unique natural comparison; `transport_bool_false`: transport fixes the Boolean object `false`; `transport_automorphisms`: transport is the identity after the constant comparison even in the one-object category with automorphism group `Perm Bool`. |
| Cocone extension | `desc_empty_unique`: the empty-fibre colimit has one functor to a fixed category; `desc_bool_collapse_not_full`: collapsing the two Boolean objects is not full; `desc_bool_identity`: fixing both Boolean objects induces an equivalence. |
| Global quotient diagram | `globalPlusQuotient_zero_exponent`: exponent zero gives zero; `globalPlusQuotient_unit`: a unit gives zero at every exponent; `globalPlusQuotient_zero_section`: the quotient by a positive power of zero retains every section. |
| Profinite function diagram | `profiniteFunctions_empty_stage`: the empty stage gives zero; `profiniteFunctions_singleton_stage`: evaluation gives the coefficient ring; `profiniteFunctions_two_point_stage`: two evaluations give its square. |
| Profinite product | `profiniteProduct_empty`: the product has no points; `profiniteProduct_point`: a singleton recovers the coefficient affinoid; `profiniteProduct_two_points`: two points give its binary coproduct. |
| Full subdiagrams | `fullSubdiagram_empty`: empty full subcategories give an empty colimit; `fullSubdiagram_whole`: all objects of the constant Boolean category recover that category; `fullSubdiagram_singleton`: retaining only `false` gives a category equivalent to the one-point category. |
| Cospan morphisms | `cospan_constant_empty_hom`: no representative connects the two distinct Boolean objects; `cospan_constant_identity`: constant point fibres give a singleton quotient; `cospan_constant_automorphisms`: the quotient recovers the original Hom set, including its automorphisms. |
| Finitely presented module category | `fpModules_zero_ring`: every module over the zero ring is zero; `fpModules_rank_one`: the free rank-one module is finitely presented; `fpModules_infinite_basis`: a countably infinite free module over a nonzero ring is not finitely presented. |
| Étale subcategories | `etaleSubcategories_empty`, `etaleSubcategories_identity`, `etaleSubcategories_split`: the empty arrow, identity and split degree-two arrow belong to both the qcqs and the qc separated subcategories. |
| Detection boundaries | `finiteStage_identity_detection`: in a constant affinoid diagram, pullback to the limit detects whether an arbitrary étale morphism is an isomorphism; `finiteStage_empty_detection`: a map from an empty space to a nonempty space is not surjective. |
| Separatedness and isomorphism detection | `finiteStage_glued_not_separated`: gluing two copies along a nonclosed open gives a nonseparated fold; `finiteStage_glued_becomes_iso`: restriction to the gluing domain makes the fold an isomorphism; `finiteStage_glued_proper`: the original fold is not an isomorphism if the gluing domain is proper. |
| Cantor digit function | `cantorDigits_zero`: the all-zero sequence has value zero; `cantorDigits_singleton`: the sequence supported at `n` has value `p^n` in `ℂ_p`; `cantorDigits_zero_locus`: only the all-zero sequence vanishes, also for `p = 2`; `finiteStage_nonflat_quotient`: its principal quotient of `C(S,ℂ_p)` is not flat; `finiteStage_punctured_cantor`: the complement of the zero sequence is open, noncompact, and not pulled back from any finite coordinate set; `finiteStage_quotient_no_descent`: no algebra over a finite-coordinate product of fields base-changes to this principal quotient; `finiteStage_punctured_cantor_space`: the actual open perfectoid subspace is étale, not quasicompact, and is not the preimage of any subset at a finite stage. |
| Failure of faithfulness without quasicompactness | `finiteStage_nonqc_faithfulness`: over the contracting perfected-disc tower there are two maps with nonquasicompact étale source which agree over the limit and disagree at every finite stage. |

### Examples

The worked examples of this layer are the profinite set `S = lim_n {0,1}^n` over a perfectoid field
`K`, run through every construction: `R⁺ = C^0(S, O_K)` and `R = C^0(S, K)` as the completed direct
limit of the `K^{S_n}`, with `R⁺/ϖ^n` the locally constant functions to `O_K/ϖ^n`, the function
`s ↦ Σ_k s_k ϖ^k` outside every finite stage, and the uncompleted `LC(S, K)` as the non-example; the
limit space `S × Spa(K, O_K)` with underlying space `S × |Spa(K, O_K)|`, its restriction to a clopen
`C × Spa(K, O_K)`, the base change `S × Y_0` of a finite étale `Y_0`, the Cantor-set open `S ∖ {s}`
and the non-quasicompact `X ∖ ({s₀} × Spa(K, O_K))` that do not descend, and finite étale, qcqs
étale and quasicompact separated étale spaces over `S × Spa(K, O_K)` being locally constant on `S`;
the non-injective system `R_n = K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩` with `T^{1/p^m} ↦ ϖ^{1/p^m}T^{1/p^m}`, where `ι_0(T) = 0`
and `colim R_n⁺ → R⁺ = O_K` is neither injective nor, for the profinite system, surjective; the
residue-field limit `Spa(K(x), K(x)⁺) = lim_{U ∋ x} U` with `|Spa(K(x), K(x)⁺)| = ⋂ U`; the
non-perfectoid tower `Spa(ℚ_p(p^{1/p^n}), ℤ_p[p^{1/p^n}])`, excluded from the construction;
`C^0({0,1}^{ℵ₁}, ℂ_p)` with its cofinal countably generated subrings `C^0({0,1}^J, ℂ_p)`;
`|C^0({0,1}^ℕ, ℂ_p)| = 2^{ℵ₀}` below every cutoff cardinal; the discrete, constant, finitely
presented module and non-naive 2-colimits; the finitely presented non-flat `C^0(S, K)/(f)` that comes
from no finite stage; and the glued non-separated `Y_1` over `{|T| ≤ |ϖ|}` that becomes separated
over `{|T| ≤ |ϖ|^2}`.

Layer P5 carries no Lean `example` in `Suggested.lean`; its Checks are the computations above.

### Dependencies

## Layer P6: `κ`-small perfectoid spaces and pro-étale morphisms

The layer builds the size and the pro-étale notions on which the pro-étale and v-sites of
DiamondsAndVStacks rest. It defines `κ`-small and uniformly `κ`-small perfectoid spaces for an
uncountable strong limit cardinal `κ`, proves the cover criterion with its uniform bound for
singular `κ`, and proves closure under open subspaces, finite disjoint unions and tilting,
and closure of uniformly `κ`-small spaces under fibre products. It also
records the finite-stage form of ECD Proposition 6.4(iv). It then defines affinoid pro-étale
morphisms as cofiltered limits of affinoid étale ones, pro-étale morphisms as their local form,
and the product `X × S` of an affinoid perfectoid space with a profinite set; proves that
`X_proét^aff` is the pro-category of the affinoid étale site, with its `κ`-bounded refinement; and
proves the stability of (affinoid) pro-étale morphisms under composition, base change,
cancellation, sections and small limits, that Zariski closed immersions and diagonals are
pro-étale, and the comparison with Scholze 2013's affinoid perfectoid objects. Throughout, a
perfectoid space is one of layer P2 (P2.10), locally `Spa(R, R⁺)` for a perfectoid Tate pair in
the sense of ECD Definition 3.1, with no perfectoid base field; étale morphisms are those of layer
P3 (P3.15, ECD Definition 6.2); cofiltered limits of affinoid perfectoid spaces are those of layer
P5 (P5.3).

### P6.1 `κ`-small perfectoid spaces

The first five subsections concern `κ`-small perfectoid spaces: the definition, its uniform variant,
the cover criterion, the closure properties and the finite-stage descent of affinoid étale objects.

**`κ`-small perfectoid spaces.** (*kappa-small-perfectoid-space*) Fix a cardinal `κ` with `ℵ₀ < κ`
that is a strong limit (`2^λ < κ` for every cardinal `λ < κ`); every cutoff cardinal of
[ECD] Lemma 4.1, pp. 19–20, is one, and since Mathlib's
`Cardinal.IsStrongLimit` counts `ℵ₀` as a strong limit, `ℵ₀ < κ` is a separate hypothesis. A
perfectoid space `X` (layer P2 (P2.10): an adic space locally isomorphic to `Spa(R, R⁺)` for a
perfectoid Tate pair `(R, R⁺)` in the sense of ECD Definition 3.1, with no perfectoid base field)
is `κ`-small if (i) its underlying set `|X|` has cardinality `#|X| < κ`, and (ii) for every open
affinoid perfectoid subspace `U = Spa(A, A⁺) ⊆ X` (so `A = O_X(U)`) the ring `A` has cardinality
`#A < κ`. Cardinalities are those of underlying sets; the plus rings carry no condition; clause
(ii) quantifies over all open affinoid subspaces, of which there are at most `2^{#|X|} < κ`, so no
separate count of charts is imposed; neither clause implies the other (a one-point space with a
large field; a disjoint union of `κ` points). The predicate is invariant under isomorphism and
monotone in `κ`; the bound in (ii) is not uniform over the charts, the stronger notion with a
single bound `λ < κ` being P6.2, and for quasicompact `X` the two agree. In `PerfectoidSpace`,
define `IsKappaSmall` as the structure `IsKappaSmall κ X` with the two clauses, with projections
`IsKappaSmall.card_lt` (`#|X| < κ`) and `IsKappaSmall.card_sections_lt` (`#O_X(U) < κ` for every
open affinoid perfectoid `U ⊆ X`); prove transport along `X ≅ Y`,
`IsKappaSmall.mono` (`κ ≤ κ'` carries `κ`-small to `κ'`-small), `IsKappaSmall.restrict` (open subspaces
of `κ`-small spaces are `κ`-small) and `IsKappaSmall.empty`
(for `1 < κ`); define
`KappaSmall`, the full subcategory of perfectoid spaces on the `κ`-small objects, with
the instance `KappaSmall.essentiallySmall`; the affinoid form `IsKappaSmall_affinoid κ (R, R⁺)`
is stated for an arbitrary Huber ring `R` by the three clauses `#Spa(R, R⁺) < κ`, `#R < κ` and
`#R⟨T/s⟩ < κ` for every presentation with `T` generating the unit ideal. For general Huber
rings this is a cardinal predicate, with no assertion that `R` is the ring of global sections.
For perfectoid `R`, such presentations give a rational basis, and for uncountable strong limit `κ`
these clauses are equivalent to the two clauses above and to `#R < κ` alone (P6.3 (d)). The predicate
and its monotonicity are meaningful for all cardinals; uncountability and the strong-limit
condition are hypotheses of the comparison and closure theorems. For `κ`-small `X`,
`X_proét,κ` is the category of `κ`-small perfectoid spaces pro-étale over `X` (ECD Definition 8.1),
on which the sites of
DiamondsAndVStacks layer D2 live ([ECD] §4, Def. 4.2, p. 20; [ECD] §4, after Def. 4.2, p. 20, for
the standing hypothesis on `κ`; [ECD] §8, Def. 8.1, p. 39). *Needs:* layer P2 (P2.10, P2.9); layer P1 (P1.1); Mathlib `Cardinal.IsStrongLimit`, `Cardinal.mk`,
`Cardinal.mk_set`, `CategoryTheory.EssentiallySmall`.

**Checks.**

- Computation: for every cardinal `κ` with `ℵ₀ < κ` and `κ` a strong
  limit, `Spa(C_p, O_{C_p})` is `κ`-small: it has one point and `#C_p = 2^ℵ₀ < κ`.
- Degenerate: the empty perfectoid space has zero points and a
  one-element section ring, so it is `κ`-small exactly when `1 < κ`, including `κ = ℵ₀`.
- At cutoff `2` the empty perfectoid space is small, and every nonempty perfectoid space is
  excluded: an affinoid perfectoid neighborhood of a point has at least two sections.
- Boundary: no affinoid pair
  satisfies the cardinal predicate at `κ = 0` or `κ = 1`; the zero ring satisfies it at `κ = 2`.
- `not_isKappaSmall_Cp_aleph0` (non-example) — `Spa(C_p, O_{C_p})` is not `ℵ₀`-small.
- Strict boundary: for a Huber pair over `R`, `κ`-smallness
  and `κ ≤ κ'` imply `κ'`-smallness, but the pair is never `#R`-small: equality with
  the section-ring cardinal is excluded by the strict bound, including for the zero ring.
- Characterisation: for an affinoid perfectoid space
  `X = Spa(A, A⁺)`, `IsKappaSmall κ X ↔ #A < κ`.
- `not_isKappaSmall_bigField` (non-example) — for `K` the completion, for the Gauss norm, of the
  perfection of `F_p((t^{1/p^∞}))(x_β : β < κ)`, a perfectoid field with `#K ≥ κ`, `Spa(K, K°)` has
  one point but is not `κ`-small: clause (i) does not imply clause (ii).
- `not_isKappaSmall_sigma` (non-example) — the disjoint union of `κ` copies of `Spa(C_p, O_{C_p})`
  is not `κ`-small, although each open affinoid subspace (a finite union of copies) has ring of
  cardinality at most `2^ℵ₀` (equal to `1` for the empty open): clause (ii) does not imply
  clause (i).

The global predicates use `Perfd`, its underlying pre-adic space and its affinoid perfectoid opens
(P2.10), together with `ofPair` from P2–P4.
`IsKappaSmall.card_sections_lt` measures the ring of sections over each open affinoid perfectoid
subspace, so different presentations of an open do not change the condition. The cardinal `κ`
lives in the universe `u` of the spaces and their section rings (`κ : Cardinal.{u}`), so no lifting
of cardinalities is needed. Global versions of the first, second and fourth Checks are stated on
`Perfd`; Lean examples state the strictness boundary at `0`, the empty-space cutoffs `1` and `2`,
and the exclusion of nonempty spaces at `2`.

**Checks for the full subcategory.**

- `kappaSmall_inherited_maps` — the Hom type between two `κ`-small objects is exactly the Hom
  type between their underlying perfectoid spaces, including noninvertible maps.
- `kappaSmall_empty_object` — the empty space is an object precisely above the threshold `1`.
- `kappaSmall_excludes_Cp_aleph0` — no object at cutoff `ℵ₀` has underlying space `Spa(C_p,O_Cp)`.

For the large-field Check, construct `GaussPerfectoidField K J` and `gaussPerfectoidField K J`:
a complete perfectoid field with maximal plus ring, an isometric map from `K`, and independent
variables `t_{j,n}` satisfying `t_{j,n+1}^p=t_{j,n}`. Require the Gauss maximum-coefficient norm
on every finite polynomial level and density of the subfield generated by the constants and all
`t_{j,n}`. These equations specify the completion of `K(t_j^{1/p^∞})`; the map on constants
and the variables determine every continuous map out of it. Counting rational expressions and
Cauchy sequences gives `#J ≤ #L ≤ (#K+#J+ℵ₀)^ℵ₀` (the completion estimate of [ECD] Remark 4.3,
p. 20, applied to this dense field).

**Checks for the Gauss field.**

- `gaussField_empty_variables` — for `J=∅`, the map `K → L` is bijective.
- `gaussField_two_terms` — for one variable, `‖a+b t₀‖=max(‖a‖,‖b‖)`.
- `gaussField_distinct_variables` — with two variables, `t_{false,0} ≠ t_{true,0}`.
  Thus the lower cardinal bound counts distinct field elements, even in characteristic two.

Lean: `PerfectoidSpace.IsKappaSmall` (fields `card_lt` and `card_sections_lt`, over the affinoid
perfectoid opens), `IsKappaSmall.mono`, `IsKappaSmall.restrict`.

### P6.2 uniformly `κ`-small perfectoid spaces

**Uniformly `κ`-small perfectoid spaces.** (*uniformly-kappa-small-perfectoid-space*) Let `κ` be an
uncountable strong limit cardinal. A perfectoid space `X` is uniformly `κ`-small if there is a
cardinal `λ < κ` such that `#|X| ≤ λ` and `#O_X(U) ≤ λ` for every open affinoid perfectoid
subspace `U ⊆ X`; equivalently, `X` is `κ'`-small (see *kappa-small-perfectoid-space*) for some cardinal
`κ' < κ` (take `κ' = λ⁺`, which is `< κ` because `κ` is a limit cardinal). Properties: (a)
uniformly `κ`-small implies `κ`-small; (b) a quasicompact `κ`-small perfectoid space is uniformly
`κ`-small, so the two notions have the same affinoid and the same qcqs objects; (c) if `κ` is regular
(a strongly inaccessible cardinal) the two notions agree; (d) they differ for every singular `κ`
(take `cf κ` summands), in particular for every `κ` of cofinality `ω₁` such as the cutoff
cardinals `κ(µ)` with `cf µ = ω₁` constructed in the proof of ECD Lemma 4.1:
`⊔_{α<ω₁} Spa(K_α, K_α°)`, with perfectoid fields `K_α` whose cardinalities are `< κ` and
cofinal in `κ` (for infinite `λ < κ` the completed perfection of `𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞}))(x_β : β < λ)` has
cardinality between `λ` and `2^λ < κ`), is `κ`-small (`ℵ₁ ≤ 2^{ℵ₀} < κ` points, finite products of
the `K_α` as affinoid rings) and not uniformly `κ`-small. The uniformly `κ`-small spaces
satisfy the cover criterion and the stability under fibre products that ECD Proposition 4.4 states
for `κ`-small spaces (P6.3, P6.4); ECD's own set-theoretic statements (Proposition 6.4, Lemma 11.22)
are formulated with such a uniform bound `κ' < κ`, and the class is intended for the cutoff
cardinals of [ECD] Lemma 4.1, pp. 19–20, which are in general singular. In
`PerfectoidSpace`, define `IsUniformlyKappaSmall` as the predicate
`∃ λ < κ, #|X| ≤ λ ∧ ∀ U, #O_X(U) ≤ λ`, `U` ranging over the affinoid perfectoid opens; prove the
reformulation `IsUniformlyKappaSmall κ X ↔ ∃ κ' < κ, IsKappaSmall κ' X`,
`IsUniformlyKappaSmall.isKappaSmall` (a), and the statements for (b) (quasicompact `κ`-small spaces
are uniformly `κ`-small) and (c) (the two notions agree for regular `κ`), the affinoid criterion
`IsUniformlyKappaSmall κ (Spa(A, A⁺)) ↔ #A < κ`, `IsUniformlyKappaSmall.isOpen` (open subspaces,
with the same `λ`) and `IsUniformlyKappaSmall.fibreProduct` (P6.4) ([ECD] §6, Prop. 6.4, final
sentence, p. 27; [ECD] §4, proof of Lem. 4.1, p. 20, for `cf κ(ω₁) = ω₁ < κ(ω₁)`, the singular
cutoff of the separating example). *Needs:* *kappa-small-perfectoid-space*;
*complete-tate-ring-cardinality*; layer P2 (P2.8, P2.3); layer P1; Mathlib `Cardinal.iSup_lt_of_lt_cof_ord`, `Cardinal.IsRegular`, `Cardinal.mk_iUnion_le`.

**Checks.**

- Computation: `Spa(C_p⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, O_{C_p}⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩)` is
  uniformly `κ`-small with `λ = 2^ℵ₀` for every uncountable strong limit `κ`.
- Degenerate: the empty perfectoid space is uniformly `κ`-small with
  `λ = 1`: its point set is empty and its ring of sections on the empty affinoid open is the zero
  ring, whose underlying set has one element. For arbitrary cutoffs it is uniformly `κ`-small
  exactly when `1 < κ`; Lean examples accept it at `2` and reject it at `1`.
- Every nonempty perfectoid space fails uniform smallness at cutoff `2`, since uniform
  smallness implies smallness; a Lean example mirrors this boundary.
- Characterisation: for a quasicompact
  perfectoid space `X`, `IsUniformlyKappaSmall κ X ↔ IsKappaSmall κ X`.
- `not_isUniformlyKappaSmall_of_cof_omegaOne` (non-example) — for `κ` with `cf κ = ω₁` and
  perfectoid fields `K_α` (`α < ω₁`) with `#K_α < κ` cofinal in `κ`, `⊔_{α<ω₁} Spa(K_α, K_α°)` is
  `κ`-small and not uniformly `κ`-small.

**Completion cardinality.** (*first-countable-completion-cardinality*)
P6.2 owns `completion_cardinality_bound`: for `G : Type u` with `AddGroup G`,
`UniformSpace G`, `IsUniformAddGroup G`, `T2Space G` and `FirstCountableTopology G`,
a dense subset `A ⊆ G` with `#A ≤ λ` and `ℵ₀ ≤ λ` gives
`#(UniformSpace.Completion G) ≤ λ^ℵ₀`, all cardinals in universe `u`.
Commutativity and completeness of `G` are not required. This is the sequence argument
of [ECD] Remark 4.3, p. 20. DiamondsAndVStacks D0.24 consumes this theorem and
uses cardinal arithmetic to conclude `λ^ℵ₀ ≤ 2^λ < κ` for `λ < κ` and strong-limit `κ`.

The cardinal bounds behind the uniform notion are ring-theoretic
(*complete-tate-ring-cardinality*). Let `A` be a complete Hausdorff Tate ring (Tau Ceti
`IsTateRing`, with its topology complete and separated). (a) If `D ⊆ A` is a dense subset
with `#D ≤ λ` for an infinite cardinal `λ`, then `#A ≤ λ^ℵ₀ ≤ 2^λ`: apply
`completion_cardinality_bound` below to the additive group of `A` (Hausdorffness is needed, else limits of sequences are not
unique; completeness is not needed for (a), only for the setting of (b)). Prove: (b) with `λ_A := #A + ℵ₀`: (b1) for a rational subset `U = R(T/s)` of `Spa(A, A⁺)` the
rational localisation `A⟨T/s⟩` (Tau Ceti `completionLocObj`) has cardinality `≤ λ_A^ℵ₀`, the image
of `A[1/s]` being dense; (b2) a finite étale `A`-algebra `B` with its canonical topology has
`#B ≤ λ_A`, being a quotient of some `Aⁿ`; (b3) for morphisms of complete Tate pairs `A → B` and
`A → C`, the completed tensor product `B ⊗̂_A C` (AdicSpacesPartII R0.3
(*completed-tensor-product*)) and its
uniformisation (AdicSpacesPartII R0.4 (*uniform-completed-tensor-product*)) have cardinality `≤ (#B·#C·ℵ₀)^ℵ₀`, the image of `B ⊗_A C` being dense;
(c) if `κ` is an uncountable strong limit, the bound in (a) is `< κ` when `λ < κ`;
the bounds in (b1)–(b2) are `< κ` when `#A < κ`, and those in (b3) when both `#B < κ`
and `#C < κ`. The
localisation, finite étale and completed tensor clauses (b) are this target's; the first
countability needed here holds because the `ϖⁿA₀` form a countable basis of neighbourhoods
of `0` (Tau Ceti `IsPseudoUniformizer.hasBasis_nhds_zero`) ([ECD] §4, Rem. 4.3, p. 20, for (a);
[ECD] §4, proof of Prop. 4.4, pp. 20–21, for (b1)). *Needs:* *first-countable-completion-cardinality*; Tau Ceti
`TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing`, `TauCeti.Huber.IsPseudoUniformizer.hasBasis_nhds_zero`,
`TauCeti.Huber.PairOfDefinition.completionLocObj`; AdicSpacesPartII R0.3, R0.4
(*completed-tensor-product*, *uniform-completed-tensor-product*);
Mathlib `FirstCountableTopology`, `UniformSpace.Completion`, `Cardinal.power_mul`,
`Cardinal.power_le_power_right`.

The proposed Lean ring bounds are `rationalLocalization_cardinality`, `finiteAlgebra_cardinality`
and `completedTensor_cardinality`. The tensor statement uses the supplied adic scalar maps;
continuous maps from a Tate base are adic. The finite-algebra bound only requires a finite module.

Lean: `PerfectoidSpace.IsUniformlyKappaSmall`, `IsUniformlyKappaSmall.isKappaSmall`,
`completion_cardinality_bound` (*first-countable-completion-cardinality*).

### P6.3 the cover criterion for `κ`-smallness

**Cover criterion for `κ`-smallness.** (*kappa-small-cover-criterion*) Let `κ` be an uncountable
strong limit cardinal and `X` a perfectoid space. Prove: (a) if `X` is `κ`-small, then `X` is
covered by fewer than `κ` open affinoid subspaces `Spa(A, A⁺)` with `#A < κ` (namely by all of
them: there are at most `2^{#|X|} < κ`); (b) if `X` has a cover `{U_j = Spa(A_j, A_j⁺)}_{j∈J}` by
open affinoid subspaces with `#A_j < κ` for all `j`, then every open affinoid subspace
`U = Spa(A, A⁺) ⊆ X` has `#A < κ` (the sheaf condition embeds `A` into a finite product
of rings of rational subspaces of the cover charts), so such an `X` is `κ`-small as soon as `#|X| < κ`; (c) if moreover
`#J < κ` and `sup_j #A_j < κ` — automatic when `J` is finite, or when `#J < cf κ` — then
`#|X| < κ`, and `X` is `κ`-small, indeed uniformly `κ`-small (see *uniformly-kappa-small-perfectoid-space*);
(d) in particular an affinoid perfectoid space `Spa(A, A⁺)` is `κ`-small iff `#A < κ`, and a
quasicompact perfectoid space is `κ`-small iff it has a finite cover by open affinoid subspaces whose
rings have cardinality `< κ`; (e) the converse of (a) as printed in ECD Proposition 4.4 — a cover by
fewer than `κ` open affinoids with rings of cardinality `< κ`, without a uniform bound, implies
`κ`-small — holds for regular `κ` and can fail as soon as `cf κ ≤ #J < κ`: for `κ` of cofinality `ω₁` (such
as the cutoff cardinal `κ(ω₁)` of the proof of ECD Lemma 4.1) and perfectoid fields `K_α`,
`α < ω₁`, with `#K_α < κ` cofinal in `κ`, the disjoint union of the perfectoid discs
`Spa(K_α⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, K_α°⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩)` is covered by `ω₁ < κ` open affinoids with rings of
cardinality `< κ` and has at least `κ` points. Part (c) needs the uniform bound, and (e) records
exactly where the printed statement needs it. These are the affinoid criterion (in Lean
`isKappaSmall_presentationLimit_iff`: for uncountable strong limit `κ`, `Spa(A, A⁺)` of a perfectoid
pair is `κ`-small iff `#A < κ`) and the cover statement (a cover by open affinoids with `#A_j < κ` and
`#|X| < κ` gives `κ`-small) of P6.1 ([ECD] §4, Prop. 4.4, p. 20, the printed statement, whose correct parts are (a)–(d); [ECD]
§4, proof of Prop. 4.4, p. 20, for (b) and for the step that needs `sup_j #A_j < κ`; [ECD] §4,
proof of Prop. 4.4, p. 21, for the embedding into a finite product in (b)). A countable disjoint
union of copies of `Spa(C_p, O_{C_p})` is `κ`-small for every cutoff `κ` by (c) (`#J = ℵ₀ < cf κ`).
*Needs:*
*kappa-small-perfectoid-space*; *uniformly-kappa-small-perfectoid-space*;
*adic-spectrum-cardinality*; *complete-tate-ring-cardinality*; layer P2 (P2.10, P2.9, P2.8,
P2.3); layer P1; Tau Ceti
`TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.spectralSpace_spa_of_pairOfDefinition`; Mathlib
`Cardinal.iSup_lt_of_lt_cof_ord`, `Cardinal.mk_iUnion_le`, `Cardinal.mk_set`.

The point count behind (a) and (c) is the following (*adic-spectrum-cardinality*). Let `A` be a
Huber ring and `A⁺ ⊆ A` a subring, with no hypothesis on `A⁺` or on the topology. Prove that
`#Spa(A, A⁺) ≤ 2^{#A·#A}`: a point of `Spv A` is determined by its valuative relation
`{(a, b) ∈ A × A : |a(x)| ≤ |b(x)|}` (Tau Ceti `ValuationSpectrum.ext'`), so `Spa(A, A⁺) ⊆ Spv A`
injects into the power set of `A × A`; for `A` infinite this is `2^{#A}`. Consequently, if `κ` is
an uncountable strong limit and `#A < κ` then `#Spa(A, A⁺) < κ`, and a perfectoid space covered by
open affinoids `Spa(A_j, A_j⁺)`, `j ∈ J`, has at most `#J · sup_j 2^{#A_j·#A_j}` points ([ECD] §4,
proof of Prop. 4.4, p. 20, the injection into the binary relations on `A` and the bound
`2^{#A·#A}`). *Needs:* Tau Ceti `TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum`, `TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.ext'`,
`TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.spa`; Mathlib `Cardinal.mk_set`, `Cardinal.mk_prod`,
`Cardinal.mul_eq_self`, `Cardinal.mk_le_of_injective`, `Cardinal.mk_iUnion_le`.

**Check: `not_isKappaSmall_gaussDisc_sigma`.** Let `κ` be a strong limit with
`cf κ = ℵ₁ < κ`, let `L` be a characteristic-`p` perfectoid field with `#L < κ`, and
choose infinite variable sets `J_α` for `α < ω₁` with `#J_α < κ` cofinal in `κ`.
For `K_α = (gaussPerfectoidField p L J_α).field`, the theorem supplies compatible
pseudouniformizer roots and takes the discs on `discPair`. Each disc ring has
cardinality `< κ`; the `ω₁` coproduct inclusions are open immersions and cover the
coproduct. Its point set has cardinality at least `κ`, so it fails `IsKappaSmall`.
Indeed, characteristic `p` supplies compatible roots for every integral field element,
whose evaluations give distinct disc points. The Gauss field cardinal bounds make
the stage sizes cofinal. This is the negative control for the converse printed in
[ECD] Proposition 4.4, pp. 20–21, using the completion estimate of Remark 4.3, p. 20.
This coproduct Check is specified in this README only.
