### P6.4 closure properties of `κ`-small perfectoid spaces

**Closure properties of `κ`-small perfectoid spaces: open subspaces, disjoint unions, fibre
products.** (*kappa-small-closure*) Let `κ` be an uncountable strong limit cardinal. Prove: (a) an
open subspace of a `κ`-small (resp. uniformly `κ`-small) perfectoid space is `κ`-small (resp. uniformly
`κ`-small) (`IsKappaSmall.isOpen`, `IsUniformlyKappaSmall.isOpen`); (b) a disjoint union
`⊔_{j∈J} X_j` is uniformly `κ`-small if `#J < κ` and all `X_j` are `κ'`-small for one `κ' < κ`; finite
disjoint unions of `κ`-small spaces are `κ`-small; (c) (ECD Proposition 4.4, 'in particular') for
morphisms `X → Z ← Y` of perfectoid spaces with `X` and `Y` uniformly `κ`-small (`Z` arbitrary, not
necessarily `κ`-small), the fibre product `X ×_Z Y` (layer P2 (P2.16), over a general perfectoid
Tate base, with affinoid charts given by the uniform completed tensor product) is uniformly
`κ`-small (`IsUniformlyKappaSmall.fibreProduct`): if `#|X|, #|Y| ≤ λ` and all open affinoid rings of
`X` and `Y` have cardinality `≤ λ` (`λ ≥ ℵ₀`), then `X ×_Z Y` is covered by at most `2^λ` open
affinoids `U ×_W V` with rings of cardinality `≤ λ^ℵ₀` and has at most `2^{2^λ}` points; in
particular fibre products of `κ`-small quasicompact (for instance affinoid) perfectoid spaces are
`κ`-small. When `X`, `Y` and `Z` are all affinoid, their fibre product is affinoid. Affinoidness is
not asserted over an arbitrary base: gluing two copies of a perfectoid closed disc along its
non-quasicompact open unit disc gives two affinoid charts whose fibre product is that open disc; (d) for `κ` of
cofinality `ω₁` the unrestricted statement fails: for a perfectoid field `L` of characteristic `p`
with `#L < κ`, and perfectoid fields `K_α ⊇ L` (`α < ω₁`) that are completed perfections of
`L(x_β : β < λ_α)` for the Gauss norm, with infinite `λ_α ≥ #L` cofinal below `κ`, `X := ⊔_α Spa(K_α, K_α°)` is `κ`-small but
`X ×_{Spa(L, L°)} X` is not, since `Spa(K_α ⊗̂_L K_α)` has at least `λ_α` points: the
Gauss-isometric automorphisms obtained by permuting the variables give distinct graph points ([ECD] §4,
Prop. 4.4, p. 20, for (c) with the hypotheses under which it holds; [Berkeley] Lecture 8,
Prop. 8.2.5(3), p. 59, for the fibre products whose size (c) bounds). Part (d) shows that ECD's
'stable under finite products' needs the uniform or quasicompact hypothesis for singular `κ`.
*Needs:*
*uniformly-kappa-small-perfectoid-space*; *kappa-small-cover-criterion*;
*adic-spectrum-cardinality*; *complete-tate-ring-cardinality*; layer P2 (P2.16, P2.13); layer P1;
AdicSpacesPartII R0.4 (*uniform-completed-tensor-product*).

**Checks for small fibre products.**

- For `κ`-small affinoid perfectoid `X → Z` with affinoid perfectoid `Z`,
  `X ×_Z Z ≅ X` is `κ`-small and affinoid.
- For `κ`-small affinoid perfectoid `X = Spa(A,A⁺)` and `Y = Spa(B,B⁺)` over
  affinoid perfectoid `Z = Spa(C,C⁺)`, the completed-tensor presentation of P2.16
  gives an affinoid `κ`-small `X ×_Z Y`.
- Let `K` be a characteristic-p perfectoid field with `#K < κ`. Its perfected
  projective line `X`, obtained by gluing the perfected closed discs with rings
  `K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩` and `K⟨T^{-1/p^∞}⟩` along the perfected unit annulus, is
  quasicompact and `κ`-small. Laurent coefficients give `Γ(X,O) = K`, while zero
  and infinity are distinct points, so `X` is not affinoid. With
  `Y = Z = Spa(K,K°)`, the fibre product `X ×_Z Y ≅ X` remains non-affinoid.

**Check: `not_isKappaSmall_gaussField_fibreProduct`.** Under the same strong-limit,
cofinality, characteristic and variable-cardinality hypotheses as the disc Check,
the theorem constructs the scalar maps from `(L,L°)` into the Gauss field pairs and
uses their induced coproduct map `f : X → Spa(L,L°)`. The space
`X = ⊔_{α<ω₁} Spa(K_α,K_α°)` is `κ`-small, whereas `pullback f f` has at least `κ`
points and fails `IsKappaSmall`. Permutations of the infinite variable set `J_α`
give at least `#J_α` distinct graph points in each diagonal component. The scalar
maps are required to equal the Gauss construction's maps on constants. The Check,
specified in this README only, retains both the small source and its non-small self-fibre product.
This tests the finite-product assertion of [ECD] Proposition 4.4, p. 20, in the
slice over `Spa(L,L°)`; it applies also at `p = 2`.

Tilting preserves `κ`-smallness (*kappa-small-tilting*). For a perfectoid Tate ring `A` with tilt
`A♭` (layer P1), prove `#A♭ ≤ (#A)^ℵ₀` and `#A ≤ (#A♭)^ℵ₀·ℵ₀`, the tilt being the inverse limit
along `x ↦ x^p`. Consequently, for an uncountable strong limit `κ` and a perfectoid space `X` with
tilt `X♭` (layer P2 (P2.11)), `X` is `κ`-small iff `X♭` is `κ`-small (tilting invariance of `IsKappaSmall`), and
`X` is uniformly `κ`-small iff `X♭` is; tilting restricts to an equivalence between `κ`-small perfectoid
spaces over a perfectoid space `S` and `κ`-small perfectoid spaces over `S♭`; no base field, any
characteristic ([ECD] §3, after Lem. 3.10, p. 16); so the diamond `Spd` of DiamondsAndVStacks layer D6
keeps `κ`-small objects `κ`-small. *Needs:* layer P1 (P1.27); layer P2 (P2.11, P2.2); *kappa-small-perfectoid-space*;
*uniformly-kappa-small-perfectoid-space*; Mathlib `Cardinal.power_le_power_right`.

For every uncountable strong limit `κ` and every `X : Perfd p`,
`kappaSmallSliceTilt` restricts P2's `sliceTiltFunctor p X` to the full subcategories
whose source spaces are `κ`-small; the base `X` need not be `κ`-small.
The tilting invariance of `IsKappaSmall` identifies the object predicates, and its isomorphism
invariance ensures that the inverse equivalence also preserves them.
`kappaSmallSliceTilt_obj` identifies its underlying object with
`(sliceTiltFunctor p X).obj Y.obj`, and `kappaSmallSliceTilt_map` identifies its
underlying morphism with `(sliceTiltFunctor p X).map f.hom`, under these same
cardinal hypotheses ([ECD] Corollary 3.20, p. 19; Definition 4.2 and the cardinal
estimate in Remark 4.3, p. 20; Lemma 3.10, p. 16).

**Checks.**

- `kappaSmallSliceTilt_object` sends a specified arrow `Y → X` with `κ`-small source
  to the arrow obtained by applying `tiltFunctor`.
- `kappaSmallSliceTilt_morphism` sends the map in a commuting triangle to its
  image under `tiltFunctor`, including triangles between distinct objects.
- `kappaSmallSliceTilt_identity` sends `X → X` to `X♭ → X♭` when `X` is `κ`-small.

Every affinoid perfectoid space is the cofiltered limit of its `κ`-small perfectoid sub-pairs, the
`κ`-bounded form of ECD Proposition 6.5 (*kappa-small-perfectoid-subpairs*). Let `(S, S⁺)` be a
perfectoid Tate pair (ECD Definition 3.1, no base field) with a pseudouniformiser `ϖ` such that
`ϖ^p` divides `p` in `S°`, and let `A ⊆ S` be a subset. Prove that there is a closed subring
`S' ⊆ S` containing `A ∪ {ϖ, ϖ^{-1}}` with `#S' ≤ (#A + ℵ₀)^ℵ₀` such that, with the subspace
topology, `S'` is a perfectoid Tate ring, `S'° = S' ∩ S°`, and `(S', S' ∩ S⁺)` is a perfectoid Tate
pair. Consequently, for an uncountable strong limit `κ` and a morphism
`Y = Spa(S, S⁺) → X = Spa(R, R⁺)` of affinoid perfectoid spaces with `#R < κ`, the set `P_κ(Y/X)`
of closed subrings `S' ⊆ S` of cardinality `< κ` that contain the image of `R` and for which
`(S', S' ∩ S⁺)` is a perfectoid Tate pair, ordered by inclusion, satisfies: (a) it is directed, and
every subfamily of cardinality `≤ λ` whose members have cardinality `≤ λ`, for an infinite
`λ < κ` with `#R ≤ λ`, has an upper bound of cardinality `≤ λ^ℵ₀`. Including `#R` in this
bound also covers the empty subfamily;
in particular it is `ω₁`-directed whenever `cf κ > ω`, as for every cutoff cardinal (ECD
Lemma 4.1 (ii)), but not for `κ = ℶ_ω` when `#S ≥ ℶ_ω`: a countable family of members with
cardinalities below and cofinal in `ℶ_ω` has no upper bound in `P_κ(Y/X)`; (b) `⋃ S' = S` and
`⋃ (S' ∩ S⁺) = S⁺`; (c)
`Y = lim_{S' ∈ P_κ(Y/X)} Spa(S', S' ∩ S⁺)` in perfectoid spaces over `X`, a cofiltered limit of
`κ`-small affinoid perfectoid spaces over `X` whose colimit of plus rings is already complete. For
countable `A` this is P5.6 (every affinoid perfectoid space is an `ω₁`-cofiltered limit of
topologically countably generated ones), of which this is the `κ`-bounded form. For singular `κ` and `#S ≥ κ`, `P_κ(Y/X)` is not `κ`-directed: a family of size `cf κ`
with sizes cofinal in `κ` has no upper bound. If `#S < κ`, it instead has the largest member `S`.
The general directedness statement in (a) uses a uniform bound
([ECD] §6, proof of Prop. 6.5, p. 29, the countable case, whose sub-pair construction is made
explicit and bounded by `κ`; [ECD] §8, proof of Prop. 8.2, p. 39, the `κ`-bounded form used in
DiamondsAndVStacks layer D2 for cutoff-independence, where (a) states the directedness that holds).
*Needs:* layer
P1 (P1.1); layer P5 (P5.3); *kappa-small-perfectoid-space*; *kappa-small-cofiltered-limits*; Tau
Ceti `TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing`, `TauCeti.Huber.powerBoundedSubring`,
`TauCeti.Huber.isIntegrallyClosedIn_powerBoundedSubring`; Mathlib `Subring.topologicalClosure`.

**Checks for the subpair poset `KappaSubpairs` and for disjoint unions.**

- `kappaSubpairs_top` — if `#S<κ`, the whole subring `S` is the greatest member.
- `kappaSubpairs_empty_family` — for the identity `R → R`, no member can have cardinality
  at most `λ<#R`, even when the family to be bounded is empty.
- `kappaSubpairs_cofinal_sequence` — if a sequence of members has sizes cofinal in `κ`
  (in particular the `ℶ_ω` example), no single member bounds that sequence.
- `kappaSubpairs_two_members` — two members have a common upper bound under the stated
  uncountable strong-limit and base-ring bounds.
- `sigmaPoints_empty`, `sigmaPoints_singleton`, `sigmaPoints_two_components` — geometric
  coproducts have respectively zero points, the original space, and disjoint images of the two
  component inclusions. The homeomorphism `sigmaPoints` sends the image of `x∈X_j` to `(j,x)`.

`KappaSubpairs` is a subtype of the subrings of `S`, ordered by inclusion. Its conditions
are closedness, containment of the image of `R`, the cardinal bound, and existence of a perfectoid
pair mapping homeomorphically onto that closed subring, with plus ring the inverse image of `S⁺`.
The topology and plus ring are induced from `S`. The singular disjoint-union Check is also stated for any small index
set of size `<κ` whose field cardinalities are cofinal in `κ`; this includes the `ω₁` case above.

`exists_small_closed_perfectoid_subpair` states the closed subring construction with the
pseudouniformizer and its inverse included. `KappaSubpairs.diagram` uses the chosen embedded

`KappaSubpairs.isLimit` gives its universal property. `plusDiagram`, `plusCocone` and
`plusIsColimit` identify the uncompleted integral colimit with `S⁺`.

- `subpair_diagram_identity` — the identity inclusion induces the identity geometric map.
- `subpair_plus_zero` — the integral colimit inclusion sends zero to zero.
- `subpair_top_iso` — a member equal to the whole subring has an invertible inclusion.

For the finite-product Checks, put `D_n = C({0,1}^n,R)` with `R` a perfectoid

### P6.5 affinoid étale objects descend to a finite stage

**ECD Proposition 6.4(iv) in the form used by the pro-étale calculus: affinoid étale objects and
surjectivity descend to a finite stage.** (*affinoid-etale-finite-stage-assembly*) Let
`X_i = Spa(R_i, R_i⁺)`, `i ∈ I`, be a cofiltered inverse system of affinoid perfectoid spaces of
any characteristic, over no base field, over a small index category, with limit `X = Spa(R, R⁺)`
(layer P5 (P5.3): `R⁺` the `ϖ`-adic completion of `colim R_i⁺`, `R = R⁺[1/ϖ]`). For a perfectoid
space `T` write `T_ét^aff` for the category of affinoid perfectoid spaces étale over `T` (ECD
Definition 6.2, layer P3 (P3.15)). (a) (ECD Proposition 6.4(iv), which is P5.13.4, *affinoid-etale-finite-stage-6-4-iv*) The base change functors induce an equivalence
`2-colim_i (X_i)_ét^aff → X_ét^aff`. (b) (Descent of surjectivity) If `Y_i ∈ (X_i)_ét^aff` and
`Y_i ×_{X_i} X → X` is surjective, there is `j_0 → i` such that `Y_i ×_{X_i} X_j → X_j` is
surjective for every `j → j_0` — the qcqs étale case of P5.12
(*finite-stage-isomorphism-detection* (a), ECD 6.4(ii)), restricted to affinoid étale objects. (c) (Relation to the
quasicompact separated stage of layer P5) If `Y ∈ X_ét^aff` and `Z_i → X_i` is a qcqs étale model
of `Y` (`Z_i ×_{X_i} X ≅ Y`; layer P5 (P5.12), ECD 6.4(ii)), then `Z_i ×_{X_i} X_j` is affinoid
perfectoid and isomorphic over `X_j` to the model given by (a) for all `j` beyond some `j_0`.
Affinoidness at a finite stage is the content of (a) and is not a consequence of ECD 6.4(ii)–(iii)
(P5.13.4 (c)). (d) (Relative form) If `B` is an affinoid perfectoid space and
the `X_i → B` are compatible étale maps (for instance a pro-étale presentation of `X` over `B`),
then every `Y_i ∈ (X_i)_ét^aff` and every `Y_i ×_{X_i} X_j` for `j → i` lies in `B_ét^aff`, with
structure map the projection to `X_j` followed by `X_j → B`, so the finite-stage
models of (a) are affinoid étale over `B`. The compatibility of the equivalences of ECD 6.4 (i)–(iv) with the inclusions
`X_fét ⊆ X_ét^aff ⊆ X_ét,qc,sep ⊆ X_ét,qcqs` is P5.13.4
(*etale-descent-to-finite-stage-6-4*) and is not restated. No step uses v-descent, a diamond atlas
or the comparison of analytic adic spaces with diamonds. The equivalence (a) is imported from
P5.13.4; (c)–(d) are the consequences the proofs of ECD Lemma 7.11(i), Lemma
7.18 and Proposition 8.5 use ([ECD] §6, Prop. 6.4(iv), p. 27,
for (a); [ECD] §6, proof of Prop. 6.4, p. 28, for the division of labour between P5's (ii) and
P5.13.4's essential surjectivity recorded in (c); [ECD] §7, proof of Lem. 7.18, p. 37, for the use of
(a) and (b) in the cover construction of DiamondsAndVStacks layer D1, downstream). *Needs:*
P5.13.4; layer P5 (P5.3, P5.12); layer P3 (P3.15, P3.16); layer P2 (P2.16).

DiamondsAndVStacks consumes this result; its layer D0 is not a prerequisite.

For (a), the assembly target *affinoid-etale-finite-stage-assembly* of this subsection cites
P5.13.4's *affinoid-etale-finite-stage-6-4-iv*, specified in this README: its
essential surjectivity (named `affinoid_etale_finite_stage_essSurj` in its Examples) and its
Hom-colimit bijection are the supplied affinoid-pair statements ([ECD] Proposition 6.4(iv),
pp. 27–28).
P5's `finiteStage_surjectivity` supplies (b); surjectivity remains true after
further base change. `finiteStage_affinoid` retains the eventual affinoidness assertion.
For (c), `finiteStage_affinoid_model_iso` takes a qcqs étale model `Z_i`, an affinoid étale
model `W_l`, and an isomorphism of their pullbacks over `X`. It gives a common stage
`j → i`, `j → l` at which, and after every further `k → j`, the pullback of `Z_i` is affinoid
and isomorphic to the pullback of `W_l` in `smallEtale p X_k`; the isomorphism therefore
commutes with the maps to `X_k` ([ECD] Proposition 6.4(ii), (iv), pp. 27–28).

For (d), `finiteStage_relative` (*affinoid-etale-relative-finite-stage-models*) takes the
affinoid diagram, its natural transformation to the constant diagram at `B`, étaleness of
every component, and an affinoid étale `Y_i`. It places both `Y_i` and each 
`etaleBaseChange` along `X_j → X_i` in `AffinoidEtale p B`. The structure map is the
projection to `X_j` followed by `X_j → B`, and equals the projection to `Y_i` followed by
`Y_i → X_i → B`. This statement also holds for arbitrary perfectoid `B`; the affinoid case
is (d) ([ECD] Proposition 6.4(iv), pp. 27–28; proof of Lemma 7.11(i), p. 33).

**Check.** `finiteStage_relative_nonetale` excludes a map to `B` that is not étale from
`AffinoidEtale p B`, even if its source is affinoid. Identity transitions recover the
original relative model, and empty affinoid models satisfy the same base-change statement.

### P6.6 affinoid pro-étale morphisms

Affinoid pro-étale morphisms are the cofiltered limits of affinoid étale ones.

**Affinoid pro-étale morphisms and pro-étale presentations.** (*affinoid-pro-etale-map*) Let
`f : Y → X` be a morphism of perfectoid spaces (layer P2 (P2.10)). `f` is affinoid pro-étale if
`Y = Spa(S, S⁺)` and `X = Spa(R, R⁺)` are affinoid perfectoid and there are a small cofiltered
category `I`, a functor `i ↦ (Y_i → X)` from `I` to `X_ét^aff` (affinoid perfectoid spaces
`Y_i = Spa(S_i, S_i⁺)` with an étale structure map to `X` in the sense of ECD Definition 6.2, and
`X`-morphisms as transition maps) and an `X`-isomorphism `Y ≅ lim_i Y_i`, the limit taken in
perfectoid spaces (layer P5 (P5.3): `S⁺ ≅` the `ϖ`-adic completion of `colim S_i⁺` for a
pseudouniformiser `ϖ` of `R`, and `S = S⁺[1/ϖ]`). The data `(I, (Y_i), the isomorphism)` is a
pro-étale presentation of `f`. The transition maps are `X`-morphisms between étale `X`-spaces and
hence étale (layer P3, P3.18); they are not required to be surjective or finite étale, which
distinguishes these presentations from those of Scholze 2013 used in AdicEtaleGeometry A1.12;
`I` is small but of arbitrary size; being affinoid pro-étale is the existence of a presentation,
and in a formalisation a presentation is a limit cone in perfectoid spaces over `X` together with
the étaleness of the legs' index objects. `X_proét^aff` denotes the full subcategory of perfectoid
spaces over `X` on the affinoid pro-étale `X`-spaces. In `PerfectoidSpace`, define
`ProEtalePresentation` as the structure (small cofiltered `I`, functor `I ⥤ X_ét^aff`,
`X`-isomorphism of `Y` with its limit), `IsAffinoidProEtale` as `Nonempty (ProEtalePresentation f)`
and `AffinoidProEtale` as `X_proét^aff`; prove `IsAffinoidProEtale.of_presentation`,
`IsAffinoidProEtale.of_isEtale` (an étale morphism of affinoid perfectoid spaces is affinoid
pro-étale, by the constant presentation), `IsAffinoidProEtale.id`,
`ProEtalePresentation.isLimit` (the cone `Y → Y_i` is a limit cone in perfectoid spaces over `X`),
`ProEtalePresentation.plusModEquiv` (`O⁺(Y)/ϖ ≅ colim_i O⁺(Y_i)/ϖ`),
`ProEtalePresentation.homeomorphLimit` (`|Y| ≃ₜ lim_i |Y_i|`, ECD 6.4(o)),
`ProEtalePresentation.range_eq_iInter` (the image of `|Y|` in `|X|` is the intersection of the
quasicompact open images of the `|Y_i|`), `IsAffinoidProEtale.isProConstructible_range` (that image
is pro-constructible and stable under generalisation), `isAffinoidProEtale_iff_canonical`
(see *canonical-pro-etale-presentation*), and the stability lemmas `IsAffinoidProEtale.comp`
(see *affinoid-pro-etale-composition*), `IsAffinoidProEtale.baseChange`
(see *affinoid-pro-etale-base-change*) and `IsAffinoidProEtale.of_comp`
(see *affinoid-pro-etale-cancellation*) ([ECD] §7, Def. 7.8(i), p. 32; [Berkeley] Lecture 8,
Def. 8.2.1, p. 57, the same notion on rings: `(B, B⁺)` is a completed filtered colimit of
perfectoid pairs étale over `(A, A⁺)`). *Needs:* layer P2 (P2.10, P2.9); layer P3 (P3.15, P3.18);
layer P5 (P5.3); AdicSpacesPartII R0.19.5–R0.19.8 and P5.4’s perfectoid limit comparisons; Mathlib `CategoryTheory.IsCofiltered`,
`CategoryTheory.Limits.IsLimit`.

**Checks.**

- `isAffinoidProEtale_rationalSubset` (computation) — for a rational subset
  `U = X(f_1, …, f_n / g)` of an affinoid perfectoid `X`, the inclusion `U ↪ X` is affinoid
  pro-étale with the presentation indexed by a point.
- `isAffinoidProEtale_id` (degenerate) — the identity of an affinoid perfectoid space is affinoid
  pro-étale, as are the map from the empty space `∅ = Spa(0, 0) → X` (`X × ∅`, the constant
  presentation) and every finite étale `Y → X` between affinoid perfectoid spaces (constant
  presentation).
- `isAffinoidProEtale_origin` (computation) — for `K = Q_p(p^{1/p^∞})^∧` and
  `X = Spa(K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, K°⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩)`, the origin `Spa(K, K°) ↪ X` is affinoid pro-étale with
  the presentation `(X_n = {|T| ≤ |p|ⁿ})_n`, and it is not étale (its image is not open).
- `not_isAffinoidProEtale_openUnitDisc` (non-example) — the open unit disc `{|T| < 1}` of the
  perfectoid closed disc is étale, hence pro-étale, over it but not affinoid pro-étale: it is not
  quasicompact, hence not affinoid.
- `not_isOpenMap_of_isAffinoidProEtale` (non-example) — for a perfectoid field `K` and an infinite
  profinite set `S` with a non-isolated point `x`, `Spa(K, O_K) × {x} → Spa(K, O_K) × S` is
  affinoid pro-étale and not open ([Berkeley] Lecture 8, Rem. 8.2.3): affinoid pro-étale maps are
  not étale-local products.

**Checks for presentations and the affinoid category.**

- `presentation_singleton` — the constant presentation of an affinoid étale map has exactly
  one indexing object.
- `presentation_empty_source_nonempty_index` — the empty open subspace has a one-stage
  presentation whose stage has no points.
- `twoPoint_transition_nonidentity` — the two-sheet presentation in P6.9 has a genuine
  constant-zero transition, which is distinct from the identity over a nonempty base.
- `presentation_rational_constant` — a rational inclusion has a one-object presentation;
  its transition is the identity, without a surjectivity requirement on the inclusion.
- `affinoidProEtale_identity_object`, `affinoidProEtale_empty_object`,
  `affinoidProEtale_excludes_open_disc` — the full category contains the identity and empty
  objects and excludes the non-quasicompact open disc.

### P6.7 pro-étale morphisms

Pro-étale morphisms are the morphisms that are affinoid pro-étale locally on source and target.

**Pro-étale morphisms of perfectoid spaces.** (*pro-etale-map*) A morphism `f : Y → X` of
perfectoid spaces, over no base field, is pro-étale if for every `y ∈ Y` there are an open
neighbourhood `V ⊆ Y` of `y` and an open subset `U ⊆ X` with `f(V) ⊆ U` such that `V` and `U` are
affinoid perfectoid and `f|_V : V → U` is affinoid pro-étale (see *affinoid-pro-etale-map*); ECD's
'open subset `U`' is taken affinoid, as the restriction `f|_V` must be affinoid pro-étale. `V` and
`U` can be chosen rational inside any given neighbourhoods of `y` and `f(y)`
(see *pro-etale-local-shrinking*); `X_proét` denotes the category of perfectoid spaces pro-étale over
`X` with all `X`-morphisms, which are automatically pro-étale (see *pro-etale-stability-and-limits*),
and for `κ`-small `X`, `X_proét,κ` is its full subcategory of `κ`-small objects. Pro-étale morphisms
need not be open nor locally of finite type; being pro-étale is local on the source and, for open
covers, on the target, but not local on the target for the pro-étale topology. This is neither
Mathlib's pro-étale site of a scheme (`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.ProEt`, defined by weakly étale
maps) nor Scholze 2013's `X_proét` of a locally noetherian adic space (AdicEtaleGeometry
A1.12). In `PerfectoidSpace`, define `IsProEtale` as the structure above and `ProEtaleOver` as
`X_proét`, with the instance `ProEtaleOver.hasPullbacks` (fibre products, computed in perfectoid
spaces); prove `IsProEtale.of_isAffinoidProEtale`, `IsProEtale.of_isEtale` (étale maps are
pro-étale, *pro-etale-local-shrinking*), `IsProEtale.of_openCover` (if `X = ⋃ U_α` and every
`f⁻¹(U_α) → U_α` is pro-étale then `f` is), `IsProEtale.restrict` (`f|_V : V → U` for open `U ⊆ X`,
`V ⊆ f⁻¹(U)`), `isProEtale_iff_exists_rational` (rational `V ∋ y`, `U ∋ f(y)` with `f(V) ⊆ U` and
`V → U` affinoid pro-étale), `IsProEtale.comp`, `IsProEtale.baseChange`, `IsProEtale.of_comp`
(see *pro-etale-stability-and-limits*) and `IsProEtale.diagonal` (see *diagonals-are-pro-etale*) ([ECD] §7,
Def. 7.8(ii), p. 32; [Berkeley] Lecture 8, Def. 8.2.1, p. 57, the same definition; [Berkeley]
Lecture 8, after Prop. 8.2.5, p. 59, the failure of locality for the pro-étale topology). *Needs:*
*affinoid-pro-etale-map*; layer P2 (P2.10, P2.11); Mathlib `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.ProEt`.

**Checks.**

- `isProEtale_openImmersion` (computation) — the inclusion of the open unit disc `{|T| < 1}` into
  the perfectoid closed disc over a perfectoid field is pro-étale.
- `isProEtale_id` (degenerate) — the identity of any perfectoid space is pro-étale.
- `isProEtale_prod_locallyProfinite` (computation) — for a perfectoid space `X` and a locally
  profinite set `S` (e.g. `Q_p`), `X × S := ⋃ X × S_c` over the compact open `S_c ⊆ S` is pro-étale
  over `X` ([Berkeley] Lecture 8, Ex. 8.2.2).
- `not_isOpenMap_of_isProEtale` (non-example) — `Spa(K, O_K) × {x} → Spa(K, O_K) × S` (`x` a
  non-isolated point of a profinite `S`) is pro-étale and not open ([Berkeley] Lecture 8,
  Rem. 8.2.3).

**Checks for the global categories.**

- `proEtaleOver_identity` and `proEtaleOver_open_disc` — the identity and the open disc
  inclusion are objects of the category, although the second is not an affinoid object.
- `proEtaleOver_inherited_maps` — all morphisms over the base are retained.
- `smallProEtale_identity` — the identity is an object whenever its base is `κ`-small.
- `smallProEtale_empty` — for `1<κ`, the empty object lies over every base.
- `smallProEtale_zero_cutoff` — at cutoff zero the category has no objects.

### P6.8 the product with a profinite set

Products with infinite profinite sets supply affinoid pro-étale maps that are not étale.

**The product `X × S` of an affinoid perfectoid space with a profinite set, and its relative form
`X ×_{S₀} S`.** (*product-with-profinite-set*) Let `X` be an affinoid perfectoid space,
`φ : |X| → S₀` a continuous map to a profinite set and `S → S₀` a continuous map of profinite sets.
Write `S → S₀` as a cofiltered limit of maps of finite discrete sets `S_k → S₀,k` (`k ∈ K`)
compatible with `S → S₀` (Mathlib `Profinite.asLimit`, `DiscreteQuotient`). Each
`φ_k : |X| → S₀,k` is locally constant, so `X = ⊔_{t∈S₀,k} X_{k,t}` with `X_{k,t} := φ_k⁻¹(t)` open
and closed, hence a rational subset cut out by an idempotent of `O(X)` (`O_X` is a sheaf, layer P2
(P2.8)); `X ×_{S₀,k} S_k := ⊔_{s∈S_k} X_{k,image(s)}` is affinoid perfectoid and affinoid étale over
`X`. Define `X ×_{S₀} S := lim_k X ×_{S₀,k} S_k` (limit in perfectoid spaces, layer P5 (P5.3)), and
`X × S := X ×_∗ S = lim_k X × S_k`. Prove: (a) for every perfectoid space `T` over `X`,
`X`-morphisms `T → X ×_{S₀} S` correspond to continuous maps `|T| → S` over `S₀`, so the
construction is independent of the presentation and functorial in `S → S₀`; (b)
`X ×_{S₀} S → X` is affinoid pro-étale with the above pro-étale presentation; (c)
`|X ×_{S₀} S| = |X| ×_{S₀} S`; (d) `O⁺(X × S) = C⁰(S, O⁺(X))` and `O(X × S) = C⁰(S, O(X))`,
continuous maps for the `ϖ`-adic topology on `O⁺(X)` (for `X = Spa(K, O_K)` this is ECD's
`Spa(C⁰(S, K), C⁰(S, O_K))`); (e) for a morphism `T → X`, `T ×_X (X ×_{S₀} S) = T ×_{S₀} S`; (f)
`(X × S)♭ = X♭ × S`; (g) for `S` locally profinite, `X × S` is glued from the `X × S_c` over the
compact open subsets `S_c ⊆ S` and is pro-étale, not affinoid unless `S` is compact, over `X` when `X` is nonempty; for `X = ∅` the product is empty for every `S`.
For nonempty `X` and infinite profinite `S`, `X × S` is not the disjoint union of `#S` copies of `X`. The same construction
`S × X := lim ⊔_{s ∈ S_j} X`, with `|U × S| = |U| × S` and `Hom(V, U × S) = Hom(V, U) × C(|V|, S)`,
is AdicEtaleGeometry A1.12 (*profinite-set-objects*) in Scholze's pro-étale site of a locally
noetherian adic space; here the carrier is the category of perfectoid spaces over an affinoid
perfectoid `X` with ECD's limit, and the relative form `X ×_{S₀} S` is added. In `PerfectoidSpace`,
define `prodProfinite` (`X × S`) and `fibreProdProfinite` (`X ×_{S₀} S`) with the projection
`prodProfinite.fst : X × S → X`; prove `prodProfinite.isAffinoidProEtale` (b),
`prodLocallyProfinite.homEquiv` (`Hom(T, X × S) ≃ Hom(T, X) × C(|T|, S)`),
`prodProfinite.homeomorph` (`|X × S| ≃ₜ |X| × S`),
`fibreProdProfinite.homEquiv` (`Hom_X(T, X ×_{S₀} S) ≃ {continuous |T| → S over S₀}`),
`fibreProdProfinite.homeomorph` (`|X ×_{S₀} S| ≃ₜ |X| ×_{S₀} S`), `prodProfinite.plusEquiv` (d),
`prodProfinite.map` (a continuous `S → S'` induces `X × S → X × S'`, with `map_id`, `map_comp`),
`prodProfinite.baseChange` (the absolute case of (e)), `fibreProdProfinite.baseChange` (e),
`prodProfinite.tilt` (f), `prodLocallyProfinite` with its
projection `prodLocallyProfinite.isProEtale` (g), and `prodProfinite.finiteIso`
(`X × S ≅ ⊔_{s∈S} X` for finite `S`). For finite `S`,
`prodProfinite.isEtale` states that the projection is étale in A1’s local-description sense;
for affinoid `X`, its affinoid source is supplied by `prodProfinite.isAffinoidProEtale`
([ECD] §7, after Def. 7.8, p. 32, the definition
`X × S = lim X × S_i`; [Berkeley] Lecture 8, Ex. 8.2.2, p. 57, the construction for arbitrary
perfectoid `X` and locally profinite `S`; [ECD] §11, Ex. 11.12, p. 58, the relative form
`Z ×_{π0(Z)} (π0(Z) ×_T S)` used for compact Hausdorff spaces).
*Needs:* *affinoid-pro-etale-map*; layer P5 (P5.3); layer P2 (P2.8, P2.3, P2.16, P2.11);
AdicEtaleGeometry A1.12 (*profinite-set-objects*, for the comparison only); Mathlib
`Profinite`, `Profinite.asLimit`, `DiscreteQuotient`, `FintypeCat.toProfinite`, `ContinuousMap`,
`LocallyConstant`.

**Checks.**

- `prodProfinite_finite` (computation) — for a finite discrete `S`, `X × S ≅ ⊔_{s∈S} X` and
  `O(X × S) = O(X)^S`.
- `prodProfinite_punit` (degenerate) — `X × {pt} ≅ X` and `X × ∅ = ∅`.
- `prodProfinite_Zp_sections` (computation) — `O(Spa(C_p, O_{C_p}) × Z_p) = C⁰(Z_p, C_p)` and
  `O⁺ = C⁰(Z_p, O_{C_p})`.
- `not_prodProfinite_eq_sigma` (non-example) — for nonempty `X` and infinite profinite `S`,
  `X × S` is not `⊔_{s∈S} X`: the
  latter is not quasicompact; `C⁰(S, O(X))` is a proper subring of all functions
  `∏_{s∈S} O(X)`. At a non-isolated point `s`, the function equal to `1` at `s` and `0` elsewhere
  is outside the image of the underlying-function map of `prodProfinite.sectionsEquiv`.
  The Check uses a nontrivial affinoid pair and a non-isolated point of `S`.
  For `X = ∅` both products are empty and both section rings are the zero ring.

The projections and coordinate maps are part of the product interface.
`prodLocallyProfinite.homEquiv` sends a morphism to its projection and its continuous
`S`-coordinate. Its `homeomorph` has exactly these two coordinates.
`fibreProdProfinite.homEquiv` is the corresponding equivalence over `X`, with the equation
`a ∘ b = φ ∘ t`; its homeomorphism sends a point to a pair satisfying that equation.
`prodProfinite.sectionsEquiv` and `plusEquiv` use the topologies of the complete pair and its
plus subring. Pullback of a constant section becomes the constant function with that value.
These equations also fix functoriality, base change and tilting.

**Checks for relative and locally profinite products.**

- `fibreProdProfinite_identity` — the projection for `S → S₀ = id` is an isomorphism.
- `fibreProdProfinite_empty` — an empty source `S` gives the empty space, for every `φ`.
- `fibreProdProfinite_point` — when `S₀` is a point, the relative product is `X × S`.
- `prodLocallyProfinite_singleton` — the projection for a singleton is an isomorphism.
- `prodLocallyProfinite_Qp_noncompact` — for nonzero affinoid `X`, `X × Q_p` is not affinoid.
- `prodLocallyProfinite_empty_base` — `∅ × Q_p` is empty.
- `prodProfinite_empty` — `X × ∅` has no points, including for nonempty `X`.
- `pointSection_singleton`, `pointSection_two_points`, `pointSection_empty_base` — the
  section at a singleton is an isomorphism; two different points give different sections
  when `X` is nonempty; over an empty `X` every such section is an isomorphism.
  For a nonisolated point, `not_isOpenMap_of_isAffinoidProEtale` and
  `not_isOpenMap_of_isProEtale` use this same section and its map on points.

### P6.9 the pro-category equivalence

P6.9 owns the perfectoid realization `proEtaleEquivalence` on the carrier
`Pro(C) = (CategoryTheory.Ind Cᵒᵖ)ᵒᵖ`, with its generic Hom and limit API supplied by
AdicSpacesPartII R0.19.9 on Mathlib's carrier. P6.10 owns its bounded
subcategory, and P6.12 owns the cofiltered-limit interface and flattening functor.
DiamondsAndVStacks D0.13 consumes these constructions. The next four subsections
identify `X_proét^aff` with this pro-category and give the `κ`-bounded, Zariski-closed
and limit consequences.

**Affinoid pro-étale spaces over X are the pro-objects of the affinoid étale site.**
(*pro-etale-pro-category-equivalence*) Let `X` be an affinoid perfectoid space, `X_ét^aff` the
category of étale maps `Y → X` from affinoid perfectoid spaces (essentially small and finitely
complete, *affinoid-etale-size-bound*, *canonical-pro-etale-presentation*; `Pro` is taken with small
cofiltered index categories after replacing `X_ét^aff` by a small skeleton) and `X_proét^aff` the
category of affinoid pro-étale maps `Y → X` (see *affinoid-pro-etale-map*). Let `Pro(X_ét^aff)` be the
pro-category (*pro-object-flattening*; the opposite of Mathlib's `Ind` of the opposite
category), with objects formal limits `"lim" Y_i` over small cofiltered categories and
`Hom("lim" Y_i, "lim" Z_j) = lim_j colim_i Hom_X(Y_i, Z_j)`. Prove that the realisation functor
`ρ_X : Pro(X_ét^aff) → X_proét^aff`, `"lim" Y_i ↦ lim Y_i` (limit in perfectoid spaces), is an
equivalence of categories, with quasi-inverse `Y ↦ "lim"_{(T,t)∈E_Y} T`; equivalently, for
affinoid pro-étale `Y = lim Y_i` and `Z = lim Z_j` over `X`,
`Hom_X(Y, Z) = lim_j colim_i Hom_X(Y_i, Z_j)` ([ECD] §7, Prop. 7.10, p. 33; [ECD] §7, proof of
Prop. 7.10, p. 33, the structure of the proof; [Berkeley] Lecture 8, Lem. 8.2.4, p. 57, the Hom
formula). For `X = Spa(C, O_C)` with `C` algebraically closed, `X_ét^aff ≃ FinSet` and the theorem
reads `Pro(FinSet) ≃ Profinite ≃ X_proét^aff`, `S ↦ X × S`
(see *affinoid-pro-etale-over-geometric-point*). *Needs:* *pro-object-flattening*; *affinoid-pro-etale-map*;
*affinoid-etale-size-bound*; *maps-to-etale-factor-through-finite-stage*;
*canonical-pro-etale-presentation*; layer P5 (P5.3); AdicSpacesPartII R0.19.9 (the generic Pro carrier and Hom formula);
Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Ind`, `CategoryTheory.Functor.IsEquivalence`.

The size of the affinoid étale site (*affinoid-etale-size-bound*). Let `X = Spa(R, R⁺)` be an
affinoid perfectoid space and `μ(X) := (#R + ℵ₀)^ℵ₀`. Prove: (a) every `Y ∈ X_ét^aff` (étale in the
sense of ECD Definition 6.2, layer P3 (P3.15)) has `#O_Y(Y) ≤ μ(X)` and `#|Y| ≤ 2^{μ(X)}`, with no
size hypothesis on `X`; (b) `X_ét^aff` is essentially small, with at most `2^{μ(X)}` isomorphism
classes of objects and `#Hom_X(Y, Y') ≤ 2^{μ(X)}`; (c) if `κ` is an uncountable strong limit and
`X` is `κ`-small, then every object of `X_ét^aff` is `κ`-small, `X_ét^aff` has fewer than `κ`
isomorphism classes of objects, and all its Hom-sets have fewer than `κ` elements; in particular
the isomorphism classes of affinoid étale surjections onto `X` form a set of cardinality `< κ`,
the count in ECD's proof of Lemma 7.18 ([ECD] §7, proof of Lem. 7.18, p. 36, for the bound
`μ(X)` and the counting in (b); [ECD] §6, Def. 6.2(ii), p. 26, for the local structure used in (a),
the printed `y ∈ Y` being read `y ∈ V`). *Needs:* layer P3 (P3.15, P3.14); layer P2 (P2.3, P2.8);
*kappa-small-perfectoid-space*; *complete-tate-ring-cardinality*; *adic-spectrum-cardinality*;
Mathlib `Cardinal.power_mul`, `CategoryTheory.EssentiallySmall`.

Maps from a cofiltered limit of affinoid perfectoid spaces to a qcqs étale space factor through a
finite stage (*maps-to-etale-factor-through-finite-stage*). Let `X` be an affinoid perfectoid
space, `(Y_i)_{i∈I}` a cofiltered system of affinoid perfectoid spaces over `X` (compatible
structure maps; no étaleness assumed) with limit `Y = lim_i Y_i` (layer P5 (P5.3)), and `T → X` an
étale morphism from a quasicompact quasiseparated perfectoid space (for instance `T ∈ X_ét^aff`).
Prove that `colim_i Hom_X(Y_i, T) → Hom_X(Y, T)` is bijective: every `X`-morphism `Y → T` factors
through some `Y_i`, and two `X`-morphisms `Y_i → T` that agree on `Y` agree on `Y_j` for some
`j → i` ([ECD] §7, proof of Prop. 7.10, p. 33, the reduction to an étale target; [Berkeley]
Lecture 8, proof of Lem. 8.2.4, p. 58, the route through rational embeddings and finite étale
maps). *Needs:* layer P5 (P5.3, P5.12); layer P3;
layer P2 (P2.16, P2.15).

The canonical presentation (*canonical-pro-etale-presentation*). Let `X` be an affinoid perfectoid
space and `g : Y → X` a morphism from an affinoid perfectoid space. Let `E_Y` be the category of
pairs `(T, t)` with `T ∈ X_ét^aff` and `t : Y → T` an `X`-morphism, with morphisms
`(T, t) → (T', t')` the `X`-morphisms `u : T → T'` with `u ∘ t = t'` — the category of elements of
`Hom_X(Y, −)` on `X_ét^aff`. Prove: (a) `E_Y` is essentially small and cofiltered (finite limits in
`X_ét^aff`); (b) there is a canonical `X`-morphism `c_Y : Y → lim_{E_Y} T` (limit over a small
skeleton, in perfectoid spaces); (c) `g` is affinoid pro-étale iff `c_Y` is an isomorphism
(`isAffinoidProEtale_iff_canonical`); (d) for any pro-étale presentation `Y = lim_{i∈I} Y_i`, the
functor `I → E_Y`, `i ↦ (Y_i, pr_i)`, is initial ([ECD] §7, proof of Lem. 7.11(iv), p. 34, the
finite limits in `X_ét^aff`; [ECD] §7, Lem. 7.13, p. 34, the same canonical index category in
ECD's topological model: the factorisations `X^wl → T → X` through finite disjoint unions of
rational subsets form a cofiltered category with limit `X^wl`). For `Y ∈ X_ét^aff`, `(Y, id)` is
initial in `E_Y` and `c_Y` is the identity. *Needs:* *affinoid-pro-etale-map*;
*affinoid-etale-size-bound*; *maps-to-etale-factor-through-finite-stage*; layer P5 (P5.3); layer
P2 (P2.16); layer P3; Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Functor.Elements`,
`CategoryTheory.IsCofiltered.of_hasFiniteLimits`, `CategoryTheory.Functor.Initial`,
`CategoryTheory.Functor.initial_of_exists_of_isCofiltered`,
`CategoryTheory.Functor.Initial.limitIso`, `CategoryTheory.EssentiallySmall`.

**Checks for the canonical category and the Hom convention.**

- `canonical_etale_initial` — when `Y → X` is affinoid étale, `(Y,id)` is initial in `E_Y`.
- `canonical_empty` — over affinoid `X`, the empty source also gives an initial factorization.
- `canonical_two_arrows` — take `Y=X`, `T=X×{false,true}`, and the section selecting `false`.
  The identity of `T` and the constant-`false` map are distinct for nonempty `X`, but agree
  after that section. This tests the triangle equation `t ≫ u=t'` and its equalizing direction.
- `proHom_precompose_two_points` — on two points, first the constant-zero map and then the
  transposition gives the constant-one map.
- `proHom_postcompose_two_points` — reversing their order gives the constant-zero map.
  `ProEtalePresentation.homStage` precomposes in the source index; `homDiagram` postcomposes
  in the target index. The Hom equivalence identifies a factorized arrow with its class in
  that source colimit at each target stage.

The small indexing model is Mathlib's `SmallModel` of `CanonicalEtaleIndex`, the latter being
`StructuredArrow (Over.mk f)` into the affinoid étale category. `canonicalCone_π` fixes its
components to the factorization maps. The realization `proEtaleEquivalence` uses the opposite
of Mathlib's `Ind` of the opposite small affinoid étale category; its cone is required to be a
limit in perfectoid spaces over `X`.

- `proHom_transition_precompose` and `proHom_transition_postcompose` put these computations
  inside `homStage` and `homDiagram`. The presentation has index `0 → 1`, both stages the
  two-sheet cover, and transition the constant-zero map. Precomposing the transposition gives
  constant one; postcomposing its colimit class gives the class of constant zero.
- `twoPoint_transition_nonidentity` — for nonempty base, that transition differs from the
  identity; an implementation using a constant identity diagram would fail this Check.

`affinoidEtale_objects_cardinality` counts a skeleton, `affinoidEtale_hom_cardinality` bounds
its Hom sets, and `affinoidEtale_isKappaSmall` gives the strong-limit consequence.

### P6.10 `κ`-small affinoid pro-étale spaces

**Bounded pro-category.** P6.10 owns `PerfectoidSpace.HasKappaSmallPresentation`
and `PerfectoidSpace.ProKappa`. For `C : Type u` with `Category.{v} C` and
`κ : Cardinal.{v+1}`, the predicate on `Z : (Ind Cᵒᵖ)ᵒᵖ` means that there are
`I : Type v`, a small cofiltered category structure on `I`, and `D : I ⥤ C` with
`Cardinal.lift #(Σ i j : I, i ⟶ j) < κ` and
`Z ≅ op ((Ind.lim Iᵒᵖ).obj D.op)`. The lift puts the arrow count in the cutoff's
universe; counting all arrows also bounds objects by their identities.
`ProKappa κ C` is Mathlib's full subcategory for this predicate.
`HasKappaSmallPresentation.of_diagram` supplies the predicate from the displayed
strict arrow bound, hence an object of `ProKappa`; no strong-limit or cutoff
hypothesis is required for this construction ([ECD] §7, Proposition 7.10 and
the description of `Pro_κ` on p. 33). DiamondsAndVStacks D0.13 uses these same
carriers; its unlifted cutoff `κ : Cardinal.{v}` corresponds to `Cardinal.lift κ` here.

**`κ`-small affinoid pro-étale spaces are the pro-objects with fewer than `κ` indices.**
(*kappa-bounded-pro-etale-presentations*) Let `κ` be an uncountable strong limit cardinal and `X` a
`κ`-small affinoid perfectoid space. Prove: (a) an affinoid pro-étale `Y → X` is `κ`-small iff it
admits a pro-étale presentation `Y = lim_{i∈I} Y_i` with `#Mor(I) < κ`; all `Y_i ∈ X_ét^aff` are
then `κ`-small (see *affinoid-etale-size-bound*); (b) with `Pro_κ(X_ét^aff)` the full subcategory of
`Pro(X_ét^aff)` of pro-objects isomorphic to one indexed by a cofiltered category with fewer than
`κ` morphisms, the realisation `ρ_X` of *pro-etale-pro-category-equivalence* restricts to an
equivalence `Pro_κ(X_ét^aff) ≃ X_proét,κ^aff` with the full subcategory of `κ`-small affinoid
pro-étale `X`-spaces (ECD states this without proof); (c) every affinoid pro-étale `Y → X` is the
limit, along a directed poset, of `κ`-small affinoid pro-étale `Y_J → X`: for a presentation indexed
by `I`, `J` runs over the cofiltered subcategories (not required to be full) of `I` with fewer than
`κ` morphisms and `Y_J := lim_{i∈J} Y_i` (the pro-étale form of the first step of ECD's proof of
Proposition 8.2; for arbitrary affinoid `Y` see *kappa-small-perfectoid-subpairs*). Fullness cannot
be demanded in (c): the one-object category of an arbitrarily large commutative monoid with an
absorbing zero is cofiltered, but its only nonempty full subcategory contains all endomorphisms,
whereas the non-full subcategory generated by the identity and zero is small and cofiltered
([ECD] §7, Prop. 7.10, p. 33, for (b), where ECD prints 'objets'; [ECD] §7, after Prop. 7.10,
p. 33, the meaning of `Pro_κ`; [ECD] §8, proof of Prop. 8.2, p. 39, for (c)). *Needs:*
*pro-etale-pro-category-equivalence*; *affinoid-etale-size-bound*;
*kappa-small-cofiltered-limits*; *canonical-pro-etale-presentation*;
*kappa-small-perfectoid-space*; *kappa-small-perfectoid-subpairs*; AdicSpacesPartII R0.19.5–R0.19.8 and P5.4’s perfectoid limit comparisons;
[ECD] Lemma 4.1, pp. 19–20 (choice of cardinal); Mathlib `CategoryTheory.IsCofiltered`.

Cofiltered limits of uniformly bounded `κ`-small affinoid perfectoid spaces are `κ`-small, the
set-theoretic clause of ECD Proposition 6.4 (*kappa-small-cofiltered-limits*). Let
`X_i = Spa(R_i, R_i⁺)`, `i ∈ I`, be a cofiltered system of affinoid perfectoid spaces with limit
`X = Spa(R, R⁺)` (layer P5 (P5.3)). Prove: (a) if `#Mor(I) ≤ λ` and `#R_i ≤ λ` for all `i`, with
`λ` infinite, then `#R ≤ λ^ℵ₀` (the ring-level bound `#R ≤ (#Mor(I)·sup_i #R_i)^ℵ₀` of layer P5
(P5.7)), so for an uncountable strong limit `κ > λ`, `X` is `κ`-small and uniformly `κ`-small; (b) if
`κ` is a cutoff cardinal ([ECD] Lemma 4.1, pp. 19–20), `I` is `λ`-small for some `λ < κ`
and all `X_i` are `κ`′-small for one strong limit `κ′ < κ`, then `X` is `κ`-small; if `κ′ = κ_λ` is a
strong limit of cofinality `> λ` (clause (iii) of the cutoff lemma), then `X` is even `κ_λ`-small, so
the bound does not grow with the diagram; (c) the uniform bound cannot be dropped: for `κ` of
cofinality `ω₁` and a tower of perfectoid fields `K_0 ⊆ K_1 ⊆ … ⊆ K_α ⊆ …` (`α < ω₁`) with
`#K_α < κ` cofinal in `κ`, the `X_α = Spa(K_α, K_α°)` are `κ`-small, `I = ω₁` has fewer than `κ`
elements, and the limit (the completed union) is not `κ`-small ([ECD] §6, Prop. 6.4, final sentence,
p. 27, for (b); [ECD] §6, proof of Prop. 6.4, p. 27, including the `κ_λ` refinement). *Needs:* layer P5 (P5.3, P5.7); *kappa-small-perfectoid-space*;
*uniformly-kappa-small-perfectoid-space*; *complete-tate-ring-cardinality*;
*first-countable-completion-cardinality*; [ECD] Lemma 4.1, pp. 19–20 (choice of cardinal);
Mathlib `Cardinal.iSup_lt_of_lt_cof_ord`.

**Check: `not_isKappaSmall_gaussField_cofilteredLimit`.** Let `κ` be a strong limit
with `cf κ = ℵ₁ < κ`, and let `L` be a characteristic-`p` perfectoid field with
`#L < κ`. Choose increasing infinite subsets `S_α` of one variable set, indexed
by `α < ω₁`, whose cardinalities are `< κ` and cofinal in `κ`. Such subsets can
be taken as initial segments of a set of size `κ`. The theorem supplies a functor
of perfectoid pairs identified at stage `α` with
`(gaussPerfectoidField p L S_α).field.toPairCat p`. Its maps preserve constants
and every variable root under `S_α ⊆ S_β`; these are the Gauss-isometric field
inclusions. The opposite space diagram has fewer than `κ` morphisms and every
stage is `κ`-small. Its `cofilteredLimit` has a global section ring of cardinality
at least `κ`, hence is not `κ`-small. This Check, specified in this README only, retains the small
stages and non-small limit. This distinguishes the stagewise bound from the common
bound required by [ECD] Proposition 6.4, final sentence and proof, p. 27; the
completed-union description is that proposition's opening construction.

Affinoid pro-étale spaces over a geometric point are products with profinite sets
(*affinoid-pro-etale-over-geometric-point*). Let `C` be an algebraically closed perfectoid field
and `X = Spa(C, O_C)`. Prove: (a) the functor `F ↦ X × F = ⊔_F X` from finite sets to `X_ét^aff`
is an equivalence; (b) the functor `S ↦ X × S` from profinite sets to `X_proét^aff`
(see *product-with-profinite-set*) is an equivalence: every affinoid pro-étale `Y → X` is
`X`-isomorphic to `X × S` for a profinite set `S`, and `S ≅ |Y|`; (c) the hypothesis `C⁺ = O_C` is
needed: if `C` admits an open bounded valuation subring `C⁺ ⊊ O_C` of rank two, obtained
by composing the rank-one valuation of `C` with a nontrivial rank-one valuation of its residue
field, choose a unit `u ∈ C⁺` of `O_C` with positive residual valuation. The rational locus
`|1| ≤ |u|` is `Spa(C, O_C)`. Its open immersion into `Spa(C, C⁺)` is affinoid étale and not of the form `Spa(C, C⁺) × S` ([ECD] §7, after
Def. 7.8, p. 32, for (b)). *Needs:* *pro-etale-pro-category-equivalence*;
*product-with-profinite-set*; layer P3 (P3.15, P3.7); *pro-object-flattening*;
Mathlib `Profinite.asLimit`, `FintypeCat.toProfinite`, `IsAlgClosed`.

In (a), `geometricPointFiniteEquivalence` is pinned by
`geometricPointFiniteEquivalence_obj`: for an algebraically closed `AffinoidField p` with
`K.plus.toSubring = powerBoundedSubring K`, its value on every `F : FintypeCat` is isomorphic
in `Over X` to `Over.mk (prodProfinite.fst p X (FintypeCat.toProfinite.obj F))`.
Thus the comparison preserves the structure map to `X`; `prodProfinite.finiteIso`
identifies its source with `⊔_F X`. This is the finite-set case of the product construction
in [ECD], the example after Definition 7.8, p. 32.

Checks (with the same algebraic-closedness and plus-ring hypotheses):

- `geometricPointFiniteEquivalence_obj_empty` — `Fin 0` maps to the projection `X × ∅ → X`.
- `geometricPointFiniteEquivalence_obj_singleton` — `Fin 1` maps to the one-copy projection over `X`.
- `geometricPointFiniteEquivalence_obj_pair` — `Fin 2` maps to the split two-copy projection over `X`.

Zariski closed immersions are affinoid pro-étale, by the rational-intersection presentation
(*zariski-closed-immersions-are-pro-etale*): for `X = Spa(R, R⁺)` affinoid perfectoid and `I ⊆ R`
any ideal, the universal perfectoid space `Z_I = lim_F U_F` over `V(I) = ⋂_F U_F` (the limit over
the rational subsets `U_F = X(F/1)`, `F ⊆ I` finite, P4.14 (a)–(b), through which every Zariski
closed immersion with locus `V(I)` factors isomorphically, P4.14) is a pro-rational subspace, hence
affinoid pro-étale over `X` in the sense of *affinoid-pro-etale-map* with pro-étale presentation
`(U_F)_F` by rational open immersions; strong Zariski closedness (P4.15) is not needed ([ECD] §7,
Rem. 7.9, p. 32; [Torsion] §II.2, proof of Lem. II.2.2, p. 14). For
`K = Q_p(p^{1/p^∞})^∧`, `X = Spa(K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, K°⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩)` and `I = (T)`, `V(I)` is the origin
and `Z_I = Spa(K, K°)`, presented as `lim_n {|T| ≤ |p|ⁿ}`, a Zariski closed immersion that is not
étale. *Needs:* layer P4 (P4.14, P4.12, P4.4); layer P5 (P5.3); layer P2 (P2.3);
*affinoid-pro-etale-map*; Tau Ceti `TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.rationalSubset`.

**Checks for bounded pro-objects and the rank-two boundary.**

- The constant, zero-and-one and two-stage Checks below apply to `HasKappaSmallPresentation` and
  to `ProKappa` alike.
- The constant pro-object of any `c : C` supplies an object at cutoff `2`.
- `ProKappa 0 C` is empty, including when `C` is empty (a Lean `example`).
- `ProKappa 1 C` is empty even for a nonempty category: every cofiltered
  index has an object and its identity arrow.
- Every constant pro-object admits a presentation with one arrow,
  so it belongs at cutoff `2`.
- No pro-object admits a presentation with fewer than one arrow;
  the bounded subcategories at `0` and `1` are empty.
- A diagram `0 → 1` realizes its initial stage, so its pro-object
  already belongs at cutoff `2`, although that chosen diagram has three arrows.
- `large_zero_monoid_cofiltered` / `zeroMonoidPresentation_cofiltered` — the identity cover
  indexed by a monoid with absorbing zero has a cofiltered index and identity cone legs.
- `large_zero_monoid_arrow_count` / `zeroMonoidPresentation_arrow_count` — the arrow set of
  this presentation has cardinality `#M`, although it presents the identity cover.
- `large_zero_monoid_nonfull` / `zeroMonoidPresentation_nonfull` — for nontrivial `M`, the
  two-element submonoid `{0,1}` embeds faithfully and injectively on objects in the presentation;
  restricting the diagram along this embedding still gives the constant identity cover.
- `large_zero_monoid_proper_embedding` — for `2 < #M`, restricting the identity-cover
  presentation to `{0,1}` gives a cofiltered, faithful, injective-on-objects subdiagram that
  is not full.
- `zeroMonoidPresentation_bounded` — if `κ ≤ #M`, with the universe lift understood,
  the small subdiagram supplied by `bounded_subdiagram_approximation_not_full` is not full.
- `rankTwo_two_points`, `rankTwo_generic_one_point`, `rankTwo_etale_not_product` — a rank-two
  plus ring gives two valuation points; replacing it by the norm unit ball gives one point;
  that rational étale inclusion is not a product with any profinite set.

For the last three Checks, `RankTwoGeometricPoint` carries an algebraically closed perfectoid
field and a proper plus valuation ring whose only valuation overrings inside the norm unit ball
are itself and the unit ball. This is the rank-two case of P4's valuation-overring description.
`rankTwoGeometricPoint` constructs one by taking the completed algebraic closure of a Gauss
field with transcendental residue and composing its norm valuation with a nontrivial rank-one
residue valuation. `generization_rational` identifies the generic-point map with a rational
localization. It does not assert this for an arbitrary proper plus ring.

`bounded_subdiagram_approximation` states the directed approximation with a faithful,
injective-on-objects embedding of each small cofiltered index into the original index.
`zeroMonoidPresentation` constructs the identity-cover presentation for any affinoid perfectoid
`X` and monoid with zero `M`; all its diagram arrows and cone legs are identities. Its three
Checks above test the cone, arrow count and restriction to `{0,1}`.
`bounded_subdiagram_approximation_not_full` applies `bounded_subdiagram_approximation` to
this presentation when `κ` is strong limit, `ℵ₀ < κ`, `X` is `κ`-small and `κ ≤ #M` after
lifting universes. It produces a nonempty cofiltered presentation `Q` and a faithful,
injective-on-objects embedding with fewer than `κ` arrows that cannot be full: fullness
would already require all `M` endomorphisms at any one object. This is a specialization of
[ECD] Proposition 8.2, proof, p. 39.
`cofilteredLimit_uniform_card` retains one common ring-and-arrow bound. The bounded equivalence
is tied to the original realization by `proEtaleKappaEquivalence_forget`.

Lean: `PerfectoidSpace.HasKappaSmallPresentation`, `ProKappa`, `HasKappaSmallPresentation.of_diagram`.

### P6.11 Zariski closed equals strongly Zariski closed

**Zariski closed equals strongly Zariski closed.** (*zariski-closed-equals-strongly-zariski-closed*)
For an affinoid perfectoid space `X = Spa(R, R⁺)` and a morphism `f : Z → X` of perfectoid spaces,
`f` is a Zariski closed immersion if and only if `f` is strongly Zariski closed: the direction
strongly Zariski closed ⇒ Zariski closed, the case of an already given surjective perfectoid
quotient `R → S`, is P4.16 (*strongly-zariski-closed-is-zariski-closed*), and the direction
Zariski closed ⇒ strongly Zariski closed is ECD Theorem 5.8, proved in P4.15 through the
perfectoidisation of semiperfectoid rings ([BS22] Theorem 7.4 and Remark 7.5, via surjectivity of
perfectoidisation). Apply `stronglyZariskiClosed_iff_zariskiClosed`
from P4.15 to obtain the consequences for the pro-étale calculus below. Their completed
character-algebra application is given by `CharacterCompletion.fourier_surjective` and
`fourier_kernel_nontrivial`, with the coefficient conventions below. For every ideal `I ⊆ R`
the map `R → S_I` (layer P4 (P4.14)) is surjective with
kernel `I^perf = {h : |h| = 0 on V(I)}`, `S_I⁺` is the integral closure of the image of `R⁺`, and
`R⁺ → S_I⁺` is almost surjective. For `R = ℂ_p⟨T^{±1/p^∞}⟩` and `I = (T − 1)` this gives
`R ↠ C⁰(ℤ_p, ℂ_p)` (Fresnel–de Mathan), contradicting Scholze's Remark II.2.4 and Bhatt's
Warning 9.4.2. The kernel is strictly larger than `(T − 1)`: writing `f = Σ_a c_a T^a`
(`a ∈ ℤ[1/p]`, `c_a → 0`), `(T − 1)R` is the set of `f` with `Σ_{k∈ℤ} c_{a+k} = 0` for every
`a`, the inverse being `d_a := Σ_{k≥1} c_{a+k}` with `‖d‖ ≤ ‖c‖`, so `(T − 1)` is closed and
`R/(T − 1) = ℂ_p⟨μ_{p^∞}⟩` (the `c_0`-completed group algebra, `T^{k/pⁿ} ↦ [ζ_{pⁿ}^k]`); the
element `Σ_{ζ∈μ_{pⁿ}} [ζ]` of norm `1` maps to the function `pⁿ·1_{pⁿℤ_p}` of norm `|p|ⁿ`, so
the surjection `ℂ_p⟨μ_{p^∞}⟩ → C⁰(ℤ_p, ℂ_p)` is not bounded below and, by the open mapping
theorem, has a nonzero kernel `I^perf/(T − 1)`, consisting of elements of spectral norm `0`.
**Checks for the coefficient and character conventions.**

- `division_by_T_sub_one` — in the rational unit-annulus pair of `discPair`, take
  `T = rationalMap (rootX 0)`. The coefficients `c₀ = −1`, `c₂ = 1`, zero elsewhere,
  give `d₀ = d₁ = 1` by the positive-index tail formula, and their images satisfy
  `(T − 1)(d₀ + d₁T) = c₀ + c₂T²` in this pair's ring.
- `two_character_sum` — `finiteFourier 2 1 (-1)` sends `[0]+[1]` to the values `2,0`.
  The image has norm `1/2` and the group-algebra coefficient norm is `1`.
  These are computations from the coordinate and character formulas in this subsection.

The finite group-algebra restriction of the character map is `finiteFourier`: for a primitive
`pⁿ`-th root `ζ`, it sends `[a]` in `C_p[Z/pⁿ]` to `b ↦ ζ^{ab}` and coefficients to constant
functions. Its coefficient norm is the maximum of the coefficient norms; its target uses the
supremum norm on functions on the finite group. This is the finite-level part of the completed
map above; `fourier_surjective` states surjectivity of the completed map.

**Checks for the Fourier map.**

- `fourier_two_character_norm` — for `p=2`, `n=1`, `ζ=-1`, the group-algebra element
  `[0]+[1]` has coefficient norm `1`; its image takes values `2,0` and has norm `1/2`.
- `fourier_constant` — `c[0]` maps to the constant function `c` at every level.
- `fourier_level_zero` — at level `0`, the group is trivial and the map returns the sole
  coefficient. These are direct computations from the displayed character formula.

The completed carrier `CharacterCompletion` is a complete normed `C_p`-algebra with a dense
algebra map from `C_p[μ_{p^∞}]` whose norm is exactly the coefficient maximum. Here
`pPowerRoots` uses the union of Mathlib's `rootsOfUnity` subgroups. The continuous character
`pPowerCharacter` is fixed by `ζ ↦ (x ↦ ζ^(x mod pⁿ))` whenever `ζ^(pⁿ)=1`.
`CharacterCompletion.fourier_single` fixes the completed transform on the dense group algebra;
`fourier_surjective` and `fourier_kernel_nontrivial` state the completed comparison above.

**Checks for the completion and its characters.**

- `completedFourier_zero` and `completedFourier_constant` — zero maps to zero and `c[1]`
  maps to the constant function `c`.
- `completedFourier_two_characters` — in the completed algebra at `p=2`, `[1]+[-1]`
  has norm `1`, while its Fourier transform takes values `2,0` at `0,1` and has norm `1/2`.
- `completion_distinct_coefficients` — `[ζ]-[η]` has coefficient norm `1` for distinct roots.
- `pPowerRoots_one`, `pPowerRoots_minus_one_two`, `pPowerRoots_two_not_root` — the identity
  is a root, `-1` is a two-power root, and `2` is never a root of unity in `C_p`.
- `pPowerCharacter_at_zero`, `pPowerCharacter_one`, `pPowerCharacter_minus_one` — every
  character is `1` at zero, the identity root gives the constant character, and at `p=2`
  the character of `-1` takes values `1,-1` at `0,1`.

Nothing else in layers P0–P7 uses the stronger direction (the diagonal and Zariski closed
pro-étale statements of this layer need only the elementary one); layer [P8](../PerfectoidTowers/README.md#layer-p8-finite-quotients-and-closed-perfectoid-loci-in-towers) and AdicEtaleGeometry
layer A3 use it downstream ([ECD] §5, Thm 5.8 with proof, p. 25; [ECD] §5, after Def. 5.7, p. 24, the
correction of Scholze's Remark II.2.4; [AWS] Lecture 2, Thm 2.9.12, an independent route; [AWS]
Lecture 2, Ex. 2.4.10, the example `I = (T − 1)`). *Needs:* layer P4 (P4.15, P4.16, P4.12, P4.13,
P4.14).

Sections of affinoid pro-étale maps are affinoid pro-étale (*affinoid-pro-etale-sections*). Let
`f : Y → X` be affinoid pro-étale with pro-étale presentation `Y = lim_{i∈I} Y_i`, and `s : X → Y`
a section of `f` (`f ∘ s = id_X`). Prove that `s` is affinoid pro-étale, with pro-étale
presentation `X ≅ lim_i (X ×_{Y_i} Y) → Y`, where `X → Y_i` is `s_i := pr_i ∘ s` and `Y → Y_i` is
`pr_i` ([ECD] §7, proof of Lem. 7.11, p. 33, the statement and the presentation). *Needs:* *affinoid-pro-etale-map*; layer P3; layer P2 (P2.16);
layer P5 (P5.3).

### P6.12 limits in the affinoid pro-étale category

**`X_proét^aff` has all small limits, computed in perfectoid spaces.** (*affinoid-pro-etale-limits*)
For an affinoid perfectoid space `X`, prove that the category `X_proét^aff` has all small limits,
and that they are computed in perfectoid spaces over `X`: the final object is `id_X`; fibre
products `Y ×_Z Y'` of objects of `X_proét^aff` are the fibre products of perfectoid spaces;
cofiltered limits are the limits of layer P5; every small limit is a cofiltered limit of finite
limits of affinoid perfectoid spaces, and the inclusion `X_proét^aff → (perfectoid spaces over X)`
preserves all small limits. Under `ρ_X` (see *pro-etale-pro-category-equivalence*) the categorical statement — `Pro(C)` has
all small limits for `C = X_ét^aff` finitely complete — uses the opposite of Mathlib
Ind categories and the cofiltered-limit instance below, with
`C` essentially small and finitely complete; what is proved here is that `ρ_X` carries those limits
to the limits of perfectoid spaces ([ECD] §7, Lem. 7.11(iv), p. 33; [ECD] §7, proof of
Lem. 7.11(iv), p. 34, the finite limits in `X_ét^aff`). *Needs:*
*pro-etale-pro-category-equivalence*; *affinoid-pro-etale-base-change*;
*affinoid-pro-etale-cofiltered-limits*; *affinoid-pro-etale-composition*;
*affinoid-pro-etale-cancellation*; *canonical-pro-etale-presentation*; layer P2 (P2.16);
*pro-category-cofiltered-limits*; Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Ind`,
`CategoryTheory.Limits.hasLimits_of_hasColimits_op`, `CategoryTheory.Limits.HasLimits`.

**Cofiltered limits of pro-objects.** (*pro-category-cofiltered-limits*)
Mathlib's `HasFilteredColimits (Ind Cᵒᵖ)` instance and
`CategoryTheory.Limits.has_cofiltered_limits_op_of_has_filtered_colimits`
supply `HasLimitsOfShape I (Ind Cᵒᵖ)ᵒᵖ` directly, for `C : Type u`
with `Category.{v} C` and `I : Type v` a small cofiltered category.
AdicSpacesPartII R0.19.9 supplies the generic cofiltered-limit API; the downstream
consumer DiamondsAndVStacks D0.13 uses the same Mathlib instances. Finite limits in the
affinoid étale category then supply all small limits as used above ([ECD] proof of
Lemma 7.11(iv), pp. 33–34).

**Flattening pro-objects.** (*pro-object-flattening*) P6.12 owns `proFlatten`,
`proFlatten_adjunction` and `proFlatten_obj`; DiamondsAndVStacks D0.13 consumes them.
`proFlatten` sends a pro-object
of pro-objects to the limit of its cofiltered presentation. For any category `C`,
`proFlatten_adjunction` makes this functor right adjoint to the constant pro-object
functor `δ : Pro(C) → Pro(Pro(C))`, with `Pro(C) = (Ind Cᵒᵖ)ᵒᵖ`.
For the adjunction chosen from this theorem, write `η` for its unit and `ε` for its
counit. For every `X : Pro(C)` and `Y : Pro(Pro(C))`, `proFlatten_obj` gives
`δ(η_X) ≫ ε_{δ(X)} = id_{δ(X)}` and
`η_{proFlatten(Y)} ≫ proFlatten(ε_Y) = id_{proFlatten(Y)}`.
These are applications of Mathlib's triangle identities to the flattening
construction used in [ECD] proof of Lemma 7.11(i), p. 33.
The Checks `proFlatten_constant`, `proFlatten_empty`, and
`proFlatten_two` below fix its constant-object behavior.

Base change of affinoid pro-étale maps (*affinoid-pro-etale-base-change*). Let `f : Y → X` be
affinoid pro-étale with pro-étale presentation `Y = lim_{i∈I} Y_i`, and `g : X' → X` a morphism
from an affinoid perfectoid space. Prove that `Y' := X' ×_X Y` is affinoid perfectoid and
`f' : Y' → X'` is affinoid pro-étale with pro-étale presentation `Y' = lim_i X' ×_X Y_i`
(`IsAffinoidProEtale.baseChange`), and that `|Y'| → |X'| ×_{|X|} |Y|` is surjective ([ECD] §7,
Lem. 7.11(ii), p. 33; [ECD] §7, proof of Lem. 7.11, p. 33). *Needs:* *affinoid-pro-etale-map*;
layer P2 (P2.16); layer P3 (P3.16); layer P5 (P5.3); AdicSpacesPartII R0.19.5–R0.19.8 and P5.4’s perfectoid limit comparisons.

Cofiltered limits of affinoid pro-étale `X`-spaces are affinoid pro-étale, the geometric form of
`Pro(Pro(C)) → Pro(C)` (*affinoid-pro-etale-cofiltered-limits*). Let `X` be an affinoid perfectoid
space and `(Y_k)_{k∈K}` a small cofiltered diagram in `X_proét^aff`. Prove that its limit
`Y = lim_k Y_k` in perfectoid spaces (layer P5 (P5.3)) is affinoid pro-étale over `X` and is the
limit of the diagram in `X_proét^aff`; under `ρ_X`, `Y` corresponds to the limit in
`Pro(X_ét^aff)` of the corresponding pro-objects (the flattening `Pro(Pro(C)) → Pro(C)` is
the functor `proFlatten` on opposites of Mathlib Ind categories), so `ρ_X` preserves cofiltered limits ([ECD] §7,
proof of Lem. 7.11, p. 33, the categorical input made geometric; [Berkeley] Lecture 8,
Prop. 8.2.5(3), p. 59, existence of the limits). Prove preservation of the limit by its Hom
universal property and finite-stage factorisation. *Needs:* *pro-etale-pro-category-equivalence*;
*maps-to-etale-factor-through-finite-stage*;
*canonical-pro-etale-presentation*; layer P5 (P5.3); *pro-object-flattening*.

Composites of affinoid pro-étale maps are affinoid pro-étale (*affinoid-pro-etale-composition*).
If `g : Z → Y` and `f : Y → X` are affinoid pro-étale, prove that `f ∘ g : Z → X` is affinoid
pro-étale (`IsAffinoidProEtale.comp`): for pro-étale presentations `Y = lim_{i∈I} Y_i` over `X`
and `Z = lim_{j∈J} Z_j` over `Y`, each `Z_j` is `Y`-isomorphic to `W_j ×_{Y_{i(j)}} Y` for some
`i(j) ∈ I` and `W_j ∈ (Y_{i(j)})_ét^aff` (see *affinoid-etale-finite-stage-assembly*), and the transition maps between the `Z_j` descend after refinement by
*maps-to-etale-factor-through-finite-stage*. Use the category of all such finite-stage
models and compatible refinements, retaining each index `i(j)`: prove it is
cofiltered and that its affinoid étale `X`-diagram has limit `Z`
([ECD] §7, Lem. 7.11(i), p. 33; [ECD] §7, proof of Lem. 7.11, p. 33, the reduction used by
*pro-etale-stability-and-limits*). *Needs:* *affinoid-etale-finite-stage-assembly*;
*maps-to-etale-factor-through-finite-stage*; *affinoid-pro-etale-map*; layer P2 (P2.16); layer
P3.

`CompositionModel` records a pair of stages, an affinoid étale model over the first stage,
and its base-change isomorphism to the second. Its arrows retain both indexing refinements,
the map of models and the compatibility with that isomorphism. `diagram`, `cone`,
`cofiltered`, `essentiallySmall` and `isLimit` state the simultaneous descent construction.

**Checks for simultaneous models.**

- `composition_model_constant` — two one-stage étale presentations admit the original
  composite source as a model.
- `composition_model_empty_stage` — an empty model has an empty base-changed stage.
- `composition_model_two_sheets` — over a nonzero affine base, the two-sheet constant
  presentation has a two-sheet model whose structure map is not an isomorphism.
- `composition_model_identity` additionally checks that the model diagram sends identity
  refinements to identity arrows, in agreement with its functor structure.

Morphisms between affinoid pro-étale `X`-spaces are affinoid pro-étale
(*affinoid-pro-etale-cancellation*). Let `Y → X` and `Y' → X` be affinoid pro-étale. Prove that
every `X`-morphism `g : Y → Y'` is affinoid pro-étale (`IsAffinoidProEtale.of_comp`); consequently,
for `Y' ∈ X_proét^aff`, an affinoid perfectoid space `Z → Y'` is affinoid pro-étale over `Y'` iff
`Z → X` is affinoid pro-étale, so `(Y')_proét^aff ≃ X_proét^aff/Y'` (slice category) ([ECD] §7,
Lem. 7.11(iii), p. 33; [ECD] §7, proof of Lem. 7.11, p. 33). *Needs:*
*affinoid-pro-etale-base-change*; *affinoid-pro-etale-composition*;
*affinoid-pro-etale-sections*; layer P2 (P2.16).

### P6.13 stability of pro-étale morphisms

The last two subsections globalise the affinoid stability results to pro-étale morphisms of
arbitrary perfectoid spaces and compare with Scholze 2013.

**Stability of pro-étale morphisms: composition, base change, cancellation and limits.**
(*pro-etale-stability-and-limits*) Composition (`IsProEtale.comp`), base change along arbitrary
morphisms of perfectoid spaces (`IsProEtale.baseChange`) and cancellation (`IsProEtale.of_comp`)
for pro-étale morphisms are the affinoid statements *affinoid-pro-etale-composition*,
*affinoid-pro-etale-base-change* and *affinoid-pro-etale-cancellation* of P6.12 passed to the
general case by *pro-etale-local-shrinking*, and the limits of `X_proét^aff` for affinoid `X` are
*affinoid-pro-etale-limits* (P6.12); none is restated here. Consequences: `X_proét` (perfectoid spaces pro-étale over `X`, with
all `X`-morphisms) contains `X_ét`, is closed under fibre products, which are computed in
perfectoid spaces (`ProEtaleOver.hasPullbacks`), and for `Y ∈ X_proét`, `Y_proét ≃ X_proét/Y`.
These are the stability assertions the big and small pro-étale sites of DiamondsAndVStacks layer
D2 rest on; pro-étaleness is not claimed to be local on the target for the pro-étale topology
([ECD] §7, Lem. 7.11, p. 33; [Berkeley] Lecture 8, Prop. 8.2.5, p. 58, Berkeley's version of the
same lemma). *Needs:*
*affinoid-pro-etale-base-change*; *affinoid-pro-etale-composition*;
*affinoid-pro-etale-cancellation*; *pro-etale-local-shrinking*; *affinoid-pro-etale-limits*;
*pro-etale-map*; layer P2 (P2.16).

Étale maps are pro-étale, and affinoid pro-étale maps restrict to affinoid opens
(*pro-etale-local-shrinking*). Prove: (a) every étale morphism of perfectoid spaces is pro-étale
(`IsProEtale.of_isEtale`), and every étale morphism between affinoid perfectoid spaces is affinoid
pro-étale (`IsAffinoidProEtale.of_isEtale`); (b) if `f : Y → X` is affinoid pro-étale, `U ⊆ X` is
an open affinoid perfectoid subspace and `V ⊆ f⁻¹(U)` is an open affinoid perfectoid subspace,
then `f|_V : V → U` is affinoid pro-étale; (c) consequently `f : Y → X` is pro-étale iff every
`y ∈ Y` has rational neighbourhoods `V ∋ y` and `U ∋ f(y)`, inside any given neighbourhoods, with
`f(V) ⊆ U` and `f|_V` affinoid pro-étale (`isProEtale_iff_exists_rational`); pro-étaleness is local
on the source (`IsProEtale.of_sourceOpenCover`: if `Y = ⋃ V_α` and all `V_α → X` are
pro-étale, so is `f`), local on the target for open covers (`IsProEtale.of_openCover`), and stable under
restriction to open subspaces of the source and over open subspaces of the target
(`IsProEtale.restrict`) ([ECD] §7, proof of Lem. 7.11, p. 33, the reduction made precise;
[Berkeley] Lecture 8, Def. 8.2.1, p. 57, locality on source and target). *Needs:* *affinoid-pro-etale-map*; *pro-etale-map*;
*affinoid-pro-etale-base-change*; *affinoid-pro-etale-composition*; layer P3 (P3.15); layer P2
(P2.3).

Diagonals and graphs of morphisms of perfectoid spaces are pro-étale (*diagonals-are-pro-etale*).
Let `f : Y → X` be any morphism of perfectoid spaces, with no separatedness or finiteness
hypothesis. Prove: (a) the diagonal `Δ_f : Y → Y ×_X Y` (layer P2 (P2.16)) is pro-étale
(`IsProEtale.diagonal`); if `X = Spa(R, R⁺)` and `Y = Spa(S, S⁺)` are affinoid, `Δ_f` is a Zariski
closed immersion, cut out by the kernel of the multiplication map `S ⊗̂_R S → S`, and affinoid
pro-étale (see *zariski-closed-immersions-are-pro-etale*); (b) for morphisms `Y → X` and `Y' → X` and
an `X`-morphism `g : Y → Y'`, the graph `Γ_g : Y → Y ×_X Y'` is pro-étale, affinoid pro-étale when
`X`, `Y`, `Y'` are affinoid ([ECD] §7, Rem. 7.9, p. 32, for (a); [ECD] §5, proof of Prop. 5.9,
p. 25, the affinoid diagonal is strongly Zariski closed; [ECD] §11, proof of Prop. 11.4, p. 55,
the consumer in DiamondsAndVStacks layer D4).
*Needs:* *zariski-closed-immersions-are-pro-etale*; layer P4 (P4.18, P4.13); layer P2 (P2.16);
*pro-etale-map*; *pro-etale-local-shrinking*; *pro-etale-stability-and-limits*.

`proFlatten` takes the limit of the cofiltered presentation of a pro-object of
pro-objects. The unit and counit equations of `proFlatten_obj` identify the two
composites with identities on constant and flattened objects. The Checks
`proFlatten_constant`, `proFlatten_empty`, and `proFlatten_two` recover a constant
pro-object, the unique endomorphism of the empty finite set, and the four endomorphisms
of the two-point set.

### P6.14 comparison with Scholze 2013's affinoid perfectoid objects

**Scholze 2013's affinoid perfectoid objects of `X_proét` give affinoid pro-étale perfectoid spaces
in the sense of ECD Definition 7.8.** (*scholze-2013-affinoid-perfectoid-comparison*) Let `K` be a
perfectoid field of characteristic `0` (Scholze 2013's setting), `X` a locally noetherian adic
space over `Spa(K, K⁺)`, and `X_proét` Scholze's pro-étale site (AdicEtaleGeometry A1.12, on the
category `pro-X_ét` of AdicEtaleGeometry A1.12). Let `U = lim U_i ∈ X_proét` be affinoid
perfectoid (Scholze 2013, Definition 4.3: a pro-étale presentation by affinoid
`U_i = Spa(R_i, R_i⁺)` whose completed colimit `(R, R⁺)` is a perfectoid affinoid
`(K, K⁺)`-algebra) and `Û := Spa(R, R⁺)`; the comparison is with the base-field-free notion of
this layer restricted to spaces over `Spa(K, K⁺)`. Prove: (a) if `V_i → U_i` is étale and a
composite of rational subsets and finite étale maps, then `V := V_i ×_{U_i} U` is affinoid
perfectoid and `V̂ = V_i ×_{U_i} Û` (fibre product of adic spaces over `K`) is an object of
`Û_ét^aff`, étale in the sense of ECD Definition 6.2 (Scholze 2013, Lemma 4.5(i)); (b) if
`V = lim_k V^{(k)} → U` is a cofiltered limit in `X_proét` of objects `V^{(k)} → U` as in (a), then
`V` is affinoid perfectoid and `V̂ = lim_k V̂^{(k)}` (limit in perfectoid spaces, layer P5) is
affinoid pro-étale over `Û` with pro-étale presentation `(V̂^{(k)})_k` (*affinoid-pro-etale-map*,
`isAffinoidProEtale_scholze2013`); `V ↦ V̂` is functorial, being induced on pro-objects by the
functor of (a) followed by the realisation of *pro-etale-pro-category-equivalence*; (c) boundary:
Scholze 2013's presentations require eventually finite étale surjective transition maps over a
locally noetherian base, ECD's do not; the erratum restricts only the covering families of
`X_proét`, not its objects, so (a)–(b) are unaffected; no converse is asserted (an affinoid
pro-étale `Û`-space need not come from `X_proét`) ([Sch13] §4, Def. 4.3(i), p. 23, the objects
compared; [Sch13] §4, Lem. 4.5(i), p. 23, for (a); [Sch13] §4, proof of Lem. 4.6, p. 25, for (b);
[Sch13E] item (1), p. 1, for (c)).
*Needs:* AdicEtaleGeometry A1.12 (Scholze 2013's pro-étale site, for the comparison only); layer P2
(P2.3); layer P3 (P3.16, P3.15); layer P5 (P5.3);
*affinoid-pro-etale-map*; *pro-etale-pro-category-equivalence*.

The ring presentation in Definition 4.3(i) has the carrier `ScholzeAffinoidTower`:
strongly noetherian Tate stages over a characteristic-zero perfectoid field, finite étale
surjective transitions, and a perfectoid colimit in complete Huber pairs. `map_stage` fixes
the induced completion map on every stage. `rational_baseChange` and `finiteEtale_baseChange`
state the two elementary factors of (a) as pushouts of complete Huber pairs. The global
comparison in (b) additionally uses the classical `AdicSpace.ProEtaleSite` carrier and the
identification of its affinoid pro-objects with these ring presentations.

`ScholzeAffinoidTower.isAffinoidProEtale_scholze2013` states (b) on these completed
ring presentations. Fix a small cofiltered category `J`, towers `B j`, their completed-pair
diagram `D : Jᵒᵖ ⥤ PairCat p`, and an affinoid étale diagram `E` over `A.realization`,
expressed in `affinoidEtaleSmall`. Require `D.obj (op j) = (B j).completedPair` and a
natural isomorphism from the spectra of `D` to the underlying spaces of `E`; this identifies
both the stages and their transition maps. Choose a stage and compatible pseudouniformizer
roots for P5's `completedColimitPair`. For the map `a` from `A.completedPair` to that
completion, require that every spectral projection followed by its map to `A.realization`
equals `spaFunctor.map a.op`. The theorem says this spectral map is affinoid pro-étale and
supplies a `ProEtalePresentation` with index `J` and diagram `E` transported from the small
model. It also gives an isomorphism, **over `A.realization`**, to `proEtaleEquivalence.cone E`,
carrying each projection to the corresponding completed-pair inclusion. This is the
presentation `(V̂^{(k)})`; `proEtaleEquivalence.cone_pt` identifies its vertex with
`ρ_X("lim" E)`. Thus the completion, its structure map, and its specified presentation are
all related in the statement. Source: [Sch13] Lemma 4.6 and its proof, pp. 24–25, together
with [ECD] Definition 7.8(i), p. 32, and Proposition 7.10, p. 33.

`ScholzeAffinoidTower.isAffinoidProEtale_scholze2013_naturality` specifies the map of
realizations for a natural transformation `α : D → E` of small cofiltered affinoid étale
diagrams over `A.realization`. The map obtained by applying `proEtaleEquivalence` to the
induced pro-object map, followed by the `j`th projection, equals the source projection
followed by `α.app j`. Combined with the preceding isomorphisms, this identifies the maps
of completed towers with `ρ_X` on morphisms, including identity and composition, rather than
only identifying their objects ([Sch13] paragraph after Definition 4.3, p. 23;
[ECD] Proposition 7.10, p. 33). These are limits of perfectoid realizations; comparison with
the original noetherian stages uses AdicSpacesPartII R0.20.1–R0.20.2's `IsTildeLimit` and
`IsTildeLimit.baseChange`, with the completed-direct-limit criterion of
*tilde-limits-affinoid-criterion*.

**Checks for the cofiltered realization.**

- `isAffinoidProEtale_scholze2013_constant` — a constant pro-object realizes to its original
  affinoid étale object over the base.
- `isAffinoidProEtale_scholze2013_empty_stage` — an empty stage forces an empty realization;
  the index category itself remains nonempty by cofilteredness.
- `isAffinoidProEtale_scholze2013_two_stages` — for a diagram `0 → 1`, projection to stage
  `0` is an isomorphism and projection to stage `1` is that isomorphism followed by the given
  transition. The transition is retained, with no identity or surjectivity assumption.
- `isAffinoidProEtale_scholze2013_constant_zero_transition` — in the two-stage diagram
  `X × {0,1} → X × {0,1}` with transition `(x,s) ↦ (x,0)`, the realization is the first
  two-sheet cover: the projections are the identity and the constant-zero map. For nonempty
  `X`, the two sheets of the limit survive although the transition is not surjective.

**Checks for the completed tower.**

- `scholze_completion_identity` — the identity map of a tower realizes to an isomorphism.
- `scholze_completion_empty` — a zero-ring stage forces the completed spectrum to be empty.
- `scholze_completion_two_points` — a tower with one object and only its identity arrow,
  whose stage has two spectral points, retains those two points after completion.

### P6.16 the perfectoid torsor presentation

**Perfectoid torsor presentation.** (*perfectoid-cover-presentation*) Let `p` be a prime and
`(A, A⁺)` a Huber pair with `A` a complete Hausdorff Tate ring, `A⁺` any ring of integral
elements, and no sheafiness of `(A, A⁺)`; existence of a presentation (`exists`) assumes that `p`
is topologically nilpotent in `A`. A *perfectoid torsor presentation* of
`(A, A⁺)` consists of a profinite group `G` (Mathlib `ProfiniteGrp`), a complete Huber pair
`(Ã, Ã⁺)` with `Ã` a perfectoid Tate ring (layer P1), a continuous action of `G`
on `(Ã, Ã⁺)` by automorphisms of Huber pairs, and a `G`-invariant morphism of Huber pairs
`q : (A, A⁺) → (Ã, Ã⁺)`, such that

`(a) Ã ⊗̂ᵘ_A Ã ≅ (C^0(G, Ã), C^0(G, Ã⁺)),  b ⊗ b′ ↦ (g ↦ b·g(b′))   (uniform completed tensor     product, AdicSpacesPartII layer R0); (b) Spa(q) : Spa(Ã, Ã⁺) → Spa(A, A⁺) is surjective and open with fibres exactly the     G-orbits, so |Spa(Ã, Ã⁺)|/G ≅ |Spa(A, A⁺)|.`

`Spa(q)` is moreover spectral, in particular quasi-compact, for every morphism `q` out of the Tate
pair `(A, A⁺)` (Tau Ceti `Huber.Pair.Hom.isSpectralMap_spaComap_of_isTateRing` in
`TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/AdicSpace/Spa/MorphismSpectral.lean`), so the quasi-compactness that
[ECD] Prop. 15.4 records is automatic and is not an axiom of the record.

The *perfectoid cover* is `X̃ = Spa(Ã, Ã⁺)`; the *induced perfectoid equivalence relation* is
`R̃ = Spa(C^0(G, Ã), C^0(G, Ã⁺)) ≅ G × X̃`, with `s, t : R̃ ⇉ X̃` induced by `b ↦ (g ↦ b)` and
`b ↦ (g ↦ g·b)`, identity `X̃ → R̃` (evaluation at `1`) and composition induced by
`C^0(G, Ã) → C^0(G × G, Ã)`, `f ↦ ((g,h) ↦ f(gh))` in edge coordinates — the action groupoid of `G` on `X̃`, with all objects affinoid
perfectoid. This is the generalized-affinoid presentation of [ECD] §15: `(A, A⁺)` need not be
sheafy, while `X̃` and `R̃` are affinoid perfectoid. `R̃` is an equivalence relation only in the
category of v-sheaves (DiamondsAndVStacks layer D6): on underlying sets
`|R̃| → |X̃| ×_{|Spa A|} |X̃|` is surjective but not injective. Define
the structure `Huber.PerfectoidTorsorPresentation p P` for `P = (A, A⁺)` (`p.Prime`, `G : ProfiniteGrp`, a
complete perfectoid pair `(Ã, Ã⁺)` with continuous `G`-action, a `G`-invariant `q`, and axioms
(a), (b)); define `ofTower` (for a finite étale torsor tower `T` over `A`, take `G = lim G_i` and
`(Ã, Ã⁺) = (Â_∞, Â_∞⁺)`, assembled field by field from [*perfectoid-uniform-completion*](#p1-32-split-tate-rings) (P1.32),
`completionAction_spec` (*completed-tower-pair*), the self-product identification of
[*completed-tower-self-product*](../AdicEtaleGeometry/README.md) (AdicEtaleGeometry A4.5) (axiom (a)), the perfectoid relation from

`(C^0(G, Ã), C^0(G, Ã⁺))` with `relation.source`, `relation.target`,
