**Checks.**

- *nonprime_indices* — `PerfectoidTorsorPresentation` over `(Q₂,ℤ₂)` is empty at parameters 0 and 1 and inhabited at parameter 2.

- *relation_source* — source applied to that point is `x` (`spa_relation_source`).

- *quotient_trivial* (degenerate) — the quotient homeomorphism of `ofPerfectoid` sends `[x]`

### P6.17 comparison interfaces with diamonds

**`Spd` of a Tate Huber pair and the perfectoid torsor.**
(*spd-of-tate-huber-pair-and-perfectoid-torsor*) The analytic half of [ECD] §15 — Lem. 15.3,

supplied by this layer is the declaration `Huber.PerfectoidTorsorPresentation.exists`: for a prime
`p`, every Huber pair `(A, A⁺)` with `A` a complete Hausdorff Tate ring in which `p` is

DiamondsAndVStacks layer D6's targets *spd-of-a-tate-pair* (D6.1) and *spd-is-a-spatial-diamond*
(D6.3), which consume this record (for a Tate `ℤ_p`-algebra that is not complete, through its
completion, as in the conventions of this layer) and justify nothing here. *Needs:*
[*perfectoid-cover-presentation*](#p6-16) (P6.16). README only (no Lean declaration).

- The analytic presentation of `ℚ_p` has completed pair `(ℂ_p,O_ℂ_p)`.
- For a perfectoid pair the analytic input uses the original plus ring and trivial group.
- On the underlying space, a nontrivial stabilizer gives distinct groupoid arrows with the same endpoints; set-level injectivity cannot replace the diamond interpretation.

#### Presentation examples

For `(ℚ_p, ℤ_p)`, the tower of finite Galois extensions has uniform completion `ℂ_p`.
Its profinite limit group `G` gives `ℂ_p ⊗̂ᵘ_{ℚ_p} ℂ_p ≅ C^0(G, ℂ_p)` and
`|Spa ℂ_p|/G = |Spa ℚ_p|`. For `(ℚ_p⟨T⟩, ℤ_p⟨T⟩)`, the completed tower is
perfectoid although the original ring is not: approximate p-power roots of `T`
modulo `ϖ^p` exist in its power-bounded subring. The incomplete ring `ℚ_p[T]`
illustrates the completeness hypothesis. A perfectoid pair has the trivial
presentation with `G = 1`.

The following Checks specify the presentation's carrier, action, plus ring,
quotient and groupoid maps; their statements are README targets.

| Definition | Checks |
| --- | --- |
| `Huber.PerfectoidTorsorPresentation` | *presentation_prime*, *test_Qp*, *test_perfectoid*, *test_relation_not_injective* |
| `Huber.PerfectoidTorsorPresentation.q` | *tower_structure_map*, *perfectoid_identity_map*, *presentation_base_invariant* |
| `Huber.PerfectoidTorsorPresentation.ofTower` | *tower_carriers*, *tower_structure_map*, *test_finite_level*, *completion_test_Qp*, *completion_test_trivial* |
| `Huber.PerfectoidTorsorPresentation.relation` | *relation_plus_constants*, *relation_plus_pointwise*, *relation_plus_target* |
| `Huber.PerfectoidTorsorPresentation.relation.source` | *relation_source_values*, *relation_unit_source*, *relation_source* |
| `Huber.PerfectoidTorsorPresentation.relation.target` | *relation_target_values*, *relation_unit_target*, *relation_identity* |
| `Huber.PerfectoidTorsorPresentation.relation.unit` | *relation_unit_value*, *relation_unit_source*, *relation_unit_target* |
| `Huber.PerfectoidTorsorPresentation.relation.composition` | *relation_composition_value*, *relation_composition_units*, *relation_composition_associative*, *relation_composition_noncommutative* |
| `Huber.PerfectoidTorsorPresentation.uniformCompletedTensorEquiv` | *presentation_tensor_left*, *presentation_tensor_right*, *presentation_tensor_plus* |
| `Huber.PerfectoidTorsorPresentation.spaQuotientHomeomorph` | *quotient_projection*, *quotient_fibre*, *quotient_trivial* |
| `Huber.PerfectoidTorsorPresentation.spa_relation_homeomorph` | *relation_evaluation*, *relation_source*, *relation_identity* |
| `Huber.PerfectoidTorsorPresentation.ofPerfectoid` | *perfectoid_identity_map*, *quotient_trivial*, *test_perfectoid*, *perfectoid_not_Qp* |

- *presentation_prime* — the perfectoid parameter cannot be 0 or 1.
- *presentation_base_invariant* — q is fixed pointwise by the action.
- *relation_plus_constants* — a constant function is integral exactly at its value.
- *relation_plus_pointwise* — every value, not just the identity value, must be integral.
- *relation_plus_target* — an orbit function of an integral element is integral.
- *relation_source_values* — source has the same value at two group elements.
- *relation_target_values* — target is the orbit function and starts at a.
- *relation_unit_value* — the unit selects identity evaluation.
- *relation_unit_source* — source restricted along the unit is the identity.
- *relation_unit_target* — target restricted along the unit is the identity.
- *relation_composition_value* — two edges multiply in traversal order.
- *relation_composition_units* — either identity edge can be deleted.
- *relation_composition_associative* — rebracketing three edges does not change the value.
- *presentation_tensor_left* — the left tensor insertion is constant.
- *presentation_tensor_right* — the right insertion evaluates the action.
- *presentation_tensor_plus* — the isomorphism preserves the entire plus ring.
- *test_spa_target_convention* — evaluation at `(g, x)` followed by the target map gives the
  pullback of `x` along the ring action of `g`, which is `g⁻¹ • x`: the ring action is pulled back
  contravariantly (it follows from `spa_relation_target`).
- *tower_continuousMap_perfectoid* — for `ofTower T`, every `C^0(G^k, Â_∞)` is perfectoid,
  `k = 0` included (it follows from `relation_isPerfectoid`).
- *action_inverse_three* — On the regular `ℤ/3` torsor, `galoisTensorMap` of `1 ⊗ δ₁` has value 1 at group coordinate 1 and the identity point, but value 0 at group coordinate 2.
- *relation_composition_noncommutative* — For a presentation with group identified with permutations of three letters, `relation.composition` of the function detecting `g(0) = 1` gives 1 on `((01),(12))` and 0 in the opposite order.

### Examples

The worked examples of this layer are the checks above: `Spa(C_p, O_{C_p})`, the perfectoid disc
and the empty space as `κ`-small and uniformly `κ`-small spaces, with the one-point space over a field
of cardinality `≥ κ`, the disjoint union of `κ` points and the `ω₁`-indexed disjoint unions over
cofinal fields `K_α` as the non-examples that separate the notions for singular `κ`; rational
subsets, the identity and the origin of the perfectoid disc as affinoid pro-étale maps, the open
unit disc as a pro-étale map that is not affinoid pro-étale, and `Spa(K) × {x} ↪ Spa(K) × S` as a
pro-étale map that is not open; `X × S` for finite `S`, for `S = {pt}`, `∅` and `Z_p`, against
the disjoint union of `#S` copies; and, in the subsections, `Pro(FinSet) ≃ Profinite ≃ Spa(C, O_C)_proét^aff`, the origin `Spa(K, K°) = lim_n {|T| ≤ |p|ⁿ}` as a Zariski closed immersion
that is affinoid pro-étale and not étale, and `R ↠ C⁰(ℤ_p, ℂ_p)` for `I = (T − 1)`.

`doubled_disc_overlap` uses the geometric pushout of two closed discs along the open unit disc.
The fibre product of the two chart inclusions is not affinoid, testing the affine-base hypothesis
in the fibre-product statement.

The Lean `example`s of `Suggested.lean` for this layer check that no perfectoid space is `0`-small
(smallness is a strict bound) and that `ProKappa 0 C` is empty.

## Layer P7: tilde-limits and Frobenius-controlled towers

The layer builds tilde-limits `X ~ lim_i X_i` of analytic adic spaces and their perfectoid form,
the residue-field variant of Scholze's perfectoid paper, and the good affinoid perfectoid subsets
through which a tilde-limit is computed at a finite level; Frobenius-controlled integral towers
with their completion, the uniformity bound and the perfectoid Frobenius criterion that makes their
completed generic fibre a perfectoid tilde-limit; preperfectoid spaces and the strong completion;
cofinality witnesses for towers indexed by compact open subgroups; the uniqueness and
representability of perfectoid tilde-limits, their comparison with inverse limits of represented
functors (the comparison with diamonds belongs to DiamondsAndVStacks), their restriction to opens
and rational subsets, étale and finite étale base change and gluing; the limit of a tower of perfectoid spaces with affinoid transition maps; the
comparison of étale topoi along a tilde-limit of noetherian adic spaces; and the regular finite flat
towers of Česnavičius whose completion is perfectoid. AdicSpacesPartII R0.20.1 owns the intrinsic
tilde-limit relation; this layer adds the perfectoid specialisations.

### P7.1 tilde-limits of analytic adic spaces

**Tilde-limits of analytic adic spaces.** (*tilde-limit-of-analytic-adic-spaces*) Let `I` be a
small cofiltered category, `(X_i)_{i ∈ I}` a diagram of analytic adic spaces (the Foundations of
adic spaces roadmap (AdicSpaces), layer 5) whose transition maps are quasicompact and
quasiseparated, and `X` an analytic adic space with compatible morphisms `φ_i : X → X_i`. Two
separate conditions: (T) the continuous map `|X| → lim_i |X_i|` is a homeomorphism; (D) every
`x ∈ X` has an open affinoid neighbourhood `U = Spa(A, A⁺)` such that, writing the morphisms
`U → X_i` through open affinoid subspaces `Spa(A_i, A_i⁺) ⊆ X_i`, the union over `i` of the images
of `A_i → A` is dense in `A`. `X ~ lim_i X_i` (`X` is a tilde-limit of the `X_i`) means (T) and (D).
Neither `X` nor the `X_i` is required to be quasicompact or locally noetherian; the perfectoid
tilde-limits of P7.2 are the tilde-limits whose `X` is perfectoid. AdicSpacesPartII R0.20.1 owns the
intrinsic relation `AdicSpace.IsTildeLimit` with its affinoid criterion
(*tilde-limits-affinoid-criterion*: `AdicSpace.IsTildeLimit.affinoid` and the completed-direct-limit
criterion, the latter specified in AdicSpacesPartII R0.20.1's README only); P7.1 uses only this sub-target. The base change
`AdicSpace.IsTildeLimit.baseChange` (*tilde-limit-base-change*, AdicSpacesPartII R0.20.2) is used in P7.12.
P7 specializes the intrinsic relation to analytic Yoneda carriers.
Here `AdicSpace.IsTildeLimit` expresses its analytic Yoneda form (the
predicate (T) and (D) on `X`, the system and the cone); prove `IsTildeLimit.homeomorph` (the
homeomorphism `|X| ≃ lim_i |X_i|`) and `IsTildeLimit.dense_image` (the density clause (D) at every
point) ([SW13] §2.4, Definition 2.4.1, pp. 19–20, which does not require the spaces to be analytic).
The comparison with the arbitrary-open density condition of [Huber96] §2.4,
Definition 2.4.2, p. 125 is `PerfectoidSpace.IsTildeLimit.toHuber` in P7.2. *Needs:* AdicSpaces
layer 5; Mathlib `CategoryTheory.IsCofiltered`, `TopCat.limitCone`, `Dense`.

**Comparison with the intrinsic supplier.** `AdicSpace.IsTildeLimit.ofAdicSpace_iff`
states, for a small cofiltered diagram `D : I ⥤ TauCeti.AdicSpace` and cone `c`,

`AdicSpace.IsTildeLimit (D ⋙ ofAdicSpace) (ofAdicSpace.mapCone c)   ↔ AdicSpacesPartII.AdicSpace.IsTildeLimit D c.`

Its hypotheses are analyticity of `ofAdicSpace.obj c.pt` and of every
`ofAdicSpace.obj (D.obj i)`, and `AdicSpace.Qcqs (ofAdicSpace.map (D.map a))`
for every transition `a`. Honesty follows from the `TauCeti.AdicSpace` carriers.
Neither compactness of the levels nor a perfectoid apex is assumed. These
extra analytic and transition hypotheses belong to P7's Yoneda form; the
PartIV relation itself imposes only topology and density. Transport identifies
the point maps with the same cone projections and identifies sheafy affinoid
charts and their ring maps ([SW13] Definition 2.4.1, pp. 19–20; AdicSpacesPartII R0.20.1).

**Checks for the comparison.**

- `IsTildeLimit_ofAdicSpace_constant` — an analytic identity cone satisfies the
  Yoneda relation, including the nonperfectoid case `Spa(ℚ_p, ℤ_p)`.
- `IsTildeLimit_ofAdicSpace_empty` — a diagram of empty honest spaces with empty
  apex satisfies both relations.
- `IsTildeLimit_ofAdicSpace_nonanalytic` — the intrinsic relation holds for the
  identity cone on a nonanalytic honest space, whereas the Yoneda analytic form
  fails. Thus the analytic hypothesis in the equivalence is essential.

**Density on Yoneda charts.** (*yoneda-tilde-limit-dense-charts*)
`AdicSpace.HasDenseCharts` is the chart-density clause in the analytic Yoneda
comparison, using `AdicSpace.chartImage` and open affinoid factorizations
([SW13] Definition 2.4.1, pp. 19–20). The general adic-space predicate and
completed-affinoid criterion remain AdicSpacesPartII R0.20.1’s supplier contracts.

**Checks.**

- `tildeLimit_const` (degenerate) — `X ~ lim X` for the constant diagram.
- `tildeLimit_perfectoid_torus` (computation) — `Spa ℂ_p⟨T^{±1/p^∞}⟩ ~ lim_n Spa ℂ_p⟨T^{±1/p^n}⟩`,
  with (D) witnessed by the Laurent polynomials in `T^{1/p^n}` ([Sch13] Example 4.4, p. 23;
  [SW13] Proposition 2.4.2, p. 20). Downstream,
  [`PerfectoidTowers.Perfectoid.TorsorDescent.rootTorusTower_exists`](../PerfectoidTowers/README.md#layer-p9-continuous-torsor-descent-with-coefficients) contains this example as its
  specialization to `ℂ_p`, with a chosen compatible system of primitive roots of unity, its
  `ProetaleGaloisTower.tilde` field giving the global predicate and its coordinate equations the
  finite-level maps; PerfectoidTowers is not an input here.
- `tildeLimit_not_uncompleted` (non-example) — the uncompleted colimit `colim ℂ_p⟨T^{±1/p^n}⟩` is
  not complete, so it is not the ring `O(X)` of the tilde-limit (its `Spa`, as an adic space, is
  that of its completion, Tau Ceti `TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.spaCompletionHomeomorph`); the
  completion is required for the ring, not for the space. The example states that the
  union of the finite-level function images in `perfectedTateAlgebra.laurent` is dense
  and is not a complete subset: the convergent series `∑_{n≥0} p^{n+1}T^{1/p^{n+1}}`
  lies outside it. The inherited topology is the common `p`-adic Tate topology
  ([Sch13] Example 4.4, p. 23; [SW13] Proposition 2.4.2, p. 20).
- `isTildeLimit_affinoid` (compatibility) — the affinoid predicate `IsTildeLimit_affinoid` on
  a filtered system of Huber pairs `(A_j, A_j⁺)` with a cone to `(R, R⁺)` (no perfectoid
  hypothesis on `R`) is (T) for `Spa(R, R⁺) → lim Spa(A_j, A_j⁺)` (an embedding with image the
  compatible families) together with (D) for the single affinoid `U = Spa(R, R⁺)` and the levels
  `V = Spa(A_j, A_j⁺)`: `⋃_j im(A_j → R)` dense in `R`; when the source and target pairs are complete and sheafy with Tate coordinate rings, it
  implies (T) and (D) above and is the
  form in which the checks of P7.2 are stated. The matching example applies
  `PerfectoidSpace.IsTildeLimit_affinoid.isTildeLimit` to this same cone.
- `isTildeLimit_affinoid_Qp` (computation) — the identity cone on `Spa(ℚ_p, ℤ_p)`
  is an analytic tilde-limit, without a perfectoid hypothesis.

- `tildeLimit_empty` (degenerate) — the identity cone on the zero affinoid has empty point space
  and is a global tilde-limit.
- `tildeLimit_density_needed_global` (non-example) — the global cone from `Spa(C_p)` to the
  constant `Spa(Q_p)` system fails section density, despite having the correct point space.

- `tildeLimit_test_malformedDiagram` (non-example) — on the one-object system of the
  dual-number pair over `ℂ_p`, setting the identity transition to `a + bε ↦ a` violates
  the diagram identity: `ε ↦ 0 ≠ ε`. The affinoid predicate rejects it.
- `tildeLimit_test_dualNumberTwoTerm` (convention) — the reduction homomorphism from the
  dual-number pair to `ℂ_p` satisfies `IsTildeLimit_affinoid` for the one-object system.
  In its source `(a + bε)² = a² + 2abε`; the same homomorphism sends this square to `a²`
  and kills the nonzero element `ε`, including when `p = 2`. This uses the affinoid comparison
  with AdicSpacesPartII R0.20.1, with the nonreduced behaviour of [SW13] Proposition 2.4.4, p. 20.

For a small filtered category `J`, a functor `B : J ⥤ CAff` and a cocone `b`,
`PerfectoidSpace.IsTildeLimit_affinoid.isTildeLimit` assumes that all `B_j` and `b.pt`
are sheafy with Tate coordinate rings (completeness and Hausdorffness are part of `CAff`).
The affinoid predicate is evaluated on the ring maps `B.map` and `b.ι.app`.
Its conclusion is `AdicSpace.IsTildeLimit (B.op ⋙ S) (S.mapCone b.op)`, where `S`
is the lift of `spaYFunctor` to `YonedaAdicSpace`: the apex is `ofSpaY b.pt`, and the
projection to `ofSpaY (B.obj j)` is induced by `b.ι.app j`. Thus (T) uses these precise
maps and (D) is witnessed by the whole affinoid chart. Maps between these affinoids
are qcqs; no separate transition hypothesis is needed. This is the analytic Yoneda
comparison with AdicSpacesPartII R0.20.1's `IsTildeLimit.affinoid`, not another intrinsic
criterion ([SW13] Definition 2.4.1, pp. 19–20).

The global carrier of this analytic tilde-limit is the Yoneda-adic category supplied by
AdicEtaleGeometry A1.16, into which perfectoid spaces embed through `YonedaAdicSpace.ofAdicSpace`.
`YonedaAdicSpace.IsAnalytic` means a cover by Tate affinoids ([Berkeley] Definition 4.3.2,
printed p. 33). Affinoid sheafiness is AdicEtaleGeometry's `R.Sheafy` for an object `R` of `CAff`, namely Tau
Ceti's `IsSheafyForEveryPresentation` on the plus ring. `AdicSpace.IsHonest` means that every point
lies in an open affinoid chart satisfying this predicate; the same predicate supplies the
finite-level hypothesis of `Perfectoid.FrobeniusTower.isTildeLimit` and the sheafiness
hypotheses of `GoodAffinoid.isUniformCompletion` and `IsPreperfectoid.closedSubspace`.
**Checks.** `IsHonest_empty` holds for an empty point space; `IsHonest_sheafy_affinoid`
holds for `ofSpaY R` given `R.Sheafy`; `IsHonest_perfectoid` holds for every
`PerfectoidSpace.Perfd p`, using its sheafy perfectoid charts (P2.6).
Both the source and the levels of `IsTildeLimit` are analytic and honest. `Qcqs` tests inverse
images of affinoid open charts for quasicompactness and quasiseparatedness. `chartImage` includes
all finite-level affinoid factorizations, with their ring maps. `HasDenseCharts` imposes
density on an open cover. The homeomorphism is fixed by
`IsTildeLimit.homeomorph_apply`: its coordinates are the cone maps. For initial reindexing,
analyticity, honesty and qcqs transitions of the original diagram remain hypotheses ([SW13] Definition 2.4.1, pp. 19–20).

### P7.2 perfectoid tilde-limits

The next three subsections fix the perfectoid form of the tilde-limit, the residue-field variant of
Scholze's perfectoid paper, and the good affinoid perfectoid subsets through which a tilde-limit is
computed at a finite level.

**Perfectoid tilde-limits `X ~ lim X_i` of analytic adic spaces.** (*perfectoid-tilde-limit*) Fix a
prime `p`. Let `I` be a small cofiltered category, `i ↦ X_i` a functor from `I` to analytic adic
spaces (AdicSpaces layer 5: every point analytic, sheafy) whose transition morphisms
`f_a : X_j → X_i` (`a : j → i`) are quasicompact and quasiseparated, `X` a perfectoid space in the
sense of P2.10 ([ECD] Definition 3.19: locally `Spa(R, R⁺)` with `R` a perfectoid Tate ring in the
sense of [ECD] Definition 3.1, of characteristic `0` or `p`, no base field; sheafy by P2.6), and
`φ = (φ_i : X → X_i)_i` a compatible family of morphisms of adic spaces (`f_a ∘ φ_j = φ_i`). The
pair `(X, φ)` is a perfectoid tilde-limit of `(X_i)`, written `X ~ lim_i X_i`, if it is a
tilde-limit in the sense of *tilde-limit-of-analytic-adic-spaces*, i.e. (a) the continuous map
`|X| → lim_i |X_i|` into the limit of the underlying topological spaces (Mathlib `TopCat.limitCone`)
is a homeomorphism, and (b) every `x ∈ X` has an open affinoid neighbourhood `U = Spa(A, A⁺) ⊆ X`
such that the union, over `i ∈ I` and over open subsets `V ⊆ X_i` with `φ_i(U) ⊆ V`, of the images
of the restriction maps `O_{X_i}(V) → A` is dense in `A`. Conventions: (i) the index category is
cofiltered and only the transition maps, not the `X_i`, are required to be quasicompact and
quasiseparated; (ii) no perfectoid base field is fixed: the `X_i` may be of characteristic `0` or
`p`, and `X` may lie over a different base than the `X_i` ([CHJ] Theorem 2.8: the `X_i` over `Q_p`,
`X` perfectoid; Scholze's universal cover of an affinoid over `Q_p` with limit over `C_p`); (iii)
the two conditions (a) and (b) are independent and both are required (the checks
`isTildeLimit_test_density_needed` and `isTildeLimit_test_topology_needed`); (iv) a tilde-limit is
not a categorical limit in adic spaces: `X ~ X_0` may hold with `X ≇ X_0` ([SW13] §2.4, after
Proposition 2.4.4, p. 20). Equivalent forms of (b), used throughout the layer: (b′) there is an
open cover of `X` by affinoids `U = Spa(A, A⁺)` for which `colim_{(i, V)} O_{X_i}(V) → A` has dense
image, `V` running over open affinoids of `X_i` through which `U → X_i` factors ([SW13] §2.4,
Definition 2.4.1, p. 19); (b″) the same with `U` affinoid perfectoid and `V` a quasicompact open at
one level (the good affinoid perfectoids of P7.4; [Survey] §2, Definition 2.20 and Remark 2.21,
p. 11). The equivalences (b) ⇔ (b′) ⇔ (b″) given (a) are *good-affinoid-perfectoid-basis*. Only the
density clause is formulated with sections; the weaker residue-field variant of [Sch12] Definition
7.14 is P7.3. In `PerfectoidSpace`, abbreviate `IsTildeLimit` by `AdicSpace.IsTildeLimit` on the underlying
adic spaces, `IsTildeLimit.homeomorph` (`|X| ≃ lim_i |X_i|` induced by `φ`) and
`IsTildeLimit.dense` (every `x ∈ X` has an affinoid open neighbourhood `U` with
`⋃_{i, V ⊇ φ_i(U)} im(O_{X_i}(V) → O_X(U))` dense in `O_X(U)`, with `U` sheafy);
prove `IsTildeLimit.toHuber`: for a perfectoid apex `X`, honest analytic levels `X_i`,
qcqs transition maps, and qcqs point spaces of `X` and every `X_i`, the perfectoid
predicate is equivalent to Huber's two conditions. The first is a homeomorphism
induced by the cone projections; the second uses sections on arbitrary opens, as
specified by - `isTildeLimit_test_empty` (degenerate): the identity cone on a zero perfectoid
  pair is a perfectoid tilde-limit. Together with `isTildeLimit_test_const` and the global
  `isTildeLimit_test_density_needed`, this tests the global predicate itself.

`PerfectoidSpace.openChartImage` below. Huber's setting is qcqs
pseudo-adic spaces and adic morphisms ([Huber96] §2.4.1 and Definition 2.4.2, p. 125);
this comparison concerns honest analytic adic spaces, regarded as pseudo-adic
spaces with their full point spaces. Morphisms between these analytic spaces are
adic (AdicSpacesPartII R0.1, `Huber.IsAdicHom.of_isTateRing`). Prove also `IsTildeLimit.iff_goodCover` (`X ~ lim X_i`
iff (a) holds and `X` is covered by good affinoid perfectoids; *good-affinoid-perfectoid-basis*),
`IsTildeLimit.lift` (for a perfectoid space `Y`, compatible maps `ψ_i : Y → X_i` factor uniquely as
`φ_i ∘ g`; *tilde-limit-perfectoid-uniqueness*), `IsTildeLimit.uniqueIso` (two perfectoid
tilde-limits of the same system are uniquely isomorphic compatibly with the cones),
`IsTildeLimit.ofIso` (transport along an isomorphism `X ≅ X'` commuting with the cones),
`IsTildeLimit.open_baseChange` (restriction to the preimage of an open subset at a finite level;
*tilde-limit-rational-restriction*), `IsTildeLimit.reindex` (invariance under an initial change of
index category; *tilde-limit-cofinal-change*), `IsTildeLimit.const` (the constant system on a
perfectoid space with the identity cone is a tilde-limit) and `IsTildeLimit.spectralSpace` (if all
`X_i` are qcqs, `|X|` is a spectral space and each `φ_i` is a spectral map; [Sch12] §7, Remark 7.15,
p. 44; AdicSpacesPartII R0.19.5–R0.19.8 and P5.4’s perfectoid limit comparisons) ([SW13] §2.4, Definition 2.4.1, pp. 19–20). *Needs:*
*tilde-limit-of-analytic-adic-spaces*; P2.10; P2.6; Mathlib
`CategoryTheory.IsCofiltered`, `TopCat.limitCone`.

**Checks.**

- `isTildeLimit_test_perfectoidDisc` (computation) — for an integral perfectoid ring `S`,
  a regular parameter `π`, `π`-adic completeness and `π^p ∣ p`, the generic cone of
  `FrobeniusTower.disc S π hπ hp` satisfies the global `PerfectoidSpace.IsTildeLimit`.
  Its stages are the completed disc algebras with transition `T ↦ T^p`.
- `isTildeLimit_test_perfectoidTorus` (computation) — for a complete nonarchimedean
  perfectoid normed field `K` of characteristic zero, topologically nilpotent `p`,
  `PseudoUniformizerRoots p K`, and compatible primitive `p^n`-th roots of unity,
  the torus tilde-limit is `K⟨T^{±1/p^∞}⟩` with transitions `T ↦ T^p`.
  The example uses `FrobeniusTower`: each integral stage is the completion of
  `K°[T, T⁻¹]` along `ϖ`, the transitions fix coefficients and raise `T` to its
  `p`-th power, and the completed generic cone satisfies `PerfectoidSpace.IsTildeLimit`.
  The projection pulls the level-`n` coordinate back to `T^{1/p^n}`.
  This existence statement holds without choosing roots of unity; with compatible
  primitive roots, [`PerfectoidTowers.Perfectoid.TorsorDescent.rootTorusTower_exists`](../PerfectoidTowers/README.md#layer-p9-continuous-torsor-descent-with-coefficients)
  equips it with the Galois action downstream (not an input here) ([Sch13] Example 4.4, p. 23,
  and Lemma 4.10(iii–iv), pp. 26–27).
- `isTildeLimit_test_const` (degenerate) — for a perfectoid space `X` and the constant system
  `X_i = X` (`I` the one-object category) with `φ = id`, `X ~ lim X_i`; more generally any
  isomorphism `X ≅ X_0` of adic spaces with `X` perfectoid exhibits `X ~ X_0`.
- `isTildeLimit_test_not_categorical` (non-example) — set `K = C_p`. The quotient
  `φ : K[ε]/(ε²) → K` satisfies the single-affinoid predicate `IsTildeLimit_affinoid`
  for the one-object diagram, while `φ` is not injective. Thus this affinoid
  tilde-limit condition does not force the cone map to be an isomorphism.
  The pair on `DualNumber C_p` has plus ring `O_{C_p} + C_p ε`, and `φ(a + bε) = a`.
  Its product topology has ring of definition `O_{C_p} ⊕ O_{C_p} ε`.
  Every valuation kills `ε`, so the map on spectra is a homeomorphism of one-point
  spaces; the coefficient map is surjective and kills the nonzero element `ε`.
  This concretely illustrates the distinction following [SW13] Proposition 2.4.4, p. 20.
- `isTildeLimit_test_density_needed` (non-example) — the point `Spa(C_p, O_{C_p})` with its map to
  the constant system `Spa(Q_p, Z_p)` satisfies (a) (both spaces are one point) but not (b) (`Q_p`
  is not dense in `C_p`); (a) alone does not define tilde-limits.
- `isTildeLimit_test_topology_needed` (non-example) — for a nonzero perfectoid Tate ring `R` and
  `X = Spa(R⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩)`, mapping `X` into the first summand of `X_n := D_n ⊔ D_n`
  (`D_n = Spa(R⟨T^{1/p^n}⟩)`) satisfies (b) but not (a) (`|X| → lim |X_n|` misses the second
  summand); (b) alone does not define tilde-limits. The example uses `FrobeniusTower.disc`
  for an integral perfectoid ring `S`, a regular nonunit `ϖ`, `ϖ`-adic completeness and
  `ϖ^p ∣ p`. Natural first and second inclusions, with a binary coproduct at every level,
  specify the doubled diagram. The first-summand cone has `AdicSpace.HasDenseCharts` and
  an embedding on points, but misses a compatible family in the second summands; it
  therefore fails the global `PerfectoidSpace.IsTildeLimit` predicate. The nonunit
  hypothesis excludes the empty generic fibre ([SW13] Definition 2.4.1, pp. 19–20).
- `isTildeLimit_test_huber_compat` (compatibility) — for a perfectoid `X`, honest analytic
  `X_i`, qcqs transitions, and qcqs `X` and `X_i`, `IsTildeLimit.toHuber` identifies the
  perfectoid predicate with the projection-compatible homeomorphism and arbitrary-open
  section density of [Huber96] Definition 2.4.2, p. 125.

`PerfectoidSpace.openChartImage D c R u` is the subset of `R.A` obtained from
sections on all finite-level opens: choose `i`, an open immersion `v : V → D_i`,
and a factorization `f : Spa^Y(R) → V` with `f ≫ v = u ≫ φ_i`. A coefficient `r`
belongs to the image exactly when some `s : globalFunctions V` pulls back to
`toGlobalFunctions R r`. For sheafy `R`, this is the image in `O_X(U) = R.A`;
`V` need not be affinoid or quasicompact. These are the sections in [Huber96]
Definition 2.4.2(b), p. 125, using AdicEtaleGeometry A1.16's `globalFunctions`,
`globalFunctions.map`, `toGlobalFunctions`, and `IsOpenImmersion`.
`IsTildeLimit.dense` gives this density without requiring qcqs total spaces.

**Checks for `openChartImage`.**

- `openChartImage_constant` — the identity cone on `Spa^Y(R)` has image all of `R.A`,
  since the whole finite-level open and its identity restriction supply every coefficient.
- `openChartImage_zero` — for a zero coordinate ring and any chart map into a cone
  over a cofiltered category, the image is `{0}`; the index category is nonempty.
- `openChartImage_nondense` — for the constant `Spa(Q_p, Z_p)` system with apex
  `Spa(C_p, O_{C_p})`, even sections on arbitrary opens have nondense image in `C_p`.
  The only nonempty open of the finite-level point is the whole point.

The predicate `PerfectoidSpace.IsTildeLimit p D c` records that `c.pt` is perfectoid and
that `AdicSpace.IsTildeLimit D c` holds. Thus its topology and density are exactly those of P7.1.
`IsTildeLimit.lift` quantifies over every perfectoid source and every compatible cone, and
`uniqueIso` requires compatibility with every projection ([SW13] Proposition 2.4.5, pp. 20–21).

### P7.3 residue-field tilde-limits

**Residue-field tilde-limits `X ~′ lim X_i` over locally noetherian adic spaces.**
(*residue-field-tilde-limit*) Let `I` be a small cofiltered category, `(X_i)` an `I`-indexed system
of quasicompact quasiseparated locally noetherian analytic adic spaces (AdicSpacesPartII R0.6:
covered by `Spa(A, A⁺)` with `A` a complete strongly noetherian Tate ring; the transition maps are
then automatically qcqs), `X` a perfectoid space and `φ = (φ_i : X → X_i)` a compatible family.
Then `X ~′ lim X_i` (Scholze's notation `X ~ lim X_i` of Definition 7.14, written `~′` in [SW13]
after Theorem 2.4.7) means: (a) `|X| → lim_i |X_i|` is a homeomorphism, and (c) for every `x ∈ X`
with images `x_i = φ_i(x)`, the map of completed residue fields `colim_i k(x_i)^ → k(x)^` has dense
image, where `k(y)^` is the completion of the residue field of `O_{Y,y}` for the valuation of `y`
(equivalently, `colim_i k(x_i) → k(x)` has dense image for the valuation topologies). No perfectoid
base field is fixed ([Sch12] works over a perfectoid field `K`; the definition and the results of
P7.15 use only that `X` is perfectoid and the `X_i` are qcqs locally noetherian); by Remark 7.15,
(a) forces `|X|` to be spectral, in particular `X` quasicompact and quasiseparated. The density
condition is pointwise on residue fields; the sectionwise condition of P7.2 implies it
(see *tilde-limit-implies-residue-field-tilde-limit*). In `PerfectoidSpace`, define
`IsResidueFieldTildeLimit` (the structure with fields `homeomorph` and `residueField_dense`),
`IsResidueFieldTildeLimit.homeomorph` (`|X| ≃ lim |X_i|`) and
`IsResidueFieldTildeLimit.residueField_dense` (for every `x`, `colim_i k(x_i)^ → k(x)^` has dense
image); prove `IsResidueFieldTildeLimit.spectralSpace` (`|X|` is spectral and `X` is qcqs; Remark
7.15), `IsResidueFieldTildeLimit.of_isTildeLimit` (every tilde-limit over qcqs locally noetherian
`X_i` is a residue-field tilde-limit), `IsResidueFieldTildeLimit.of_bijective` (for `X`
quasicompact and quasiseparated, bijectivity of `|X| → lim |X_i|` together with (c) already gives
(a); *residue-field-tilde-limit-etale-base-change*). The map into the compatible families
is defined by the cone legs, with compatibility given by cone naturality. Also prove
`IsResidueFieldTildeLimit.etale_baseChange` (for `Y → X_i` étale,
`Y ×_{X_i} X ~′ lim_j Y ×_{X_i} X_j`; Proposition 7.16) and `IsResidueFieldTildeLimit.reindex`
(invariance under an initial change of index category) ([Sch12] §7, Definition 7.14, pp. 43–44;
[Sch12] §7, Remark 7.15, p. 44; [SW13] §2.4, after Theorem 2.4.7, p. 21). *Needs:* AdicSpacesPartII
R0.6; P2.10; P2.5; AdicSpacesPartII R0.19.5–R0.19.8 and P5.4’s perfectoid limit comparisons; Mathlib `SpectralSpace`, `IsSpectralMap`.

**Checks.**

- `isResidueFieldTildeLimit_test_disc` (computation) — for a perfectoid field `K`,
  `Spa(K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, K°⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩) ~′ lim_n Spa(K⟨T^{1/p^n}⟩, K°⟨T^{1/p^n}⟩)`: the underlying
  spaces agree by the tilde-limit of the disc tower, and at every point the colimit of the residue
  fields is dense.
- `isResidueFieldTildeLimit_test_point` (degenerate) — for a perfectoid field `K`, the constant
  system `Spa(K, K°)` (noetherian, as `K` is a field) with the identity satisfies
  `Spa(K, K°) ~′ lim Spa(K, K°)`.
- `isResidueFieldTildeLimit_test_not_dense` (non-example) — `Spa(C_p, O_{C_p}) → Spa(Q_p, Z_p)`
  (constant system) satisfies (a) but not (c): `Q_p` is not dense in `C_p`.
- `isResidueFieldTildeLimit_test_of_tildeLimit` (compatibility) — if `X ~ lim X_i` in the sense of
  P7.2 and all `X_i` are qcqs locally noetherian, then `X ~′ lim X_i`.

- `isResidueFieldTildeLimit_test_empty` (degenerate): the zero affinoid's constant
  system has no residue-field conditions. The point, empty, closed-field-extension non-example
  and section-density implication are examples of `IsResidueFieldTildeLimit`.

An affinoid description of the pointwise condition uses
`AdicSpace.CompletedResidue R x = Completion (WithVal (residueFieldValuation x))`.
`residueMap` is the canonical evaluation from `R`; `residueImage` consists of fractions of
functions from a common finite-level affinoid chart, with nonzero denominator at the point and a
commuting square into the cone. The source chart may shrink around the point for each fraction.
`residueRestriction` is the continuous residue-field isomorphism for that open immersion,
fixed on evaluated functions by `residueRestriction_map`. It transports the fraction into the
fixed completed residue field. `affinoidPoints_naturality` requires the affinoid point
identifications to commute with the pinned maps of valuation spectra. Around each point of the source, `IsResidueFieldTildeLimit`
requires such fractions to be dense. The chart point is identified with the given global point
through the supplied spectrum homeomorphism. This expresses the residue condition through
valuation fields ([Sch12] Definition 7.14, pp. 43–44).

### P7.4 good affinoid perfectoid subsets

**Good affinoid perfectoid subsets of a tilde-limit.** (*good-affinoid-perfectoid*) Let
`(X_i)_{i∈I}` be as in P7.2, `X` a perfectoid space with a compatible cone `φ`. A good affinoid
perfectoid of `(X, φ)` is a triple `(W, i_0, V)` where `W = Spa(R, R⁺) ⊆ X` is an affinoid
perfectoid open subset (P2.9), `i_0 ∈ I` and `V ⊆ X_{i_0}` is a quasicompact open subset such that
(i) `W = φ_{i_0}^{-1}(V)`, and (ii) writing `V_a := f_a^{-1}(V) ⊆ X_j` for `a : j → i_0` (the slice
category `I/i_0`, cofiltered), the ring map `colim_{a ∈ (I/i_0)^op} O_{X_j}(V_a) → R` has dense
image, for the topology of `R` (no topology is placed on the colimit). When moreover the `V_a` are
affinoid, `V_a = Spa(A_a, A_a⁺)`, the pair `(R, R⁺)` is determined by the system
(see *good-affinoid-uniform-completion*). This is the form of Scholze's survey (the paragraph before
Proposition 2.22: dense image and homeomorphism with the limit of the finite-level affinoids), of
[Torsion] Theorem III.1.2(iii) and Definition III.3.5(i) (`V` the preimage of an affinoid `V_m` at
finite level, `lim H⁰(V_m, O) → H⁰(V, O)` with dense image), and of [CHJ] Theorem 2.8 (standard
affinoids pulled back from level `K(p^N)`). Under `X ~ lim X_i` the homeomorphism
`|W| ≅ lim_a |V_a|` is automatic, since `W` is the preimage of `V`. In `PerfectoidSpace`, define
`GoodAffinoid` (the data `(W, i_0, V)` with `W = φ_{i_0}^{-1}(V)` and dense image of
`colim_a O(V_a)` in `O(W)`) and `GoodAffinoid.level` (the level `i_0` and the finite-level
quasicompact open `V ⊆ X_{i_0}`); prove `GoodAffinoid.preimage_eq` (`W = φ_{i_0}^{-1}(V)`),
`GoodAffinoid.denseRange` (`colim_a O_{X_j}(V_a) → O_X(W)` has dense range),
`GoodAffinoid.homeomorph` (under `X ~ lim X_i`, `|W| ≃ lim_a |V_a|`), `GoodAffinoid.rationalSubset`
(a rational subset of `W` is good at a possibly larger level; *good-affinoid-perfectoid-basis*),
`GoodAffinoid.raise` (`(W, i_0, V)` is good at every level `j → i_0` with the preimage `V_a`),
`GoodAffinoid.isUniformCompletion` (if all `V_a` are affinoid, `O_X(W)` is the uniform completion
of `colim_a O(V_a)`; *good-affinoid-uniform-completion*) and `GoodAffinoid.finiteEtaleEquiv` (if
all `V_a` are affinoid, `FÉt(O_X(W)) ≃ 2-colim_a FÉt(O(V_a))`) ([Survey] §2, after Remark 2.21,
p. 11; [Survey] §2, Definition 2.20, p. 11; [Torsion] §III.1, Theorem III.1.2 (i)–(iii), p. 28;
[CHJ] §2, Theorem 2.8, p. 11). *Needs:* P2.9; Mathlib `CategoryTheory.IsCofiltered`.

**Checks.**

- `goodAffinoid_test_disc` (computation) — in the perfectoid disc tower over a perfectoid Tate
  ring `R`, `W = {|T| ≤ |ϖ|} ⊆ Spa(R⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩)` is good at level `0` with `V = {|T| ≤ |ϖ|}`: its
  coordinate ring is the rational localisation `R⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩⟨T/ϖ⟩`, and the image of
  `colim_n R⟨T^{1/p^n}⟩⟨T/ϖ⟩` contains the image of `R[T^{1/p^∞}, T/ϖ]`, which is dense.
- `goodAffinoid_test_empty` (degenerate) — the empty subset, with `V = ∅` at any level, is a good
  affinoid perfectoid (`R = 0`).
- `goodAffinoid_test_not_dense` (non-example) — for `Spa(C_p)` over the constant system
  `Spa(Q_p)`, `W = Spa(C_p)` is the preimage of `V = Spa(Q_p)` but `Q_p` is not dense in `C_p`, so
  `W` is not good.
- `goodAffinoid_test_ecd_limit` (compatibility) — if all `X_i = Spa(R_i, R_i⁺)` are affinoid
  perfectoid, the limit `Spa(R, R⁺)` of [ECD] Proposition 6.5 (`R⁺` the `ϖ`-adic completion of
  `colim R_i⁺`) is good at every level with `V = X_{i_0}`.

- `goodAffinoid_test_const` (computation): the whole constant perfectoid affinoid
  is good at the sole level and its chart has full image. The empty and nondense Checks likewise
  quantify over the full `GoodAffinoid` record, including its finite open.

The affinoid pieces of a tilde-limit are computed by their finite-level coordinate rings
(*good-affinoid-uniform-completion*): let `X ~ lim X_i` be a perfectoid tilde-limit and
`(W, i_0, V)` a good affinoid perfectoid (see *good-affinoid-perfectoid*), `W = Spa(R, R⁺)`, such that
every `V_a` (`a : j → i_0`) is affinoid, `V_a = Spa(A_a, A_a⁺)` (for instance when the transition
maps are affinoid), and let `(C, C⁺)` be the completed direct limit of the `(A_a, A_a⁺)`
(*tilde-limit-from-completed-colimit*, Tate case with a pseudouniformiser `ϖ ∈ A_{i_0}` that is
also one of `R`). Then (i) the canonical map `(C, C⁺) → (R, R⁺)` identifies `(R, R⁺)` with the
uniformization of `(C, C⁺)` ([KL15] §2.8, Definition 2.8.13, p. 63; AdicSpacesPartII R0.4),
`R⁺` being the integral closure of the closure of the image of `C⁺`, `Spa` being unchanged by
uniformization; in particular `R` (perfectoid, hence uniform, P1.1) is determined by the system
`(V_a)`; (ii) `GoodAffinoid.finiteEtaleEquiv` composes algebraic finite-stage descent
(AdicEtaleGeometry A1.0.3), AdicEtaleGeometry A1.0.5's `finiteEtale_completedColimit` for `L = colim_a A_a → C = L̂`, and
AdicEtaleGeometry A4.4's
`Huber.Pair.uniformization.baseChange_finiteEtale_equivalence` for `C → Cᵘ`,
then uses (i) to identify `Cᵘ` with `R`. This gives the scalar-extension equivalence
`2-colim_a FÉt(A_a) → FÉt(R)`, also for every rational localisation of `W`
pulled back from a finite level ([KL15] §2.8, Proposition 2.8.16(a), p. 64;
[Berkeley] Lecture 7, Theorem 7.4.8 and its following corollary, printed p. 54;
[SW13] §2.4, proof of Proposition 2.4.5, p. 21 (the form of (i) inside the uniqueness proof)).
*Needs:* *good-affinoid-perfectoid*; *tilde-limit-from-completed-colimit*; AdicSpacesPartII R0.4;
P1.1; AdicEtaleGeometry A1.0.5; AdicEtaleGeometry A1.16 (the Yoneda carrier), A1.0.3 and A4.4; Tau Ceti
`TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.mem_of_forall_vle_one`.

`GoodAffinoid` records the perfectoid pair of the chart, its open immersion, the finite level,
the quasicompact open immersion there, the equality of inverse images and density. Sections on
later inverse images are morphisms to the supplied affine line; equality after restriction to
an affinoid chart is equality of these morphisms. Consequently the density field also covers
nonaffinoid finite-level opens. `IsTildeLimit.iff_goodCover` assumes the topology of the limit,
analytic honest levels and qcqs transitions, and characterizes density by coverage with this
data ([Survey] Proposition 2.22, p. 11).

`affinoidFiniteEtaleDiagram` uses the finite étale categories of the specified
finite-level affinoids and algebraic scalar extension on arrows. Its Checks
`affinoidFiniteEtaleDiagram_identity`, `affinoidFiniteEtaleDiagram_zero` and
`affinoidFiniteEtaleDiagram_two` compute the identity transition, the zero algebra
and the split rank-two algebra. `GoodAffinoid.isUniformCompletion` gives the
universal mapping property against complete uniform Tate pairs;
`GoodAffinoid.finiteEtaleEquiv` identifies its inverse functor on every finite-stage
object with this scalar extension.

**Topology of a good chart.** (*good-affinoid-homeomorph*)
`GoodAffinoid.homeomorph` restricts the tilde-limit homeomorphism to the inverse
image of its finite-level open. Its coordinate formula is the given chart followed
by each cone projection ([SW13] Definition 2.4.1, pp. 19–20).

**Raising a good chart.** (*good-affinoid-raise*) `GoodAffinoid.raise` takes a
good chart and a qcqs transition `j → W.level`. `GoodAffinoid.raise_spec` fixes
the new level as `j`, preserves the chart image, and identifies the new finite-level
open with the inverse image of the old one ([Survey] proof of Proposition 2.22, p. 11).

**Finite étale algebras on a good chart.** (*good-affinoid-finite-etale-equivalence*)
`GoodAffinoid.finiteEtaleEquiv` uses a perfectoid tilde-limit, a good chart, and
a compatible sheafy Tate affinoid presentation of the finite-level inverse images.
Its inverse is scalar extension along the specified maps into the good chart’s ring;
`affinoidFiniteEtaleDiagram` supplies the diagram. It composes the
algebraic colimit equivalence of AdicEtaleGeometry A1.0.3, A1.0.5's
`finiteEtale_completedColimit`, the imported
`Huber.Pair.uniformization.baseChange_finiteEtale_equivalence`, and the ring
identification from `GoodAffinoid.isUniformCompletion`. The two completion steps
use [Berkeley] Theorem 7.4.8 and its corollary, printed p. 54, and [KL15]
Proposition 2.8.16(a), p. 64, respectively. The colimit may be nonseparated;
no injectivity or finite étaleness of the transition maps is required.

### P7.5 Frobenius-controlled integral towers

The next two subsections define the integral towers whose transition maps are eventually Frobenius
modulo `ϖ^p` and compute their completed generic fibre; that this generic fibre is a perfectoid
tilde-limit is P7.13.

**Frobenius-controlled integral towers.** (*frobenius-controlled-integral-tower*) Fix a prime `p`.
A Frobenius-controlled integral tower `(A_•⁺, ϖ, m_0, w)` consists of: (1) a sequence of rings
`A_0⁺ → A_1⁺ → A_2⁺ → ⋯` with transition maps `t_m : A_m⁺ → A_{m+1}⁺`; (2) an element `ϖ ∈ A_0⁺`
(its images again written `ϖ`), the compatible pseudouniformiser, such that every `A_m⁺` is
`ϖ`-torsion-free and `ϖ`-adically complete (Mathlib `IsAdicComplete (Ideal.span {ϖ}) A_m⁺`) and
`p ∈ ϖ^p A_0⁺` (the condition `ϖ^p | p` of [ECD] Definition 3.1, placed on the integral model);
then every `A_m⁺/ϖ^p` is an `F_p`-algebra and absolute Frobenius induces a ring homomorphism
`Φ_m : A_m⁺/ϖ → A_m⁺/ϖ^p`, `x ↦ x^p` (well defined because
`(x + ϖy)^p ≡ x^p mod pϖA_m⁺ + ϖ^pA_m⁺ = ϖ^pA_m⁺`); (3) the eventual Frobenius lifting condition
modulo `ϖ^p`: an index `m_0` and, for every `m ≥ m_0`, a ring isomorphism
`w_m : A_{m+1}⁺/ϖ ≅ A_m⁺/ϖ^p` such that (i) `t_m ∘ w_m = Φ_{m+1}` as maps
`A_{m+1}⁺/ϖ → A_{m+1}⁺/ϖ^p` (`t_m` reduced modulo `ϖ^p`), and (ii) the `w_m` are compatible with
the transition maps: `w_{m+1} ∘ t_{m+1} = t_m ∘ w_m` as maps `A_{m+1}⁺/ϖ → A_{m+1}⁺/ϖ^p` (`t`
reduced modulo `ϖ` on the left and modulo `ϖ^p` on the right). The `w_m` are data, exist only from
`m_0` on, and characteristic `p` is allowed (`p = 0 ∈ A_m⁺`, as for relative Frobenius towers over
a perfect base). The generic fibres are the complete Tate rings `A_m := A_m⁺[1/ϖ]` with ring of
definition `A_m⁺` (`ϖ`-adic topology) and the Huber pairs `(A_m, A_m⁺⁺)` with `A_m⁺⁺` the integral
closure of `A_m⁺` in `A_m`; `X_m := Spa(A_m, A_m⁺⁺)`. The finite levels `A_m` are not assumed
perfectoid (in the sources they are strongly noetherian). Source form: if all `A_m⁺` are flat
algebras over an integral perfectoid ring `O` with `ϖ ∈ O` (`O = Z_p^cycl` or `O_K` for a
perfectoid field `K`) and `t_m` modulo `ϖ^p` is identified, `O`-linearly, with the relative
Frobenius of `A_{m+1}⁺/ϖ^p` over `O/ϖ^p`, then `w_m` is the composite of the canonical isomorphism
`A_{m+1}⁺/ϖ ⊗_{O/ϖ, Φ_O} O/ϖ^p ≅ (A_{m+1}⁺/ϖ^p)^{(p)} ≅ A_m⁺/ϖ^p` with
`A_{m+1}⁺/ϖ ≅ A_{m+1}⁺/ϖ ⊗_{O/ϖ, Φ_O} O/ϖ^p` (`ϖ` is required to be a non-zero-divisor, `ϖ^p | p`, and `O` is
`ϖ`-adically complete; then `Φ_O : O/ϖ ≅ O/ϖ^p` is bijective by [BMS] Lemma 3.10(i)); in [Torsion] `ϖ = p^{(1−ε)/p}` and `ϖ^p = p^{1−ε}`.
Every construction below takes a chosen regular parameter as an explicit input. Regularity is not a
consequence of integral perfectoidness (`𝔽_p` is integral perfectoid with `π = 0`), and the
regularity required at every stage is not weakened: P7.6 uses it for the `ϖ`-torsion-freeness of
the completion. In `Perfectoid`, define
`IntegralTower` (the rings `A_m⁺`, the transition maps `t_m` and a parameter `ϖ` marked at every
stage and preserved by the transitions, regular (`ϖ`-torsion-freeness), `ϖ`-adically complete and
with `ϖ^p ∣ p` at every stage, which gives `p ∈ ϖ^pA_0⁺`), with `IntegralTower.quotient` (the stage
`A_m⁺/ϖ^k`), `IntegralTower.quotientMap` (the transition modulo `ϖ^k`) and `IntegralTower.diagram`
(the direct system, built with Mathlib's `Functor.ofSequence`); `FrobeniusTower` (an
`IntegralTower` with the index `m_0` and the isomorphisms `w_m` satisfying the lifting conditions
(i), (ii)), `FrobeniusTower.frobMod`
(`Φ_m : A_m⁺/ϖ →+* A_m⁺/ϖ^p`, built from Mathlib `frobenius` on the `F_p`-algebra `A_m⁺/ϖ^p`),
`FrobeniusTower.genericFibre` (the Huber pairs `(A_m, A_m⁺⁺)` and `X_m`), `FrobeniusTower.Hom`
(compatible ring maps `A_m⁺ → B_m⁺` sending `ϖ` to `ϖ` and intertwining the `w_m`; identity and
composition, with a common eventual starting index), `FrobeniusTower.ofRelativeFrobenius` (the tower from flat `ϖ`-adically complete
algebras over an integral perfectoid `O` with a non-zero-divisor `ϖ`, `ϖ^p | p`,
`O` `ϖ`-adically complete, whose transition maps reduce modulo `ϖ^p` to relative
Frobenius over `O/ϖ^p`), `IntegralTower.const` (the constant tower on a ring `A` with a chosen
regular parameter `π` as explicit input, `A` being `π`-adically complete with `π^p ∣ p`) and
`FrobeniusTower.constPerfectoid` (its Frobenius control with `w = Φ`, which exists exactly when
`A/π → A/π^p` is bijective, for instance when `A` is integral perfectoid for this `π` (P1.24), as
for `R°` with a pseudouniformiser of a perfectoid Tate ring) and `FrobeniusTower.perfection` (the relative
Frobenius tower of a flat `t`-adic algebra over a perfect base of characteristic `p`;
*perfection-tilde-limit*); the lifting conditions are the fields `FrobeniusTower.transition_comp_lift`
(`t_m ∘ w_m = Φ_{m+1}` for `m ≥ m_0`) and `FrobeniusTower.lift_comp_transition`
(`w_{m+1} ∘ t_{m+1} = t_m ∘ w_m` for `m ≥ m_0`); prove `FrobeniusTower.shift` (dropping the first `k` terms, lowering `m_0`, gives a Frobenius-controlled
tower with the same completion) and that
`Φ : colim_m A_m⁺/ϖ → colim_m A_m⁺/ϖ^p` is bijective (*frobenius-tower-uniformity-bound*)
([Torsion] §III.2.3, proof of Corollary III.2.19, p. 42 (transition maps equal to relative
Frobenius modulo `p^{1−ε} = ϖ^p`); [Torsion] §III.2.3, proof of Corollary III.2.19, pp. 42–43 (the
colimit Frobenius isomorphism `R_∞/ϖ ≅ R_∞/ϖ^p`); [Torsion] §III.2.3, proof of Corollary III.2.19,
p. 43 (a tower of flat formal schemes over `Z_p^cycl`); [BHW] §5.2, proof of Theorem 5.11, p. 22 of the arXiv manuscript
(relative Frobenius modulo `p^{1−δ}`)). *Needs:* Mathlib `IsAdicComplete`, `Ideal.span`,
`frobenius`, `integralClosure`; Tau Ceti `TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing`,
`TauCeti.Huber.IsPseudoUniformizer`; P1.1; P1.3.

**Checks.**

- Computation: for a perfectoid Tate pair `(R, R⁺)` and `ϖ ∈ R⁺` with
  compatible `p`-power roots and `ϖ^p | p` in `R⁺`, `A_m⁺ = R⁺⟨T^{1/p^m}⟩` with inclusions `t_m` and
  `w_m : (R⁺/ϖ)[T^{1/p^{m+1}}] → (R⁺/ϖ^p)[T^{1/p^m}]`, `r T^{a/p^{m+1}} ↦ Φ(r) T^{a/p^m}`, is
  Frobenius-controlled with `m_0 = 0`; likewise the torus `R⁺⟨T^{±1/p^m}⟩`.
- Degenerate: for an integral perfectoid ring `S` that is
  `ϖ`-torsion-free and `ϖ`-adically complete with `ϖ^p | p`, the constant tower `A_m⁺ = S`,
  `t_m = id`, with `w_m = Φ : S/ϖ ≅ S/ϖ^p` (bijective by [BMS] Lemma 3.10) is Frobenius-controlled.
- Non-example: for a perfectoid field `K` with
  pseudouniformiser `ϖ`, the constant tower `A_m⁺ = K°⟨T⟩` with identity transition maps is not
  Frobenius-controlled for any `m_0`: `t_m ∘ w_m = Φ` would make `T` a `p`-th power modulo `ϖ^p` in
  `K°⟨T⟩`, which it is not. The Check places the variable class outside the image of
  `(disc S ϖ).frobMod n` for every stage, with the disc hypotheses below and `ϖ` a nonunit.
  Reducing further modulo `ϖ` identifies the obstruction with the exponent of `T` in
  `(S/ϖ)[T]`.
- Compatibility: the tower `A_m⁺ = K°⟨T⟩` with transition maps
  `T ↦ T^p` is isomorphic, as a direct system, to the compatible-root disc tower `K°⟨T^{1/p^m}⟩`
  (via `T ↦ T^{1/p^m}` at level `m`), hence Frobenius-controlled; the definition is invariant under
  isomorphism of direct systems. In the integral presentation `disc S ϖ`, the example
  asserts that each `toCompleted n` is injective, that successive inclusions commute
  with `transition n`, and that `discCompletionEquiv` sends `aT^k` at stage `n` to
  `aT^{k/p^n}`. Thus each stage is isomorphic to its finite-root image, with
  coefficients fixed and the transition direction specified. It uses the regularity,
  integral-perfectoid and completeness hypotheses of `disc`
  ([SW13] discussion before Definition 2.3.4, p. 17; [Torsion] proof of
  Corollary III.2.19, pp. 42–43).
- Characterisation: for a perfect complete nonarchimedean
  field `k` of characteristic `p`, a pseudouniformiser `t`, and a flat `t`-adically complete
  `k°`-algebra `B`, use the base twists `B_m = B ⊗_{k°, F^{-m}} k°` and the transitions
  `b ⊗ c ↦ b^p ⊗ c`. These preserve `t` from the right factor and form the tower of P7.13.

- Convention: for `p = 2`, `(disc S ϖ).frobMod n`
  sends the class of `a+bT` modulo `ϖ` to `a²+b²T²` modulo `ϖ²`.
  This uses the integral-perfectoid, completeness and parameter hypotheses of `disc` below.
- Convention: over `𝔽₈`, choose
  `a³+a+1=0`, so `a⁸=a` and `a²≠a⁴`. On `perfectionStage` for `𝔽₈[T]`,
  `perfectionTransition` sends `(a+T)⊗a` to `(a²+T²)⊗a`, keeping the right factor fixed;
  `inverseFrobeniusIterate` sends `a` to `a⁴` at stage one. Thus the tensor twist is
  distinguished from forward coefficient Frobenius ([Torsion] Definition III.2.18, p. 42).
- Convention: the composite of two `discPower 2`
  maps sends `a+bT` to `a+bT⁴` in `discIntegral S ϖ`, for any commutative coefficient ring.
  It fixes coefficients; `frobMod` squares them. The associated generic-fibre diagram is
  contravariant, as specified by `genericDiagram_step`.
- Non-example: squaring modulo `4` is not additive:
  `(1 + 1)² = 0` but `1² + 1² = 2`. Correspondingly, no `IntegralTower 2` can have a
  stage identified with `ℤ₂` whose marked parameter is `2`: its `divides` field would
  require `4 ∣ 2`. This tests the hypothesis used by `frobMod` to make its target
  characteristic two ([Torsion], proof of Corollary III.2.19, pp. 42–43). A Lean `example` states
  the general form: at `p = 2` a stage with parameter `2` is the zero ring, since `4 ∣ 2` with `2`
  regular makes `2` a unit.
- Non-example (regularity): `𝔽_p` is integral perfectoid with `π = 0` but has no regular parameter
  for which it is adically complete (`0` is a zero-divisor, and a nonzero parameter is a unit, for
  which adic separatedness forces the zero ring), so it has no constant tower; more generally no
  stage of any `IntegralTower` is a field (a Lean `example`).
- Convention: the consecutive maps of `IntegralTower.diagram` are the transition maps (a Lean
  `example`).

- Degenerate: all quotients of a tower of zero rings are zero.
- Non-example: a nonzero stage cannot have zero
  marked parameter, by regularity.
- Non-example: no Frobenius tower can be identified
  with the constant restricted-disc system with identity transitions and the same parameter.
- `frobeniusTowerHom_test_identity` (computation) — the identity tower morphism fixes `1+T`
  in the disc's zeroth stage.
- `frobeniusTowerHom_test_zero` (degenerate) — every two morphisms into a tower of zero rings
  agree on every stage element.
- `frobeniusTowerHom_test_parameter_not` (non-example) — a morphism cannot kill the marked
  parameter of a nonzero target stage.
- `genericFibre_test_zero` (degenerate) — a zero integral stage has zero localized coordinate ring.
- `genericFibre_test_parameter_inverse` (computation) — the marked parameter becomes a unit
  in every generic fibre, also in characteristic `p`.
- `genericFibre_test_transition_twoTerms` (compatibility) — the map between generic fibres sends
  `1+ϖ²` to `1+ϖ²` at the next stage.
- `relativeTwist_test_zero` (degenerate) — a zero next stage has zero scalar extension.
- `relativeTwist_test_base` (computation) — the constant base stage gives `O/ϖ^p` after twisting.
- `relativeTwist_test_nonzero` (non-example) — this base twist is nonzero when `ϖ` is not a unit.

- `perfection_test_parameter` (computation) — the marked right scalar `1 ⊗ t` is fixed.
- `perfection_test_zero` (degenerate) — a zero input algebra gives zero stages and zero completion.
- `perfection_test_twoTransitions` (convention) — two transitions send `b ⊗ c` to `b^(p²) ⊗ c`.
  These and the relative-Frobenius Characterisation above test the constructed tower.
- `perfection_lift_scalar` (computation) — at `n = 0`, the right coefficient of `1 ⊗ c`
  becomes `c^p` under the quotient lift.
- `perfection_lift_left` (convention) — for every `n`, the lift sends `[b ⊗ 1]` to `[b ⊗ 1]`.
- `perfection_lift_nilpotent` (non-example) — if `ε^p = 0` and `[ε ⊗ 1]` is nonzero
  modulo the stage-zero parameter's `p`th power, the transition sends `ε ⊗ 1` to zero
  but the lift of `[ε ⊗ 1]` is nonzero. This applies to the square-zero generator above,
  including `p = 2`.

- `frobeniusMod_test_twoTerms` computes the disc quotient map on `a+bT` as
  `a^p+b^p T^p`; `frobeniusMod_test_zero` makes it bijective on a zero stage, while
  `frobeniusMod_test_disc_not` denies surjectivity for the nonzero residue disc.
- `shift_test_zero` fixes `1+ϖ²` after a shift by zero; `shift_test_start` makes the new
  starting index zero once the shift reaches the old starting index;
  `shift_test_empty` preserves zero completion after any shift.

`IntegralTower` records the complete integral models before imposing Frobenius control.
Its parameter is marked at every stage and preserved by the transition maps; regularity and
`ϖ^p | p` are stagewise requirements. Its `diagram` iterates the consecutive ring maps.
`FrobeniusTower` adds the eventual quotient isomorphisms and both commuting squares above.
`Hom` preserves the parameter and transitions at every level, and the quotient lifts from
a recorded common index onward. Composition raises this index past the start of the intermediate
tower as well as those of the two morphisms. `discIntegral S ϖ` is
`AdicCompletion (ϖ) S[T]`; `discPower` is fixed on polynomial images by substitution `T ↦ T^p`.
`disc S ϖ` has these stages, transition maps and coefficient-Frobenius lifts. The hypotheses are
that `S` is integral perfectoid, `ϖ` is regular, `ϖ^p | p`, and `S` is `ϖ`-adically complete.
The constant-disc non-example assumes `ϖ` is not a unit, so that its residue polynomial ring
is nonzero.

`FrobeniusTower.discPowerHom S ϖ k` is the endomorphism of `disc S ϖ` given
at every stage by `T ↦ T^k`, with coefficients fixed and starting index zero.
It has the same integral-perfectoid, regularity, divisibility and completeness
hypotheses as `disc`. The lift calculation raises coefficients to their `p`th
powers while leaving the coordinate exponent unchanged; this is the affine
relative-Frobenius calculation in [Torsion] Definition III.2.18 and the proof
of Corollary III.2.19, pp. 42–43.

- `discPowerHom_constant` evaluates `k = 0` on `a+bT`, obtaining `a+b`.
- `discPowerHom_quadratic` evaluates `k = 2` at every stage, obtaining `a+bT²`.
- `discPowerHom_lift_coefficients` computes both sides of `Hom.lift_comm` for
  the quadratic map on `[a+bT]`: both are `[a^p+b^pT²]` modulo `ϖ^p`.
  These three Checks test `Hom` as well as `discPowerHom`.
- `Hom_disc_lift_forced` tests a family of disc ring maps preserving the
  parameter and transitions, without assuming quotient-lift compatibility:
  compatibility follows because substitution `T ↦ T^p` is injective modulo
  `ϖ^p`. Thus such a family on this disc cannot violate `lift_comm`.

`relativeTwist` is the tensor product
`(A_{m+1}⁺/ϖ) ⊗_{O/ϖ, Φ_O} (O/ϖ^p)`; the scalar map into the next stage sends the base parameter
to its marked parameter. This equation also proves containment of the principal ideals
needed for the quotient scalar map; for the constant base tower it is the identity equation.
`relativeTwistLeft` sends `x` to `x ⊗ 1`. The base Frobenius is
bijective, hence this map is bijective. `ofRelativeFrobenius` takes flat models, scalar-linear
transitions and scalar-linear identifications of these twists with `A_m⁺/ϖ^p`; the characteristic
equations specify relative Frobenius and the right scalar inclusion. Compatibility of the
quotient lifts with transitions is a conclusion. These are the
relative-Frobenius presentations in [Torsion], proof of Corollary III.2.19, pp. 42–43.

The constructor `FrobeniusTower.perfection` uses a perfect characteristic-`p` base `O`, a flat
`O`-algebra `B`, a regular `t ∈ O`, and `t`-adic completeness of `B`. Its stage `n` is
`B ⊗_{O,F^{-n}} O`; `perfectionTensor n b c` is `b ⊗ c`. The parameter is `1 ⊗ t`, and
`perfectionTransition_tensor` sends `b ⊗ c` to `b^p ⊗ c`. This keeps the right scalar fixed
([Torsion] §III.2.3, Definition III.2.18, p. 42). With these hypotheses, the lift specification of
`FrobeniusTower.perfection` gives the chosen base-change isomorphism
`w_n : B_{n+1}/(1 ⊗ t) → B_n/(1 ⊗ t)^p` by
`w_n([b ⊗ c]) = [b ⊗ c^p]`. The tensor balancing follows from
`F^{-(n+1)}(a)^p = F^{-n}(a)`; perfectness of `O` gives the inverse on coefficients.
The Frobenius square alone does not specify this lift: for the flat algebra
`B = O[ε]/(ε²)`, the transition kills `ε`, while the lift retains its class whenever
`O/(t^p)` is nonzero. No reducedness hypothesis is imposed on `B`.

Checks of the relative constructor itself use its scalar-linear presentations:
`ofRelativeFrobenius_test_scalar` computes the transition on `1+ϖ` from the base;
`ofRelativeFrobenius_test_zero` gives zero completed generic fibre for zero models;
`ofRelativeFrobenius_test_parameter_not` excludes a zero marked parameter in a nonzero stage.

The following Checks evaluate the constructor's quotient lift, under exactly its
flatness, completeness, marked-parameter and relative-presentation hypotheses
([Torsion], proof of Corollary III.2.19, pp. 42–43):

- `ofRelativeFrobenius_lift_scalar` sends `[c]` from the scalar ring to `[c^p]`.
- `ofRelativeFrobenius_lift_tensor` writes `j(x)=x⊗1` and computes the lift on
  `j⁻¹(x⊗c)` as `e(x⊗1)·c`, for `c ∈ O/ϖ^p`. The right tensor scalar is
  retained; a scalar entering through the left factor is Frobenius-powered.
- `ofRelativeFrobenius_lift_two_terms` specifies `e(x⊗1)=[a]` and
  `e(y⊗1)=[b]`, then computes the constructed lift of `[cx+dy]` as
  `[c^p a+d^p b]`. This tests the presentation on two independent terms and
  fixes which coefficients are powered.

For the constant constructor, `constPerfectoid_test_zero` gives zero generic completion and
`constPerfectoid_test_lift_twoTerms` sends `a+b` modulo `ϖ` to `a^p+b^p` modulo `ϖ^p`.

**Relative Frobenius constructor.** (*relative-frobenius-tower*)
`FrobeniusTower.ofRelativeFrobenius` is the scalar-linear constructor of P7.5,
with flat integral models, a marked non-zero-divisor, completeness, and the specified
relative Frobenius presentations. Its Checks are the scalar, zero-model and
nonzero-parameter examples above. The characteristic-`p` perfection construction
has the separate label *perfection-tilde-limit* ([Torsion] Definition III.2.18, p. 42).

Lean: `Perfectoid.IntegralTower`, `IntegralTower.const`, `IntegralTower.quotient`,
`IntegralTower.quotientMap`, `IntegralTower.diagram`, `FrobeniusTower`.

### P7.6 completion and inversion of a Frobenius-controlled tower

**Completion and inversion of a Frobenius-controlled tower.** (*frobenius-tower-completion*) For a
Frobenius-controlled integral tower `(A_•⁺, ϖ, m_0, w)` (see *frobenius-controlled-integral-tower*)
define: `A_∞⁺ :=` the `ϖ`-adic completion of the direct limit `colim_m A_m⁺` (Mathlib
`AdicCompletion (Ideal.span {ϖ})` of the colimit in `CommRingCat` of `IntegralTower.diagram`, for
which `Ring.DirectLimit` is an equivalent model); `A_∞ := A_∞⁺[1/ϖ]`, topologised so that
`A_∞⁺` is an open ring of definition with the `ϖ`-adic topology (a complete Tate ring with
pseudouniformiser `ϖ`); `A_∞⁺⁺ :=` the integral closure of `A_∞⁺` in `A_∞` (a ring of integral
elements). This is the completed direct limit of Tate pairs of
AdicSpacesPartII R0.19.7 (*spa-of-filtered-colimit-of-tate-pairs*) applied to `(A_m, A_m⁺⁺)` with the rings of definition
`A_m⁺`, which for perfectoid levels is the construction of P5.1–P5.2; what is added for a
non-perfectoid tower is the completion/inversion formula: (i) `A_∞⁺/ϖ^k A_∞⁺ = colim_m A_m⁺/ϖ^k A_m⁺` for every
`k ≥ 1`; (ii) `A_∞⁺` is `ϖ`-torsion-free (the `ϖ`-torsion-freeness of the `A_m⁺` is what makes the
direct limit and its completion `ϖ`-torsion-free), so `A_∞⁺ ⊆ A_∞`; (iii) `(A_∞, A_∞⁺⁺)` is the
completed direct limit of the Huber pairs `(A_m, A_m⁺⁺)` in the sense of
*tilde-limit-from-completed-colimit* and of AdicSpacesPartII R0.19.7 (compatible rings of definition `A_m⁺` with
ideals of definition `ϖA_m⁺`, so `ϖA_{m'}⁺ = (ϖA_m⁺)A_{m'}⁺`); (iv) the construction depends only on the tail
of the tower (shift invariance) and is functorial for morphisms of towers. No uniform completion is
taken: by *frobenius-tower-uniformity-bound* the `ϖ`-adic topology on `A_∞⁺` is already the
spectral topology of `A_∞`. In `Perfectoid`, define `IntegralTower.colimitParameter` (the image of
`ϖ` in `colim_m A_m⁺`) and `IntegralTower.completedPlus` (`A_∞⁺`, defined for the underlying
integral tower of a Frobenius tower),
`FrobeniusTower.completed` (`A_∞ = A_∞⁺[1/ϖ]` with `A_∞⁺` an open ring of definition),
`FrobeniusTower.completedPair` (the Huber pair `(A_∞, A_∞⁺⁺)`; Tau Ceti `Huber.Pair`) and
`FrobeniusTower.toCompleted` (the compatible maps `A_m⁺ → A_∞⁺` and
`(A_m, A_m⁺⁺) → (A_∞, A_∞⁺⁺)`); prove the quotient formula (simp:
`A_∞⁺/ϖ^k ≅ colim_m A_m⁺/ϖ^k` for all `k ≥ 1`), that `A_∞⁺` is `ϖ`-torsion-free, the instance that
`A_∞` is a complete Tate ring with pseudouniformiser `ϖ` (Tau Ceti `Huber.IsTateRing`,
`Huber.IsPseudoUniformizer`), the universal property (compatible maps `A_m⁺ → B` into a
`ϖ`-adically complete ring sending the common `ϖ` to the element defining the adic topology of `B`
extend uniquely to a continuous map `A_∞⁺ → B`, uniqueness from density of `colim A_m⁺`), shift
invariance (the completion of a shifted tower is canonically the same), functoriality
`completed_map` (a morphism of towers induces a continuous map of completions; identity and
composition) and `FrobeniusTower.isCompletedDirectLimit` (`(A_∞, A_∞⁺⁺)` is the
completed direct limit of the `(A_m, A_m⁺⁺)`) ([Torsion] §III.2.3, proof of Corollary III.2.19,
p. 43 (the completion formula); [Torsion] §III.2.3, Definition III.2.18 (ii), p. 42 (the same
formula for the perfection tower, with `R^{perf} = R^{perf+}[t^{-1}]`); [ECD] §6, Proposition 6.5,
p. 29 (the analogous formula for towers of perfectoid rings, which the construction extends to
non-perfectoid finite levels)). *Needs:* *frobenius-controlled-integral-tower*; AdicSpacesPartII R0.19.7; P5.1;
Mathlib `AdicCompletion`, `Ring.DirectLimit`, `IsAdicComplete`, `integralClosure`; Tau Ceti
`TauCeti.Huber.Pair`, `TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing`.

**Checks.**

- Computation: for the compatible-root disc tower over
  `(R, R⁺)`, the completion is `R⁺⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩` (the `ϖ`-adic completion of `R⁺[T^{1/p^∞}]`) and
  `A_∞ = R⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩`.
- Degenerate: for the constant tower of an integral
  perfectoid `S` (`ϖ`-torsion-free, `ϖ`-complete), the completion is `S` and `A_∞ = S[1/ϖ]`.
- Non-example: for the disc tower over a nonzero `R`, the element
  `Σ_{n≥1} ϖ^n T^{1/p^n}` lies in `A_∞⁺` but in no `A_m⁺`: the direct limit itself is not complete,
  so the formula needs the completion.
- Characterisation: `A_∞⁺/ϖ^p ≅ colim_m A_m⁺/ϖ^p` as
  rings, compatibly with the maps from the `A_m⁺`.
- Compatibility: if every `A_m⁺` is the ring of integral
  elements of a perfectoid Tate ring, the completion agrees with the ring `R⁺` of [ECD] Proposition
  6.5 for the limit of the `Spa(A_m, A_m⁺)`.

- Degenerate: completion and subsequent
  localization of a tower of zero rings remain zero. The constant Check tests bijectivity of the
  canonical stage map; the quotient Check evaluates the marked parameter modulo its square.

- `completedPair_test_zero` gives the whole zero ring as the plus ring.
- `completedPair_test_inverse_not` excludes `ϖ⁻¹` from the plus ring when the generic fibre
  is nonzero.
- `completedPair_test_field` recovers `(C_p,C_p°)` from its constant integral tower, with the
  equivalence fixed on every integral coefficient.
- `completed_map_quadratic_root` applies `completed_map (discPowerHom S ϖ 2)`
  to the first root `x = T^{1/p}`, obtaining `x² ≠ x`. Under
  `discCompletionEquiv` this is the monomial of exponent `2/p` with coefficient
  one. In addition to the disc hypotheses, `ϖ` is a nonunit; reduction modulo
  `ϖ` distinguishes the two monomials, including when `p = 2`
  ([Torsion] Definition III.2.18, p. 42).
- `completed_map_test_identity` fixes `1+ϖ²`; `completed_map_test_zero` sends every element to
  zero in a zero target; `completed_map_test_parameter_not` forbids killing the parameter of
  a nonzero target completion.

The constructors use `IntegralTower.colimitRing`, its canonical stage maps and their common
`colimitParameter`. `completedPlus` is its principal-adic completion; `completed` localizes at
the completed parameter. The topology is characterized by `completed_nhds_zero`: images of
powers of the parameter ideal form a neighbourhood basis at zero. `completedPair` takes the
integral closure of this integral model in its localization. The quotient comparison
fixes every finite-stage element; `completed_map_stage` and
`completed_shift_stage` fix the maps on the same dense images. The completion lift fixes the
parameter in the target complete ring, so its ring map is automatically continuous for the
principal-adic topologies. These formulas specialize the completion in [Torsion], proof of
Corollary III.2.19, p. 43, without assuming perfectoid finite stages.

`discCompletionEquiv` identifies the integral completion with the principal-adic completion
of the monoid algebra on the nonnegative `p`-power rational exponents. Its monomial equation
sends the level-`n` monomial `aT^k` to `aT^(k/p^n)`. The disc Check computes the image of the
first root. The missing-series Check uses `Σ_{n≥0} ϖ^(n+1) T^(1/p^(n+1))` and asserts that its
sum is outside every finite generic fibre.

`IntegralTower.quotientDiagram k` is the direct system of the stage quotients by `ϖ^k`.
`quotientColimit` and `quotientColimit_mk` identify its colimit with the quotient of the ring
colimit, fixing every stage element. The quotient formula above combines this
comparison with completion and fixes its stage maps.
`isCompletedDirectLimit` asserts the full `IsCompletedColimitOfTower` predicate for the
constructed generic fibres, their maps, their integral models and their marked parameter.
`perfectoidDiagram` regards the same generic-fibre diagram as a diagram in `Perfd` when its
levels are perfectoid; the compatibility Check above compares its P5 limit with the
constructed completion by an isomorphism commuting with every projection.

Checks `completedQuotient_test_zeroPower`, `completedQuotient_test_parameter` and
`completedQuotient_test_twoTerms` respectively compute the zero ring for exponent zero, zero
for the marked parameter modulo itself, and `1` for `1+ϖ²` modulo `ϖ²`.

Lean: `IntegralTower.colimitParameter`, `IntegralTower.completedPlus`.

### P7.7 preperfectoid adic spaces

**Preperfectoid adic spaces.** (*preperfectoid-space*) Let `X` be an analytic adic space in the
generality of [SW13] §2.1 (an analytic Yoneda-adic space, AdicEtaleGeometry A1.16; the sheafy
adic spaces of AdicSpaces layer 5 form a full subcategory). For an open affinoid `U = Spa(A, A⁺) ⊆ X`
with a pseudouniformiser `ϖ ∈ A⁺`, the strong completion `(Â, Â⁺)` of `(A, A⁺)` is the completion
of `(A, A⁺)` for the topology on `A` that gives `A⁺` the `ϖ`-adic topology (`Â⁺` the `ϖ`-adic
completion of `A⁺`, `Â = Â⁺[1/ϖ]`; independent of `ϖ`); it is taken for the `ϖ`-adic topology on
the plus ring, not the natural topology of `A`. `X` is preperfectoid if `X` has a cover by open
affinoids `U_α = Spa(A_α, A_α⁺)` whose strong completions `(Â_α, Â_α⁺)` are perfectoid Tate pairs
([ECD] Definition 3.1). Over a perfectoid field `K` this is [SW13] Definition 2.3.4 (they complete
for the `p`-adic topology on `A⁺`); [SW13] Definition 2.3.9 defines `X` over `Spa(Q_p, Z_p)` to be
preperfectoid when every base change to a perfectoid field of characteristic `0` is, and
Proposition 2.3.10 compares the two when `X` lies over a perfectoid `K`. The natural topology of
`A` and the `ϖ`-adic topology of `A⁺` can differ, and then `A` itself need not be perfectoid: the
nonreduced point `Spa(K[ε]/(ε²), O_K + Kε)` is preperfectoid with strong completion `(K, O_K)`.
Locally closed subspaces of preperfectoid spaces are preperfectoid ([SW13] Propositions 2.3.7 and
2.3.11). In `PerfectoidSpace`, define `strongCompletionPair` (for a Huber pair `(A, A⁺)` with
pseudouniformiser `ϖ ∈ A⁺`: `(Â, Â⁺)` with `Â⁺` the `ϖ`-adic completion of `A⁺` and
`Â = Â⁺[1/ϖ]`) and `IsPreperfectoid` (`X` is covered by open affinoids with perfectoid strong
completion); prove `strongCompletionPair_indep` (the strong completion does not depend on the
choice of `ϖ`), `IsPreperfectoid.of_isPerfectoid` (instance: perfectoid spaces are preperfectoid),
`IsPreperfectoid.openSubspace` (open subspaces of preperfectoid spaces are preperfectoid),
`IsPreperfectoid.closedSubspace` (closed, hence locally closed, subspaces are preperfectoid; [SW13]
Proposition 2.3.7, p. 18), `IsPreperfectoid.baseChange` (for `X` over a perfectoid field `K`, preperfectoid
over `Spa(Q_p, Z_p)`, i.e. after all base changes to perfectoid fields, implies preperfectoid over
`K`; [SW13] Proposition 2.3.10) and `strongCompletion` (the strong completion `X̂`
of P7.8) ([SW13] §2.3, Definition 2.3.4, pp. 17–18; [SW13] §2.3, Definition 2.3.4, p. 18 (the
`p`-adic, i.e. `ϖ`-adic, topology on the plus ring); [SW13] §2.3, Remark 2.3.5, p. 18 (the
non-reduced example)). *Needs:* AdicEtaleGeometry A1.16; P1.1; P2.10; Mathlib `AdicCompletion`.

**Checks.**

- `isPreperfectoid_test_nonreducedPoint` (computation) — for a perfectoid field `K`,
  `Spa(K[ε]/(ε²), O_K + Kε)` is preperfectoid: the `ε`-component is infinitely `ϖ`-divisible in
  `O_K + Kε`, so the `ϖ`-adic completion of the plus ring is `O_K` and the strong completion is
  `(K, O_K)`.
- `isPreperfectoid_test_perfectoid` (degenerate) — every perfectoid space is preperfectoid, with
  every affinoid perfectoid its own strong completion.
- Boundary: the zero-variable formal disc has generic fibre `Spa(ℚ_p, ℤ_p)`, whose strong
  completion is itself. It fails `IsPreperfectoid` because `ℚ_p` is not perfectoid
  ([ECD] Remark 3.3, p. 14), although every base change to a characteristic-zero perfectoid
  field `K` is `Spa(K, K°)`, so it satisfies [SW13] Definition 2.3.9.
- `isPreperfectoid_test_disc_not` (non-example) — for a perfectoid field `K`, the closed unit disc
  `D = Spa(K⟨T⟩, K°⟨T⟩)` is not preperfectoid: every nonempty open affinoid of `D` is `Spa(A, A⁺)` with `A` a
  reduced one-dimensional `K`-affinoid algebra and `A⁺` bounded, so the strong completion is
  `(A, A⁺)` itself, and `A` is not perfectoid (for `A = K⟨T⟩`, `T` is not a `p`-th power modulo
  `ϖ^p` in `K°⟨T⟩`; in general the reduction `Ã = A°/A°°` is a reduced finitely generated
  `k`-algebra of dimension one, whose fraction fields are not perfect, so Frobenius on `A°/ϖ` is
  not surjective).
- `isPreperfectoid_test_overField` (compatibility) — for `X` over a perfectoid field `K` of
  characteristic `0`, `X` is preperfectoid in this sense iff it is preperfectoid over
  `Spa(K, O_K)` in the sense of [SW13] Definition 2.3.4: `K° ⊂ A⁺` contains a pseudouniformiser `ϖ`
  with `ϖ^p | p` and `p | ϖ^N`, so the `ϖ`-adic and `p`-adic topologies on `A⁺` agree.
  The example expands the field-relative condition on the same Yoneda-adic open charts:
  their `strongRing` with parameter `p` is perfectoid. It states the equivalence with
  `IsPreperfectoid` and records the two divisibilities and equality of Mathlib's
  `Ideal.adicTopology` on each chart's plus ring
  ([SW13] Definition 2.3.4, pp. 17–18).

- `strongCompletionPair_test_perfectoid` (compatibility) — the canonical map on a perfectoid
  pair is bijective.
- `strongCompletionPair_test_zero` (degenerate) — a zero pair has zero strong integral and
  generic completions.
- `strongCompletionPair_test_nonreducedPoint` (computation) — for the dual-number point over
  `C_p`, an identification of its strong completion with `C_p` sends `a+bε` to `a`.
- `isPreperfectoid_test_empty` (degenerate) — the empty affinoid satisfies the local cover condition.

`strongPlus R ϖ` is the existing principal-adic completion of `R⁺`; `strongRing R ϖ hϖ`, with `hϖ` asserting that `ϖ` is a pseudouniformiser in `R`,
is its localization at the completed parameter. `strong_nhds_zero` fixes the topology by the
images of powers of `(ϖ)`. In `strongCompletionPair` the plus ring is the image of the completed
plus ring. The map from the original pair is fixed on `R⁺` by
`strongCompletionPair.toCompletion_plus`; its extension uses that `ϖ` is a pseudouniformiser
in `R`. `IsPreperfectoid` requires an analytic source and an open cover by pairs with perfectoid
strong completion ([SW13] Definition 2.3.4 and Remark 2.3.5, pp. 17–18).

**Closed subspaces.** (*preperfectoid-closed-subspaces*)
`IsPreperfectoid.closedSubspace` takes an analytic source and a preperfectoid target,
with closed-subspace charts given by surjective quotient maps and the integral closure
of the image plus ring. It concludes preperfectoidness of the source
([SW13] Proposition 2.3.7, p. 18).

**Absolute and relative preperfectoidness.** (*preperfectoid-base-change*)
`IsPreperfectoid.baseChange` assumes preperfectoidness after every perfectoid-field
base change over `ℚ_p` and concludes it over the given characteristic-zero perfectoid
field ([SW13] Proposition 2.3.10, pp. 18–19).

### P7.8 the strong completion

**The strong completion `X̂` of a preperfectoid space and `X̂ ~ X`.** (*strong-completion*) Let
`X` be a preperfectoid analytic adic space (see *preperfectoid-space*), over no base field ([SW13]
state it over `Spa(K, O_K)`). There is a perfectoid space `X̂` with a morphism `X̂ → X` (of
Yoneda-adic spaces) such that: (i) `|X̂| → |X|` is a homeomorphism; (ii) for every open affinoid
`U = Spa(A, A⁺) ⊆ X` whose strong completion `(Â, Â⁺)` is perfectoid, the corresponding open
subspace of `X̂` is `Spa(Â, Â⁺)`; (iii) `X̂` is universal for morphisms from perfectoid spaces to
`X`: every morphism `Y → X` with `Y` perfectoid factors uniquely through `X̂`; (iv) when `X` is an
adic space in the sense of AdicSpaces layer 5 (sheafy affinoid coordinate rings), `X̂ ~ X`, i.e.
`(X̂, X̂ → X)` is a perfectoid tilde-limit of the one-object system `X` in the sense of
*perfectoid-tilde-limit* ([SW13] Proposition 2.4.4, stated there for adic spaces in their §2.1
generality). `X̂` is unique up to unique isomorphism by (iii). In `PerfectoidSpace`, define
`strongCompletion` (the perfectoid space `X̂` of a preperfectoid `X`, with its map to `X`) and
`strongCompletion.map` (a morphism of preperfectoid spaces induces one of strong completions;
identity and composition); prove `strongCompletion.homeomorph` (`|X̂| → |X|` is a homeomorphism),
`strongCompletion.affinoid` (over `U = Spa(A, A⁺)` with perfectoid strong completion, the open
subspace of `X̂` is `Spa(Â, Â⁺)`), `strongCompletion.lift` (every morphism from a perfectoid space
to `X` factors uniquely through `X̂`), `strongCompletion.isTildeLimit` (`X̂ ~ X`) and
`strongCompletion.of_perfectoid` (for `X` perfectoid the canonical map `X̂ → X` is an isomorphism)
([SW13] §2.3, Proposition 2.3.6, p. 18 (properties (i)–(iii)); [SW13] §2.4, Proposition 2.4.4,
p. 20 (property (iv))). *Needs:* *preperfectoid-space*; *perfectoid-tilde-limit*; P2.3; P2.10;
AdicEtaleGeometry A1.16.

**Checks.**

- `strongCompletionPair_test_nonreducedPoint` (computation) — the strong completion of
  `Spa(K[ε]/(ε²), O_K + Kε)` over a perfectoid field `K` is `Spa(K, O_K)`.
- `strongCompletion_test_perfectoid` (degenerate) — for `X` perfectoid, the canonical `X̂ → X` is
  an isomorphism.
- `strongCompletion_test_not_iso` (non-example) — the map `Spa(K, O_K) → Spa(K[ε]/(ε²), O_K + Kε)`
  is a homeomorphism with dense image on functions but not an isomorphism of adic spaces: `X̂ ~ X`
  does not mean `X̂ ≅ X`.
- `strongCompletion_test_universal` (characterisation) — for every perfectoid `Y`,
  `Hom(Y, X̂) → Hom(Y, X)` is bijective; for the non-reduced point this says every map from a
  perfectoid space kills `ε`.

- `strongCompletion_test_empty` (degenerate): the strong completion of an empty
  preperfectoid space has no points. The perfectoid and dual-number non-isomorphism Checks test
  the global canonical map.

- `strongCompletion_map_component_swap` takes `Y = X × {false,true}` for a
  perfectoid `X` with a specified point `x`, and completes the map exchanging
  the two components. Through `strongCompletion.homeomorph`, the lift of
  `(x,false)` maps into the true component and is not fixed. The input includes
  the preperfectoidness of `Y`; this is a finite-product computation using
  [SW13] Proposition 2.3.6, p. 18.
- `strongCompletion_map_test_id` (compatibility) — on a perfectoid object the identity remains identity.
- `strongCompletion_map_test_empty` (degenerate) — all maps out of an empty completion agree.
- `strongCompletion_map_test_nonreduced` (computation) — completing the dual-number reduction
  makes its map an isomorphism.

`strongCompletion.ι` is the canonical morphism to the original space.
`homeomorph_apply`, `affinoid_ι` and `map_ι` identify respectively its point map, its affinoid
coordinate map and its functoriality square. `lift` gives a unique factorization of every map
from a perfectoid source, which also determines `map_id` and `map_comp` ([SW13] Proposition
2.3.6, p. 18).

### P7.9 cofinality witnesses for level families

**Cofinality witnesses for families of compact open subgroups.** (*level-cofinality-witness*) Let
`G` be a Hausdorff topological group in which the compact open subgroups form a basis of
neighbourhoods of `1` (a locally profinite group: a profinite group, or `G(Q_p)` for a linear
algebraic group `G` over `Q_p`). Write `CO(G)` for the set of compact open subgroups, a cofiltered
category under inclusion (`K′ → K` when `K′ ⊆ K`; `K ∩ K′` is compact open). A level family is a
