cofiltered category `J` with a functor `j ↦ K_j` to `CO(G)`. A cofinality witness for `(K_j)` is a
function `U ↦ j(U)` from the open subgroups `U` of `G` (equivalently from open neighbourhoods of
`1`) to `J` with `K_{j(U)} ⊆ U`; the witness is data. By Mathlib's criterion
`CategoryTheory.Functor.initial_of_exists_of_isCofiltered` (morphisms in `CO(G)` are unique, so the
second condition is automatic), a witness makes `j ↦ K_j` an initial functor `J → CO(G)`; hence,
for every tower `(X_K)_{K ∈ CO(G)}` of analytic honest adic spaces with qcqs transition maps (a Shimura
tower at `p`) and every perfectoid `X` with compatible maps, `X ~ lim_{K ∈ CO(G)} X_K` iff
`X ~ lim_{j ∈ J} X_{K_j}` (see *tilde-limit-cofinal-change*). A level family without a witness only
computes the tilde-limit of the subtower it indexes: no infinite-level statement for the full tower
follows from it. The existence of a witness for decreasing sequences inside a compact open subgroup is
characterised by the library: a directed family of closed subgroups of a compact group whose
intersection lies in an open subgroup has a member inside it (Tau Ceti
`Subgroup.exists_le_of_iInf_le_of_directed`), and conversely the open normal subgroups of a
profinite group are a neighbourhood basis of `1` (Mathlib
`ProfiniteGrp.exist_openNormalSubgroup_sub_open_nhds_of_one`); so a decreasing family of open
subgroups of a profinite group is cofinal iff its intersection is trivial, compactness being
essential. Hence the principal congruence subgroups `H ∩ (1 + p^n M_N(ℤ_p))` (`n ≥ 1`) of a closed
`H ⊆ GL_N(ℤ_p)` are cofinal (their intersection is trivial), `Γ_0(p^n)` and `Γ_1(p^n)` are not
(both contain the unipotent upper triangular subgroup; the `Γ_0`-, `Γ_1`- and `Γ`-level towers
are distinct towers, [BHW] §5.2, proof of Theorem 5.11, p. 22 of the arXiv manuscript), and a family below a cofinal
family is cofinal. In `PerfectoidSpace`, define `LevelFamily`
(a cofiltered `J` with a functor to the compact open subgroups of a locally profinite `G`),
`CofinalityWitness` (a choice `j(U)` with `K_{j(U)} ⊆ U` for every open subgroup `U`),
`CofinalityWitness.ofDecreasing` (a decreasing sequence of open subgroups of a compact open `K_0`
with trivial intersection has a witness), `CofinalityWitness.principalCongruence` (the family
`1 + p^(n+1) M_N(Z_p)` is witnessed in `GL_N(Q_p)`),
`CofinalityWitness.principalCongruence_closed` (for a closed subgroup `H ⊆ GL_N(Z_p)`,
its intersections with these levels are witnessed in `H`, with its subspace topology;
the entrywise bound is `|g_ij − δ_ij| ≤ p^(-(n+1))`),
`CofinalityWitness.conj` (if `(K_j)` is witnessed, so is `(gK_jg^{-1})` for `g ∈ G`),
`CofinalityWitness.mono` (if `K′_j ⊆ K_j` compatibly and `(K_j)` is witnessed, so is `(K′_j)`) and
`CofinalityWitness.openNormal` (in a profinite group the open normal subgroups are witnessed;
Mathlib `ProfiniteGrp.exist_openNormalSubgroup_sub_open_nhds_of_one`); prove
`CofinalityWitness.initial` (a witnessed family `J → CO(G)` is a Mathlib
`CategoryTheory.Functor.Initial`) and `CofinalityWitness.isTildeLimit_iff` (for a tower `(X_K)`
whose every level is analytic and honest and whose every transition is qcqs, and perfectoid `X`
with a compatible cone: `X ~ lim_{CO(G)} X_K ⟺ X ~ lim_J X_{K_j}`). Apply
`IsTildeLimit.reindex` using `CofinalityWitness.initial`; the three hypotheses concern the full
tower, including levels and arrows outside the chosen family. The qcqs condition is the one in
[SW13] Definition 2.4.1, pp. 19–20; analyticity and honesty are the additional conditions of this
roadmap's analytic Yoneda comparison with AdicSpacesPartII R0.20.1 ([Sch13E] item (1), p. 1 (reindexing a
cofiltered system along a cofinal map); [CHJ] §2, Theorem 2.8, p. 11 (the infinite-level Shimura
curve indexed by the principal congruence levels `K(p^n)`); [BHW] §5.2, proof of Theorem 5.11,
p. 22 of the arXiv manuscript (the `Γ_0`-, `Γ_1`- and `Γ`-level towers treated separately: different level families give
different level problems)). *Needs:* Mathlib `OpenSubgroup`, `ProfiniteGrp`,
`ProfiniteGrp.exist_openNormalSubgroup_sub_open_nhds_of_one`, `CategoryTheory.Functor.Initial`,
`CategoryTheory.Functor.initial_of_exists_of_isCofiltered`, `CategoryTheory.IsCofiltered`.

The records `LevelFamily J G` and `CofinalityWitness F` themselves make sense for any group
with a topology: `J` is cofiltered, `F.level j` is an open subgroup, each level is compact,
and `a : i → j` gives `F.level i ≤ F.level j`. Functor laws are automatic in this poset.
`CofinalityWitness F` chooses `levelFor U` with `F.level (levelFor U) ≤ U`. The neighbourhood-basis
interpretation and the comparison with the full tower above use the locally profinite hypotheses.
Prove `CofinalityWitness.not_nonempty_of_common_element`: if `x` belongs to every level and some
open subgroup `U` excludes `x`, there is no witness (apply its defining inclusion to `U`).

**Checks.**

- `cofinalityWitness_test_trivialGroup` (degenerate) — the one-object constant family at the
  whole trivial group `Multiplicative (ZMod 1)` has a witness.
- `cofinalityWitness_test_twoLevels` (convention) — in the two-element group, use
  the category `0 → 1` with levels `{1} → G`. The inclusions point from smaller
  subgroups to larger ones, and `levelFor U = 0` is a witness for every open `U`.
- `cofinalityWitness_test_finiteConst_not` (non-example) — the one-object constant family at
  the whole two-element discrete group `Multiplicative (ZMod 2)` has no witness, since the
  trivial open subgroup excludes its nonidentity element. This is a valid `LevelFamily`.
- `cofinalityWitness_test_principalCongruence` (computation) — in `G = GL_N(Q_p)` the family
  `K(p^n) = 1 + p^n M_N(Z_p)` (`n ≥ 1`) has the witness `U ↦` the least `n` with `K(p^n) ⊆ U`, which
  exists by `Subgroup.exists_le_of_iInf_le_of_directed` since `⋂_n K(p^n) = {1}`.
- `cofinalityWitness_closed_rankZero` — in rank zero every level is the whole trivial group.
- `cofinalityWitness_closed_trivial` — for `H = {1}` every level is the whole of `H`.
- `cofinalityWitness_closed_scalar` — for `H = GL_1(Z_p)`, membership at index `n`
  is exactly `|g_00 − 1| ≤ p^(-(n+1))`.
- `cofinalityWitness_test_discrete` (degenerate) — for `G` finite with the discrete topology, the
  one-element family `K = {1}` has the witness `U ↦ ∗` (in particular for the two-element
  group `Multiplicative (ZMod 2)`); for a tower over `CO(G)` with every level analytic and honest,
  all transitions qcqs, and `X_{1}` perfectoid, its value `X_{1}` is then a perfectoid tilde-limit.
- `cofinalityWitness_nonanalyticLevel` (non-example) — a nonanalytic level anywhere in the
  full tower prevents any cone from satisfying `PerfectoidSpace.IsTildeLimit`.
- `cofinalityWitness_nonhonestLevel` (non-example) — a nonhonest level anywhere in the full
  tower likewise prevents the full tilde-limit predicate.
- `cofinalityWitness_nonqcqsTransition` (non-example) — a transition of the full tower that
  is not qcqs prevents the full tilde-limit predicate, even if a chosen family omits that arrow.
- `cofinalityWitness_test_gamma0_not` (non-example) — in `GL_2(Q_p)` the decreasing family
  `Γ_0(p^n) = {(a b; c d) ∈ GL_2(Z_p) : c ≡ 0 mod p^n}` has no witness: every `Γ_0(p^n)` contains the
  upper-triangular unipotent `(1 1; 0 1)`, which lies outside the open subgroup `K(p)`. Its
  tilde-limit (the anticanonical `Γ_0(p^∞)` level) does not by cofinality compute the full infinite level (a constant tower can still have
  the same limit along either family).
- `cofinalityWitness_test_const_not` (non-example) — the constant family `K_j = K` with `K ≠ {1}`
  (`G` infinite profinite) has no witness; the limit of the subtower is `X_K` itself.
- `cofinalityWitness_test_initial` (compatibility) — a witness makes `j ↦ K_j` a Mathlib
  `Functor.Initial` `J → CO(G)`, so `Functor.Initial.limitIso` identifies `lim_J |X_{K_j}|` with
  `lim_{CO(G)} |X_K|`.

`CompactOpenSubgroup G` is the subtype of open subgroups with compact underlying set.
`LevelFamily.functor` uses the inclusion order on this subtype. `CofinalityWitness.initial` is
the adapter from the chosen neighbourhood inclusions to Mathlib initiality; it adds no new
categorical criterion. The matrix Check expresses `K(p^(n+1))` inside `GL_N(Q_p)` by the entrywise
bounds `|g_ij-δ_ij| ≤ p^(-(n+1))`. The `Γ₀` Check includes integrality of both the matrix and its
inverse, and the bound on its lower-left entry; it denies a witness for this family.

### P7.10 uniqueness and representability of perfectoid tilde-limits

A perfectoid tilde-limit is determined by the system: this subsection and the next prove that it
represents the inverse limit of the represented functors on perfectoid spaces, hence is unique up
to unique isomorphism, and compare it with inverse limits of represented functors; the further
comparison with inverse limits of diamonds is DiamondsAndVStacks', downstream.

**A perfectoid tilde-limit represents `lim_i Hom(−, X_i)` on perfectoid spaces and is unique.**
(*tilde-limit-perfectoid-uniqueness*) Let `(X_i)_{i∈I}` be a cofiltered system of analytic adic
spaces with quasicompact quasiseparated transition maps and `X ~ lim X_i` a perfectoid tilde-limit
(see *perfectoid-tilde-limit*). Then for every perfectoid space `Y` (of any characteristic, over no
fixed base field), and more generally every analytic adic space `Y` with a basis of open affinoids
`Spa(B, B⁺)` with `B` uniform (for instance `Y` stably uniform; only uniformity of these coordinate
rings is used, not perfectoidness; [SW13] state it for perfectoid affinoid `(K, O_K)`-algebras),
the map
`Hom(Y, X) → lim_i Hom(Y, X_i)`, `g ↦ (φ_i ∘ g)_i`, is bijective. Consequently: (i) `X` represents
the functor `Y ↦ lim_i Hom(Y, X_i)` on perfectoid spaces; (ii) if `(X′, φ′)` is another perfectoid
tilde-limit of the same system, there is a unique isomorphism `X ≅ X′` compatible with the cones;
(iii) a morphism of systems `(X_i) → (X′_i)` (over a common index category) induces a unique
morphism between perfectoid tilde-limits commuting with the cones; (iv) over a base `S` (all `X_i`
over `S` compatibly), the same holds for `S`-morphisms. Injectivity is by density and existence
starts from the good affinoid perfectoids ([SW13] §2.4, Proposition 2.4.5, p. 20; [SW13] §2.4,
proof of Proposition 2.4.5, p. 21; [Survey] §2, Proposition 2.23, p. 12 (representability)).
`IsTildeLimit.lift` states the perfectoid-source case with `Y : Perfd p`.
`IsTildeLimit.lift_uniform` states the extension to an honest analytic Yoneda adic space:
its point space has a basis consisting of images of open immersions `Spa^Y(B) → Y`,
where `B : CAff` is sheafy, Tate and uniform. For every compatible cone with vertex `Y`,
there is a unique morphism to `X` commuting with all projections. The uniform-source
extension uses the completion argument in [SW13] Proposition 2.4.5, pp. 20–21;
uniformity bounds the power-bounded elements of each source chart.
*Needs:* *perfectoid-tilde-limit*; *good-affinoid-perfectoid*; *good-affinoid-perfectoid-basis*;
P1.1; P2.10; Tau Ceti `TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.mem_of_forall_vle_one`,
`TauCeti.Huber.IsPseudoUniformizer`, `TauCeti.Huber.Pair.Hom`.

The existence step rests on the fact that good affinoid perfectoids cover a tilde-limit and are
stable under rational subsets (*good-affinoid-perfectoid-basis*): let `(X_i)` be a cofiltered
system of analytic adic spaces with qcqs transition maps and `X` a perfectoid space with a
compatible cone such that `|X| → lim |X_i|` is a homeomorphism. (i) If `X ~ lim X_i`, then `X` is
covered by good affinoid perfectoids with `V` affinoid at their level. (ii) If `(W, i_0, V)` is good
and `U ⊆ W` is a rational subset, then `U` is good at some level `j → i_0` with a quasicompact open
`V′ ⊆ V_a`; if `V` is affinoid, `V′` can be taken a rational subset of `V_a`. (iii) Hence the good
affinoid perfectoids form a basis of the topology of `X`. (iv) Conversely, if `X` is covered by
good affinoid perfectoids, then `X ~ lim X_i`. Consequently the conditions (b), (b′), (b″) of
*perfectoid-tilde-limit* are equivalent given (a) ([Survey] §2, Proposition 2.22, p. 11
(statements (i), (ii)); [Survey] §2, proof of Proposition 2.22, p. 11 (descent of the quasicompact
open to a finite level, and density on rational subsets); [Stacks] Tag 0A30, Lemma 5.24.6
(quasicompact opens of a cofiltered limit of spectral spaces come from a finite level)). *Needs:*
*perfectoid-tilde-limit*; *good-affinoid-perfectoid*; P2.3; P5; AdicSpacesPartII R0.19.5–R0.19.8 and P5.4’s perfectoid limit comparisons; Tau
Ceti `TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.exists_mem_nhds_forall_rationalSubset_eq_of_sub_mem`,
`TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.spaComap_preimage_rationalSubset`,
`TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.rationalSubset`.

### P7.11 represented functors and finite-level descriptions

**Finite-level analytic carriers.** (*finite-level-analytic-carriers*)
`TowerGeometry.IsFinite` tests finiteness using cartesian affinoid charts and
AdicSpacesPartII R0.13’s finite pair maps. `TowerGeometry.IsOverZp` requires
topological nilpotence of `p` on each affinoid chart. These are the finite-transition
and residue-characteristic hypotheses of [HJ] p. 26 and Lemma 5.11, p. 32;
[P8](../PerfectoidTowers/README.md#layer-p8-finite-quotients-and-closed-perfectoid-loci-in-towers) uses the same carriers.

**The raw compact-open covering condition; the v-site is DiamondsAndVStacks'.**
(*perfectoid-untilt-test-sheaves*) P7 uses no topology on perfectoid spaces. The only covering
condition it refers to is the raw one: for a category `C : Type v` with `Category.{u} C` and a
functor `sp : C ⥤ TopCat.{u}`, a `Type u`-indexed family covers when its images cover each compact
open exactly by finitely many compact opens, Mathlib's `IsCompactOpenCovered` ([ECD] Definition
8.1(iii), p. 39). The v-site built on that condition belongs to DiamondsAndVStacks: the precoverage
`vPrecoverage` and the generated Grothendieck topology `vTopology` to its D2.2, subcanonicity and
v-descent to its D2.7; it is not an input here. No local spectrality is required to define either
object; nonempty spaces with no nonempty compact opens need not exclude the empty cover. Their
specializations to `Perfd p`, along the inclusion `ObjectProperty.ι (isPerfectoidSpace p)` followed
by the underlying space, are DiamondsAndVStacks' as well.

Checks of the covering condition and of the precoverage and topology that DiamondsAndVStacks D2.2
builds on it (specified in this README only):

| Check | Instance and outcome |
| --- | --- |
| `vPrecoverage_point` | The identity presieve covers the terminal object of `Fin 2`, with the constant one-point space functor. |
| `vPrecoverage_empty` | An object with empty underlying space admits the empty covering presieve. |
| `vPrecoverage_nonempty` | At the terminal object of the constant one-point `Fin 2` diagram, the empty presieve is not covering. |
| `vTopology_point` | The sieve generated by the identity covers the same one-point object. |
| `vTopology_empty` | The constant empty-space functor on `Fin 2` generates the maximal topology. |
| `vTopology_nonempty` | The empty sieve does not cover the terminal object for the constant one-point functor. |

The specialized Checks `vPrecoverage_identity`, `vPrecoverage_empty`,
`vPrecoverage_nonempty`, `vTopology_identity`, `vTopology_empty` and
`vTopology_nonempty` test the identity, empty perfectoid space, and nonempty
perfectoid space, respectively. Local spectrality makes the last case valid.
The comparisons below are stated for represented functors, not sheaves:
`VQuotient.representedFunctor p` sends an analytic Yoneda-adic space `X` to the functor
`Hom(−, X)` on perfectoid test spaces (P7.10). That these functors are v-sheaves for
DiamondsAndVStacks' topology (subcanonicity, D2.7; [ECD] Theorem 8.7, p. 43), and that they agree
there with the sheafified restricted Yoneda functor on perfectoid objects, are downstream statements
of DiamondsAndVStacks; nothing here uses them.
Checks `representedFunctor_identity`, `representedFunctor_empty` and
`representedFunctor_two_points` test the identity map, empty target with nonempty source, and a
product with two points. This is the carrier for the represented comparison below;
DiamondsAndVStacks supplies its downstream diamond interpretation.

**Tilde-limits and inverse limits of represented functors.**
(*represented-functor-comparison*) Work with the represented functors on perfectoid test spaces,
`VQuotient.representedFunctor p : YonedaAdicSpace ⥤ ((Perfd p)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type 2)`; no topology is used.
For spaces over `Spa(Z_p, Z_p)`, these functors describe the diamond functors with the
untilt retained. The diamond interpretation, and the sheaf property on DiamondsAndVStacks' v-site,
are downstream comparisons in DiamondsAndVStacks D2.7 and D5–D6; the statements here use only the
represented functors.

(i) Let `D` be a small cofiltered system of honest analytic adic spaces over `Z_p`
with qcqs transition maps, and let `c` be a perfectoid tilde-limit cone.
`VQuotient.tildeLimit_represented_comparison` says that `representedFunctor` sends `c` to a
limit cone and gives an isomorphism from its vertex to `limit (D ⋙ representedFunctor p)`.
Its composite with each limit projection is `representedFunctor(c.π_i)`. The theorem also
gives `|c.pt| ≃ lim_i |D_i|`, with the same projections on points. Thus the functor
isomorphism and the topological comparison both use the given cone. On DiamondsAndVStacks' v-site
this becomes, downstream, `X^◇ ≅ lim_i X_i^◇`, compatibly with
`|X^◇| = |X| ≅ lim_i |X_i| = lim_i |X_i^◇|`.
`VQuotient.tildeLimit_represented_of_adic` gives the represented limit for a genuine
adic-space cone after `YonedaAdicSpace.ofAdicSpace`, with the tilde-limit hypothesis
on that Yoneda cone, a perfectoid vertex, analytic levels over `Z_p`, and qcqs
transitions. The general adic-space predicate is supplied by
`AdicSpacesPartII.AdicSpace.IsTildeLimit`.
The presheaf factorization theorem remains `IsTildeLimit.lift` in P7.10
([SW13] Proposition 2.4.5, pp. 20–21).

(ii) For a filtered diagram `B : J ⥤ CAff` of sheafy Tate pairs over `Z_p`, take a
completed-colimit cocone `b` satisfying `IsCompletedColimitOfTower`, with compatible
rings of definition and a common pseudouniformizer. Set
`U = CAff.of (Pair.uniformization b.pt.P)`, using AdicSpacesPartII R0.4.
`VQuotient.completed_colimit_uniformization_comparison` constructs the cone from
`Spa(U)` using the composites `B_j → b.pt → U`, proves that its image under
`representedFunctor` is a limit, and gives the represented form of
`lim_j Spd(B_j) ≅ Spd(U)`. The inverse isomorphism followed by
each limit projection is induced by that composite of pair maps. It also identifies
`|Spa(U)|` with the compatible finite-level points. If `U.A` is perfectoid, the same
cone is a perfectoid tilde-limit. The general completed-affinoid tilde-limit theorem
is the completed-direct-limit criterion of AdicSpacesPartII R0.20.1's *tilde-limits-affinoid-criterion*
(AdicSpacesPartII R0.20.1); P7.11 adds its
represented-functor comparison, using the uniformization universal property
([SW13] Proposition 2.4.2, p. 20; [KL15] Definition 2.8.13, p. 63).
The diamond interpretation gives `|lim_j X_j^◇| ≅ |Spa(U)|` downstream.

(iii) Suppose the levels are locally noetherian analytic over `Z_p`, the transition
maps are finite, the vertex of `c` is perfectoid, and
`IsLimit ((representedFunctor p).mapCone c)` holds. No density hypothesis is imposed.
`VQuotient.represented_limit_homeomorph` gives the homeomorphism induced by `c`.
`VQuotient.represented_limit_affinoid_basis` says that the inverse images of
finite-level affinoid opens which are affinoid perfectoid form a neighborhood basis
([HJ] Lemma 5.11, p. 32). If all levels are qcqs,
`VQuotient.represented_limit_quasicompact_open` descends each quasicompact open to
one finite level; the same statement applies after restriction over a qcqs open.
For an affinoid tower with an affinoid perfectoid representative,
`VQuotient.represented_limit_rational_subset` descends each rational subset to
finite rational data generating an open ideal. These are the finite-level
descriptions in the proof of [HJ] Lemma 5.11, p. 32, together with the spectral
quasicompact-open descent of P5.4.

The density condition remains a separate assertion.
`VQuotient.represented_uniformization_density_iff` takes the completed affinoid
system of (ii), a perfectoid pair `R`, and a map `q : b.pt → R` whose induced
`representedFunctor` map is an isomorphism. The union of the images of `B_j → R` is dense
if and only if the uniformization of `b.pt` is perfectoid. Apply this on the
finite-level affinoid inverse images from (iii) to obtain the density criterion
for `W = φ_a⁻¹(Spa(A_a, A_a⁺))`; when it holds, `W` is the spectrum of that
uniformization by its universal property and full faithfulness on perfectoid
test spaces ([SW13] Proposition 2.4.5, pp. 20–21; [KL15] Definition 2.8.13, p. 63;
[HJ] Lemma 5.11, p. 32).

**Checks.** `tildeLimit_represented_comparison_identity` gives the limit cone for a
constant perfectoid space. `tildeLimit_represented_comparison_empty` gives no
sections of the empty affinoid over a perfectoid field test space.
`represented_uniformization_density_iff_wrong_cone` excludes `Spa(Cp) → Spa(Qp)`
from the isomorphism hypothesis on represented functors, even though their underlying spaces each
have one point. These three Checks are specified in this README only.

The completed-direct-limit supplier in AdicSpacesPartII R0.20.1 gives tilde-limits
(*tilde-limit-from-completed-colimit*), with P7 using its Tate corollary:
let `(A_i, A_i⁺)_{i∈I}` be a filtered direct system of complete Huber pairs (Tau Ceti `Huber.Pair`)
with continuous transition maps, and assume there are rings of definition `A_{i,0} ⊆ A_i` mapped
into one another and finitely generated ideals of definition `I_i ⊆ A_{i,0}` with
`I_j = I_i A_{j,0}` for `j ≥ i`. Let `A := colim_i A_i` with the topology making
`A_0 := colim_i A_{i,0}` an open subring with the `I`-adic topology, `I := colim_i I_i`; let `A⁺ :=`
the integral closure in `A` of the image of `colim_i A_i⁺`, and `(Â, Â⁺)` the completion. Then (i)
`(A, A⁺)` is a Huber pair and the maps `(A_i, A_i⁺) → (A, A⁺)` are continuous; (ii) a valuation on
`A` is a continuous valuation with `|A⁺| ≤ 1` iff its restrictions to all `A_i` are, so the
restriction map `Spa(Â, Â⁺) = Spa(A, A⁺) → lim_i Spa(A_i, A_i⁺)` is a bijection, and it is a
homeomorphism; (iii) every rational subset of `Spa(A, A⁺)` is the preimage of a rational subset of
some `Spa(A_i, A_i⁺)` — in the Tate case (ii) and (iii) use
AdicSpacesPartII R0.19.7 (*spa-of-filtered-colimit-of-tate-pairs*), and the Huber-pair generality with ideals of definition
`I_i` belongs to AdicSpacesPartII R0.20.1; (iv) `colim_i A_i → Â` has dense image. Consequently, if the
`X_i = Spa(A_i, A_i⁺)` are adic spaces (`A_i` sheafy) and `Â` is perfectoid (a hypothesis of this
clause, supplied by P7.13, by P7.14, or by the application), then `Spa(Â, Â⁺) ~ lim_i X_i`. In the
Tate case with compatible pseudouniformiser `ϖ ∈ A_{i_0,0}`, the hypotheses hold with
`I_i = ϖA_{i,0}` ([SW13] §2.4, Proposition 2.4.2, p. 20; [SW13] §2.4, proof of Proposition 2.4.2,
p. 20 (step (ii))). *Needs:* *perfectoid-tilde-limit*; P5; Mathlib `Ring.DirectLimit`; Tau Ceti
`TauCeti.Huber.Pair`, `TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.spa`, `TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.spa_integralClosure`,
`TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.spaComap`, `TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.spaComap_preimage_rationalSubset`,
`TauCeti.Huber.IsRingOfIntegralElements`.

The Tate data predicate `IsCompletedColimitOfTower` uses a filtered category `J`, Huber pairs `P_j`,
a target Huber pair `Q` on `R`, transition maps `f` and a cone `g`, with identity, composition
and cone laws. It does not require the finite rings to be complete or perfectoid. Its additional
data are rings of definition `A_{j,0}` preserved by `f` and `ϖ ∈ R`; it requires `R` Hausdorff
and complete, `ϖ` a pseudouniformiser lifted from one finite ring of definition, and the closure
`R₀` of the subring generated by `⋃ g_j(A_{j,0})` to be an open ring of definition with ideal
`(ϖ)`. The union `⋃ g_j(A_j)` is dense, `Q.plus` is the closure of the integral closure of the
subring generated by `⋃ g_j(P_j.plus)`, and divisibility by `ϖ^n` in `R₀` is detected at a finite
stage for each finite-stage element and lift of `ϖ`. This predicate records the Tate
tower data used by `FrobeniusTower.isCompletedDirectLimit`; it does not define another
tilde-limit relation. The ideals are indexed by `n ∈ ℕ`; at `n = 0` divisibility by `1`
imposes no restriction.

`IsCompletedColimitOfTower.isTildeLimit_affinoid` is the corollary for a small filtered
`B : J ⥤ CAff` with cocone `b`, sheafy levels and sheafy apex, and the predicate above
on `B.map` and `b.ι.app`. Completeness and Hausdorffness come from `CAff`;
perfectoidness is not assumed. Apply the completed-direct-limit criterion of AdicSpacesPartII R0.20.1's
*tilde-limits-affinoid-criterion* after restricting to the
cofinal category under a stage carrying a pseudouniformiser `w` mapping to `ϖ`.
At each later stage use its image as the sole generator (`m = 1`), and use `ϖ` at
the apex. The existing rings of definition are retained with these principal ideals.
Density supplies approximation modulo powers, `exists_dvd_of_dvd` supplies finite-stage
detection, and `plus_eq` supplies the closed integral closure defining the plus ring.
The supplier gives the point-space homeomorphism; cofinality transports it to the
original system and `h.dense` supplies the single-affinoid density clause.
AdicSpacesPartII R0.20.1 supplies the criterion on complete sheafy carriers ([SW13] Proposition 2.4.2, p. 20).

For `B : J ⥤ CAff` and its cocone `b`,
`PerfectoidSpace.IsCompletedColimitOfTower.isTildeLimit` assumes the same completed-colimit
predicate on `B.map`, `b.ι.app`, `B₀` and `ϖ`, with every level sheafy and Tate and
`b.pt.A` a perfectoid Tate ring at the fixed prime `p`. It concludes
`PerfectoidSpace.IsTildeLimit p (B.op ⋙ S) (S.mapCone b.op)`, with the same `S` as above.
In particular, this states `Spa(Â, Â⁺) ~ lim_j Spa(A_j, A_j⁺)` on the global carrier;
sheafiness of the apex follows from perfectoidness (P2.6). It combines
`IsCompletedColimitOfTower.isTildeLimit_affinoid` with the preceding bridge, as the
perfectoid specialization of AdicSpacesPartII R0.20.1's completed-direct-limit criterion
([SW13] Proposition 2.4.2, p. 20).

**Checks for `IsCompletedColimitOfTower`.**

- `completedColimit_perfectoid` (compatibility) — the completed-colimit hypotheses with
  sheafy Tate levels and a perfectoid apex give the global perfectoid tilde-limit on the
  induced cone, by `IsCompletedColimitOfTower.isTildeLimit`.

- `completedColimit_test_const` (degenerate) — a complete perfectoid Tate pair `(R, R⁺)`
  with `ϖ ∈ R⁺` a pseudouniformiser is its own completed constant system, taking `A₀ = R⁺`.
- `completedColimit_test_Qp` (computation) — the constant pair `(ℚ_p, ℤ_p)` with
  `A₀ = ℤ_p` and `ϖ = p` satisfies the predicate, although `ℚ_p` is not perfectoid.
- `completedColimit_test_not_dense` (non-example) — the constant `(ℚ_p, ℤ_p)` system with
  cone to `(ℂ_p, O_{ℂ_p})` fails density, even though both spectra are one point.
- `completedColimit_test_zeroParameter` (non-example) — the constant `(ℚ_p, ℤ_p)` system
  with `ϖ = 0` fails the pseudouniformiser condition.

Quasicompact opens and rational subsets of a tilde-limit come from finite level
(*rational-subsets-from-finite-level*): let `X ~ lim X_i` be a perfectoid tilde-limit. Clauses
(i) and (ii) use AdicSpacesPartII R0.19.8 (*quasicompact-opens-in-limits-of-spectral-spaces*)
and P5.4's *descent-of-quasicompact-opens*, applied to the homeomorphism `|X| ≅ lim |X_i|`: (i) every
quasicompact open `U ⊆ X` is `φ_i^{-1}(U_i)` for some `i` and a quasicompact open `U_i ⊆ X_i`; if
`U_i, U′_i ⊆ X_i` are quasicompact open with `φ_i^{-1}(U_i) ⊆ φ_i^{-1}(U′_i)`, then
`f_a^{-1}(U_i) ⊆ f_a^{-1}(U′_i)` for some `a : j → i`, and likewise for equalities, finite unions
and finite intersections; (ii) a finite cover of a quasicompact open `U ⊆ X` by quasicompact opens
is the preimage of a finite cover at some finite level; what is added is (iii) if `(W, i_0, V)` is good with
`V = Spa(A, A⁺)` affinoid and `U = W ∩ {|f_k| ≤ |g| ≠ 0}` is a rational subset of `W`, there are
`j → i_0` and `f′_k, g′ ∈ O(V_a)` with `U = φ_j^{-1}(U_a(f′/g′))` for the rational subset
`U_a(f′/g′)` of `V_a` when `V_a` is affinoid; in general `U = φ_j^{-1}` of the quasicompact open
`{|f′_k| ≤ |g′| ≠ 0} ⊆ V_a` ([CHJ] §2, proof of Theorem 2.17, p. 16; [Survey] §2, proof of
Proposition 2.22 (ii), p. 11; [Stacks] Tag 0A30, Lemma 5.24.6 (part (i))). *Needs:*
*perfectoid-tilde-limit*; *good-affinoid-perfectoid*; *good-affinoid-perfectoid-basis*;
AdicSpacesPartII R0.19.5–R0.19.8 and P5.4’s perfectoid limit comparisons; P5; Tau Ceti
`TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.exists_mem_nhds_forall_rationalSubset_eq_of_sub_mem`,
`TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.spaComap_preimage_rationalSubset`.

Tilde-limits are invariant under initial changes of index category (*tilde-limit-cofinal-change*):
let `u : J → I` be an initial functor between small cofiltered categories (Mathlib
`CategoryTheory.Functor.Initial`; for directed sets, a coinitial subset). For a system
`(X_i)_{i∈I}` of analytic adic spaces with qcqs transition maps, a perfectoid space `X` and a
compatible cone `(φ_i)`, `X ~ lim_{i∈I} X_i` iff `X ~ lim_{j∈J} X_{u(j)}` for the restricted cone
`(φ_{u(j)})`. In particular: (a) for every `i_0 ∈ I` the forgetful functor `I/i_0 → I` is initial,
so a tilde-limit depends only on the tail of the system; (b) for `I = ℕ` (as an inverse system) any
infinite subsequence may be used; (c) for level families of compact open subgroups with a
cofinality witness (see *level-cofinality-witness*), the full tower and the witnessed subtower have the
same perfectoid tilde-limits ([Sch13E] item (1), p. 1; [CHJ] §2, Theorem 2.8 and the remarks after
it, p. 11). *Needs:* *perfectoid-tilde-limit*; Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Functor.Initial`,
`CategoryTheory.Functor.Initial.limitIso`, `CategoryTheory.Functor.initial_of_exists_of_isCofiltered`,
`TopCat.limitCone`.

### P7.12 locality and gluing of perfectoid tilde-limits

Perfectoid tilde-limits are local on a finite level and glue; the restriction, finite étale and
étale base-change results used in the gluing are stated with it.

**Locality and gluing of perfectoid tilde-limits.** (*tilde-limit-gluing*) Let `(X_i)_{i∈I}` be a
cofiltered system of analytic adic spaces with qcqs transition maps, `i_0 ∈ I`, and `(V^α)_α` an
open cover of `X_{i_0}` (a cover by opens of one finite level), with preimages
`V^α_a := f_a^{-1}(V^α) ⊆ X_j` (`a : j → i_0`). (i) Locality: a perfectoid space `X` with a
compatible cone satisfies `X ~ lim X_i` iff for every `α` the open subspace
`U^α := φ_{i_0}^{-1}(V^α)` satisfies `U^α ~ lim_a V^α_a`. (ii) Gluing: if for every `α` the system
`(V^α_a)_a` has a perfectoid tilde-limit `U^α`, then there is a perfectoid space `X` with a
compatible cone and `X ~ lim X_i`; `X` is glued from the `U^α` along the open subspaces
`U^{αβ} ⊆ U^α` that are the restrictions of `U^α` to `V^α ∩ V^β` (see *tilde-limit-rational-restriction*),
identified by the unique isomorphisms of *tilde-limit-perfectoid-uniqueness* (which also give the
cocycle condition). (iii) Torsion-paper form: suppose that for all large `m` the `X_m` are the
generic fibres of a tower and that `|lim_m X_m|` is covered by subsets `W` that are preimages of
affinoid opens `V_m = Spa(R_m, R_m⁺) ⊆ X_m` for all sufficiently large `m` (the level at which the
affinoid description starts may depend on `W`; compatible with the transition maps) such that,
with `R_∞⁺` the `ϖ`-adic completion of `colim_m R_m⁺` and `R_∞ = R_∞⁺[1/ϖ]`, `(R_∞, R_∞⁺⁺)` is
perfectoid (`R_∞⁺⁺` the integral closure of `R_∞⁺`); then there is a unique perfectoid space `X_∞`
with `|X_∞| = lim |X_m|` and `X_∞ ~ lim X_m`, whose restriction to each `W` is `Spa(R_∞, R_∞⁺⁺)`
([Torsion] §III.3, Definition III.3.5 (ii), p. 56 (perfectoid subsets of the topological limit are
those covered by affinoid perfectoid subsets); [Torsion] §III.3, after Definition III.3.5, p. 57
(the perfectoid structure is obtained by gluing the affinoid pieces `Spa(R_∞, R_∞⁺)`); [Torsion]
§III.2.3, proof of Corollary III.2.19, p. 43 (existence on affinoids by the completed direct limit
and uniqueness by representability, which is what makes gluing possible)). *Needs:*
*perfectoid-tilde-limit*; *tilde-limit-perfectoid-uniqueness*;
*tilde-limit-from-completed-colimit*; *tilde-limit-rational-restriction*; P2.10; P2.

Restriction of a tilde-limit to compatible open and rational subsets
(*tilde-limit-rational-restriction*): let `X ~ lim X_i` be a perfectoid tilde-limit, `i_0 ∈ I`,
`U_{i_0} ⊆ X_{i_0}` an open subset at one finite level (in particular a rational subset of an
affinoid open), `U_a := f_a^{-1}(U_{i_0}) ⊆ X_j` for `a : j → i_0` (the transition maps restricted
to the `U_a` stay qcqs), and `U := φ_{i_0}^{-1}(U_{i_0})`, an open perfectoid subspace of `X` (P2).
Then `U ~ lim_{a ∈ I/i_0} U_a` (the slice category `I/i_0`, which is initial in `I` by
*tilde-limit-cofinal-change*). Moreover, if `(W, i_0, V)` is good with `V = Spa(A, A⁺)` affinoid and
`U_{i_0} = V(f/g)` is a rational subset of `V`, then `W ∩ U = Spa(R⟨f/g⟩, R⟨f/g⟩⁺)` is the rational
localisation of `(R, R⁺) = (O(W), O⁺(W))` at the pulled-back parameters (P2.3), it is good at level
`i_0` with the rational subset `V(f/g)` (*good-affinoid-perfectoid-basis* (ii), P7.10), and
`colim_a O_{X_j}(V_a(f/g)) → R⟨f/g⟩` has dense image
([BHW] §5.2, proof of Theorem 5.11, p. 22 of the arXiv manuscript (restriction of a perfectoid tilde-limit to an open
subset pulled back from finite level); [Survey] §2, proof of Proposition 2.22, p. 11 (density on
rational subsets)). *Needs:* *perfectoid-tilde-limit*; *good-affinoid-perfectoid*;
*good-affinoid-perfectoid-basis*; *tilde-limit-cofinal-change*; P2; P2.3.

Finite étale base change of perfectoid tilde-limits (*tilde-limit-finite-etale-base-change*): let
`X ~ lim X_i` be a perfectoid tilde-limit, `i_0 ∈ I` and `g : Y_{i_0} → X_{i_0}` a finite étale
morphism of analytic adic spaces (AdicEtaleGeometry A1.3). Put
`Y_a := Y_{i_0} ×_{X_{i_0}} X_j` for `a : j → i_0` (finite étale over `X_j`) and
`Y := Y_{i_0} ×_{X_{i_0}} X`. Then `Y` exists in adic spaces, is a perfectoid space, `Y → X` is

good with `V = Spa(A, A⁺)` affinoid and `g^{-1}(V) = Spa(B, B⁺)` with `B ∈ FÉt(A)` and `B⁺` the
integral closure of `A⁺` (AdicEtaleGeometry A1.2), then the preimage of `W` in `Y` is
`Spa(B ⊗_A R, (B ⊗_A R)⁺)` with `(B ⊗_A R)⁺` the integral closure of `R⁺`, and
`colim_a (B ⊗_A O(V_a)) → B ⊗_A R` has dense image; it is good at level `i_0` with
`V′ = g^{-1}(V)` ([Sch12] §7, Lemma 7.3 (iii), p. 40 (existence and perfectoidness of the base
change); [Sch12] §7, Proposition 7.10, p. 43 (characteristic `0`); [Torsion] §III.2.4, before Lemma
III.2.25, p. 49; [BHW] §5.2, proof of Theorem 5.11, p. 22 of the arXiv manuscript (a finite étale tower over a perfectoid
tilde-limit); [Sch13] §4, Lemma 4.5, p. 23 (the analogous base change for affinoid perfectoid
pro-étale presentations)). *Needs:* *perfectoid-tilde-limit*; *good-affinoid-perfectoid*;
*good-affinoid-perfectoid-basis*; *good-affinoid-uniform-completion*;
*tilde-limit-rational-restriction*; *tilde-limit-gluing*; AdicEtaleGeometry A1.2 and A1.3; P3.16;
P3.10; P3.17; P3.

**General base-change supplier.** (*tilde-limit-base-change-comparison*)
`AdicSpacesPartII.AdicSpace.IsTildeLimit.baseChange` is the R0.20.2 theorem for
the intrinsic adic-space relation. Its hypotheses include qcqs spaces, adic
transitions and cone maps, and a base-change map locally of finite type on charts.
For analytic étale base change, apply it on qcqs affinoid charts, transport by
`AdicSpace.IsTildeLimit.ofAdicSpace_iff`, and use P3.15 to prove perfectoidness
of the apex. The resulting Yoneda theorem is
`PerfectoidSpace.IsTildeLimit.etale_baseChange`; its hypotheses specify pullback
squares at every level of `Over i` and at the apex, and compatibility with both
projections. `PerfectoidSpace.IsTildeLimit.finiteEtale_baseChange` and
`PerfectoidSpace.IsTildeLimit.open_baseChange` are its finite étale and open-immersion
corollaries. They use AdicEtaleGeometry's `YonedaAdicSpace.IsFiniteEtale`,
`IsEtaleLocalDescription` and `IsOpenImmersion`; only preservation of perfectoidness
and carrier transport are added here ([SW13] Proposition 2.4.3, p. 20).

Étale base change of perfectoid tilde-limits (*tilde-limit-etale-base-change*): let `X ~ lim X_i` be a
perfectoid tilde-limit, `i_0 ∈ I` and `g : Y_{i_0} → X_{i_0}` an étale morphism of analytic adic
spaces in the sense of AdicEtaleGeometry A1.3 (locally an open immersion into a space finite
étale over an open subset). Put `Y_a := Y_{i_0} ×_{X_{i_0}} X_j` and `Y := Y_{i_0} ×_{X_{i_0}} X`.
Then `Y` exists, is a perfectoid space étale over `X` (P3.15), and `Y ~ lim_{a ∈ I/i_0} Y_a`. The
adic-space statement — a tilde-limit is preserved by base change along a morphism locally of weakly
finite type, [SW13] Proposition 2.4.3 by reference to Huber's Remark 2.4.3 — is AdicSpacesPartII
R0.20.2 (*tilde-limit-base-change*); what is proved here is the case in which the base change of
the perfectoid space `X` is again perfectoid, the sectionwise version of [Sch12] Proposition 7.16; for non-étale `g` the fibre
product `Y` need not be perfectoid and is not considered here (Zariski-closed base changes are
[P8.21](../PerfectoidTowers/README.md#layer-p8-finite-quotients-and-closed-perfectoid-loci-in-towers)); an open immersion `U_{i_0} ⊆ X_{i_0}` recovers *tilde-limit-rational-restriction* ([SW13]
§2.4, Proposition 2.4.3, p. 20; [Sch12] §7, Proposition 7.16, p. 44; [BHW] §5.2, proof of Theorem
5.11, p. 23 of the arXiv manuscript (étale base change)). *Needs:*
*perfectoid-tilde-limit*; *tilde-limit-finite-etale-base-change*;
*tilde-limit-rational-restriction*; *tilde-limit-gluing*; AdicEtaleGeometry A1.3;
