### P7.13 the perfectoid Frobenius criterion

The criterion makes the completed generic fibre of a Frobenius-controlled tower a perfectoid
tilde-limit; its three ingredients are the Frobenius bijection with the uniformity bound, the tilt
of the limit, and the perfection of a characteristic-`p` space as the tilde-limit along relative
Frobenius.

**The perfectoid Frobenius criterion: Frobenius-controlled towers have perfectoid tilde-limits.**
(*perfectoid-frobenius-criterion-for-towers*) Let `(A_•⁺, ϖ, m_0, w)` be a Frobenius-controlled
integral tower (*frobenius-controlled-integral-tower*; the eventual Frobenius lifting modulo `ϖ^p`
is the only input beyond `ϖ`-torsion-freeness and `ϖ`-adic completeness) with generic fibres `(A_m, A_m⁺⁺)` and
completion `(A_∞, A_∞⁺⁺)` (see *frobenius-tower-completion*). Then: (i) `A_∞` is a perfectoid Tate ring
in the sense of [ECD] Definition 3.1 (complete, uniform, with the pseudouniformiser `ϖ` satisfying
`ϖ^p | p` in `A_∞°` and `Φ : A_∞°/ϖ ≅ A_∞°/ϖ^p`), when `A_∞ ≠ 0`, of characteristic `p` exactly when `p = 0` in
`A_∞` (so whenever some `A_m⁺` has characteristic `p`; a non-injective `t_m` may kill `p` at a
finite level even if `A_0⁺` has characteristic `0`), and `(A_∞, A_∞⁺⁺)` is a perfectoid Tate
pair; (ii) the restriction map identifies
`|Spa(A_∞, A_∞⁺⁺)|` with `lim_m |Spa(A_m, A_m⁺⁺)|`, and, when the `A_m` are sheafy (for instance
strongly noetherian, as for affinoids of rigid spaces), `X_∞ := Spa(A_∞, A_∞⁺⁺) ~ lim_m X_m` in the
sense of *perfectoid-tilde-limit*, `X_∞` is unique up to unique isomorphism, and it represents
`lim_m Hom(−, X_m)` on perfectoid spaces; (iii) global form: let `(𝔛_m)` be a tower of flat
`ϖ`-adic formal schemes (over a `ϖ`-adically complete base) with generic fibres `X_m` analytic adic
spaces, and suppose `𝔛_{m_0}` has an affine open cover by `Spf A_{m_0}⁺` whose preimages `Spf A_m⁺`
(`m ≥ m_0`) form Frobenius-controlled towers compatibly with restriction; then the generic fibres
have a perfectoid tilde-limit `X_∞ ~ lim X_m`, glued from the `Spa(A_∞, A_∞⁺⁺)`
(see *tilde-limit-gluing*), which is the generic fibre of the formal scheme `lim 𝔛_m` (limit in formal
schemes, affine-locally `Spf A_∞⁺`). This theorem concerns towers whose finite levels are not
perfectoid; the case of perfectoid finite levels is P7.14 ([Torsion] §III.2.3, proof of Corollary
III.2.19, p. 42 (the eventual Frobenius lifting condition: transition maps equal to relative
Frobenius modulo `p^{1−ε} = ϖ^p` with `ϖ = p^{(1−ε)/p}`); [Torsion] §III.2.3, proof of Corollary
III.2.19, p. 43 (the tilde-limit and its uniqueness from the completed limit; the completed limit is
a perfectoid integral algebra in the sense of [Sch12] Definition 5.1(ii), reached here over no base
field via [BMS] Lemmas 3.10 and 3.21); [BHW] §5.2, proof of Theorem 5.11, p. 22 of the arXiv manuscript (the
Hilbert-modular instance: relative Frobenius modulo `p^{1−δ}`); [Sch13] §4, Example 4.4, p. 23 (the
torus tower over a perfectoid field)). *Needs:* *frobenius-controlled-integral-tower*;
*frobenius-tower-completion*; *frobenius-tower-uniformity-bound*;
*tilde-limit-from-completed-colimit*; *tilde-limit-perfectoid-uniqueness*; *tilde-limit-gluing*;
*perfectoid-tilde-limit*; P1; P1.1; P2.6; P2.10.

Frobenius on the completed tower is bijective modulo `ϖ`, and the uniformity bound
`ϖA_∞° ⊆ A_∞⁺` holds (*frobenius-tower-uniformity-bound*): let `(A_•⁺, ϖ, m_0, w)` be a
Frobenius-controlled integral tower with completion `(A_∞⁺, A_∞, A_∞⁺⁺)`
(see *frobenius-tower-completion*); only the terms `m ≥ m_0` matter. Then: (i)
`Φ : A_∞⁺/ϖ → A_∞⁺/ϖ^p`, `x ↦ x^p`, is a bijection (in fact `colim_m A_m⁺/ϖ → colim_m A_m⁺/ϖ^p`
is, and these are the quotients of `A_∞⁺`); (ii) `A_∞⁺` is a `ϖ`-torsion-free, `ϖ`-adically
complete ring with `p ∈ ϖ^pA_∞⁺` and bijective Frobenius modulo `ϖ`, hence an integral perfectoid
ring in the sense of [BMS] Definition 3.5 (Lemma 3.10(ii)); (iii) uniformity bound: `A_∞⁺ ⊆ A_∞°`
and `ϖ·A_∞° ⊆ A_∞⁺`; more precisely, after replacing `ϖ` by a unit multiple admitting a compatible
system of `p`-power roots ([BMS] Lemma 3.9), the cokernel of `A_∞⁺ → A_∞°` is killed by every
`ϖ^{1/p^n}`, i.e. `A_∞⁺ → A_∞°` is an almost isomorphism for the ideal `(ϖ^{1/p^∞})` (P1);
consequently `A_∞°` is bounded, `A_∞` is uniform, and the `ϖ`-adic topology on `A_∞⁺` is the
topology of the spectral norm of `A_∞`; (iv) `A_∞⁺⁺` satisfies
`A_∞⁺ ⊆ A_∞⁺⁺ ⊆ A_∞° ⊆ ϖ^{-1}A_∞⁺` ([Torsion] §III.2.3, proof of Corollary III.2.19, pp. 42–43
(the colimit Frobenius isomorphism `R_∞/ϖ ≅ R_∞/ϖ^p`); [BMS] §3.2, Lemma 3.10 (ii), p. 22 (step
(ii)); [BMS] §3.2, Lemma 3.21, p. 27 (passage to the Tate ring and the uniformity bound)). *Needs:*
*frobenius-controlled-integral-tower*; *frobenius-tower-completion*; P1 (P1.24, P1.25); Mathlib
`frobenius`, `AdicCompletion`, `Ring.DirectLimit`.

The tilt of the limit of a Frobenius-controlled tower (*frobenius-tower-tilt*): let
`(A_•⁺, ϖ, m_0, w)` be a Frobenius-controlled integral tower and `(S_•⁺, t, m_0, w′)` a
Frobenius-controlled integral tower of characteristic `p` (`p = 0` in `S_0⁺`), together with ring
isomorphisms `α_m : A_m⁺/ϖ^p ≅ S_m⁺/t^p` for `m ≥ m_0` compatible with the transition maps (and
with the `w`, `w′`), and quotient isomorphisms `β_m : A_m⁺/ϖ ≅ S_m⁺/t`
induced by the `α_m`. The quotient map uses `(t^p) ⊆ (t)`, from `1 ≤ p`;
parameter-preserving tower morphisms likewise carry `(ϖ^p)` into `(t^p)`. Require `α_m ∘ w_m = w′_m ∘ β_{m+1}`; the comparisons need not lift
to the integral rings. The completed tilt theorem `completed_tilt` states that the perfectoid
Tate ring `S_∞ = S_∞⁺[1/t]` of *perfectoid-frobenius-criterion-for-towers* is perfect and that
there is a unique topological ring isomorphism `e : A_∞♭ ≅ S_∞` preserving the Huber-pair
plus rings and satisfying the following characteristic equation. Write
`c : A_∞⁺/ϖ ≅ S_∞⁺/t` for the colimit of the `β_m`: for finite-level representatives with
`β_m([a]) = [b]`, require `c([ι_m(a)]) = [ι_m(b)]`. For every compatible integral root sequence
`x ∈ lim_{z ↦ z^p} A_∞⁺`, its image under `e` lies in `S_∞⁺`, and
`c([x⁽⁰⁾]) = [e(x)]`. Thus the square with sharp on the source and reduction modulo `t`
on the target commutes on the completed integral models, before taking integral closures.
The inverse Frobenius limits of these quotients determine the integral comparison uniquely
([BMS] Lemma 3.2(i), p. 19).
For every such `ϖ♭` with `(ϖ♭)⁽⁰⁾ = ϖu`, `u ∈ (A_∞⁺)ˣ`, also require
`e(ϖ♭) = tv` for some `v ∈ (S_∞⁺)ˣ`; such a choice of `ϖ♭` exists by [BMS] Lemma 3.9,
p. 22, and the sharp quotient has kernel `(ϖ♭)` by Lemma 3.10, pp. 22–23.
Under this isomorphism, `Spa(S_∞, S_∞⁺⁺)` is the tilt of
`Spa(A_∞, A_∞⁺⁺)`, and in the global form of the criterion the tilt of `X_∞` is the limit of the
characteristic-`p` tower ([Torsion] §III.2.3, proof of Corollary III.2.19, p. 43 (the tilt
identification from the congruence of the two towers); [Torsion] §III.2.3, before Definition
III.2.18, p. 42 (the characteristic-`p` side is a perfection)). *Needs:*
*perfectoid-frobenius-criterion-for-towers*; *frobenius-tower-completion*;
*frobenius-tower-uniformity-bound*; P1; P1.27.

Checks for the completed tilt theorem `completed_tilt`:

- `completed_tilt_identity_reduction`: for a characteristic-`p` tower compared with itself,
  the canonical tilt isomorphism sends an integral root sequence to its zeroth coordinate,
  so the quotient comparison is the identity.
- `completed_tilt_zero_reduction`: when both completed integral models are zero, their quotient
  rings admit exactly one isomorphism and every representative equation holds.
- `completed_tilt_swap_reduction`: on the split characteristic-two quotient `𝔽₂ × 𝔽₂`,
  swapping the factors sends `(1,0)` to `(0,1)`. It cannot satisfy the identity comparison;
  preservation of integral elements alone would not detect this change.

The perfection of a characteristic-`p` adic space is a tilde-limit along relative Frobenius
(*perfection-tilde-limit*): let `k` be a perfect complete nonarchimedean field of characteristic `p`
with pseudouniformiser `t` (more generally a perfect complete Tate ring of characteristic `p` with
`t ∈ k°` admitting all `p`-power roots), `(S, S⁺)` a complete Tate pair over `(k, k°)` with `S⁺`
flat over `k°` and `t`-adically complete. Put `S_m⁺ := S⁺ ⊗_{k°, F^{-m}} k°`, with the `k°`-algebra
structure from the right factor, and use the transitions `s ⊗ c ↦ s^p ⊗ c`. These are well defined:
`(as)^p ⊗ c = s^p ⊗ F^{-(m+1)}(a^p)c = s^p ⊗ F^{-m}(a)c`.
No identification of a Frobenius twist with `S` as a `k`-algebra is required. (i) This tower is
Frobenius-controlled with `ϖ = 1 ⊗ t` and `w_m` the base-change isomorphisms
of `FrobeniusTower.ofRelativeFrobenius`, specified for `FrobeniusTower.perfection` by its lift
specification (P7.5): `w_m([s ⊗ c]) = [s ⊗ c^p]`;
(ii) its completion is `S^{perf⁺} :=` the `t`-adic
completion of `colim_m S_m⁺` with
`S^{perf} = S^{perf⁺}[1/t]`, a perfect, hence perfectoid, Tate ring; (iii) if `S` is sheafy,
`Y^{perf} := Spa(S^{perf}, S^{perf⁺⁺}) ~ lim_m Y_m`, where
`Y_m = Spa(S_m⁺[1/t], S_m⁺)` and `Y = Y_0 = Spa(S, S⁺)`, the maps `|Y^{perf}| → |Y|`
are homeomorphisms, and `Y^{perf}` is the unique perfectoid space over `k` with this property; (iv)
for an analytic adic space `Y` over `k` covered by such affinoids, the `Y^{perf}` glue to a
perfectoid space `Y^{perf} ~ lim_Φ Y` (see *tilde-limit-gluing*). Here `lim_Φ Y` denotes this tower of base twists. The corresponding statement for flat
`t`-adic formal schemes `𝔜`: `lim_Φ 𝔜` is representable by the perfect flat formal scheme
`𝔜^{perf}`, locally `Spf(R^{perf})`, compatibly with generic fibres ([Torsion] §III.2.3,
Definition III.2.18 (ii), p. 42 (statements (ii)–(iv) over the base of the source; the tilde-limit
is that of Scholze–Weinstein); [Torsion] §III.2.3, Definition III.2.18 (i), p. 42 (the
formal-scheme version)). *Needs:* *frobenius-controlled-integral-tower*;
*frobenius-tower-completion*; *perfectoid-frobenius-criterion-for-towers*; *tilde-limit-gluing*;
P1; P1.1.

Lean: `FrobeniusTower.isIntegralPerfectoid_completedPlus` (the completion `A_∞⁺` of a
Frobenius-controlled tower is integral perfectoid, the integral form of (i) of
*perfectoid-frobenius-criterion-for-towers*, [BMS] Lemma 3.10(ii)).

### P7.14 limits of towers of perfectoid spaces

The easy limit theorem: when every finite level is already perfectoid, the limit exists in
perfectoid spaces and is a tilde-limit.

**Towers of perfectoid spaces with affinoid transition maps have perfectoid tilde-limits.**
(*limit-of-perfectoid-tower*) Let `(X_i)_{i∈I}` be a cofiltered system of perfectoid spaces whose
transition maps are affinoid (for every `a : j → i` and every affinoid open `V ⊆ X_i`, `f_a^{-1}(V)`
is affinoid; hence qcqs; as for finite étale towers of affinoids). Then: (i) the limit
`X := lim_i X_i` exists in the category of perfectoid spaces, glued from the affinoid limits of
P5.3; (ii) `X ~ lim_i X_i` (see *perfectoid-tilde-limit*), and `X` represents `lim_i Hom(−, X_i)`
on perfectoid spaces (P7.10 (i) once (ii) is known); (iii) for `i_0 ∈ I` and an affinoid perfectoid
open `V = Spa(R_{i_0}, R_{i_0}⁺) ⊆ X_{i_0}` with preimages `V_a = Spa(R_a, R_a⁺)`, the preimage of
`V` in `X` is the completed direct limit `Spa(R, R⁺)` of P5.1–P5.2 (`R⁺` the `ϖ`-adic completion
of `colim_a R_a⁺`, `R = R⁺[1/ϖ]`, perfectoid); (iv) `|X| ≅ lim_i |X_i|` (P5.4); (v) if `I` is
`ω_1`-cofiltered, `colim R_a → R` and `colim R_a⁺ → R⁺` are bijective (P5.5 applied to the
affinoid pieces). Every finite level is already perfectoid here; the theorem is
distinct from *perfectoid-frobenius-criterion-for-towers*, whose finite levels are not perfectoid
([BHW] §5.2, proof of Theorem 5.11, p. 23 of the arXiv manuscript; [ECD] §6,
Proposition 6.5, p. 29 (the affinoid case); [ECD] §6, proof of Proposition 6.5, p. 29 (the universal
property on affinoids)). *Needs:* P5.3; P1.25; *frobenius-tower-uniformity-bound*;
*tilde-limit-from-completed-colimit*; *tilde-limit-perfectoid-uniqueness*; *tilde-limit-gluing*;
*perfectoid-tilde-limit*; P2.9; P5.2; P1.

### P7.15 noetherian tilde-limits and the comparison of étale topoi

**Tilde-limits `X ~ lim X_i` of noetherian adic spaces and the comparison of étale topoi.**
(*tilde-limits-and-etale-topos-comparison*) Let `(X_i)_{i∈I}` be a cofiltered system of
quasicompact quasiseparated locally noetherian analytic adic spaces (AdicSpacesPartII R0.6; no
perfectoid base field is assumed, and the `X_i` may lie over `Spa(Q_p, Z_p)` while `X` lies over a
perfectoid field), `X` a perfectoid space (its étale site is that of [Sch12] Definition 7.11 /
[ECD] Definition 6.2) and `X ~′ lim X_i` (*residue-field-tilde-limit*; this holds whenever
`X ~ lim X_i`, *tilde-limit-implies-residue-field-tilde-limit*). Then: (i) `|X|` is a spectral space
and `X` is qcqs ([Sch12] Remark 7.15); (ii) (Theorem 7.17) the étale topos `X_ét^~` of the
perfectoid space `X` (P3.18) is the projective limit of the fibred topos `(X_{i,ét}^~)_i` of the
étale topoi of the `X_i` (AdicEtaleGeometry A1.6, equal to Huber's): `X_ét^~` is equivalent to
the topos of sheaves on the colimit site `colim_i (X_i)_{ét,qcqs}` (objects qcqs étale over some
`X_i`, morphisms the filtered colimits of Hom sets, coverings the families that are coverings at
some finite level), compatibly with the pullback morphisms `X_ét^~ → X_{i,ét}^~`; (iii) (Corollary
7.18) for `i_0 ∈ I` and a sheaf of abelian groups `F_{i_0}` on `X_{i_0,ét}`, with pullbacks `F_j` to
`X_{j,ét}` (`j → i_0`) and `F` to `X_ét`, the natural map `colim_j H^n(X_{j,ét}, F_j) → H^n(X_ét, F)`
is bijective for all `n ≥ 0` (for sheaves of sets, `n = 0`; for sheaves of groups, `n ≤ 1`). When
`X` is itself locally noetherian (and not assumed perfectoid), the corresponding statements are
Huber's Proposition 2.4.4 and Corollary 2.4.6 ([Huber96], §2.4, pp. 127–129); the perfectoid extension uses
local factorisation of étale maps and finite étale descent by henselian approximation (AdicEtaleGeometry A1.0.5).
On the good affinoid charts of P7.4, `GoodAffinoid.finiteEtaleEquiv` supplies this descent
by composing AdicEtaleGeometry A1.0.5's `finiteEtale_completedColimit` ([Berkeley] Theorem 7.4.8 and
its corollary, printed p. 54) with AdicEtaleGeometry A4.4's
`Huber.Pair.uniformization.baseChange_finiteEtale_equivalence`
([KL15] Proposition 2.8.16(a), p. 64). Corollary 7.19
is *etale-topos-invariance-under-inseparable-towers* ([Sch12] §7, proof of Theorem 7.17, p. 44;
[Sch12] §7, Corollary 7.18, p. 44 (statement (iii)); [Sch12] §7, before Definition 7.14, p. 43 (the
purpose of the comparison); [SW13] §2.4, Theorem 2.4.7, p. 21 (restatement of (ii) for the
sectionwise tilde-limit); [Sch13] §4, proof of Theorem 4.9, p. 26 (the application over `Q_p`)).
*Needs:* *residue-field-tilde-limit*; *tilde-limit-implies-residue-field-tilde-limit*;
*residue-field-tilde-limit-etale-base-change*; *tilde-limit-qcqs-etale-finite-stage-descent*;
P3.20; P3.21; P3.18; P3.15; AdicEtaleGeometry A1.0.5; AdicEtaleGeometry A1.3, A1.6 and A4.4; AdicSpacesPartII R0.6;
AdicSpacesPartII R0.19.5–R0.19.8 and P5.4’s perfectoid limit comparisons; P5; Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Limits.limit`, `TopCat.Presheaf`.

The colimit site's `residueEtalePrecoverage` consists of finite families represented
at a common finite stage and jointly surjective there. `residueEtaleTopology` is
the topology it generates. `residueEtaleTopos` identifies sheaves on this site
with sheaves on the perfectoid étale site; its presheaf equation specifies
restriction to every finite-stage object ([Sch12] Theorem 7.17).

For abelian coefficients, `residueEtaleSheafPullback` and
`residueEtaleLimitSheaf` are the inverse-image functors on A1's finite-stage
`YonedaAdicSpace.smallEtaleTopology` and on `smallEtaleTopology p ⟨c.pt, h.perfectoid⟩`,
respectively. `residueEtaleSheafPullback_universal` and
`residueEtaleLimitSheaf_universal` characterize them by Hom equivalences natural
in both sheaves, using geometric base change on the qcqs bases. Coefficients are
in `AddCommGrpCat.{2}` and cohomology in universe 3; these size choices allow
Mathlib's sheafification and `HasExt.standard` without a small skeleton.
For `h : IsResidueFieldTildeLimit p D c`, an initial stage `i`, a sheaf `F` there,
and any `n : ℕ`, `residueEtaleCohomologyDiagram` is indexed by `(Over i)ᵒᵖ`:
its value at `a : j → i` is `Sheaf.H (a* F) n`. The arrows and the legs of
`residueEtaleCohomologyCocone` are induced by exact inverse image on Ext,
as specified by `residueEtaleCohomologyDiagram_map` and
`residueEtaleCohomologyCocone_map`; the natural coefficient comparisons are
chosen independently of `F` and `n`. The cocone's vertex is
`Sheaf.H ((residueEtaleLimitSheaf p D c h i).obj F) n` on the perfectoid site.
The cohomology comparison (*etale-cohomology-along-residue-field-towers*)
`residueEtaleCohomologyColimit` asserts its universal property, and
`residueEtaleCohomologyColimit_isIso` states that its canonical map from the
filtered colimit is an isomorphism of abelian groups ([Sch12] §7, Corollary 7.18,
p. 44). This includes degrees zero and one and all higher nonnegative degrees;
no torsion or constructibility condition is imposed on the abelian sheaf.

**Checks.** `residueEtaleSheafPullback_identity`, `_zero`, and `_constant`
identify identity pullback, preservation of the zero sheaf, and pullback of
constant abelian coefficients. `residueEtaleLimitSheaf_zero`, `_constant`, and
`_transition` check zero coefficients, constant coefficients, and compatibility
with a finite-stage transition. `residueEtaleCohomologyDiagram_identity`, `_zero`,
and `_degreeZero` check identity arrows, zero cohomology for the zero sheaf in
every degree, and the identification of degree zero with sections at a terminal
étale object. `residueEtaleCohomologyCocone_zero`, `_degreeZero`, and `_degreeOne`
check the zero vertex, the same sections convention on the perfectoid site, and
bijectivity of the degree-one colimit comparison.

**Checks.** For both `residueEtalePrecoverage` and `residueEtaleTopology`,
`_identity` covers an object by itself, `_empty` covers an empty finite-stage
object by the empty family, and `_nonempty` excludes the empty covering of an
object whose pullback to the limit has a point.

A perfectoid tilde-limit over qcqs locally noetherian spaces is a residue-field tilde-limit
(*tilde-limit-implies-residue-field-tilde-limit*): let `X ~ lim X_i` be a perfectoid tilde-limit
(see *perfectoid-tilde-limit*) with every `X_i` quasicompact, quasiseparated and locally noetherian
analytic (so that `~′` is defined). Then `X ~′ lim X_i` (see *residue-field-tilde-limit*): for every
`x ∈ X` with images `x_i`, `colim_i k(x_i)^ → k(x)^` has dense image ([SW13] §2.4, after Theorem
2.4.7, p. 21). *Needs:* *perfectoid-tilde-limit*; *residue-field-tilde-limit*;
*good-affinoid-perfectoid-basis*; P2.5.

Étale base change of residue-field tilde-limits, and bijectivity suffices
(*residue-field-tilde-limit-etale-base-change*): let `X ~′ lim X_i` be a residue-field tilde-limit,
`i_0 ∈ I` and `g : Y → X_{i_0}` an étale morphism of qcqs locally noetherian analytic adic spaces
(Huber's étale, equal to the local description of AdicEtaleGeometry A1.3). Put
`Y_a := Y ×_{X_{i_0}} X_j` (`a : j → i_0`) and `Y_X := Y ×_{X_{i_0}} X`, a perfectoid space étale
over `X`. Then (i) `Y_X ~′ lim_a Y_a`; (ii) (the remark in the proof) in Definition 7.14, if `X`
is quasicompact and quasiseparated, `|X| → lim |X_i|` is bijective and the residue-field condition
(c) holds, then `|X| → lim |X_i|` is already a homeomorphism (a bijective, generalizing, spectral
map of spectral spaces), i.e. `X ~′ lim X_i`; quasicompactness cannot be dropped: for a perfectoid field `K`, let
`X_n = ⨿_{a ∈ ℤ/p^nℤ} Spa(K, K°)` with transitions induced by reduction of the index. The space
`X = ⨿_{a ∈ ℤ_p} Spa(K, K°)` maps compatibly to this tower, bijectively onto the underlying limit
`ℤ_p`, with all completed residue fields equal to `K`. Its underlying space is discrete, whereas
`ℤ_p` has its compact nondiscrete topology; thus the map is not a homeomorphism; for an open immersion `Y ⊆ X_{i_0}`, `Y_X` is the open
subspace `φ_{i_0}^{-1}(Y)` ([Sch12] §7, Proposition 7.16, p. 44 (statement (i)); [Sch12] §7, proof
of Proposition 7.16, p. 44 (statement (ii)); [Stacks] Tag 0A2Z, Lemma 5.24.5 (spectrality of
`lim |X_i|` used in (ii))). *Needs:* *residue-field-tilde-limit*; P3.16; AdicEtaleGeometry A1.0.5; P2.5;
AdicEtaleGeometry A1.3; AdicSpacesPartII R0.19.5–R0.19.8 and P5.4’s perfectoid limit comparisons; P3.

Qcqs étale spaces over a residue-field tilde-limit descend to a finite level
(*tilde-limit-qcqs-etale-finite-stage-descent*): let `X ~′ lim X_i` be a residue-field tilde-limit
with all `X_i` qcqs locally noetherian analytic and `X` perfectoid. Then: (i) base change induces an
equivalence of categories `2-colim_i (X_i)_{ét,qcqs} → X_{ét,qcqs}` between qcqs étale adic spaces
over the `X_i` (AdicEtaleGeometry A1.6) and qcqs étale perfectoid spaces over `X` (P3.18), and
likewise `2-colim_i (X_i)_{fét} → X_{fét}`; (ii) a finite family of morphisms `(Z^k_i → Y_i)_k` in
`(X_i)_{ét,qcqs}` is jointly surjective after base change to `X` if and only if it is so after base
change to some `X_j`. This is the perfectoid-limit analogue of [ECD] Proposition 6.4(i)–(ii)
(P5.12), with the `X_i` locally noetherian instead of affinoid perfectoid ([Sch12] §7, proof of
Theorem 7.17, p. 44 (finite étale maps descend by henselian approximation, AdicEtaleGeometry A1.0.5); [ECD] §6, proof of
Proposition 6.4, p. 28 (the graph argument for fullness, and essential surjectivity); [Berkeley]
Lecture 7, after Theorem 7.4.8, p. 54 (finite étale algebras over completed colimits of complete
Tate rings)). *Needs:* *residue-field-tilde-limit*; *residue-field-tilde-limit-etale-base-change*;
AdicEtaleGeometry A1.0.5; P3.18; P3.15; P2.5; AdicEtaleGeometry A1.3 and A1.6; P5.12; AdicSpacesPartII R0.19.5–R0.19.8 and P5.4’s perfectoid limit comparisons; P5; P3.

`analyticQcqsEtale` is the qcqs full subcategory of A1’s
`YonedaAdicSpace.smallEtale`. Its perfectoid target `qcqsEtale p X` uses
`smallEtale p X`, the restriction of A1’s `IsEtaleLocalDescription` to
`Perfd p`, with site comparison `smallEtaleAdicEquiv`. Quasi-compactness
of its structural map and diagonal is R0’s `AdicSpace.QuasiCompact`,
applied through `toAdicSpace`. Thus the perfectoid carrier retains its
objects and commuting triangles while using the supplied morphism predicates.
Checks `qcqsEtale_identity`, `qcqsEtale_empty`, and `qcqsEtale_noncompact`
include the identity and empty open immersion and exclude an étale arrow
whose adic representative fails R0 quasi-compactness.
`analyticEtalePullback_spec` and `analyticEtalePullback_map` specify geometric
pullback and its maps in this same A1 site. Étaleness is A1's local description
around each point, as in `IsResidueFieldTildeLimit.etale_baseChange`.
`IsResidueFieldTildeLimit.level_isAnalytic` extracts each stage’s analytic Tate charts
from its locally noetherian hypothesis ([Sch12] §7, p. 39).
`residueEtaleDiagram` is the corresponding finite-stage pseudofunctor;
`residueEtaleComparison_spec` identifies its comparison with pullback to the
perfectoid limit. Under the residue-field tilde-limit hypotheses above,
`residueEtaleComparison_isEquivalence` gives the equivalence,
`residueEtaleComparison_finite` detects A1's `YonedaAdicSpace.IsFiniteEtale`
at a finite stage, and `residueEtaleComparison_cover` detects finite covering
families after passage to a later stage. On the perfectoid carrier,
`IsFiniteEtale p` is the restriction of this same A1 predicate.
These are the finite-stage assertions in the proof of [Sch12] Theorem 7.17, p. 44.

**Checks.** `analyticQcqsEtale_suppliedEtale` and
`analyticEtalePullback_suppliedEtale` extract A1's local étale condition.
`analyticQcqsEtale_nonqcqs` excludes a supplied étale object whose structural
map is not qcqs; `analyticQcqsEtale_fullHom` retains every A1 morphism between
qcqs objects. `residueEtaleComparison_suppliedFiniteEtale` expresses the
finite-stage criterion with A1's finite étale predicate on both sides.
`residueEtaleDiagram_suppliedCover` identifies finite-stage covering sieves
with A1's pointwise covering condition.

The cartesian projections are chosen simultaneously and naturally:
`analyticEtalePullbackProjection_exists` supplies this family,
`analyticEtalePullbackProjection` selects it, and
`analyticEtalePullbackProjection_isPullback` and
`analyticEtalePullbackProjection_naturality` specify its cartesian squares
and its compatibility with every map of étale objects.
`analyticEtalePullbackIdIso_exists` and
`analyticEtalePullbackCompIso_exists` give unique comparison isomorphisms
preserving these projections, for analytic bases and arbitrary composable
base maps. `analyticEtalePullbackIdIso_projection` identifies the forward
identity comparison with the projection; `analyticEtalePullbackCompIso_projection`
identifies the inverse composition comparison followed by the direct
projection with the two successive projections. The selected
`analyticEtalePullbackIdIso` and `analyticEtalePullbackCompIso` supply the
identity and composition fields of `residueEtaleDiagram`, after transport
along the diagram's identity and composition equations. For the cofiltered
system `D` and `h : IsResidueFieldTildeLimit p D c`,
`residueEtaleDiagram_mapId_hom_app` identifies each identity component
with the chosen cartesian projection over `D.map (𝟙 i)`.
For `a : j → i`, `b : k → j` and a qcqs étale object `U` over `D_i`,
`residueEtaleDiagram_mapComp_hom_app` says that the forward comparison
from direct to iterated pullback, followed by the projections to the
pullback over `D_j` and then to `U`, equals the direct projection to `U`.
The component already lies over `D_k`, so these equations determine it
by the pullback universal property. Mathlib's
`pseudofunctorOfIsLocallyDiscrete` supplies `map₂` by equality transport;
there is no additional choice of a transformation on 2-morphisms.
`IsResidueFieldTildeLimit.level_isAnalytic` supplies all analytic-base
hypotheses. The underlying universal property is geometric base change
in [Sch12] Proposition 7.16 and the proof of Theorem 7.17, p. 44.

**Checks.** `residueEtaleDiagram_identity_projection` fixes the unit
component, `residueEtaleDiagram_two_steps` fixes the order of the two
successive projections, and `residueEtaleDiagram_nontrivial_automorphism`
shows that postcomposing the unit component with a nonidentity automorphism
changes it. Thus a permutation of an étale object's components cannot be
inserted into the unit comparison.

**Checks.** `analyticEtalePullbackProjection_square` fixes the structural
map equation, `_empty` has empty source over an empty étale object, and
`_isomorphism` makes the projection invertible along an invertible base
map. For each of `analyticEtalePullbackIdIso` and
`analyticEtalePullbackCompIso`, `_projection` fixes the comparison,
`_empty` retains the empty object, and `_not_twisted` excludes any map
that changes the projection to the original étale object.

**Checks.** For `analyticQcqsEtale` and `analyticEtalePullback`, `_identity`
recovers the given object, `_empty` stays empty, and `_split` pulls back an
isomorphism to an isomorphism. For `residueEtaleDiagram` and
`residueEtaleComparison`, `_identity` fixes identity maps, `_empty` stays empty,
and `_sections` detects equality of maps at some later finite stage.

`IsResidueFieldTildeLimit.level_isAnalytic` supplies analyticity of each
noetherian analytic finite stage for A1’s `YonedaAdicSpace.smallEtaleTopology`
in `inseparable_tower_etale_topos` ([Sch12] Definition 7.14, pp. 43–44).

Towers with homeomorphic, purely inseparable transition maps do not change the étale topos
(*etale-topos-invariance-under-inseparable-towers*): in the situation of
*tilde-limits-and-etale-topos-comparison* (`X ~′ lim X_i`, `X_i` qcqs locally noetherian analytic,
`X` perfectoid), assume that every transition map `X_j → X_i` induces a homeomorphism `|X_j| → |X_i|`
and purely inseparable extensions of completed residue fields (a universal-homeomorphism condition,
typically relative Frobenius in characteristic `p`). Then for every `i` the pullback
`X_ét^~ → X_{i,ét}^~` is an equivalence of topoi; in particular `H^n(X_ét, F) = H^n(X_{i,ét}, F_i)`
for every abelian sheaf `F_i` on `X_{i,ét}` with pullback `F` ([Sch12] §7, Corollary 7.19, p. 44;
[Sch12] §7, proof of Corollary 7.19, p. 44 (by reference to Huber)). *Needs:*
*tilde-limits-and-etale-topos-comparison*; *perfection-tilde-limit*;
*tilde-limit-qcqs-etale-finite-stage-descent*.

<a id="p7-16-rigid-proetale-site"></a>

### P7.16 the pro-étale site of a rigid space

**Pro-étale site of a rigid space; affinoid perfectoid objects.** (*proetale-site*) Let `X` be a
locally noetherian adic space over `Spa(k, k°)` for a complete nonarchimedean field `k ⊇ ℚ_p`. Its
pro-étale site `X_proét` — objects the pro-objects `lim U_i` of `X_ét` along cofiltered diagrams
with finite étale surjective transition maps from some index on, coverings the families with the
corrected transfinite covering condition ([Sch13E], correction (1), p. 1), and the morphism of sites
`ν : X_proét → X_ét` — is AdicEtaleGeometry layer A1 ([*pro-etale-morphism*](../AdicEtaleGeometry/README.md) (AdicEtaleGeometry A1.10),
[*pro-etale-site-corrected*](../AdicEtaleGeometry/README.md) (AdicEtaleGeometry A1.12), API `AdicSpace.ProEtale.ProEt`, `IsProEtale`, `ProEtalePresentation`),
with its site and carrier interfaces supplied by AdicEtaleGeometry A1.10–A1.12; it is not built again here. An
object `U = lim U_i ∈ X_proét` with each `U_i = Spa(R_i, R_i⁺)` affinoid is affinoid perfectoid if
the pair obtained by completing `colim R_i⁺` for the `p`-adic topology and then
inverting `p`, with `R⁺ = (colim R_i⁺)^∧` and `R = R⁺[1/p]`, is a perfectoid
Tate pair (the objects compared in [P6.14](README.md), [*scholze-2013-affinoid-perfectoid-comparison*](README.md), which also
supplies the functoriality of `U ↦ Û` and the fact that `Û` is affinoid pro-étale over the
completion of a smaller object); the associated affinoid perfectoid space `Û = Spa(R, R⁺)`
satisfies `Û ~ lim U_i` ([P7.2](README.md)). What is proved here: affinoid perfectoid objects form a basis
of `X_proét` ([Sch13] Proposition 4.8 proves this over a perfectoid field `K` of characteristic
`0` and Remark 4.11 extends it to any such `k` by base change), products of an affinoid perfectoid
object with a profinite set are affinoid perfectoid ([Sch13] Corollary 6.6), and the points of
`Spa(R, R⁺)` (not all continuous valuations of `R`: `R⁺` need not be `R°`) correspond to the
points of `lim |U_i|`. In the perfectoid-base comparison consumed by DiamondsAndVStacks D2, a constant
pro-object `U_i = U = Spa(R₀, R₀⁺)` is affinoid perfectoid iff
`(R₀, R₀⁺)` is a perfectoid Tate pair. Define `ProEtaleSite.IsAffinoidPerfectoid` (the predicate
on `U = lim U_i` of AdicEtaleGeometry's site with its perfectoid pair `(R, R⁺)`); prove
`ProEtaleSite.affinoidPerfectoid_basis` (the affinoid perfectoid objects form a basis) ([Sch13]
§3, Definition 3.9, p. 15; §4, Definition 4.3 and Lemma 4.5(i), p. 23,
Proposition 4.8, p. 25, Lemma 4.10, final clause, and Remark 4.11, p. 26;
§6, Corollary 6.6, p. 36). *Needs:* AdicEtaleGeometry layer A1
(*pro-etale-site-corrected*); [P6.14](README.md); [P7.1](README.md); [P7.2](README.md); [P5.1](README.md).


**Checks.**

- The `ℂ_p` root-torus object has completed pair `ℂ_p⟨T±¹/p^∞⟩` with its power-bounded plus ring.
- The constant disc over a complete discretely valued mixed-characteristic field fails the perfectoid-object predicate.
- The empty object over an allowed p-adic base has the zero completed pair and satisfies the affinoid-perfectoid condition.

**Coverings on the supplied site.** (*proetale-site-coverings*) Its Checks
apply `AdicEtaleGeometry.AdicSpace.ProEtaleSite.mem_topology_iff` and
`isCovering_of_isFetTower` directly; the corrected topology belongs to AdicEtaleGeometry A1.


**Checks.**

- The identity family is a covering in the corrected topology.
- A supplied finite étale surjective tower gives a covering by `isCovering_of_isFetTower`.
- A family omitting a point of the pro-object cannot pass the supplied jointly-surjective covering condition.

*Needs:* AdicEtaleGeometry A1.10–A1.12 (*pro-etale-site-corrected*),
with the transfinite covering convention of [Sch13E], correction (1), p. 1.

**Affinoid perfectoid objects.** (*proetale-affinoid-perfectoid-objects*)
`ProEtaleSite.IsAffinoidPerfectoid` is existence of an `AffinoidPresentation`
with the completed perfectoid pair specified above ([Sch13] Definition 4.3(i), p. 23).

*Needs:* P5.1; P6.14; P7.1–P7.2; AdicEtaleGeometry A1.12's site carrier
and affinoid presentations ([Sch13] Definition 4.3(i), p. 23, Remark 4.11, p. 26).

**Checks.**

- `proEtale_torus_tower` (computation) — over `ℂ_p`, with compatible primitive
  `p`-power roots of unity and pseudouniformizer roots, the root-torus site object
  has an `AffinoidPresentation` whose stages are the relative torus, whose
  transitions raise its coordinate to the `p`th power, and whose pair is
  `ℂ_p⟨T^{±1/p^∞}⟩` with its power-bounded subring. The Check explicitly concludes
  `ProEtaleSite.IsAffinoidPerfectoid`. The general perfectoid-base and discrete-base
  cases are `proEtale_torus_tower_general` and `proEtale_torus_tower_discrete` below
  ([Sch13] Example 4.4, p. 23).
- `prodProfinite_Zp_sections` (computation) — supplied by [P6.8](README.md)
  on its perfectoid-space carrier: `O(Spa(ℂ_p, O_{ℂ_p}) × ℤ_p) = C⁰(ℤ_p, ℂ_p)`, with integral
  sections `C⁰(ℤ_p, O_{ℂ_p})`.
- `proEtale_not_affinoid_perfectoid` (non-example) — a constant object `Spa k⟨T⟩`, with `k`
  complete discretely valued of mixed characteristic `(0,p)`, is not affinoid perfectoid:
  `k⟨T⟩` is not perfectoid.

`ProEtaleSite.proEtale_rootTorus_exists` constructs this site object over a
complete nonarchimedean perfectoid field `K` of characteristic zero with
`p` topologically nilpotent and a chosen system of pseudouniformizer roots.
It requires no roots of unity in `K`. Its stages are AdicEtaleGeometry’s
`relativeTorus`, with structural maps the iterates of the coordinate p-power
endomorphism; its `AffinoidPresentation.pair` is the [P1](README.md) completed Laurent pair.
The Check `proEtale_torus_tower_general` uses this statement ([Sch13] Example 4.4,
p. 23). The `proEtale_torus_tower_discrete` Check excludes the same coordinate-root
presentation over a complete mixed-characteristic field with discrete valuation:
its coefficient values remain discrete, so adjoining only variable roots cannot
supply the pseudouniformizer required for perfectoidness. The constant-disc negative Check applies
`ProEtaleSite.IsAffinoidPerfectoid` to the constant object of this site.

`ProEtaleSite.AffinoidPresentation.baseMap` is the structure map
`X → Spa(ℚ_p, ℤ_p)`, obtained by composing the map to `Spa(k, k°)` with the
base-field map. `AffinoidPresentation` also carries an affinoid presentation in the actual
pro-étale site, an isomorphism from the `p`-adic completion of its integral section
colimit to the plus ring of a perfectoid pair, and the localization property after
inverting `p`. `IsAffinoidPerfectoid` means existence of all this data, including
`baseMap`. The presentation and predicate follow [Sch13] Definition 4.3, p. 23,
with the base-field scope of Remark 4.11, p. 26.
`AffinoidPresentation.points` identifies the spectrum of the completed pair, with its
specified plus ring, homeomorphically with the pro-object's space ([Sch13] Lemma 4.10,
final clause, p. 26; Lemma 4.5(i), p. 23, supplies the étale base-change compatibility).

**Checks.** Both carriers have `_empty` (the empty object), `_nonperfect` (the
constant rational `2`-adic point is excluded), and `_profinite` (products with a
profinite set preserve the condition) examples.
The `_padic_base` Checks extract the map to `Spa(ℚ_p, ℤ_p)` from the predicate.
The `_char_p` Checks exclude every site object over the spectrum of a complete
nontrivially valued characteristic-`p` field, including the empty site object:
that nonempty base admits no map to `Spa(ℚ_p, ℤ_p)`. This predicate is scoped
to a `p`-adic base; characteristic-`p` perfectoid spaces use the supplied P6 predicate.

Lean: README only.


### P7.16a finite flat regular towers with algebraically closed residue field

**Finite flat regular towers with algebraically closed residue field.**
(*regular-finite-flat-residue-tower*) Let `(R, m)` be a complete regular local ring (Mathlib
`IsRegularLocalRing`, of any characteristic) with residue field `k`. There is a filtered direct
system of finite flat `R`-algebras `R_i` such that each `(R_i, mR_i)` is a regular local ring and
`(lim→ R_i, m·lim→ R_i)` is a regular local ring with algebraically closed residue field. If `k` is
separably closed of characteristic `p > 0`, the `R_i` may be chosen of `p`-power rank over `R`
(then `k̄/k` is purely inseparable and its finite subextensions have `p`-power degree). The colimit
is Noetherian (a filtered colimit of noetherian local rings along flat local homomorphisms
`R_i → R_j` with `m_iR_j = m_j` is a noetherian local ring with maximal ideal `m_i` extended); it
is not claimed to be complete (`𝔽̄_p⟦x⟧ ⊋ colim 𝔽_{pⁿ}⟦x⟧`). The proof uses the three Cohen
presentations:
`R ≅ k⟦x_1, …, x_n⟧` (equal characteristic); `R ≅ W⟦x_1, …, x_n⟧` with `W` a complete discrete
valuation ring with uniformizer `p` (`p ∈ m∖m²`); `R ≅ W⟦x_1, …, x_n⟧/(p − f)` with
`f ∈ (p, x_1, …, x_n)²` (`p ∈ m²`), together with the regularity, normality, power-series,
quotient and filtered-colimit comparison theorems these presentations need ([Čes] §5, Lemma 5.1,
p. 11; [Čes] §5, proof of Lemma 5.1, pp. 11–12 (the ramified case of the construction)). *Needs:*
Mathlib `IsAdicComplete`, `Module.Flat`, `IsRegularLocalRing`.

**Cohen coefficient rings and regular presentations.** (*regular-cohen-presentations*)
`RegularTower.CohenDVR p k` is a characteristic-zero complete DVR with maximal ideal `(p)` and
specified residue isomorphism with `k`. `cohen_equalCharacteristic` assumes completeness and
regularity of `R` and equality of its characteristic with that of its residue field.
`cohen_unramified` and `cohen_ramified` assume characteristic zero and residue characteristic
`p`, splitting according to whether `p ∉ m²` or `p ∈ m²`. Their conclusions are precisely the
three displayed presentations. The forms used here are stated in [Čes], proof of Lemma 5.1,
pp. 11–12. The coefficient-ring existence theorem is also
[Stacks, Theorem 10.160.8, Tag 032A](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/032A).

`powerSeries_regular_field` and `powerSeries_regular_cohen` assert regularity for finitely many
variables over a field and over a Cohen DVR, respectively
([Stacks, Remark 10.160.9, Tag 032C](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/032C)).
`ramified_quotient_regular` assumes `f ∈ (p,x_1,…,x_n)²`: then `p-f` is part of a regular system
of parameters, and its quotient is regular
([Stacks, Lemma 10.106.3](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00NN)).
`regular_normal` asserts integral closedness of a regular local domain
([Stacks, Lemma 10.157.5, Tag 0567](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0567)).
`powerSeries_finite_flat` extends a finite flat local map of Cohen coefficient rings to their
finite-variable power-series rings ([Čes], proof of Lemma 5.1, pp. 11–12).
`exists_residueTower` names the finite flat regular system and the algebraically closed residue
field of its regular colimit. In the equal-characteristic construction its maximal-adic
completion is `k̄⟦x_1,…,x_n⟧`; the mixed-characteristic construction uses the completed coefficient
DVR and then the indicated quotient. Noetherianity in this construction follows by faithful-flat
descent from these completions ([Čes], proof of Lemma 5.1, pp. 11–12;
[Stacks, Tag 033E](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/033E),
[Tag 05UU](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05UU),
[Tag 00MK](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00MK)).

Checks:

- `cohen_test_equalChar_zeroVariables` (degenerate) — applying
  `cohen_equalCharacteristic` to a field `k` chooses `n=0`; its resulting presentation is
  `k ≃ (ResidueField k)⟦Fin 0⟧`. The Check retains the theorem's regularity, completeness
  and equal-characteristic hypotheses and tests its chosen number of variables.
- `cohen_test_ramified_two` (computation) — `W⟦X⟧/(p-X²)` is regular, including at `p=2`.
- `cohen_test_parameter_nonunit` (non-example) — the marked `p` in a Cohen DVR is not a unit.

- `cohen_test_parameter_not_square` (non-example) — the coefficient parameter of
  `CohenDVR` satisfies `p ∉ m²`.
- `cohen_test_wrong_characteristic` (non-example) — the characteristic-zero ring of
  `CohenDVR` cannot be isomorphic to a characteristic-`p` residue field.
  Together with `cohen_test_parameter_nonunit`, these test the coefficient-ring carrier.

The coefficient-extension interface `coefficient_extension` supplies an integral DVR extension
of a Cohen DVR with uniformizer `p`, algebraically closed residue field, and a finite flat DVR
subextension containing each element. It does not assert that this integral extension is
complete. `powerSeriesDiagram` applies finite-variable power series coefficientwise.
`powerSeries_colimit_field` completes the union of finite coefficient-field extensions at the
ideal generated by the variables. `powerSeries_colimit_cohen` completes at `(p,x_1,…,x_n)` and
uses the `p`-adic completion of the coefficient colimit on the right. The latter assumes
complete DVR stages with uniformizer `p`, finite flat over a fixed Cohen DVR. These are the
completion comparisons in [Čes], proof of Lemma 5.1, pp. 11–12.
`exists_residueTower_primePower` states the rank refinement with separably closed residue
field of characteristic `p`; its stages have rank `p^e` for some `e≥0`.

`powerSeries_colimit_regular` asserts regularity of the same finite-flat coefficient-extension
colimit before completion. `ramified_colimit_completion` starts with `f` in the square of the
maximal ideal at a fixed stage: quotienting the colimit by `p-f` gives a regular local ring,
and its maximal-adic completion is the quotient by the coefficientwise image of `p-f` over the
completed coefficient DVR ([Čes], proof of Lemma 5.1, pp. 11–12).

### P7.17 finite flat regular towers with perfectoid completion

**Finite flat regular towers with perfectoid completion.** (*regular-finite-flat-perfectoid-tower*)
Let `(R, m)` be a complete regular local ring of mixed characteristic `(0, p)` with perfect residue
field `k` (so `W ≅ W(k)` in the Cohen presentations of *regular-finite-flat-residue-tower*), and
`W := W(k)`. There is a tower `{R_m}_{m≥0}` of finite flat `R`-algebras `R_m` of `p`-power rank
over `R`, each a regular local ring, such that the `p`-adic completion `R̂_∞` of
`R_∞ := lim→_m R_m` is perfectoid (integral perfectoid in the sense of [BMS] Definition 3.5, so
`R̂_∞[1/p]` is a perfectoid Tate ring). Explicitly: if `p ∈ m∖m²`, then `R ≅ W⟦x_1, …, x_n⟧` and
`R_m := W[p^{1/p^m}]⟦x_1^{1/p^m}, …, x_n^{1/p^m}⟧`; if `p ∈ m²`, then `R ≅ W⟦x_1, …, x_n⟧/(p − f)`
with `f ∈ (p, x_1, …, x_n)²` and `R_m := W⟦x_1^{1/p^m}, …, x_n^{1/p^m}⟧/(p − f)`. The finite levels
are not perfectoid, and `R_∞` is not complete. The criterion used is [Čes] Lemma 4.7, in the
instance proved here: for a `p`-torsion-free ring `S` with `(ϖ^p) = (p)` for some `ϖ ∈ S`, if `S`
is integrally closed in `S[1/p]` then `x ↦ x^p : S/ϖ → S/p` is injective, and if moreover every
element of `S/p` is a `p`-th power then the `p`-adic completion of `S` is perfectoid ([Čes] §5,
Lemma 5.2, p. 12; [Čes] §5, proof of Lemma 5.2, p. 12 (the reduction of the ramified case to a unit
multiple of `p`); [Čes] §4, Lemma 4.7, p. 8 (the criterion)). *Needs:*
*regular-finite-flat-residue-tower*; P1; Mathlib `WittVector`, `IsIntegrallyClosedIn`,
`IsAdicComplete`, `IsRegularLocalRing`.

`RegularTower.exists_perfectoidTower` names the sequence of finite flat regular algebras,
the `p`-power rank condition, and integral perfectoidness of the `p`-adic completion of
its ring colimit. The perfect residue-field hypothesis is an explicit `PerfectRing` assumption;
completeness of the initial regular local ring is maximal-adic ([Čes] Lemma 5.2, p. 12).

### Examples

The compatible-root disc and torus run through the whole layer: for a perfectoid Tate ring `R`
whose pseudouniformiser `ϖ` has compatible `p`-power roots,
`Spa(R⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, R⁺⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩) ~ lim_n Spa(R⟨T^{1/p^n}⟩, R⁺⟨T^{1/p^n}⟩)` along
`T^{1/p^n} ↦ T^{1/p^n}`, and likewise for `R⟨T^{±1/p^∞}⟩` ([Sch13] Example 4.4 for the torus over a
perfectoid field); the whole disc is good at level `0` with `V = X_0`, and so is its rational subset
`{|T| ≤ |ϖ|}`, every rational subset of the perfectoid disc being the preimage of a rational subset
at a finite level; the Huber pairs `(R⟨T^{1/p^n}⟩, R⁺⟨T^{1/p^n}⟩)` with `A_{n,0} = R⁺⟨T^{1/p^n}⟩`,
`I_n = ϖA_{n,0}` have completed direct limit `R⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩`, already uniform, and every finite étale
`R⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩`-algebra is defined over some `R⟨T^{1/p^n}⟩`; the integral tower `R⁺⟨T^{1/p^m}⟩`
with `w_m(r T^{a/p^{m+1}}) = Φ(r) T^{a/p^m}` is Frobenius-controlled with `A_∞⁺ = R⁺⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩`,
`A_∞° = R°⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩` and the bound `ϖR°⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ ⊆ R⁺⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩` (because
`ϖR° ⊆ R°° ⊆ R⁺`); the characteristic-`p` tower `R♭⁺⟨T^{1/p^m}⟩` with `α_m` induced by
`R⁺/ϖ^p ≅ R♭⁺/(ϖ♭)^p` gives the tilt `R♭⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩`; two perfectoid tilde-limits of the tower (for
instance `R⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩` and its presentation through `T ↦ T^p` transition maps) are uniquely
isomorphic; the preimage of the torus `{|T| ≥ 1}` is `~ lim` of the tori `{|T^{1/p^n}| ≥ 1}`; over a
perfectoid field `K` the Gauss point `x` has `k(x_n)^` the completion of `K(T^{1/p^n})` for the Gauss
norm, whose union is dense in `k(x)^`, so the tower is a residue-field tilde-limit; every finite
étale cover of the perfectoid disc is pulled back from some `K⟨T^{1/p^n}⟩`; and for `p ≠ 2` the
Kummer cover `S ↦ S² = T` of the perfectoid torus pulls back to
`Spa(K⟨S^{±1/p^∞}⟩) ~ lim Spa(K⟨S^{±1/p^n}⟩)`.

The Shimura towers are the geometric instances. [Torsion] Theorem III.1.2 and Corollary III.2.19:
the Siegel anticanonical tower `X(p^{-m}ε)` (`ε < 1/2`) has, over an affine `Spf R_{m_0}`,
preimages `Spf R_m` forming a Frobenius-controlled integral tower with `ϖ = p^{(1−ε)/p}`, `R_∞` the
`p`-adic completion of `colim_m R_m`, absolute Frobenius inducing `R_∞/p^{(1−ε)/p} ≅ R_∞/p^{1−ε}`,
whence unique perfectoid spaces `X_{Γ_0(p^∞)}(ε)_a ~ lim_m X_{Γ_0(p^m)}(ε)_a` (and similarly `X*`,
`A`) over `Q_p^cycl` whose tilt is the open subset of the perfection `X′*perf` where `|Ha| ≥ |t|^ε`
(using `X′*(p^{-m}ε)/t^{1−ε} = X*(p^{-m}ε)/p^{1−ε}`, Theorem III.2.15(i)), `X′*perf` over
`F_p((t^{1/(p−1)p^∞}))` being the tilde-limit of the Siegel space along relative Frobenius
(Definition III.2.18); `|X*_{Γ(p^∞)}|` is glued from the `Spa(R_∞, R_∞⁺)` over affinoid perfectoid
subsets (Definition III.3.5) with `X*_{Γ(p^∞)} ~ lim_{K_p} X*_{K_p}`, unique up to unique
isomorphism, the principal congruence subgroups `K(p^n) = ker(GSp_{2g}(Z_p) → GSp_{2g}(Z/p^n))`
having a witness in `GSp_{2g}(Q_p)` so that the tower may be indexed by `n`, while the anticanonical
levels `Γ_0(p^m)` have none and their tilde-limit is the `Γ_0(p^∞)`-level; and the finite étale
`D_m → X_{Γ_0(p^m)}(ε)_a` pulls back to the perfectoid `D_{mΓ_0(p^∞)}` (§III.2.4). [CHJ] Theorem 2.8:
`X_∞` is glued from the two good affinoids `V_i = π_HT^{-1}(V_i)` pulled back from level `K(p^N)`,
indexed by the cofinal `K(p^n)`, and the rational subset `X_{∞,w}` of `V_1` is the preimage of an
affinoid `S ⊆ X_{K(p^N)}` (proof of Theorem 2.17). [BHW] Theorem 5.11: `X_{Γ_0*(p^∞)}(ε)_a ~ lim_n X_{Γ_0*(p^n)}(ε)_a` for Hilbert modular varieties via relative Frobenius modulo `p^{1−δ}` (Lemma
5.12), restricted from `X*(p^{-∞}ε) ~ lim X*(p^{-n}ε)` to the open modular locus; the finite étale
`X_{Γ_1*(p^n)} → X_{Γ_0*(p^n)}` pulls back to a tower of finite étale perfectoid spaces whose limit
is the perfectoid tilde-limit `X_{Γ_1*(p^∞)}(ε)_a`; the `Γ_0`-, `Γ_1`- and `Γ`-towers are distinct
towers, not cofinal reindexings. [HJ] Lemma 5.11 and its proof ([P8](../PerfectoidTowers/README.md#layer-p8-finite-quotients-and-closed-perfectoid-loci-in-towers)): for locally noetherian `X_i` with finite
transition maps and `X = lim X_i^◇` perfectoid, `X` has a basis of affinoid perfectoid opens pulled
back from finite levels, and for affinoid `X_i` every rational subset of the limit is pulled back
from a finite level.

The pro-finite-étale and formal examples: the universal pro-finite-étale cover
`X_∞ = Spa(Â_∞, Â_∞⁺)` of a connected affinoid noetherian `X = Spa(A, A⁺)` over `Spa(Q_p, Z_p)`
satisfies `X_∞ ~ lim X_i` for the finite étale `X_i = Spa(A_i, A_i⁺) → X` in both the sectionwise
and the residue-field sense, has no nonsplit finite étale covers, and
`H^j(X_{∞,ét}, L) = colim_i H^j(X_{i,ét}, L)` for all `j ≥ 0` ([Sch13] Theorem 4.9, the form used downstream in
`p`-adic Hodge theory); for the universal finite étale `G_i`-torsor tower `A → A_i` of a Tate
`Z_p`-algebra, the uniform completion of `colim A_i` is perfectoid,
`Spd(Â_∞, Â_∞⁺) = lim Spd(A_i, A_i⁺)` and `Spa(Â_∞, Â_∞⁺) ~ lim Spa(A_i, A_i⁺)` ([ECD] Lemma 15.3,
Proposition 15.4); `T(G)^{ad} ~ lim G[p^n]^{ad}` ([SW13] §3, proof of Proposition 3.3.2); the
generic fibre of `Spf Z_p⟦X_1^{1/p^∞}, …, X_n^{1/p^∞}⟧` is preperfectoid relative to
`Spa(Q_p, Z_p)` in [SW13] Definition 2.3.9: after each base change to a characteristic-zero
perfectoid field it has perfectoid strong completions locally ([SW13] Example 2.3.12,
Proposition 2.3.13 and the paragraph following it, p. 19). This relative condition does not
imply P7.7's `IsPreperfectoid` before base change; the zero-variable case is
`Spa(Q_p, Z_p)`, which fails that absolute condition. For a perfectoid field `K` the strong
completion of
`Spa(K[ε]/(ε²), O_K + Kε)` is `Spa(K, O_K)`, with `Spa(K, O_K) ~ Spa(K[ε]/(ε²), O_K + Kε)` although
the two spaces differ, while for `X` perfectoid `X̂ = X`; the perfected projective space
`((P^n)^{ad})^{perf} ~′ lim_φ (P^n)^{ad}` over a perfectoid field of characteristic `p` ([Sch12] Theorem 8.5)
has equal étale topoi at every level, whereas the Frobenius tower `T ↦ T^p` of `P^n` in
characteristic `0` has non-inseparable residue extensions and only the limit statement of P7.15
applies; for `Y = Spa(k⟨T⟩, k°⟨T⟩)`, `Y^{perf} = Spa(k⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, k°⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩)` with
`Y^{perf}_ét ≃ Y_ét`; and a pro-étale `G`-tower of perfectoid spaces `X_j → X` has
`X_∞ = lim X_j` ([P9.4](../PerfectoidTowers/README.md#layer-p9-continuous-torsor-descent-with-coefficients) in the perfectoid case).

The regular towers: for `R = 𝔽_p⟦x⟧` the colimit `lim→ 𝔽_{p^n}⟦x⟧` is not complete, its completion
`𝔽̄_p⟦x⟧` being strictly larger, and for `k = 𝔽_p` the levels `𝔽_{p^n}⟦x⟧` have rank `n`, not a
`p`-power; for `R = ℤ_p⟦x⟧/(p − x²) = ℤ_p[√p]`, `p ∈ m²`, `R_i = W(𝔽_{p^i})[√p]` with `i` ordered by
divisibility, and the colimit is regular with parameter `x = √p`; for `R = ℤ_p` (`n = 0`),
`R_m = ℤ_p[p^{1/p^m}]` and `R̂_∞` is the `p`-adic completion of `ℤ_p[p^{1/p^∞}]`, a perfectoid ring,
while every finite level fails the perfectoid criterion: for `m ≥ 1`, `R_m/p ≅ 𝔽_p[T]/(T^{p^m})` and
`T` is not a `p`-th power, and at `m = 0` Frobenius on `𝔽_p` is surjective but no `ϖ ∈ ℤ_p` has
`(ϖ^p) = (p)`; for these displayed towers the residue field stays `k`, so perfectoidness of their completion
  forces `k` perfect, since Frobenius surjectivity descends to `k`; and the
completion is `p`-adic, not `m_∞`-adic.

The Lean `example`s of `Suggested.lean` for this layer check that the consecutive maps of the tower
diagram are the transition maps, that at `p = 2` a stage with parameter `2` is the zero ring, and
that no stage of an integral tower is a field (so `𝔽_p` has no constant tower).

localisation, open subspaces and fibre products; P2.3, P2.5, P2.6, P2.9, P2.10), P3 (finite étale and étale morphisms, the étale site and the tilting equivalence;
P3.10, P3.15–P3.18, P3.22), P5 (the limit of affinoid perfectoids, qcqs étale descent; P5.2, P5.3,
P5.12); AdicSpacesPartII R0.19.5–R0.19.8 and P5.4’s perfectoid limit comparisons.

AdicEtaleGeometry A1.0.3–A1.0.5 (finite étale colimits and completion) and A4.4 (uniformization).

## Downstream consumers

DiamondsAndVStacks D0–D6 consumes P0–P7's perfectoid algebra, spaces, tilting,
pro-étale calculus and completion bound: D0 uses `ProKappa` and `completion_cardinality_bound`
(P6.10, P6.2) and Cartan's lemma on acyclic bases, the classical case of P0.29; D1–D6 use perfectoid
spaces, tilting, almost purity, finite-stage descent and the `κ`-small and pro-étale calculus of
P0–P6; D2–D3 use the Amitsur complex and descent of P0.25; D3 restricts the separatedness of P4.19
to perfectoid spaces; and D5 and D3 use the spectrum comparison of P1.12 and the mod-`ϖ` chain of
P1.28. DiamondsAndVStacks owns the v-site (precoverage and topology in D2.2, subcanonicity and
v-descent in D2.7), built on the compact-open covering condition that P7 uses without any topology.
It owns `Diamond`, `IsSpatial` and spatiality, and the comparison of its characteristic-`p` diamond
functor with the represented functors of P7.11. PerfectoidTowers P8–P9 imports both roadmaps for
finite quotients, spatial presentations, closed loci and continuous torsor descent; its P8.14
(Zariski-closed embeddings over every affinoid perfectoid open) and P8.15 (analytic separatedness,
which uses the diagonal over an analytic base of P2.17) are distinct from P4.16 and P4.19.

AdicEtaleGeometry supplies generic henselian approximation and completed-colimit finite étale
comparisons in A1.0.4–A1.0.5, and the algebraic torsor-tower and completion theory in
A4.2–A4.5 and A4.7. Its finite-group module descent in A4.2a uses the Galois tensor
isomorphism and Mathlib's faithfully flat descent over arbitrary commutative rings;
PerfectoidTowers P9 applies it to coefficient descent. P3.21 provides the integral almost
cohomological specialization of AdicEtaleGeometry A1.6a's stable-basis vector-bundle theory.
Sousperfectoid frames and spaces use P1.1's predicate
`Perfectoid.IsPerfectoidTateRing` in P3.17a. Every perfectoid space is sousperfectoid:
apply `Huber.IsSousperfectoid.of_isPerfectoidTateRing` to its affinoid perfectoid charts.
AdicSpacesPartIV R5.5 consumes this class and P3.17b's polydisc calculation to construct
products with smooth rigid spaces. Perfectoid torsor presentations belong to P6.16–P6.17;
their v-sheaf and diamond interpretations belong to DiamondsAndVStacks D6.
Perfectoid Shimura varieties and period
spaces use these foundations.
